The Dark Sea Wyvern Abyssal Lagiacrus (ラギアクルス希少種, Ragiakurusu Kishō-shu) is a Leviathan introduced in Monster Hunter 3 Ultimate.
It is a Rare Species of the Lagiacrus.
Summary
A dark-shelled Rare Species of the Lagiacrus illuminated only by the blue glow of their electrical organs. Being elderly individuals of the species, they possess a larger body and are exclusively encountered underwater. The electrical organs of Abyssal Lagiacrus are enhanced with age and can hold a powerful charge continuously, greatly amplifying the monster's electrical output. In combat, these Leviathans can create swirling underwater vortexes that can suck away a Hunter's very breath.

Physiology
The Abyssal Lagiacrus is technically not a separate species from the regular Lagiacrus, instead, it is an elderly Lagiacrus that has grown too large and heavy to venture onto land. As a result, it moved into the sea permanently, its body changing and adapting to dark depths over untold years of fully aquatic life. These changes have manifested most prominently in the Leviathan's coloration: the Abyssal Lagiacrus is jet-black, blending into the dark sea. However, despite its dark surface, the scales of the Abyssal Lagiacrus have been noted to give off an eerie, unearthly glow. Its dark form is illuminated by a constant stream of electricity that flows across the body, and like with the regular species, this charge seems to be concentrated at the Deathly Shockers on its back. These organs are more powerful than their counterparts on the regular species and are said to be able to electrify entire seas. However, the origin of this perpetual electric charge is believed to be due to a separate organ, called a Dynamo, that is only found in the body of the Abyssal Lagiacrus. How exactly it functions is unknown, although it appears to supply the Rare Species with nearly endless electric energy.
Behavior
The Abyssal Lagiacrus is extremely elusive and rare, to the point where its existence was long only known about through an ancient scroll. It has often been called the Lord of the Underworld throughout history due to its mysterious nature and seeming dominion of the deepest depths. It has only been encountered in the Underwater Ruins near Moga Village and appears to be quite aggressive, attacking Hunters on sight.
Development
When the base species of Lagiacrus was originally created, its fight design included an even more intense focus on underwater action. However, as Monster Hunter 3 was the first game to feature underwater combat, the decision was made to tone down underwater encounters as a way to ease players into this all-new combat style. As a result, Lagiacrus was redesigned to be fought both on land and in water. For Monster Hunter 3 Ultimate, Abyssal Lagiacrus was chosen as a way to revive that original fight concept for Lagiacrus, being an encounter that takes place entirely underwater.
As it was going to share an arena with Ceadeus, a lot of thought went into how to differentiate the Abyssal Lagiacrus from the marine Elder Dragon while also producing the kind of impact a Rare Species monster deserves. The monster was made nimble and agile, in constrast to the giant and lumbering Ceadeus. Simultaneously, the Abyssal Lagiacrus was designed to notably larger than the base species. This element was included for two reasons: It made the monster more intimidating and made it more suitable for four hunter multiplayer, as the larger body would offer more surface to attack during a crowded battle.
According to Kaname Fujioka, the Abyssal Lagiacrus being constantly charged up with electricity was an aspect intended to create a naturally tense atmosphere, with the monster glowing in the dark sea. Additionally, this behavior would instantly communicate the rare species' superiority over the base species.

The Sulfur Slashing Wyvern Acidic Glavenus (ディノバルド亜種, Dinobarudo Ashu) is a Brute Wyvern introduced in Monster Hunter World: Iceborne.
It is a Subspecies of the Glavenus.
Summary

They have exchanged the huge, rugged blade of their common counterparts for sleeker, more precise ones, which are properly revealed once the crystals on their tail have been stripped away.

Physiology
The Acidic Glavenus is a Subspecies of the Glavenus that displays the same general body build as the common species, however, there several visual differences to be found. The Acidic Glavenus has a dark-green shell accented with pale yellows and whites in certain areas, and the tail of this Subspecies has been noted to be shorter and thinner in comparison.
While the common Glavenus can be found in a variety of biomes, the Acidic Glavenus is highly specialized for life in the Rotten Vale of the New World. The most characteristic adaptation of this Subspecies is the emergence of an entirely new organ dedicated to protecting the Brute Wyvern from the detrimental effects of the bacterial effluvium residing in the Vale. This special organ separates the effluvia that is ingested through feeding and breathing into a segmented chamber, where the harmful bacteria gets broken down and digested. Through this, the Acidic Glavenus extracts energy from the digested effluvium, a process which produces various waste materials that combine into a highly corrosive fluid. This fluid is continuously expelled through glands on the tail, where it can crystalize and accumulate over time if it is not removed regularly. The secretion of this fluid is stimulated by physical exertion. This same mechanism is believed to aid in removing toxins from the Brute Wyvern's body, which may explain why the Acidic Glavenus displays an higher than average resistance to Poison.
The corrosive fluid that is expelled on the tail's surface plays a crucial role in the Brute Wyvern's combat style, as the fluid's acidic properties corrodes armor and defensive plating rapidly, making the tail swipes even deadlier than before. As the tail is swung around, the acid can be flung at enemies in liquid and crystalline forms. As the Acidic Glavenus moves around in battle, the glands excrete increasing amounts of acid, which continues to crystalize as it remains and accumulates. Eventually, the tail becomes covered in large crystalized sheets of solidified acid. In this state, the tail spreads the corrosive substance in large quantities with every swing and poses the greatest danger. however, the weight of the crystals slows the Acidic Glavenus down, and it will usually scrape the acid off with its jaws to restore the balance and weight of its tail.
Behavior
The Acidic Glavenus is highly specialized to life in the Rotten Vale and Rotted region of the Guiding Lands, and is thus not found anywhere else. Due to its sophisticated effluvia filtration system, the Acidic Glavenus can traverse the entire Vale and even feed on infected prey. When fighting an adversary, the Acidic Glavenus makes ample use of its tail, albeit in a slightly different way to its nominate species. While the regular Glavenus often uses its thick and heavy tail like a Great Sword, the Acidic Glavenus' thinner tail is wielded with grace akin to a Longsword.

Physiology
The Agnaktor is a unique Leviathan found in volcanic regions adapted to live in and near lava. It is covered head to tail in a red-shelled armor that is known for its heat resistant properties. A large dorsal sail adorns the back, and the tail tapers into a vertical fin. Most notable is the monster's yellow beak, which produces a characteristic clacking sound when opened and shut rapidly. Like many Leviathans, the Agnaktor is capable of swimming through a medium, although while most other monsters of its class swim through water or sand, the Agnaktor instead submerges itself in lava and even burrows through hard volcanic bedrock. This rock burrowing behavior is enabled through the beak, which is specialized in concentrating an enormous amount of force into its tip and is extremely tough. The Agnaktor can thus use it to break into the bedrock through an initial crack, before drilling into it further by performing spiraling movements aided by its flexible spine. However, while the beak appears to be the primary feature that allows for rock burrowing, it is believed to have evolved partially in order to break through the tough shells of armored Herbivores, such as the Rhenoplos.
The Leviathan's ability to submerge itself in lava is enabled by a curious feature of its shell armor. The gaps between the scales of the Agnaktor continuously secrete a specialized body fluid that functions as a buffer layer between the lava and the shell. This further enhances the fire resistance of the shell, thus allowing the monster to swim through lava without much trouble. This body fluid has another function beyond this, as when the Agnaktor emerges from lava, special grooves and protrusions on the surface of its shell catch small chunks of lava that are then adhered to the shell by the buffer fluid. This covers the Leviathan in hot lava initially, before shortly transforming into hardened volcanic rock that temporarily fuses to the body upon cooling, acting as a powerful defensive measure. This rigid and powerful shield can deflect most attacks, yet will melt away as soon as the monster burrows again.
Another noteworthy physiological feature of the Agnaktor lies in its Scalding Pleura, a specialized organ that interacts with its volcanic environments. The Agnaktor's Pleura collects the various molten materials the Leviathan swallows as it swims through lava, sectioning them off safely from the rest of the body. The collected materials can then be reheated and concentrated in the Pleura before being expelled from the mouth in the form of a concentrated jet of lava, not unlike the heat ray of the Gravios. On behalf of its Pleura, the Agnaktor wields an extremely powerful weapon. The organ additionally seems to have other functions too, as it has been observed that various molten rocks and ores congregate and fuse into an armor plate on its chest, roughly where the Pleura is located.
Behavior
The Agnaktor inhabits volcanic areas such as the Volcanic Hollow, and while it was once considered rare, there have been more frequent sightings in recent years.
As a large carnivore, the Agnaktor feeds on most smaller monsters in its environment, although possesses a specific preference for the Rhenoplos. The Agnaktor leaves behind extremely distinct predation marks as a result of using its beak to drill through its prey's tough hide. However, it is not secure in its position on the food chain, as both the juvenile and adult Agnaktor must be prepared to either flee from, or fend off the powerful Brachydios.
During the breeding season, the Agnaktor must race others of its kind to the top of the nearest volcano, as that is where mating occurs. In order to do this, it must learn how to both burrow through volcanic rock and how to seamlessly leap out of the floor of a cave and immediately dig into the cave's ceiling so as to ensure maximum speed. The ability to burrow through ceilings is thus seen as an indicator that an Agnaktor has successfully mated before.
Once mating has occurred, the female Agnaktor produces between 20 and 30 young, who initially grow inside of eggs that are themselves inside of the mother. Rather uniquely, these eggs hatch before they exit the body, resulting in live birth. The juvenile Agnaktor is called an Uroktor, and only very few among a clutch will live long enough to grow into their mature form. Regardless of whether the Leviathan is a juvenile or adult, it can be found conversing with other Agnaktor and Uroktor using its distinctive beak-clacking, which may be used in any number of social behaviors.

Physiology
The Ahtal-Ka is a large Neopteron whose body is covered in a glistening golden carapace which shines with a mysterious beauty. The front of its body is patterned with several blue stripes, with additional purple stripes present on its forearms and legs; these purple parts of its shelling typically fetch for much higher prices. Some parts of the Ahtal-Ka’s shell additionally display iridescent properties, changing in color depending on the angle from which they are viewed. In contrast to this colorful display, the backside of the Ahtal-Ka is a much duller brown in coloration. As it appears to blend into its surroundings when viewed from above, the Ahtal-Ka is believed to have evolved this duller coloration to aid in camouflaging into the sandy environments it lives in. The Ahtal-Ka sports three frills around its head that resemble a royal headress, with the anterior most ending in two pointed tips. The Ahtal-Ka possesses six limbs: four of them are used for walking, while the anterior most limbs are modified into grasping appendages bearing a pair of sharp Foreblades that boast tremendous slicing ability and serve as very effective weapons against threats. Its abdomen is large and sports five pointed claws at its tip, making the entire appendage resemble an upturned hand.
Likely the Ahtal-Ka's most recognizable feature is its ability to produce a fine golden thread from its abdomen composed of a fine crystalline pattern. This silk can be shot from the abdomen before expanding into a net, or as a thread to latch onto objects, from which the Ahtal-Ka will proceed to carry said object on its back. The object is kept connected to the abdomen through a thread connected to its Foreblades, helping to keep it secured in place, with the silks superb tensile strength preventing it from snapping even as the object in question is forcibly swung around. However, carrying heavy objects typically strains the Ahtal-Ka and it will lose its balance if its head receives too much damage, dropping the object it was carrying in the process. In addition to this, the Ahtal-Ka is capable of creating a highly corrosive gas that can be sprayed from its underside and which can be released in high enough quantities to even still be performable while the monster is controlling its nest. Further, the Ahtal-Ka secretes a liquid pheromone that is highly fragrant in nature, the odor being strong enough to be detected for several miles.
Currently, each Ahtal-Ka thus far encountered by the Guild has been recognised to be female, and it is currently unknown what a male Ahtal-Ka looks like.
Behavior
The Ahtal-Ka is most famed for the construction of its mobile nest, the Ahtal-Neset. It is constructed out of materials that it has scavenged from its surroundings to form a protective layer of armor around itself, with these materials often being forcibly and almost haphazardly attached together, making it clear the Neset is not a true living organism. While the Ahtal-Ka will use natural materials in the construction of its Neset, with there being some rumored sightings of individuals constructing their nests entirely out of natural materials, it has been observed to primarily utilize man-made materials for construction. In one case, an individual was reported using the hull of a ship to form the head of its Neset. This likely stems from the fact that these man-made materials are far stronger than anything found in nature, providing the Ahtal-Ka with a much stronger foundation for its nest. Before human civilization existed, it was likely that the Ahtal-Ka constructed its nest out of natural materials, such as stone and wood. When the monster was first discovered, it was originally believed to be a moving fortress of absolutely immense size, which confused researchers when it could seemingly disappear so easily. However, it was uncovered that the Neset was merely being puppeteered by the much smaller Neopteron.
This preference in materials may lead to the Ahtal-Ka ransacking towns and fortresses alike in search of better materials to further improve upon its nest, which it is noted to never stray too far away from. This typically occurs when it has to renew its nest's armor with a fresh coating of materials after it has shed its previous batch. Spelling disaster for whatever settlement it chooses to attack, there are often reports of entire fortress walls suddenly vanishing after an Ahtal-Ka has raided. However, the Ahtal-Ka can be quite picky about what materials it chooses to use for its Neset, leaving behind anything that it does not wish to utilize. The design that the Neset takes is influenced by the Neopteron's upbringing, with it purposely shaping its nest to resemble any creatures it encountered during its growth that appeared to be powerful. Once constructed, the nest is both held together and controlled by the golden silk of the Ahtal-Ka. In order to puppeteer its movements, the Ahtal-Ka typically resides within a large golden cocoon at the center of the nest and attaches its golden silk to various different parts of its creation. However, if the golden silk wrapped around the Neset were to be cut, the Ahtal-Ka would lose control over its nest, preventing it from moving for a time. If enough silk is destroyed, the Neset will eventually collapse in its entirety.
While the Ahtal-Ka primarily resides within sandy environments, it tends to form a permanent territory and will periodically embark on migratory journeys to find a new location to settle in. This is the primary purpose behind the construction of its Neset, which is designed to allow for easy migrations between settlements. The Ahtal-Ka has even been known to use the ruins of human-made structures as temporary homes, with one individual having been found in a ruined castle it had reconstructed to its former glory seemingly overnight, keeping it intact through the use of its golden silk. Once it has settled in its new habitat, the Ahtal-Ka typically keeps its Neset burrowed beneath the ground when not in use, bringing it to the surface only when needed to fight off potential threats. As the Ahtal-Ka unearths its nest, a large amount of sand is kicked up into the air, causing a localized sandstorm. Alongside its Neset, the Ahtal-Ka generally keeps a few spare objects inside its dwelling to be used as weapons against intruders, appearing to favor Dragonators in particular, often keeping several beneath the ground which it will unearth to launch at enemies.
Music
Main article: Ahtal-Ka (Music)
"Queen of the Ruined Castle" and "Castle on the Run" are Ahtal-Ka's 1st and 2nd phase theme respectively, with the latter playing when Ahtal-Neset is unleashed. During the final phase, a looped version of " Proof of a Hero (MHXXver.) " plays.
Development
Daisuke Ichihara had a dilemma on what to use for the final boss of Monster Hunter Generations Ultimate, and had seemingly two choices; the regular large monsters that players hunt or the huge monsters in special hunts, like Lao-Shan Lung. Regular monsters had the advantage of being able to be hunted by normal weapons the player is used to, while the extra-large monsters could generate the excitement of an event-like hunt where the player can make full use of field equipment, so both of these types of monsters would make good final bosses. However, a person in charge of the planning staff suggested, "Why not make a monster that allows you to enjoy both?" Thus, in order to incorporate the two versions of playability into the same monster, Ahtal-Ka was created as a normal-sized monster that becomes gigantic after covering themselves in rubble.
Ahtal-Ka was inspired by the Devil's Flower Mantis, a mantis species native to Africa, which helped with the ancient Egyptian motif the Neopteron possessed, with the bandage-like patterns on its body inspired by mummies and pharaohs.

Physiology
The Ajarakan is a Fanged Beast with an ape-like build and stance, boasting a muscular body with highly developed forelimbs that can grapple foes and easily climb terrain, while its hind limbs are much smaller in comparison. Its body is covered in metallic scales and shells that are mostly red in coloration and become darker towards the ends of its limbs, while the scales on its face and upper body have tinges of teal resembling oxidized copper. The Ajarakan's face is affixed in a perpetual snarl and crowned with a flame-like crest, while its back similarly is adorned with a much larger carapace of twisted, flame-like shells. Its long tail is thick and ends with a wide, gnarled, club-like structure at the tip. It has highly dexterous hands with four digits each—including an opposable thumb—on the back of its hands, the Ajarakan grows hardened, white pads that allow it to walk on its knuckles comfortably.
The scales of the Ajarakan are spiked at their tips and somewhat resemble small flames; they are extremely tough, able to resist scratches from even the hardest stone. These scales form the Ajarakan's shell, characterized by its rough surface texture, and allow it to produce numerous sparks in response to the slightest friction. Its dense structure allows the shelling to withstand the explosive force the Ajarakan wields. Multiple sections of these shells then merge on the back of the Ajarakan into its distinctive ridge, which is often likened to flames in color and shape. It is believed the unique shell structure of the Ajarakan develops through a process in which the oils of the Oilwell Basin cling to its body and react with its scales, transforming them into this peculiar shape and color.
The bone marrow of the Ajarakan maintains a high temperature and is considered almost too hot to handle, a trait it shares with the brainstem of the monster—the Ajarakan's medulla is constantly burning, as if all of the Ajarakan's heat was concentrated in it. Like many other monsters, the Ajarakan may rarely grow a jewel in its body, which glows red and is claimed to contain the power to detonate bedrock.
The Ajarakan covers itself in molten metal that hardens and reinforces its carapace and scales; by scraping the metal on its carapace against itself or the ground, the Ajarakan is able to generate immense amounts of heat and friction. Through this, the Ajarakan is able to reach a high enough temperature to melt parts of the ground as well as any incoming bullets. Continuous friction will cause its body temperature to further rise, softening its outer shell and causing it to glow incandescently in the process; merely approaching the Ajarakan in this state will wear down Hunters and require them to counteract the heat through Cool Drinks.
Behavior
Referred to as the Great Ape by the residents of Azuz, the Ajarakan is primarily active during the Firespring of the Oilwell Basin and will aggressively attack any potential prey or intruders on sight. When engaging a target, the Fanged Beast will beat its tail against the carapace on its back as both a warning and to heat itself up, before roaring and beginning to attack. The Ajarakan has been observed hunting in packs consisting of 2-3 individuals.
Monster Hunter Wilds
The concept behind Ajarakan's design was inspired by the feeling of heat reflecting off of concrete roads and the ground during sunny summer days. Patterns running from the shoulders down to the fingers were added to make the Ajarakan's arms feel longer than they are. The final 3D Model of Ajarakan used in the game was created by the creative studio VOLTA.

Physiology
The Akantor is a gargantuan Flying Wyvern characterized by its massive black armor shells, armored tail, and large tusks; it is considered to be one of the largest species of monster found within volcanic regions. The body of the Akantor is covered in thick black scales that possess a faint glow, they are tough enough that even lava fails to melt them. These scales must be cooled before use due to having spent so much time submerged in lava. The outermost shells are actually dead tissue, formed from its body's surface secreting a calcium-rich fluid, whereupon volcanic minerals are also deposited, increasing the shell's luster and hardness. Excluding the underbelly's tanned scales, this armor covers the entire body, with a collar-like structure at the chin protecting the wyvern's fleshy neck. On the back, the armored shell gives way to the Akantor's distinct dorsal spikes that are aligned in three rows running parallel down the spine; it is believed these spikes originally evolved as a defense against foes larger than it. The armor spines of the Akantor are a mesh-like structure of thick fleshy tendons, an adaptation entirely unique to the Akan family.
The limbs of the Akantor are lined with black shells in hexagonal patterns. While usually a quadraped, the Akantor's hind limbs are strong enough to temporarily support its weight, usually when it is letting loose a roar. With its powerful forelimbs and hard claws, the Akantor is able to smash apart bedrock with ease and shred all that is caught in its charge, even altering the surrounding landscape around itself. The Akantor's tail, which acts to counterbalance its weight, is able to be swung as an effective weapon, its massive barbs powerful enough to gouge the earth and demoralize prey.
A very characteristic feature of the Akantor is the twin pair of tusks jutting out from the wyvern's lower jaw. These enormous fangs can pierce even the thickest of armor and appear to be used in hunting prey, such as the Gravios —a monster the Akantor is capable of lifting and throwing in its mouth. These tusks work in tandem with its forelimbs to allow it to quickly bury into mediums as hard as solid rock. As a result of the Akantor's tusks growing in layers from the center outward, their ringed structure mimics that of a tree; their hard base making them ideal for crafting equipment. In correspondence, the Akantor's tusks are known to inflict severe damage upon any foes caught by its bite once it has been pushed to a state of rage.
Able to weaponize its voice in a similar manner to the Tigrex, the Akantor's roar is amongst its most notable abilities, with it possessing such power that the magma around it erupts. While the Akantor's body contains no elemental organs, it appears to instead contain an internal structure that allows it to generate shockwaves capable of exceeding the speed of sound, allowing it to scream devastating wind-tunnels into form that appear to contain trace amounts of Dragon element. These condensed air blasts allow it to splinter ships from great distances, with one such roar wrecking the massive galleon the Cheeko Sands Chief sailed the seas upon.
Like many monsters, the Akantor grows gems inside of its body over time, sometimes called Conquest Spheres. These gems are said to grant the power of supremacy to those who hold them, and legends speak of an Ancient World-King that once wielded such a stone during his reign.
Classification
While the Akantor is currently classified as a Flying Wyvern, its existence originally sparked debate amongst scholars on what exactly it should be considered to be. Upon its initial discovery, the Akantor was believed to be an Elder Dragon, as it seemed to share no ancestry to any known extant monster species. Its role in various mythologies further encouraged its classification as a dragon rather than a wyvern. However, later discoveries revealed the Akantor's skeletal structure bore key resemblances to Flying Wyverns—such as the Tigrex—alongside certain well researched extinct species: the Sheralos. In particular, the way the fourth claw on each forelimb is positioned appears to indicate it is a vestigial wing bone that has degenerated over time. These insights coincided with the Royal Academy's largest revision of its evolutionary trees at that time, leading to the Akantor being reclassified as a Flying Wyvern. This decision remains a topic of debate to this day.
Behavior
The Akantor is exclusively found in remote areas with volcanic activities, although is known to rarely venture closer to inhabited regions. While uncommon, these migrations are known to be highly destructive, threatening even entire kingdoms. Due to this, the Royal Capital and the Hunter's Guild maintain a standing force in the volcanic region at all times specifically to intercept the Akantor should it begin to move towards civilization. This strategy has thus far demonstrated middling success, as even monitoring the Akantor is a difficult task, with observational teams surveying the area being known to occasionally lose contact and vanish.
The Akantor is a fierce predator that preys upon armored monsters such as the Gravios and Basarios, with its armor leaving it near completely unaffected by their heat rays. When charging, the Akantor calculates the distance between itself and its target, such that if one were to miscalculate the distance, they'd be trampled. Prominently, the Akantor is an unreasonably aggressive wyvern that will not tolerate other life living within its territory, be it human observers, large monsters, or even ships far off the coast; no difference has been found between its passive and offensive states in terms of brutality. Observations of the Akantor remain rare due to the wyvern's speculated extremely small population.
History & Mythology
The Akantor has a long history of influencing mythology and being shrouded in mystery, as even the name "Akantor" itself means "Disaster" in the ancient language of Pokke. Besides this, the Akantor has received many other nicknames in the past, such as Black God and Tyrant of Fire, and is also considered as one half of a duo called the Twin Walls. There are even some legends that describe it as having "a sea of blood" in its maw, and that its tusks are "two crescent moons" with which it "devours the sun". In light of these legends, it is worth noting the appearance of the Akantor often coincides with droughts and heavy rain, with monsters—such as the Anteka —acting cautiously and fleeing the area.
Amongst the many mythos surrounding the Akantor, one legend in particular firmly inserts itself within the mythology of Pokke Village. It tells of an ancestor of the Pokke Village Chief and Treshi who drove the wyvern away to the Volcanic Belt using a massive sword. The same sword, seemingly crafted from the materials of a legendary Elder Dragon, can be found within a nearby cave. However, the Aknator's wrath would not be satiated within the Volcanic Belt, and it would emerge many centuries later and unleash ruin on nearby villages, resulting in numerous casualties. In high alert, the Hunter's Guild would deploy battalions of Hunters possessing a Hunter Rank of 6 and above to direct and slay the massive wyvern. Upon managing to drive the Akantor back to the Battleground, one last Hunter would be tasked by the Guild Master himself to finally slay the Black God. Due to the risk of causing mass panic and confusion in the general populace, hunts targeting the Akantor tend to be done with secrecy as a priority.
In another instance, the Akantor was directly responsible for the creation of the secluded settlement, Cheeko Sands. The Wyverian chief of Cheeko Sands was once a merchant, sailing the seas with her hunter husband and several Felyne crew members. However, their ship would get spotted and splintered apart by a single sonic blast from the Akantor; the Wyverian's husband would be lost to the waves in the chaos and leave the lady and her crew adrift to the wreckage. Surviving the ordeal, the Wyverian lady and her Felyne crew would wash up upon a tropical archipelago off the coast of the Primal Forest and rebuild from the tragedy. By repurposing the washed up wreckage of their ship, the Felynes and the Chief would construct the foundation of what would become Cheeko Sands, and through salvaging the waves of other lost cargo and shipwrecks, an extensive and flourishing community of Felynes was established on the islands, guided by their captain turned Chief. Nonetheless, that traumatising day haunts those who survived the Akantor—particularly the Chief, who lost her dear beloved.

Physiology
The Aknosom is a medium-sized Bird Wyvern identifiable by its strange, umbrella-like appearance, and possesses a coat of scales whose renowned beauty is amplified by their stunning glow. Items crafted from them are desired by royal guards and are so valuable, even the wealthy struggle to get a hold of them. This ivory coat grows darker in color closer to the underside and legs of the monster, culminating in black scales that run along its neck and terminate in a patch of black feathers on its chest. The Aknosom has a short and wide tail covered in bony bumps and which concludes in a gray, hook-like structure, as well as powerful legs ending with red-tinted claws.
The Aknosom has a distinct, comb-like crest atop its head that consists of overlapping, beige, bony plates layered over long, red spines arranged in a fanning pattern. The spines are connected by flexible red webbing that grant the Aknosom the ability to fold the crest in and out like a paper fan. In front of this crest rests a secondary smaller, more bony crest with a frill of hardened feathers lining it, it is marked by red and black patterns resembling an eye, a common element in many ghost stories. Highly durable and often employed for violent physical attacks, the way this flashy crest sways like a flower is hauntingly beautiful. The Aknosom's head is covered with dull, red scales that are accompanied by a pair of yellow, beady eyes. Its coal-black beak is elongated and tough, often being utilized by the Bird Wyvern as a weapon against enemies, primarily in the form of piercing stabs. The beak is known to be used in arts and craft due to the red which lines its edge resembling lipstick, although the truth for this crimson coloration is far more sinister.
The undersides of the Aknosom's large wings are orange with a beige gradient moving closer to the upper edge, while the top sides bear a more striking yellow hue which transitions to a deep-brown towards the edges. The bony fingers of each wing are brownish-orange in color, with the outermost bone on each finger being tipped with a large red claw. Along the upper edge of each wing is a set of white-feathered scales capable of folding in a similar manner to the head crest, their lightness and flexibility aiding the Aknosom in its dance-like movements. These tough, quality feathers are used by the Aknosom to block incoming attacks and slash at targets, although have found additional use in being crafted into umbrellas.
Stored within the Aknosom's body is a flammable venom produced from its diet, which it can ignite and spit out as a means of attack. This generally takes the form of viscous fireballs that bounce around terrain and leave behind long-lasting burning patches on impact.
Behavior
The Aknosom is a solitary and highly territorial monster that will frequently attempt to intimidate intruders, which is achieved by spreading out and flaring both its wings and headcrest to appear larger. Should the intrusion persist, the Aknosom will viciously attack by slamming down on enemies with its beak and headcrest, acrobatically kicking at them with its legs, or by spitting fire. It is frequently seen adopting a stance where it stands on one leg with its wings and crests folded up, bestowing the Aknosom with its distinct parasol-like silhouette.
In addition to using it for intimidation, a male Aknosom will use its crest to attract females during the mating season. Mating pairs of Aknosom will remain with each other for the entirety of the mating season leading up to the point of egg laying, in contrast to their usually solitary habits.
The Aknosom is omnivorous and has been seen feeding on plants, small animals, and insects alike.
Development
The Aknosom was based on the kasa-obake (傘おばけ), an umbrella yōkai that ambulates by hopping on its single leg; Aknosom's introduction in Rise features it folding its wings in and hopping, resembling its inspiration. The design team additionally modeled Aknosom after a crane because the bird resembled an umbrella when standing on one leg.

Physiology
The Alatreon is an imposing Elder Dragon covered in a black coat of armored scales. Its general body structure is similar to many other Elder Dragons, and closely resembles the Kushala Daora's in particular: four walking limbs, two additional limbs in the form of large wings, a horned head, and a long tail. However, the Alatreon displays several unique anatomical features, such as the horns on its head that are extremely large and thick, ending in a multi-pronged mess of edges and tips. Additionally, the tail of the Alatreon is wide and bulky, and notably features a tall sail membrane connected by a row of spikes along its top ridge.
The Elder Dragon's scales are another bizarre physiological characteristic of its: scales will typically point backwards in most monsters, and any rare forward facing scales are called Reverse Scales to denote their special quality. Yet the Alatreon is covered wholly in Reverse Scales, with all of its shell segments and scales pointing forwards. This odd quality gives the scale coat a jagged and aggressive appearance. By themselves, the Alatreon's scales are said to be sharp and evoke the qualities of polished metal. When observed closely, they appear to emit a soft, purple glow, likely a result from the traces of each element contained within them.
The largest and most evident Reverse Scales have grown densely clustered on the Alatreon's chest, forming a structure that connects to the pectoral muscles of the Elder Dragon. This structure can be freely adjusted by the Alatreon to ensure it does not interfere with its mobility, and it is believed to protect the chest from erupting magma and boiling-hot underwater geysers.
The most infamous aspect of the Alatreon is without question its unrivaled command over the elements—notably, the Alatreon is capable of shifting between three states: Fire Active, Ice Active and Dragon Active. Each state greatly affects the color of the glow emanating from the scales and is visibly distinct from the others, lending credence to rumors insistent on its shifting appearance. In the Fire Active state, the Alatreon's body is shrouded in a crimson and orange glow, and the Elder Dragon is capable of spitting oil-like liquid that it then ignites with its powerful flame breath. Meanwhile, the Ice Active state is characterized by an azure glow, in which the Alatreon exhales freezing mists that create solid icicles seemingly out of thin air. Finally, in its Dragon Active state, the Alatreon takes on a deep-purple glow and can violently release the Dragon element as it rampages, as well as make use of each and every element.
Across all elemental states, the Elder Dragon is able to wield lightning by concentrating electricity in its horns and augment its physicality with the Dragon element. However, this specific mechanism has only been seen in the Alatreon encountered in the Secluded Valley of the New World, with the Alatreon fought in the Sacred Land and Ingle Isle appearing to utilize these modes differently. In the Old World, the Alatreon periodically switches active states when transitioning between terrestrial and aerial combat, preferring to use the Fire and Dragon elements whilst grounded, and the Ice and Thunder elements when airborne. Thus far, the Water element has not been seen being utilized by the Elder Dragon in the Old World.
Unraveling the exact mechanism that allows the Alatreon to wield elements in this way has proven challenging. One key observation is that no elemental organs—such as a Flame Sac —have ever been confirmed to exist inside of the Elder Dragon's body. Instead, it appears the Alatreon's body can produce and circulate Dragon energy, and it is believed the active states are set metabolic modes that allow the Alatreon to convert that energy into the various elements. While this conversion appears to be linked to the scales, it has conjointly been suggested that the dragon's massive horns play a vital role in this process. Corroborating the belief is the observation that breaking the horns temporarily disrupts the Alatreon's ability to switch between its active states. Similarly, the Alatreon fought in the Sacred Land is rendered unable to fly once the horns are broken.
Switching between the elements appears to require large amounts of Dragon energy, which is thought to be the reason why the Alatreon seems to only rarely switch between the Fire and Ice Active states directly, often instead first concentrating dragon energy in its Dragon Active state. Once a critical threshold of Dragon energy has been reached, the Elder Dragon can initiate the conversion. As the elements react with each other, an extremely devastating shockwave containing traces of every element is released from the Alatreon's body in a phenomenon titled, Escaton Judgement. While Hunters consider this the Alatreon's ultimate attack, it is possible this is not an attack at all from the Elder Dragon's perspective, merely being a necessary behavior it performs to maintain its elemental metabolism. Be that as it may, the Escaton Judgement is a disastrous event that instantly annihilates all living creatures within range. Curiously, the Escaton Judgement has only been observed in Alatreon found in the New World.
The degree of control the Alatreon wields its elemental properties with is unknown, as while early reports describe the Elder Dragon as elementally unstable, more recent observations and documentation compiled by the Research Commission suggests the Alatreon possesses ample control over its abilities. Further, it is possible the elemental instability refers to the tales about the Elder Dragon's fluctuating appearance stemming from its constant shifting of elemental states, rather than a lack of direct control. Regarding the Alatreon found in the Sacred Land and the Alatreon fought in the Secluded Valley, it is unknown what the differences may mean, or how they came to be.
Behavior
While no natural habitat has ever been confirmed for the Alatreon, its scales and shell armor appear to be adapted to life in extreme conditions, such as the center of volcanoes or the deepest trenches of the ocean. It has only ever been sighted in three places: the Sacred Land, Ingle Isle, and the Secluded Valley. The appearance of the Alatreon in the New World was a shock to the Research Commission, and it has been theorized it appeared in response to the emergence of the Safi'jiiva, another powerful Elder Dragon.
Albeit extremely rare, all encounters with the Alatreon have been characterized by extreme aggression, with the Elder Dragon attacking anything it sees on sight. It is said to be particularly merciless to those who dare touch its scales.
Mythology
The word "Alatreon" means Dawn's Triumph, and is said to symbolize a final victorious stand against a natural disaster. The otherworldly nature and ferocious elemental power of the Alatreon have made it a creature of myth—simply uttering the Elder Dragon's name causes panic, and it is feared as the Symbol of Destruction by some. This reputation was amplified by contradictory accounts of the Alatreon appearing different every time it was encountered, which has since been explained as a consequence of the its shifting elemental states. Hailed as the strongest Elder Dragon and feared even by the gods, there are many who revere and worship the Alatreon as an old god. As well, there are some who believe that its existence best be forgotten, having all documents describing it be burned.
Music
Main article: Alatreon (Music)
"Chime from a Shimmering Bell", also known as "Bonus Track" (Japanese シークレットトラック２, lit. "Secret Track 2") in Monster Hunter 3 Original Soundtrack, is Alatreon's theme. It is notable for using organs and electric guitars, and includes a motif from "To One with Life", Tri 's main theme.
When slain in Iceborne, "Success!!!" plays as the Quest Complete theme, instead of the Iceborne version.
Monster Hunter World: Iceborne
Kaname Fujioka said that portraying Alatreon as an Elder Dragon that could handle multiple elements instead of specialising in a single distinctive attribute made the monster well received by everyone, becoming a monster that people always asked the team to include. Since Yuya Tokuda, the director of World, originally designed Alatreon, they hoped to include it in the base game, but this did not come into fruition due to various circumstances. Thankfully with Iceborne, they decided to make Alatreon return in the expansion.
Like many returning monsters, the team made major changes to Alatreon's design in Iceborne. The spikes on its chest, legs and arms became longer. The wing membranes became much lighter in color, showing off a more irridescent sheen, and the third wing finger was shifted up to be joined with the top two. The tail was made more chunky, and a spike at the end of it was added.
In older games, Alatreon could only switch elements depending on its state, such as Ice element while flying. This time however, they implemented a cycle of switching elements, and added Dragon as a buffer because they thought that if used well, it would prevent the switch between Fire and Ice, allowing for more strategy development. Furthermore, by adding Escaton Judgement, they hoped that players would enjoy the tense situation of facing a forbidden monster. With this monster requiring elemental damage, they thought it was a strong representation of the theme of Iceborne.
Alatreon was originally set to release in May 2020 for Iceborne, but due to the Covid-19 outbreak, the title update including the monster was postponed until July, also affecting the voiceovers for the Italian, French and Spanish language versions of the game.

Large and lithe Leviathans noted for their brush-like tail that oozes a golden liquid capable of turning the ground around them into mud, which they will fling as large waves. Commonly referred to as "Hermits of the Swamp", Almudron usually keep to themselves, however they will aggressively chase off anything that encroaches on their mudflats. They are capable of creating towering structures of mud, as well as large mud balls which they carry around in their tails.

Physiology
The Almudron is a large serpentine Leviathan with beige water-repellent scales that become increasingly brownish-orange towards the underside of the body. Its upper body and the outer edges of the limbs are instead covered by layered dark-brown shelling, formed from overlapping scales having fused with the Almudron's mucus and any surrounding mud over time. Flanked by small reddish ridges, a pair of elevated ridges of the shelling adorns the Almudron's head, forming a structure resembling a hood. Its eyes are narrow and orange, with yellow irises.
The Almudrons head is sports a pair of long orange whiskers, alongside a mud-covered tuft resembling a beard, bestowing the Leviathan its signature elderly appearance. These whiskers are used to better sense prey and enemies by detecting vibrations in the mud, and grow both longer and more sensitive as the monster ages; exceptionally long whiskers are seen as good luck charms. Each limb ends in large hooked claws that excel at digging through dirt; each digit has a reddish pad on the underside to prevent the Almudron from sinking into mud, while the hindlimbs in particular have webbed feet for better mobility in water and mud.
The Almudron's muscular prehensile tail accounts for a significant portion of its body length, its resemblance to a drooping willow is owed to its wide tip and the tuft of reddish hairs growing from the end, which the monster usually covers in mud. The pores on the tail secrete a thick golden mucus that has the unique property of liquefying terrain on contact, giving the Almudron its characteristic ability to create mud, then manipulate it using the brush-like hairs on its tail. It uses this ability to soften the ground for it to swim through, ensnare opponents in muddy terrain, send forth waves of mud, and reshape the surrounding terrain with structures made of dirt and mud. When angered, the mud it creates can take on strange properties due to absorbing larger amounts of the golden mucus, and can become increasingly acidic and harmful. The Almudron's tail is edible and considered to be rich in flavor if prepared properly.
Behavior
Almudron is highly reclusive and seldom ventures out of its usual habitat within mountains, although will do so should external factors encourage it. However, within its habitat, it is highly territorial and will become immediately hostile to intruders and prey alike. In addition to its claws and tails, the Almudron makes liberal use of its mud-based abilities to impair targets, with a favored tactic being to liquefy the ground beneath prey and drag them under the surface to suffocate them. When further angered, it has been observed accumulating a large ball of mud and mucus on its tail to crush prey with, eventually slamming the ball down hard enough to create an explosion when it becomes too massive to wield any longer. Although the Almudron has been observed eating fish and aquatic life, it will also attempt to prey on terrestrial creatures that come too close to the water.
During the mating season, the male Almudron will begin traversing muddy areas in search of a female. Upon finding a potential mate, he will perform a courtship ritual where he and the female wrap around each other and dance in the mud, constantly reshaping the surrounding environment in the process.

Physiology
The Altaroth is a small Neopteron found in a wide variety of regions whose size varies considerably amongst mature individuals. The carapace covering its main body is a lime-green, while its head is tinted yellow with a hood-like shell covering the back of the head. It possesses a proportionately large pair of mandibles used as offensive weaponry against threats, and while durable for their size, these mandibles are surprisingly difficult to carve from the Altaroth. Much like other small Neopterons, its body is exceptionally delicate and very easily destroyed by attacks. As a result, poisons are typically used in order to kill the monster in a way that leaves its body intact.
The abdomen of the Altaroth is transparent and coated in gray plating with a small stinger at its tip, the Neopteron's stomach is housed within. While it is relatively small at rest, the stomach can swell to several times its original size to store a wide variety of materials within. While the lining of its abdomen is thin, it is exceptionally durable, with some claiming that it is fully incapable of being torn.
Behavior
When gathering food, the Altaroth will typically travel in a small group of other Altaroth. It will travel over to its desired food source alongside its brethren and absorb it into its body, causing its abdomen to swell so as to store the absorbed nutrients. The coloration of its abdomen changes depending on what materials it has collected: mushrooms turn it blue, nuts and berries turn it green, and honey turns it orange. If the abdomen is sufficiently damaged, the absorbed materials can be collected from it.
The aggressiveness of the Altaroth is known to vary between individuals and is dependant on the Neopteron's size. An Altaroth that is smaller is typically more passive, fighting back only if antagonized first. By contrast, an Altaroth that is larger is far more territorial and will attack anything that encroaches upon its nest. Despite this aggression, the Altaroth is still known to fall prey to certain large monsters, most notably the Barroth and Volvidon.

Physiology
The Amatsu is a long, serpentine Elder Dragon covered in black shelling that, battered from the winds of countless storms, has hardened into an almost unmatched suit of armor. The shelling covering its chest in particular is capable of reflecting light, which typically shines through the gaps within storm clouds. This illumination is known to instill despair into anyone who basks within it, and is said to glow distinctly bright when the Amatsu grows especially passionate. Lining both its back and arms are several white membranes patterned with red markings; once the Elder Dragon's ire grows, these markings will begin to glow in ominous shades of red and magenta. The Amatsu's body naturally produces air currents, shielding the monster's body in an aura of wind capable of deflecting attacks and shrugging off any attempts to restrain the storm dragon. By using the various membranes across its body, the Amatsu can ride on these air currents with grace befitting a dancer, allowing it to fly without the need for conventional wings. These membranes, when worn as clothing, even allow humans to briefly float in the air. By contrast, its limbs appear relatively small—especially its hind limbs.
Extending from the slender head of the Amatsu are a pair of extremely long whiskers that are almost the length of the Elder Dragon's entire body. It is crowned with a pair of tall, golden horns that appear to lack any form of blemish, which is believed to showcase the Amatsu's pure strength; when the Amatsu is angered, its horns will additionally pulse with golden radiance. The claws on its limbs are incredibly sharp, with the mere sight of them being enough to invoke an intense feeling of fear. Adorning its long and tough tail is a webbed, paddle-like fin at its tip that aids the Amatsu in maneuvering through the storms it creates.
One noteworthy organ of the Amatsu is its Storm Vesicle, located within the Elder Dragon's head and back. This organ stores immense amounts of water inside and places it under large amounts of compression, which the Amatsu will then fire off as highly pressurized globs and jets of water with enough force to rip apart the ground below. It is claimed the Amatsu can produce and fire off enough water to wash away the entire world. In addition to this, by drawing in the air currents naturally produced by its body into a single point, the Amatsu is capable of summoning giant tornadoes capable of sending its opponents flying. The Amatsu's mere presence is enough to alter the weather around it, creating dark clouds and intense gales; the power of these storms outscale even natural disasters. Once the Elder Dragon grows especially irate, the storms it summons grow even more intense and lightning will rain down around the Amatsu. The storms that follow an Amatsu will only ever subside when the Elder Dragon itself is slain.
Behavior
The Amatsu primarily resides within high mountain ranges near the village of Yukumo, given the name of the Sacred Pinnacle. The aloof demeanor of the Amatsu has led some human cultures to worship it as a deity and messenger of the Gods. Notably, the Amatsu is seen as a direct avatar of the storm itself in Yukumo, although has occasionally been spotted outside of this range and near the village of Kamura. Legends state the Amatsu is constantly gazing down upon the world in search of a strong opponent, yet none have been able to match its sheer power. Not even the power of the Wind and Thunder serpents are enough to rival the threat posed by the Amatsu; however, before the cause of the Rampage was discovered to be the doing of the Wind Serpent Ibushi, the Elder Dragon responsible was mistakenly identified as the Amatsu on occasion.
The appearance of the Amatsu near a human settlement typically spells disaster, as the storms that follow the Elder Dragon cause devastating damage to the surrounding area, even laying entire villages or cities to waste. This reputation has caused it to become known as the Looming Calamity. One notable settlement to fall victim to the Amatsu was Tsukito City, which had its entire settlement destroyed and its Queen killed due to the sudden appearance of the Amatsu. It was only thanks to the efforts of Kagero that the Queen's daughter, Lady Yomogi, was able to survive the disaster find refuge in the village of Kamura.

Older Leshen that have grown stronger with time. They sport a lower jaw, a mane of leaves, and much larger antlers as well as possessing greater control over their environment. Physiology
The Ancient Leshen is an unimaginably old Leshen, and as such, closely resembles the younger individual. Notable differences include a visible lower jaw on its skeletal head, a mane of leaves on its shoulders, larger antlers conjoined to a collar of branches, and various fungal growths across the entire body. The Ancient Leshen does not wear any cloth on its torso, and its thin body consists of various cursed bones entangled within a mass of coiling arcane branches. After being sufficiently damaged, the green leaves making up its collar will shift to a vibrant-orange hue.
Behavior
Being a wisened, older Leshen, the Ancient Leshen is a skilled and cunning fighter, displaying more skill in all of the abilities that already makes the regular Leshen dangerous. Its control of fauna is more sophisticated, allowing for larger flocks of minions to be controlled at once. In addition, the Ancient Leshen excels at weaponizing flora and is far more capable of wielding roots and branches.
In its homeworld, the Ancient Leshen is sometimes worshipped by indigenous religions.

Physiology
Like many Brute Wyverns, the Anjanath sports powerful jaws, two muscular hindlegs, a robust tail, and short forelimbs. A distinct cover of thick feathers runs from the shoulders, across the back, and to the tip of the monster's tail. The small forearms of the Anjanath are deceptively powerful, and are used to help the Brute Wyvern with climbing up rocky cliffs. The hand is three fingered—with the middle finger being the largest—and the claws curved. The hindlimbs are developed and muscular, and the feet five toed. Contrasting against the bright-pink color of the body, these dark tufts are actually composed of small feathers, making the Anjanath the only known feathered Brute Wyvern species. The Anjanath's scales are as hard as iron and offer high defense, a sturdiness owed to having been tempered through being constantly exposed to the high body temperature and flames of the Anjanath. Although rare, these scales can combine and overlay, turning into a valuable rolled scale plate. While the Anjanath is well-known for its distinctive pink coloration, its skin lacks any natural pigmentation. The vivid, pink hue is the result of the Anjanath's internal blood flow being made visible through the skin, whose surface is translucent.
The Anjanath's coat is believed to aid in temperature regulation, helping the wyvern maintain the high body temperatures necessary for any sudden activity. Due to the coat's feathers being thick and densely packed, it provides protection against physical attacks and is resistant to flame; the latter property has made it a material occasionally utilized by firefighters, As well, high quality cuts of the fur are treated as an item of luxury due to their stoutness and healthy coat. It is speculated that, when young, the Anjanath sports a far more developed coat of feathers which naturally degenerates as the Brute Wyvern matures. However, there have thus far been no sightings that confirm the theory. The Anjanath tail is covered in highly flexible feathers along its top side and retractable spikes on the underside. These features can be extended at will and when fully flexed, allow the Anjanath to create small gusts of wind by swinging its tail. Able to be used in the crafting of weapons, the tail is considered a delicacy in certain regions. Situated on the hip are a pair of extendable sail membranes full of capillaries that remain retracted against the Anjanath's body until enraged. For this reason, they have been theorized to serve as temperature regulators, potentially compensating for the Anjanath's lack of sweat glands.
In comparison to other Brute Wyverns, the Anjanath's skull is long, slender, and underbitten at the tip of the snout. Having been shaped by the pressure and heat inside the mouth, the fangs are large and tough, and will eventually develop in size and heat resistance. Protruding from the lower jaw's lip are eight large, conical fangs, three pairs of which are long enough to overlap on the upper jaw. The Anjanath's olfactory senses are exceptionally well developed and enable it to track prey through scent alone. The nostrils are large and able to unfurl by raising the nose hood, exposing their sinuses as a horn-like structure on the tip of the snout, further enhancing the Anjanath's sense of smell. Much remains unknown about the bone structure that enables this ability, and the structure of the nosebone is a hotly debated research topic as a result. Should the Anjanath survive countless battles, its nasal bone will grow to an impressively large size.
A defining feature of the Anjanath is its ability to produce and spit fire, achieved through a mechanism in its throat that takes the form of a specialized organ that stores a combustion promoting substance. When enraged, the Anjanath will begin accumulating the substance, indicated by the reg glow taken on by the throat. Simultaneously, the Anjanath produces a flammable mucus through an organ believed to be connected to the nostrils. As it releases the combustive substance alongside the mucus from its nasal cavities, exposure to the air causes the mixture to ignite into flames, allowing the Anjanath to breathe fire. The Anjanath is only capable of this feat when it enters a form considered separate from its enraged state where it has become overcome with rage, called its Fired Up state. Although it is now able to spew fire to clear the area around its head, or in a long and straight line, it may show signs of fatigue afterwards that suggests it requires the full extent of its power to do so. While able to maintain its Fired Up state for some time, the Anjanath will inevitably have to expel all its internal heat at once when it can longer contain it within its body. Alternatively, should the heat contained within the Anjanath's mouth explode from an external force, it will be sent reeling back.
Like many other monster species, the Anjanath may grow a valuable gem inside its body. Formed through the continuous accumulation of impurities and marginal waste materials, the gem of the Anjanath shines brilliantly and is said to be tinged with fire.
Behavior
The Anjanath is extremely aggressive and known to pursue prey for vast distances. In the New World, this has even lead it to sometimes chase targets all the way to the Wildspire Waste from the Ancient Forest. The Anjanath does not seem to differentiate between minor and major threats, and appears to attack with full force regardless of the situation. This high degree of aggression may be linked to the Brute Wyvern's strong food motivation—the Anjanath has been observed eating as often as five Aptonoth a day. Solitary by nature, the Anjanath patrols its vast territory daily, marking its borders with mucus up to thirty times each day. Within its territory, the Anjanath hunts alone and typically chooses the Aptonoth as its preferred prey. Curiously, the Anjanath does not use its flame breath at all whilst hunting, however, it has been noted that it prefers the taste of raw meat over cooked meat.
Due to its aggression, the Anjanath often finds itself embroiled in territorial disputes with other monsters. During such skirmishes, the Anjanath extends its sails, tail feathers, and nostrils, and will focus on inflicting physical damage first. Using its powerful body, the Anjanath brutally assaults its enemy. The Anjanath is a relatively calculated fighter, as its brutish barrage primarily serves to wear down its opponent and buy time for the its Flame Sac to charge up. Once ready, the Anjanath will enter its Fired Up state and use its physique or powerful jaws to drive its target into a corner, upon which it will unleash a barrage of flames. As it does not appear to use its fiery breath whilst hunting, it has been theorized this aggressive behavior is only displayed during fatal battles against invaders or another Anjanath.
When not in combat, the Anjanath has been observed sunbathing in the Ancient Forest. Why it takes part in such an activity remains unclear, nonetheless, the Anjanath is known to seek out the opportunity to sit in the sun at least three times a day. Very little is known about the intraspecific social behavior of the Anjanath, although the sails have been proposed to be a possible means of communication between individuals.
Monster Hunter: World
Anjanath was designed as an early skill-check for new players. Due to its aggression and overall power, it forced players to learn about guarding, blocking and healing. The team also wanted to create a monster that would be dangerous to every player regardless of their chosen weapon type.
Conceptually, Anjanath was part of the three monsters that the Ancient Forest map was designed around, with each representing a different type of movement - the four-legged Great Jagras, the flying Rathian and the two-legged Anjanath. The forest in turn influenced Anjanath's design as well - looking at the dense foliage that would realistically obscure vision, the team thought of a monster that could use scent to track prey and players.
Visually, Anjanath was intended to be the Monster Hunter Team's take on a feathered dinosaur, with an emphasis on how feathers could be used to create an expressive design. Kaname Fujioka likened its plumeage to that of a vulture.

The Violent Saw Wyvern Anorpatis (アノルパティス, Anorupatisu) is a Flying Wyvern introduced in Monster Hunter Frontier G2.

Physiology
The Anteka is a small species of Herbivore whose body is covered primarily in rusty-orange fur that fades to white along its back and around its feet; each of its legs ends with a pair of hooves. It possesses a tall hairless nose, yellow eyes with vertical pupils, and a tuft of white fur around its chin. Easily the most iconic feature of the Anteka is the large pair of twisting antlers extending to the sides of its head before curving upwards into twin points. The base of the antlers additionally feature a pair of upwards-pointing spikes. Unlike the Kelbi, there is pratically no difference between a male and female Anteka.
Behavior
The Anteka primarily resides within snowy mountain ranges, although it has been found in other cold climates. It travels in small groups that are typically larger than just an immediate family. While it is typically seen as a docile monster, it has a habit of raising its horns while it is moving around, often resulting in injury to anyone carelessly standing too close. The antlers primarily function as a method of intraspecies competition, with them being used to signal its presence in a territory to scare off rivals, or—failing that—to fight with other Anteka over territory. The antlers also serve as effective weapons when attempting to fight off larger threats, with the Anteka typically resorting to headbutting its target. Alongside this purpose, a proverb in eastern regions claims the antlers of the Anteka to be beneficial to apothecaries due to their medicinal properties.
Development
Anteka was in part designed and tested by Yasunori Ichinose. It was originally very aggressive and would chase players down relentlessly. The original Antekas were in fact many times more dangerous than even Bullfango and could KO players by hitting them before they had recovered from their previous animation. The team decided that the monster would have to be changed, but before that, they wanted to let Ryozo Tsujimoto test out the unchanged Anteka. He immediately died and requested that the monster be made less menacing, much to the bemusement of the rest of the team.

Physiology
The Apceros is a sturdy quadrupedal Herbivore that inhabits arid environments; its limbs support a bulky body, from which protrudes a small head and a long tail ending in a large spiked club. This tail acts as its primary form of defense, being capable of injuring larger wyverns. Much of the body is covered by smaller tan scales and large bronze-colored scutes, whereas the underside's soft skin is a much paler tone comparatively. Its scales and skin are adapted to retain water in its dry habitat. Although the Apceros exclusively walks using all four of its legs, it is capable of rearing up on its hind legs for short periods of time.
The Apceros' barrel-shaped torso is protected from attacks by its most distinctive feature: a hefty, turtle-like shell. This thick shell covers the back of the Herbivore and terminates at the base of the tail, with five rows of especially thick scutes protecting the dorsal surface of the shell. From end to end, the carapace remains mostly flat, although slightly upturns over the shoulders. From side to side, it curves down towards the monster's flanks, with the back edge of the shell being lined with four large spikes, two protecting each back leg. The head of the Apceros is wide, wedge-shaped, and supports a short rounded beak. The scalp is protected by a thick headplate that forms a small frill behind the head, and the small eyes have yellow irises and slit pupils; two large horns behind the eyes point out to the side.
The Apceros is often hunted for the delectable meat hidden beneath its thick, armored hide, as well as for a particular organ of its. The meat is usually roasted in large portions for Hunters with large appetites. Due to a recently made discovery, it has been revealed that—if prepared correctly—the Apceros' liver grants a variety of beneficial effects that may be used for medicinal purposes.
Behavior
In both the Old World and New World, the Apceros is found in small groups that inhabit hot climates, such as deserts and volcanoes, feeding on the hardy plants and vegetation able to endure the harsh conditions. However, it itself is a common food item for large monsters found in the same environments, such as the Glavenus. Thus, in the New World, the Apceros will enter a defensive formation alongside other members of its herd in an attempt to defend against nearby large monsters, unlike most other Herbivores. By positioning itself alongside two others, angling its shell outward, and lifting its tail high in the air, the Apceros is able to construct a three-sided, stalwart, circular barrier capable of withstanding assault from larger threats. In one instance, a member of the Research Commission was able to use the huddled Apceros' formation to survive and escape the claws of a large monster by entering their defensive ring. Should one of the three Apceros be killed however, the formation will fall to ruin and the remaining two will flee to safety.
The behavior of the Apceros in the New World differs greatly in comparison to that of individuals in the Old World. In addition to a never before seen protective formation, the New World's Apceros can be seen migrating through the Wildspire Waste's rocky landscape alongside two others, never feeding in a single place for too long and making regular trips to the swampy marsh for a drink: the most dangerous place for the Apceros due to the myriad of predators also visiting it to quench themselves. Further, it possesses a much calmer disposition towards hunters, although will still fiercely retaliate if provoked. Should it grow agitated, it will express its anger by rearing up on its hind legs, raising its spiked club, or swinging its head. In comparison, in the Old World, the abundance of predators and harsh environment has made the Apceros highly territorial. It has grown to be innately aggressive towards hunters due to their frequent nest raiding, attempting to either headbutt or lash at them should they draw too near, and even going so far as to chase them out of the area.
In rocky alcoves, far from any feeding sites, the Apceros will lay its protein-rich eggs and protect them from danger without rest, chasing off and pursuing any thieving creature it catches skulking about. An unfortunately common occurrence for the Herbivore due to the nutritious properties of its eggs drawing the attention of many; nest raiders, such as the Kulu-Ya-Ku, pay frequent visits in search of their golden treasure. Whereas in the eyes of the Guild, the eggs are a valuable commodity, and for both humans and Felynes, the eggs are a common cooking ingredient. A Young Apceros grows quickly to defend itself from predators, although the adult Apceros will defend the young with the same fervor as protecting any eggs.

The Apex Arzuros is an Arzuros that has been altered by the struggle of overcoming the violent storms of the Wind Serpent Ibushi, emerging in a vastly empowered form.
