Physiology
Originally documented as long having been extinct, the Arkveld is a large muscular Flying Wyvern covered in tough gray scales, with snow-white fur on its chest, wing membranes, and tail. The scales are noted to be extremely hard while also having fairly brittle edges. The fur meanwhile consists of strong intertwining strands that create a resistant mesh, further increasing the wyvern's defense. It has five claws per limb, with its forelimbs' fourth and fifth digits seemingly developed into chains, and zygodactyl hindlimbs, much like the Seregios. The Arkveld additionally has two curved horns resembling tusks whose mere sight despirit any seeking to oppose it, as well as an upward pointed, cone-shaped nose. The wyvern's back is well-armored as it is covered with white overlapping shells that function much like plate armor. A large bump protrudes from the top of its back plates, which has been noted to occasionally attract lightning strikes during the Sandtide in the Windward Plains. Its tail is rather flat, flexible, and covered with rocky plates, with incredibly thick muscles that allow it to freely extend and bend at will.
The Arkveld's most unique aspects are the chain-like structures extending from the lower segment of its front limbs, referred to as Chainblades. Each Chainblade is comprised of numerous pointed rocky carapaces, called Calloushells, that grow from a branching central mass of highly flexible muscles and sinew, seemingly formed from extensions of the fourth and fifth digit of its claws fastened together. The shells are normally tightly compacted and layered, forming a curved blade-like structure the Arkveld can use to slash opponents, however, they may be separated. Upon being unfolded, the Chainblades transform into a highly flexible, whip-like tendril the Arkveld can manipulate freely for combat and mobility, such as to strike or grapple targets from afar, or pull itself across terrain. Despite their thin appearance and incredible dexterity, the Chainblades carry an immense amount of strength, being able to individually grapple, restrain, and even lift monsters larger in size than the Arkveld itself, or deliver brutal strikes capable of killing a monster as large as the Doshaguma in a single blow.
The Calloushells additionally house unique organs that can absorb elemental energy from both the environment and other monsters, which the Arkveld can convert into Dragon elemental energy for its own use with extraordinary conversion speed and efficiency. The sinews within the Chainblades are often seen pulsing with pale purple light when absorbing or emitting energy. When the Arkveld is sufficiently enraged and powered up, it can enter an Unleashed State, where the Arkveld separates the two digits of its Chainblades and splits each one for a total of four tendrils. It then charges the Chainblades with Dragon energy, allowing them to create explosive discharges when striking enemies or terrain. However, the elemental capacity of these organs can be overloaded, causing harm to the wyvern and forcing it to retract the Chainblades as it recovers. The Arkveld additionally may grow a mysterious gem inside its body that emits a pulsating pale light which appears to absorb life.
Although it can eat normally, the Arkveld is able to feed by directly absorbing energy from the environment or its prey. This process has the additional mechanism of absorbing certain properties from its prey, and is the factor that is speculated to have altered the behavior and physiology of the Guardian Arkveld. This behavioral alteration based on elemental energy can also have unintended consequences, as was the case when the Dragontorch became diseased with the Frenzy and resulted in infected Wylk poisoning the food chain, becoming bioconcentrated in the apex predators of each region that were subsequently fed on by the Arkveld. This infected energy had maladaptive effects on the Arkveld's physiology: while not directly receiving the Frenzy infection, the Arkveld still experienced intense destructive impulses. This consequently lead to it attempting to kill every monster it came across with no regard for predation, forcing the Hunter to slay it.
In an unusual circumstance, an Arch-Tempered specimen was observed manifesting powers similar to those of a Guardian monster, showcasing the ability to discharge Wylk as well as rapidly regenerate from wounds, boasting a regeneration speed greater than that of even a true Guardian. While channeling these powers, the Arkveld displayed a pattern of glowing white veins all over its body, identical to those of the Guardian Arkveld. The precise reason and mechanism behind this development is unknown.
The Arkveld appears to lay eggs with white flaky shells and lilac inner membranes. The eggs' membrane absorb ambient elemental energy to nourish the growing Arkveld, causing the shell to gradually grow more brittle until the newborn Arkveld can break it and hatch. The initial generation of the Arkveld born from the Guardian Arkveld emerged through parthenogenesis, with the Construct laying eggs without the need for fertilization. However, it is unknown if the resulting generation inherited this ability or not, nor if it was a trait native to the original species.
Behavior
The Arkveld is highly nomadic in nature and can be found in any environment; it sleeps at no fixed spots in a given locale, often invading the nests of other monsters to sleep in. It is highly aggressive towards both Hunters and monsters alike, often attacking on sight and attempting to feed on the latter should they wield elemental energy. An often used tactic of the Arkveld is to use its chains to first knock other monsters prone with a heavy blow, then constrict and drain them with its Chainblades. Its invasive and voracious tendencies often lead to conflict with other monsters, particularly as it tends to gravitate towards powerful targets with large amounts of elemental energy to drain. Due to its sheer power and energy absorption, as well as the dexterity with which it uses its Chainblades, the Arkveld is often able to violently depose any local apex predators and become a dominant force in any ecosystem it chooses to live in. In the Ruins of Wyveria, it can be observed breaking open Guardian cocoons and devouring the dormant Guardians within.
The Arkveld often tends to its Chainblades and can be seen grooming them with its mouth or claws. A mysterious behavior also seen in the Arkveld is it rubbing and swirling its chains against the ground in an arc-like pattern as the sinews glow, leaving dark marks and scales on the ground. The Arkveld can also occasionally be observed preening itself, leaving sharp fragments on the ground.
History
For a long time, the Arkveld had been documented as an Extinct Species by the Hunter's Guild. However, this was changed upon the discovery of Nata during an expedition along the border of the Forbidden Lands, with the boy recalling how his village was laid to waste by a monster called the White Wraith. Following an expedition, the White Wraith was eventually identified to be the Guardian Arkveld by the people of Sild, and although the Guardian was ultimately slain, it managed to lay one or more eggs before its death that would birth a new generation of the species. The Guild continues to closely monitor the species to watch for any drastic effects its re-introduction into the ecosystem may pose.
A species that highly resembles the Arkveld is noted to exist in ancient records. However, this ancient species is not known to possess either elemental absorption or conversion abilities.

Physiology
Bearing the moniker of Blue Bear Beast due to its coloration, the Arzuros is a relatively small, ursine-like Fanged Beast whose lower half is covered in bluish-green fur and patterned with several cream spots over its rear; this fur is both short and taut. The dorsal side of its upper body is covered in quality, dark-blue shells that are thick enough to protect the Arzuros from the fangs of most ordinary monsters it shares its environment with. Additionally, this carapace is highly flexible, aiding the Arzuros' movement as well as making the material easy for blacksmiths to forge with. The sides of the Arzuros' body are lined with a row of blonde fur, with additional tufts present on both its head and chest; unlike the fur present on the rest of the body, it is significantly softer. The fur covering the Arzuros' body helps to protect it from the harsh climates it inhabits, however, in stark contrast to the rest of the body, the underside of the Arzuros' torso is almost entirely hairless.
The most recognisable feature of the Arzuros are the brown, armored braces present on its forelimbs that are lined with several sharp thorns. These braces are the beast's primary weapon against threats, with the spikes being designed to inflict deep wounds onto its targets. They are extremely hard, enough to break most weapons. This is thought to be due to the hardened honey that covers them. Each brace ends in four sharp, orange claws, as well as an opposable thumb that allows the Arzuros to grab and hold its food as it eats. In order to aid it in tracking down food, the Arzuros possesses both a keen sense of hearing and an amazing sense of smell, although, both of these traits result in loud noises and strong odors causing the beast to recoil. The Arzuros has red eyes and a disproportionately long tongue, which it typically lets hang outside of its mouth.
Behavior
The Arzuros is commonly sighted in the mountains surrounding the villages of both Yukumo and Kamura, with it preferring to inhabit hot and humid mountainous forests. It is an omnivore famed for its gluttonous appetite, being almost always found eating something. The Arzuros is known to hunt fish and will utilize the armored braces on its forearms to swipe them out of the water; as a result, undigested fish are frequently found in its stomach. However, the Arzuros' favorite food is Honey, which it is famed to steal off Hunters before pausing to devour it on the spot, completely oblivious to any potential threat surrounding it.
Despite its broad diet, the Arzuros' body has little resistance to poisons not part of its typical sources of food. Thus, once the Arzuros has found itself a designated feeding ground, it will map out the locations of any beehives in the region, purposely travelling to and feeding from multiple hives to prevent itself from depleting its entire supply of honey. Should another creature intrude upon its feeding territory, the Arzuros will attempt anything it can to eliminate the threat. When a threat is spotted, the Arzuros will rear up on its hindlegs, spread its forelimbs wide, and growl in an attempt to intimidate the potential threat.
The fur and shell of the Arzuros are commonly utilized by the people of Yukumo, particularly hunters. They are viewed as a symbol of regional pride, with the clothing typically being referred to as the "Yukumo Style," even when fashioned in other villages, such as Kamura. The combination of both soft and tough fur found on the Arzuros' body makes clothing made from it perfect wear for hunters.
Super Biology Information
The Super Biology Book Series collects the thoughts and theories of real scientists that were asked to speak about monsters from the Monster Hunter series. Thus, they are inherently speculative and should be seen as such.
Zoological Author Yuumin Mori compares the Arzuros to real bears and asserts that if they were to exhibit similar breeding behaviors, the Arzuros species would consist of solitary males and females that only meet up during the breeding season. Offspring would then be raised only by the mother and gain independence upon reaching sexual maturity. Mori notes however that there are various factors that might contradict this: Arzuros appear to live in mild, warm environments that see little seasonal variation, which in turn would make a dedicated breeding season unnecessary. Additionally, the behavior of Arzuros does not match real bears perfectly, as they seem to actively encroach on humans, while real bears are generally timid. It is also notable that Arzuros are never seen with their young, which leads Mori to wonder if maybe this species raises its young entirely within hidden burrows. A similar behavior is seen in Pandas and Polar Bears, and Mori notes that the large claws of the Arzuros would allow females to dig impressive burrows with ease.
In another comparison to bears, Mori states that the stable habitat of the Arzuros might eliminate the need for hibernation. If its environment continuously provides them with food, then it is likely that the Arzuros does not hibernate. But even if its habitats experience seasons of scarcity, that may still allow the Arzuros to avoid hibernation as long as its staple food source remains accessible.
On the matter of the Arzuros’ anatomy, Mori takes a closer look at the blue fur. Since the Arzuros depends on honey, it is likely that this monster evolved alongside the species of bees that produce it. Insects are known to be able to see ultraviolet light, allowing them to perceive visual indicators that are invisible to humans. Mori thus theorizes that the blue fur of an Arzuros might actually have bee-repellent patterns on it that are only visible by insectoid eyes. These patterns would dissuade the bees from attacking the beast, allowing for easy, stress-free honey meals. The shells of the Arzuros may also have evolved to maximize feeding success; Mori notes that the large, spiked carapaces on the monster’s forearms do not offer all that much defense against physical attacks - the Arzuros’ habit of standing upright puts its arms into a defensively awkward position. Instead, Mori proposes that this species was likely much smaller in the past, small enough for bee swarms to pose a more significant threat. As the arms of this smaller ancestor would have been the most exposed to the bees while the monster reaches into the hive, it is thus possible that the arm shells developed as a defense against stings. The well-developed armor shells of the modern Arzuros would thus be remnants of this small ancestor.

Physiology
The Ash Kecha Wacha is a Subspecies of the Kecha Wacha adorned in a primarily ashy-white fur coat covering its limbs, back, and tail—granting it the nickname of White Monkey Fox. Its back is mottled by darker spots, with the end of its tail and each limb being colored a dark-black; these dark spots only further elevate the fur's beauty. By contrast, the torso is coated in pale, yellowed fur. Its gliding membrane is patterned in deep, yellow and orange hues reminiscent of a pair of eyeballs, with similar coloration additionally being found within the interior of the Fanged Beast's three-spiked ears. While the skin covering its face and trunk is a deep red, its actual eyes are a bright blue.
Like its relative, the Ash Kecha Wacha possesses three long and sharp claws on each of its hands that are used for effortless arboreal traversal and as effective weapons in combat. The arms' rigid bones contribute to this strength, making an excellent frame for smiths to form gear from in spite of their rarity. Despite preferring to roam along the ground,, the strong, prehensile tail of the Ash Kecha Wacha easily suspends its body using the hidden hooked claw at its tip, acting as a third complimentary limb for arboreal traversal alongside its arms.
Contrasting the Kecha Wacha, this Subspecies instead possesses a Flame Sac that grants it the ability to spit out a flammable liquid produced internally, often done to either intimidate or attack opponents. This liquid is formed from the insects and nuts the Fanged Beast ingests fermenting and mixing within the Flame Sac to form its flammable liquid that ignites upon exposure to air, allowing it to fire off volleys of fireballs from its trunk.
The outsides of the Ash Kecha Wacha's ears are colored black and patterned by orange and yellow markings resembling a cycloptic eye. Notably, while still flexible and sensitive to sound, these ears are significantly more durable compared to the standard species'. As a result, when folded over the face, they serve to block out loud noises and blinding flashes of light whilst additionally acting as an effective shield, with their strength being enough that most blades are incapable of leaving a mark upon them. Dependant on the age and inhabited environment, the patterns decorating the ears vary in appearance across individuals.
Behavior
Unlike the Kecha Wacha, the Ash Kecha Wacha prefers to roam the ground, granting it a wider range of movement and allowing it to inhabit a wider range of habitats. The Ash Kecha Wacha is quick to fold its ears over its face when confronted, doing so even when it is yet to have become angered. As a result, it is recommended for Hunters to instead attack the hindlegs and tail. In addition to using its ear patterns as an intimidation display towards perceived threats, they are utilized during courtship rituals.

Physiology
Classified as a Subspecies of the Lao-Shan Lung, the Ashen Lao-Shan Lung has earned the title of Rock Mountain Dragon due to the differing coloration of its ash-gray shell. Sharing the bodily features and general physiology of its basal counterpart, the Ashen Lao-Shan Lung is peculiar for its lack of elemental organs and wings, and as is the case with the standard Lao-Shan Lung, this Subspecies must grow its carapace over many years by melding various minerals, sediments, and volcanic ash onto its surface by way of its body's intense heat. This process appears to have given the Ashen Lao-Shan Lung its dull, gray-toned appearance, as striking visual contrasts between individuals has been noted to occur in the Lao-Shan Lung dependant on what minerals meld with the thick shell. Much like its regular counterpart, the Ashen Lao-Shan Lung slowly moves through settlements unimpeded, crushing villages and towns alike underfoot and using its incredible bulk and horn to smash through any unlikely obstacles. When faced with a fortress wall, the Elder Dragon will shift into a bipedal stance to attempt to smash through, resting back on its large tail.
Behavior
The Ashen Lao-Shan Lung interacts with the world around it in much the same way as its standard counterpart does, periodically migrating for reasons currently unknown through routes that occasionally intersect with settlements. It is theorized that the Elder Dragon spends much of its time in dormancy due to the extremely long process of forming its shell, awakening only under certain conditions. The Hunter's Guild handles cases regarding the Ashen Lao-Shan Lung by maintaining defensive pushes at fortresses that have been established along the Elder Dragon's routes, aiming to repel and redirect it into safer routes. In order to achieve this goal, various artillery and siege weaponry is used in attempt to dissuade or slay the Elder Dragon, notably in the form of cannons and Dragonators. Although destructive in its travels, the Ashen Lao-Shan Lung is rather peaceful and will rarely ever intend to attack other living beings, even paying little mind whilst being bombarded by heavy artillery on its march towards its destination. It will only ever tend to attack the barricades and walls that prove too inconvenient for the Elder Dragon to simply step over, in which case it will employ its strength and bulk to get past the momentary obstacle.

Physiology
Like most other monsters of its class, the Astalos is a large Flying Wyvern that sports four limbs, with the front pair having been modified into a large pair of wings. Its back is protected by a black, heavily-segmented, armored shell covered in rows of hard and sharp spikes, causing serious injury in anyone who touches it carelessly. By contrast, its underbelly is lined with lime-green scales capable of reflecting sunlight, giving them an almost rainbow-like glint. While both its shelling and scaling appear tough, they are both actually quite flexible. The Astalos' slender, yet strong body and its thin wings make it highly suited for flight, allowing it to even rival the aerial maneuverability seen within the Rathalos.
The most striking trait of the Astalos is its sophisticated electrical generation mechanism, which is what granted it the nickname of Electric Wyvern. Its electricity is generated through the use of several piezoelectric organs formed from modified muscles, which the Astalos can vibrate rapidly to build up an electrical charge. This produced charge is then stored within three electricity-storing organs located throughout its body, and once an organ becomes fully-charged, that part in-question takes on a bright green glow. When all of them become filled with electricity, the wyvern enters a state of high excitability, becoming even more vicious in the process, with its produced electricity stimulating its muscles and enabling them to exert even greater forces than before. Once the charge kept within these parts exceeds the capacity its body can hold, it is forcibly discharged in a powerful explosion, returning the Astalos' body parts to normal. A special carapace, known as an Electroscale, grows over the piezoelectric organs of the Astalos in order protect them. These scales aid in the generation of electricity through their highly conductive nature, even after being separated from the body. It is for these reasons that these Electroscales are the first materials researchers jump towards when reports of an Astalos occur.
While several parts of its body are capable of generating electricity, the mechanism behind each is different. One of these organs is located within the prominent crest atop its head, which consists of three individual spines connected by a thin lime membrane constituting of its muscle tissue, allowing the different sections of its crest to move independently. By opening and closing them rapidly it is capable of generating an electrical charge, which gets stored within the first of its storage organs located beneath the wyvern's carapace. While already a powerful weapon when swung around, the crest can form into a blade-like shape when electrically charged, allowing for even more merciless blows. The crest's electrical generation is aided by an extremely high-quality and highly conductive material found within it, allowing it to freely-manipulate its own high voltage currents.
Another of the Astalos' defining features defining features is its wings, which consist of a thin, yet beautiful membrane reminiscent of those possessed by many Neopterons. Despite this, the wings are one of its most powerful weapons. Unlike most other Flying Wyverns, the Astalos' wings sport several talons that grow downwards, making it much easier to scrape its wings across the ground, and allowing them to cut through prey with a single swipe. While these talons are naturally black, they will turn a vibrant green when exposed to electricity. Much like its crest, the Astalos possesses piezoelectric organs inside its wing membranes that generate electricity through the vibrations that occur during its attacks, with the electricity being stored within the second of its storage organs—located at the base of its wingtalons. Once fully charged, streaks of electricity begin appearing along the membrane as the wing takes on an iridescent, rainbow-like beauty. Even when removed from its body, these membranes still remain faintly charged and can cause small electric shocks in any who touch them. The Astalos is known to take meticulous care of its talons, rubbing them against the ground in order to keep them well polished.
The last of the Astalos' piezoelectric organs is located within the bifurcated, scissor-shaped blade at the tip of its tail. Electricity is generated in the tail by rubbing the two halves of its scissor-blade together, and while it can be stored inside of the third and final storage organ that is also located inside of the tail's tip, it can alternatively be released in the form of an electrical beam. Additionally, the tail tip of the Astalos accumulates a paralyzing toxin inside itself that can be administered through the many jagged spines inside the scissor-blade.
Electric gemstones that pulse with intense energy have been found inside the body of the Astalos.
Behavior
The Astalos is believed to have a small overall population, with adult individuals being considered quite rare. It is primarily found in forested areas that feature open skies and dense vegetation, allowing for its verdant coloration to provide camouflage, and that provide a degree of warmth and humidity, which makes them ideal for generating static electricity. For this reason, the Astalos instinctively avoids cold regions with low humidity. The Astalos' preferred areas are also those favored by the Rath family, resulting in the two species frequently fighting over both food and territory.
Infamous for its temper, the Astalos is a relentlessly aggressive monster that tolerates absolutely no intrusions into its large territory, violently clashing with any creature it considers unwelcome. Compared to this ferocious temperament however, the actual hunting strategy of the Astalos is much less active. After accumulating a sufficient charge, the Astalos will seek out a suitable spot in its territory and begin releasing the charge as a steady and powerful current into the surrounding air. This creates a death zone that instantly electrocutes any smaller monster that steps into it. The Astalos can then gorge itself on whatever creature has come too close to it and perished, which often times includes the Vespoid and Velociprey. While it is carnivorous, unlike most other Flying Wyverns, the Astalos uses its wingarms as tools whilst feeding, using the spikes coating their underside to tear its prey apart, spraying large scraps of meat around itself as it feeds. After feeding, it will proceed to clean its talons by pecking at them with its mouth.
While nothing is known about the Astalos' courtship or mating behavior, it has been observed the wyvern lays large clutches of eggs, of which only a handful of hatchlings survive into adulthood. This is due to the harsh upbringing the Astalos must endure: a parent will only guard the eggs until the first one hatches, after which they will immediately abandon the clutch. Thus, the juvenile Astalos must fend for itself from offset, with its diet primarily consisting on Hornetaurs during the early years. However, should the juvenile Astalos notice that it has grown notably faster and larger than one of its peers, it will take the opportunity and readily engage in cannibalism. As the clutch battles for survival, each juvenile aims to be the first to learn and master its electric generation ability, as this appears to be the determining factor in which individuals are able to live into their adult years.

Physiology
The Aurora Somnacanth is a Subspecies of the Somnacanth differentiated by its pale-gray scales, shimmering bluish-indigo fins, and command over ice. Its scales are wrapped in cold air and rime, producing snowy dust when wind blows over them, while its cortex has grown much harder as a result of being frozen to the core. Its claws have become more silver and metallic, with the frontmost being covered in sharp icy blades to better extract frozen prey. The Aurora Somnacanth's eyes are yellow with red irises, while the area around them—alongside the inside of its mouth—glow with a ghastly pale light. The largest fin on its head is lined with frozen barbs and a layer of frost that forms a face-concealing veil, and will begin glowing a vibrant blue when the monster is enraged.
Instead of the sleeping powder produced by the nominate species, the Aurora Somnacanth utilizes a Cryo Sac to produce and expel supercooled air from its gills and mouth. In addition to serving as a method of attack by freezing enemies and creating explosions of ice, the Aurora Somnacanth instantly freezes its surroundings and nimbly maneuvers using the slippery ground. The ice crystals it scatters around itself shimmer when exposed to light, particularly from its head crest, giving the Subspecies its namesake aurora-like sheen when angered.
Behavior
Unlike the nominate species, the Aurora Somnacanth is primarily terrestrial and seldom ventures into water. It shares the territorial disposition of the standard variety, fiercely attacking any who venture into its turf. The Aurora Somnacanth is more violent than its regular counterpart, immediately resorting to direct attacks and physical blows, rather than disabling the target and attacking them when they are weakened. However, unlike the normal Somnacanth, the Aurora Somnacanth has not been observed hunting for oysters or using them in combat.

Physiology
The Azure Rathalos largely resembles the common Rathalos, although displays a few noteworthy differences. The most glaring is the coloration: the Azure Rathalos is covered in a blue shell and sports green wing membranes, the shade of which can vary drastically between regional populations. Why and how this coloration came to be is still debated, however, one hypothesis that has been brought forth suggests it may be related to camouflage. The blue shell of the Azure Rathalos would make it blend into the skies when viewed from below, and the green membranes may help it not stick out when grounded in a forest. However, the Azure Rathalos found in the New World sports a significantly more muted variation of this green coloration.
Alongside its altered color, the Azure Rathalos' carapace has been noted to be much tougher than the red shelling of the common Rathalos, especially around the wings. This effectively adamantine armor offers vastly superior protection and is additionally very heat resistant, a trait believed to enable the Azure Rathalos' extended presence in volcanic regions. The wings of the Azure Rathalos are quite muscular and allow the Subspecies to rule over the skies even better than his crimson counterpart. The Azure Rathalso is an excellent flier, and the added armor on the wingarms and sturdier wing membranes reduce the risk of injury to the wings.
Much like the Rathalos, the Azure Rathalos possesses both venom glands and Flame Sacs, which are used for venomous talon swipes and flaming breath attacks. The flame breath of the Azure Rathalos is noted to be more variable in strength, with its potency increasing as the wyvern becomes angrier. This seems to be linked to an expansion of the lungs, resulting in increasingly violent air flow and temperature within the flame organ.
The Azure Rathalos' increased physical strength and airborne agility appears to come at a cost, as the Subspecies has been observed slumping to the ground in exhaustion after prolonged battle, implying reduced endurance and stamina compared to the common species.
How and why the Azure Rathalos evolved is generally unknown, although two theories have been posited for its presence in the New World. The first suggests that a number of standard Rathalos settled in the Elder's Recess and were altered by the region's energy in the process, while another popular hypothesis explains the Subspecies' presence being due to having migrated from the Old World.
Behavior
The Azure Rathalos is consistently noted to be much more aggressive and irritable than the common Rathalos. Further, he has been observed dominating and harassing the common species and is believed to have an instinctual aggression towards the standard Rathalos. When engaging an enemy, the Azure Rathalos attempts to overwhelm them with long combos of airborne attacks.
The Azure Rathalos pairs up with the Pink Rathian. In the New World, the Azure Rathalos spend most of the year in the Elder's Recess and move down south to meet the Pink Rathian to reproduce during the mating season. This migration is believed to be due to the sweltering heat and extreme competition in the Elder's Recess making it a poor nesting ground, as it would pose a substantial risk to any hatchlings.

Physiology
The Baggi is a small Bird Wyvern covered primarily in blue scales, sporting tan scales along its underside and black scaling on both its limbs and the tip of its tail. Noted to be slightly tougher than those of its close relative, the Jaggi, these scales aid the wyvern in camouflaging into snowy environments, with the hide beneath the scaling being especially well-adapted for life within harsh climates. Additionally, it possesses an array of small black horns at the front of its head, with small tufts of black feathering being present atop its head and along its back. The Baggi's most noteworthy feature is the Sleep Sac present in its body, capable of spitting out a tranquilizing fluid that can knock a grown man unconscious in seconds. The Baggi is well-regarded for its high degree of intelligence.
Behavior
Much like most other Dog Wyverns, the Baggi is a social monster lead by an alpha, the Great Baggi, who is the largest and strongest member of the pack. The Baggi works alongside its leader in order to ambush prey, such as the Popo. In order to do so, the Great Baggi will typically command its subordinates to lure the target into narrow passageways, making the prey easy to pick off. This tactic is one of the reasons why the Baggi is considered to be highly intelligent. It is additionally known to respond to calls for aid from its alpha, immediately rushing to its side to aid it. The Baggi is typically sent out to cover a wide area in order to hunt for prey, although this leaves it sensitive to invading monsters who seek to take over its territory. In order to fight off intruders, the Baggi will utilize sheer numbers to overwhelm the target, refusing to back down even when its opponent is several times larger than it.

Physiology
The Balahara is a serpentine, worm-like Leviathan with a slender beige body covered in hard black scales and padded shells, enhanced in hardness through the absorption of Fulgurite present in its natural habitat. Particularly hard quality shelling can be found covering the Balahara should it be wrapped in pure Fulgurite. The Balahara's scales demonstrate variable quality, with some having their usefulness in craftsmanship limited by the erosion caused by the monster's constant digging, While other scales of greater quality are thick and durable enough to carve through stone without sustaining damage. The Balahara has four stubby limbs and a drill-like tail it uses to propel itself through earth with great force, allowing it to quickly dig around. This tail also doubles as a weapon in combat: dexterous in nature, the Balahara excels in skewering targets and keeping opponents at bay with a variety of jabbing and sweeping motions. In addition to its offensive functionality, the tail stores large amounts of fat and nutrients, and contains enough energy to continue moving for some time when severed. Due to this, the Balahara may purposely shed its tail as a distraction when in mortal peril.
Its pointed skull is covered in larger shells and built to withstand violent dives into sand, while its mouth has a unique tripartite structure that folds outwards when opening its jaws. The mouth's edges are lined by numerous sharp teeth and rows of blue eye-like sensory organs lining the edges. These "eyes" are capable of normal sight, although it often relies on its hearing while submerged. The insides of its throat have a luminescent bluish-teal glow provided by the bacteria in its secreted mucus, which is believed to aid visibility during sandstorms or whilst tunneling. This mucus is also expelled from the Balahara's mouth as a means to attack, resembling a dark green fluid when not glowing.
Using its flexible skeleton and powerful tail, the Balahara is able to maneuver around uneven terrain and swiftly tunnel through sand and bedrock by spinning its entire body like a drill, protected by its hard scales and skull. As well, it is able to loosen the sand it digs through to create pits of quicksand that trap prey and suck them below the surface. When digging, the Balahara expels sand through its gills as it displaces the ground beneath it, which it then violently puffs from the gill-like flaps on its neck when angered. The Balahara takes ore into its body through unknown means and refines it over the course of many years into a lustrous Black Pearl, a jewel with bewitching beauty.
Behavior
Dwelling in arid desert habitats, such as the Windward Plains, the Balahara is an ambush predator who lures its prey into quicksand traps and sucks them into its lair to be devoured, although it has also been seen actively pursuing prey as well. They have been observed hunting both by themselves and in larger packs, demonstrating considerably higher aggression in these hordes. Referred to as the Sand Leviathan by the residents of the Windsong Village, this swarming behavior often elicits the need for an escort to accompany villagers attempting to travel across the sands, lest they risk being overwhelmed by sheer numbers.

Physiology
This Subspecies shares many physiological features with the common Gigginox, although is distinguished by certain unique characteristics. The Baleful Gigginox maintains the same posture and gait of its related species and possesses a similar degree of agility, allowing it to cling to walls and ceilings. The most immediately noticeable difference between the two is the Subspecies' highly saturated, deep-yellow hide that colors its topside, noted to possess a high-end texture and elasticity. Meanwhile, its underside is dressed in purple skin lightly mottled with shades of blue and yellow, it is notably durable and extraordinarily elastic. When enraged, the Baleful Gigginox's yellow hide will transition into a deep-red, with the hide around the head hardening in the process.
The Baleful Gigginox is believed to be a random mutation in which the development of the external glands was altered, turning them into capacitor organs and causing them to manage electricity rather than filtering blood into toxins; these organs glow a bright-green and adorn the Subspecies' head, tail, and belly. The Baleful Gigginox's claws additionally maintain a degree of electrical charge, even after being harvested, with researchers hoping to harvest them as an energy source. Primarily, this mutation has bestowed the Baleful Gigginox with Thunder Sacs that allow it to generate and discharge lightning. Rather than expel a toxic gas, it can create a field of electricity around it and even fire paralyzing orbs of lightning from its circular maw. However, should the Baleful Gigginox's capacitor organs sustain too much damage, its long ranged electrical blasts will weaken; a similar effect will occur if its head sustains heavy damage as well.
While the regular species is notoriously fertile, the Baleful Gigginox has thus far never been spotted laying eggs or reproducing in any way. Instead, it solely lays explosive sacs of paralytic thunder during combat.
Behavior
Like its common counterpart, the Baleful Gigginox is entirely endemic to the Tundra and is predominantly found lurking in the region's various caves, where it is known to endanger miners. It shares the same hunting strategy and prey items, and will store food it wishes to eat later on within its caves. One of few differences between the two species may be observed when the wyvern pins prey down to ingest; while the Gigginox does so from cave ceilings, the Baleful Gigginox prefers to be on the ground when doing so. Due to its mutation, the Baleful Gigginox is a rarer sight to behold, and the electric orbs it spits are used to stun prey.
The dissection of the Baleful Gigginox's body has provided key resources that helped further the research of counteractant medicines. As well, its paralytic agent is a key component in the development of more potent Shock Traps.

Physiology
The Banbaro is a large Brute Wyvern covered in a thick layer of clear-white fur along its back and all around its large, broad tail, with its underside being coated in reddish-brown scales. The most noteworthy feature of the Banbaro are the large pair of horns present atop its head. These cup-shaped horns serve as impressive weapons, and when the Banbaro charges whilst scraping its horns across the ground, a variety of debris will accumulate atop their flattened surface. Typically comprised of rocks, this debris can then be either thrown at the Banbaro's target, or slammed onto the ground, where they will remain until smashed by the Banbaro again and scattered across the area. On occasion, the Banbaro can pick up large trees in its charges. Its hoofed hindlegs are incredibly muscular, helping to support its massive body as it charges.
While it would appear the Banbaro possesses two horns at first glance, it actually possesses three, with the third typically being kept flattened inconspicuously against its face. This horn can be extended at will and appears to aid the larger pair of horns in holding onto logs whilst the Banabro is charging. In addition, alongside several rows of shelling along the Banbaro's back, the horn will stand up on its own when its becomes agitated, This is believed to aid the Banbaro in regulating its own body temperature when angered, although, due to the fur covering its back, this change can easily go unnoticed.
The Banbaro is famed for its remarkable adaptability that allows it to survive in environments which it seems ill-suited towards, such as deserts and volcanic regions. To accomplish this, the Banbaro has a highly complex thermoregulatory system. When its body temperature drops, it creates space between its shelling, making it less exposed to the outside air and helping it to retain heat. Whereas when its body temperature increases, the shelling on its body increases in volume, helping to cool itself down as more heat is allowed to escape.
Behavior
While its thick fur originally lead the Hunter's Guild to believe the Banbaro was specialized to live exclusively in cold regions, it was eventually spotted roaming around several parts of the New World. This initial migration was believed to be caused by a further cooling of the Hinterlands reducing the food supply for the Banbaro and causing it to immigrate in search of different feeding grounds. While its thermoregulatory system allows it to easily buffer changes in temperature, the Banbaro still appears to avoid spending prolonged periods of time in the Rotten Vale and the Elder's Recess.
Typically, the Banbaro is a peaceful herbivore, however, should it be harmed in any way—or another monster begins to invade its territory—its temperament quickly sours and it will proceed to charge down the perceived threat with its horns. This demeanor has granted it the nickname of the Ferocious Bull Wyvern. Furthermore, this aggressive demeanor is believed to have evolved to combat the Beotodus, which shares the same habitat as the Banbaro.
Whilst its horns are useful weapons in combat, the Banbaro additionally uses them for feeding. These horns can be effectively utilized to both cut down trees as well as plow through snow, granting the Banbaro access to the soft roots and shoots it primarily feeds upon. It will feed on the insect larvae dug up in the process as well, which act as the Brute Wyvern's primary source of protein. By doing this, the Banbaro in turn cultivates the surrounding soil, allowing bacteria and other underground microorganisms to encourage the germination of more plant life.
The name "Banbaro" is derived from the language of the Boaboa. The Banbaro holds a great deal of cultural significance to the Boaboa, with the Brute Wyvern's bold and fearless nature in the face of potential danger causing it to be revered and even envied by the tribe.

Physiology
The Barioth is a large Flying Wyvern and sports the characteristic body plan of the class: its forelegs are modified into wings, while the hind legs remain terrestrial. The Barioth has a long tail with a forked tip and sports long amber colored tusks that protrude from its upper jaw. Its snowy body is covered in plated pale armor and luxurious, angelically soft fur, which is often sought after by noble families who consider it a symbol of power.
The shell armor of the Barioth is colored white to help the wyvern blend in with its snowy environments. All across the shell, along the wing bones and even on the bottom of the feet, the Barioth sports distinct conical spikes. These structures serve to dig into the icy soil of the tundra and enhance the Barioth's grip on the surfaces it walks upon, preventing involuntarily sliding. Short as they may be, the Barioth's spikes are extremely strong and even enable the wyvern to cling to walls for brief periods of time by digging them into solid rock or ice. Moreover, the Barioth's spikes are not actually connected to the wyvern's skeleton, and are also not made out of bone either. Instead, these spikes are modified parts of the armor shell that have undergone extreme keratinization which has changed them into sharp, pointed cones.
As is typical for a Flying Wyvern, the Barioth sports large wings on its forelegs. However, being a close relative of the Nargacuga, it shares the same quadrupedal gait as it when walking, with the winged forelegs serving as anterior walking limbs. Despite this, the wings of the Barioth are extremely well developed, making the species the most proficient at flying amongst the Winged Foreleg Wyverns. The Barioth can adjust the extension of its wing membranes through a joint in the outer wing bone, aiding in its aerial mobility. However, it notably struggles with flapping its wings for long periods of time and is not a true master of the skies, instead, its wings particularly excel at gliding.
A notable characteristic of the Barioth are its large tusks, which are unique amongst Flying Wyverns. These extremely long and sharp teeth are specialized in penetrating the thick layers of fat and fur which are typical in arctic prey. The pointed tips of the tusks are not the only weaponized component either, as the front edge of the teeth are serrated and can shred through material, while the back edge is razor sharp and specializes in cleaving through tissue. The famous amber color of the tusks is the result of iron from the Barioth's diet being deposited in them across the wyvern's life in order to reinforce them. In a similar vain, the Barioth's eyes have the peculiar property of changing color, a result from this wyvern's habit of squinting during daylight conditions to reduce the effect of the sun's glare reflecting off of the snowy landscape; the half-closed eyes reflect light such that they appear ice-blue in this state. In low-light conditions on the other hand—such as within caves—the Barioth opens its eyes fully so as to take in as much light as possible, which in turn causes the eyes to reflect a different range of light and appear as yellow or orange instead. When the Barioth grows enraged, blood flow around its eyes increases in a similar manner to the Nargacuga, adding a noticeable red hue to its eyes' color.
The Barioth is capable of spitting out ice projectiles that create small cyclones upon impact, this ability relies on the use of a Frost Sac, an organ that produces and stores freezing liquids in the wyvern's body. When the Barioth stimulates its Frost Sac, the organ begins to contract and pump, shooting the liquid across the rim of a spiraling canal where it gains momentum and spins. As it accelerates, the liquid interacts with the airways of the Barioth, adding further speed to it. When the correct speed is reached, the liquid is funneled to the throat and spat out through the mouth. Instantly upon exiting the body, the arctic ambient temperatures cause the liquid to freeze solid into a large ice projectile. As this projectile travels, it retains the momentum and spin it gained from inside the Barioth's body, causing it to travel rapidly. Upon impact, the ice does not simply shatter, and instead creates a spiraling wind blast due to the stored spin. As these winds pick up the shattered ice fragments, they form into the Barioth's characteristic cyclone.
The male and female Barioth do not possess obvious visual differences, although the latter is considered to be stronger and more aggressive. Meanwhile, the juvenile Barioth more or less resembles a mature individual, with the exception of a few notable differences. It entirely lacks the shell armor and is instead covered wholly in soft fur that ensures the juvenile stays warm in its youth, as its internal thermoregulatory functions take time to fully develop. As the young Barioth matures, its fur gradually falls out and is replaced by white shelling. The juvenile Barioth is born with its tusks already present, although they are much duller in color than in an adult. This is due to the color originating from iron in the blood of the young Barioth's prey being deposited in the tusks, a process that occurs over the wyvern's lifetime. Thus, the iron deposits and the resulting color are absent in the juvenile Barioth.
The Barioth encountered in the New World is quite similar to the population of the Old World, although the former is noted to be much more athletic and agile. It additionally displays an anatomical difference: while the Old World Barioth possesses three wing bones—one outer folding bone and two supporting membrane bones—the New World Barioth seems to only possess the outer bone. As well, a Barioth that is able to survive to old age in the New World and adapt to the extremely harsh conditions within the unexplored regions of the Hinterlands will sometimes display significant physiological changes. Such an individual is considered a Variant, and is called the Frostfang Barioth.
Behavior
The Barioth lives in arctic regions, where it quite often takes on the position of apex predator. It is an intelligent and cunning monster that uses its eyesight and camouflage to ambush prey unseen. The Barioth is known to adapt its hunting strategy based on the size and defensive properties of its prey. In the case of small targets, the Barioth simply attempts to overpower them, although when hunting large game, the Barioth will focus on delivering a killing bite with its enormous tusks. Should the initial pounce fail, the Barioth will shift its strategy, attempting instead to immobilize its victim with its cyclone breath. Once a target is unable to escape or evade, the Barioth will then once again attempt to end the fight with a deadly bite. If even this fails, the Barioth will attempt to slash at and injure the prey repeatedly, hoping for it to die from blood loss. Once a kill is secured, the Barioth will hold the carcass down with its wing arms and begin feasting. In order to maximize the nutritious benefit of its hunts, the Barioth is specialized in accessing and devouring the internal energy-rich organs of its victims. To do so, it uses its tusks to saw and carve through the body to access the best parts, cutting off small chunks at a time which it then eats.
Opposite sex individuals generally do not congregate, instead staking out separate territories far away from one another. However, when the breeding season comes, the male Barioth will begin intruding into the territories of females, flaunting its tusks around in a bid to get attention; the size and shape of the male's tusks is a crucial factor in determining sexual fitness. The female Barioth will then judge the male harshly, with unimpressed females brutally chasing off rejected suitors. After a Barioth pair has found each other and copulation is complete, the female will remain active and continue hunting up until the pregnancy begins hindering her movements. As gestation progresses, the female Barioth will seek out a cave in remote mountain ranges to serve as her nest and nursery, where she gives birth to a litter of 1-3 Barioth cubs.
Super Biology Information
The Super Biology Book Series collects the thoughts and theories of real scientists that were asked to speak about monsters from the Monster Hunter series. Thus, they are inherently speculative and should be seen as such.
Fossil Expert Yoshitsugu Kobayashi notes various interesting features of the Barioth’s anatomy: Its many spikes may serve not just as mobility tools and weapons, but also as additional temperature regulators by not shedding heat. The arms meanwhile are notable for being furry like those of a mammal, but protruding to the sides like it is more commonly the case in reptiles. The spiked tail of the Barioth meanwhile reminds Kobayashi of the thagomizers seen in Stegosaurus. As for the species’ infamous tusks, Kobayashi compares them to those of a sabre-toothed cat such as Smilodon: They are arched, long and sharp. Given these characteristics and a real-life analogue, Kobayashi confirms that the Barioth would likely be able to kill prey in a single strike from its tusks - provided it isn’t much larger than itself.
In terms of behavior, Kobayashi proposes that Barioth likely only have two to three offspring at a time. Keeping the size of litters small reduces the opportunity cost of raising each individual cub, which is why such birth rates are favored in cold environments. Overall, Kobayashi expects Barioth to be involved parents that invest a lot of energy into raising their children, likening their rearing behavior to that of polar bears.

The Barnos (バルノス, Barunosu) is a small Wingdrake introduced in Monster Hunter: World.
Summary
Aggressive Wingdrakes with toothy maws which inhabit volcanic environments, with some even being sighted following the volcanic Elder Dragon Zorah Magdaros. Preferring to swarm their targets in small groups, they are quick to start confrontations, and are known to spit an acidic agent at targets several times their own size, pursuing their target even when they flee their turf.

Physiology
The Barnos is an aggressive Wingdrake native to the New World. It is similar to other Wingdrake species in that it possesses a large head with a beak, forelimbs evolved for flight, taloned feet, and a tail. Its bony frame is protected by bumpy brown scales, except for the tan skin on its chest and stomach. It has a narrow head dominated by a hooked beak containing knife-like teeth; the upper set projects past the lower jaw. The eyes have sapphire irises and round pupils, and starting above the eyes and pointing backward are two horns.
The Barnos has a wide chest and spikes on its upper back. Each of its long forelimbs has three digits: a free thumb with a claw, and two elongated digits that support a wing membrane. The membrane extends to the shortened tail. The long legs end in zygodactyl feet and each toe has a strongly curved talon, the curvature of the which makes it easy for a Slinger to grab onto the feet, as well as difficult for the Wingdrake to dislodge it.
Under the mouth is an expandable pouch that holds a yellow fluid. The Barnos can regurgitate this fluid for two purposes: an acidic bile that corrodes the armor of its target, and a strong scent that attracts the ire of other Barnos.
Behavior
The Barnos lives in the harsh and rocky regions of the New World, primarily the Elder's Recess and volcanic region of the Guiding Lands. It is seen in groups of three and is the most aggressive species of Wingdrake, considering any creature as an intruder in its territory. If a Hunter stands in front of one, the whole flock will immediately begin their assault. The Barnos circles over its target before attacking by ramming, pecking, and spitting acid. Sometimes, a member of the flock will seemingly lose interest in the battle or even leave to another area, with the other two following at different times. Strangely, any individuals that retreated may soon return to fight again, so the trio takes turns fleeing and fighting. The Barnos rarely, if ever, lands on the ground.
The Barnos nests in volcanic and tropical environments as it prefers high temperatures, with the magma-covered shell of the Zorah Magdaros providing ample heat for the Wingdrake to roost. Flocks of the wyvern have been observed following the giant dragon as it moves through the New World.
Taking enough damage will briefly leave the Barnos vulnerable to a hunter's Slinger, allowing them to latch the Slinger onto the Wingdrake's feet, upon which the monster will then fly to a neighboring area before the Slinger detaches, and the Wingdrake will fly back to its original position.
Development
Monster Hunter World: The Official Complete Works shows concept art as if it were sketches of monsters made by members of the Research Commission based on limited evidence. Concept art of the Barnos includes four viscous-looking Wingdrakes, all of which have dark colors and spit acid. One has a heated chin spike that could carve rock, two have strange mammalian faces, and the last hangs upside down like a bat.

Physiology
The Barroth's whole body is covered in orange-brown scales and plates, which are often coated in mud as it rolls around the swamp. The topside scales are a darker brown, while its underside is a pale beige. Most notably, it's head consists of the hardest of these shells and is often used in much the same way as a large hammer for attacking. This cranial shell must be maintained through regular grooming, as well, the Barroth displays minor sexual dimorphism, as a male will sport a relatively larger head than the female. Located on top of the head, the nostrils are specially adapted to suit the Barroth when it bathes in the marshes. When angered by an intruder's attack, the Barroth is known to exhale sharply through these nostrils, producing visible steam from it. As well, the Barroth has evolved a number of nostrils so that it may exchange plenty of air whilst mud bathing.
The other plates covering the body are likewise thick and sturdy, as the mud coating hardens under the sun. This hardening process repeats and forms multiple layers of tough clay armor, which provides formidable defenses and additionally acts as a shock absorber. The Barroth's tail is armored like the rest of the body, and is considered a delicacy. Shaped like spades, the Barroth's stubby claws sharp and have been polished due to its constant digging of sand and dirt. These claws can even dig through solid rock, which allows the Barroth to feed on its favourite meal: Carrier Ants.
Behavior
The Barroth patrols its territory in the nearby swampy and arid regions where it leaves muddy territorial markings, and if it spots an intruder whilst patrolling, it will grow fierce and territorial. Its habit of using mud in combat led to the creation of its nickname, the Mud Brute. Even if apex monsters—such as the Diablos —encroaches on its territory, the Barroth will fearlessly weaponize its powerful, yet nimble, legs to challenge the opponent. The Barroth will intimidate invaders by using the muddy material covering its body, as the highly viscous mud can slow down the movement of a target and may even bring it to a complete stop. However, the mud additionally acts as a defensive shield for the Brute Wyvern. If it loses too much of this muddy barrier, the Barroth may retreat to search for a mud bath. In the Wildspire Waste, the Barroth frequently competes with the Jyuratodus and engages in many Turf Wars in their shared muddy environment.
The Barroth takes mud baths on a regular basis to protect its body from the dry and arid heat of the desert, as well as from parasites or blood-feasting insects. On especially sunny days, the Barroth is known to dive into a mud swamp and relax with only its nostrils exposed to the air. This also acts as natural camouflage, concealing the Brute Wyvern from its natural enemies. In the Old World, the Barroth will fiercely compete with others of its kind during the dry season, whereas such behavior has not been observed in the New World. There have been reports of individuals who have lost their lives during such battles due to cranial damage from powerful headbutts. It is possible that the New World ecology altered the species' behavior in territorial disputes.
The Barroth may utilize mud for breeding habits. The oviparous female accepted into a male's marsh will build a mound of mud, in which she will lay 10-20 eggs. While a male Barroth typically mates with only one female, reports suggest that if a swamp is considerably wide, a male may mate with several females. Both the male and female share duties in brooding, as the male will keep a sharp eye out for intruders and protect the female and the eggs. This behavior has only been recorded in the Old World, although the New World population likely shares the same breeding ecology. In regards to the eggs, they are kept warm by geothermal heat and usually hatch in a few months. The hatchlings will feed on small mud-dwelling insects, and once they reach an appropriate size, they emerge from the mound and destroy nearby anthills, starting their habit of preying on all the insects living there. A Hatchling resembles its parents from birth, and its cranial region develops with maturity. The Barroth's powerful legs develop during these early days as well, as the Barroth is forced to wade through viscous mud when young. As it matures, it must groom its head to account for changes in the head's weight and balance. In order to remove dirt and grime from its nostrils, the Barroth may frequently be seen rubbing its head against the ground.
While the New World Barroth primarily feeds upon Carrier Ants, the Barroth in the Old World primarily feed on Altaroth. This Barroth has even been observed using its large crown to destroy the dens of the Neopteron, allowing them to easily feed on them.
Monster Hunter: World
Kaname Fujioka said that Barroth's purpose in World was to teach the player how to dodge a charge and then follow it up with an attack. The development team brought it in as soon as they came up with the Wildspire Waste. Expanding on Barroth would create an easy-to-understand tutorial experience, and was designed to be a wall for players so that once they learn how to deal with it, it's easy. They added environmental elements by having Barroth coat itself in mud. If the player uses aspects of the terrain to their advantage when avoiding Barroth's charges, they'll be greatly rewarded, so Fujioka feels that this variation of Barroth is much easier to deal with than in past games.
Originally, Barroth's design played with the idea of how the hardness of a monster's body could change by coating it in mud. Previously, the player had no choice but to spam attacks in older games, but with the slinger and a few other useful options for fighting introduced for World, it allowed players more ways to react to the toughness of a monster's body than ever before. As a roaming monster, Barroth is most easily dealt with if the player takes advantage of its turf wars with Jyuratodus.

Physiology
As a juvenile Gravios, the Basarios has a notabe rock-hard shelling with an appearance remarkably similar to actual rocks. This slate-gray carapace, known as Gravite, is covered with several large rock-shaped bumps along its spine, with those over its back being especially prominent. Despite its immature state, the Basarios' carapace is actually tougher than that of the full-grown Gravios' due to the large amount of ore the wyvern has consumed for its growth. These minerals are then digested inside of its body and slowly accumulate inside of its outer-shell, calcifying in the process and causing its shelling to grow both larger and tougher as it slowly matures, with the amount of ore inside of it often overtaking the amount of organic material. As a result, rare minerals can often be extracted from its body, leaving it a common target for Hunters. For instance, an accumulation of mineral components near its tear ducts often results in the formation of small faintly-pink gems. Interestingly, the Basarios boasts two horns atop its nose, whilst the Gravios only has one.
Like most Flying Wyverns, its forelimbs have been fashioned into a pair of wings, which bear a pale tan membrane alongside pickaxe-like wing claws. These claws are used alongside its incredibly tough head to easily bore into and move through the ground. However, as the wings have specialized to be used in digging, they have subsequently lost most of their former flexibility, causing the Basarios to have declined in its ability to fly and leaving it capable of only briefly lifting itself off the ground. In comparison to the Gravios' large and spiky clubbed tail, the Basarios' tail is stubby and thin, yet despite this it still incorporates high-grade minerals into itself that grants it surprisingly high strength.
The Basarios internally possesses a Flame Sac that accumulates dust inside of itself; by igniting this dust and expelling it onto its surroundings, it is capable of breathing both fireballs and rays of heat, although the latter attack is something it is not proficient at and can often fail to perform. In addition, releasing this much heat has the consequence of scorching its own shell in the process, causing it to turn spongy in texture and glow red-hot, making it much easier to damage. Another application of its internal heat allows it to vaporize poison located in its body to release a toxic gas from its underside, either to steadily deal damage overtime or act as a narcotic. The underside of its body appears to be the wyvern's natural weak spot, as it bears a relatively thin covering in comparison to the rest of its body armor, with it being known to be especially susceptible to damage from explosives. Nonetheless, its chest's shelling does sport overlapping layers to somewhat protect its weak point.
Behavior
The Basarios primarily resides within volcanic areas and other environments with similar barren rocky areas where its camouflage is the most effective. It is not a particularly agile or active wyvern due to its rocky carapace, and being a juvenile it has little hunting experience, therefore it primarily relies on ambush tactics when hunting. To accomplish this, it will burrow itself into the ground and leave its back exposed, causing it to strongly mimic a boulder. Once potential prey unknowingly approaches the hidden monster, typically small monsters or insects, it will leap out of the ground and consume them. If it senses an enemy, it can charge them down using the full-force of its rocky exterior. The Basarios also sleeps while half of its body is underground, with its hard shelling preventing most monsters from successfully predating upon it and allowing it to rest peacefully amongst the environment.
As the Basarios feeds upon organic materials, it will also consume the rocks in the surrounding area. Additionally, there are certain types of bacteria found inside of volcanic rocks capable of generating usable energy from inorganic materials. As a result, when these minerals are digested by the wyvern, the bacteria is cultivated within its digestive tract and gradually allows it to obtain energy solely from inorganic materials as it matures. The full maturation process can take quite a long time as it slowly accumulates enough bacteria; once it begins to feed on gunpowder-rich minerals, it is officially recognized as having become a Gravios. This behavior is considered an excellent example of a symbiotic relationship in a particularly food-poor environment such as volcanoes.
Super Biology Information
The Super Biology Book Series collects the thoughts and theories of real scientists that were asked to speak about monsters from the Monster Hunter series. Thus, they are inherently speculative and should be seen as such.
Fossil Expert Yoshitsugu Kobayashi muses that the large body of the Basarios would come with distinct advantages and disadvantages. Its size probably deters most predators and also aids in temperature regulation: A larger body has less surface area compared to volume than a smaller body, which means that there is less surface from which heat can radiate into or out of the body leading to a constant internal temperature. This however, Kobayashi asserts, is likely also the main drawback of such a massive body. Since heat cannot easily leave the body, accumulated heat is harder to shed, which can be dangerous for the monster. Kobayashi theorizes that the Basarios’ slow movements are possibly a result of this interaction as well, as motion would produce additional heat - something the wyvern would ideally want to avoid if possible.
The stone-like armor of the Basarios reminds Kobayashi of dermal armor plates found on Ankylosaurus. He theorizes that the armor of such a juvenile is thick and heavy to protect it during the maturation process, hence their massive, boulder-like shape. This particular shape might in fact have been selected for due to it also doubling as camouflage.

Physiology
The Baunos is a carnivorous Wingdrake from the Forbidden Lands that, much like other Wingdrakes, resembles a miniature Flying Wyvern. It has a flexible neck and tail, a beak, a compact body, back limbs with claws, and a pair of front limbs modified into large wings. It stands in an upward stance using both its legs and wings and is wrapped primarily in brownish-gray skin, with its face and the underside of its wings having a red color. Black fuzz covers its back, while red feathers cover the ventral surface of the neck, coat the chest, and surround the eyes—a turquoise line of skin runs from the lower beak down to the chest, bisecting the red. The Baunos is able to vibrate the Echo Feathers on its chest to emit a deafening roar, moreover, Hunters can collect these feathers with the Hook Slinger to craft Screamer Pods.
Compared to its relatives, the Baunos has a short neck and a large head. Its robust beak is lined with stout serrations for tearing into flesh, and its eyes have round pupils with golden irises, reflecting a pale yellow light when in darkness. The wings are formed from modified hands with four digits each. Three of the digits are small and clawed; they do not support the wing but are used for walking. A single long digit supports the wing membrane. The wings of the Baunos are proportionately large amongst both Wingdrakes and even other flying monsters. The Baunos' feet each have four toes with curved claws and its tail is tipped with large, black feathers.
Behavior
The Baunos is endemic to the Windward Plains and does not hunt its own prey, preferring to rather scavenge any carrion that can be spotted from vantage points. As such, it can be seen soaring over the vast arid expanse, surveying the ground in search of deceased monsters to feast upon. The Wingdrake will unleash its powerful roar to intimidate any rival scavenger or predator whenever necessary, and while on the ground, it frequently preens its wings with its beak.
The Baunos establishes colonies in the highest cliffs of the Fulgurite caves; these colonies can be identified by the white feces staining the rock and the constant warbling of its denizens. The Baunos will take shelter in this colony to avoid the lightning of the Sandtide.

Physiology
The Bazelgeuse is a large, bulky Flying Wyvern that can be found in nearly any environment. Its back and the dorsal sides of its forelimbs are covered with silver rock-like scutes bearing a bronze hue, while the scales on its underside are a darker-gray in color. It has a notably thick torso, a flat and stout head with orange eyes, and a wide and flat tail with a prominent bony spike at the tip. The Bazelgeuse's beige wings are sleek and wide, sporting a pronounced wingtalon at the first joint. Unusually for a Flying Wyvern, its flight patterns rely primarily on quiet low-altitude gliding rather than flapping motions, allowing it to stealthily scout for prey. Further, the Bazelgeuse's wings uniquely still retain function as arms, with it using its wings for stability and movement on land.
The underside of the Bazelgeuse's neck and tail are covered in gray protruding explosive scales, resembling seeds or eggs. The Blasting Scales of the Bazelgeuse are not actual scales; rather, they are formed by specialized bristle-like glands located on the monster's neck and tail, called Fuses. These Fuses continuously secrete a unique highly explosive fluid that inflates the Fuse's membrane and hardens, forming a Blasting Scale that can be dislodged from the Bazelgeuse's body as a natural consequence of the Bazelgeuse moving around. When struck, heated up, or simply exposed to the air for a long period of time, the scales detonate violently, with a single one carrying enough force to level a building. The Bazelgeuse is immune to the generated heat and explosions thanks to its incredibly resilient carapace and scales, even after diving at or slamming prey and detonating the scales. Once the scales are dropped, the glands continue to create new ones to ensure the monster always has access to its most powerful weapon. On occasion, multiple Fuses may accumulate inside its body and form a Glandflux that secretes even more explosive fluid.
When the Bazelgeuse is enraged, its metabolism and blood pressure spike, drastically increasing its body temperature. As a result, its blasting scales and the gaps between its shelling will begin to glow incandescently, making the former more volatile and reach a point where many will explode the moment they're detached from the body. The Bazelgeuse's heightened metabolism additionally leads to an increased rate of production of its volatile fluids, causing fired scales to regrow much faster and previously depleted scales to immediately regrow when entering this state.
The teeth of the Bazelgeuse are quite weak and it lacks the bite force to tear tough hides or chew bones. To compensate, the Bazelgeuse will pepper its food with its blasting scales to help break through the tough exterior of its prey. The Bazelgeuse is also capable of breathing fire despite a lack of a conventional organ or sac for flame production, being believed to instead spray the same explosive fluid in its blasting scales from glands in its mouth, with the force of the ejection causing the fluid to ignite. However, it tends to use its fire breath to detonate dislodged scales from a distance instead of directly attacking enemies.
Behavior
Feared as the Bombarding Wyvern for its destructive power, the Bazelgeuse is an aggressive and nomadic wyvern infamous for its habit of somehow sensing and swooping in on any ongoing conflict in the vicinity, viewing a virtually limitless area as its territory and being able to inhabit almost any environment. The monster sees any other large monster as a potential competitor for food and will challenge any and all intruders on sight in an attempt to monopolize their ecosystem, attacking relentlessly until they leave or die. Due to these violent tendencies, it has been described as having a berserker-like thirst for battle, sometimes leading it to attack and attempt to displace regional apex predators in a bid for territory. In spite of its aggression, the Bazelgeuse can be opportunistic when ambushing ongoing conflicts, waiting until the involved parties are wounded and weak before swooping in for a kill.
When hunting, the Bazelgeuse will generally ambush prey by indiscriminately bombing the area from afar using its blasting scales, before swooping in to leisurely prey on anything that died in the explosions. Larger or more resilient targets are instead met by the Bazelgeuse dive-bombing directly into them after peppering the area with scales, using its body to detonate the scales in a devastating blast, then engaging in direct combat should the enemy still persist. If overpowered and pinned by an enemy, the Bazelgeuse has been seen releasing and detonating a majority of its blasting scales simultaneously in an effort to break free.
As the Bazelgeuse and the Deviljho —another widespread invasive monster—share similar habits and temperaments, it is not uncommon to see the two locked in fierce combat, with the Deviljho in particular being occasionally attracted to the Bazelgeuse's territory by the plentiful prey it has gathered by driving out competitors. Ironically, the brutal territorial conflicts between the two monsters often distract them enough for all nearby prey to flee the area, leaving both predators empty-handed.
The Bazelgeuse is believed to nest at high elevations, where the altitude allows it to survey a vast area of potential territory. It is theorized the Elder Crossing and subsequent increase in monster activity, and thus potential prey, is the reason for its increased distribution and expansion from its original territory, as the Bazelgeuse had never been seen at all in the New World prior to then. Exclusively in the Elder's Recess, it is known to rub its body on the ground and leave behind misfired scales, believed to be a way of marking its turf; the behavior being specific to the locale is theorized to be due to its proximity to the wyvern's original habitat. The Bazelgeuse has rarely been spotted in the Old World, where it appears to have evolved differently compared to in the New World.
Music
Main article: Bazelgeuse (Music)
"The Invading Tyrant" is Bazelgeuse's theme. It is one of the only themes from World to get a remaster, namely in Monster Hunter Rise. The World version of "The Invading Tyrant" was voted among the Top 10 music themes in the Hunters' Choice: Top 10 Monster Themes - Monster Hunter 20 th Anniversary.
Monster Hunter: World
Yuya Tokuda stated that the team wanted to bring a new experience to the maps players are already used to as they head into harder battles. They proposed a monster that would fight over its prey, which led them to the concept of a Flying Wyvern that bombards the area. Due to this, the team heard that Bazelgeuse gained much attention from overseas players who were experiencing Monster Hunter for the first time and were glad it made a significant impact.
Since the game takes place in the New World, Kaname Fujioka thought that players would want a new troublemaker like Deviljho. Explosive bombardment was ideated from the start, and the design incorporates burning, regeneration, and awkward, seagull-like wings. Its ventral side conceals the secretory organs, so the design team made its dorsal side very simple. Fujioka thought its face was well proportioned and pretty handsome, despite its design centering around its explosive nature.

The Demon Beast Behemoth (ベヒーモス, Behiimosu) is an Elder Dragon introduced in Monster Hunter: World for a collaboration with Final Fantasy XIV.
Summary
A gigantic creature that hails from another world. Its body is packed with bulging muscles that grant the Behemoth incredible strength, making each of its strikes and swipes deadly. Uniquely, this monster is able to cast an array of magic spells, ranging from targeted lightning bolts and flaming meteors to localized tornadoes, the Behemoth wields many different arcane powers. Its most devastating attack sees it summoning a colossal meteor to obliterate its enemies.
