Physiology
Hailing from the world of Eorzea, the Behemoth is an otherworldly monster that has been tentatively classified as an Elder Dragon due to its physiology and abilities defying nature itself. The Behemoth is a member of a species of the same name native to Eorzea, believed to be descendants of the elder primal Bahamut. Its colossal frame is covered in a dark purple hide stretched tightly over rippling, dense muscles that grant the beast immense physicality and durability. Its body is noticeably top-heavy and supported by forelimbs slightly larger than its hindlimbs, with each limb ending in claws capable of slaughtering weaker prey in a single blow. Its head is mammalian in appearance and sports piercing blue eyes, numerous sharp teeth, and two enormous curved horns that glow with an ominous light, leaving even hardened warriors shaken. A mane of black fur adorns the top of its head and upper back while large, curved, black spines run along the center of its back, diminishing in size past its mane. Its tail is thick, muscular, and covered in long thin spines, allowing it to easily sweep away threats.
The Behemoth's bones support its huge body and hold an extreme amount of strength, allowing it to knock out even legendary heroes. Although usually adopting a quadrupedal stance, the Behemoth can stand on its hind limbs with no visible difficulty. Yet, despite its enormous frame, the Behemoth can move with surprising speed and agility.
The Behemoth's signature ability is the use of magic and spells, an inexplicable ability at complete odds with even other Elder Dragons. These spells include Meteor, which summons explosive fireballs from the sky, Charybdis, which creates a violent localized tornado, Thunderbolt, which summons lightning to smite targets, Comet, which creates and drops a molten boulder from above, and an unnamed spell that causes the ground to erupt with fiery explosions. When using magic, the Behemoth's horns and upper body will glow with an otherworldly light, suggesting a link between them; its mane in particular is said to be charged with the power it uses to summon meteors.
The Behemoth's most notorious spell is the Ecliptic Meteor, which calls down a flaming meteor of cataclysmic proportions and is only used when the beast is injured or angered enough. Upon impact, the meteor will engulf the immediate area in a gigantic explosion, obliterating every living being in the locale if they are unable to find adequate cover beforehand. The Behemoth itself is seemingly unaffected by the Ecliptic Meteor's explosion.
Behavior
The Behemoth has an intensely ornery disposition and instantly acts aggressive towards both humans and monsters in its vicinity. Although this can be attributed to agitation at being displaced from its home world and into an unfamiliar environment, individuals in Eorzea are also known to aggressively attack and do battle with heroes. They have gained a fearsome reputation in their homeland as beasts of legend and are among the strongest monsters one can face. Although the Behemoth is known to actively hunt, it is unknown if it has any need to feed or maintain territory; much of its behavior and physiology beyond its monstrous strength remains shrouded in mystery, even in its home world.
Although intelligent enough to make full use of its arsenal of spells, the Behemoth is a highly physical fighter that uses brutal attacks from all parts of its body, primarily using its clawed forelimbs to crush and slash foes, or goring them with its huge horns. When angered, it will also notably single out the most dangerous threat to itself, attacking them relentlessly; as it focuses its rage towards a single target, its muscles glow a very bright and vivid red. When mortally injured, the Behemoth will attempt to perform a final Ecliptic Meteor, seemingly in a last ditch effort to take its attackers down alongside it.
The Behemoth is typically known to live atop mountains in Eorzea, occasionally descending to hunt, although the only sighting in the New World was in the volcanic Elder's Recess. As this was merely the location the Behemoth landed in after being transported to the New World, it remains unknown if the beast would stay there if left to its own devices.

When slain in World, "A Victory Fanfare Reborn (Full)" plays as the Quest Complete theme, and is from the same soundtrack.

Physiology
The Beotodus is a tundra-dwelling Piscine Wyvern adapted to living in frigid environments. Its hide is navy-blue with a single yellow stripe that runs down either side of its body, transitioning to pink on the underbelly. It sports four dorsal fins: a large dorsal ray fin between its shoulders, a set of two posterior lobe fins, and a small lobe fin near the tail; the bulbous tail sports a single short caudal fin. The Beotodus' soft-rayed pectoral fins are the largest on its body, each sporting a single elongated claw. Additionally, it has two small cranial fins on each side of its head.
The jaws of the Beotodus sport two rows of teeth; the first row is adorned with large thick fangs, while the second row is lined with smaller needle-like teeth. Each side of the upper jaw has three large canine teeth and two front incisors. The canines of the lower jaw protrude outwards at a slight angle, and there is a notable gap between the incisors on the lower jaw. When feeding, the Beotodus bites into its prey, before twisting with its body's strength to tear off chunks to swallow whole. Protected by thick black plating, its head features a large, black, wedge-shaped horn. The horn's shape is specially adapted for burrowing into and swimming through snow. As the wyvern moves through the snow, the horn pushes snow to the sides of the body. When half-submerged, the Beotodus can still breathe through the nostrils located on the top of its head. The pointed horn is incredibly sturdy, tempered by the harsh cold environment.
A peculiar trait of the Beotodus lies in its legs. The fin-like protrusions on its upper thighs aid it in steering when it is submerged and break through thick layers of snow. This kicks up a lot of loose snow, which the Beotodus flings at its prey to drain their stamina and hinder their movement. While valuable to the Beotodus' ability to live in the tundra, these leg fins are particularly vulnerable when exposed. Due to this, Hunters are encouraged to target the ridges on the monster's thighs to limit its movement. The Beotodus prefers being half-submerged in the snow, as it is noted to be uncomfortable and clumsy when it comes to walking on land. The Beotodus is adept in detecting prey whilst submerged through a sonar-like sensory organ that detects vibrations. When raising its head above the snow, it restlessly surveys the surrounding area for prey and predators. It has surprisingly well-developed vision, helping it identify the movement of prey.
The Beotodus is known to be ovoviviparous, having evolved to have its young hatch from fertilized eggs within their mother before being born. As a result, the young Beotodus does not receive nutrients from the mother, instead relying on the eggs for nutrition. When the eggs can no longer sustain the Beotodus' unborn young, the young will cannibalize each other inside the womb; this development process leads to only 2-3 individuals being born into the outside world per clutch. While highly unusual for wyverns, it serves as an effective strategy to ensure only the most adept survivalists are given the opportunity to thrive.
Behavior
The Beotodus is extremely territorial, demonstrating overwhelming aggression when hunting or defending its territory from intruders, however, this aggression is not without reason. As a result of its inept walking abilities, the Beotodus' range of activity is limited due to its preference of areas with soft snow it can burrow into, causing it to be extremely defensive of its territory. It can often be seen engaging in territorial disputes with the Banbaro, who shares a preference for the same habitat. In order to protect itself when above ground, the Beotodus covers itself in a thick layer of snow to protect the vulnerable parts of its body. Should the snow fall off, it simply burrows into the snow to re-arm itself.
The Beotodus' favorite prey is the Popo, which it hunts by ambushing them from beneath the snow, using its keen senses to detect the movement of prey via vibrations. Despite its aggression towards other monsters, the Beotodus is relatively complacent with the presence of hunters, ignoring them for a large period of time before instigating combat if left undisturbed. However, the Beotodus itself finds itself a common prey item to an unlikely source, the Boaboa. The Lynian tribe holds a strong degree of contempt towards the wyvern due to its preference for feeding on Popo, which are considered highly sacred to the tribe. The tribe has even been known to both cook the wyvern's meat and even preserve it within their dens for later consumption.
Development
Fujioka states that Iceborne was designed to bring in many returning monsters, but since the story is about an expedition headed to a new land, he wanted the first monster players encountered to be a new one. Furthermore, expanding on World, the team wanted Iceborne to emphasize elemental damage as a playstyle, with players selecting the right element to maximize their damage on each monster.
The team decided to have players encounter a new monster that specializes in the ice element to leave a strong first impression. Beotodus's ability to burrow into the snow was considered a great introduction to the new locale, the Hoarfrost Reach. So, the team built a monster based on the mud-dwelling Jyuratodus, but made the terrain a little easier to move around in.
Fujioka also notes that although it can be defeated quite easily if players use the clutch claw, it seems that many struggled because it was their first experience with Master Rank, and its movements were a bit tricky. He recalls forgetting to have cold resistance when setting out to hunt it and having a terrible time.
To create Beotodus' sound effects and emphasise its snow drilling attacks, the sound team wanted a "snowblower" effect. An electric drill was rubbed against a bucket to create a sense of reverb, and random items like pebbles and ice are placed inside the bucket to change how the reverb sounded, with the added effect of the handle rattling on the surface.

Physiology
The Berserk Tetsucabra is an emerald-green Subspecies of the Tetsucabra, renowned widely for its distinctive markings which resemble a painted face. Its body is covered by thick, green and yellow scales that have been soiled by Powderstones and form a hulking carapace that far surpasses the strength of the standard variety's. The Berserk Tetsucabra's dull red claws are robust and used to smash both Powderstones and prey alike with a shared fury.
Similarly to the common Tetsucabra, this Subspecies possesses highly specialized jaws for crushing rock; although it digs up and throws boulders in much the same way, the variety it throws explode upon impact. The Berserk Tetsucabra uses its superior jaws to crush any rocks it has unearthed, purposefully making use of the resulting blasts against foes; the explosions from the boulders it unearths cause its face to glow a bright orange. Each one akin to a giant hunk of seething-hot iron, the Berserk Tetsucabra's tusks will crunch through anything caught in its jaws. It is additionally capable of spewing a mucus from its maw that saps away the stamina of anything that comes into contact with it, however, the Berserk Tetsucabra appears to utilize it only after its tusks have been severely damaged.
Behavior
The Berserk Tetsucabra primarily inhabits subterranean and volcanic regions, and is known for its terrifying attacks and savage nature. Its ferocious appearance has caused Hunters who have faced it to bestow it the title of Rough Oni Frog, a moniker that would come to be widely adopted. In spite of its aggression and habit of digging up and hurling red-hot boulders at hunters, the Berserk Tetsucabra's behavior itself does not greatly differ from the standard Tetsucabra. While its explosive boulders are useful weapons in combat, the explosions created from the boulders are additionally utilized by the male Berserk Tetsucabra to both secure its own territory as well as to attract females it wishes to mate with.

Physiology
The Bishaten is a relatively small Fanged Beast covered in blue fur that is accented with furrier, white tufts along its limbs, back, shoulders, and neck. The tufts of fur around the neck in particular resemble a pointed pair of ears and protect the Bishaten from the jaws of potential predators, while the tufts around its shoulders drape over in a manner resembling a scarf. The Bishaten's fur is noted to stay orderly even when treated vigorously; the finest Bishaten fur emits a soft scent reminiscent of persimmon. Its forearms bear a pair of small wings covered in bright-blue feathers, which at most are capable of only short bursts of gliding. Instead, their feathers primarily provide stability while the Bishaten is moving or holding itself upright, allowing it to ride the wind to accelerate its movements. The claws of the Bishaten are small, yet still capable of tearing enemies to shreds. Its face is red and has a beak-like, bony horn protruding from the nose, said to resemble a monk's hat.
The Bishaten has a distinctive, muscular tail that ends in a five-fingered claw structure, with the claw itself being covered in a bony carapace called a Tailcase. This tail is strong enough to support the monster's entire weight and prehensile enough to be effectively used as an additional limb; the Bishaten makes use of this property to stand on its tail as well as use it to grab objects or terrain. The tail claws have considerable grip strength and traction, while the Tailcase is smooth and allows the bishaten to slide around when standing on the back of its tail claw. The hardened Tailcase in conjunction with the tail's strength lends it unprecedented power as a bludgeon, with swings from the tail able to shatter rock and reduce large trees to splinters. However, the Bishaten is prone to becoming unbalanced and toppling over if its tail is attacked whilst supporting its weight.
The Bishaten has a pouch on its stomach that is used to store and age fruits for later consumption or use. The properties of the Bishaten's stomach are able to prefectly age meat, although the result is only palatable to monsters.
The Bishaten appears almost identical regardless of its sex, being differentiated only by the appearance of its neck fur and horns.
Behavior
Highly mischievous and curious, the Bishaten is infamous for its tendency to bother and harass other creatures, including humans. While it is omnivorous in nature, it has a preference for fruit, particularly Jumbofruit. Additionally, the Bishaten makes liberal use of the fruits it gathers as weapons to pelt its unlucky victims with. It is often seen moving by standing on its tail and using its wings to glide across the ground in a manner compared to a spinning top.
In battle, the Bishaten has been observed to be resourceful and cunning. In addition to wielding its tail with extreme dexterity, it gathers and utilizes Poisonfruit, Flashfruit, and Parafruit in combat, demonstrating awareness of their different uses and taking full advantage of them to debilitate enemies. The Bishaten will also cover its eyes and mouth to protect itself from the bright flashes and harmful gases released by these fruits, however, it can still be blindsided if its dropped fruit is picked up and used against it.
The female Bishaten lives in packs composed of other females and young, while the male Bishaten is solitary and only joins a female herd during the breeding season.
Development
The design team based Bishaten on the tengu (天狗/てんぐ), dangerous yōkai resembling humanoids with a mix of primate and avian features, often depicted wearing long-nosed masks. Bishaten was specifically designed after both a traditional tengu and the karasu-tengu (烏天狗), which has a more crow-like beak and facial shape. While the Bishaten was designed with more primate features, its tail was designed to resemble the fans tengu are commonly depicted as holding. The Bishaten's face was designed to be highly emotive, with its use of fruits in battle also showing off its high intelligence.

Physiology
A Subspecies of the Diablos defined as a female individual whose body has entirely turned black during the breeding season, the Black Diablos bears an otherwise close resemblance to the standard Diablos. Thick armor plates protect her bulky body, and the muscular wings are adorned with blunt claws used for swift burrowing. Her thick tail ends in a massive club that can shatter rock, and her head sports a spiked frill, curved tusks, and the two twisting horns for which the Diablos is known. However, the Black Diablos' shell differs from that of the normal Diablos in both its composition and quality.
The Black Diablos boasts greatly enhanced physical strength compared to the regular Diablos, being capable of smashing through rock and lifting other monsters with ease. Her strength is great enough to ward off powerful monsters, such as the Deviljho. Further, should the Black Diablos become Tempered, she will rival even Elder Dragons in physical prowess.
Behavior
During the breeding season, a female Diablos will produce a surge of hormones that cause physical and behavioral changes. The black coloration serves as a signal to a male Diablos that the female is ready to mate—or has already done so—as well as to warn other monsters of her heightened aggression. It is theorized that the darker coloration absorbs more sunlight, which raises her body temperature for the development of her eggs. The color lasts until the brooding season.
Amongst the many changes in the Black Diablos’ behavior is an increased survival instinct and thus greatly increased aggression; treating even her mate as an intruder. While a courted male and female pair will share a territory, they will not cooperate in finding food or defense. When the female turns black, she will engage in battle with the male as if they were fighting for territory. On occasion, one will break the other’s horn. Despite her increased vigilance during the gestation period, it is not confirmed if the Black Diablos cares for her young.
The Black Diablos fights similarly to the regular Diablos, albeit with greater aggression and cunning. She has been noted to circle her target and wait for the right time to attack, and is also proficient at tracking her opponent's movements and changing the direction of a charge to strike her target. With her greater tracking ability, the Black Diablos utilizes new methods of charging at opponents, displaying greater speed and turning with a tighter arc. Like the normal Diablos, she will attack opponents from above and below the surface. However, the Black Diablos prefers to violently launch herself from the ground instead of pulling herself out.
Fortunately, the Black Diablos is reclusive and does not leave her cave unless in search of food. While the regular Diablos prefers cacti with the highest moisture content, the Black Diablos instead seeks out cacti with the most nutrients for her young, and will visit the same cactus patch five to six times a day.
With her great power and ferocity, the Black Diablos dominates her sweltering territory, as few monsters can match her strength. The reason behind the Black Diablos' classification as a Subspecies despite being a temporary seasonal form of a female Diablos is to warn Hunters of the danger they will face, as many hunters have fallen victim to her unusual tactics and deadly attacks.
Development
According to Yuya Tokuda, Black Diablos was added to Monster Hunter: World because they wanted a harder monster variant for the Wildspire Waste. Her aggression towards regular Diablos is inspired by a certain animal that attacks its mate, though he did not specify which species.

The Corpse Coat Dragon Blackveil Vaal Hazak (死を纏うヴァルハザク, Shi o Matou Varuhazaku) is an Elder Dragon introduced in Monster Hunter World: Iceborne.
It is a Variant of the Vaal Hazak.
Summary
Vaal Hazak who have left behind the Rotten Vale to venture into new territory. In doing so, the effluvium usually clinging to them has transformed into spore-filled pustules that cover their entire body, including their eyes, leaving them completely blind. These spores spew out clouds of effluvium at anything that approaches them. A Blackveil's presence is enough to bring about widespread ecological disaster.

Physiology
As a Variant, the Blackveil Vaal Hazak is similar in appearance to the standard species, possessing silver, fish-like scales and bony hooks adorning its body. It is a hexapedal Elder Dragon with four slender legs with hooked claws, and a pair of wings with reduced membranes. The head sports two pairs of lower jaws, both with long curved teeth. The primary feature of the Blackveil Vaal Hazak that differentiates it from its counterpart lies in its macabre form of armor.
Much like the Vaal Hazak, the Blackveil Vaal Hazak conceals itself in rotting flesh that is held by the hooked spikes throughout its body. However, rather than bear the usual dark-crimson shade, this Variant cloaks itself with black flesh. Growing atop the flesh coating is a strange fungus that forms a symbiotic relationship with the Blackveil Vaal Hazak and its effluvial bacteria, this fungus develops large, gray sporangia that cover the Elder Dragon's abdomen, tail, and eyes. These sporangia fill with effluvium from the Elder Dragon and periodically release it in bursts, protecting the Blackveil Vaal Hazak on all sides and continuously spreading spores and miasma throughout the environment. The fungus ejects such a large amount of effluvium that a gray haze falls upon the area.
The fungus becomes more active as the air grows more saturated with miasma. In addition, the effluvium rapidly infects nearby monsters—from which the Blackveil Vaal Hazak is able to draw energy from—allowing the Variant to move to new habitats. The Blackveil Vaal Hazak can additionally exhale greater quantities of effluvium at once than the regular Vaal Hazak and produce it at a faster rate, however, a drawback of the fungus' growth is that it covers the Elder Dragon's eyes and renders it blind. Unless the fungus has been removed, this makes Flash Pods ineffective against the Blackveil Vaal Hazak.
Behavior
As is the case with the Vaal Hazak, this Variant is found in the Rotten Vale. However, it may also be found in the Ancient Forest and Rotted Region of the Guiding Lands, unlike the base species. Within the Rotten Vale, its behavior is similar to that of the base species, however, the Blackveil Vaal Hazak's blindness makes it difficult for it to detect potential threats—even if a Hunter is directly in front of it, the Elder Dragon may not be aware of their presence. As it wanders the depths of the Vale, the Blackveil Vaal Hazak will often pause and roar at a seemingly nonexistent foe, before continuing walking. If it sits for a prolonged period, it may leave Tainted Spores on the ground, which a hunter can use to track the Elder Dragon.
The presence of the Blackveil Vaal Hazak changes the ecosystem of the Ancient Forest due to the sporangia constantly ejecting effluvium into the atmosphere, their output increasing as the fungus grows on the body. When they reach a certain size, the sporangia release a huge amount of miasma at once, creating a localized environment that is similar to the Rotten Vale. The effluvium infects denizens of the forest, such as the Jagras, Aptonoth, and Mernos, and the Blackveil Vaal Hazak then feeds on the nutrients the bacteria has extracted from infected victims. The sight of spores spreading from its body as it strides around evokes imagery of death itself, and it is for this reason the Variant was bestowed the Blackveil moniker that distinguishes it from the Vaal Hazak. Under normal circumstances, the Vaal Hazak cannot survive outside of the Rotten Vale due to its reliance on the effluvium. Thus, it is believed the Blackveil Vaal Hazak adorns itself in fungus to grant it the ability to change the environment to one that benefits it, allowing it to expand its range to outside of the Vale. It moved to the Ancient Forest as the fungus it had acquired in the Rotten Vale is also present there, as well as displayed higher activity. The Blackveil Vaal Hazak may appear in other locations besides the Ancient Forest.
In combat, the Blackveil Vaal Hazak exhales greater volumes of miasma and spreads it more thoroughly. The fungus on its body releases puffs of effluvium in all directions independently of the Blackveil Vaal Hazak's movements, making it dangerous to approach. Attacking the sporangia disables them. Should the fungus be allowed to grow enough, the sporangia will suddenly swell to incredible sizes, prompting the Elder Dragon to rise into the air and launch clumps of noxious spores from its body. These spores leave thick clouds of effluvium where they land, draining the life out of any creature standing in them. The fungus temporarily stops releasing miasma after this attack.
Development
After the defeat of Velkhana, the development team wanted a Variant or Subspecies of an Elder Dragon to raise the threat of the next battle. They decided against adding a Variant of a returning monster like Kushala Daora and developed one for one of the new Elder Dragons, Vaal Hazak. The choice to create a Variant seen outside of the base monster's original habitat was to instill the dread of the idea that something could displace an Elder Dragon. Blackveil Vaal Hazak was conceptualized as a walking fortress. A monster that moves slowly but is always defended on all sides.

They live in tight-nit packs led by an alpha male Blangonga, who the subordinates will follow and obey the commands of diligently. Physiology
The Blango is a small Fanged Beast covered almost entirely in a long coating of thick snow-white fur that serves to block out the cold as well as act as its main form of armor to protect it from damage. This fur is especially prominent around its neck, with two large tufts being present atop its head that grant it the appearance of possessing a mane, hence the nickname of Snow Lion. Its skin is a pale blue, with patches of this skin being visible on the monster's forehead, hands, feet, and belly. The Blango also possesses a hairless face decorated with hard orange ridges above its eyes and mouth, while its cheeks are covered in creased cyan skin.
In order to defend itself, the Blango primarily attacks by digging up snow in its hands, before compacting it and chucking it at targets; it is highly agile and able to move quickly even through deep snow. Moreover, by inhaling the cold air from the mountains and storing it within a specialized organ in its body—where the air is cooled even further—it is capable of expelling a short-ranged breath that instantly freezes upon contact with outside air, allowing it to freeze its prey in place. The breath weapon utilized by the common Blango is notably weaker than that produced by the troop's commander.
Behavior
The Blango lives within large troops in snowy mountain regions, where they are lead by a dominant Blangonga. While a single Blango is typically not much of a threat by itself, it is highly cooperative and almost militant in nature, and will diligently follow the commands given to it by the Blangonga leading the pack. This cooperation is demonstrated through the pack's method of hunting: the Blangonga will order several of its troops to hide underneath the snow near a potential escape point for its prey, with the remainder of the troop joining the commander in chasing the prey towards the established ambush point. Once the prey has arrived, the hidden Blango will leap out of the ground, blocking the escape path for the chosen target and barraging them with a stream of near constant blows, almost guaranteeing the troop will kill the prey. The Blango pack is loyal enough to its commander to, at times, serve as a distraction towards opponents when the Blangonga finds itself in a disadvantageous position, allowing for their leader to retreat and catch its breath.
The Blango is generally a fairly cowardly monster, often being intimidated away from a target if it is making sufficiently loud noise. As well, troops of Blango typically keep their distance from Herbivores, such as the Popo. The roar of the Blangonga seems to stir within the Blango: a strong fighting spirit, exciting it and its brethren enough to go on the offensive. Despite this high degree of coordination, the loyalty of the Blango to its Blangonga is highly conditional, being based on the leader's perceived fitness. The highly-enlarged fangs of the Blangonga are its primary status symbol that indicate its authority within the troop, and if these fangs are to be broken, the Blango will become notably agitated and stop following its former leader's commands.
However, the cooperation of the pack does not extend only to combat, as during the cold season, the Blango is known to hibernate alongside its packmates inside mountain caves. In order to keep each other warm, the troop will typically huddle around the leading Blangonga. The Blango will additionally construct nests during this period to sleep atop, typically consisting of dead and decaying plant matter, such as branches and leaves.

Physiology
The Blangonga is a Fanged Beast distinguished by its coat of long snow-white fur that covers almost its entire body, with patches of cool-blue skin being exposed on its hands, feet, belly and face. This resilient coating of fur acts to insulate the Blangonga from the frigid cold and additionally serves as protection from attacks, being comparable in strength to iron chainmail. While most of the hard fur that covers its body is pointy and needle-like, the fur on the tail is quite soft and pleasant to the touch.
The Blangonga possesses a highly ornate face. The majority of its face is covered in toughened orange ridges, with a pair of sideways facing horns jutting out just above its mouth; the exposed skin from its forehead to the crown of its head is a pale-blue. Just below its eyes the Blangonga sports a pair of cyan cheeks that, when the beast becomes agitated, flush a deep red. Sprouting from its cheeks are a pair of long white whiskers whose tips are colored a deep yellow; these whiskers only sprout on the Blangonga and help to display is authority and might over the rest of its pack. However, the most notable feature of the Blangonga is its large tusk-like canines that protrude out of its mouth considerably due to them being too large to be able to fit inside its mouth. They are as thick as a human thigh, with their sharpness being comparable to that of a knife. These fangs act as the main symbol of the Blangonga's authority and are what allow it to perform its commanding howls. Breaking these tusks will cause the Blangonga to lose the respect of its troops, who will no longer obey its commands.
Like other Fanged Beasts of similar build, the Blangonga primarily walks on the knuckles of its hands. Compared to its subordinates, the Blangonga displays both significantly higher agility and physical strength, enabling it to tear significantly larger chucks of ice out of the ground compared to a standard Blango. The Blangonga may also use its highly muscular forelegs to easily burrow into the snow to ambush its prey from below. Further, the Blangonga is capable of expelling a super-cooled breath from its mouth capable of freezing its opponents in place. This breath is generated through it inhaling the cold mountain air of its home and cooling it down further in its specialized organ, causing it to freeze instantly in the open air. Compared to the standard Blango, the strength of the Blangonga's cold breath is notably greater.
Behavior
Much like the Blango, the Blangonga is exclusively found within mountainous regions covered in snow. The Blangonga lives within a troop consisting of other Blango, where it acts as the troop's leader. During the cold season, the Blangonga and the rest of its pack have been observed huddling together and hibernating in mountain caves to keep each other warm, sleeping atop beds constructed from dead branches and leaves. In order to mark out the territory for both it and the remainder of its troop, the Blangonga will leave behind lumps of its own dung.
The Blangonga's physical strength allows it to maneouver around easily, even within deep snow, with the movements of both it and its troop being compared to those of military soldiers. Befitting this militant-like demeanor, the Blangonga is famous for its usage of highly sophisticated social hunting strategies through its control over its Blango. Firstly, it will order several of its Blango to hide underneath the snow near a potential escape point for its prey. Aided by the remainder of the troop that is not hidden, the Blangonga identifies prey and subsequently chases it towards where its brethren lie in wait, upon which they will subsequently leap out from hiding and block any potential escape as well as pelt them with simultaneous attacks, ensuring that the confused target is almost certainly taken down.
A similiar tactic has additionally been utilized against Hunters, with the emerging Blango serving to both distract their target and overwhelm them with a swarm of attacks to take them down. This can additionally serve the purpose of keeping the opponent of the Blangonga busy while it itself is injured or otherwise disadvantaged, allowing it to more easily catch its breath before returning to the fight. The roar of the dominant Blangonga has the power to rile up the fighting spirit within its pack, encouraging them to take down their target. Both of these strategies, which take advantage of the environment in which it lives, help to demonstrate the high intellect possessed by the Blangonga.
The Blangonga's intelligence has additionally been demonstrated through the observation of it grooming itself once struck by Paintballs, rendering it ineffective. This implies a degree of awareness in the role the scent produced by a paintball plays in a hunter's ability to detect it. As a result, there have been many cases of hunters becoming discouraged and giving up hunting after failing to outsmart the Blangonga. Despite its appearance being far removed from them, it is believed the Blangonga is perhaps the monster closest to humans in terms of behavior due to its sense of responsibility when it comes to the rest of its pack.
Super Biology Information
The Super Biology Book Series collects the thoughts and theories of real scientists that were asked to speak about monsters from the Monster Hunter series. Thus, they are inherently speculative and should be seen as such.
Zoological Author Yuumin Mori notes the adaptations that likely enable the Blangonga’s existence in its cold habitats. He proposes that the Blangonga likely possesses an undercoat beneath its visible fur that allows for greater heat retention. Additionally, the Blangonga might maintain a layer of subcutaneous fat to further brave the cold temperatures. Beyond that, Mori states that one solid approach to determining how the Blangonga has adapted to the cold would be to study related species that live in different environments (such as the Copper Blangonga). Whichever traits those relatives lack were likely serving the purpose of cold climate survival.
On the matter of related species, Mori ponders the differences in intelligence between the Blangonga and the Congalala. As Blango and Blangonga are known to hunt in packs unlike the Conga, this might imply a greater degree of social intelligence. Mori points out an additional piece of evidence - Blangonga has flat teeth aside from its tusks, which is atypical for carnivores. He thus proposes that Blango and Blangonga initially evolved as herbivores and developed meat-eating gradually as a cultural practice. In that regard, this species might be intelligent enough to undergo a similar cognitive evolution as humans. Mori however stresses that one should not underestimate the Congalala either, as its highly decorated body also suggests great social intelligence. To Mori, these two beast species represent two viable paths to higher intellectual abilities in the animal kingdom. As for real life analogues, Mori compares the Blangonga to a chimpanzee, as they too hunt in groups. However, Blangonga seems also quite similar to Baboons, which also structure their society around large alpha males that rule over groups of about ten individuals.

Physiology
As a Deviant, the Bloodbath Diablos broadly resembles the regular Diablos while also displaying several significant differences: it sports greater muscle mass, with its legs in particular being more developed, and its face, horns, frill, torso, wingarms, feet, and tail tip all bear a dark-blue coloration. This eye-catching darker tone is the consequence of the blood and bodily fluids from the Bloodbath Diablos' opponents splattering across its body over the course of many repeatedly fierce battles, in particular across the most frequently used parts to attack, such as the horns and tail. The Bloodbath Diablos' shell has been tempered by the blows of numerous hunters and proudly bears the scars of previous battles. The famed discoloration of the Deviant ebbs off at the tips of the horns, whose pale tone stems from being worn down through repeated battle. Consequently, the horns have hardened significantly and boast remarkable piercing power, having grown sharper after each conflict. While the right horn is unusually large and thick, the left horn consists of three separate horn tips sprouting from a single horn base.
Due to the impressive horns of the Diablos often being a target of hunters during their hunts, there is a rumor with plausible believability that has been circulating among those who have witnessed the Bloodbath Diablos. It claims that a young Diablos had one of its horns broken off by hunters and that its malevolence and desire for vengeance against them manifested in its deformed horns. The horns are markers of the cause behind the Deviant's emergence: after having one of its horns be broken by a hunter in its youth, the memory and trauma of the event drives the individual to harbor intense hatred and a desire for revenge against the whole world, including hunters. Furthermore, alongside its natural talent, this individual would possess the potential to cultivate greater strength and recuperate from losing its horn. It is precisely due to this potential for growth that it would continue to develop to such an extent, garnering its strength from having survived and faced all sorts of life threatening scenarios. After suffering such an injury, the Bloodbath Diablos would have had to rely on its singular remaining horn, causing it to mutate and grow enlarged. Thus, while the left horn has warped into a distorted shape as the Deviant continued to grow, the right horn is now thicker and stronger due to having to compensate for its absence.
When pushed into an enraged state, the Bloodbath Diablos' circulatory system undergoes heightened activity and causes its frill, horns, and wings to become stained blood-red. Due to the Bloodbath Diablos growing completely uncontrollable, this extremely dangerous form is known as its Rampage State. However, should the Deviant be brought to its knees by an opponent, it will manifest one final gasp of ferocious vengeance and push its already powerful body further beyond its limits. In this state of extreme rage, known as its Frenzied Rampage State, blood flow throughout the Bloodbath Diablos' body grows more pronounced and causes its veins to alight with a vivid, pulsating, flame-like pattern across its frill, horns, and wings. This fresh pattern across the horn's surface, coupled with their differing appearance, is why the pair are feared as The Devil's Crown. Evoking the image of a creature burning its life away in a desperate stand, the large volumes of blood circulating during this state of hyperactivity enhances its physical abilities, allowing it to perform sharp charges and quick turns. The source of this superior circulation lies in its organs, which have evolved to outlast opponents during sustained combat and which enable it to maintain a rapid combat readiness.
While the Frenzied Rampage State is characterized by significantly heightened circulation, it is defined just as much by the sudden and rapid increase in body temperature. As the skin's blood vessels become more apparent and appear bright-red, bodily fluids are secreted in an attempt to suppress the extreme rise in body temperature. However, during the intense movements the Bloodbath Diablos performs whilst attacking, this fluid comes into contact with its high-temperature carapace and instantly evaporates. The subsequent rising steam erupts and triggers a scalding explosion that obliterates everything in the Bloodbath Diablos' vicinity.
Behavior
Considered to be a threat on par with the Valstrax, the Bloodbath Diablos is an unimaginably cruel monster that is spoken of in desert legends as having razed armies and besieged entire cities and nations. In the past, this extremely aggressive Deviant has been known to cause the evacuation of entire villages and annihilate even veteran Hunters. It is believed that trauma from its painful life experience catalyzed this Deviant into a violent and destructive disposition. Due to its power and aggression eclipsing even other Deviants, the Bloodbath Diablos has been feared as a "Deviant among Deviants." As well, alongside its aggression that makes it instinctively view hunters as enemies, its tendency to wipe out anything in its path is what earned it the epithet, Bloodbath. Due to the threat the Bloodbath Diablos inherently poses, its appearance is an emergency that may only be dealt with by Wycademy Hunters who possess a Special Permit, as is the case with every other Deviant.

Physiology
The Bnahabra is a small species of Neopteron found in a wide variety of different habitats. Sharing a similar build to the closely related Vespoid, its body is slender with elongated legs and a pair of delicate wings on its back that keep it almost perpetually airborne. The exact patterning and coloration of the Bnahabra's wings is known to vary between regions. They are sharp and difficult to forge, as well as able to slice just as effectively as any well-honed knife. The primary aspect that differentiates it visually from its cousin is the large, boomerang-shaped plating present behind the head. The body of the Bnahabra is exceptionally delicate and very easily destroyed, thus it is typically best for Hunters to utilize poisons to kill the Neopteron if its parts are intended to be harvested.
Much like the Vespoid, the Bnahabra additionally possesses an elongated stinger at the end of its body, formed from a hollow tube. Inside its body is stored a paralytic venom, its main weapon against threats. This venom can be injected into an opponent's body, leaving its victims immobilized. Alongside this venom, it produces a specialized bodily fluid that may be fired from its abdomen to hasten the rate of decomposition of these corpses. This fluid can additionally be fired at opponents to lower their resistances, with the exact properties of this fluid varying between different individuals in different environments.
Behavior
The Bnahabra is a highly territorial monster, relentlessly stinging anything that encroaches upon its turf. It will lay its eggs in the corpses of monsters and utilize the unique quality of its specialized bodily fluid to provide its offspring with a free meal.

The Boaboa (ボワボワ, Bowabowa) is a small Lynian introduced in Monster Hunter World: Iceborne.
Summary
Tribal Lynians that wear masks imitating the look of a Popo and who have made their settlement within the Hinterlands. While they share their cousins' usage of a variety of different ailments, with the colour of their mask's horns denoting their preference, their preferred weapon of choice are hand-crafted hammers and spears. Boaboa are noted for their strong contempt towards the Beotodus, which they frequently hunt for its meat, with a successful hunt being seen as a rite of passage.
Main Series
Monster Hunter World: Iceborne:???
???
Physiology
The Boaboa is a small Lynian covered almost entirely in bright-white fur on their cylindrical body and very stubby limbs. By contrast, their face is hairless, possessing black skin, beady yellow eyes, and gaping teeth. However, the true face of the Boaboa is rarely ever seen due to them primarily wearing a hood and cape constructed out of brown fur to conceal it, with only their eyes being visible through the hood's "mouth". Various smaller teeth are decorated around the hood's upper lip to act as fake teeth, with a pair of tusks being used to give the impression of horns, while two smaller fragments are fashioned into false eyes. The reason why they construct these fur coating is to appear larger and more intimidating than they really are, a desire stemming from their admiration of larger monsters in their environment, such as the Popo. However, the individual arrangement of the horns seems to be nothing more than personal preference. They will never remove this fur coating in the presence of others, even including other members of their tribe, only ever doing so when the individual is bathing.
Behavior
Unlike the Gajalaka, who have tribes all throughout the New World continent, the Boaboa so far only have settlements found within the Hinterlands. One such settlement was found within the southwestern outskirts of the Hoarfrost Reach, with the secret entrance being hidden behind a waterfall leading into a hot spring. They themselves live within a large community and construct their dwellings inside large burrows, with hot spring-containing caverns seeming to be a preferred place where they settle due to the soothing nature which they provide. The hot springs additionally serve as a place where they can wash off any dirt that has accumulated on their fur coating, which they seem to cherish immensely.
The Boaboa are primarily a hunting society who place a strong virtue in an individual's strength and ability to hunt their target. To sustain the tribe, small patrol groups are sent out from the main settlement in order to capture their prey, before bringing it back to their hidden dens. In order to hunt, the Boaboa have been seen wielding a wide variety of weapons, such as fur-covered hammers with spiked tips held together by rope, long wooden spears constructed out of processed bones, and hand-crafted throwable bombs with a patchwork casing made from skin and containing a large amount of flammable materials. The hammers and spears they wield are frequently laced with a wide variety of toxins to further impede their target, with the coloration present on both their false eyes and the tips of their horns demonstrating which type they are proficient with. Purple patterns indicate a health-draining toxin, cyan patterns indicate a sedative toxin, and yellow indicating a paralyzing neurotoxin, while those with orange markings do not appear to wield any ailments whatsoever. During a hunt, the Boaboa follow the commands given to them by their patrol group's leader, with them often launching attacks with their spears in unison after given the command to.
Furthermore, individuals with green markings who appear to be friendlier than the other members of their tribe have been spotted; if one was attempting to befriend such an individual, gifting a handcrafted fur coating would typically suffice. The Boaboa are capable of some degree of communication with humans and, with those who they especially trust, will cooperate alongside them to bring down a shared target; they will even engaging in bartering for specific goods. In contrast to these individuals, the Boaboa who partake in scouting excursions are aggressive towards anyone they deem as an outsider to their territory—be it human or a large monster—and will bravely retaliate against them. Much like the Gajalaka, they are opportunistic about when they strike, being particularly attracted when a potential target is knocked down, or becomes trapped in some way.
Like the other Lynians found throughout the New World, the Boaboa display their own unique cultural practices. In particular, they are shown to hold the Popo in especially high regard due to them serving as the basis of their own survival as both a source of food and materials. They perceive the Herbivore as being under their command, with their involvement in its life varying depending on the situation. While they are frequently seen riding atop a lone Popo in order to move it towards a certain location, it can vary as to whether or not the tribe is trying to guide it back towards the herd it was separated, or is instead taking it back towards their den. By virtue of their respect for the Herbivore, the Boaboa model the characteristic hoods they wear after the beast, and similarly construct their ornamental horns to resemble the Popo's tusks as a symbol of strength. They also appear to have immense respect for another herbivorous monster of the Hinterlands, the Banbaro, who they admire for its dignified and fearless demeanor in battle. The current name used by the Guild for the wyvern was even derived from the native name used by the Boaboa. However, not every monster within the Hinterlands is the subject of their admiration. In particular, the tribe harbors a strong animosity towards the Beotodus due to its perceived behavior of arbitrarily killing the Popo, which are sacred to the tribe. Consequently, the Piscine Wyvern is a common victim of the Boaboa's hunting excursions, with them even being known to utilize the wyvern's primary diet of Popo as a form of bait. Once it has been killed, the tribe has been demonstrated to cook the meat acquired from its carcass before eating it, with them even going so far as to construct pottery in order to preserve the meat for later consumption. Amongst the tribe, successfully hunting a Beotodus is considered to be a test of skill for an upcoming hunter.

The Boltreaver Astalos is a Mutation. It is unlocked by raising Astalos's Ecosystem Rank to S in an area that has the thunder element and at least 3 thunder element monsters.
Physiology
The Boltreaver Astalos closely resembles the Astalos, albeit with a few key physiological differences. This Deviant is generally notably larger than the regular individual and sports visibly enlarged electrical organs. The head crest additionally sports large frontal spines that are absent in the standard variety, with a singular striking horn protruding from the front. The greatest physiological difference, however, is the enhanced functionality of the wyvern's electrical organs, which are altered to allow for a much more potent electrical charge; any who get caught by its potent lightning will vanish on the spot, leaving behind nothing but a shadow. The resulting current further highlights this Deviant's altered body, as the charged limbs turn a brilliant azure color, as opposed to the green charge typically seen in the Astalos.
When its body is fully charged, the Boltreaver Astalos takes on an intense blue glow and becomes capable of performing many incredible feats. From extending its crest into a saber fabricated from pure electricity, to small plasma projectiles, to even electromagnetic singularities that trap enemies, the arsenal of this Deviant is as deep as it is mysterious. Many of the Boltreaver Astalos' abilities are thus considered to be operating beyond the current understanding of science. Furthermore, it has been suggested the electromagnetic properties of the Boltreaver Astalos' modified shells may improve its flight capabilities. Coincidentally, the Boltreaver Astalos is among the few Flying Wyverns that has been observed flying upside down, albeit only for brief periods.
Behavior
Much like the regular Astalos, the Boltreaver Astalos is incredibly aggressive and attacks anything it considers an intruder on sight. Due to the threat the Boltreaver Astalos inherently poses, its appearance is an emergency that may only be dealt with by Wycademy Hunters who possess a Special Permit, as is the case with every other Deviant.

The Bombadgy is a small round monster covered by pale, gray hide decorated with several dark ridges surrounded by a muted-yellow base along its back, it is known for its plump appearance. Physiology
The Brachydios is a large Brute Wyvern exhibiting the typical body shape of its classification; it is a bipedal monster with muscular hind legs and modified forelegs that are held under the torso, and sports a long, heavy tail with a thick hexagonal club at its tip. Its head is adorned with a crest of three pointed protrusions guarding the neck, a maw hidden behind shelled, exoskeletal teeth, a small and sharp nasal horn, and orange eyes. A notable anatomical feature of this Brute Wyvern are the large battering growths on its forehead and wrists, called Pounders. These growths are often tipped with colonies of explosive Slime Mold, a species that lives symbiotically on and in the Brachydios' body.
The armor shell of the Brachydios is smooth and obsidian-blue in color due to the presence of actual obsidian in the shell's composition. Moreover, as a result of being repeatedly heated by ambient volcanic heat and the Slime Mold's explosions, before subsequently cooling back down, the shell of the Brachydios develops in layers across its life in a process that creates increasingly harder overlapping sheets of the carapace with each cycle. As the structure of the shell relies on volcanic heat, a Brachydios that spends its entire life in volcanic regions would display a different shell composition compared to an individual that migrated to other climates after maturing. Yet, even within a Brachydios population comprised of individuals who have all lived in the same environment, each wyvern's coloration would differ slightly based on the precise level of erosion and type of chemical deposits the shell has endured over its life. While the armor shell of the Brachydios is tough all around, it is especially resistant on its Pounders due to the constant exposure to the Slime Mold—shells from these areas are given the name Ebonshell to differentiate them.
The Pounders of the Brachydios are entirely unique amongst monsters. Their peculiar shape develops over the Brachydios' life as they are exposed to the repeated detonations of the Slime Mold. Like with the armor shell, albeit more broadly, this process fuses different minerals and chemicals into the Pounders that make them tougher over time. Perhaps shockingly, the Pounders are not part of the wyvern's skeleton, rather, they develop as an extension of the armor shell itself. A Brachydios Pounder consists of a hard outer layer that shares its composition with the armor shell, as well as a keratinous inner core. These two layers are connected by a porous, lattice structure that serves as the nesting grounds for the symbiotic Slime Mold.
As is the case with most Brute Wyverns, the Brachydios' hind legs are extremely powerful and allow it to move quickly despite its size. Uniquely, the Brachydios can jump quite high into the air, allowing it to leap at enemies in ways that even other monsters in its class cannot match. While the structure of the hind legs is quite typical for a Brute Wyvern, the forelegs of the Brachydios are exceptionally well-developed, sporting high density muscles that allow it to wield its Pounders like battering rams and slug enemies to death. Interestingly, the Brachydios does possess fingers, although, they are folded under its Pounders. Despite their length and sharp claws, the Brachydios' fingers are generally considered to be vestigial. However, individuals in the New World have been observed digging their fingertips into the ground to provide grip whilst pivoting their bodies around during combat.
A Juvenile Brachydios can be easily distinguished from an adult by its softer and more colorful shell. It does not yet possess the hard, obsidian-laced armor at birth, and its initial shell is significantly less resistant before it grows and develops throughout adolescence. Since a juvenile Brachydios' shell has not yet been blackened by explosions and volcanic heat, it is notably more vibrant than the seen in an adult Brachydios.
Materials retrieved from the Brachydios can have various uses, for instance, the bone marrow of the Brute Wyvern is extremely sticky and highly sought after for welding. As well, the Brachydios may also grow valuable gems inside of its body, much like many other wyverns.
Slime Mold Symbiosis
A peculiar trait of the Brachydios species is that it lives in a symbiotic bond with a kind of Slime Mold. This colonial bacteria appears as a viscous, green liquid that is concentrated most notable on the Pounders of the wyvern, living inside and on top of them. The Slime Mold requires three conditions to be able to reproduce: Contact with air, momentum, and physical impact. When these three conditions are met, the Slime Mold is activated into its fruiting state, where it transitions from its usual green color, to yellow, and then to red. A short while after reaching this stage, the affected Slime Mold detonates in a fiery explosion that kills off the exploding parts of the mold. As they die, however, the bacteria release large clusters of germ cells, scattering them around such that they land on other surfaces where they can immediately begin growing into a new mold colony. Growing on the Pounders of the Brachydios is thus a reliable way to regularly fulfill the three conditions for reproduction, as the wyvern often swings its Pounders around while in combat.
In exchange for aiding with its reproduction, the Slime Mold grants the Brachydios the destructive power of its explosions, enhancing the physical attacks of the Brute Wyvern with the resulting detonations. The Brachydios can also choose to leave fruiting slime clusters on other surfaces to serve as traps for its enemies—including even covering said enemies in the Slime Mold and letting it explode whilst on their skin. The Slime Mold can even be used as an adhesive, allowing the Brachydios to haul its body weight up the steepest rock faces despite lacking articulated forelimbs, achieved through punching rapidly up the cliffside. This symbiosis even confers a degree of control onto the Brachydios; through the process of co-evolution, the Brachydios produces a chemical compound from the tip of its tongue that can serve as nourishment for the Slime Mold and which stains the pink flesh with vibrant green. Thus, when the wyvern decides that it needs more slime, it can lick its Pounders to promote growth in the Slime Mold at command. In higher quantities, this compound can also artificially induce the fruiting stage in Slime Mold.
The Brachydios can take this control even further once it grows enraged, as when the wyvern's body temperature spikes, the nourishing chemical in its saliva begins to evaporate and is exhaled through the Brachydios' mouth. This vapor envelops the body and stimulates the Slime Mold to grow rapidly and spread across the entire body of the Brachydios, whilst also entering its agitated fruiting state and turning yellow. During this state, the Slime Mold explodes more rapidly and violently.
The Slime Mold appears to be instinctively attracted towards bonding with the Brachydios, as scattered germ cells will grow unusually quickly if they come into contact with such a host, as well as migrate into the Pounders just as rapidly. Once bonded, the Slime Mold cannot be entirely removed from the Brachydios, although small clusters of it can be washed off through exposure to water. While it is often referred to as a single species, the characteristic mucus of the Slime Mold is actually an amalgam of different bacteria, some of which are considered harmful to humans.
Behavior
The Brachydios is a solitary creature that primarily inhabits volcanic regions. More specifically, the Brachydios spends its youth near volcanoes in order to properly develop its armor shell. Once this stage has been reached it will migrate away, although some individuals may choose to stay in volcanic zones—it is unknown what exactly determines this behavior. Besides volcanic regions, the Brachydios is often sighted in arctic tundras.
Being a highly aggressive carnivore, the Brachydios relentlessly hunts down prey using its many powerful weapons. The Brachydios has been known to ambush the Uroktor, using quick repositioning to scare them into the Slime Mold puddles created by its punches. The destructive power of its explosive slime mold allows the Brachydios to prey upon dangerous monsters, such as the Uragaan or Agnaktor, blasting through their armor of cooled lava and inflicting grave injuries that allow it to overpower them with its brute strength. By cleverly weaving around its adversaries whilst preparing and unleashing powerful explosions, the Brachydios can dominate other monsters even in prolonged combat. Its collaboration with the Slime Mold allows for truly incredible maneuvers, such as digging the head Pounder into the ground to spread primed mold unconventionally through the earth, before promptly detonating it across a large area with next to no warning.
While being largely solitary, the Brachydios does occasionally encounter other members of its species, although this is usually prevented through territorial markings made by leaving behind distinctive slime residues at key locations. Should a meeting occur in spite of this, the size of the Brachydios' pseudo-fangs, the girth of its Pounders, and the vibrance of its Slime Mold are used to determine and enforce a social hierarchy. This primarily comes into play during the mating season, a time where the male and female Brachydios will congregate in large groups, and the males are ranked based on their physical characteristics alongside the quality and density of their Slime Mold. The highest ranked male gains mating rights, whereas the lower ranked individuals must choose to either mate in secret, or challenge their superiors in a test of strength. The ferocity of this competition forces the male Brachydios to constantly improve its Slime Mold and seek out more of it, which may occasionally lead to the emergence of a Raging Brachydios in rare circumstances.
Once mating has occurred and a new generation has been sired, the juvenile Brachydios will remain with its parents, however, this is not a close or warm bond. The Brachydios' parents do nothing to actively parent their young or protect them from harm, instead merely tolerating their presence within their territory until the child is grown. The only inheritance a juvenile Brachydios receives from its parents is the Slime Mold, which it acquires from them shortly after birth. This gift does not come without dangers, however, as depending on the exact qualities and shape of the juvenile's shell, it may not be able to withstand the explosions caused by its own slime and perish unfortunately soon after birth. As a result, the Brachydios has a high rate of infant mortality, and only the strongest individuals that master the Slime Mold survive into adulthood.

Monster Hunter 3 Ultimate
Brachydios was created by Yuya Tokuda. The production of Monster Hunter 3 had focused on three groups of monsters: Flying Wyverns, Leviathans and Brute Wyverns. During the early planning stages of Monster Hunter 3 Ultimate, the development team noticed that while both Flying Wyverns and Leviathans had received a Flagship Monster - Rathalos and Lagiacrus respectively - the Brute Wyvern class still lacked one such representative. It was thus decided that the Flagship Monster of Monster Hunter 3 Ultimate would be a Brute Wyvern.
When thinking about how to create Brute Wyvern that could stand out enough to be a proper flagship, Tokuda believed that it would be interesting to create a Brute Wyvern that primarily uses its forelegs to attack, in contrast to the vestigial forearms of Barroth and Deviljho. Together with the Brute Wyvern skeleton's highly developed hind legs, this idea resulted in the concept of a Brute Wyvern that uses swift footwork to reposition and outmaneuver the player, with its forelegs being the main weapon. With the help of Kaname Fujioka, Tokuda created a prototype brute wyvern concept that would run around the arena and use its hooked, highly articulate hands to grab onto walls mid-charge to change directions rapidly, allowing it to fling itself around the map with extreme speed. But even before this idea could be turned into a playable test monster, it was scrapped - both Tokuda and Fujioka agreed that it would feel boring to just have another monster whose main attack strategy was simply charging at the player.
Following the rejection of the first concept, Tokuda and Fujioka landed on the idea of the monster punching the player instead. With skilled footwork, this concept monster would circle around players and deliver devastating blows with its well-developed fists. This approach seemed more promising, and a very quick test monster was created. Visually, it was a simple dark colored brute wyvern with no distinct features - the only visual design choice at this point was to have its body be black or dark blue, to contrast with the intended volcanic habitat of the monster. While testing this prototype, Tokuda wondered if the fight would be more interesting if the monster could somehow restrict the player's movement and thus further emphasize its own agility. Eventually, this led to the concept of the wyvern laying mines around the area to threaten players that moved carelessly. Tokuda then researched ways to have this ability tie into the monster's ecology, eventually creating the idea of an explosve slime mold. Through these additions, the prototype punching wyvern became Brachydios.
Once the Brachydios' design and combat idea were set, the team created the first fully playable test version of the monster. Tokuda advised them to ignore hardware limitations and game balance for the moment and simply push the monster's slime production and aggression to the absolute maximum. The resulting hunt was completely impossible to beat, and the team then worked backwards by gradually removing and weakening the monster's most problematic moves. Both Tokuda and Fujioka insisted however that Brachydios should not be weakened too much, as they wanted it to be "the strongest Flagship Monster ever made".
Monster Hunter 4
Brachydios' inclusion in Monster Hunter 4 mostly revolved around implementing feedback received after the release of Monster Hunter 3 Ultimate. This included removing or changing attack patterns that had proven to be nearly unavoidable in the previous game.

Physiology
A notably hostile Subspecies of the Tigrex, the Brute Tigrex is known for its fierce disposition and incredible physical prowess. It bears a distinct blackened hide with orange stripes along its back, forelimbs, and tail. The shade of black may vary between individuals depending on their environment; at birth, the Brute Tigrex's shell is gray and will darken over time. Alongside aiding it with camouflaging in volcanic regions, the dark coloration absorbs sunlight to help maintain the Brute Tigrex's body temperature.
The composition of the Brute Tigrex's carapace contains volcanic ash and powdery minerals that has adhered to the body's surface due to the intense heat of the volcanic environment it inhabits. This compositional change is repeated intermittently during its growth and results in the shell's dark coloration, high viscosity, and increased robustness. Additionally, sturdy plating surrounds the spinal cord to provide support whenever the monster charges. Observable from a cross-section of the shell are rings that mark the cycle of melting and solidification, the continued layering of volcanic materials has rendered the shell incredibly heat-resistant as well. It is said the Brute Tigrex can come into contact with magma for a short period of time without suffering damage to its internal organs. Due to foreign matter occasionally adhering to the shell, it exhibits poor conductivity and is prone to becoming brittle when exposed to moisture. The nature of the carapace makes it difficult to forge, however, it is valuable due to its ability to withstand violence.
In comparison to the type species, the Brute Tigrex has a stronger cardiopulmonary system and an increased metabolism as a result. Its body requires a significant amount of energy to maintain, and it is thought to be less energy efficient than the Tigrex. Furthermore, it is difficult for the Brute Tigrex to maintain its body temperature in cold areas due to how much energy its body uses—it is cold-blooded and thus relies heavily on ambient warmth to help maintain its body temperature. However, this strengthened cardiopulmonary system is what allows the Brute Tigrex to produce a frighteningly powerful roar. This roar is produced by inhaling and compressing a large amount of oxygen within the lungs, which is then released all at once. The monster's strong vocal cords amplify the sound, creating a powerful shockwave that can blow anything away; it is also able to adjust the trajectory and size of the shockwaves produced by its roar. The Brute Tigrex's respiratory organs are collectively referred to as the Great Screamer Sac, which encompasses its lungs, airways, vocal cords, and diaphragm. These organs are prone to necrosis, and extracting them in a complete state is exceptionally rare.
The Brute Tigrex's enhanced cardiopulmonary function additionally grants comparatively superior physical strength to the Subspecies. Its claws are powerful enough to shred both flesh and bone, and it is capable of crushing stone and iron with its jaws.
Behavior
The Brute Tigrex is notably more aggressive than the base species, which is thought to be a result of its heightened metabolism. Consequently, it requires a large amount of energy to function, forcing it to constantly search for food. It is an obligate carnivore and employs a similar hunting technique to the Tigrex, although with some notable differences. The Brute Tigrex makes use of varied movements, ensuring its prey will be unable to predict its next move. Using its keen sense of smell, the Brute Tigrex will sometimes track down and attempt to snatch prey already captured by other predators.
The Brute Tigrex has a limited habitat range in comparison to the regular Tigrex and is found only in hot climates, such as volcanoes and deserts. By living in warm regions, the Brute Tigrex negates the need to expend additional energy maintaining its body temperature, allowing it to display its full physical capabilities. In the New World, the Brute Tigrex lives in the Elder's Recess and the Vale region of the Guiding Lands. It is unknown why the wyvern is drawn to the Vale region specifically, although there do exist theories. It is speculated the abundance of food is what draws it there, which—in combination with the miasma—it may use to build up its shell in the absence of heat.

Physiology
The Bulldrome is the dominant male of a herd of Bullfango and is largely similar in appearance, being a quadrupedal beast with a huge pair of tusks, although he is notably larger in his overall size. While most of his body is similarly covered in brown fur, the hair that was previously silver or black has been replaced by even longer white hairs on both cheeks that also run down the back like a mohawk. The skin of the Bulldrome is notably tough and unblemished, a fact likely attributed to the fact his hide is too tough to be scratched through regular means.
A notable feature of the Bulldrome is his asymmetrically curved tusks, with one growing to be much longer than the other; which tusk is longer differs between individuals and is behaviorally determined. Each Bullfango has one tusk it prefers to use when digging up soil and looking for food, resulting in that particular foraging tusk being ground down through use and becoming shorter. While this difference is hardly noticeable in the Bullfango, it is much more pronounced in the Bulldrome. Whichever tusk the Bulldrome does not prefer for foraging is instead used for intimidation to indicate his individual strength, or in combat against other members of his species that could challenge his dominance; these fights result in the tusk growing harder and more scarred over time. This tusk can even grow and develop to be comparable to the horn of the Diablos.
Behavior
Much like his smaller counterpart, the Bulldrome can inhabit a wide variety of different habitats. He is known to lead herds of Bullfango, and has earned the nickname of Great Boar by virtue of possessing the greatest strength and the highest vitality amongst them. In return for him gaining a monopoly on mating with the females within the herd, he is responsible for protecting the remainder from any potential predators, with him typically leading any aggressive charge against intruders. However, the beast is known to occasionally abuse his position of power, muscling the smaller Bullfango out of their feeding spots in order to forcefully take the food for himself instead.
In order to determine which member of the herd is in charge and gains access to breeding rights, large male Bullfango will engage in competitions that involve using their impressive tusks to butt heads with each other, with the winner of these fights gaining the privilege of leading the herd.

Physiology
The Bullfango is a small Fanged Beast with a short, squat body covered primarily in a dense coating of tough and bristly brown fur. The fur around its face is a deep-silver, and it possesses a mohawk of black fur along its back alongside three pairs of off-white bumps of skin. Easily its most recognizable feature is the large pair of tusks protruding from its top jaw, with a large nose present at the end of its snout and each of its feet ending with a pair of hooves.
Behavior
The Bullfango is known to inhabit a wide variety of habitats, from frigid mountains to humid marshlands. While it typically lives within large herds led by a dominant male Bulldrome, there have been plenty of instances of individuals instead choosing to live a solitary life. Unlike the closely related Mosswine, this beast possesses a foul temperament with a strong instinct to protect its territory. If something unknown crosses into the Bullfango's field of vision, unable to tell if it is friend or foe, it will instinctively react by immediately charging down whatever it is it has detected; these charges are powerful enough to send any human flying from the force of the impact. This behavior can even extend to other members of its own herd, who the beast will pursue just as aggressively if it does not recognize them. While a single Bullfango is typically not much of a threat by itself, an entire heard charging down a potential target can quickly become overwhelming, so it is generally cautioned by the Guild to avoid engaging with the beast unless it is absolutely necessary.
In order to determine the leader of the herd, the largest Bullfango males will engage each other by repeatedly butting heads with one another—utilizing their tusks in the process—with the strongest individual being crowned the new leader of the herd. Despite the species' overall high levels of fertility, female Bullfango will only ever mate with the herd's dominant male.
While it is omnivorous, it primarily prefers to feed upon plants. The Bullfango is itself frequently hunted by humans for its meat, which is beloved by many people, in large part due to its unique flavor.

The Ocean Dragon Ceadeus (ナバルデウス, Nabarudeusu) is an Elder Dragon introduced in Monster Hunter 3.
Summary
Titanic deep-sea Elder Dragons who have only recently been discovered to exist. Ceadeus are identifiable by their impressive beard and oversized horn, which grows endlessly throughout their lives, to the point where they can even partially cover one of their eyes. These legendary sea dragons are known to scrape their horns along the sea bed as a way of wearing them down, often causing powerful and devastating quakes as a result.

Physiology
The Ceadeus is a large marine Elder Dragon adorned with silvery-white scales, earning it titles such as the "Crescent Moon Suspended in the Sea", and other names pertaining to the moon. It has a long, slender body fully built for life underwater, possessing two front limbs in the form of flippers and a fluke-like tail to help maneauver around. The Ceadeus has a large beard of fur that extends from its bottom jaw to right above its flippers. Despite being called fur, it is said to be quite hard, enough to be used when crafting weapons. One of the most prominent features are the twin curved horns sprouting from its head; when cut open, the horns can be found bearing countless rings akin to a tree, which are theorized to serve the same function and allude to the age of an individual Ceadeus. Another notable feature are the several Luminous Organs that line the Elder Dragon's underside, from the hood behind its head, to halfway down its abdomen. It is theorized that these organs are used to either help it search for prey, or communicate with others of its kind. Much of what is known about the Ceadeus is scarce due to there being very few sightings of the Elder Dragon. While it is believed it breathes through lungs, it is also thought it can hold its breath for several days before needing to resurface.
Behavior
As with its physiology, much of what is known about the Ceadeus' behavior is scarce. However, from the few interactions the Guild has had, it can be determined to be rather passive. When fought, the Ceadeus ignores attacking Hunters, only occasionally thrashing defensively. Only when it has been injured enough, or once cornered, will Ceadeus lash out against its aggressors. In which case, it will use its own bulk to slam into foes, fire jets of water from afar, or even ram its horns into them. The Elder Dragon's timid nature was documented in an expedition from the Scriveners when searching for the marine Elder Dragon, having one surface near their vessel. Even when getting close, the Ceadeus made no acknowledgement of them and continued its travel. Amongst locals, passed down legends have spoken of its temperament, to the degree that it has been revered as a God amongst them. In some legends, its passive nature has turned it into a symbol of bountiful catching, blessing people with plenty of fish whenever it arrives. However, others have made note of the extents of its rage, bringing forth earthquakes and tsunamis that can wipe out whole villages.
