Physiology
The Ceantaur is a small juvenile Carapaceon species that is both related to and resembles the Hermitaur, sharing a similar general build: four legs for locomotion, black eyes suspended on stalks, a long pair of antennae, and two limbs adapted into sharp grasping pincers. The Ceanataur uses these pincers to attack, although they are significantly smaller and less serrated than in adult individuals. Also like the Hermitaur, it uses an externally gathered organic shell to armor its soft backside, with these shells often sporting a notably darker coloration. The most notable difference between the two is their coloration, with the Ceanataur sporting a bright-blue carapace covered in pale-white stripes. Its body is also notably more angular and pointed than its Hermitaur cousin's.
The juvenile Ceanataur possesses a poison gland within its body, allowing it to spray out small globs of poison to deter threats. However, when it matures into its adult stage—the Shogun Ceanataur—this gland is slowly atrophied. On rare occasions, the Ceanataur may be born lacking a poison gland altogether, forcing it to rely entirely on its claws in order to survive and consequently develop unusually.
Behavior
The Ceanataur is primarily found within both marshlands and volcanoes. This appears to be the case due to the species having a high resistance to heat, yet little to none to the cold—both juvenile and adult individuals spend time in these areas as the ground temperature is maintained at a near constant. This behavior is in direct contrast to the Hermitaur, with the difference thus being believed to be the reason behind the two Carapaceons' differing habitat preferences. Within these habitats, the Ceanataur has a preference for remaining inside dark places, such as caves. However, the fact it can be found outside of them indicates a strong degree of adaptability.
The Ceanataur hunts in a near identical way to the Hermitaur: hiding underground and resurfacing only when something passes above it, upon which it will attack with its claws and poisonous discharge. Its diet is highly varied, with it feasting on insects as well as scavenging on the carcass of other monsters.

Physiology
The Cephadrome is an intraspecies variation of the Cephalos and a desert-dwelling Piscine Wyvern. It can be distinguished from its subordinates by its larger stature and darkened hide, and is said to have a lifespan twice as long as the Cephalos. A Cephadrome emerges when a Cephalos distinguishes itself as the largest and strongest member of its pack. Once this social status is achieved, the individual's body secretes a special hormone that kickstarts the transformation into a Cephadrome; it is believed this process is meant to solidify that individual's command over the pack and prevent repeated in-fighting.
The Cephadrome is a desert specialist with a body evolved specifically for swimming through sand; its flattened skull allows it to push through and displace fine sand around its smooth body, allowing it to traverse across sand with ease. Its large pectoral fins and caudal fin further aid it in this regard. The hide of the Cephadrome features a blackened dorsal coloration with a pale underbelly; although its scales are naturally blue and retain moisture, it will occasionally develop a vivid purple scale. Over time, sand adheres to the scales and dulls their blue coloration, giving the Cephadrome its sand-colored hide. Due to the scales being moisture-absorbent, they have a strange texture that Hunters like. The Cephadrome has six ray-fins: two long pectoral fins, a fanned dorsal fin, a large caudal fin, an adipose fin, and an additional small fin on the ventral side of its tail. These fins secrete a paralytic toxin and are very sharp.
The Cephadrome's eyes are located on the topside of its flat skull. Due to its sand-dwelling lifestyle, the Cephadrome has extremely poor eyesight and relies almost entirely on its sensitive hearing to find prey. It is able to detect the movement of prey by listening for footsteps from beneath the surface of the sand, where it then ambushes them from beneath their feet. The Cephadrome's excellent hearing subsequently makes it sensitive to sudden loud noises, causing it to jump out of the sand from shock. Located on the underside of its skull, the Cephadrome's mouth contains a row of sharp jagged teeth strong enough to bite through the hide of a Carapaceon. While sand often gets in the Piscine Wyvern's mouth as it swims through it, the Cephadrome can use this sand as a way to attack prey and ward off predators. The sand that gets inhaled is clumped together using its saliva, where it can then be spat out at enemies. However, the sand may sometimes be swallowed, in which case it is sent to a specialized bladder organ that absorbs nutrients, such as iron; the leftover sand can then be regurgitated in clumps.
Behavior
The Cephadrome leads large groups of Cephalos and is the only known Piscine Wyvern to live in a group. It spends most of its life living beneath the sand, emerging occasionally for air, and only becomes active at night. Although the Cephadrome appears to have a larger habitat range than the Cephalos, it is often seen hunting alongside them and naturally assuming a leader position. The Cephadrome leading a pack positions itself in the front when hunting and is the first to eat as a result. When the Cephadrome makes a kill, it will drag its prey underneath the sand to eat. Only the Cephadrome is allowed to reproduce within the pack.
Monster Hunter
During the production of Monster Hunter, a peculiar bug caused the armor sets of Plesioth and Cephadrome to be switched around, with the former's materials being needed for the latter's armor recipe and vice versa. While this was a mistake, the development team thought that it was interesting and that this would likely surprise players. Thus, they left the two armors switched.

Physiology
The Cephalos is a Piscine Wyvern sporting the typical body plan for its class, with it usually being covered by the large amounts of sand that has adhered to its surface and which turns its body a light tan, concealing the brilliant and natural blue color of its scales underneath. This blue coloration is believed to be derived from the large amounts of moisture retained inside of them, granting the scales a bizarre texture. On occasion, these thick scales may also take on a desirable and vivid purple hue. The jaws of the Cephalos are known for their rows of jagged and razor-like teeth, which are designed to sink deep into prey, with the strongest and sharpest of these fangs able to easily crush through a Carapaceon's shell. These fangs are additionally capable of delivering a neurotoxic venom able to easily immobilize its prey.
The Cephalos sports a pair of forelimbs modified into giant orange fins. It additionally sprouts a dorsal fin above its hips as well as three fins along its tail: a small dorsal fin at the tail's midpoint, a small anal fin near the tail's tip, and a final larger caudal fin positioned at the end. Unlike those of the Cephadrome, which also act as a store for its paralytic venom, the wyvern's fins are not venomous and do not secrete any toxic agent, although they are very sharp, with the sharpness of these fins being known to vary significantly between individuals. Like the scales, some fins may become discolored and instead display a faint, cute, pink coloration.
The Cephalos is a wyvern capable of a rare ability that few wyverns are capable of replicating: the ability to swim through fine sand as if it were a liquid. While originally having believed to have been adapted for an aquatic lifestyle, in order to have acquired this trait, its body has evolved to be rather unusually shaped. The specialized shape of its broad and flat head allows it to displace heavy sand and burrow beneath it with ease, while the smooth and flowing contours of its body allows for ease of traversal, allowing it to move through the deserts it inhabits as if swimming. However, as it is unable to breathe whilst swimming in the sand, it must regularly surface onto land to acquire fresh air. As a trade-off, the effects of this lifestyle have caused its eyesight to deteriorate, rendering it effectively blind, yet this has forced another of its senses to heighten in acuity. The Cephalos' hearing is highly developed and it is entirely reliant on detecting sound to navigate and hunt, able to pick up on the footsteps and even breathing of its prey from below the sand's surface before emerging for an attack. However, this acute hearing has its drawbacks. Any loud noises made while it is swimming—such as the roars of the Diablos, or a forceful strike to the ground—are transmitted directly to its ears, with the sheer shock of its hearing being stimulated to this extent causing it to leap out of the sand, forcing it out of hiding.
As the Cephalos swims through the sand, it will inevitably accidentally swallow large quantities of sand, which accumulates in both its lungs and its stomach. This swallowed sand is sent to a specialized organ inside of its body known as a Sand Sac, in which useful nutrients such as iron can be absorbed from the sand before it is forcefully expelled from the body. This adaptation is able to be weaponized against threats: by solidifying the sand using a mucus secreted from its palate, the Cephalos is able to spit out the sand as a projectile clump with considerable power.
Behavior
Found exclusively in deserts and known as the Sand Wyvern, the Cephalos is unusual amongst Piscine Wyverns for living in large groups led by a larger individual, known as a Cephadrome. Although it seldom surfaces as it swims, it appears to become particularly active during the night and may be sighted alongside countless other Cephalos swimming and leaping out of the moonlit sands during these cold nights. Once it detects prey by utilizing its keen sense of hearing, it and its pack will swim around their target and gradually wear them down by leaping at or spitting sand at them, finishing by dragging the target into the ground below, where it will be devoured. These attacks are coordinated by the leading Cephadrome and, as compensation for this, it is allowed to eat before the rest of the pack.
The leader of the pack is determined by who is the physically largest member, with these individuals secreting a specialized hormone internally that transforms them into a Cephadrome; only these individuals possess the right to reproduce. A female Cephalos lays her eggs during the rainy season, as that is the time where the amount of water within the desert is at its highest, with her specifically laying them inside of an oasis. The eggs will only proceed to hatch once the dry season begins, although the parent Cephalos play no part in raising their young. The juveniles will begin to practice their swimming abilities in the muddy sand near these oasis, before moving into true desert sand once they hit maturity.

Physiology
The Ceratonoth is an armored Herbivore that roams in large herds. Broad tan scales cover the dorsal and lateral sides of the body, getting larger as they go from the head to the end of the tail. The tail is at least as long as the rest of the body, with the scales that hang down the tail being similar in appearance to roof shingles, making it broader than the torso. The Ceratonoth is quadrupedal and stands on four stout legs, each foot sporting five short toes with small claws. The skull is long and narrow, with the snout ending in a blunt beak. The eyes reflect a yellowish-orange light when in the dark.
The Ceratonoth displays noticeable sexual dimorphism: the male is larger than the female and duller in color. While the most obvious feature is the three huge spikes that protrude from the male's back, more subtle differences between the two include the male’s longer legs and snout, shorter tail, and more pronounced scales on his elbows. On rare occasions, a male Ceratonoth can be black in color instead of tan. The male Ceratonoth is specially adapted to face the dangers of the Sandtide due to his dorsal spikes attracting and absorbing lightning strikes. With the male absorbing lightning strikes, every monster in his immediate vicinity is safe from them, hereby protecting his harem of females.
Behavior
To provide protection, the Ceratonoth has adapted to live in herds, which is usually in the form of several females led by a single male, although multiple herds may come together when grazing. A herd will concentrate near water sources that support open plains of grass, where its members spend much of the day grazing.
The behavior of the Ceratonoth changes during the Sandtide, leading to the herd fleeing into a more secluded location, such as caves and canyons. The herd is so panicked during these stampedes that its members will squeeze through tight spaces and run past predatory monsters. If the herd runs past cliffs, some females may be pushed over the edge and even fall to their deaths. Whether they flee or stay put, the females will gather around the male and lie down with their tail curled to the side, leaving only their armored backs exposed. The male will stand in the center, protecting the herd from lightning strikes. The herd is vulnerable to predators while in this formation as they will not flee until a few of them have perished, with common predators including the Bulaqchi, Talioth, Doshaguma, and Rey Dau. When the Sandtide is not occurring, the Ceratonoth will simply flee from threats as a herd.

Physiology
Although its general morphology matches that of typical Elder Dragons—such as the Kushala Daora or Teostra —the Chameleos is peculiar even amongst its peers, and is adorned all over by several unusual features. Protruding outwards from its flat hooded head is a singular sharp horn that gives off a faint-white glow; this remarkably hard horn is a highly valued commodity for its interior decorating capabilities and general ease of use. The Chameleos' deep-purple hide possesses a very strange texture that calms the soul of those who touch its captivating surface, and its wings bear an odd shape unseen in other monsters. The discolored membrane of the Chameleos' wings are incredibly durable despite their thin and light structure, much like the rest of the Elder Dragon's surface. Despite its strength, however, this invaluable material's primary quality is the odd texture it shares with the hide. Additionally, the feet possess bizarre toes resembling a Gekko's that end in small and sharp, curved claws which are beloved by smiths for their ease of use; their strength and sharpness makes each curved claw an exceptional weapon. The Chameleos uses these toes to provide plentiful grip and adhesiveness as it climbs walls.
The Chameleos' ovular head sits atop a long, upright neck, from each side of its hood extend five small and curved spikes that subtly emit a pale glow reminiscent of the nasal horn's very own. Nestled into the head are a pair of huge, green-toned eyeballs that are shielded by large, purple eyelids decorated with luminous rings. Unlike any other monster, the Chameleos possesses the unique and unusual ability to move each eye independently of one another and freely rotate them in any direction, allowing it to watch the sky and earth in unison to quickly lock onto an object's position. Hidden within the jaws is the Elder Dragon's long and dexterous, sticky tongue that can be quickly flung out and reeled back in to easily snatch up insects, small animals, scrape off dirt and debris from its back, or lick up mushrooms and various ores.
Stretching nearly as long as its body, the tough, distinctive tail of the Chameleos is unmistakeable in its unique shape; deriving out of its unusually wide base—from which hang eight small and glowing, pale coils—it suddenly narrows and coils into itself. Due to its bizarre texture in particular, the Elder Dragon's hardened tail makes for an excellent crafting material. The Chameleos is able to make use of the odd appendage to batter opponents by striking the ground with enough force to shatter rock, or by fanning it to generate small gusts of wind to push them away. Other times, the Chameleos may be sighted using its tail to rustle patches of tall grass and disturb small insects into flight, who it will then feed upon by catching them with its tongue. Furthermore, the coiled section of the tail serves as an additional sensory organ for the Chameleos by mimicking the function of the cochlea, an aural organ that resides in the inner ear of certain creatures. This auditory organ is used by the Chameleos to check for threats from behind, and when paired with its wide field of vision, it is said the Elder Dragon possesses no blind spots.
The Chameleos' mastery over a variety of lethal poisons and toxins is unmatched, as even the Rathalos —which itself possesses a strong resistance to poisons—will instantly succumb to the effects of those spewed by the Elder Dragon. The Chameleos produces its deep-purple poisons by mixing ingested substances with bodily fluids that it then spews in the form of clumped globules, or a mist that disperses once expelled. The latter is only possible due to a specialized organ within the body that vaporizes the liquid poison into a gas using ultrasonic vibrations. By fanning them towards and away from itself using its wings and tail, the Chameleos is able to freely manipulate the positions of the poison clouds it leaves lingering throughout an area.
Amongst the various toxins spat by the Chameleos, one in particular stands out for its ability to shut down the body. Taking on a pale-yellow hue, this slimy liquid enters the target's body upon contact and combines with natural sugars to transform into lactic acid and cause severe fatigue. Alongside causing a person's entire body to go limp with a mere touch, the liquid shuts down the victim's ability to vocalize and call for aid by paralyzing the vocal cords. These effects are thought to be caused by a special gas emitted from the liquid, however, the precise nature of this gas remains under investigation. Another diet dependant toxin spat in concentrated globules bears a similar appearance to the exhaustion inducing poison, although its effect is corrosive and dissolves through the defenses of targets. However, as the toxins the Chameleos produces vary greatly depending on what food it has consumed, it is believed the Elder Dragon's abilities may differ widely depending on its habitat as a result. Thus, it is assumed for this reason that the Chameleos has not been seen utilizing certain abilities in recent times, such as the stamina draining toxin as well as vocal cord paralysis. Due to its ability to both generate and make use of a variety of neurotoxins, the Chameleos boasts an assured degree of resistance against other ailments, such as paralytic agents.
Within the Chameleos' body may form a rare gemstone that exhibits a stunning, multi-colored glow. Further, despite its numerous odd facets, the Chameleos has a notably close relation to the Abyssal Dragon, Namielle.
Invisibility
Existing initially only as a rumor due to its particularly rare sightings, the Chameleos is claimed to be able to suddenly disappear into thin air. Through these rumors, there exists a legend that claims the Chameleos would vanish those who incur its wrath without a trace, with some adults even making use of the folklore surrounding the Elder Dragon to scare unruly children into behaving, lest they be stolen away by the mist. Similarly, the village of Kamura would bestow it the title of Ancient Phantom, considering it a divine, invisible guardian of the Shrine Ruins that would confront interlopers and thieves. The Chameleos' ability to vanish would remain poorly understood prior to having been thoroughly researched, partially due to a few details that left scholars with several questions. It was noticed that whilst concealing itself, the Chameleos' tongue would remain visible as it extends out, making scholars wonder if its ability only affected the outer surface of its body. After having observed that the tail was the last part of the Elder Dragon to come into view, a separate theory—at the time lacking evidence—suggested the tail may act as a reservoir for bodily fluids that alter the Elder Dragon's skin. Many of the breakthroughs in understanding how the Chameleos' semivisibility functioned were discovered by an amateur apprentice of the Scriveners, the very same who had been the first to capture and test a vial of the Elder Dragon's fatigue inducing poison for study.
Upon obtaining a sample of the Chameleos' skin, she began experimenting by exposing it to various elements to no avail, notably by holding open flames to its surface and dousing it in water. It would not be until some time after that she would finally be graced with a reaction; after accidentally dropping a Thunder Sac atop its surface, the apprentice noted the way the skin completely altered its color and began to change its texture. Thus, it was proposed the Chameleos may have a Thunder Sac, or a specific system in its body it uses to circulate weak electrical currents through bodily fluids across its body to alter its color and conceal itself. To blend into the background of its environment, the Chameleos is able to change the color of its skin by running a faint electrical current across its surface, this ability appears to stem from its diet containing a wide variety of minerals and ores, such as Dragonite Ore and Meldspar Ore, amongst many others. Most notably, this includes Fucium Ore, which was discovered to be contained within the Chameleos' body. The metallic component within the ore—responsible for binding materials together—combines with the Elder Dragon's Blood and is believed to alter its flow throughout the body and consequently change the color of the Chameleos' skin.
To further enhance its ability to blend with its environment, the Chameleos will exhale a pale mist from its mouth that layers the surrounding area in a dense fog. Able to refract light, this mist contains trace amounts of a potent neurotoxin that confuses those who inhale it and distorts one's ability to see the Chameleos, causing intense hallucinations and a sense of "not being present." By making use of the electrical current running through its skin, the Chameleos is able to refract light when it is enveloped in this fog to near completely conceal itself. Perhaps the most vital instrument of the Chameleos, its horn refracts light around it and contains an organ responsible for its ability to disappear. The act of suddenly vanishing is performed by quick spinal reflexes, and as the Chameleos is shrouded by the mist, its crest spikes, tail coils, and large rostral horn all glow a bright purple. When fully veiled, the Chameleos appears as no more than a faint haze mired by its hallucinogenic mist. To combat this, Hunters have learnt that sufficiently damaging the horn renders the Elder Dragon unable to vanish from sight; severing the tail appears to have a similar effect. While the mechanisms behind this fantastical ability are understood after thorough research, it remains unknown why the Chameleos possesses such an ability.
Behavior
The Chameleos is an Elder Dragon species that has long been known to exist, however, sightings of it are extremely sparse and rare due to its famed vanishing ability. Known as the Mist Dragon, the plentiful legends and tales of its ability to suddenly vanish into the environment like a chameleon earnt it the name, Chameleos. It is a mysterious Elder Dragon whose existence has been questioned for a long time, and which has been said to reside between the border of this world and the afterlife, with much remaining unclear about it even in recent reports. The Chameleos primarily moves around slowly with frequent stutters in its rhythmic movement, although will showcase sudden bursts of speed in its movements when necessary. Additionally, it is known to frequently take to the skies, during which it invariably scatters poison.This peculiar habit of its—alongside its vanishing ability and tendency to steal items—left some researchers to wonder if this may be why the Chameleos is classified as an Elder Dragon.
Sightings of the Chameleos uniquely appear to be limited to areas with high humidity, such as jungles, mountain streams, waterfalls, and marshlands; this is believed to be due to its habit of appearing alongside mist. While it rarely attacks other creatures within its territory, the Chameleos will take action to remove those who are foolish enough to intrude, and it is said the Elder Dragon will leave alone those who cower before it in awe, satisfied by their lack of hostility. Even so, a legend persists that one precious item belonging to the victim will vanish along with it. Even amongst Elder Dragons, the Chameleos is highly intelligent and understands what is most important to humans, able to quickly swipe away crucial supplies using its tongue, often causing research expeditions hoping to study its biology to suddenly need to abandon their investigation and turn back. In other cases, the Chameleos has been known to ransack the cargo of an entire caravan before anyone spots it.
The Chameleos has been known to cause trouble under the influence of the Rampage, and concerns of the Elder Dragon approaching the great town of Dundorma has necessitated urgent requests to repel or slay it. When battling against hunters, the Chameleos has learnt that stealing recovery items which are crucial to them, such as Potions or Rations, will demoralise them and cause them to retreat. Furthermore, when faced with hunters hailing from Kamura who empower themselves with the pollen gathered by Spiribirds, the Chameleos will enhance its strength by stealing and eating the pollen directly from their Petalaces. Coupled with its physical prowess, mastery over toxins, and the ability to vanish and quickly reposition, the Chameleos is a formidable adversary.

Physiology
The Chaotic Gore Magala is a Gore Magala that had attempted to molt into a Shagaru Magala, yet failed and has been left in a painful half-formed state. There can only ever be one Shagaru Magala in the world at once, and as soon as such a dragon achieves maturity, it begins protecting itself against potential usurpers. The Shagaru Magala achieves this by utilizing its unique strain of the Frenzy Virus (狂竜ウイルス, "Mad Wyvern Virus") that has an additional effect on other Gore Magala, suppressing their ability to mature and molt, and thus enforcing the supremacy of the current Shagaru Magala. Any negligent Gore Magala that attempt to molt in spite of the presence of the Shagaru Magala will see themselves mutate into a Chaotic Gore Magala; this process is irreversible and always fatal to the now malformed Variant.
The body of this deformed monster is subsequently unusual in appearance: the left side still resembles that of a normal Gore Magala—covered in and armored by a dark carapace—by contrast, whereas the right side is defined by an uneven emergence of Shagaru Magala scales and shells bursting forth from the black body. The wing membranes of the Chaotic Gore Magala seem to possess the brilliant glow of those found on the Shagaru Magala, although their color remains smothered under the characteristic dark cloak of dander intrinsic to the Gore Magala. The body of the Chaotic Gore Magala contains the raw power of an Elder Dragon and traps it in a vessel that cannot control or temper it, causing the creature unimaginable agony at all times as its tissue breaks down continuously.
Among its many unusual features, the Chaotic Gore Magala possesses a pair of Diametrical Horns; while the right horn is an actual horn and strongly resembles those of the Shagaru Magala, the left "horn" retains the antenna-like structure that is seen in the Gore Magala. While the right horn is always erect, the left horn generally stays folded down on the head until the monster enrages. It has been noted that even though the left horn appears superficially to not have been altered by the partial molt, it is actually saturated with small golden veins all across its surface. These veins appear to perpetually push and twist the horn into becoming a proper Shagaru Magala horn, a fruitless effort that only adds to the creature's suffering. This process is so violent that it produces an eerily audible sound, described as a "squeaking." Compared to the hardened horns of the Shagaru Magala, the base of the malformed horn sprouting from the Chaotic Gore Magala's right side is positioned noticeably lower.
The scales of the Chaotic Gore Magala are said to wriggle due to the many layers of black and golden material fighting over control. These two materials actively try to devour and usurp one another, creating an undulating surface. This is especially pronounced in the rare Contrary Scales that sometimes can be retrieved from the body of the Chaotic Gore Magala. Curiously, the right side of the Chaotic Gore Magala's face possesses a small and red eye, the left eye socket meanwhile remains empty. However, it is unknown if the creature is able to actually see through its right eye.
Behavior
The Chaotic Gore Magala was originally discovered on Heaven's Mount, and has since been sighted in other regions, such as the Ruined Pinnacle and the Shrine Ruins. Due to the constant and horrible pain of its malformed existence, the Chaotic Gore Magala is extremely aggressive and will attack just about anything it sees. As it wields the power of the Shagaru Magala with none of its wisdom or restraint, the Chaotic Gore Magala is able to unleash devastating attacks, both with its body and through its use of the Frenzy Virus. Additionally, it has been observed that it rapidly oscillates between different states of its Frenzy State due to its unstable power, making it an unpredictable fighter.

Physiology
The Chatacabra's bunched body is unlike that of other larger Amphibian species, evoking instead the body structure typically associated with certain Fanged Beasts, largely due to its posture, well developed and muscular forelimbs, and its knuckle-walking. A thick blue-green hide streaked by black stripes—which are particularly prominent around its back, rear, and hindlegs—cover its topside, whereas its underbelly is a light, creamy, tan coloration. Owed to its gluttonous diet, the Chatacabra's hide possesses elastic qualities that make the material easy to mold, and is of a distinctly finer quality when tempered by its harsh environment. The jagged scales of the Chatacabra are particularly sturdy and ideal for crafting armor, with higher quality scales boasting far greater durability.
The sturdy forearms of the Chatacabra are covered by stout plating that has been smoothed and strengthened through a lifetime of repeated licking; constant friction from being dragged against the ground has polished them to a shining gleam. These forelimbs store a mucus-like adhesive substance that allows the Chatacabra to collect strewn chunks of rock and ore when angered by scraping its arms on the ground to create an armored covering, heightening the power and range of its strikes considerably.
The Chatacabra's skull is flat and broad, with the bulbous lower jaw being under-bitten and twice as large as the upper jaw; it is characterized by remarkably dense plating studded by jagged protrusions that cover the thick leathery hide, forming a prickly "beard" on its chin. Housed within the jaws is the Chatacabra's exceptionally long tongue whose coating of very sticky saliva allows it to slurp up prey items without trouble as well as affix rocks to its evolved forelimbs. The tongue is tipped with numerous soft and prickly taste buds at its end: their developed sensitivity allows the Amphibian to safely check food items for unwanted stimulants—such as poisons or spice—by preemptively prodding them with its tongue's sensitive tip.
Behavior
Although also able to appear in the Wounded Hollow, the Chatacabra is naturally endemic to the Windward Plains and roams all throughout the region. While it does not pose as big of a threat to the Sandfolk as the Balahara or Doshaguma packs, they must still be wary of the monster, colloquially referring to it as the Giant Toad. As it wanders the Windward Plains, the Chatacabra will investigate whatever oddities catch its attention, such as Camps, Hunters, or other monsters. Should it deem them threatening, the Chatacabra will use its sticky tongue and hefty forelimbs to batter its target, as well as adorn its forelimbs with rubble if further agitated. It can oftentimes be seen engaging in battles against Talioth packs or other large monsters.
When not engaged in territorial disputes, the Chatacabra may be observed living out an otherwise peaceful routine. It is most commonly sighted during the season of Plenty, when it will venture into the savanna to quench its thirst from the river's edge, bask in the sunlight. As it does so, it may quickly fling its tongue out to catch the unsuspecting insects hovering nearby who, alongside the Bulaqchi and Windrustlers, comprise its diet. Due to its voracious nature, the Chatacabra will commonly behave recklessly in regards to feeding, as evidenced by hunters who have been able to trick the Giant Toad into swallowing Barrel Bombs whole. Once it has filled its belly, the Chatacabra is prone to regurgitating pieces of swallowed Bulaqchi as it roams its wide territory. Once it arrives at the oasis secluded between the dunes towards the south, it can be observed drinking its fill, or soaking and bathing itself in the water. When it grows weary, the Chatacabra will retreat to a hidden Fulgurite cavern that offers it a safe haven from other monsters in which it may freely rest.

Physiology
The Comaqchi is a small Neopteron that displays many traits similar to the Bulaqchi, such as a slender frame with four walking legs, although there are key differences between the two species. Rather than raptorial forelimbs, the Comaqchi sports blunt, club-like appendages used for bludgeoning prey. Its legs and exoskeleton exhibit sparse hair-like structures and are typically a pastel-pink coloration, although some individuals display a subtle blue hue. This exoskeleton is also much smoother and more rounded than that of its relative. The eyes are a gradient of light pink and blue, and the region below the eyes bears eyelash-like markings. The mouth possesses multiple palps and an elongated clypeus. It additionally brandishes a prominent blue stinger at the tip of its long flexible tail.
Behavior
The Comaqchi has thus far only been discovered in the Iceshard Cliffs of the Eastlands, and can often be observed hanging onto the sides of walls in groups of three, waiting for suitable quarry to approach close enough. When a target comes within range, it will descend upon them alongside its group, surrounding and striking the target with its forelimbs, before finally injecting them with a sedative from its stinger. Once the victim has fallen asleep, the Neopteron will begin to feed on them in tandem with the rest of the colony, eating its fill until it is either satisfied or its prey has awoken. Preferential prey items are highly variable, as the Comaqchi targets large monsters and even Hunters. Despite this tenacity, if the colony fails to subdue a target it will often give up the hunt entirely, clambering back onto the wall to await a new opportunity.

Physiology
The Conga is a pink-furred Fanged Beast with a thick and stocky body, messy green hair, and a long flexible tail. It possesses a wide snout and maw as well as two tusks on its lower jaw. The upper lip is modified into hardened plate with a serrated lower edge, resembling a row of external teeth. The Conga's tail sports a leathery fold on the underside that can be used to grasp objects, while its hands are armed with long straight claws.
The Conga will eat almost anything due to its omnivorous nature, yet it displays a passionate preference for mushrooms and will ignore all other foods in favor of them. The great variety of substances it may ingest mix together in its gut and produce an extremely foul-smelling gas, which builds up over time within the monster's round belly and can be later released from the rectum.
A Conga that grows large enough and performs the correct social rituals may become an alpha leader, called a Congalala.
Behavior
The Conga can be found in warm regions, such as jungles or swamps. In these zones, it will form a pack consisting of many other Conga and usually one singular Congalala. The Conga and its pack roam their territory as a unit, although do not display any advanced teamwork like their close relative, the Blango. Despite this, there is still a hierarchy to the pack: the Congalala is considered the leader, with the two largest Conga taking on the positions of second and third ranked members respectively. This hierarchy is relevant in matters of succession.
When a Conga has grown large enough, and desires to become a Congalala, it will seek out and use juices from its favorite plants to shape its messy head hair into a cone. This is the symbol of authority within the pack's social structure, and a Conga displaying it serves as a claim to the top position within the pack. Should that pack already have a Congalala, then this claim instead becomes a challenge, which in turn results in a physical fight between the current leader and the challenger—the winner is allowed to take the throne. However, not any Conga is allowed to challenge the boss, only the second and third ranked Conga of the pack are allowed to issue a legitimate challenge. Should any lesser Conga display the cone of authority, it would be beaten violently as punishment by the pack, its challenge being taken as invalid and voided.

Physiology
The Congalala is a male Conga that has grown to become the leader of his pack, as such he largely resembles his smaller counterparts, sporting a similar coating of glossy and stout pink fur. However his fur is a notably paler shade, and his underside, face, hands, and legs contrastingly are completely hairless, being covered instead with a dark-gray hide. He can be distinguished from his smaller brethren by several features—such as his overall larger size, or his longer and more developed tail—with perhaps his most distinguishing feature being the peculiar conical tuft of hair atop his head, sporting the same yellowish-green coloration of the Conga's hair tuft. This vibrant crest-like hair of the Congalala is not a naturally grown structure, instead it is created by the Congalala as he announces his intention to become the pack leader. By using juices and saps extracted from crushed plants and fruits, the Congalala forces his usually messy head hair to stand on end, styling it into a conical shape. It has been noted that the juices the Congalala uses for this tend to be derived from plants and fruits the beast personally likes, with him deciding which to use based on whichever odors he personally finds to be the nicest. This tidied headdress functions akin to a crown, establishing the Congalala as the pinnacle of his pack's social hierarchy.
Comparatively, the Congalala's fangs are hard and blunt, and are ill-suited for use in tearing, serving instead to crush food as well as anything else they get a hold of. These solid fangs are even sturdy enough to crunch apart entire boulders, turning them into dust. As with the Conga, he only sports teeth on his lower lip, with his upper lip instead possessing a sharpened row of small teeth-like protrusions that aid in biting. The forelimbs of the Congalala sport shaggier fur compared to those of the Conga, with it hanging from his arms as thick unkept curtains of pink fur. His claws are also notably sharper and longer than those of his pack mates, with them primarily being used to expertly style his hair into its signature style. While often useful in combat, able to gouge though anything they attempt to slash, they impede the Congalala's ability to grasp objects due to their length. To compensate, the prehensile tail of the Congalala has evolved a leathery tip that is able to serve effectively as a third dexterous arm, grabbing and holding onto objects with surprising proficiency.
The Congalala is infamous for his ability to expel noxious gases from both his maw and rectum. Specifically, the gases produced by regular digestion are expelled as flatulence, with it being produced in abundance due to large amount of food the beast consumes. This gas possesses an especially strong odor, with mere exposure to it being enough to induce stinging eyes. This stench also imbues itself into consumable supplies, such as Potions and Rations, upon contact and causes them to foul and spoil, preventing them from being able to be consumed. Meanwhile, irregular waste components from his diet—such as toxic or even explosive compounds—are funneled through the mouth and expelled as a breath. The Congalala possesses powerful enzymes in his stomach that allow him to break down fungus based poisons and convert them into gases to be exhaled. Curiously, these enzymes cannot separate and neutralize poisons bound to flesh due to alterations to the substance's chemical structure, rendering him vulnerable to Poisoned Meats. The beast can additionally inflate his belly to serve as a protective shield, as the hard skin on his naked abdomen is able to deflect certain attacks. However, doing so leaves the Congalala out of breath for a short while.
Behavior
The Congalala is generally found in warm and damp regions, such as jungles or swamps, with his common appearance in temperate environments leading to him being well researched. He lives alongside a relatively small pack, in which there is only ever one Congalala who acts as the leader of the troop; once a male Conga has grown strong enough to feel confident in his dominance, he will use juices from his favorite plants to style his hair into a cone. This behavior serves as a sign of power as well as a challenge to the incumbent Congalala. This assertion of intent is followed by a physical fight, after which the usurping Conga may become the next troop leader should he win. However, not any Conga can attempt this—only the second and third ranked members of a pack may issue such a challenge. If any lesser Conga is spotted styling his hair, he will immediately be assaulted by the pack's leader with no regards to the usual proceedings of the challenge. Maintenance of the cone is crucial if the beast wishes to maintain his spot at the top, as the straighter and longer this cone is, the more respect he commands from the rest of the pack.
Just like the Conga, the Congalala is omnivorous and is noted to have a voracious appetite, with him being spotted eating nearly all of the time. His devotion to food appears to surpass that of his lesser brethren, as the Congalala has been observed gorging himself on outright harmful foods, such as rotten meat, even after suffering its effects. In order to find food, he relies on his excellent sense of smell, sniffing out any mushrooms that happen to be growing in the vicinity. The Congalala has even been known to steal food directly from Hunters.
When provoked, the Congalala first responds with the species' traditional threat display: the beast stands up on his hind legs, stretches his arms to the side, and shakes his rear while expelling a small cloud of rancid gas. If this warning is not enough, the Congalala is prone to go on the offensive, battering enemies with his heavy body and slashing at them with his sharp claws. When he grows especially irritated, the skin along his nose and rear will flush a bright red. Further, the Congalala weaponizes his flatulence and breaths, and is commonly known to hold onto a variety of mushrooms with his tail and devouring them during combat to use their toxins in the form of a variety of poisonous breaths against his adversaries, including paralyzing or even combustible ones. As the exact effect of this breath depends of the kind of mushroom consumed, the combat ability of the Congalala varies by which region he inhabits. When in the Scarlet Forest, the Congalala is reportedly able to dig up and make usage of a rare black truffle that grants his breath multiple noxious properties simultaneously following consumption.
Super Biology Information
The Super Biology Book Series collects the thoughts and theories of real scientists that were asked to speak about monsters from the Monster Hunter series. Thus, they are inherently speculative and should be seen as such.
Zoological Author Yuumin Mori compares the Congalala’s ability to derive different toxic effects from its food to the toxin accumulation within animals such as pufferfish and Poison dart frogs. Specifically, Mori proposes that the Congalala is able to isolate and concentrate specific amino acids within the food that it ingests, allowing the beast to accumulate specific compounds for different purposes. These might even include purposes other than combat: Mori suggests that since Conga and Congalala live in social groups, they might utilize certain odors and gases as a way to communicate with each other, and that the ability to produce a variety of gases based on diet might have developed as a social adaptation initially.
Looking at the Congalala’s anatomy, Mori notes its fluffy prehensile tail. This physical trait, which is also seen in arboreal animals such as New World Monkeys, Binturongs and Kinkajous, is strongly associated with tree-dwellers. The long, sharp claws of the Congalala also match adaptations commonly seen in arboreal species. Yet, Congalala are always seen with their feet firmly planted on the ground, and no tree-climbing behavior has been observed so far. Mori wonders if maybe the Congalala’s ancestors might have originally been tree-dwellers which gradually spent more time on the ground, until the species had grown large enough to make a grounded lifestyle more viable than one spent climbing across branches. The fact that Congalala can get up on their hind legs for social displays might also point to this, additionally suggesting that the evolutionary pressures that grounded this species were social in nature. Mori points out that the claws of the Congalala are also notable for being seemingly completely useless for its current lifestyle, as the long claws prevent any meaningful dexterity. He thus asserts that they are mostly vestigial, and that the presence of these claws in a fully terrestrial species could imply that the Congalala might have suffered a rapid and aggressive change in habitat, forcing it fully onto the ground before its body had time to catch up.
The most striking trait of the Congalala is perhaps its pink fur, which puzzles Mori somewhat. In the dense jungle, such a coloration is likely to stand out, after all. Considering the adult Congalala’s size, the fact that it can afford such a color might indicate that the beast does not fear many natural predators. Thus, the fur may have evolved without any consideration for camouflage and is instead related to social behavior among the pack. Alternatively, Mori notes that the gases produced by the Congalala are not invisible, but rather distinctly colored, from brown to yellow to purple. The beast’s pink fur might thus actually function as camouflage after all, but only when the Congalala is surrounded by clouds of its own gas, allowing it to use its flatulence as an escape tactic as well.
Regarding the Congalala’s use of feces and flatulence for defensive purposes, Mori compares it to skunks, which spray foul anal secretions at enemies, and hippos, which spin their tails to scatter their feces across a wide area. Such behavior is generally associated with a desire to avoid combat, which is further evidenced by the Congalala’s flat dentition - it is not a predator and generally wants to be left in peace. This behavior, alongside the decorative adaptations and social structures of the Conga species, might imply a significant degree of intelligence. Mori states that a common origin point for intelligence to evolve is the presence of mutual social bargaining, and that Congalala certainly appears to fulfill the necessary conditions. He stresses however that one would have to further corroborate this idea by studying individual Congalala to observe if each pack member displays a sense of individuality and culture.
If a human were to encounter a Congalala, Mori would advise them to be extremely cautious. Congalala are likely not aggressive by nature, but they are probably sensitive to territorial invasions and might react negatively to a careless approach. On the other hand, Mori also compares the Congalala to bears, which are also large animals that are both fairly uninterested in conflict and yet extremely deadly if encountered. Thus, Mori proposes that the best way to avoid death at the hands of a Congalala would be to slowly back away from it without letting down your guard.

The Water Bewitching Bird Coral Pukei-Pukei (プケプケ亜種, Pukepuke Ashu) is a Bird Wyvern introduced in Monster Hunter World: Iceborne.

A highly colorful Subspecies of the Pukei-Pukei that have discarded their bodies' toxic capabilities in favor of a range of water-based attacks fueled by the water-rich flora native to their habitats, instead of the Poisoncups preferred by the main species. These monsters are able to expel high-pressure water streams from both their mouth and tail, and use their characteristically long and flexible tongue to manipulate the streams of water expelled from their mouth to split apart these streams and fire water jets in multiple directions.

Physiology
The Coral Pukei-Pukei sports a striking appearance, exhibiting a primarily maroon and light-blue body that more closely matches the sprawling coral forests it calls home. This Subspecies' signature plumage, found around the neck and on the ends of the wingarms, carries a bright, yellow-orange coloration. Like the main Pukei-Pukei species, these feathers are coated in light-reflecting, crystalline particles that allow the Coral Pukei-Pukei to manipulate the refraction angle and brightness of the feathers in accordance to its mood. When in an agitated state, the feathers fan out aggressively and exhibit a more vivid orange, and when the Coral Pukei-Pukei is frightened, the plumage noticeably recedes and takes on a much duller coloration.
Another notable feature of the Coral Pukei-Pukei is its exceptionally stretchy tongue, which is said to be able to extend up to 20 meters in length. The tongue is useful for lapping up coral eggs and filtering local flora for moisture, however, it may also be employed as a weapon and swung around in combat. The Coral Pukei-Pukei possesses a specialized sac in its head that it is able to fill with large amounts of water. The stored water is then able to be spat out in volleys as projectiles, or fired as high pressure streams for greater precision. When firing the latter, the Coral Pukei-Pukei can curl up its tongue and split the high pressure stream, resulting in it suddenly fanning out from either side.
In a similar manner, the tail, is able to fire high pressure water streams and is highly flexible, granting it considerable combat advantages over the head. As the Coral Pukei-Pukei moves large volumes of water through it to attack, the tail can be observed to rhythmically swell and shrink. The tail's length and flexibility allows streams to be adjusted to sweep across an area, whereas the head is largely only able to fire straight ahead. Furthermore, the tail is able to move freely while airborne, giving the Coral Pukei-Pukei the ability to fire these streams while hovering with its wings. Finally, freeing up the head grants the Coral Pukei-Pukei the especially deadly ability to simultaneously intake water with its head from nearby corals whilst firing water with its tail.
Behavior
The Coral Pukei-Pukei primarily roams the Coral Highlands, although it has also been sighted in the Coral Region of the Guiding Lands. Further, while the standard variety is typically known to be herbivorous, the Coral Pukei-Pukei has been observed to enjoy consuming coral eggs with its long tongue, in addition to the local flora. The Coral Pukei-Pukei's diet is highly important for fueling its water attacks, as the Coral Highlands contains surprisingly few bodies of water that allow the Subspecies to replenish its stores. Thus, the Coral Pukei-Pukei seeks out large, soft coral structures on the ground, such as those found in the Shamos' nest, and with these coral, the Coral Pukei-Pukei is able to plunge its head inside and pump the coral's water stores into its own body. Aside from this behavior, the Coral Pukei-Pukei has been reported to wrap its tongue around certain plants, such as lichens and various mosses, to filter out their moisture for itself. In the Guiding Lands where bodies of water are less scarce, the Coral Pukei-Pukei has been observed to pump water into its body directly from ponds and streams.
Like the main species, the Coral Pukei-Pukei is a very timid creature and seldom pick fights with monsters stronger than itself. For instance, in its new habitats, the Paolumu is one major competitor for coral eggs that the Coral Pukei-Pukei tends to avoid. Against weaker threats, such as the Shamos —who tend to occupy the same spaces where the water storing coral appear—the Coral Pukei-Pukei will be more inclined to fight for territory.

Physiology
The Cortos is a unique Wingdrake that lives in the Hinterlands. Like others of its kind, it possesses a large head, forelimbs modified into wings, taloned hindlimbs, and a tail. Its body is covered in angular scales; the ones on its dorsal surface are white, and the ones on its ventral surface are greenish gray. A row of larger scales runs down the spine. The first odd feature is its head, as unlike all other Wingdrakes, the Cortos lacks a beak, instead it has a wide snake-like mouth and a slightly upturned nose—inside the mouth is a small number of needle-like teeth. The red eyes have slit pupils and are placed near the front of the flattened skull, while the neck is long and similarly flattened.
A muscular chest and shoulders support the wings, with each wing possessing four digits: the first has been reduced to a spur, and the next three support the wing membrane. The trailing edge of the wings has a zigzagged shape that resembles large feathers, and the wing membranes are white with a black outline. The feet are orange and each sport three toes that have strongly hooked claws. The tail is long and flattened—like the neck—and at the tip of the tail is a single spike.
The Cortos possesses a unique venom that reduces the victim's immunity to the elements. In the frigid habitats the Cortos inhabits, this fluid hinders its prey's resistance to the cold, making escape near impossible.
Behavior
The Cortos is known from the Hoarfrost Reach and Tundra Region of the Guiding Lands. It patrols its territory through specific routes in flocks of two or three and is an opportunistic predator that flies in search of carcasses, raw meat, or weakened creatures. Although less docile than other Wingdrakes, it is usually hesitant to prey on hunters and is fearful of larger monsters. However, it will attack hunters who have been afflicted with an ailment or knocked off their feet, and any hunters that stand near them too long will also be attacked, although in this case the Cortos' assault will cease if a large monster approaches. It attacks prey by either swooping down on it, or spitting resistance-reducing venom.
The Cortos rarely lands, and only does so to groom itself or briefly look around. When it suffers damage its flight will briefly falter and a hunter may latch onto its feet with their Slinger, the panicking Wingdrake will then fly to one of the other areas its flock frequents, with the hunter in tow. The Slinger will then dislodge, and the Wingdrake will fly back to its original position.

Physiology
True to its name, the Crimson Fatalis is a variation of the Fatalis tainted in deep-red scales that emit light in the darkness. Although the exact variation type is cloudy, it is likely an injured Fatalis that fled from Castle Schrade to a volcano. While the Elder Dragon's underside is a saturated crimson, its upper side and pair of wings are jet-black, with the latter emitting a crimson glow at their ends reminiscent of lava in the night. Much like its teeth, the spikes that line its back are an ashen-gray, while the frill-like membrane of its cheeks are red. In contrast, the flesh inside the Crimson Fatalis mouth is a vivid, indigo-blue coloration.
With the exception of its asymmetrical crown, the Crimson Fatalis' stature and silhouette does not differ from that of the Fatalis. Standing out amongst the cluster of horns atop the head is the Elder Dragon's inner left horn that extends far more in length and breadth than the rest of the horns, which retain a similar size to one another. When the Crimson Fatalis' crown is shattered, the sheer rage born from the Hunter who injured it surges throughout its body, bolstering its metabolism and causing the broken horn to regenerate rapidly, swelling considerably in size. All of its horns glow red at their tip—even once severed—with the largest horn emanating more light.
The Crimson Fatalis boasts even more potent fire attacks than its regular counterpart and, akin to the Dalamadur, is able to call down what appear to resemble flaming meteors from the sky. It does so by roaring and erupting the surrounding volcanic environment, manipulating the expelled magma to then rain down as fireballs and explaining why it always appears in volcanic craters, the area of a volcano that is most concentrated with lava. Furthermore, the Crimson Fatalis is capable of spreading and detonating clouds of explosive dust when fought in the Ingle Isle.
Yet there exists a more powerful and mysterious variation of this Elder Dragon, one overcome with rage and whose blood-red armor is far more vivid, its claws and spines appearing ablaze. This individual can summon raging fireballs that sprout from and hop across the ground, as well as flare its wings and induce scorching heatwaves; its every step explodes with flame. When enraged, a blazing glow that casts a hellish visage shrouds the Elder Dragon and causes its horns, chest, wings, and tail end to glow intensely. The source of this particular Crimson Fatalis' anomalous strength remains unknown.
Behavior
Unlike the Fatalis and Old Fatalis who tend to appear in the ancient ruins of once lively civilizations, the Crimson Fatalis instead roosts in volcanic regions, such as the Battleground and Ingle Isle. Amongst its counterparts, the Crimson Fatalis is the most aggressive.

It is a Variant of the Valstrax.

Physiology
The Crimson Glow Valstrax is a mutant Valstrax characterized and driven mad by the increased Dragon energy production in its body. While it largely resembles the standard Valstrax in appearance, the rampant Dragon energy coursing through the Crimson Glow Valstrax's body has resulted in numerous altered features, as can be seen in the gleaming shells layering its body. Comprising its silvery body are shells capable of withstanding both supersonic speeds and boiling temperatures, although the combination of Dragon energy spewing from the Crimson Glow Valstrax's outer shells and the air resistance during high speed flight has caused the body's lustrous scales to become blackened and soot-stained—the characteristic crimson trail that forms as the Elder Dragon flies similarly gets stained in appearance.
Additional examples of the Crimson Glow Valstrax's features having been altered include its scales being tinged crimson and the red-hot shells around its shoulders emitting a glittering crimson light. Even the brilliance of a shimmering jewel bestowed by a great king pales when compared against the radiance of this sinister and bewitching light, the eerie red gleam of which is where the Variant's epithet of Crimson Glow originates from. The rampant Dragon energy is the culprit behind each of this Variant's differing traits and takes the form of a boiling-hot draconic fluid; the power radiated by its intense heat is calamitous, so much so the mere act of touching the harvested liquid fills one's mind with catastrophe. As the Crimson Glow Valstrax soars through the sky at blistering speeds, it circulates vast quantities of air through its body and utilizes internal organs to convert it into Dragon element, which in turn allows it to achieve its explosive speed. While the standard Valstrax expels Dragon energy from its nostrils and wings when agitated, the Crimson Glow Valstrax releases it from its chest as well.
The flickering and defining crimson glow is the result of Dragon energy leaking and reacting with the atmosphere, however the true nature of its blazing glow is an eruption of its own unique energy, known as Dragonheart (龍気). The leading theory behind the Crimson Glow Valstrax's mutation is that the presence of this energy in its body has been profoundly heightened, causing the Elder Dragon to be thrown into a ferocious frenzy. Once a massive volume of air is taken in through the slits in its chest, the Crimson Glow Valstrax channels an even greater amount of Dragon energy into its wings, entering an especially dangerous state signified by its wings glowing a deep crimson in an almost otherworldly fashion. In this powered-up state where its released Dragon energy has grown especially volatile, the Crimson Glow Valstrax is capable of aerial movements unbound by the constraints of gravity, enabling it to hover in the air, blow away targets with blasts of energy, and spear them with supersonic wing strikes. However, delivering a strong strike to its wings whilst they are charged with Dragon energy will disrupt the flow of energy through its body and cause a reaction akin to an internal explosion. Further, the Crimson Glow Valstrax can be prevented from channeling Dragon energy into its wings by being interrupted while intaking air through its chest, causing the energy to combust and for it to suffer severe damage.
Behavior
The Crimson Glow Valstrax dwells in the far reaches of the sky and typically secludes itself in the upper atmosphere. Its presence has long been sighted in the sky as the Crimson Comet, and charting the locations of recorded sightings reveals it to always be on the move across the continent, with the Crimson Glow Valstrax indiscriminately attacking anything that enters its sight. Having been driven mad by its own rampant energy, it descends to a lower than usual altitude when in a berserk state and relentlessly hunts prey, incinerating them with Dragon energy and consuming them for fuel. If one is to hear a distant unfamiliar cry and notice a dark shadow be cast upon the sky, they would be wise to flee their current location immediately, for if the shadow is that of the mutant Valstrax there is a risk of the surrounding area being reduced to charcoal in an instant. On occasion, the movement of the Crimson Glow Valstrax has been mistaken for that of a comet.
As it descends to viciously prey upon other monsters, it circles its prey from above before violently crashing down upon them and trampling them in a supersonic Ambush. Lashing out at whatever catches its attention, the Crimson Glow Valstrax preys upon a wide variety of monsters and will even go so far as to target other Elder Dragons, even one as powerful and disastrous as the Amatsu. If the Thunder Serpent Narwa and the Wind Serpent Ibushi are considered beings that bring forth calamity, then the appearance of this mutant could very well be likened to a calamity descending from the heavens. Feared for its lack of any equal, the Crimson Glow Valstrax is a terrifyingly powerful Elder Dragon that threatens to sunder the very earth, with there being a myriad of legends foretelling the despair and destruction it brings. As such, any Hunter able to defeat this Variant Elder Dragon is regarded as having achieved the pinnacle of their vocation.
The Crimson Glow Valstrax is an extremely dangerous Variant that leaves disaster in is wake, raining down draconic projectiles that sear the land as it jets through the sky. The consequence of the Elder Dragon's presence can be seen in the Sandy Plains, and the many scattered ruins littering its terrain. According to historical records, what was once a flourishing trade hub known for its enormous oasis was transformed into the barren and sandy landscape it remains now by the abnormal weather conditions triggered at the arrival of a "crimson star from the heavens," forcing the people who once lived there to abandon the region. Moreover, through an old hunter's scattered messages in the region, an inscription was found in a home which had been buried under sand that read "As the crimson glow falls upon us, our people flee this land; but I promise to survive, that we two may reunite."
History & Mythology
The Crimson Glow Valstrax is trailed by a long and ancient history of legends that warn of its wrath as well as foretell its appearances. It is often viewed as a symbol of despair and believed to have destruction as its sole intent, being spoken of as the Scourge of the World and personified as an evil star in timeworn tomes. Additionally dubbed the Star of Despair, the Crimson Glow Valstrax is feared for the darkness and anguish that will spread across the land at its arrival, with one foreboding legend in particular cautioning of the Elder Dragon's appearance: "Behold in fear this strange, crimson-glowing, malevolent star. Its radiance will reduce the earth to ashes and tear through the heavens, ushering in eternal darkness." Further, several parts of the mutant Valstrax's body are tied to beliefs of calamity: its scales are thought to portend disaster and depict a dragon spirit symbolizing the approach of calamity, and a red orb within the body is seen as the source of evil heavenly calamities.
Not all legends of the Crimson Glow Valstrax speak of its destructive nature however, as some fables instead merely tell of its appearance. During the Rampage, as the incident grew in scale, an echoing cry could be heard from no discernible location, which gave rise to a legend of a comet falling from the sky. It was this legend that led to the belief the hordes of monsters had likely served as an ideal feeding ground for the Elder Dragon. Additionally there exist numerous meteor legends born from the sight of the Crimson Glow Valstrax soaring through the sky after people had discovered fallen fragments that were shed from its body during flight, leading to them describing it as a "red star falling from the heavens." It is now known that these fragments are the result of parts of the Elder Dragon's shell being gradually worn down after withstanding the shock of supersonic flight as well as boiling Dragon energy over a long period, causing them to flake off the body and fall to the ground. However, contrasting the typically foreboding mythos that surround it, one legend proclaims the spirit of the Crimson Glow Valstrax to bring a person good luck.

Physiology
The Dah'ren Mohran is a mountainous Elder Dragon that glides across and burrows through the sea-like sands of the Great Desert. Its body is bulky and streamlined, with a thick tail, proportionally short, stout forelimbs, vestigal hindlimbs, and a lone, magnificent horn growing outward from its snout. Its cream-colored underside is the only portion of its body left exposed, in contrast, the entire rest of its grand body is covered by the Elder Dragon's Rockskin: a massive carapace that boasts an overwhelming, almost otherworldly presence. The exterior's deep-red hue originates from the thick layer of oxidized metals that have adhered to the Elder Dragon's outer shell over the course of its long life. As it swims through the sand, a wide variety of rare minerals accumulate on the Dah'ren Mohran's body that help to both form and mend its shell. Amongst the rare variety of minerals gathered and expelled by the Dah'ren Mohran's body, two particularly exceptional materials stand out: the Earth Dragongem, heralded as one of the toughest materials from the Elder Dragon's already impervious body, and the Earth Dragonsphire, a jewel rumored to be the source of the Dah'ren Mohran's nature bending power.
Much like its close relative—the Jhen Mohran—the Dah'ren Mohran is famed for being a "Living Mine" due to the valuable and precious materials that can be mined from its back. Amidst the ores that may be mined from the Dah'ren Mohran are the rare and valuable Dragonite, the mysterious Fucium, and the durable as well as flexible Meldspar. It is due to these minerals that have lodged themselves into the hide that the Dah'ren Mohran's dense shell is comprised of layers similar to those found in bedrock. Furthermore, the heavy Rockskin has grown unimaginably hard, to such an extraordinary degree that even great mountains appear as piles of sponge in comparison. The Dah'ren Mohran's heavy Bloodscales, which emit a deep, crimson glow akin to a sunset, have been polished and granted a unique texture by the endless surfing across the desert's rough sands. Amongst them, scales that have been particularly smoothed by the course sands are considered quite rare and valuable. Each foreleg is defended by thick, layered plating known as an Allbrace; strong enough to support the great weight of the Dah'ren Mohran, it has been elegantly dusted by sand. This powerful foreleg armor forges well and is known to produce excellent equipment, with it being noted to gain strength when exposed to water. Hunters may climb aboard the Elder Dragon's back once the protective plate armor has been destroyed, atop of which can be seen the blow holes that eject rocks at assailants. One particular ore generated from within the Dah'ren Mohran's own body, known as Dah'renstone, is especially desired for its ability to produce a unique and high-quality metal.
The grand, spiraling horn is the Dah'ren Mohran's most distinctive feature; it is hardened magnificently by age and capable of pulverizing anything in its path. It is believed the spiral horn allows the Dah'ren Mohran to burrow even deeper into the Great Desert than the Jhen Mohran, possessing the ability to bore through tougher bedrock. While the two Elder Dragon species both feed by taking in minerals from their surroundings, the Dah'ren Mohran's ability to burrow deeper results in the minerals that accumulate on its shell to possess a differing composition. Correspondingly, having evolved to excel at drilling through the earth, harvested horns are used by humans as a tool for excavation. Under the horn lies the Elder Dragon's vast maw; able to stretch wide enough to reach its forelegs, it inhales massive amounts of sand and ingests the microorganisms and minerals hidden within. While primarily performed as a form of filter feeding, it may also be done with the intention of violently expelling it at targets in the form of a destructive, large-scale breath attack. When it is performing this—or other similarly dangerous attacks—hunters may strike the large gong on their Dragonship to stagger the Elder Dragon. As the Dah'ren Mohran has highly sensitive ears it uses to monitor the surface while it lurks beneath the sands, the gong's echoing ring is able to momentarily stun the giant.
Behavior
The Dah'ren Mohran reigns over the stretch of the Great Desert that falls under the jurisdiction of the Val Habar Guild, and may be sighted relatively frequently. Through these sightings, the Elder Dragon's habit of smashing apart obstacles that lie in its path with its spiral-shaped horn can be observed, which has earned the Dah'ren Mohran the moniker of Colossal Mountain Dragon. Due to the valuable resources that litter its back, the Dah'ren Mohran's periodic appearances are often accompanied by groups of sandskiffs hoping to strike it rich. However, those who seek to harvest the lucrative materials must first climb aboard the Elder Dragon's arms from their ship, requiring the sturdy foreleg plating to be destroyed beforehand. It was for this reason that the original caravans, which would one day gather together and form Val Habar, chased the colossal Elder Dragon in the past—tying the bustling city to the hunt of the Dah'ren Mohran with an inseparable bond. During the period the Dah'ren Mohran appears, a festival that calls forth all manner of skilled hunters to partake in and show off their mettle is held within Val Habar, awarding the victor with the honor of challenging the great Elder Dragon.
The Dah'ren Mohran may occasionally endanger Val Habar with its activity and elicit an immediate all-hands response by the Hunter's Guild, who will then send out however many Dragonships are available. Fortunately, the Dah'ren Mohran's arrival is often preceded by a swarm of Remobra that act as a warning for any travelling the vast sands, allowing any who are prepared to fire off a distress signal and alert the bustling city. In one instance, Val Habar was saved from the Dah'ren Mohran's fury by being repelled before it reached the city through the combined efforts of an aspiring hunter, several Dragonships, and the Ace Hunters. On one occasion, the Dah'ren Mohran even threatened to crush the town of Dundorma.
Alongside established records, there exists an old sketch drawn by a member of the Scriveners that embarked on a hunt. Resembling the Dah'ren Mohran, the illustration depicts a colossal creature that, rather than possess a gargantuan horn, lacks anything of the sort; it is instead characterised by a wide, flat head. Due to the clear distinction in the shape of the head, it is thought that perhaps the creature may be a different species.

Physiology
The Daimyo Hermitaur is a large Carapaceon covered in a crimson exoskeleton patterned with white stripes, it is almost twice the size of the much younger and smaller Hermitaur. This shell is surprisingly light for its size, although it is incredibly thick, resulting in it being both easy to use in crafting and capable of producing strong armor. The Daimyo Hermitaur additionally possesses black eyes suspended on stalks, a long pair of antennae, and a circular jaw lined with mandibles. Six limbs protrude from the Daimyo Hermitaur's body; four of these are utilized for walking, whilst the front pair have been fashioned into large, shield-like claws. While these claws serve as the Daimyo Hermitaur's primary weaponry, able to easily slice through rock, they also provide the monster with a potent defense. By holding its claws in front of its face, the Daimyo Hermitaur is able to shield itself from attacks and enter a heavily fortified stance. However, especially loud noises can easily disrupt and stun the Carapaceon whilst it holds this stance due to the sound reverberating inside of its claws. The shelling composing the Daimyo Hermitaur's claws is as hard as metal and tough enough to be used as fortification material in the construction of castles.
The backside of the Daimyo Hermitaur is completely unarmored and exceptionally soft, as a result, it will typically use the skulls of other monsters—most commonly that of the Monoblos—as protection, granting it the nickname of Shield Crab. While the horn present on the Monoblos skull is highly decayed, it is still extremely durable, allowing the Daimyo Hermitaur to use it as an effective weapon to pierce its opponents with. In addition to using the skull's horn, the Daimyo Hermitaur is able to spray out a concentrated stream of bubbles that have accumulated around its mouth further to defend itself.
Occasionally, the Daimyo Hermitaur will produce jewel-like objects inside of its abdomen, such as Black Pearls or Crab Pearls. They form when impurities, like sand, find their way inside the shell the Daimyo Hermitaur wears, and when combined with several layers of secreted bodily fluids from the abdomen, a pearl is formed. These pearls are highly sought after due to their beauty, by both Hunters and seemingly the Gypceros as well.
Behavior
The Daimyo Hermitaur typically prefers to live in sandy areas and is most active during the warm and breeding seasons, it typically does not fight with other monsters unless it needs to protect its territory. The Daimyo Hermitaur is an omnivore and feeds on a large variety of food, such as sand-dwelling insects and plants which grow near bodies of water, it will even scavenge on dead fish. Using its large pincers, it will tear off anything edible it finds, before lifting it into its mouth. As well, the Daimyo Hermitaur uses it claws to burrow into the sand, typically leaving the Monoblos skull exposed in order to disguise itself. While this burrowing is primarily done as a means of transportation, it may also be used offensively, as the Daimyo Hermitaur uses the Monoblos skull to skewer prey from below.
As the Daimyo Hermitaur ages, it must replace its old shell with new ones it finds to be more comfortable. Upon finding a new shell, it first uses its claws to measure the space inside to see whether or not its body could fit. If it deems it a good fit, the Daimyo Hermitaur will shed its old shell and move into the new one. Like most other Carapaceons, the Daimyo Hermitaur is highly valued for its taste. The meat under the claws are said to be very satisfying meals, while the abdomen is especially prized for being delicious.
