Physiology
A tremendously titanic, serpentine Elder Dragon spoken of in fairy tales, so great in size it is comparable to the peak of a mountain itself, the Dalamadur is acclaimed for its destructive movements and the innumerable blades that line its steely-blue body. It possesses a set of arms protruding from its chest with huge hooked claws, two large spurs jutting out its hips, and a rattle-like tail resembling giant shears. Its thick, pliant scales—deemed the King of all Scales —have a glistening sheen to them and bestow a body as hard as diamond to the Elder Dragon, able to repel even the sharpest of blades.
The Dalamadur's backside is enveloped with near totality by unique, hooked scales that are used by the giant serpent to tear down mountains as it slithers by. Called Glaives, these onyx scales vary greatly in size, ranging from small studs and spikes protruding from its hide, to large hooks that gouge mountains beyond recognition. These Glaives form in dense clusters predominantly along the top side of the upper body and its tail end, lessening in density past the main body. The largest set amongst the Dalamadur's Glaives rest atop its back; called Fanblades, they are the most developed pair across the Elder Dragon's body and dwarf all others, the very earth screams as its carved by them. The Dalamadur is further able to enhance the lethality and destructiveness of its Glaives as it moves by finely controlling the contractions of its muscles, resulting in it leaving behind rough, jagged paths as it carves out and terraforms the land around it. This control extends to the tail, allowing it to unleash powerful rattles and scar the earth by gouging out ravines.
In order for the Dalamadur to sustain its strength, it will bask beneath the sun and take in solar energy to recharge itself as well as build up its own store of potent energy that boosts the core temperature of its body drastically upon accumulating. The Dalamadur's chest acts as a way for it to vent its extreme internal temperature outwards, appearing as a giant, glowing fracture across its chest adorned with large Glaives; it is the toughest area of the Dalamadur's already impenetrable body, virtually indestructible. When the Elder Dragon angers, its internal temperature soars, forcing its now glowing chest to vent it outwards and create a superheated air pocket around the torso that scorches all who get too close. Throughout its superheated, rage-induced state, pulsing veins surround its eyes and rattle-like tail end, highlighting them with a vivid sanguine. Standing out against the Dalamadur's steely scales and the dense thicket of black hooks that crown its pointed head are the pair of piercing, scarlet-red eyes that have been deemed too intimidating for unready artisans to work with. The jaws of the Elder Dragon are no less intimidating, as they are able to open deceptively wide, house giant fangs within, and instantly paralyze Hunters with a mere flick of the tongue.
In spite of its near unrivalled size, the Dalamadur possesses unmatched physicality in comparison to other similarly gargantuan Elder Dragons. It frequently incorporates twisting and twirling motions as it moves, carving the world around it and tearing down towering pillars of stone. The twisted, spiral bones of the Dalamadur have been tempered to an unparalleled degree and offer astounding strength to the Elder Dragon that, in unison with the numerous Glaives along its body, allows it to cause crustal deformation and erratic shifts in the terrain. According to the report by the Guild team that was sent to confirm the Elder Dragon's presence, shifts in the landscape followed its roars, and a mere twist of its torso carved valleys from mountains. The threat posed by the Dalamadur's increasing activity had the Guildmaster of Val Habar fear for the safety of the world; fortunately, the Guild was quick to employ its vast resources and lend aid.
In addition to tremendous physical power and an armored hide, the Dalamadur possesses potent elemental and seemingly astral abilities. It is able to expel colossal, azure fireballs from its maw as well as wield a mysterious and unknown element that shines a pale-blue light. This unique energy—different to the established elements—is condensed within the body before being expelled from the Dalamadur's jaws in the form of a flame-like breath. Without a doubt the Elder Dragon's most inexplicable power, however, is its ability to summon a cascade of Malevolent Stars at its behest. When the Dalamadur appears, it is bathed by a ray of light that shines upon it as countless meteors rain from the heavens, akin to a natural disaster. Following the cataclysmic phenomenon's barrage, fallen rocks comprised of a variety of mysterious and difficult to forge ores embed into the ground, with those remaining intact following the impact being called Shattered Omens. Further research into the Shattered Omens' composition has revealed the presence of foreign minerals that have never been mined elsewhere in this world. Moreover, a dormant pair of Shattered Omens emitting a soft, azure glow may be found deep within the depths of the Rotten Vale. Should sufficient physical force be applied to the resting pair, such as that from another monster's attacks, they will reawaken and ignite the surrounding area with their energy.
Behavior
The Dalamadur is an aggressive Elder Dragon that does not delay displaying its power before those who intrude upon its territory, demolishing vast stone structures and mountain peaks with a casual ease. It crushes and sends a tall peak tumbling down, as well as slams its tail across the Speartip Crag, splitting its landscape down the middle with a chasm. Its roars reshape the terrain and are deafeningly loud, accompanied by a distinctive sound produced by the rattling of its tail. The Dalamadur is responsible for altering the country of Shiki's geography into the unstable mess it remains to this day, having unnaturally caused tectonic shifts in the foundations of the land long, long ago when it slithered through Heaven's Mount. Its endless blades carved the region's numerous mountains, causing cascades of rubble to fall endlessly from peaks held together by nothing more than entangled vines.
History & Mythology
A legendary Elder Dragon with a common place in folklore, until irregular geological shifts confirmed its existence to the Guild, the Dalamadur was thought to merely be a fairy tale. Throughout the many legends and stories collected by the Val Habar Guildmaster from across the land, the inclusion of a mountainous serpent remained a constant, with each and every one specifying the same location. Since ancient times, these fairy tales have spoken of the Dalamadur, which was named the Serpent King Dragon by virtue of its snake-like appearance. It is said that it is a "King who sings of a thousand ancient times," and more akin to a natural disaster than a living creature. One particular tale of Cathar —born from the icicle-like shape of the sacred Mt. Tenku —tells of a great, wounded serpent reshaping the peak in its agony. This same story was passed onto the Guildmaster, who himself later passed it unto a famed Caravan Hunter.
These numerous tales and myths scattered throughout the land are the reason for the Dalamadur's discovery in the modern day, as once the Guild began receiving reports of unusual changes in the terrain near Speartip Crag, the Guildmaster was quick to relate them to the legends. This prompted multiple investigations into the fairy tales by the Guild, which ultimately culminated in bringing the legends of the Dalamadur into reality. During the process of investigating the validity of the myriad stories, a sketch drawn by a member of the Scriveners was unearthed. It illustrated an unidentified species that bears a striking resemblance to the Elder Dragon in question, depicting a serpentine monster of great scale that sported four limbs and was covered by copper, tooth-like protrusions all over.
Beyond the shores of the Old World are documented remains of the Elder Dragon within the New World. Making up the Rotten Vale, as well as sections of the Rotted region of the Guiding Lands, lie several gargantuan skeletons that have been reported by hunters to belong to the Dalamadur. It is presumed the originators of the remains must have died in the region long ago in ancient times on account of the Dalamadur being spoken of only in fairy tales up until its recent discovery, although it is not known why they are there. Long ago, after an ancient Dalamadur had died in the New World, the Old Everwyrm emerged and created the Rotten Vale by shifting the terrain through seismic activity where the ancient Dalamadur had died. However, the foundation of the valley's ecosystem would only be established once several other Dalamadur crossed to the New World at a later point in time and similarly perished. Considering the size and age of the remains, it is currently unclear as to whether the skeletons originate from ancient Dalamadur individuals—who perhaps reached the Vale and grew in size—or if they instead belong to a related species of yore. Finding an answer has proven to be difficult, however, as several of the skeletons overlap with one another, further muddying any attempts at verifying the truth.
Recently, a lone Dalamadur skeleton of equivalent size has been discovered in the Forbidden Lands, embedded in the mountains of the Wounded Hollow and stretching across the valley of the Grand Hub. It is currently unknown how it relates to those in the New World, or what history it has in the Eastlands.

Physiology
The Delex is a small Piscine Wyvern adapted to living exclusively within the sands of deserts. Its body is covered in tan scaling that is counter-shaded lighter on its underbelly, while its back is patterned with cyan stripes. Unusually for a Piscine Wyvern, the Delex completely lacks any form of legs, instead only possessing a pair of slender pectoral fins as well as a small anal fin. In addition to these, it possesses two dorsal fins, with the front fin being significantly smaller than the back fin. The fins are said to be exceptionally strong compared to other fish, propelling the wyvern through the sands as if it was swimming through water. Its head is long and slender, its jaws filled with several thin and conical teeth. The Delex possesses an exceptional sense of hearing, although this often results in it having an unfortunate sensitivity to loud noises that makes it highly vulnerable to Sonic Bombs.
Behavior
The Delex will typically travel in small schools consisting of around four to five other Delex, often tailing after larger monsters in order to scavenge on any food left behind. Notably, the presence of either of the sand-surfing Elder Dragons is often accompanied by a school of Delex trailing behind it. However, the Delex is capable of hunting prey if needed, with a pack typically surrounding a target whilst taking turns lunging at them; it can also spit sand swallowed and stored within its body at potential prey. However, if one member of the group is sufficiently hurt or killed, all of the Delex will immediately turn-tail and flee the scene to escape the potential threat. The Delex has been known to fall prey to the Jhen Mohran as well, with the guts of the wyvern being found inside of the Elder Dragon's jaws. As well, it may hitch a ride aboard hunting sandskiffs by leaping onto the deck and attacking the crew, although will usually hop off shortly after.

The Axe Beetle Desert Seltas (アルセルタス亜種, Aruserutasu Ashu) is a Neopteron introduced in Monster Hunter 4 Ultimate. It is a Subspecies of the Seltas.
Summary
An olive-green-and-yellow Seltas Subspecies with large forked horns. While equally fast in the air as the common species, Desert Seltas are also able diggers. The main difference between them and standard Seltas is seen in the fluids sprayed from the tip of their abdomen, which now have paralytic properties. They are often seen alongside their female mates, the Desert Seltas Queen.

Physiology
As a Subspecies, the Desert Seltas bears a close resemblance to the Seltas physiologically; its body is covered in a naturally thick and strong pale-gold shell that is granted additional strength through a bodily fluid secreted onto its surface. Unlike the single-pronged horned possessed by the Seltas, the Desert Seltas bears a two-pronged horn mottled by several blood-orange sharp spikes along its dorsal surface; the inner surface is notably sharp, rendering it especially dangerous. Additionally, the horn is prone to getting lodged into walls if the Desert Seltas charges into them at too high of a speed. As well as being used as offensive weaponry, the Desert Seltas utilizes his horn to burrow into and through the ground. The Desert Seltas possesses compound eyes colored a bright lime.
Much like the Seltas, the Desert Seltas possesses six limbs: four of these limbs are used for locomotion, with the front two are fashioned into a pair of scythe-like claws. The range of attack these forelimbs possess is notably greater in the Desert Seltas comparatively. On his back the Desert Seltas has a pair of thin, yet powerful wings—these properties make them a highly versatile crafting material. These wings are folded under his elytra when not in use, although the Desert Seltas does prefer to spend most of his time flying. The Desert Seltas contains several Paralysis Sacs inside of his body, allowing him to fire off globules of paralytic venom through the stinger on his abdomen.
Behavior
Despite his title, the Desert Seltas does not exclusively live in desert environments and has been seen inhabiting locations such as the Ancestral Steppe. The Desert Seltas spends most of his time burrowed into the ground, waiting for prey to pass overhead. Once a suitable target is spotted, the Desert Seltas will emerge from the ground and into the air to attack and subdue his prey. Once secured, the Desert Seltas will proceed to drag his meal back underground.
The Desert Seltas Queen is almost always seen alongside at least one Desert Seltas. She is capable of releasing pheromones from her underside to command and enslave the Desert Seltas, typically instructing him to rest atop her back in order to aid in combat. Despite the sheer difference in size, the Desert Seltas is strong enough to lift the Queen, being capable of even pulling her out of Pitfall Traps should the need arise. The relationship between the male and female Desert Seltas is notably even more intense than the common Seltas'. Alongside frequently cannibalizing her mate when in desperate situations, the Desert Seltas Queen will additionally utilize him as a projectile by violently firing him off from her back, shattering and killing the male upon impact.

Physiology
The Desert Seltas Queen is one of the largest known Neopterons and a Subspecies of the Seltas Queen. Her body is protected by a brownish-gold shell bearing several rows of pale spots outlined in brown down the front legs, claws, and back. The shelling covering her back is especially streamlined, aiding in directing blows away from vital areas to reduce the damage of impacts. Additionally, the outside of the body is coated in a dense layer of short hair-like structures that trap sand in the environment, helping to protect the Queen from the harsh desert sun. The Desert Seltas Queen possesses six limbs: four are used for locomotion while the front-most pair are fashioned into shield-like claws and mottled with red shelling around their perimeter. Believed to be an adaptation to shield the face from damage, the shelling covering her forelegs is especially thick. Alongside shielding her face from potential blows, these claws aid the Desert Seltas Queen in moving across otherwise tough to traverse terrain, with their beefy nature helping to improve her traction.
At the end of the Desert Seltas Queen's tail is a pair of exceptionally large scissor-like blades coated in several spikes on their inner edge. These pincers are notably elongated compared to the standard Seltas Queen's, with the Desert Seltas Queen displaying greater proficiency at using them in combat. The hairs coating these pincers allow them to detect subtle vibrations within the sand, allowing the Desert Seltas Queen to easily locate both Desert Seltas and potential prey buried underground. She will then utilize her pincers to forcefully rip them out of the ground; this strategy prevents her target from escaping, no matter what it does.
The Desert Seltas Queen contains several Aqua Sacs inside her body that store and produce the Neopteron's Water element in the form of a circulatory fluid used to produce a highly potent acid. The back of the Desert Seltas Queen's mandibles contain a secretory organ to release this acid in the form of several large balls of water similar to a cannon, hence her nickname of Cannon Beetle. However, much about this particular apparatus remains the subject of ongoing research. The Desert Seltas Queen is additionally capable of releasing pheromones from her underside to attract any nearby Desert Seltas towards her and enslave them to work under their Queen.
Behavior
The Desert Seltas Queen is always accompanied by at least one male Desert Seltas. Compared to the common Seltas species, the Desert Seltas Queen is noted for her more violent temperament, both towards opponents and her own mate. Once the Desert Seltas Queen has summoned a Desert Seltas to her side using her pheromones, she will forcibly grab him using her extended pincers and inject him with pheromones, enslaving him in the process. This causes the crescent pincers to become coated in a layer of pheromones that must be removed should a blacksmith wish to work with the material. Despite the sheer difference in size, the Desert Seltas is strong enough to lift the Queen, being capable of even pulling her out of Pitfall Traps should the need arise.
Much like the Seltas Queen, the Desert Seltas Queen will not hesitate to kill and cannibalize her own mate if she grows too tired. In addition to this, by grabbing the Desert Seltas with her pincers and applying a high-amount of water pressure onto him while he is resting on her back, the Desert Seltas Queen is capable of firing her mate like a cannonball, shattering his body upon impact. Upon doing so, the Desert Seltas Queen will simply grab another Desert Seltas out from under the ground as a replacement, immediately placing him back onto her back.

Physiology
The Deviljho is a large, bipedal Brute Wyvern that closely resembles the typical build of its class. Its compact torso is wrapped in bulbous muscles and covered by dark-green scales, with the largest muscles forming a hump over its shoulders. A line of small spikes runs down the spine and powerful legs hold up the body. The arms are tiny by comparison, and each ends in two fingers tipped with dull-red claws. A row of spikes runs down the length of the tail's top and bottom, with two more lines on each side.
The Deviljho has a wide head with a rounded snout; its eyes are small and yellow with slit pupils, and above is a pronounced brow. Unlike most Brute Wyverns, the Deviljho lacks any horns or crest atop its head, instead, it sports very robust jaws. The jaw adductor muscles are bright pink and well-developed. The area behind the adductor muscles lacks scales, which gives the illusion the Deviljho's mouth continues into the neck. Rows of razor-sharp teeth line both the inside and outside of the maw, and are much more concentrated at the front of the mouth. The Deviljho continuously grows more teeth throughout its life, and will rub its jaws on the ground to remove teeth that are old or damaged. This action leaves chipped fangs in the ground that Hunters may use to track the Brute Wyvern.
The Deviljho's muscles are extremely large and dense, granting it terrifying strength. The Deviljho is easily capable of breaking through fallen trees, launching boulders, and lifting other large monsters. Its legs are powerful, able to cause small tremors from the force of its stomps. The Deviljho has a faster metabolism than other wyverns, allowing it to be active for longer periods. However, due to its fast metabolism and large muscles, the Deviljho requires an exorbitant amount of calories and is persistently hungry, causing its mouth to constantly drool. Its saliva is highly acidic, able to melt through the armored shells of other monsters and even deteriorate the steel plating of a hunter's armor.
When enraged, adrenaline causes the Deviljho's body to go into overdrive and increase blood flow, swelling the muscles and making them glow red. The most notable effect is that the Deviljho will begin to produce Dragon energy, breathing streams of Dragon element vapor upon its opponents. There is a cost to this additional power, however, as the swelling causes the skin to tear and reopen old wounds. Additionally, if the Deviljho is to sustain significant damage to its chest, it can result in its Dragon abilities completely shutting down, albeit only temporarily.
The physique of individuals found in the New World differs from those of the Old World. The New World Deviljho is generally more muscular—particularly in the head and neck region—however, its chest is leaner. The reason for this increased muscle mass is unknown, although it may be related to the tendency New World individuals have of carrying large prey in their jaws. Like most monsters in the New World, the Deviljho can become Tempered, however, instead of becoming Tempered by absorbing bioenergy, the Deviljho may become Tempered if its diet is rich in Streamstones.
Behavior
The Deviljho is primarily driven by its insatiable hunger and endlessly wanders in search for more prey, using its strong sense of smell to search for food. The Deviljho's prey selection includes small Herbivores, large wyverns, Elder Dragons, and even its own kind. The Deviljho will pursue any creature indiscriminately. Smaller prey is swallowed whole immediately, whereas larger prey has to be torn apart before consumption.
The Deviljho is a nomadic species, it will often enter any habitat and rapidly deplete the monster population, disrupting the balance of the environment. Due to cases such as this, the Deviljho is considered a threat on par with Elder Dragons. Even the sight of the Deviljho imposes fear in other monsters. Fortunately, its tendency to travel and short lifespan make it as rare as Elder Dragons as well. The Deviljho has been observed to hunt the apex monsters ruling the location it invades, it may also take the former ruler's nest as temporary shelter. Against Flying Wyverns, the Deviljho will counter their aerial attacks by seizing them in its jaws and slamming them against the ground. The Deviljho's violent nature has earned it many names, such as Gluttonous Demon and World Eater.
Despite the Research Commission surveying the New World for four decades, it wasn't until a surge of bioenergy invigorated life across the continent that the Deviljho was first sighted. The Brute Wyvern likely evaded detection by living in yet-undocumented regions of the New World, however, how it came to the continent in the first place is unknown. Currently, there are two hypotheses: the Deviljho had only recently migrated from the Old World, or another monster partaking in the Elder Crossing inadvertently transported Deviljho eggs with it.
Once the Deviljho's prey is firmly in its maw, it will throttle and slam it on the ground. Regardless of whether the prey dies or not, the Deviljho may walk around with its meal still in its jaws. If it spots another potential prey item, the Deviljho becomes so excited it forgets it already has a meal in its mouth and will pursue the new target. It will use the creature in its mouth as a brutal weapon, slamming its new target with its old prey and causing significant damage to both.
Although usually unmatched, the Deviljho of the New World is in fierce competition with another volatile monster, the Bazelgeuse. Both species are powerful monsters that roam across the continent and decimate the local ecosystems they reside in. When the two meet, they engage in brutal territorial battles that send other creatures running. This makes it harder for the victor to find prey when the fight is over.
Super Biology Information
The Super Biology Book Series collects the thoughts and theories of real scientists that were asked to speak about monsters from the Monster Hunter series. Thus, they are inherently speculative and should be seen as such.
Fossil Expert Yoshitsugu Kobayashi takes a look at the Deviljho’s maw and notes that the monster’s appearance and description imply that it is polyphyodont, meaning that it continuously sheds and regrows teeth throughout its life like many sharks. If those teeth were to regrow on a set cycle, one could determine the age of a Deviljho by analyzing a single tooth socket to see how many times a tooth has regrown. Kobayashi proposes the example that if the upper and lower jaws each house 30 teeth and a Deviljho were to live to 100, then each jaw would produce a staggering 3000 teeth over the course of the wyvern’s life.
On the matter of the wyvern’s body temperature, Kobayashi asserts that the absolute limit of any creature’s internal body temperature is 45 °C, as beyond that, structural proteins begin to denature and warp. The individual limit of any species is additionally related to the size and mass of the body. At roughly 20 meters in length, the Deviljho likely resides near the upper limit of what is physically possible.
When discussing the Deviljho’s cannibalism, Kobayashi explains that a species devouring one of its kin is more common in nature than one might think - it is even believed that Tyrannosaurus rex did it too. Usually though, cannibalism occurs in species with high population density, which does not seem to be the case with the Deviljho. Instead, Kobayashi proposes that cannibalism in Deviljho occurs simply as part of the natural food chain: Deviljho inherently see each other as prey, and thus weaker Deviljho get eaten.
It is evident that the Deviljho bears many similarities to the T.rex. Both are defined by strong, muscular hindlegs, near useless forearms and a thick long tail. Both are also associated with tremendous bite force. Just as the T.rex was a formidable predator that nevertheless did not “collapse” the ecosystems it inhabited, so too does Kobayashi believe that the Deviljho would probably not cause environments to fully deteriorate. After all, the Deviljho is part of the ecosystem, not above it.

Physiology
The Diablos is a powerful herbivorous Flying Wyvern and close relative of the Monoblos, although it grows to a notably larger size. It displays the typical body plan of its class: a large head held low by the neck, two arms modified into wings, a short torso carried by two legs, and a long tail, although its frame is beefier than most other Flying Wyverns. With the exception of its lighter underside and gray legs, most of the shelling covering its body is in shades of light-tan. These shells are incredibly dense and much heavier than would appear at first glance, with continuous exposure to sand further hardening this shelling. Its back is protected by several overlapping, upwards-slanting, disc-shaped plates whose rock-hard nature and extreme sturdiness make them especially difficult to carve off. Just like the rest of the shell, these plates harden over time by exposure to sand.
The most striking feature of the Diablos is its pair of massive twisting horns, granting it the nickname of "Horned Wyvern". They are incredibly thick and protrude outwards from the top of its skull before curving back together, with this shape making them ideal at clearing a path while digging. The exact shape and angle of these horns vary by individual, and some rarer shapes are considered to be more valuable than others. The Diablos' horns grow throughout the wyvern's life and tend to be notably longer in an older individual. When broken, the cross-section of the horns reveals concentric rings, with a greater number of rings also indicating an older individual. Behind its horns and at the back of its skull it sports a thick spiked frill. Unlike the beaked jaws of the Monoblos, it possesses a large mouth with long incisor-like fangs at the front of its mouth, as well as two large tusks that jut from its upper jaw. The roars it can let loose are especially loud, with some Hunters even reporting ruptured eardrums from standing too close to the roaring wyvern.
The Diablos' front limbs are modified into a large pair of wings supported by three fingers, and when attempting to intimidate potential enemies, it will spread out its wings to their maximum size. Despite this, it is unable to fly for more than a moment, with its wings instead primarily being used for digging; its impressive musculature allows it to burrow with incredible speed and fluidity. As the Diablos spends most of its time underground, it has relatively poor vision that it compensates for by possessing a strong sense of hearing, allowing it to perceive what is happening above ground whilst remaining below before thrusting itself upwards from directly underneath targets. However, this comes at the cost of sudden loud noises, such as those produced by explosives, startling the wyvern while it concentrates underground, causing it to surface and flail as if caught in a Pitfall Trap. Yet, when it grows especially angry, these loud noises no longer appear to phase it; this is believed to be the case due to its raw anger overriding any other form of emotion. The Diablos' legs are muscular with large plating over the thighs, allowing it to charge forward with speed despite its large size; its horns make these charges especially deadly, allowing it to easily pierce through rock. Its tail splits at its end, forming a twin-pointed club that serves as an excellent weapon against threats, possessing enough force to bend even steel hammers.
After recent discoveries, the bone marrow of the Diablos was found to possess powerful organic binding properties, which is believed to be responsible for the dense carapace that covers the wyvern's body. While its medulla is extremely difficult to carve, it is also of great value to researchers.
Behavior
The Diablos is a herbivore found almost exclusively in deserts, with it occupying a large territory marked by distinctive paired scratches made by its horns. Due to its remarkable sense of hearing, it has a strong dislike of loud noises, which causes it to spend most of its time secluded away inside caverns and only rarely leaving to feed. This dislike has led it to frequently attack any Noios from annoyance of their loud calls, bursting out from its lair and leaving behind deadly quicksand traps in its wake. It is famed for its highly aggressive territoriality, showcasing no mercy to anything that intrudes upon its territory, even up to its own kind. Unlike other Flying Wyverns, which typically choose not to interfere with other members of their species, the Diablos is famed for repeatedly engaging in battle with fellow Diablos. Males in particular frequently clash with each other, typically over either territory or mates. These fights consist of the males locking and bashing their horns together in a test of strength, the loser being decided by who is knocked over or concedes first and the winner proceeding to roar triumphantly. These conflicts may damage the horns of one of the combatants irreparably, making life significantly harder for that individual.
The Diablos' aggression is caused by its diet consisting predominantly of cacti, and in order to maintain its size it will monopolize vast swaths of land with abundant cacti patches. It will even chase off any other herbivore who intrudes upon its patches, ranging from Apceros to other Diablos. The Diablos feeds on the same patches of cacti five to six times a day, with this habit being suggested to be due to its preference for cacti with either high water content or an appealing taste—feeding on a diet of water-rich cacti allows the Diablos to forgo searching for bodies of water to drink from. The arrangement of its fangs allow it to easily gnash through the cacti's tough skin easily consume the juicy pulp inside. In the New World, the Diablos' biggest competitors for food are the minuscule Carrier Ants under its feet. These tiny insects feed on cacti without the wyvern noticing, at times diminishing the cacti patches by causing the plants to wither, forcing the wyvern to expand its territory even further.
During the breeding season, a mated pair of Diablos can be seen sharing a territory with each other peacefully. However, even during this relatively peaceful time, this relationship is limited to merely tolerating the other in its territory, with them holding no strong care towards each other. Around the time the female Diablos is about to layer her eggs, her coloration will darken and she will transform into a Black Diablos. Her aggression reaches even greater heights in this state and she will even treat her mate as an intruder, often leading to her chasing her partner out of her territory.
Due to its immense strength, the Diablos has few predators. It rules over its territory with an iron horn, attacking other monsters it comes across. Its ferocity has earned it many titles, such as the Tyrant of the Desert and the Lord of the Wildspire Waste, the latter by the First Wyverians of the New World.
Development
During the production of Monster Hunter: World, when it came to decide what kind of monster should rule the Wildspire Waste, Yuya Tokuda figured no monster fits the role better than Diablos. The collapsing sand pit was born from Kaname Fujioka’s desire for a hazard that rivaled the Ancient Forest’s waterfall that could also function a way to pit Diablos against other monsters despite its reluctance to leave its cave.

The Molten Black Dragon Dire Miralis (グラン・ミラオス, Guran Miraosu) is an Elder Dragon introduced in Monster Hunter 3 Ultimate.
Summary
Gigantic, black Elder Dragons that rarely emerge from the deep sea. Their flesh appears to be coursing with magma, with the resulting runoff from their body staining the water around them a deep red. Their wings resemble volcanoes and they, along with the spouts along their neck and tail, can eject flaming debris, wreaking havoc across a large area. Little is known about this beast, other than that its appearance spells disaster.
Main Series

Following reports of earthquakes in the Tainted Sea, the Guild sends out a research ship to investigate. Upon its disappearance, an entire fleet of ships accompanied by a battleship is sent out, which report Dire Miralis heading towards Port Tanzia. Recognising the threat posed to not only the port, but the entire region, the Hunter is requested to slay the Elder Dragon.
Physiology
The Dire Miralis is a gargantuan, legendary Elder Dragon likened to a living calamity, frighteningly little is known about it. It is amongst the largest known Elder Dragons, outclassed in size by only a handful of larger monsters, such as the Jhen Mohran and Zorah Magdaros. The Dire Miralis is clad in black scales and shells alongside a bright, magma-like fluid, called Gushing Magma. This fluid circulates throughout the Dire Miralis' entire body and spills from openings lining its spinal column, bestowing upon it an appearance akin to an erupting volcano. Each scale found on its body is eerily beautiful and has been likened to a "Burning Flower" as a result; together, they forge the Dire Miralis' fiery-black exterior. The rocky shells that formed along its spine—from its clustered horns to its tail end—arose from cooled Gushing Magma and are very hot to the touch. Similarly, its sharp, scorching claws cleave through victims like hardened flame.
Protruding from the Dire Miralis' back are two wing-like structures resembling cannons; incapable of lifting the giant Elder Dragon, they instead eject vast amounts of scorching hellfire high into the sky that rains down across entire areas as a barrage of molten magma. Embedded behind its hips is a large, scalding organ known as a Smelter that roils with Gushing Magma. It is one of few vulnerabilities in the Elder Dragon's armor that, when destroyed, halts all circulation of the lava-like substance through its body, robbing the exterior of its glow. However, deep inside the Dire Miralis' body is the legendary Dire Dragongem, which is formed from the crystallization of the Gushing Magma. Mysteriously, the dragon's heart continues to somehow beat even after having been carved from the body.
Once enraged, the Dire Miralis can enter an armored state that greatly bolsters its defense, deflecting any attacks that come its way. During this state of near invulnerability, only soft patches of Gushing Magma and its glowing Smelter remain susceptible to attacks, however, should the main Smelter in its abdomen be damaged enough, the Dire Miralis will be forced to exit this state.
As a relative to the Fatalis, the Dire Miralis shares many similarities to the Black Dragon: its posture is identical when standing upright on its hindlegs and it utilizes similar physical and fire attacks, even sharing a similar naming convention for its eyes, ominously called the Miralis Evil Eye.
Behavior
The Dire Miralis has only been sighted roaming the depths within the Tainted Sea, an expanse that was seemingly destroyed in the past by the Elder Dragon, although is otherwise considered a peaceful stretch of ocean. Due to the Gushing Magma constantly spilling out from the Dire Miralis' body, it creates pockets of blood-red water whenever it appears, commonly seen on the beaches that serve as the sites of battles against the dragon. Little else is known about its behavior as the Dire Miralis remains a mystery to this day, with even the greatest scholars of the Guild merely knowing it only as a monster from legends.
History and Mythology
Feared as the Lord of Hellfire and Calamity, the Dire Miralis is heralded as both the giant who birthed creation, and the devil fated to destroy the world. A legend of Port Tanzia says "When the sea turns red, a legendary monster appears," affirming that the Dire Miralis is the same Elder Dragon the original builders of Tanzia battled against in the Tainted Sea, which is how the legend was passed down. The sea turning red was initially a rumor which has since been confirmed, with the Dire Miralis being believed to be the cause behind the phenomenon.
It is an Elder Dragon that was only found in legend and whose existence wasn't officially confirmed until the Guild sent an observation vessel into the Tainted Sea to investigate the cause of various earthquakes. The research ship went missing soon after, prompting the Guild to send a fleet of ships protected by a battleship in search of it. The fleet reported the presence of the very same Elder Dragon that once brought ruin across the land, terrorized the port town, and sunk several islands long ago, managing to alert the Guild of it approaching Tanzia before it too ominously vanished without a trace.

The background context for the ecology video was that the Observatory Boat saw red spots popping up in the ocean, when suddenly Dire Miralis rises up, sweeping the boat away.

Physiology
The Dodogama is a medium-sized Fanged Wyvern with a pudgy build. The scales of its large expandable belly are white, while the dorsal scales are a pleasant blue patterned with orange stripes that run from its shoulders to the tip of its tail. Three rows of small dermal spikes and lateral spines line the sides of the belly, and the front limbs are particularly muscular. The Dodogama's diet consists of an assortment of rocks and minerals, although it holds a preference for dragon crystals—crystals that are naturally formed in the Elder's Recess —which are particularly rich in energy. The rubble consumed by the Dodogama is stored in its mouth cavity, where the minerals are broken down into nutrients. The energy from the dragon crystals is consumed, while the excess substances remain stored in the monster's jowls. The dragon crystals the Dodogama devours mix with its saliva and form explosive rocks that are spat at foes, however, the rocks are extremely volatile and are prone to detonating when jostled.
The Dodogama's body temperature is higher than other monsters due to the chemical processes needed for it to process its diet of rocks and minerals. The reaction that occurs between dragon crystal minerals and the monster's saliva generates a significant amount of heat. Thus, due to a lack of thermoregulatory organs, the Dodogama must manage its body temperature by expanding its stomach and increasing the surface area of the skin that makes contact with the ground. By doing this, the Dodogama is able to offset some of the excess heat produced by the processing of rocks.
The jaw and throat of the Dodogama is covered in thick shell plates. These shell plates are heat and explosive resistant, and form a shovel-like shape when the Dodogama opens its mouth, allowing it to gorge on rocks and dragon crystals. Its lower mandible features a powerful muscle that lets it carve dragon crystals from the ground, and the jaw makes up for 30% of the Dodogama's body weight. The position of the plates that line its jowls change with the stretching of the skin: the plates form a seamless shell that protects its throat and jaw when its stomach is empty, and as it stores rocks and in its mouth cavity, the skin stretches and exposes the soft flesh beneath the shell plating. Due to the exothermic chemical reaction that occurs as the Dodogama processes its food, the lower jaw glows red when it has stored the maximum amount of rocks it can.
Behavior
Unlike other Fanged Wyverns in the New World, the Dodogama is solitary in nature. It is believed that due to its ore-based diet, the Dodogama would not benefit from a pack lifestyle. Despite its harmless appearance, the Dodogama is not docile and will aggressively attack enemies with its brute strength. When confronted, it will release a barrage of explosive rocks from its mouth to scare away any potential enemies, including monsters larger than itself. It can often be seen patrolling its territory with its mouth full in preparation for encountering another monster. If its initial threat display does not deter its opponent, it is quick to flee.
The Dodogama will dig small ditches in the ground and bury the majority of its body in order to sleep. Sleeping in these small holes allows it to blend into its surroundings while protecting its vulnerable stomach.

While typically solitary in the Scarlet Forest, they are known to form packs in the Windward Plains led by an alpha, distinguished by its greater size and deep-red patches on its mane. When weakened, Doshaguma will enter a state of brutal rage, causing their muscles to swell and opening up old wounds.

Physiology
The Doshaguma is a large, brown-furred Fanged Beast with a quadrupedal gait and a bulky, ursine body shape, although it is capable of adopting a bipedal stance for periods of time. Its furless face is flat and wrinkled, and is adorned by a large mane of fluffier fur. Its giant, slobbering maw is beset by a pair of tusks capable of chewing through flesh and bone, and beneath the many folds of its wrinkled face hides a pair of small, beady eyes. The Doshaguma's heavily muscled forelegs are covered in rough, studded hide, and each paw is armed with five claws capable of easily cutting through skin, muscle, and tissue without chipping. Its upper back has a distinct hump, formed by the muscles connecting to its forelegs to give the beast its immense strength; sufficient anger can cause old wounds to tear open from the swelling of its muscles.
The stiff and bristly texture of the Doshaguma's fur makes for a durable crafting material, and so tempered by harsh climates that it is more akin to armor. While its hide similarly bears countless scars from a lifetime of brutal conflict, the fur and hide on its stomach is weaker in comparison and may be targeted when it is exposed as the Doshaguma rears up on its hindlegs. The tail of the Doshaguma is of moderate length and minimal thickness.
The female Doshaguma is considerably smaller than the male and additionally lacks a large mane and the muscular hump atop her back. In contrast, the Alpha Doshaguma can be identified by its much larger size and striking red mane in comparison to the standard Doshaguma.
Behavior
Brutish and aggressive, the Doshaguma is ferociously territorial and will attack any interlopers on sight, overwhelming enemies and prey with pure physical strength. It is known to prey on Herbivores such as the Ceratonoth and Dalthydon, carrying them back to its lair in its jaws, and will even throw them at other foes in the vicinity. The Doshaguma's aggressive and predatory behavior often involves it in disputes with other predators of its habitats, such as the Balahara and Lala Barina. While the Alpha Doshaguma is a more dominant force in the food chain, it still needs to be wary of local apex predators, such as the Rey Dau or Uth Duna.
Although it is generally a solitary creature, the Doshaguma has been occasionally observed moving in a pack composed of other Doshaguma. As the Doshaguma is powerful enough to be self-sufficient, it is speculated it may join a pack solely due to the prospect of bringing down more powerful prey it would otherwise be unable to kill by itself. As a result of this, packs of the Doshaguma have virtually no cooperation nor unity, and the members are prone to violent infighting over food and resources.
On occasion, a larger Alpha Doshaguma may rally a pack of followers by using their superior strength to force the others to submit. Emboldened and kept in line by the Alpha's strength, these packs exhibit more aggressive roaming and predatory behavior, and are slightly more unified under the Alpha's commands. However, the death of the Alpha will cause the pack to fall into disarray and scatter in short order.
Doshaguma are typically found in the Scarlet Forest, but may roam into the Windward Plains in search of food, especially when in a pack.

Physiology
The Dreadking Rathalos can be distinguished from the regular Rathalos through his sheer size: with a body length of 24 meters, he easily dwarfs the common Rathalos. However, this is not merely an increase in stature, as from the wingarms to the wingspikes—as well as to the dorsal shells—the Dreadking Rathalos displays exaggerated physical features that appear to have all grown beyond their usual limits. He has also been noted to sport more accentuated patterns on his wing membranes.
While it is unknown how the Dreadking Rathalos comes to be, apart from his increased size, this Deviant is defined by two key physiological alterations. The shell of the wyvern is notably darkened and appears to have evolved to specifically repel elemental attacks, moreover, the Flame Sac of the Dreadking Rathalos is modified to produce a secondary substance in addition to the flame powder the regular species uses. This secondary substance adds viscosity and longevity to the fireballs the Deviant expels, allowing them to persist after landing on a surface and explode after a short period of time.
Behavior
Like with many Deviants, very little is known about the Dreadking Rathalos aside from his aggressive disposition. His status as a Deviant does not appear to limit his social standing, as the Dreadking Rathalos has been observed coexisting—and potentially pairing up with—both the regular Rathian and the Dreadqueen Rathian. Due to the threat the Dreadking Rathalos inherently poses, his appearance is an emergency that may only be dealt with by Wycademy Hunters who possess a Special Permit, as is the case with every other Deviant.

Physiology
The Dreadqueen Rathian resembles the standard Rathian in her rough body shape, although displays some significant differences. The scales and shells of the Dreadqueen Rathian are a dark-green with various purple hues, quite unlike the pure-green seen in the standard Rathian. The tail's tip is also much spikier, growing larger and denser bundles of spines.
The Dreadqueen Rathian appears to have a highly increased rate of poison production, and the poison created in her body is many times more deadly than the poison produced by the regular Rathian; this improved poison may hang around in the air in a gaseous form after it has been expelled. Furthermore, the tail spikes are able to detach from the tail tip quite easily, impaling the ground and oozing out both liquid and gaseous poison into their immediate surroundings.
The Dreadqueen Rathian's poison production is so extreme that the compounds leak into every part of her body, seeping into her shell and oozing from the gaps between her scales—this is believed to be the reason for her darkened coloration. As a result, the Deviant's scales are incredibly poisonous to the touch and can only be handled by highly skilled blacksmiths.
Behavior
Very little is known about the Dreadqueen Rathian's behavior, although she has been observed spending time alongside her regular counterpart on rare occasions. Due to the threat the Dreadqueen Rathian inherently poses, her appearance is an emergency that may only be dealt with by Wycademy Hunters who possess a Special Permit, as is the case with every other Deviant.
Development
The core design idea behind Dreadqueen Rathian was to depict a Rathian with superior poison abilities. The tail was made spikier to emphasize the concept of the spikes falling off and sticking into the ground. This idea originated from the a concept of a Rathian that could stick its tail spikes into the ground to produce a poison swamp on demand.
Much thought went into how to keep this Deviant dangerous even for experienced players. The design team thought that poison was not a particularly hard status to deal with, and so devised the Noxious Poison ailment to challenge even veteran players. This is also the reason why the Poison Immunity Skill was changed to Poison Resistance, in order to prevent players from fully negating the Dreadqueen's poison too easily.

Physiology
The Duramboros is a massive Brute Wyvern covered in a brown armor shell. Atop its back grow two distinct humps that sit even higher than the top of its head, which itself is crowned with two large, curved, yellow horns that taper into dull tips. On the underside of its body, the Duramboros grows tufts of shaggy, brown fur. Perhaps the most impressive trait of the Duramboros is its long, powerful tail that is tipped with a massive, boulder-like growth interspersed with sharp shell edges. While the front limbs of the wyvern are small, the hind limbs are muscular and thick, able to hold up the heavy body reliably.
The shell of the Duramboros is quite unusual; composed of multiple brown scales overlapping into wide plates, the shell produces an uneven surface that is sturdy, yet flexible. This uneven shell attracts all sorts of smaller organisms, ranging from moss to mushrooms, that then grow on the Duramboros' body. Their presence aids in insulation, moisture retention, and even shock absorption, however, the organism layer on the shell cannot entirely negate the Duramboros' natural weakness to cold temperatures. The exact species of moss and fungi that grows on the Duramboros varies from region to region.
The Duramboros' most vulnerable physical feature is its pair of humps. While they are protected at the top by a thin, yet durable armor plate, they are ultimately made of soft flesh and are quite sensitive as a result. The humps serve as fat storage for hibernation purposes, although they can also be accessed as an emergency energy supply if necessary. Should such dire circumstances arise, the humps will expel sweat to cool down the body, the heat produced will then evaporate the sweat and produce vapor clouds above the raging Duramboros. Due to their high fat content and soft tissue, the Duramboros' humps are prized as a delicacy.
The most impressive weapon the Duramboros possesses is its massive, heavy tail that is tipped with a large sphere. This hardened shell sphere is solid enough to crush just about any enemy it directly impacts. In addition to its sheer weight, the tail tip is adorned with sharp shell discs that add a cutting edge to the tail's blunt force. These discs are known to grow for as long as the Duramboros lives, and have even been observed fully regenerating after being broken. Aside from the tail, the Duramboros able to use its massive horns to defend itself, however, they are not nearly as powerful as they might appear to be at first. The Duramboros' horns are direct extensions of the skull bone, with their bases connecting almost directly to the cranial cavity in which the brain is located. Should this base shatter, its splinters could easily find their way into the brain and cause major—or sometimes lethal—damage. Even minor impacts to the horns can cause temporary dizziness, for this reason, the Duramboros generally avoids fighting with its horns.
The pitifully small arms of the Duramboros are believed to be vestigial. While they once may have held a purpose, they have degenerated into being nearly entirely useless, serving only as an aid when the wyvern gets up from the ground after laying down. The Duramboros possesses four stomachs that maximize its ability to digest its signature diet, which consists of wood. For unknown reasons, the Duramboros produces an entirely unique type of mineral within its body called Durambolite.
The Juvenile Duramboros hatches from an egg and is, at most, two meters long at birth. It cannot yet digest plant matter and must spend its earliest years feeding on mushrooms, nuts, and the dung of the adult Duramboros. Aside from its size, a juvenile can be easily distinguished by its uneven tail tips, which it must shape into a sphere by smashing it into the ground at various angles over the course of its adolescence.
Behavior
The Duramboros can be found in forest regions where it stakes out territories that it defends violently if it senses an intruder, however, it is not considered an aggressive species under normal circumstances. While it is fairly active during the warm months, the Duramboros will dig itself underground and enter hibernation during the cold seasons. During its active periods, the herbivorous Duramboros will exclusively feed on wood, and different individuals will prefer different kinds of trees. The Duramboros will judge the quality of any given tree first by smell, followed then by rubbing its tail against it, observing how the wood reacts to pressure. Once the Duramboros has found a type of tree that it likes, it will jealously repel any interlopers from getting near it—this massive wyvern needs an enormous quantity of wood each day, and it is not keen on sharing. However, the wood is not all it is after, as the Duramboros also feeds on the many different insects that live on trees, crushing their bodies into an enzyme-rich fluid that aids in digestion. During lean periods, the Duramboros has even been observed eating the moss off of its own body.
For most of the time, the male and female will Duramboros live apart. While the female congregate in large groups consisting of other females, the male Duramboros wanders the wilds alone—it has been ascertained that the solitary males are who the Hunter's Guild deals with. Should two males meet, comparisons of the arrangements of plants and fungi on the shell serve as a way to determine the social hierarchy. Further, the shape and size of the horns is also considered a determinant of sexual fitness and can additionally aid in establishing dominance between males. Should none of these features be enough to definitively determine a dominant between the two, the male Duramboros will escalate into a physical conflict. Due to the risk of brain damage, they will typically forgo actually clashing horns, choosing instead to dig up soil with them and fling it into the air to demonstrate their horns' size and power.
The juvenile Duramboros will spend its youth in the female groups, being raised communally by a cohort of mature female Duramboros. Upon reaching its mature size, however, the Duramboros leaves its original group and ventures into the wilds.
Super Biology Information
The Super Biology Book Series collects the thoughts and theories of real scientists that were asked to speak about monsters from the Monster Hunter series. Thus, they are inherently speculative and should be seen as such.
Fossil Expert Yoshitsugu Kobayashi observes that the large curved horns of the Duramboros are similar to those found in many species of mountain sheep. He ponders that while these horns likely developed initially for combat purposes, evolutionary pressures selected for increasingly large horns, until their utility as a display feature to mates and rivals alike became more central. Ironically, the horns that developed to win fights now likely serve to prevent them, by intimidating would-be adversaries into submission non-violently. As for the structure of the horns, Kobayashi proposes that they likely consist of a bone growing out of the skull, which is then encased in layers of keratinized material. The tail likely consists of a similar arrangement.
After considering the various physical adaptations of the Duramboros, Kobayashi asserts that this species would likely have no natural predators: Its massive size, powerful muscles and highly developed defensive structures would render it nearly invincible. The fact that the Duramboros does not appear to be very aggressive supports this idea, as it would not have to fear many enemies. Additionally, the wyvern’s ability to store nutrients in its hump when they are abundant means that the Duramboros would not need to put itself in dangerous situations to secure food either, as it could just survive off of its stockpile during leaner times. Moreover, the hump might even allow this species to migrate regularly.

Physiology
Contrasting the Odogaron's sanguine coloration, the Ebony Odogaron's scaling is comprised of a variety of hues: its body and legs are toned a faint blue, while jet-black scales cover its feet, head, and run along the length of its spine towards the tail end where they transition to a rich violet. Its torso and shoulders are additionally speckled with patches of red draconic energy; this red accentuation helps to give the dark-blue color of its body an almost ominous appearance. As is the case with its counterpart the Ebony Odogaron possesses a unique claw structure, possessing four claw-like spikes alongside six true claws which are typically kept folded upwards until its becomes enraged. While the Vale acclimated Odogaron sports bone-toned claws, the Ebony Odogaron instead wields claws that have been stained red by the Dragon element coursing through its body. In addition to the deep lacerations its claws are capable of inflicting, the Ebony Odogaron is able to imbue its claw strikes with the Dragon element it has acquired, making its slashes especially dangerous; this ability alongside its appearance is what granted it the nickname of Wicked Claw Wyvern.
A distinctive trait of the Ebony Odogaron that only further solidifies it as a greater threat than the standard variety is its acquisition and usage of the Dragon element. Although its fangs and claws are inherently imbued with the rare element's properties, the Ebony Odogaron is most notable for its usage of the element in the form of a breath attack. Rather than simply expel the element the Ebony Odogaron appears to chew and swallow chunks of meat, infusing them with Dragon element internally before regurgitating them back into its mouth and spitting them at targets in a process similar to rumination. Having been infused with the Dragon element, strikes from the Ebony Odogaron's claws and fangs strip away the elemental abilities of its adversaries.
A monster capable of utilizing the Dragon element is considered extremely rare, and in the case of the Ebony Odogaron it is believed to stem from its diet. While the standard Odogaron is known to carry around chunks of meat in its jaws, the frequency and intensity of this behavior is greatly exaggerated in its Subspecies. Even as it is engaged in combat, the Ebony Odogaron will invariably carry meat when moving between areas and will satiate itself through the meat chunk once more after having arrived at a new location. After which, the Dragon element in its upper body will activate, bestowing it a terrifying visage: black smoke will escape from its jaws and a red light resembling lightning will cloak its upper body. This process, performed by a desire to enhance its capabilities to better battle its opponent, has been termed the Ebony Odogaron's Berserker State. The biological cost for this state appears to be excessively high and thus, while this frenzied state dramatically boosts its combative abilities, it is highly taxing to the Ebony Odogaron and will reverse if it grows fatigued or hungry. Further making it a double-edged sword for the Ebony Odogaron, should enough elemental attacks be accumulated on the head whilst it is wreathed in Dragon energy its Berserker State will be counteracted.
Behavior
Following the Research Commission's encounter with the Velkhana in the Elder's Recess, a "song" stemming from the Old Everwyrm was heard across the New World, causing numerous environmental anomalies all throughout that would result in a dramatic surge of encounters surrounding newly sighted Subspecies. While not a historically unprecedented event, the sudden appearance of previously undiscovered Subspecies shook the established research foundations of the Commission's expedition teams. Additionally, an increase in the amount of SOS Flares fired was noted, indicating a decline in the New World hunters' fighting strength. Previously undocumented variations of the Odogaron were amongst those included in the reports surrounding the emerging Subspecies; one exhibited individual was noted to possess what appeared to be bioluminescence in its tail and forelimbs, whereas another was encased with a golden shell devoid of any patterns, its head and tail seemingly mutated by the attributes of the Dragon element.
In the wake of the continent-wide disturbances, the Ebony Odogaron's presence was confirmed to span the entirety of the New World, believed to be the case notably due to its procurement of the Dragon Element. While expansion into a diverse variety of environments would ordinarily result in increased competition against monsters wielding an assortment of different elements, the Dragon element's well-known effect of weakening—or even nullifying—another's elemental abilities has allowed the Ebony Odogaron to expand its habitat range considerably. Although current reports confirm this expansion to have been successful, prior to the Ebony Odogaron's established territory range being known, there was concern of its appearances in other locales significantly affecting its behavior. Prowling endlessly in search of sustenance, the Ebony Odogaron demonstrates extreme ferocity and a particularly noteworthy territorial instinct. It has been sighted subduing the standard variety when in the Coral Highlands as well as attacking without hesitation when confronted even by Elder Dragons, such as the Blackveil Vaal Hazak.
The Ebony Odogaron's superiority to the standard variety is evident, demonstrating outstanding agility and skill in combat by maneuvering into blind spots and delivering successive strikes. This feral Subspecies unleashes relentless assaults, coordinates leaps and flanking maneuvers to deliver successive strikes, and instantly counterattacks; its powerful charges aimed at tearing into prey are also a grave threat during battle. The Ebony Odogaron frequently overwhelms and fatally wounds Hunters by utilizing its Dragon element in tandem with its agility. Whether influenced by the Dragon element, the Ebony Odogaron displays extraordinary barbarity and its acute movements are difficult to track with the naked eye. The method with which it makes use of its breath attack is also characteristic, as while most other monsters would aim directly at their target, the Ebony Odogaron will instead expel the infused meat chunks at the feet of its target. The power of the attack is not particularly noteworthy, although if one gets distracted by the breath attack and consequently loses sight of the Subspecies they may suffer a vicious blow from their blind spot. The Ebony Odogaron's enhanced agility and the Dragon infused chunks it spews make it an unmanageable threat, even for seasoned hunters.
Possessing several desired traits—a keen sense of smell, ability to traverse any terrain, broad territory range, and desire to relentlessly pursue prey—the Ebony Odogaron was chosen as the blueprint for creating a watchful sentry for the now decrepit Wyveria.

Behavior
The Epioth is a fully-aquatic monster found within both fresh and saltwater environments. It spends most of its time peacefully swimming about and feeding upon aquatic grasses and mosses, its primary source of food, and will frequently surface in order to bathe in the sun. It is typically a peaceful monster and very timid by nature, only ever retaliating if it is attacked. If it senses a threat approaching itself, it enters a state of panic and begins to swim around in incredibly haphazard patterns, although it appears not to flee the scene of said threat.

Physiology
The Espinas is a bulky Flying Wyvern known for its incredibly thick carapace, sharp thorns, and large nasal horn. Its green scales allow it to blend into the jungle and forest environments it inhabits, while the horn and many spikes that adorn its body keep it safe should the Espinas be disturbed, the tip of each one secreting a deadly toxin. These spines run all the way down to its powerful tail, which when swung is said to be able to crush the bones of other monsters and topple trees in a single blow.
Along with its many spines, the Espinas is capable of breathing a potent mix of fire and various poisons concentrated within its blood from ingesting poisonous prey, granting its fireballs potent paralytic and toxic properties. These fireballs will leave smoldering patches of flame and toxic smoke on impact.
When sufficiently disturbed and the Espinas gets agitated, the blood vessels residing within its carapace and webbing expand, becoming visible as pulsing red streaks all over the dorsal carapace of the wyvern's body and the underside of its wings. This increase of blood flow throughout the body softens the tough carapace that usually protects the Espinas and allows it to charge at its foes with increased ferocity.
Behavior
The Espinas is docile when unprovoked, often found lazing about areas such as the Jungle, where it consumes small prey such as Poisontoads or Hornetaur.
While resting, it will ignore most attacks against it as its carapace and array of toxic spikes ward off the attacker. If a smaller monster or Hunter rubs up against it, the Espinas may scrape either its head or tail from side to side whilst asleep.
When provoked, the Espinas will fight with unrelenting fury, using extremely violent physical charges and swings with its thorny body and prominent horn, or blasting them with a barrage of toxic fireballs. This level of aggression is usually unmatched within the locale, allowing the Espinas to fend off other apex monsters in its area, like the Nargacuga. Ordinarily no other monster dares to challenge the Espinas, although the Kushala Daora has been noted to fight with it over territory, with the Espinas sometimes being able to throw the Elder Dragon over its head and repel it.
Music
Main article: Espinas (Music)
"Endless Maze" is Espinas' theme. A similar situation to Rathalos, the HR100+ Great Forest theme "終わりなき迷路" was only associated with Espinas, and it was not until Monster Hunter Rise: Sunbreak that "Endless Maze" would be tied to Espinas itself in-game. It is the first theme from Frontier rearranged for a main series game.
Monster Hunter Frontier
Espinas' design was inspired by rose thorns. Made with the forest setting in mind, its behavior conjured of remaining still and retaliating against anything that approaches, much like the rose thorns. Its body is camouflaged and it doesn't move like a plant, as if it had been undiscovered. Humourously, in fact, Espinas was dormant in the concept stage for six months from the time the teaser image for the monster was created until it was actually added in the game.
Monster Hunter Rise: Sunbreak
When Yoshitake Suzuki was assigned as Director on Sunbreak, he decided at a very early stage when coming up with the monster roster, that he wanted to have a monster from Frontier. He explained that he was a fan of the game and had good memories playing it, and was sad to see the service ending in December, 2019. It was a server-operated online game, which meant that fans would not be able to play the game anymore, so Suzuki thought about what he could do for his fellow Frontier fans. Thus, Espinas was chosen to return.
Since Sunbreak is the follow-up to Rise, Suzuki had to carry over the general world design, gameplay, and systems. Within those constraints, he wanted to spice and freshen up the experience. Espinas fit that concept "to a tee", so he was very particular about making sure the monster was compatible with Sunbreak, while also preserving the monster’s visual image, ecology, and actions from Frontier. For example, Espinas is always asleep at the start of the quest. When the player starts attacking it, it will wake up, and in the original game, it would keep walking around unbothered by the player. However, since Sunbreak needed to preserve the quest tempo of Rise, the team made some tweaks and changed it so that it now immediately starts attacking as soon as the player wakes it up. The team also changed the thickness of its hide depending on it's enraged status, and they were aware of having to balance respect towards the source material with the needs and gameplay of Sunbreak. He had to keep compatibility in mind, so he firmly restricted the only Frontier monsters to be Espinas, and used all his passion as a fan of Frontier into the monster. Humourously however, Flaming Espinas was added in the second title update.
Suzuki was nervous when he showed the design document with all of the new elements, including Espinas' return, for Sunbreak to serie producer Ryozo Tsujimoto and Yasunori Ichinose, the Director of Rise, but they were both positive towards almost all of the elements Suzuki proposed, and was relieved.

Physiology
The Fatalis sports a slender, serpentine body covered by black scales, its front and hind limbs are well-developed, allowing the Elder Dragon to display both a bipedal and quadrupedal gait. The hind legs have been theorized to have structural similarities to those of a Wyverians. Its neck is disproportionately long, granting the Fatalis great flexibility in how it angles its head, which is crowned by two pairs of backward-facing horns; the larger front pair is notably more developed and holds immense strength, giving off a dark glow of disturbing allure. The black scales of the Fatalis have rings on them that evince the Elder Dragon's immense age, and each shell is comprised of multiple layers that make it impervious to standard weaponry, granting the Fatalis incredible defense. One especially noteworthy part of Fatalis' shell is the section covering its chest; the shell plate here is further hardened by having various metals—including the armor and weapons of fallen foes—melted onto it.
The Elder Dragon sports a third pair of limbs that serve as wings, each comprised of tattered membranes that stretch across the four wingfingers, along the arm, and down to the hip. They are as hard as any metal, yet still maintain a flexible and malleable quality, and despite their wrinkled and even slightly torn state, they appear to nonetheless function flawlessly for flight. Spikes of variable sizes run down the Fatalis' spine, starting at the back of the neck and continuing all the way down to the tip of the exceptionally long flexible tail.
A unique anatomical adaptation allows the Fatalis to inhale vast amounts of air and heat it with its internal body temperature to generate an extremely powerful kind of explosive flame unleashed with tremendous force, called the Kalpa Fire. When unleashed, the Kalpa Fire is extremely dangerous and can destroy nearly any kind of fortification, melting solid metal gates down to glowing heaps of slag within mere seconds. Over the course of a battle, the intensity of the Kalpa Fire can increase dramatically, growing so hot that it begins to visibly glow through the Elder Dragon's chest; at its most powerful, this devastating flame turns an incandescent blue. However, the Fatalis' Kalpa Fire is noted to weaken should its horns be injured or broken; it has been theorized that they contain within them the Elder Dragon's power.
The Fatalis' eyes are a striking orange in color and said to give off an ominous aura: hence their name, Evil Eye. They are crystalline in nature and considered one of the Three Great Treasures. Further, the Fatalis has been noted to not possess the characteristic Elder Dragon Blood —blood saturated with dragon-energy—differentiating it from other Elder Dragons.
Behavior
Very little is known about the Fatalis' behavior, although, it appears to hibernate in or near Castle Schrade for long periods at a time. Its presence seems to intimidate other monsters, as the movements of at least one Lao-Shan Lung were interpreted to be due to the Elder Dragon fleeing from the Fatalis. Conversely, there has never been any indication the Fatalis preys on other monsters.
In battle, the Fatalis appears to be somewhat cunning. It has been noted to use its fire attacks sparingly at first, gradually unleashing them more frequently as the fight goes on. Whereas once an enemy has proven themselves to be a real threat, the Fatalis begins using its fire rather liberally and will continually increase its potency. Additionally, it has a habit of sticking out its long tongue and licking its lips. However, its oddest behavior is its tendency to gather the weapons and armor of fallen enemies. It is believed that as the Fatalis sleeps on its hoard, its intense body heat melts the equipment onto its chest. This would explain the presence of metal on it, though some within the Guild argue this may simply be the result of the Elder Dragon dragging its body across the ground.
History & Mythology
The Fatalis appears throughout various myths and legends across the world, with fairy tales and nursery rhymes telling of a black dragon burning down the Kingdom of Schrade in a single fateful night, 1000 years ago. Stories of the Fatalis are especially prominent in the oral folklore of the Wyverians, although amongs the Hunter's Guild, only a handful of people actually believe it to be a fact of history. The word "Fatalis" is not actually meant to refer to a single creature. Rather, it translates to "Battle of Fate," and was originally associated with the concept of a legendary conflict. However, over time, the word became increasingly associated with the Elder Dragon itself.
The Fatalis' emergence is suggested to be somehow linked to the recent discovery and slaying of the Safi'jiiva. Additionally, at least one Guild correspondent theorizes the Fatalis may be otherworldly in nature.
