Main article: Fatalis (Music)
"The Legend Descends", previously known as "Alighting Legend", is Fatalis' theme. Its first released appearance is at the end of "The Time has Come" in the Monster Hunter Soundtrack Book. "The Legend Descends" directly uses a slower version of "Roar", which is the theme for Rathalos, simply adding vocals on top of the main melody. In Iceborne 's rendition, it is less of a direct copy and adds motifs from "Awakening", the theme for Kokoto Village.
In Monster Hunter World: Iceborne, a new track for Fatalis' second phase was added, named "Limitless Courage". It uses motifs from both World and Iceborne 's main themes, " Stars at Our Backs " and " Succession of Light " respectively. Once the Dragonator is used in the fight, "The Final Confrontation" (previously "The Final Decisive Battle") plays, which was originally used back in Lao-Shan Lung's third phase in Monster Hunter, and is a loop of " Proof of a Hero ".
When slain in Iceborne, "Triumph!" plays as the Quest Complete theme, instead of the Iceborne version.
Both of Fatalis' themes in Iceborne "The Legend Descends and "Limitless Courage" were voted among the Top 10 music themes in the Hunters' Choice: Top 10 Monster Themes - Monster Hunter 20th Anniversary.
Monster Hunter
Fatalis was designed by Kaname Fujioka.
During the development of the original Monster Hunter, two core plot elements were established early in the design process: A battle against a gargantuan dragon, and a high-difficulty online only boss monster whose equipment would serve as a trophy to show off to other players. While the former idea soon became the basis for the creation of Lao-Shan Lung, the latter concept spent much more time in the early development phase. It would eventually result in the creation of Fatalis.
Fatalis' visual design was always intended to resemble a western-style dragon and was finalized early on. The basic idea behind this decision was to imbue the monster with a sense of contrast: After getting used to fighting fairly grounded, ecologically believable creatures, the player would suddenly find themselves face to face with a dragon that seemed straight out of a fairy tale. Not only would that maximize impact, but it was also intended to make the player wonder about what other inexplicable beings might dwell in the Monster Hunter universe. This focus on contrast also influenced the design of Castle Schrade, the arena Fatalis is fought in. The rest of the game takes place in wild, naturalistic environments, so the arena was instead chosen to be made up of man-made structures.
One of the inspirations that Kaname Fujioka names for this decision was a conversation he had with another Senior Designer at Capcom about the character Haggar from the Final Fight series of games. The conversation revolved around how that character's design was just a large, muscular man without many unique features. However, by having this behemoth of a man stroll around the relatively realistic environments of the game, a sense of contrast emerged, making Haggar quite memorable to players without the need of a particularly unique design. Fujioka aimed to emulate this effect with Fatalis.
Monster Hunter World: Iceborne
While Kaname Fujioka was grateful that the endgame content for World centered around collaboration monsters, he also regretted that the team could not end it with their own monster. With the 15 th Anniversary of the series coming up, they released Fatalis with new art, and everyone speculated that it was going to be released. Taking all these into account, they decided to release Fatalis. Up until now, the gameplay has involved a series of complex exchanges, with players positioning themselves against unique mechanics and powerful attacks, like with Alatreon. However, with Fatalis, they wanted to create a monster that is worthy of being the final monster of World, and that it was firmly in line with the classic action tempo of Monster Hunter. They created a gameplay loop that required detailed movements, such as telegraphing to avoid attacks and positioning yourself in advance. They also developed Castle Schrade and designed the Fatalis fight around it, such as adding different ways to avoid its deadly breath attacks.

Physiology
The Fish vary drastically in size and appearance due to encompassing six distinct species of Monster:
The Sharq is relatively large, stout, and streamlined, sporting a white and gray countershaded body, a large mouth, and small horn-growths over its eyes. The skin of the Sharq is described as having a unique feel.
The Tuna —known also as the Perciforme —is small and slender with silver scales along its belly, dark-gray scales along its back, and long pointed dorsal and pelvic fins. Its body naturally produces Dash Extract.
The Jellyfish is colored blue with a soft umbrella-shaped body. Along its underside are several purple-tipped stinging tentacles equipped with a paralyzing venom. While normally relatively small in size, certain individuals may grow to be significantly larger.
The Arowana, more commonly known as the Burst Arowana, is small and narrow, covered in green scales with patches of orange. An anal fin lines roughly half its body length, and an elongated portion of its dorsal fin stretches over the fish's fluke. It is well known for its habit of exploding, which typically occurs upon the fish's death.
The Molid is tall and possesses a circular body that has been flattened vertically; it is notably short in length. It sports a pair of elongated bright-blue dorsal and pelvic fins that greatly extend its height.
Behavior
While the Guild collectively refers to these monsters as simply "Fish", in reality they are classified as separate organisms and each showcases their own distinct ecology. The Tuna and the Arowana are both classified as "migratory fish" and are effectively harmless to humans, the Molid and the Jellyfish are classified as "natatorial fish," and the Sharq is classified as a "carnivorous fish." It is comparatively much more aggressive and, as the classification would suggest, primarily feeds upon meat. While the Sharq is typically docile, if approached, it will respond by attempting to bite the intruder. The Gajau was similarly formerly classed as a "carnivorous fish," much like the Sharq. All Fish share a common trait of retreating if they have taken sufficient injury. As a result, if a hunter wishes to harvest parts from their body, they must utilize a Fishing Harpoon to finish them off and prevent them from fleeing. The Flooded Forest is known to serve as a breeding ground for the Arowana.

Physiology
The Flaming Espinas is a Subspecies that appears very similar to the original species, with the primary differences lying in its muted brown scales and fiery-orange spikes. Its shell has an incomparable rigidity that surpasses that of even the normal Espinas, and is additionally able to withstand intense heat, such as that from the Teostra's flame breath. When enraged, the Flaming Espinas will increase the blood flow to its hide, causing bright orange veiny patterns to appear on its dorsal plates and wing membranes.
Like the nominate species, the Flaming Espinas' body contains a highly potent poison that is expelled through its fire breath and spines, the toxicity of which is capable of withering trees with a mere touch. While this Subspecies no longer wields paralytic abilities, it is able to utilize a dense, highly concentrated acid said to melt anything it touches without a trace, corroding even the strongest of armor. This acid is believed to give the Flaming Espinas' fireballs more explosive properties, and in extreme cases, being able to devastate a wide area should the wyvern build up its flames beforehand. Unlike its poison, which primarily saturates the blood and is secreted through the spines, the Flaming Espinas' acid is separate from its blood and is stored in separate organs, being largely only being present in its fire breath. It is presumed the Flaming Espinas' acid stems from its diet, similarly to the nominate Espinas' paralytic toxin. However, which creatures it preys on to develop this acid remains under research.

Physiology
The Frostfang Barioth is a Barioth individual that has aged far beyond the species' usual limits and has survived unusually harsh conditions. It is a stage of life that only the strongest, most resilient Barioth may ever reach, as any weaker individuals perish long before becoming a Frostfang Barioth. This Variant can be identified by the additional patches of shaggy fur on the forearms and torso, as well as the icy-blue tusks covered in a permanent layer of wispy frost.
These physiological changes are derived from a peculiar phenomenon that occurs as the Barioth reaches this advanced age. The ice breath the regular individual is known for becomes increasingly more powerful, to the point where it is loaded with frost particles that actively freeze the ground as they are expelled. This enhanced ice breath appears to be the result of a more thorough mixing of the Frostfang Barioth's freezing liquid and the frigid air it inhales. This Variant wyvern additionally appears to grow a new kind of ice organ to allow for this astounding improvement to its breath attacks, however, due to the organ's tendency to decay near instantaneously upon the Frostfang Barioth's death, it has proven challenging to study so far. The Frostfang Barioth's body is thus adapted to the presence of this new advanced ice breath.
The additional fur this Variant grows is concentrated on the front of the body and likely serves to minimize adverse effects caused by the wave of extreme cold the ice breath causes. Meanwhile, the blue color and frost layer of the tusks seem to be the result of continuous exposure to the advanced ice breath, which has resulted in a permanent fusion of ice to form on the tusks. This layer can grow so thick that the Frostfang Barioth may try to scrub it off against cave walls due to the discomfort it seemingly causes. Furthermore, the core shape of the tusks appears to also change slightly with age, bearing an edge that is more suited to scraping frozen meat off of old cadavers.
Behavior
The Frostfang Barioth has thus far only been sighted in the Hoarfrost Reach. However, it is believed its native habitat is still unknown and that this Variant develops in the furthest north of the Hinterlands. An area thought to be where temperatures and prey populations are so low that the resulting struggle to survive pushes the Barioth to its limits and beyond.
When hunting, the Frostfang Barioth makes ample use of its ice breath's new ability to freeze the ground, laying traps for unsuspecting prey. Should such prey wander onto frozen ground, its movements will be impeded as the frost adheres to its legs. The Frostfang Barioth then kills its prey with a well-placed stab from its tempered tusks. In one instance, researchers carrying heavy equipment got caught up in a battle between the fierce Variant and the Velkhana. However, further verification of reports from this event is urgently needed.

Physiology
The Fulgur Anjanath is an Anjanath Subspecies that mirrors the build and external physiology of the nominate species, retaining its massive bipedal frame, powerful hind legs, and muscular jaws. In comparison to the normal Anjanath, the Fulgur Anjanath is covered by a slate-gray hide bearing a dark and jagged, striped pattern, as well as a mane of pale, silver feathers running along its spine to the tip of its tail. Starting from its midsection, its scales form a gradient that starts gray, shifts to pink, and finally to bright orange as it moves closer to its head, which has bright blue eyes and the same dark stripes as its body. Like the nominate species, the Fulgur Anjanath has a pair of gray dorsal membranes extending from the hip bones that resemble sails. These sails possess a dense capillary network used for thermoregulation, allowing the Subspecies to absorb heat and warm its body whilst sunbathing, or to cool itself down when its body temperature rises. The Fulgur Anjanath similarly possesses an indigo nose-hood that can be raised when agitated, exposing its enlarged nostrils.
The Fulgur Anjanath does not possess any organs capable of creating flames, instead, it utilizes special organs derived from muscle tissue that generate a potent electrical charge from its muscle contractions. These organs are concentrated in its mouth and dorsal membranes, causing them to become wreathed in electricity as the monster accumulates a charge; its enlarged nasal cavity additionally serves to store electricity. Due to the impressive strength and activity of its muscles, even simple motions will accumulate a comparatively large amount of electricity, as seen by sparks crackling whenever the monster bites down. When sufficiently charged up, the Fulgur Anjanath will unfurl its dorsal sails and nose-hood, and its feathers will all stand on end. The charge causes the sails to reveal bright, blue and indigo patterns resembling lightning, while the Fulgur Anjanath's nose-hood, feathers, and mouth glow with a brilliant luminescence.
By circulating the electricity through its body, the Fulgur Anjanath can stimulate and harden its already impressive muscles, greatly increasing its physical strength and resilience. As the charge overflows, the Fulgur Anjanath imbues its bites and physical blows with electrical discharges that increase their destructive potential. The Fulgur Anjanath will build up electricity faster the more agitated it grows, and has even been seen spontaneously entering a charged state when sufficiently enraged. When its body eventually reaches its charging limit during prolonged combat, it will explosively discharge all of its accumulated electricity at once, then revert to its original state. Moreover, it has been observed that attacks against the Fulgur Anjanath's head can dissipate its accumulated charge and make it lose its balance.
Similarly to the nominate species, the Fulgur Anjanath produces a yellowed mucus from its nasal cavity that can be expelled as a projectile attack. However, it has been discovered that this Subspecies' mucus contains a conductive property allowing it to be electrically charged when sprayed at attackers.
Behavior
The Fulgur Anjanath is a solitary carnivore and displays even greater aggression than its forest dwelling relative, roaming a significantly broader territorial range. Although it was initially discovered in the Hoarfrost Reach and believed to be adapted for camouflage in snowy locales, it has been reported in a shockingly wide variety of environments and climates across the New World. The Fulgur Anjanath's adaptability is believed to in part be owed to its robust thermoregulation system and voracious appetite, with it even being reported to consume tainted meat without any hesitation. It is theorized that due to there being few known Thunder elemental monsters endemic to the New World, there are equally few monsters adapted to resist electricity, allowing the Fulgur Anjanath to establish itself as a dominant force in a variety of ecosystems.
Like the nominate species, the Fulgur Anjanath uses its mucus to mark its territory and hunts small Herbivores —such as the Popo —within it, which it tracks using smell. Violently territorial, it will attack any perceived intruders or threats without hesitation and is frequently found in conflicts with other monsters, up to and including local apex predators. In combat, the Fulgur Anjanath seldom uses its electricity as a direct means of attack, preferring instead to utilize it solely to augment its unrelenting physical blows, which only grow in lethality as the wyvern continues to fight and generate electricity. As a result of the devastating, electrically-charged jaw attacks the Fulgur Anjanath employs during combat, it is known and feared as the Thunder Jaw Wyvern.
When inhabiting colder locales, the Fulgur Anjanath has been observed sunbathing with its dorsal sails flared out to capture heat from the sun.

Physiology
At first glance, the Furious Rajang simply appears to be a Rajang in its Battle Spirit State, clad in golden fur coursing with electricity. However, this seemingly mundane difference is, by itself, fairly significant; the Battle Spirit State of the regular Rajang is a trump card, a weapon used sparingly due to its enormous energy consumption. The Furious Rajang's continuous, uninterrupted use of this ability thus hints at the more profound physiological differences between this Variant and regular individuals. While it has not been definitively discovered how the Furious Rajang comes to be, most theories center around the only other physiological peculiarity of this Variant: the tail stump, which is short and deformed compared to the long tail seen in the regular Rajang.
It is well-known the tail of the Rajang serves to maintain, control, and disable the Battle Spirit State, so its deformed shape in the Furious Rajang is considered quite conspicuous. Further, it is generally agreed upon that it is the loss of the tail that causes this Variant's power to grow out of control and into a perpetually raging electric inferno. Thus far, the Hunter's Guild has proposed three theories as to how the Furious Rajang's emergence may be caused by the loss of its tail:
The fact the Furious Rajang is even capable of maintaining the Battle Spirit State for extended periods at all may be an indication this Variant already possessed unusually powerful latent potential since birth. Thus, it is feasible that its might eventually outgrew the tail's ability to contain it, leading to the tail being overloaded and essentially exploding off of the body.
As the aggressive and competitive disposition of the Rajang is well-documented, it is feasible that a raging Rajang may grow frustrated at its own limits and would subsequently—in a violent display of destructive ambition—tear off its own tail to unlock its body's full power.
Injuring the tail is generally considered the main way to incapacitate the Rajang and is a strategy used by both rival monsters and Hunters. For this reason, it is not impossible the Furious Rajang is the result of a Rajang being injured in battle and losing its tail, turning into a Furious Rajang on the spot. Whilst no Rajang has ever been witnessed turning into this Variant by hunters during battle, it may be possible this is simply an extremely rare occurrence.
However the Furious Rajang may come to be, the resulting creature is endowed with an extremely powerful body and tempered by a continuous flow of golden lightning. Its forearms' muscle fibers are as dense as metal whilst retaining their flexibility, and its muscles and joints are overall more flexible and dexterous than those seen in the standard Rajang, allowing for faster and more agile movement. The claws and fangs are significantly hardened, and the horns now pulsate with so much electricity they remain unsafe to touch even after being removed from the body. The electrified fur itself additionally undergoes changes due to the perpetual charge; the characteristic stripes found on the body of the Rajang fade over time due to the electricity, and observation of the stripes' degree of fading can be used to determine how long the Rajang has lived in this Variant state. The Furious Rajang's fur is so charged with electricity that it extends from its back in a form reminiscent of large spikes; it is questioned whether the fur itself generates the charge.
However, the most impressive physiological trait of the Furious Rajang lies internally, rather than externally. Due to the unending torrent of Thunder element within it, the Furious Rajang has pushed its own abilities beyond their limits, unlocking a completely unique weapon. By compressing and concentrating its electrical charge to an unfathomable degree, the Furious Rajang is able to generate Light Energy (気光, “kikou”), which is more powerful and focused than the regular Thunder element used by other monsters. By cloaking its body in this Light Energy as it grows enraged, the Furious Rajang is able to achieve a level of power that surpasses even the Battle Spirit State, activating a form in which both Light Energy and lightning arc in unison across its fur and through the air around the creature itself. In this Advanced Rage State, the Furious Rajang can use Light Energy to create thunderballs that fly in unusual trajectories, or inject focused currents into the earth to tear the ground beneath its adversaries asunder.
While the Furious Rajang's Advanced Rage State is extremely powerful, it does possess its weaknesses. In the absence of the tail, it appears the horns of the Furious Rajang take over the function of controlling the beast's power to some degree. Thus, significant damage to the horns will disrupt the Advanced Rage State. Additionally, use of this power and Light Energy in general appears to shorten the Furious Rajang's lifespan, as its body cannot bear the burden of such violent stimulation for very long.
Behavior
The Furious Rajang is an incredibly violent and aggressive creature that ruthlessly attacks anything it encounters. It has been noted to be aggressive beyond the point of natural survival instincts, and many believe it actively seeks to destroy its surroundings, regardless of any actual benefit to itself. Due to its mastery of the Thunder element and Light Energy, the Furious Rajang is notably more liberal in its use of weaponized electricity.
After being originally discovered by a fuel coal peddler traveling through a volcanic region, the Furious Rajang re-ignited debates regarding its species' classification; the Rajang at one point had been considered an Elder Dragon before being later identified as a Fanged Beast. The Furious Rajang, however, has since been observed facing off with and standing its ground against extremely powerful dragons, specifically the Ruiner Nergigante. As it appears to be an equal to an Elder Dragon that preys on other Elder Dragons in particular, it has been proposed the Furious Rajang specially should be classified as a "Super Elder Dragon Class" monster. While this has so far not happened, it has been discovered the Furious Rajang may at times feed on Elder Dragons, much like the Nergigante does.

The Dark Abyss Dragon Gaismagorm (ガイアデルム, Gaiaderumu) is an Elder Dragon introduced in Monster Hunter Rise: Sunbreak.
Summary
Once known only in myth as the "Archdemon of the Abyss", Gaismagorm is a colossal Elder Dragon with a hexapedal stance, boasting a unique folding jaw and enormous clawed wingarms able to dig through bedrock. Subterranean by nature, it is the true host of the Qurio swarm, which it releases to the surface to drain the life out of prey, after which they return and feed the beast. If facing an intrusion, Gaismagorm is able to wield the Qurio's stolen power for devastating explosive attacks alongside its vast physical strength.
Main Series
Monster Hunter Rise: Sunbreak: After being revealed at the end of Gathering of the Qurio, Gaismagorm is hunted as the final boss of the main campaign in the M5★ Urgent Quest: Proof of Courage. After clearing the quest, it can be fought again in the M6★ Hub Quest The Devil's Reincarnation. A Gaismagorm was responsible for the first Qurio outbreak in the Kingdom and the destruction of the Citadel, but was forced to retreat and recuperate after being defeated by a Primordial Malzeno that would later become the Malzeno threatening the Kingdom in the present. Following Malzeno's death, Gaismagorm would reclaim its Qurio and attempt to resurface again, only to be slain by the forces of Elgado and the Kingdom.

Following Malzeno's death, Gaismagorm would reclaim its Qurio and attempt to resurface again, only to be slain by the forces of Elgado and the Kingdom.
Physiology
The Gaismagorm is an incredibly ancient, gargantuan Elder Dragon sporting a hexapedal gait, somewhat similarly to the Gogmazios. Its hide is primarily gray with numerous bony ridges and twisted spines, with two pairs of particularly large spikes jutting out from its its back. Its entire body is lined with glowing, blue vents that are usually covered in layers of condensed Qurio energy, taking on a form resembling red crystals. The Gaismagorm is flightless and possesses two enormous, clawed arms in place of wings, which are dextrous and strong enough to tunnel through bedrock, grab and throw large objects, climb up sheer cliffs, and even allow the Elder Dragon to jump into the air despite its massive bulk. The physiology of the wingarms suggests the Gaismagorm was once capable of flight during ancient times, only to lose its wing membranes over time as its species adapted to a subterranean habitat. Its other four limbs are much smaller, largely only serving to support the monster's weight, while its large tail is thick and terminates in a five-fingered, clawed structure.
The Gaismagorm's head is stout and angular, and supports two twisted horns and a pair of beady, yellow eyes that glow red when the Elder Dragon is agitated. It has a remarkably unique jaw structure that causes its mouth to split apart when opening, forming a shape resembling a five-pointed star and revealing a bright blue interior; housed within is a barbed tongue flanked by countless small, sharp teeth. When sufficiently enraged and the inside of its mouth starts glowing red, the Gaismagorm sheds the layer of crystallized Qurio on its body, and its vents turn red and extrude feathery red plumes. Should it be angered even further, it will draw on more of the Qurio's power and become overloaded with energy, causing its vents to erupt with red flames. When unleashing its most devastating energy attacks, two massive plumes of Qurio energy will briefly fan out from its back, resembling a pair of flaming wings.
As the true host of the Qurio, the Gaismagorm allows the parasites to feed on its energy and use its body as a nest in exchange for being able to command them to gather nutrition and defend it. By consuming its swarm and their accumulated energy, it is able to create a crystalline shell around its body for defense, or directly wield the energy by expelling it from the vents in its arms and torso, as well as its mouth. This energy usually takes the form of explosive, crimson beams and blasts, powerful detonations augmenting its physical blows and mobility, or barrages of explosive Qurio crystals. As it consumes larger quantities of the Qurio and gorges on their stolen life energy, the Elder Dragon's ferocity increases accordingly, often indicated by it shedding its crystal shell and freeing up its vents to allow for an even greater output of Qurio energy. Its body has limits, however, and it may become overloaded if it absorbs too many Qurio at once, forcing it to shed its accumulated power with reckless abandon.
The Gaismagorm is blessed with immense physical strength and durability, able to shrug off multiple exploding Dragonators, falls from the surface to its nest, and blows of similar strength with only a brief interruption to show for them. Additionally, it boasts powerful lungs that can inhale or exhale massive amounts of air at once, which it uses to draw in or blow away targets, or suck up more Qurio to feed itself.
Behavior
The Gaismagorm's subterranean lifestyle and recent discovery left much of its behavior a mystery until recent times. When it requires energy, the Elder Dragon will dig out a large underground nest and create small pits through which it releases the Qurio to the surface. Once the parasites drain and consume all the life they can find in the area, the Gaismagorm collapses its nest into a massive sinkhole through which the Qurio return en masse to feed their host. Highly voracious, the Elder Dragon can depopulate entire ecosystems to feed itself, moving on to the next after an area has no more nutrition to offer.
Despite its aggressive nature, the Gaismagorm has a sense of self-preservation and can flee if disadvantaged, as it became more passive and hid from the Malzeno after suffering major injuries from their battle and the hijacking of its Qurio swarm, only resurfacing after the Malzeno was slain.
History & Mythology
The Gaismagorm was previously only known in Kingdom mythology as the Archdemon of the Abyss, spoken of in the legend of the same name. In it, the Gaismagorm was depicted as a demon that would surface to destroy the Kingdom should its people let their hearts fill with darkness, devouring the land and all its living souls before returning to the abyss.
When mankind is consumed by darkness, and the land falls into chaos... The Archdemon of the Abyss shall rise from the earth. The Archdemon shall devour the land, turning souls into wandering flames. And these wandering flames shall feed the beast and return to darkness. A story ends, another begins.
When mankind is consumed by darkness, and the land falls into chaos... The Archdemon of the Abyss shall rise from the earth. The Archdemon shall devour the land, turning souls into wandering flames. And these wandering flames shall feed the beast and return to darkness. A story ends, another begins.
The legend originated in ancient times when the people of the Kingdom heard a ferocious bellow from the bowels of the earth. Hundreds of years in the past, the Gaismagorm attempted to breach the surface near what would soon become the Citadel, although it was defeated and driven back underground in a destructive battle against the Primordial Malzeno defending its turf. As it nursed its wounds and created smaller craters to feed, the Gaismagorm would go on to create the large crater next to what would become Elgado Outpost in an attempt to surface again. However, it was stopped by the crater's flooding and the same Malzeno hunting it down, which had hijacked its Qurio swarm and become their host. The now corrupted Malzeno and the monsters agitated by its Qurio would destroy the Citadel, causing the Malzeno to be blamed for the anomalies and destruction. Although the Gaismagorm's echoing bellow could be heard even then, the Elder Dragon remained unseen and unknown.
The existence of the Gaismagorm was only properly documented roughly fifty years after the fall of the Citadel, when it had finished recovering from its wounds and regained control of its Qurio swarm following the death of the Malzeno that had once threatened it. After witnessing the Gaismagorm surface, proving the legend of the Archdemon was a reality, the Hunter's Guild named the beast and designated it as an Elder Dragon, before authorizing its slaying for the safety of the Kingdom.
At a later point in time, after the Gaismagorm had been slain, an additional part of the legend was discovered. This addition to the lore foretold that the Archdemon's awakening would summon the Demonlord, whose silver spear would purify the land and reduce it to ashes. This was later found to correspond to the Primordial Malzeno, which would appear in the wake of Gaismagorm's appearance; although initially believed to be aiming to destroy the Kingdom, the Elder Dragon's true intention was to purge the Archdemon and its Qurio from its territory.
Music
Main article: Gaismagorm (Music)
"Archdemon of the Abyss" is Gaismagorm's theme. As a monster with heavy ties to Malzeno, its theme, much like " Scarlet Feast ", also includes organs and vocals. After being reduced below a certain HP threshold (in the Urgent Quest, coinciding with Fiorayne's scripted knockdown), a looped version of "Proof of a Hero: Sunbreak Version" plays.
Development
As the final boss of Sunbreak and ultimate cause of the Affliction plaguing the story, Gaismagorm was designed to be a terrifying monster that would surprise players with increasingly frightening transformations as it neared death, along with incorporating elements like ballistae to make its hunt a more unique experience. To emphasize its malevolence and presence as a final boss, Gaismagorm's 3D model was designed to emphasize its sheer scale by ensuring even minor details were visible as the player drew near. Special emphasis was given to its wingarms and mouth, with the latter being designed to create a stark contrast between its closed and open state, while its transformations were also designed to evoke the feeling of an overwhelming evil, hence the overflowing flames in its final phase.
When designing Gaismagorm's sound effects, the team deviated from the typical formula for monsters, focusing more on the density and power of each individual sound created by the monster, as well as a roar designed to evoke the image of an unseen, terrifying behemoth. The writers were particular about the language used in Gaismagorm's Japanese introduction poem, using words invoking auspiciousness to create a contrast with the Archdemon and the threat it posed to humanity.

The Strange Face Tribe Gajalaka (ガジャブー, Gajabū) is a small Lynian introduced in Monster Hunter: World.
Summary
Tribal Lynians that wear ornate red masks and tan fur which obscures their true appearance, they are found throughout most of the New World, though their largest settlement lies within the Elder's Recess. Gajalaka typically hunt in small groups, utilizing a mixture of blades and throwing knives coated in various different ailments to impair their target, with some individuals even being known to use explosives; the color of their mask's markings denotes their preferred status. They are opportunistic attackers, typically waiting for their target to be downed before going on the aggressive.

Physiology
The Gajalaka is a small Lynian that resembles a human child, although they possess bright-red skin. Their head is bald with a pair of striking golden eyes, however the head is normally covered by an ornate red mask, with their eyes being visible through the mask's mouth. These masks are intricately decorated, featuring stripes and spikes along each side, false eyes and teeth, and are topped with a pair of horns. They are made to resemble a certain monster and, within the Gajalaka's culture, are a symbol of bravery in whoever wear them. Once a Gajalaka has located a mask which they particularly enjoy, they will wear it for the rest of their life. Behind the mask the Gajalaka sports a red headdress made out of feathers, while for clothing the Gajalaka typically wears a skirt, arm-guards, and boots, all of which are from straw.
A tribe of Gajalaka is lead by a Gajalaka Chief. Not only is the Chief typically larger than their fellow tribe members, his headdress is typically adorned with white fur instead of the usual red feathers, with additional tufts of white fur placed below the mask's fake eyes to give the allusion of a mustache. Additionally, the weapon he wields is often much larger and more elaborately ordained, and atop his mask lies a makeshift crown consisting of three stacked pieces of crockery with a ring of lit candles surrounding the base.
Behavior
The Gajalaka is found in caverns throughout almost the entirety of the New World continent. The Gajalaka found in the New World do not consist of a single tribe, instead there are various separated tribes scattered throughout the many biomes of the continent. One notable former hideout for the Gajalaka was located in the north of the Elder's Recess. However, when the Nergigante had failed to hunt its desired prey, it took refuge within the Recess due to the presence of many Elder Dragons in the area. As a result, it ended up utilizing the hideout as its lair, robbing the Gajalaka living in the area of their land and forcing them into the surrounding crystal caverns, most notably within the Lightstone Cave. The Gajalaka living in the Recess are said to still hold a grudge against the dragon and can therefore serve as invaluable allies in both the surveying and subjugation of the monster. However, even though one tribe of Gajalaka have allied themselves with a particular Hunter and cooperate with the Lynian Researcher, it will not stop other Gajalaka tribes on the continent from being aggressive.
Once robbed of their original hideout, the Gajalaka founded a secondary settlement within the Eastern part of the Recess, known as the Ritual Hall. The path leading from here towards their main Hideout appears to have been carved out by the Gajalaka themselves. Those living there have been observed converging and performing a dance-like ritual on a nightly basis, although they will still go on the offensive towards anyone encroaching upon their encampment while the ritual is being performed if they are spotted. The Gajalaka living here are known to keep Wigglers —creatures native to the Coral Highlands —inside of pots. A large shrine exists at the center of the hideout, decorated with a large assortment of different masks worn by the Gajalaka. Another tribe located in the Caverns of El Dorado, called the Golden Tribe, are known to coat their bodies and clothing with the gold dust from the Kulve Taroth, which they flock towards to gather from.
Considered warlike in nature, the Gajalaka is highly aggressive towards anyone who approaches their territory, considering them a target for elimination. Traveling in small groups, the Gajalaka will attack in unison anything that approaches them. Against larger targets, they are significantly more opportunistic, typically only going after them once their target has become impaired or knocked over in some way. In order to subdue their targets, they make use of a wide variety of weaponry. All Gajalaka wield short metallic blades decorated with simple patterns. These blades, alongside the throwing knives they use to hunt targets from a distance, are frequently coated with various toxins that can deplete health, inflict paralysis, or sedate their opponents. In order to delineate what type of weapon a Gajalaka uses, the patterns decorating both their weapons and their masks are color coordinated to match the appropriate toxin: health-depleting is purple, paralyzing is yellow, and sedative is cyan, while those who wield no toxins whatsoever decorate their masks with white stripes. In addition to blades, the Gajalaka can also attack with home-crafted throwing bombs. While explosives are relatively easy to craft in the New World from the abundant natural materials, the intelligence and the courage needed to craft these weapons can still be seen through their creation.
Alongside these weapons, the Gajalaka are well known for the handcrafting of a variety of different tools, with them being intelligent enough to use them frequently in their daily lives. These tools often end up scattered across the hideouts in which they live. One such example can be seen in the rafts the Gajalaka construct, which are typically given beds of straw on which they stand. These rafts are made from ornamental earthenware created by the Gajalaka as part of their daily lives and during their worship. From there, the Gajalaka will utilize their blades in order to paddle the makeshift raft. On the raft's underbelly are 3 feet that serve a unique purpose: by pointing the feet in the direction of the raft's movement, they are capable of stabilizing its movement over the water, a simple, yet extremely thoughtful design.
Unlike the written language employed by humans, the Gajalaka use a pictorial script. By understanding this language, various hidden passages within their hideouts can be uncovered. The language utilized by the Gajalaka and the language utilzed by the Grimalkyne are believed to have different linguistic roots. Additionally, the Gajalaka who live within the Recess are capable of speaking Gastodonese, allowing them to communicate with Gastodon and use them as steads.
In order to select a chief to lead them, the Gajalaka will gather in a set location, with the strongest individual amongst them being crowned the new chief. Once the chief has been selected, they must adorn a special mask and perform a ritualistic dance in order to be properly recognized as such. The Gajalaka chief is responsible for keeping hold of and passing down tribe secrets: in the case of the tribe inhabiting the Ancient Forest, their chief is responsible for holding onto knowledge of the Giant Vigorwasp, which is known to the tribe as the Supreme Healer. Within the tribe, it is regarded as being capable of healing any wound instantly and, should the chief fall ill, they will retreat to the "Tree Abyss" where it resides in order to heal themself.

Physiology
The Gajau, also known as the Catfish, is a predatory fish that poses a minor threat to Hunters. It has a wide, rounded head with skin the color of yellow mud, and its face has two small white eyes and six whiskers. Two whiskers extend from behind the nostrils while the other four extend from the chin. Its large mouth houses twelve triangular teeth, split evenly with six on the upper jaw and six on the lower; the teeth are short, yet sharp. With them, the Gajau bites into prey as large as itself, such as humans. The lower jaw protrudes farther than the upper and the Gajau has two gill slits.
The Gajau has a fat body with green skin and a white underbelly, the torso is mottled by a row of yellow spots on each side and smoothly transitions into the elongated tail. Despite its plodding appearance, it is capable of sudden bursts of strength. Unlike most other fish, it is able to use its tail to jump back into the water should it find itself on land. Behind the gills are the fish's pointed pectoral fins; starting from a similar location on its back is a row of ten dorsal fins that get smaller as they reach the caudal fin. The caudal fin is fan-shaped and small for a fish. At the end of the torso are small pelvic fins followed by an anal fin that runs along the bottom of the tail, all of the Gajau's fins are orange.
The skin of the Gajau is covered in a highly water-resistant slime, with both hunters and people of other professions using the skin to make special boots that make wading through water easier. The Gajau is additionally used by people for food: its liver is high in fat content and nutritious, while the gills are delicious if cooked long enough.
Behavior
The Gajau is predominantly found in muddy waters in warm and humid environments, although it is capable of surviving in places of higher altitude and colder temperatures. It is an aggressive monster that will readily attack terrestrial prey near water, including humans. To do this, it will swim back to a certain distance from its prey and then lunge with its mouth agape. Should the Gajau strand itself on land after a lunge, the fish will flop on the ground for a moment and then orient itself to jump back into the water. In the Scarlet Forest, the Gajau has only been observed to hunt aquatic prey: multiple individuals will gather alongside other piscivores to feed on large schools of Stardusters.
The Gajau in the Wildspire Waste tends to live in groups of two to four, with multiple Gajau surrounding their prey before attacking at different times, making them an underestimated threat among members of the Research Commission. In this sense, its hunting strategy is similar to that of small Fanged Wyverns. Although it is aggressive towards smaller creatures, it avoids large monsters and will occasionally vacate into deeper waters. Within the waters of the Forbidden Lands, one of the Gajau's known predators is the mighty Uth Duna.
The Gajau is hunted in a variety of ways in many different parts of the world; hunters from the New World and Kamura Village simply slay them using their hunting weapons, whereas the people of Moga swim in the water and use fishing harpoons to harvest the large fish. In the Forbidden Lands, hunters will fish for the Gajau using fishing rods. Being considered a Whopper, the Gajau puts up a considerable battle before a hunter can reel it out of the water.

The Gajios (ガジオス, Gajiosu) is a small Leviathan introduced in Monster Hunter Wilds.
Summary
Gray-bodied Leviathans with a serrated saw-like snout that submerge themselves and lie still in anticipation of their next meal, blending into murky waters with their muddy hide. Once prey approaches the water's edge, they swiftly lunge at their unsuspecting target, wrestling them to the ground with their jaws around their prey's neck and lacerating them with their sawblades.
Main Series

Physiology
The Gajios is similar to other Leviathans in that it has a flexible body, a long tail, and limbs sprawled to the side. However, it differs from most of its kin by having a stout torso and neck. Mossy-green, tile-like scales protect the top side of the body, while the underside has smaller white scales. New scales grow in at the midline and push older scales to the side, as this happens the old scales converge into yellow spikes pointing sideways from the Leviathan's body. The largest spikes are behind the head and behind the hip.
At the end of its thick neck is the Gajios' distinctive head, sporting a long snout filled with conical teeth. The snout is further extended by a flattened rostrum with yellow spikes on the sides, which decrease in size toward the eyes. The spikes on the rostrum can rip vulnerable wounds in victims. Due to this property, Hunters can rip off the spikes with their Hook Slinger to use as Bleeding Pods. The eyes have yellow sclera, white irises, and slit pupils. On top of the head are four pits: two small ones in front of the eyes and two larger pits behind the eyes. Together, these pits give the appearance of a human skull. Its stocky limbs are covered in smaller green scales, and each one has a line of yellow spikes. The feet have been modified into flippers, strongly webbed with short claws.
Behavior
The Gajios patrols the shallow streams that flow through the Scarlet Forest and Windward Plains, swimming with only the green dorsal surface of its body exposed. If the water is deep enough, the Gajios will submerged its body as it waits for prey to pass by, with only the tip of its nose exposed. Its primary food source is Herbivores that venture near the water, such as the Dalthydon. When its prey comes close enough, the Gajios will rush toward it and seize its quarry's neck in its jaws. Once the Herbivore is slain, the Leviathan will drag it to the riverbank and eat, sometimes engaging in a deathroll to tear out chunks of meat. The Gajios will also attack humans, although will quickly retreat if the human runs too far from the water. Multiple Gajios will attack the same prey animal if it tries to cross their stream, cutting at its legs with their rostrum.

Physiology
The Gammoth is an exceptionally large Fanged Beast—the largest currently known to the Hunter's Guild —with its size granting it the nickname of Giant Beast. Its body is covered in a thick coat of primarily deep-blue fur patterned with white eye-like markings over its shoulders. Its back is covered by several lines of white fur tipped with red, while its underside is entirely white. The Gammoth's fur tapers to white near the mid-point of its limbs, with its hindlegs transitioning afterwards to a deep-red. This pelting is resistant to cold weather, highly durable, and is able to maintain its durability even after it has sustained several physical blows, protecting its internal organs from attacks by potential predators. The Gammoth's body stores several large layers of fat that further help to insulate itself from the cold.
The Gammoth is a quadruped, with its legs being wide at the base in order to support its immense weight, while its toes are slender with sharp black hooves to allow it to dig into the snow more easily. Covering both the Gammoth's feet as well as its forehead is an especially hard, tan-colored shell that protects these otherwise vulnerable areas. While resembling scaling, this shelling is instead believed to be hardened skin. In addition to aiding the Gammoth in pushing away snow as it moves, the shelling on the legs is evolved to allow snow to adhere to it. The plates above the Gammoth's black hooves are specifically shaped to allow for snow to accumulate, with the pointed tips and upwards angling of the shelling making it easier for snow to stick, gradually causing snow to gather and adhere to the bottom of the Gammoth's leg as it walks. This helps to shield the legs with a layer of protective snow. As a result, if the shelling covering its legs is sufficiently damaged, snow will no longer be able to accumulate there as armor. Once the snow has accumulated, secretions from the Gammoth's leg further hardens the protective coating and grants it high resistance to melting, forming a Snowclod. While this snow does act as armor, its primary function is to strengthen the Gammoth's offense, with the snow violently exploding off whenever the Gammoth slams its legs down.
The shelling covering the Gammoth's forehead forms a large circular disc with additional twin ridges jutting out on either side. It helps to both protect the Gammoth's neck from damage as well as to shield the beast from oncoming blizzards. Its teeth are flexible, yet still extremely tough, allowing them to easily crush a vast array of different types of materials without scratching. Two of the Gammoth's teeth from its lower jaw have evolved into a pair of enormous upwards curving tusks, having grown significantly larger and harder over the coarse of evolution. These tusks aid the Gammoth in both combat as well as clearing any obstacles that obstruct it. Additionally, the nose and upper lip of the Gammoth has been modified into a prehensile trunk, with the tip of the trunk possessing a finger-like extension to allow the appendage to pinch and grab hold of objects. It is covered in blue fur along its topside that fades to red near the tip, with its underside being entirely hairless. This trunk is highly sensitive to vibrations in the ground, allowing it to detect the footsteps of approaching predators, and can be used by the Gammoth to dig up food from the snow in order to eat. The underside of the Gammoth's trunk is covered with several Trunkspines, giving the trunk enough strength to easy bury itself into the ground and allowing it to easily pick up and throw chunks of snow at potential threats, showcasing the full use of its trunks dexterity. The trunk may also be used to suck up liquid from the ground that it then expels as a freezing mist, either to fight off aggressors or to re-coat its limbs with a fresh layer of snow; the large size of the Gammoth provides it with the needed lung capacity to perform these attacks.
The relatively short tail of the Gammoth is coated in a layer of snow. This tail acts to protect the Gammoth from attacks from behind, as its exceptionally fluffy fur makes it easier for the claws and fangs of predators to slide off of.
As a juvenile, the Gammoth is substantially smaller than its adult counterpart and both its tusks and head-shelling is notably less developed than a fully-mature individual. Additionally, instead of the mixture of blues, reds, and whites found in the pelt of the Gammoth when matured, it sports an entirely white coat.
Behavior
The Gammoth is an obligate herbivore, feeding on plant matter such as bark, nuts, and anything else that has been buried beneath the snow. Due to its large appetite required to maintain its colossal size, the Gammoth is solitary and nomadic, always roaming around its tundra habitat. However, a mother Gammoth will typically stick near her offspring, forming a close bond with them in the process. While the Gammoth is herbivorous and ordinarily considered to be relatively peaceful, it has been said that when fighting to protect her offspring, the Gammoth is more ferocious and terrifying than any carnivorous monster.
While the Gammoth has little to fear when it comes to predation once fully matured, believed to be one of the reasons it does not form herds, the juvenile Gammoth is regularly preyed upon by larger monsters, most notably by the Tigrex; to counteract this, the calf has several ways to protect itself. The snow-white pelt of the juvenile allows it to easily blend in with its surroundings, with the calf typically crouching and shivering whenever the Tigrex approaches, pretending to be part of the snow. Additionally, the young Gammoth will often seek out the shelter of a Popo herd, which it blends into to reduce the risk of it being selected and attacked by a predator. The Popo will help protect the calf from harm and, in return, the parent Gammoth will protect the entire Popo herd from potential predators alongside her calf.
The attempted predation on the juvenile Gammoth by the Tigrex leads to a strong hatred towards the Flying Wyvern as the Gammoth ages, with it no longer fearing the Tigrex and fighting the predator as an equal or even superior upon reaching adulthood. In fact, the more the Gammoth fears the Tigrex when it is a calf, the stronger its hatred will grow when it matures; this may even lead the Gammoth to attack the Tigrex even when it is not being predated upon. When the Gammoth faces a threat to itself, her young, or her Popo herd, she will primarily rely on powerful slams that utilize the weight of her own body to easily crush her target, these blows being forceful enough to gouge holes into the ground beneath her. By taking in a deep breath, she can also use her trunk to suck in opponents towards herself.

Physiology
The Garangolm is a massive Fanged Beast with highly developed, powerful forelimbs that support a quadrupedal stance and a dense armored coating comprised of large crooked shells and spikes, which are a muted brown in color and overgrown with vegetation. These cortices plate the beast's head, back, and forelimbs, and no individual two are alike. The smaller scales that cover much of the remaining body have been hardened by a mixture of plant life and the sap-like juices produced in the Garangolm's body. By contrast, its belly is covered in naked black skin, sporting neither scales nor fur. The face is similarly covered in black skin, with prominent shell crests present atop its forehead, chin, and the sides of its head. While it possesses standard teeth, including pairs of dense and incredibly stiff fangs, its lower lip is additionally lined with rectangular scales resembling teeth; their curved shape serve to scoop loose soil into its jaws for consumption.
The forelimbs are significantly larger than the hindlimbs and are powerful enough to allow the Garangolm to lift heavy boulders of similiar size to its own body out of the ground, as well as batter and crush its opponents with pure physical power. Its shoulders are adorned with curved protrusions, while the lower arms are coated in large, upwards curving, horn-like growths running along the outer sides. The tail, referred to as a Ploughtail, is thicker than most Fanged Beasts' and is held close to the ground, ending in a pair of large, hooked claws which are in turn flanked by a smaller pair. This allows for the tail to dig up the ground in the Garangolm's wake, with each of the tail-claws additionally possessing small pockets underneath them to make digging up the soil easier.
Produced within the Garangolm's body is a sticky, sap-like fluid with fertilizing properties called Golm Thick Juice, able to rapidly accelerate the growth of plants both in the surrounding soil as well as directly on the beasts body, forming a symbiotic relationship with these plants in the process. Additionally the substance serves to both harden the plants and soil covering its body, aiding in protecting itself from threats as well to act as an adhesive for foreign objects, allowing for the augmentation of its forelimbs with hydrated mosses on its left, and volcanic minerals on its right. This behavior is what grants the Garangolm its nickname of Earth-clad Beast. This allows for blows with each respective arm to create either eruptions of water, or explosive blasts that leave behind volatile powders when they strike an enemy or the ground, with the sap helping to both aid the mosses growth and catalyze the explosions caused by the flammable gases and lava adhered to itself. The explosions generated by its right arm specifically are powerful enough to be able to launch the Garangolm into the air, with it frequently using these blasts to flank around opponents. When the Garangolm is sufficiently enraged, it will bury its face into the ground and coat it in a layer of armor as well. It can also be seen combining the effects from both of its arms, allowing for the creation of powerful eruptions of steam.
Behavior
The Garangolm is generally reputed as being of a peaceful and even somewhat timid temperament for a large monster, preferring to live within lush environments with highly fertile soil where it will not go out of its way to attack humans. However, while it prefers not to engage with territorial disputes, it will still respond aggressively to threats or when forced from its native range, with it showing a particular animosity towards the predatory Lunagaron. While patrolling its territory, it drags its tail spines along the ground to plough the soil, promoting the growth of a wide variety of flowering plants by improving the quality of the surrounding soil and fertilizing them with the sap produced by its body.
It has been noted that the Garangolm exhibits handedness, using different hands for specific purposes. The left is primarily used in feeding; being omnivorous in nature the Garangolm uses this hand to pull out mushrooms from the ground and catch fish, by contrast the right is used to groom its body and wash off dirt. It is theorized this may be the reason for the arms being coated in different materials when the Garangolm armors itself. While it typically moves by knuckle-walking, its hindlimbs are able to support a bipedal stance for brief periods of time.

Physiology
The Gargwa is a rotund Bird Wyvern covered almost completely in a coating of feathers. These feathers are colored cream along its belly and thigh, brown and orange in a striped pattern along its back, and a dark-brown around its face, with white patches around its eyes. The Gargwa possesses a yellow beak and a hardened crest atop its head, and unlike most other Bird Wyverns, it lacks any membranes on its wings, with them entirely consisting of blue-and-green feathers. However, due to their small size, these wings are considered vestigial and cannot be used by the Gargwa to fly. The Gargwa's beak is made of insulatory material, which is what allows the wyvern to safely feed on electrically charged prey, such as Thunderbugs.
Behavior
The Gargwa is omnivorous by nature and will feed upon both plants as well as insects, such as the Thunderbug. In return, the Gargwa serves as the main food source for the Zinogre, typically resulting in Thunderbugs roosting in the fur of the Zinogre to protect themselves from their main predator. The Gargwa is highly timid by nature and, if attacked from behind, is known to either lay an egg or defecate in shock before attempting to flee from the aggressor. Occasionally the Gargwa is known to lay eggs with a golden sheen; while many have theorized about what might be the reasoning behind this change, the exact cause is still unknown.
The Gargwa is often raised as livestock by various villages, such as Yukumo or Val Habar, with it frequently being used as a beast of burden to pull around carts. Additionally, the various parts and produces of the Gargwa are often utilized by humans: the Gargwa's feathers are often used as accessories in fashion, its droppings are typically dried up and turned into a powdered medicine, and its eggs—despite how expensive they can be—are a staple part of the diet in many different cultures.

Physiology
The Gastodon is a small bipedal Herbivore that shares a similar body plan to the Kestodon and certain Brute Wyverns, such as the Banbaro, due to its close taxonomic relation. Its body is covered primarily in dull, red scales, with three rows of dark-gray osteoderms being present along the wyvern's back. It supports itself on two muscular hoofed legs with armored knee-caps; the scales from the knee down sport the same gray-color as the back. Easily the most identifiable feature of the Gastodon is its thick rusty-red mane present around most of its head, neck, and chest, with some additional hair also being present on the tip of its tail. However, the face of the Gastodon is instead covered in a mix of gray and red scaling, with it sporting one nasal horn and a pair of horns curving out from the back of its head.
Unusual for a small monster, the Gastodon displays a clear physical change when it is angered. During this state, the Gastodon is capable of increasing the blood to its skin, causing it to become flushed red. Additionally, its mane will begin to glow a much brighter orange.
Behavior
The Gastodon has thus far exclusively been discovered in the New World, where it lives within volcanic environments. It is known to live in small herds, although it does not travel and instead prefers to remain in a single location whilst staying as a unit. The Gastodon is additionally famed for its fierce territoriality, with the herd acting in unison to drive a target out of their turf. At first, it will perform a threat display of slamming its head into the ground in an attempt to ward the threat off, and if that fails, it will resort to charging down its target with its large dome; it has even been known to go after monsters several times its own size. In some circumstances when it is particularly angry, the Gastodon has been known to continue pursuing a target even after it has already fled. Despite this temperament, if a member of its own herd is killed, the remaining members will often resort to simply fleeing.

Physiology
The Gelidron is a stout-bodied Amphibian with proportionally short limbs and a broad, flat tail. Its hide is iridescent and semi-transparent, with a complex pattern of yellow mottles, blue-banded stripes, and blackish-red tops that darken in coloration when the Gelidron submerges itself in oil pools.
To protect itself from the relentless geothermal heat of its habitats, the Gelidron produces a thick mucus beneath its skin that provides it with moisture and prevents it from being burned. This gelatinous layer is transparent and thickest around the Amphibian's tail and torso, giving it a rotund appearance—the actual body beneath is almost slender, with folded flanks and a light-pinkish coloration.
The skull is broad and rounded, and its small lidless eyes face upward. Its jaws are lined with tiny regular teeth, and hold a large muscular tongue covered in thick bumps. Despite its heavyset build and proportionally meager limbs, the Gelidron is a capable climber; curved claws and fine adhesive hairs on the underside of its toes enable it to scale steep walls and inclinations while traversing its cavern dwelling. It has four digits on its hands and five on its toes.
Behavior
The Gelidron is carnivorous and preys on Crudeshell Crabs, which it seizes through ambush using its powerful tongue and then swallows whole. As prey, this species is the main food source for most large carnivores in the Oilwell Basin; the Gelidron is hunted by the Kranodath, Ajarakan, Rathian and Rathalos, and even the Nu Udra. Its meat is also considered a delicacy in Azuz, where it is frequently consumed.
When a threat is identified, the Gelidron may face towards it and open its jaws while hissing, or flee into oil pools or bodies of water to bury itself in the soft sedimentary bed.

Physiology
The Gendrome is the alpha-male of a pack of Genprey and, naturally, closely resembles its smaller brethren. He similarly sports a coloration consisting of green and orange stripes with a tan underbelly and shares the massively enlarge upper fangs which protrude visibly from the mouth even when his jaws are shut. This individual emerges when a male Genprey establishes his dominance within the pack and experiences a corresponding growth spurt. He can be identified from his pack mates by his notably larger body, even longer front fangs, and greatly enlarged head crests, which forms into two triangular sails atop his head. These changes in appearance serve to make the Gendrome more conspicuous, allowing for him to more easily establish his presence amongst his peers. Additionally, his hide is much thicker and tougher than that of the Genprey due to the many years spent protecting his pack, lending the alpha greater physical resilience.
His elongated fangs fangs, alongside the sharp, scythe-like claws on his feet, also contain within them a characteristic neurotoxin which causes near-instant paralysis, being able to immobilize his targets in little more than a few seconds. As taking on Herbivores with especially hard carapaces is no small feat, this highly potent venom allows the Gendrome and his pack to take down prey which weights significantly more than he does. While this toxin inhibits the movement of his prey, it does not inhibit senses such as sight or touch; as a result, anything unlucky enough to be paralyzed by it experience the horrors of being torn apart while unable to fight back.
Behavior
Like his relatives, the Gendrome leads large packs of its smaller brethren, allowing them to hunt cooperatively. However while he has near exclusively been found living in desert regions, with occasionally ventures into other environments, groups of Genprey have curiously been spotted in swampy regions without the presence of an alpha. It seems that for unknown regions the alpha is incapable of penetrating into humid environments.
He hunts by ambushing prey with his pack before paralyzing the target with his venom. Once this is accomplished, he will leap at the target and pin it down using his supremely strong leg muscles. The wyvern then attacks his downed prey in a group, always aiming for the softest parts of the skin; the pack devours its victim while it is still alive, yet immobile and unable to fight back. This gruesome behavior has led to many Hunters avoiding assignments related to the Gendrome, as nobody wants to fall prey to such a pack. Nonetheless, the Hunter's Guild regularly receives requests for slaying Gendrome, primarily due to his tendency to stalk and harass merchant caravans passing through desert trading routes.
If a Gendrome is unable to become or remain the leader of the pack, it will be chased out of it and, unless it is able to defeat another alpha and take over his pack, be forced to live as a stray. When several such strays find themselves in a same region, they may gather to form a temporary pack consisting of only Gendrome, with no Genprey. These groups are known to be especially thirsty for battle and enjoy killing for its own sake even it is not necessary, perhaps as a way to relieve their stress.
Super Biology Information
The Super Biology Book Series collects the thoughts and theories of real scientists that were asked to speak about monsters from the Monster Hunter series. Thus, they are inherently speculative and should be seen as such.
While examining the Velocidrome, Gendrome, Iodrome and Great Jaggi all at once, Fossil Expert Yoshitsugu Kobayashi ponders the implications of their shared physical traits. He compares their size and body builds to those of Deinonychus and observes how their slender, light bodies allow for quick movements, while the sharp claws on their limbs lend themselves to shredding prey while jumping towards it. Kobayashi also asserts that based on their muscle structure, these wyverns could have a top running speed of 50 km/h. He also notes that the four wyverns all share rows of narrow, conical teeth that display the same shape throughout the entire mouth and sit with notable gaps between them. This resembles the dentition seen in piscivorous creatures such as gharials or Spinosaurus, and might imply that these wyverns eat fish.
Kobayashi notes that the crests of Velocidrome, Gendrome and Iodrome all form through physical structures growing on the head and then extend past it. He compares them to crests found on Dilophosaurus, Monolophosaurus and Guanlong, and asserts that just as is presumed in those species, the crested wyverns likely use their crests as decorations that aid in identifying and communicating to rivals and mates. Kobayashi singles out the Great Jaggi however due to it possessing a frill, which he assumes additionally serves as temperature regulation. Despite the fact that all four species work in packs, Kobayashi asserts that social behavior does not necessarily indicate a high level of intelligence. Instead, these bird wyverns strike him as creatures that flock together out of protective instinct, since individually, they are all fairly weak. He does however propose that their ability to coordinate might imply a more sophisticated social structure than initially apparent.

Physiology
Described as a subspecies of the Velociprey, the Giaprey closely resembles its nominate species in appearance, bearing a near-identical frame with a similar yellow beak-like upper jaw, a reddish-brown crest at the back of its head, tan underbelly, sharp claws on both its hands and feet, and a body covered in stripes. However, where it differs is in the coloration of its scales, with it primarily being clad in bluish-white, while the stripes along its neck, back, and tail are a dark blue. This coloration allows it to blend into its surroundings and stalk its prey unnoticed through the snow. In addition to using its claws and teeth as weaponry, it has developed the ability to spit an icy fluid due to having evolved to adapt to the cold. This fluid is believed to have originated as a form of venom that slowly altered in chemistry to fit the wyvern's new environment and ensure that a sufficient amount of prey could be secured by the pack. In comparison to the icy spit produced by its commander, the Giaprey's is noticeably weaker.
Behavior
While it was initially discovered belonging to packs of Velociprey in jungle environments, the Giaprey is currently found exclusively in cold and snowy environments. Furthermore, it lives in large packs led by an alpha male Giadrome and hunts in a very similar fashion to its cousin—repeatedly pouncing at its prey while biting with its needle-like teeth and slashing with its sickle-shaped claws—although it will also make use of its icy spit to slow down its target. It can also utilize its high agility to perform swift jumps to flank around its target, giving its prey little to no chance to retaliate against it. Its long tail serves to counter-balance its weight while it is attacking.
White Velociprey
Upon first discovery, the monster now known as the Giaprey was simply called the White Velociprey and was found inside of larger Velociprey packs. At the time, it was not considered to be distinct from its nominate species, instead being simply believed to be a Velociprey whose scales had mutated to be white, likely from albinism. However, it is worth noting that unlike those later observed in the Snowy Mountains, such individuals were both primarily found during warmer periods and lacked the ability to spit icy fluids. The exact relation between these initial sightings to the currently known Giaprey and Giadrome is unknown, although several hypotheses have been posited.
The first suggests the White Velociprey was, at the time, in the process of undergoing speciation into the Giaprey, implying the latter to have only emerged recently as a species. Another hypothesis proposes that the White Velociprey may be an abnormal Giaprey adapting to inhabiting different climates that has mixed itself into the Velociprey's packs. However, there are those who simply doubt the eye-witness accounts given by Hunters at the time and instead believe the Giaprey has simply always been the Giaprey, as well as others who believe the White Velociprey were in fact abhorrent Velociprey individuals, and that the actual Giaprey had remained undiscovered until being first sighted within the Snowy Mountains.

The Giggi is the juvenile form of the Gigginox and completely lacks eyes, much like its adult counterpart, with them having degenerated over time due to it primarily dwelling inside caves. Its entire body consists of one elongated tube coated in a soft grayish hide, with incredibly short forelimbs and only tiny nubs for hind legs. The Giggi primarily feeds by draining the blood from larger organisms; it will then convert this stolen blood into its own toxins, which it can spew at potential threats to defend itself. Once it has sensed potential prey, the Giggi will leap onto its target and begin draining them of blood, growing progressively larger in the process.
While the Gigginox is restricted to only being found in caves within Tundra environments, likely to avoid the fluids coating its body from either drying out or being washed off, the juvenile Giggi has been found inhabiting a much broader variety of regions, such as the Deserted Island. It has even been theorized that a Gigginox better adapted to these non-frigid environments may be discovered in the future. While it can survive in darkness regardless of the weather, if conditions become too harsh in the environment in which it is living, the Giggi will construct a cocoon from a thread-like mucus its body naturally produces, waiting inside until the conditions improve enough for it to emerge again. In especially harsh conditions, it has been known to band together with its brethren and form cocoons in large clusters.
