Physiology
A bizarre species of Flying Wyvern that exhibits characteristics similar to those seen in Gekkos and leeches, the Gigginox resembles more distant relatives in build, moving as a quadruped with its body held close to the ground and its wings and hindlimbs sprawled. Additionally, the Gigginox is covered in a scaleless hide, colored a pale gray-green on the dorsal and deep-red on the ventral side of its body. This hide is smooth and moist in texture, and the deep red underside is covered in fine hairs and secretions that allow it to adhere to even the ceilings of frozen over caverns; it is believed these fluids also aid the Gigginox in maintaining its body temperature in the permafrost. The piel of a fully developed specimen dissolves sweat and odors.
The skull is saucer-shaped from front to back, broad in proportion to the neck, and possesses a cylindrical maw capable of greatly expanding in form, allowing it to envelop even large prey whole and grind it down with the rows of needle-like teeth lining the inside. When the wyvern ambulates, this maw expands and retracts continually, letting out a deep wheezing noise with every breath. The vision of the Gigginox is believed to have degenerated entirely as a result of the perpetual darkness of its cavernous environment, instead navigating its surroundings via a specialized organ that detects temperatures.
Lining the sides of the skull, belly, and tail are pairs of external writhing glands, that filter out a portion of the Gigginox's own blood to produce a potent toxin. This toxin is then circulated through the entire body by a specialized capillary system to be either expulsed from the mouth as a glob of poison, or vented out as a noxious gas. These organs are additionally luminescent, which is believed to be a result of a biochemical reaction that occurs during venom production and may serve as an aposematism to warn of its toxicity. In addition to this aposematism, the Gigginox exhibits a deimatic display: it is an automimic. The tail imitates the appearance of the softer head and possesses a similar cylindrical orifice with which it can perform faux "bites", drawing attackers away from the more vulnerable body part. Lain from this orifice are gelatinous sacs that either contain eggs from which Giggi larvae hatch, or a concentrated noxious gas that erupts into a toxic cloud. To further sell the act, the wing fingers fork at their tip to imitate the padded hand on which it walks.
When enraged, the Gigginox's hide will take on a dark hue and harden significantly. This color change appears to be a consequence of the monster's toxin production increasing as it becomes excited, temporarily altering the surface of the skin in the process. Any hide that is removed while the wyvern is in this altered state will remain darkened permanently.
The Gigginox is believed to be a close relative of the Khezu, also producing the medicinally beneficial Pale Extract for an unidentified purpose within its body.
Behavior
Like most species of Flying Wyvern, the Gigginox is an active predator and feeds primarily on smaller Herbivores native to its region, such as the Popo. Prey is detected through body heat and incapacitated by a glob of poison. Once under the effects of its toxins, the victim is dragged into the Gigginox's cave and left to freeze solid, which is believed to function as a form of cold storage. This has an additional benefit, as the various corpses frozen into cave walls present a curiosity for other monsters to investigate, luring more potential prey into the den. Outside of hunting, the Gigginox spends most of its time sleeping whilst sticking to walls or ceilings, displaying an overall low level of activity. When threatened, the behavior it exhibits is very active, performing acrobatic somersaults to position itself behind its attackers and swap the relative positions of its head and tail.
Individual Gigginox have been observed tolerating the presence of one another on occasion; during especially harsh seasons, multiple adolescent individuals have been sighted constructing large cocoon colonies to keep each other warm during their slumber.
Much like the related Khezu, the Gigginox is a hermaphrodite and reproduces asexually. It has an exceptionally high reproductive rate, depositing eggs in large gelatinous sacs that hatch Giggi larvae within moments of being lain; these juveniles will seek out moist sheltered areas to protect the mucus layer on their sensitive skin. While the Gigginox is only found in the Tundra, the Giggi has been sighted in a large variety of biomes, with it being believed the high spawn rate of this species pushes juveniles to explore new territories. The Hunter's Guild expects to eventually discover various Subspecies that have adapted to all the different environments these juveniles venture into.
Super Biology Information
The Super Biology Book Series collects the thoughts and theories of real scientists that were asked to speak about monsters from the Monster Hunter series. Thus, they are inherently speculative and should be seen as such.
Fossil Expert Yoshitsugu Kobayashi points out that Gigginox’s presence in the Tundra is highly unusual. Animals with slimy skin, such as frogs, do not generally thrive in sub-zero temperatures. The Gigginox’s tendency to lie completely still in dark caves for long periods of time, far away from any sunlight, might imply that the creature is able to generate a small amount of heat within its body for base level maintenance, and that it otherwise conserves energy by simply resting. Kobayashi proposes that Gigginox go through a cycle that alternates between periods of activity and rest - and that the transition between rest and activity is when the monster would be at its most vulnerable. Gigginox likely take a long time to fully shake off their sluggishness after a rest cycle, which is when warm-blooded predators would likely have the best chances of catching it.
When discussing the reproductive biology of the Gigginox, Kobayashi asserts that in all of the animal kingdom, there are no known species that can reproduce as rapidly as this monster. Generally, vertebrates give birth in one of two ways: oviparously, where an egg is released from the body and then hatches some time later outside, and viviparously, where an egg is hatched inside of the body and the offspring develops within the gestating parent until it grows into a shape similar to an adult individual. Kobayashi theorizes thus that the Gigginox exhibits a kind of extreme viviparity, wherein countless Giggi are always hatching and growing within its body at any one time, which can then be released via slimy sacs at will. This adaptation would allow the species to proliferate rapidly.
Having lost its eyesight after spending generations in the darkness of caves, Gigginox appears to have the ability to track prey via their heat signatures. Kobayashi proposes that this ability is likely very similar to the pit organs seen in many snakes: These hollow spaces are located at the front of the face and covered by thin membranes, and are able to detect changes in temperatures near the creature. The Gigginox may use a similar adaptation to sense its surroundings. Another trait of this monster with a reptilian analogue is its ability to cling to walls - Kobayashi asserts that it likely uses tiny hairs on its underside to exploit intermolecular forces to generate adhesion, just like many geckos do.

Physiology
The Girros is a small and lithe Fanged Wyvern closely related to the similarly-built Jagras, although its body and limbs are both notably stockier. Its body is primarily covered in light-gray scales that fade into a darker shade atop the wyvern's neck, which possesses a hood that juts out sideways; the Girros' hood is notably less pronounced than the one possessed by its pack's alpha. Several yellow spots decorate the sides of this hood, and along the Girros' neck are 3 pairs of red gill slits. While the Girros typically breathes using its mouth or nostrils, due to the high amounts of effluvium concentrated within the middle-layers of the Vale which it patrols, the Girros can use these gills as additional respiratory organs. These gills are lined with cilia that help it to filter out the bacteria from the air and enable it to live in the unforgiving environment of the Rotten Vale. Despite this adaptation, the Girros is not immune from becoming infected by the effluvium.
The most notable feature of the Girros is the pair of elongated fangs on its upper jaw that permanently stick out of its mouth. These fangs are connected to a sac inside its body that secretes a paralytic toxin, allowing it to inject this venom into targets through its fangs while in combat. This allows the Girros to paralyze monsters several times its own size, such as the Odogaron.
Behavior
The Girros is primarily found within the middle reaches of the New World's Rotten Vale. It lives within a large pack lead by an alpha Great Girros, who is responsible for giving orders for the rest of the pack to obey. While primarily a scavenger that feeds on the countless bodies that have fallen into the Vale overtime, it is still capable of hunting its own prey. When hunting, the pack's Great Girros is responsible for paralyzing the chosen target, allowing for the remaining Girros to bring down the prey. In combat, the Girros obeys the commands given by the alpha through the use of its larger gills, with them vibrating to signal to the pack to subdue their target. Even individuals that are not part of the pack have been known to join in on a hunt upon hearing the call of an alpha. The Girros additionally actively takes part in defending its territory alongside the Great Girros without needing to be prompted. Even if members of the pack are killed, more will soon come rushing in to rejoin their alpha. However, without an alpha it is not nearly as bold and will typically retreat if another member of the pack is killed.
Despite usually being able to withstand the effluvium, the Girros can occasionally become infected by the bacteria if it breathes too much in, being driven mad in the process. In this state, it is notably more aggressive, with it refusing to back down even if other Girros nearby are slain. It is reduced to a mindless predator, wandering aimlessly in search of potential prey.

It is a Subspecies of the Agnaktor.
Summary
A tundra-adapted Subspecies of the Agnaktor which are notably smaller than the common species. By burying themselves in the sheets of permafrost, they coat themselves in an unusually tough layer of ice armor, though this armor eventually softens over time. When threatened, Glacial Agnaktor can fire beams of chilled water to dispatch attackers or crush them under packed snow with their elongated beak. Unlike the base species, the juvenile form of the Glacial Agnaktor is currently unknown.

Physiology
The Glacial Agnaktor resembles its fiery volcanic relative in mostly every way, barring its distinctly different coloration. Rather than be covered by bright-red shelling, the Glacial Agnaktor instead possesses a mix of icy blue-and-white shells whose cooler colors help it to better blend into its frozen habitat. Additionally, it is slightly smaller than its crimson relative. This Subspecies displays certain physiological adaptations that aid it in its survival in the tundra. Primarily, the dermal fluid that insulates the regular Agnaktor from lava is modified in the Glacial Agnaktor, now instead serving as an ice nucleator that promotes the formation of thick layers of ice. Thus, the body remains covered wholly by a transparent yet highly resistant layer of ice.
Behavior
The Glacial Agnaktor is exclusively found in the Tundra, where it prowls the frozen plains and icy caves in solitude. Just as its lava-adapted cousin burrows into solid ground with its beak, so too does the Glacial Agnaktor, only it instead uses its to dig into the unyielding permafrost. While the juvenile form of the Agnaktor is a common sight, no juvenile form of the Glacial Agnaktor has thus far been discovered.

Physiology
The Glavenus is a large Brute Wyvern whose body is covered primarily in a mixture of red scales along most of its body, blue scales on its face and the front of its legs, and cream-colored scales along its underbelly. This shelling is strong enough to resist all but the strongest of blows, with its defense being tempered due to the Glavenus' naturally high body temperature. The head is ornamented with a pair of short twin-pointed horns that transition into two rows of blue forward-curving spikes along the entire length of the back, called Pyroshells, with two especially large spikes being present above the hip. Alongside resembling flickering flames and possessing a high resistance to heat, extreme care is required when while handling these shells as a mere touch is enough to reduce one's body to ash. These shells are primarily used in heat-dispersal and, while normally a deep blue in color, increased blood flow and rising body temperature when the Glavenus grows enraged causes the Pyroshells to turn a bright-red color and become shrouded in black smoke, reflecting the wyvern's fierce temper. The shape of the Pyroshells, combined with their mineral-like texture, grants the Glavenus a uniquely intimidating aura. Its forelimbs are proportionally very short.
Easily the most iconic feature of the Glavenus is its long and muscular tail that bears a sharpened edge on its underside and greatly resembles a Great Sword, granting it the nickname of Slashing Wyvern. Comprising around half of the wyvern's total length, the tail's bright-blue coloration is owed to the many flammable iron ore deposits that coat its surface, accumulated as it is continuously scraped along the ground. As a result, by repeatedly scraping its tail across the ground, the resulting friction causes it to catch on fire and to glow red-hot, burning anything the tail makes contact with. When the Glavenus' body temperature increases as it grows enraged, the friction generated by its tail increases, resulting in it becoming super-heated much more frequently. Additionally, the Glavenus can use its red-hot tail to set the ground ablaze and, by scraping it along the ground, can send flames flying forward. The cost of this increased power is that the super-heating consequently results in the shelling of the tail becoming softened, making the blade significantly easier to sever. Small, yet sharp scales are often found growing near the Glavenus' tail, which additionally serve the role as a short blade.
However, once the temperature of the tail has been raised, soot will begin to accumulate on its surface as it starts to cool, dulling the blade in the process. In order to keep its blade in pristine condition, the Glavenus uses its specially evolved fangs—as well as four sharp points of the shelling of its face which resemble fangs—to bite into its tail and drag along its length, sharpening it in the process. The jaws' specialized shape, said by some to resemble an anvil, makes them especially easy to sharpen with. This process is done repeatedly throughout the Glavenus' life, with the repeated heating and cooling causing its tail to progressively grow sharper and more sword-like as it ages. Even just a small fragment of the tail-blade is capable of slicing through most man-made swords. Outside of their use in sharpening its tail, the Glavenus' fangs serve as formidable weapons in their own right, capable of cutting through almost anything and easily withstanding the pressure exerted by its jaws. Its hindlegs are highly muscular and possess a spring-like flexibility due to the need for them to provide stability whilst the wyvern swings its tail around, with them additionally allowing the Glavenus to out-maneuver targets through quick steps and powerful leaps.
Any accumulated soot, as well as rusted parts of its exoskeleton, are swallowed by the Glavenus and stored within its body. By using a unique organ located within its throat, known as its Bursa, this soot can be super-heated into a magma-like substance which the Glavenus can spit out from its mouth to attack with. While the lining of this organ is incredibly thin, it is capable of storing even the hottest of molten materials without as much as singeing. Upon hitting the ground, the exposure to outside air triggers a reaction within the highly flammable components of this molten slag, triggering a large explosion. However, storing this much flammable materials in its throat can be dangerous, as if its throat is sufficiently damaged, a large internal explosion may occur inside of the Glavenus' body.
Behavior
The Glavenus is commonly found within forested, arid, and volcanic environments in both the Old and New World; for the latter, it was specifically first encountered in the Wildspire Waste following the environmental changes caused by the Old Everwyrm. The Glavenus is carnivorous in nature, with its aggressive disposition leading it to prey upon Herbivores larger than itself, such as the Larinoth. When fighting its prey, the Glavenus will first uses its muscular legs to attack, before finishing them off with a powerful slam from its bladed tail, its lower body having evolved to be especially muscular to allow it to lift and swing its bladed tail with ease. However, its aggressive demeanor also means it gets into frequent territorial disputes with other large monsters. While these disputes usually end in ties, against the Rathalos, whoever initiated the attack has been observed gaining a distinct advantage—it has however been hypothesized that terrain may also play a role in deciding the victor.
Amongst males, the quality of the Glavenus' tail plays an important social role, with a harder and more vibrantly colored tail indicating more strength and dignity within an individual. As a result, to both grow its tail effectively and to more easily attract a female Glavenus to mate with, a male requires access to high-quality iron-containing minerals. The territory of the Glavenus is typically rich in excellent mineral deposits, which leads them to be highly sought after by both researchers and Hunters in search of such minerals. This desire for high-quality iron additionally leads to occasional territorial disputes between male Glavenus over areas with better minerals. These disputes typically start peacefully, with the two males shouting at each other in a furious rage, displaying their impressive jaws and vocal powers to intimidate the other. If neither ends up retreating, the battle turns physical, with the worst-case scenarios involving the two engaging in a fight to the death. The victor of the dispute is decided by whichever individual is the first to back away, have their tail broken, or die. These mineral deposits additionally serve an important role in providing the Glavenus with a place to polish its tail effectively.
When the breeding season arrives, the male and female Glavenus will meet up to form pairs, however once the eggs have been laid, the male will proceed to abandon his partner; some individuals will go on to mate with multiple females in a single breeding season. Meanwhile, the female will lay a single egg, with the hatchling Glavenus spending a very short time with its mother, learning how to both hunt and hone its tail in the process before setting out into the world to search for its own mineral veins to develop its tail with. While the fires the Glavenus generates from the friction of its tail can result in forest fires, it overall has a beneficial impact on its surrounding ecosystem. As it digs and cuts through the ground in search of minerals, it cultivates and nurtures the surrounding soil in the process, allowing for new plant-life to more easily sprout.
In some cultures, the Glavenus is instead referred to as Dinovaldo.

Monster Hunter Generations
The design of Glavenus' 3D Model was led by Kazuhisa Inuzuka.
Glavenus' design started with the idea of a tank reloading explosive shells. This was then further broken down into the basic imagery of a weapon that requires an eye-catching reload or preparation process - this would eventually become its sword tail. Visually, Yasunori Ichinose wanted to stick to a tried and true cool concept, and thus chose to focus on a silhouette resembling that of a Tyrannosaurus Rex and combining that with the image of a Western Knight.
This initial design went through various iterations, with one early version depicting Glavenus as a turtle-like creature that had a shield-like plate on its back in addition to the bladed tail.
Monster Hunter World: Iceborne
Since many players were introduced to the series of Monster Hunter through Generations (or as it was known in Japan as MHX), Kaname Fujioka said that the team wanted to include a monster that would be familiar to those players. It was impossible to include the entire Fated Four (i.e Astalos, Mizutsune, Glavenus and Gammoth), so the team chose Glavenus. It was the main Flagship Monster that was symbolic, and it could easily express strength with its unique impressive tail; a perfect fit in terms of game design.
The idea was that the old strategies from Generations would work on Glavenus to some extent, but in Iceborne, the team focused more on dealing with its tail; the key to the fight. They simplified it with its breath attacks, and because of its large tail, they thought it would be easier for players to fight it in an open area rather than a dense forest, thus it features mainly in the Wildspire Waste. In the Generations cutscenes, Glavenus and Rathian fought with each other, so the team wanted to depict the conflict again. Making the Iceborne fighting cutscene was easy from a production standpoint as Rathian also lives in the Wildspire Waste.

The Lantern Fish Wyvern Gobul (チャナガブル, Chanagaburu) is a Leviathan introduced in Monster Hunter 3.

Physiology
The Gobul is a fairly unusual species of Leviathan, as instead of the long and slender build often seen in other Leviathans, its body is flat and wide, with short stubby legs that are held directly under the torso. The limbs are tipped with fin-like hands that are quite resistant and do not wear down much over time. The Gobul's neck is short and the top of its torso forma a wide disk-like structure that tapers out at the posterior into a long tail, which possesses a swollen spiked bulb two-thirds down its length. Most notable is the Gobul's extremely large mouth filled with needle-like teeth. These teeth are not for chewing, instead being specialized in latching onto prey and not letting go.
The Gobul is covered in purple skin possessing elastic and rubbery properties, with the degree of elasticity being known to vary between individuals. The skin is edible and is considered an acquired taste, and its surface is covered in a moisturizing mucus which is sometimes used as a cosmetic product by humans. A noteworthy feature of the skin is that it is saturated with specialized cells called chromatophores, which the Gobul is able to stimulate to alter the color of its hide; this mechanism aids in the Gobul's camouflage.
The elastic skin can be inflated by the Gobul sucking in air or water, which reveals the many spikes that line the back. The shape and size of these spikes is known to vary between individuals, and both these spikes and the needles on the bulb of the tail contain a paralytic neurotoxin administered through injection. These toxins are not produced inside the Gobul's body, and are instead derived from its diet, Many critters in the Flooded Forest use toxins to survive, and after being eaten by predators, those predators are then themselves devoured by the Gobul. Thus, the toxins eventually end up inside the Gobul's body and the Leviathan in turn gains its neurotoxin from this cycle. Unlike most other parts of the Gobul's body, the toxic barbs on its are inedible.
On its chin, the Gobul grows distinct orange whiskers with swollen tips that have evolved to mimic the appearance of underwater plants found in the Flooded Forest. However, in some individuals, these whiskers are so overdeveloped that they no longer resemble those plants all that much. A distinct feature of the Gobul is the antenna atop its head that is tipped with a large bulb. This structure is called a Lantern and allows the Leviathan to produce a bright flash of light on command. The bulb is filled with symbiotic bacterial colonies that can produce bioluminescence when stimulated, and by releasing a stimulating liquid from glands inside the bulb, the Gobul can activate the bacteria and make its lantern glow.
Behavior
The Gobul is most commonly found in the Flooded Forest, although is also known to spend time in the open ocean and near Moga Woods. It employs a sophisticated hunting strategy that revolves around hiding at the bottom of rivers. By sensing the amount and type of light reflected around its body, the Gobul adjusts the chromatophores in its skin such that it shifts to the most appropriate color. It then burrows itself into the riverbed, laying in wait for prey. It perfectly blends into the environment by sticking out its whiskers, and when suitable prey swims near it, the Gobul lunges out of its hiding spot and attempts to swallow its target whole in a single bite. If that does not work, it can additionally suction the water around it through its mouth, hoping to catch its prey in the suction force. The Gobul may also use a flash from its Lantern to stun prey and prevent it from escaping, although this method is used more sparingly as the flash could attract rivals to its location. The Gobul is a voracious eater and known to swallow all sorts of junk whilst hunting. It has been noted to be especially fond of the taste of Frogs.
Life Cycle
The life cycle of the Gobul is quite mysterious; in one case, a large Gobul from the Flooded Forest was compared to a similar individual found out in the open sea. The forest Gobul was noted to have no visible sexual organs, to the point where it was not even possible to determine its sex, whereas the Gobul found in the ocean had well-developed ovaries. This might suggest the Gobul travels out to sea to mate and reproduce. The juvenile form of the Gobul has never been found, leading to the belief that it either spends its youth hiding in the deep oceans, or that it looks so different from the adult's form that researchers are continually unable to identify it.
Super Biology Information
The Super Biology Book Series collects the thoughts and theories of real scientists that were asked to speak about monsters from the Monster Hunter series. Thus, they are inherently speculative and should be seen as such.
Marine Scientist Fumihito Muto takes a look at the Gobul’s lantern and compares it to traits seen in certain fish. Anglerfish grow a similar structure - called an illicium - which allows it to emit light and bait prey. The luminous tip is often the result of symbiotic, bioluminescent bacteria, though other methods have been observed as well. Muto notes that the color of such lanterns is often fixed in the blue or green range, which is also the case for the Gobul.
Moving on to the Gobul’s body, Muto theorizes that if the monster shares an evolutionary history with anglerfish, it might possess an inverted skeletal structure compared to other monsters - the pelvic fins of the anglerfish are in front of its pectoral fins. Muto also wonders if the Gobul displays the same extreme sexual dimorphism as anglerfish, wherein the females are massive while the males are tiny. If that were to be the case, Muto argues that all the Gobul seen in the series would be females. He also asserts that it might be possible that this species is subject to an uneven sex distribution, with one sex being vastly more common than the other.
Muto next hypothesizes that the Gobul accumulates toxic compounds within its body by preying on venomous or poisonous organisms, subsequently utilizing these toxins for both offense and defense. Similar phenomena are observed in species such as the monarch butterfly, which consumes toxic plants during its larval stage, and various pufferfish, which feed on venomous or poisonous invertebrates. In the case of pufferfish, the toxins are originally produced by microorganisms and become concentrated in specific parts of the fish’s body as they move up the food chain. Muto additionally ponders that while the juvenile form of the Gobul remains unknown, it is possible that they are born in the deep sea and migrate to shallower waters as they mature. Furthermore, Muto believes that the juvenile form could look so distinct that it might be mistaken for an entirely different species. In other words, it is possible that a creature currently classified as a separate species is in fact a juvenile Gobul that later grows into its more familliar its adult form.

Physiology
Only recently confirmed to exist, the Gogmazios is a massive Elder Dragon that boasts an exceptionally long lifespan and has existed since ancient times, retaining a more primitive appearance from ages long past. Using its massive wingarms, it habitually employs a hexapedal gait in a manner similar to what can be observed in the Gore Magala and Shagaru Magala, supporting its body on all six limbs. However, the Gogmazios is additionally able to rear up onto its hind legs and enter an upright posture, supporting itself for prolonged periods of time using its gigantic forelimbs. This particular set of forelimbs resembles a pair of skeletal wings whose membranes are greatly tattered, making them poorly suited for actual flight. Instead, the Elder Dragon often makes use of them for combative purposes, combining their long reach with the red-hot, curved claws situated at the wingarms' ends to viciously sear any prey within reach. The Gogmazios' distinctively pointed, spade-shaped head is decorated with various bony protrusions. Both its back and chest are decorated by several blunt spikes hardened by a coating of blood, staining them a deep red; due to their dull edge, these twisted spikes are more attuned for crushing victims rather than slashing at them.
The Gogmazios' most infamous trait is the constant secretion of Heavy Drakesbone Oil from between its dark, navy-blue scales. A volatile substance produced within its body, this hazardous fluid coats the Gogmazios' body and hardens, granting the Elder Dragon its famed deep-black appearance whilst also acting as a natural layer of defense. As a result of its stickiness, the Gogmazios' oil covering frequently causes weapons used against it to embed into its tar-like armor, increasing the protection offered by its carapace even further. Additionally, the properties of the Heavy Drakesbone Oil will cause the various weapons and tarred ancient armaments lodged in its body to mutate over time due to prolonged exposure, requiring the abilities of a skilled smith in order to be worked into anything usable. Chief amongst the various armaments that may dress the Gogmazios' body are the Dragonator and Convergent Elderbreaker —two ancient and powerful forms of artillery entangled by the Elder Dragon's oil as it raids armories and weapon stockpiles, much like everything else lodged in its hide. In regards to the Dragonator, it does not appear to hinder the Gogmazios' movement in the slightest, as demonstrated by the Elder Dragon's remarkable agility and stamina during flight that renders the weapon's presence inconsequential.
Within the Gogmazios' body are combustion organs that break down and convert sulfur into calories, with any impurities left behind being used in the production of the Heavy Drakesbone Oil that overflows through its scales like sweat. As a result, the oil contains gunpowder components that make it extremely volatile once exposed to high amounts of heat, taking on three different states dependent on its temperature. Ordinarily, it will rest in a cooled state where it has hardened and solidified, although when heated, it will cross into an unstable and viscous liquid state. If the Heavy Drakesbone Oil is exposed to even greater temperatures still, it will vaporize and enter a gaseous state as the Gogmazios consumes calories and its body temperature rises.
In the process of the combustion organs generating calories and energy, a great amount of intense heat is produced and subsequently released from the body in the form of coal-black smoke through separate heat-dissipation organs. As the Gogmazios moves, it leaves behind small puddles of Heavy Drakesbone Oil on the ground by virtue of its overflowing production. These puddles, referred to as Super Heavy Drakesbone Oil, entrap and slow whatever they come in contact with. When necessary, the Gogmazios is capable of utilizing its oil production offensively by flinging the oil stuck on its body towards attackers and immobilizing them at a distance, as well as by spewing vast quantities of the steaming-hot oil directly from its maw. The oil covering the Elder Dragon's wingarms and tail may also be momentarily heated as they are violently scraped across the ground, igniting nearby puddles and softening from the friction at the same time.
When the Gogmazios is pushed far enough and grows irate, its internal temperature will suddenly rise significantly, heating up the oil coating its body and causing it to immediately bubble and detonate as it drips from its body. Once its body's raised temperature melts or boils away the hardened oil trapping them in a retracted state, the Gogmazios will be able to forcefully spread the membranes of its tattered wings and take flight.
However, most notable among the changes the Gogmazios undergoes during its fury is the state of the oil it spews from its maw, as typically the Heavy Drakesbone Oil is simply expelled under high pressure from the mouth, although due to the increased heat it is transformed into a devastating heat ray. Believed to be generated by the extreme compression of Heavy Drakesbone Oil within the Gogmazios' body, this heat ray forms a massive puddle of glowing oil that bubbles and detonates in a scalding explosion. While the Gogmazios performs this broiling breath attack, known as its Explosive Heavy Drakesbone Oil Breath, its chest will glow like a furnace and a fiery pattern resembling a frowning face will appear on its throat. It is a truly terrifying attack that makes hunters quake in terror, with many testimonies from individuals recounting that even those who are fortunate enough to escape the initial impact zone often still get caught by the subsequent blast. As its ferocity intensifies, the Gogmazios will fling and spew super-heated, boiling oil indiscriminately across the battlefield from the clouded skies above.
Behavior
The Gogmazios is a mysterious Elder Dragon that possesses the uncanny ability to appear and vanish without warning or trace in spite of its incredible size, earning it the nickname the Specter of War. Similarly, bestowed upon it due to the Dragonator famously lodged in in the back of a particular individual, the Gogmazios additionally bears the title of Giant Halberd Dragon. Paired with the sheer destruction it wreaks upon settlements, this unorthodox ability of its has aided it in skulking about largely unnoticed throughout history. Unlike most Elder Dragons, its presence is unspoken of in folktales and legends, being entirely absent from any records. Until its reappearance in the town of Dundorma, the Gogmazios only existed in scant sketches that transcribed the accounts of hunters who claimed to have witnessed it.
In order to sustain itself on the sulfur necessary for generating calories and producing its Heavy Drakesbone Oil, the Gogmazios often seeks out the armories of villages and nations alike by following the scent of stockpiled gunpowder. As a result, there have been a wide variety of reports of a settlement's weapon stockpiles being raided from across the land and various nations, with mysterious black ooze as the only evidence left behind. Before the Gogmazios was uncovered as the culprit behind the thievery, all anyone could do was guess as to what was happening, with one village that fell victim to a nocturnal visit from the Elder Dragon even believing a curse to be the reason behind their missing stockpile. Once the Gogmazios has sufficiently gorged itself on stolen gunpowder, it will burrow underground and enter hibernation in a prolonged state, akin to suspended animation. This process—which may last in cycles of several years, or even decades—is thought to be the reason behind its astonishingly long lifespan.
The Gogmazios does not always sneak into armories to raid them, however, as its pursuit of sulfur frequently drives it into conflict with humans. In the case of settlements smaller than Dundorma that are incapable of withstanding its assault, the Gogmazios will annihilate and reduce them to ruin, leaving behind no witnesses to tell of the Elder Dragon. However, even settlements blessed with access to Dragonators and Demolishers possess merely a fighting chance at repelling the Gogmazios rather than a secured victory. The armaments studding its carapace are all that remain to tell of the devastating raids the Gogmazios has launched throughout its life, their destructiveness believed to be at blame for why so few reports of sightings exist. For this reason, it came as a great shock to everyone when a dormant Gogmazios was discovered deep in the Forbidden Lands, resting directly under Azuz in a recently discovered expanse.
Understanding their limited available resources and that it would wipe out Azuz should it awaken, the Forbidden Lands Expedition Team called for an evacuation of the Flameborn and developed a desperate plan to discreetly dislodge and utilize the Convergent Elderbreaker against it. However, after a scout team was heading back from observing the Gogmazios, the colossal Elder Dragon had suddenly vanished without a trace and thrown the entire operation into chaos; several days would pass without any sightings of the Gogmazios, and it was suspected it would reappear alongside the approaching Firespring. In order to deal with the threat, the Ace Hunter Nadia was requested to provide assistance alongside seven other participants in an unorthodox team of eight hunters who would directly deal with the Gogmazios. Following the defeat of the Gogmazios and having learnt that it may dwell in the Eastlands, the expedition team would pay much closer attention to the Oilwell Basin and to any oddities in the region. Moreover, with the newfound knowledge that Elder Dragons are present within the Forbidden Lands, Gemma would get to work in an attempt to provide equipment upgrades for hunters from every unit using ancient artifacts.
Relation with Dundorma
During its construction, Dundorma's designers conceptualized several defensive measures to defend the city from threats, the most famous amongst them being the world's first Dragonator, considered the pinnacle of the era's technology. This Dragonator would go on to become a symbol to the people of Dundorma, its very heart, and would defend the people of Dundorma time and time again prior to being eventually retired and stored in a weapon's cache. It was then, during the age of Dundorma's forefathers long, long ago, that it was abruptly stolen; unbeknownst to the townsfolk at the time, the Gogmazios had discreetly raided their armory in search of its favorite food and incidentally stole the first generation Dragonator. The culprit behind the attack would not be identified until the same Gogmazios would return once more to Dundorma many years later; the discovery provided answers to many recent mysteries throughout the land, such as to the endless stockpiles of firepowder that had gone missing, as well as the feeling of dread heralding its attack.
It is believed that due to the vast reserves and stockpiles of gunpowder kept within Dundorma's armories, as well as its ability to withstand and rebuild from Elder Dragon attacks, the town has been marked as a valuable feeding ground for the Gogmazios. Prior to its attempted second raid, a trail of black ooze leading to Dundorma was reported by the Town Guard in nearby grasslands, alerting them to the presence of something. When the Gogmazios' existence was finally unveiled by the Dragonwatch, the Guild ordered Dundorma to use all available resources to vanquish it. Thus, after evacuating the people of Dundorma, the Town Guard rallied to lure the Gogmazios into the Battlequarters and keep it occupied to the best of their ability. During the final battle against the Gogmazios, Dundorma's original Dragonator would be severed from its back, with the firing mechanism remaining operational despite the weapon's great age and significant wear, allowing Dundorma's heart to be turned against the Gogmazios.
Following the Gogmazios' defeat at the Battlequarters of Dundorma, His Immenseness awarded the victorious hunter with the first Aged Text for avenging his forefathers, one of the Elder Hall's greatest treasures. Having proven their worth, he tasks the Valiant Hunter to decipher the prophecies foretold by the texts, and to uncover monsters similar to the Gogmazios that wander the world. Upon successfully deciphering the 9th Aged Text —entitled Aged: Pike —the coming of another Gogmazios was foretold, with the individual mentioned in the text being noted to grow more aggressive when having run out of gunpowder to feed on.

Physiology
Being a Rare Species of the Rathian, the Gold Rathian closely resembles her green counterpart. Her sole distinctive visual feature is her armor shell, which sports a shining gold coloration. It is believed this Rare Species is the result of a mutation that reverted a Rathian population back to some of their ancestral traits that the regular species had lost over eons of evolution. What brought on this mutation is unknown, although, it has been suggested to have been caused by the Gold Rathian's remote and extreme habitats. Some researchers believe that the mutation was catalyzed by the ingestion of enriched materials found only in the remote habitat this rare species dwells in. It has specifically been proposed that the mutation that gave rise to the Gold Rathian resulted from the bio-accumulation of energetically enriched minerals and ores, either by direct ingestion, or through their accumulation in species the affected Rathian preyed upon.
Beyond its coloration, the shell of the Gold Rathian displays numerous additional alterations. Believed to perhaps be due to the electrical conductivity of the precious metals present in her shell, the Gold Rathalos is vulnerable to the Thunder element. Conversely, the shell appears to be unaffected by the Dragon element. Another physiological feature that is altered in the Gold Rathian is her musculature. The leg muscles in particular are significantly empowered, granting the wyvern excellent mobility on land that far surpasses that of the common Rathian. All her muscles additionally exhibit incredible explosive force, allowing for relentless offense with never-ending attack chains, translating further into superior aerial mobility. As well, it has been noted that the very flesh of the Gold Rathian is hardened.
The Gold Rathian additionally sports a new weapon; among her clusters of venomous barbs that is shared with all known Rathian variations, this Rare Species hides a unique assortment of barbs, called Secret Thorns. These special thorns produce a secondary type of venom many times more potent than the regular poisons the Rathian is known to wield, allowing the Rare Species to swiftly repel even the Kushala Daora. By secreting this empowered venom alongside her regular toxin, the Gold Rathian can administer a supremely deadly sting with her barbs.
Perhaps the most significant trait of the Gold Rathian, however, is her vastly empowered flame breath. Due to the ways in which the remote habitat of this Rare Species has altered the body, the Flame Sac of the Gold Rathian has been found to be mutated to allow for two new functions. Firstly, the sac has been modified to be able to continuously take in air from the wyvern's respiration and funnel it into the flame production. Secondly, the flame sac now produces another substance in addition to the flame powder found in all Rathian: a flammable fluid that enhances the flames significantly. Called Rath Gleam, this special fluid is known to glow and boil seemingly on its own. Additionally, Rath Gleam protects the internal tissue of the wyvern from extreme heat. Curiously, Rath Gleam seems to be produced and concentrated in the wyvern's head, which had led to the belief that the mysterious substance might be some kind of modified cerebrospinal fluid. Through the combination of the additional air circulation and the Rath Gleam, the Gold Rathian's flame sac can activate and maintain a critical state in which heat permeates the body and allows for extremely powerful flames to be born. This ability is known as the Incandescent State.
It is believed that—aside from environmental factors—it was the ability to enter this Incandescent State that pushed the Gold Rathian towards becoming as powerful as she is, with the leading theory suggesting her body grew more powerful and resilient in order to withstand the wyvern's newfound power. A purple-blue glow envelops the body as the shell of the Gold Rathian brims with incandescent heat, which causes even the armor plates on the wyvern's head to soften. Fire production increases dramatically, to the point where small wisps of flame continuously leak from the Gold Rathian's mouth. The Gold Rathian is capable of producing a unique kind of fire, called the Incandescent Flame, which distinguishes itself through its pale-blue color. Due to the constant critical heat within the Gold Rathian's body, the wyvern can produce these magnificent flames near instantly, allowing for violent and rapid fire breaths. Aside from simply burning hotter than most fire produced by wyverns, the Incandescent Flame contains small embers that are prone to reacting with each other, resulting in powerful flame explosions and heat waves. This flame breath is so powerful that some believe it bestows the Gold Rathian with power that surpasses Elder Dragons.
Behavior
Due to her rarity and remote habitat, very little is known about the Gold Rathian. She is most commonly sighted in unusual and distant environments, such as the Guiding Lands or the Tower. However, the wyvern has been noted to pair up with the Silver Rathalos, and the two were on one occasion observed attempting to build a nest in the Elder's Recess. A Gold Rathian successfully pairing up with a Silver Rathalos would be considered a disaster, as the pair's claimed territory would have to be declared a no-man's-land due to the immense threat that these wyverns pose.
The Gold Rathian is known to be aggressive and territorial, to the point where it has been seen picking fights with Elder Dragons, such as the Kushala Daora. She is believed to derive her strength from an extremely nutritious prey species, however, what that prey might be has so far not been discovered.
Both the Gold Rathian and Silver Rathalos have held some degree of cultural significance over the years. The two were the defining members of the Rare Species classification, which was created to describe the limited remote habitat and small estimated population of these mysterious creatures. Beyond their relevance to the Hunter's Guild, the two rare wyverns have also been worshiped by various cultures across time, with the Gold Rathian being revered under the title, Golden Luna.

Unlike the typical Ceadeus, their horns appear to have grown in symmetrically, obscuring both of their eyes.

Physiology
An extremely elusive Subspecies of the Ceadeus, the Goldbeard Ceadeus is a marine Elder Dragon characterized by its lustrous, golden scales. Like the Ceadeus, it sports a whale-like body plan, a large beard that grows from its chin to its chest, and two massive horns. The hide of the Goldbeard Ceadeus, which is quite valuable as a forging material, is protected by rigid golden scales and a thick beard. The fur of this beard is rather stiff and is more akin to thin spines than fur. Despite the Subspecies' head and chest appearing larger, its skeleton is estimated to be roughly the same as the type species'. The underside of the dragon's body contains several light-emitting organs, theorized to have adapted to lure prey, or to communicate with other individuals of its species.
Its entire body is enveloped in a faint glow due to the luminous bacteria that lives on the surface of its skin. This algae reacts to the light produced by the Goldbeard Ceadeus' own bioluminescence, which greatly amplifies the light emitted from its body. In addition to the luminous bacteria, its body is home to a plant-like microorganism, likely a type of symbiotic algae. Using the carbon dioxide exhaled by the Elder Dragon and the light produced by the luminous bacteria, the symbiotic algae is capable of producing oxygen through photosynthesis. Although microorganisms also live on the skin of the base species, the Goldbeard Ceadeus' population of microorganisms is far greater comparatively and theorized to be what allows it to live in such deep waters. Some scholars believe the Goldbeard Ceadeus is an elderly Ceadeus individual that has amassed massive colonies of bacteria and algae over its lifetime, consequently changing the coloration of its scales and allowing it to forgo the need to surface for air.
Known to grow larger than those of the type species, the impressive horns of the Goldbeard Ceadeus possess extraordinary power and are thought to be unfathomably old. They contain hundreds of interior growth rings that can be observed when the horns have been severed, and if these rings are similar to the growth rings of a tree, as is suspected, then one could estimate the lifespan of an individual by counting the rings. Upon examining the growth rings of one specimen's horns, it was determined to have lived for an extraordinary length of time.
Behavior
The Goldbeard Ceadeus is found in only the deepest depths of the ocean in submerged ruins, it is often blamed for a wide variety of disasters by people. Due to its extreme rarity, little is known about the Goldbeard Ceadeus' behavior or its relation to its standard counterpart.

The Black Eclipse Wyvern Gore Magala (ゴア・マガラ, Goa Magara) is a Demi Elder introduced in Monster Hunter 4.
Summary
Black Elder Dragon-like monsters, with four legs and a pair of wingarms covered in hair-like scales that resembles a cape or cloak. As they are blind, they utilize these scales to aid their ability to sense the location and heat of other creatures. Once their senses reach its peak, Gore Magala will unfurl their feelers, which are usually flush with their head, and begin walking on their wingarms as well, which are equipped with opposable hands.
Gore Magala is a major spreader of the Frenzy Virus, with their breath and the scales from their wings being of capable infecting others with the virus.
Main Series
Monster Hunter 4: Gore Magala is first encountered in an un-named Quest, where the player must defend the Arluq, ending with Gore Magala being repelled. Gore Magala is later encountered in a mandatory Expedition, accompanied by the cutscene Aces in Danger. After being initially repelled, the player must escort the Ace Cadet and injured Ace Lancer, fending off two waves of Small Monsters as well as Gore Magala for a 2nd time in order to grant them enough time to clear a path. Afterwards, Gore Magala is first fought properly in the ★5 Urgent Quest: Tipping the Scales. The cutscene Dressed in Black will play the first time playing the Quest upon entering Area 7, causing the Gore Magala to immediately enter its Frenzied State. In Gathering Hall Quests, the Gore Magala is first fought in the ★3 Urgent Quest: Dark Wings, Dark Work. It is later fought again in the ★6 Key Quest: Dread Locked. The Caravan boards the newly constructed Arluq in an attempt to reach Cathar, however, they are hit by a storm and attacked by the Gore Magala whilst sailing. They are saved by the Ace Hunters and left stranded at Cheeko Sands, where it is learnt the Hunter's Guild has deemed the Gore Magala a major threat and marked it a target for the Ace Hunters. After their subsequent defeat against it, the Caravan's Hunter sets out to repel the Gore Magala and recover the left behind Ace Cadet and Ace Lancer, as well as their own Ace Palico who had left in an attempt to rescue them. After which, the Ace Commander formerly requests the Guildmaster to transfer their mission to slay the Gore Magala to the Caravan's Hunter. However, after it was seemingly successfully defeated, the Gore Magala would disappear and transform into something else entirely...

Physiology
The Gore Magala is an extremely unusual creature, possessing the three sets of limbs typically seen in Elder Dragons; two pairs bear its weight while walking, while the largest third pair are powerful wingarms that end in large, developed hands. Its body is covered entirely in a thick shell of overlapping, black scales, and from the membranes of its wings grow fine hairs that fall off and regenerate continually, creating a constant stream of dander that gives Gore Magala the appearance of being clad in smoke. The scales of the Gore Magala are coated in a deep-black, cornified layer, a hue described as so dark that it devours light rather than reflect it. These properties have granted these scales various reputations, as some consider them bringers of ill-fortune, whereas others view them as possessing a bewitching allure. These scales overlap and reinforce each other into an armored shell that protects the monster from harm. The Gore Magala's shells in particular are noted for their resilience, as they are said to harm the flesh of weaker attackers on contact. Harder sections of the shelling has even been rumored to induce insanity when forged as equipment.
One of the most crucial characteristics of the Gore Magala is that it is blind, possessing no visible eyes and lacking any traditional visual sense. It instead relies on an entirely unique sensory mechanism centered around the dander flowing from its wings. Fine hairs are produced constantly on the membranes of the Gore Magala's wings, which then detach to saturate the air and spread to nearby surfaces. The usually folded pair of horns that adorn its crown, called Feelers, have the peculiar ability to sense the presence of anything that is covered in the Gore Magala's scattered scales. By spreading this black dander, the Gore Magala can therefore enhance its ability to sense its surroundings, making up for its apparent blindness. The sensory acuity of the Gore Magala increases proportionally to the amount of dander that it has been able to expel.
As the amount of Frenzy particles in the area increases, the underside of the Gore Magala's wings begin to glow in various colors, transitioning from blue, to purple, and then to pink. At which point the creature alights with Frenzy, extends its horns, and wails loudly, entering a condition deemed the Frenzied State. This ability results in heightened ferocity and enhances the monster's abilities temporarily, although will wear off if the horns are damaged enough. It has been theorized that this behavior results from the Gore Magala temporarily giving in to the Frenzy Virus. Further research has suggested that the Gore Magala is able to activate this state voluntarily by stimulating its nervous system. Additionally, the purple glow that envelops the body in this state appears to be the result of the Frenzy particles within the creature's very blood becoming active, illuminating the blood vessels in select areas of the body. Due to these behaviors, the Gore Magala appears in ancient legends as a demon of disease and death.
The Gore Magala's dander serves a secondary purpose, as the tiny particles are the primary vectors that spread the Frenzy Virus (狂竜ウイルス, "Mad Wyvern Virus"), a mysterious condition that causes affected monsters to become violent and aggressive. It is called a virus due to its ability to spread from one victim to the next, resembling a viral disease. The disease takes effect when the dander is inhaled, although open wounds can also accelerate infection. Furthermore, the presence of the Frenzy Virus affects the Gore Magala's own body; accumulated clumps of the virus can crystalize into Frenzy Crystals, which the Hunter's Guild treats as highly dangerous items that must be turned in. As well, some of the scales on the Gore Magala's body absorb the Frenzy Virus over time, becoming empowered enough to earn a new name: Defiled Scales. One scale on the monster's body can be pushed even further beyond and imbued with unbelievable power.
The well-developed, muscular wingarms of the Gore Magala are covered in highly resistant plating, which deepen in hue as the monster's hunger and madness surge. While long and powerful enough to support a hexapedal stance, they are habitually folded against the Gore Magala's body, with the enormous hands resting on its shoulders. Due to their reach and power, they serve as its primary physical weapon. The claws of the wingarms are razor sharp, able to cut through living tissue with ease, as well as directly infect those they slash with the Frenzy. Rumors amongst artisans claim that even after these claws have been removed from the Gore Magala, they can still cause affliction to those that touch them. It is a fear that, curiously, predates the official discovery of the Frenzy Virus. Additionally, the Gore Magala has a flexible and whip-like tail that can be used as a devastating weapon to violently shred prey apart with its swipes. Its high destructive power comes from the many reverse scales that grow along its length.
The Gore Magala wings appear to be constantly writhing due to the endless stream of dander flowing from them, and it has been observed that torn off fragments from the membrane continue to move and writhe in spite of having been separated from the body. Due to their role in spreading the Frenzy Virus, it is said that the mere shadow of these wings causes insanity in those they cover. Sowing disease throughout the land as they flutter, these calamitous wings are unseen in the dark of the night. The Gore Magala's horns typically remain hidden by being folded neatly against the head, done to protect the valuable sensory organs from damage. However, when the dander saturation in the surrounding area reaches its apex, the horns will spring outwards and reveal themselves in order to take in as much sensory data as possible. When extended, the tips of the horns will glow in a foreboding purple, signalling they are wholly doused in the Frenzy. Due to the high risk of infection, these horns were at one point considered forbidden spoils and ill omens by the Guild.
Mysterious objects grow within the Gore Magala's body, as such, Hunters may sometimes retrieve a growth called a Nyctgem from it, which is said to imprison and swallow all nearby light.
Life Cycle
The Gore Magala is the juvenile state of the Elder Dragon, Shagaru Magala. It is theorized that this bizarre species of monster either originates from, or has a special relationship with the Sanctuary near the Wyverian settlement of Cathar. The Gore Magala is born when the scattered dander unique to the Shagaru Magala, which contains reproductive germ cells, infect a living monster. The germ cells then implant themselves and parasitically live within a Frenzied Monster, treating them as a nursery as they mature within their body. Should the infected monster be a compatible host, the germ cells will transform their host into a Gore Magala upon reaching a certain growth stage before further continuing their development. Due to this parasitic reproductive method, the Gore Magala is genderless.
Once the Gore Magala has traveled through various places and grown to maturity, it will shed its exterior shell and transition into its adult state. However, should it suffer exposure to the dander of the Shagaru Magala after its birth, the special compounds in those scales suppress its maturing process. In the worst case scenario, a suppressed Gore Magala may molt incorrectly, becoming an abominable, mutated Variant, known as the Chaotic Gore Magala. Through this, it has been determined that not all Gore Magala are capable of developing past their juvenile state. As a result, the Shagaru Magala is ensured a unilateral rule where it reigns supreme over the species as a solitary ruler, permitting other Gore Magala to exist only as its vassals.
Behavior
Although very little is known about the Gore Magala's behavior, it can often be observed twitching and convulsing as if writhing in pain, the intensity of this behavior has been suggested to be an indicator of its imminent transition into adulthood. It generally appears to roam the lands, spreading its Frenzy Virus far and wide.
As a species the Gore Magala is considered to be quite rare, and it is assumed that the total population size across the entire world is extremely small due to natural selection. The Gore Magala does not establish stable territories and is instead nomadic, wandering from place to place and maintaining small temporary domains marked by Frenzy scales in between migrations. While the Gore Magala is relentlessly aggressive towards intruders within its temporary territories, that aggression does not extend beyond the borders of the creature's domain, and it will not attack as long as one remains outside of its marked perimeter.
Super Biology Information
The Super Biology Book Series collects the thoughts and theories of real scientists that were asked to speak about monsters from the Monster Hunter series. Thus, they are inherently speculative and should be seen as such.
Fossil Expert Yoshitsugu Kobayashi explores the bizarre body of the Gore Magala by first taking a look at the absence of its eyes. Given that their eyes have degenerated, it is possible that other senses have become exceptionally well-developed. Additionally, Kobayashi wonders if they might possess a mechanism for detecting heat, akin to the pit organs found in snakes. Another possibility to him is that the ancestors of the Gore Magala evolved from creatures that lived in lightless environments, such as underground spaces or caves. For one reason or another, it seems they did not "choose" vision as their primary sense.
Next, Kobayashi considers the strange limbs of the Gore Magala. He asserts that the six limbs are most likely a deformity resulting from genetic or developmental abnormalities. Possessing four robust legs and two large wings (which also function as arms), these creatures are adapted for both terrestrial life and flight. Given that they can molt—a characteristic typical of arthropods—Kobayashi hypothesizes that the Gore Magala is a fusion of various biological forms, potentially originating from a mutation or other evolutionary anomaly.
Kobayashi is especially fascinated by the Gore Magala’s molting process. Molting is the process by which a significant portion—or even the entirety—of an organism's outer covering is shed during growth. In arthropods, molting is linked to specific stages of development, and the body's form may change as a result. In contrast, for animals such as reptiles, molting occurs as part of the renewal of their outer skin; in these cases, there is no significant change in the animal's overall form. Therefore, the fact that a Gore Magala molts and undergoes metamorphosis into a Shagaru Magala indicates that its molting process is more akin to that of an arthropod.
Another aspect of the Gore Magala that Kobayashi hones in on is the species’ rarity and implied low population size. One possible reason for their low population is that, being malformed, they may lack strong reproductive capabilities. Additionally, given that they are exceptionally powerful creatures, it is also possible that they exhaust their food sources during their growth process, leading to a decline in their own numbers. In this scenario, the reduction in their population could allow their prey base to recover, which might eventually lead to an increase in the number of Gore Magala.

Monster Hunter 4
The design process for Gore Magala was centered around the desire to make the story of Monster Hunter 4 as simple and easy to grasp as possible, in order to draw in more players. This meant that the game needed a more overt villainous force the player could be pitted against. It was thus decided that the main monster of the game would need to express a sense of evil and dread.
Initially, Yuya Tokuda wanted Gore Magala to walk on four legs. During the design process, one idea that emerged was to create a fight that would emphasize the new verticality that was at the center of Monster Hunter 4. This led to various concepts, including one where Gore Magala had the ability to cling to walls. Eventually the team landed on the concept of a monster that shifted from a four-legged stance to a six-legged one, which would alter its height notably and touch on that vertical design.
At one point, the gameplay concept was narrowed down to "a monster that can tranform, which changes it from four-legged to six-legged". Around that same time, Yuya Tokuda was experimenting with ideas on how to make late-game gameplay more interesting. He wanted to create a system that could empower various monsters beyond just giving them more health or attack power. After some coordination, the Frenzy Virus was created as a solution to both questions - it functioned as both a way for Gore Magala to transform and a narrative device that could be used to empower much of the monster roster in an interesting and memorable way.
A proposed name for Gore Magala was "Espira Magala", based on the French word for spirit.

Physiology
The Goss Harag is a muscular, largely bipedal Fanged Beast native to colder habitats, feared for its demon-like appearance. Its upper body and back are covered in a thick coat of insulating, white fur that repels snow and retains heat, while the rest of its body has a thinner layer of brown fur. Its rough, pitted hide is blue in color, covered in scars, and incredibly tough after having been tempered by the freezing external temperature as well as the Goss Harag's own burning internal temperature. Its face is distinctly bony and mask-like, sporting two pairs of stubby horns, a jagged maw, small ears, and sunken yellow eyes which lack pupils.
The Goss Harag's limbs are large and well-muscled, each bearing five rough claws and numerous hardened, black protrusions distributed across its hide, believed to be derived from additional claws. These limbs are capable of exerting an extreme amount of strength, able to shatter the ground and allow the monster to run and jump with an unexpected degree of agility. The forearms in particular are armored with carapaces called Braces, which have become hardened by the built-up layers of ice and snow, as well as their frequent use when the Goss Harag engages in combat. When angered, the Goss Harag's hide and face will flush a bright-red as a result of an increased flow of body fluids through it, which soften its hide and make it more flexible, in addition to raising its already high body temperature and increasing its vitality.
By inhaling cold air and supercooling its body fluids, the Goss Harag is able to spit out jets of freezing fluid as a means of attack, and can additionally spray this fluid on its arms to create blades or bludgeons formed from highly dense ice. These weapons may alternatively be created by the Goss Harag melting snow on its body, then re-freezing it onto its limbs. In addition to utilizing them for devastating melee attacks, the Goss Harag is known to shatter parts of its icy weapons and throw them as projectiles. However, the weight of the weapons will slow down the monster, subsequently causing it to become imbalanced and fall over should they be suddenly broken.
The Goss Harag's bile, obtained from its gall bladder, has been prized as a panacea and is claimed to grant immortality, although any actual practical uses for it remain unproven. The process of obtaining its gall bladder in the first place is difficult, however, as it degrades quickly in cold air.
Behavior
The Goss Harag is a nomadic, aggressively predatorial monster that is always prowling cold environments in search of prey to maintain its high body temperature, which may often lead it into conflict against the Tetranadon. The Goss Harag largely preys on smaller monsters, such as the Anteka or Popo, although its appetite drives it to attack large monsters it may come across as well. After having incapacitated a target, the Goss Harag may demonstrate an unusual behavior of slowly and deliberately walking up to them with a menacing gait, scraping one of its blades along the ground and only winding up for a finishing blow when standing right over the victim.
Development
The Goss Harag was based on the namahage (生剥げ/なまはげ), an oni-like yōkai that wears heavy straw garments and wields large blades, and is said to descend from snowy mountains once a year to frighten villagers. The design team was reminded of namahage when designing monsters to fit into the Frost Islands, as the namahage commonly appears in festivals in the Akita Prefecture of Japan, which has frequent cold weather and snow.

Physiology
The Gowngoat is a hooved quadrupedal Herbivore covered by thick fur and tan scales, with it sporting an exaggerated tail composed of puffed-up, darkened hair that drapes behind it. Its head possesses a dark domed cranium with several distinct ridges that protect its brow, a pair of ears directly below, blue eyes with horizontal pupils, and long locks of pale hair that droop on each side. When woven in the seams of armor, this warm Mohair provides protection against piercing strikes. The slate-gray coloration of the hairs composing its tail is believed to have evolved to allow the Gowngoat to curl into a ball and disguise itself as a rock. However, other researchers instead posit that the tail serves as a means to hide and protect newborn offspring.
Behavior
Endemic to the Citadel, the Gowngoat has a docile temperament and tends to live in herds. However, due to its timid nature, it is easily frightened and will flee at top speed alongside its group when attacked.

Physiology
The Gravios is a gigantic Flying Wyvern easily identified by its sheer size as well as its thick gray armor. It is the adult form of the Basarios, having grown to an enormous size as a result of continuing to eat rock as it has aged. Any of the leftover rocks or minerals from its digestion, such as iron or calcium, are absorbed into its skin and fused to it through exposure to intense heat, providing it with the tough and thick outer shell it is best known for, with this rock-like skin earning it the nickname of Armor Wyvern. The resulting composite possesses a highly unique layered structure that grants it an extremely high resistance to heat. Despite the shell still being quite hard, it is actually less tough than that of its juvenile self's, which likely stems from the fact that its sheer size is often enough to defend the Gravios from most perceived threats, so it does not need a tough shell to protect itself to the same degree. Various names have been given to this material: it is sometimes broadly called Gravite, while the outermost strata of the shell in older individuals is separately named Mediastinum in honor of its superior toughness.
The Gravios possesses a distinctive skull shape, with the former two nasal horns possessed by the juvenile Basarios having fused into a singular one. The armor plating covering its skull is notably hardened due to its high body temperature. Much like most Flying Wyverns, its forelimbs have been fashioned into a pair of wings, which bear a pale tan membrane supported by three of its fingers. Despite this, it does not commonly choose to take flight, typically only managing to stay airborne for a couple of seconds. However, it has been observed using its wings to briefly fly out of necessity, such as when ascending above especially tall obstacles. In comparison to the Basarios' relatively thin and stubby tail, the Gravios sports an especially bulbous tail end covered in a particularly high number of blunt protrusions.
The shelling of the Gravios is famed for its high level of resistance to heat, with it possessing enough to allow it to completely submerge its entire body in molten lava for short periods of time. However, even the sturdiest shell in the world would not be enough to allow it to wade through lava unimpeded, as the heat from the liquid would eventually reach its internal organs which would not be able to survive. Thus, to limit how much heat can affect its vital function, its organs are all concentrated in the center of the body, such that it takes the maximum amount of time possible for external heat to reach them. In combination with its massive body, this causes the Gravios to experience low thermal conductivity. However it comes with the fatal drawback of not allowing it to easily radiate heat produced inside of its own body.
Any waste materials resulting from digestion that cannot be used in the shell are repurposed in other ways. For example, any solid materials that are no longer needed are instead funneled into its Flame Sac where they can be melted down into a burning, lava-like liquid. Due to the high amount of heat generated from storing this substance internally, it must eventually be expelled from its body. The Gravios achieves this through the expulsion of a super heated breath that takes the form of a powerful heat ray. This ray additionally functions as a deadly weapon for confronting enemies, as well as as a method by which it can expel heat and prevent itself from overheating—a behavior vital for its survival. These beams are noted to be much hotter than the flames produced by other wyverns, such as those by the Rathalos.
In addition, the process of generating energy from its internal combustion reactions also produces a lot of excess heat, with more heat being generated as it burrows itself through the lava with its wings. This heat takes on the form of a flaming gas that must be regularly expelled, otherwise the excessive amount of heat may threaten to increase its body temperature beyond its natural limits. Alongside these burning gases, the Gravios is also capable of producing ones with narcotic properties, which are stored inside of Sleep Sacs until later expulsion. It is believed that these gases evolved to compensate for the wyvern's typically sluggish behavior. Covering its carapace are several small bump-like organs that serve as the method by which the wyvern is capable of expelling these various gases. A Gravios that does not manage to control its internal heat or produces an abnormal amount of it may see its carapace and even bones turn black; such an individual is called a Black Gravios.
Behavior
The Gravios is typically encountered in volcanic areas, where it feasts on the abundant ore deposits. However, it has been observed occasionally venturing outside of its usual habitat in order to feed. To accomplish this, it first submerges itself purposefully into lava to accumulate internal heat and increase the power of its already deadly heat ray, making it an excellent tool to use when hunting prey in other environments. This behavior seems to demonstrate that the wyvern is aware of how powerful its heat ray is as a weapon. The Gravios is generally left alone by other monsters due to its size, tough shell, and various powerful forms of offense. Nonetheless, in spite of its adaptations it is preyed upon by the Akantor, which resists even the power of the heat ray and can crack through its hard carapace with ease.
The moment a Basarios matures into and is recognised as a fully-fledged Gravios is said to be marked by when the bacterial colonies in its digestive tract, which have been acquired and cultivated by the wyvern gradually consuming external volcanic minerals, reach a sufficient enough size. From this point onwards, it almost exclusively eats rocks and minerals, and rarely predates upon organic matter, displaying a preference for ores containing explosive components, such as Firestones or Powderstones. The digestive process of the Gravios relies on the explosive properties of its meals: volcanic ores that enter the body heat up through the monster's internal temperature and explode inside of its gut. These explosions stimulate its bacterial cultures and causes them to begin rapidly reproducing, which releases nutrients the Gravios then absorbs. It is believed that this efficient process is what allows it to maintain its colossal size.
Super Biology Information
The Super Biology Book Series collects the thoughts and theories of real scientists that were asked to speak about monsters from the Monster Hunter series. Thus, they are inherently speculative and should be seen as such.
Fossil Expert Yoshitsugu Kobayashi notes that organisms that live in high temperature environments must develop either a method of easily shedding heat or a defense against heat entering the body. The Gravios, being perfectly adapted to volcanic habitats, has both: Its armor shell repels heat, and its heat beam serves as a way to rapidly expel thermal energy from the body. Kobayashi compares the latter method to some behaviors attributed to sauropod dinosaurs, which may have been able to shed heat through the surface of their long necks. As for the armor, Kobayashi notes that the armor shell of the Gravios is leaner and less bulky than that of its juvenile form Basarios. This is likely a modification that allows for better mobility, since the adult Gravios doesn’t have to worry as much about predators. Kobayashi also proposes that the armor plates of a Gravios might be permeated by blood vessels and thus additionally aid in heat dissipation.
On the matter of this wyvern’s diet, Kobayashi suggests that since the Basarios feeds on insects and small animals, its digestive organ might resemble a fairly standard stomach. But since the Gravios instead feeds on rocks, its digestive tract might be significantly simplified, with the individual losing more complex organ structures as it matures.
Monster Hunter
Gravios was created in order to have a high-level fight on the volcano map. The three combat elements that were proposed for it were:
a rock hard armor used to deflect attacks and bulldoze players
the ability to shroud itself in smoke and gas
a concentrated, highly deadly heat beam attack
Initially, the monster was also conceptualized as attacking players by curling up into a ball and rolling at them like a great boulder. This ability, as well as the monster's hard skin, could be countered by peeling the Gravios open, breaking its skin off until the wyvern was left in a thin, defenseless state. These two elements were however eventually discarded, and the final design did not include them.
