Physiology
An intraspecies variation of the Girros, the Great Girros acts as the leader of a Girros pack and is distinguished by its larger size and prominent hood. It sports a smooth-scaled hide with a jet-black dorsal coloration and a gray underbelly. Two long yellow stripes travel from the Fanged Wyvern's brow to the base of its neck, which transition into small splotched markings along its shoulders.
Three large gills are located on each side of the hood, lined with light-red cilia. When the concentration of effluvium in its habitat increases, the Great Girros will breathe through these gills, which utilize the cilia lining them to filter the air that enters the wyvern's body. Should a small amount of effluvium somehow bypass the cilia filter, the Great Girros is unaffected by it due to its strong immune system. Additionally, the gills serve a secondary function: communication. Using a specialized vibratory organ, the Great Girros can produce calls to summon and command its pack. These calls can be heard from a great distance, and even Girros who are not part of the Great Girros' pack will be beckoned by its calls.
Large yellow fangs protrude from the wyvern's upper jaw. The fangs are connected to a venom gland that secretes a paralytic toxin, allowing the Great Girros to paralyze its prey. Those bitten by the Great Girros' fangs continue to feel a tingling sensation throughout their body even after recovering from paralysis. Weapons made using Great Girros materials retain the fangs' paralytic properties, so great care must be taken when wielding them. Breaking the fangs only lessens the effect of the venom, and does not remove it entirely.
Behavior
The Great Girros is endemic to the New World continent, found only in the Rotten Vale and the Rotten region of the Guiding Lands. In the Vale, it nests in the upper level in tight spaces near effluvium-rich areas. Although it tends to occupy separate areas of the upper level, the Great Girros and the Radobaan may occasionally compete for food.
While the Great Girros is primarily a scavenger, it may hunt live prey alongside its pack. When hunting, it will command its pack to attack prey using vocalizations emitted from its gills. However, it tends to avoid conflict with other monsters, although not out of concern for its own pack. With such an abundance of food available in the Rotten Vale, it is inefficient to expend energy fighting for food when it can be found elsewhere, thus the Great Girros typically avoids crossing the paths of other large monsters. It is believed the Great Girros is capable of discerning the threat level of specific monsters, however, this is merely speculation.
When attracting a mate, the male Great Girros will use his vibratory organs to emit a courtship call. The gills are often scarred, as when males fight for dominance, they will target each other's gills. Females choose a mate based on how appealing a male's courtship call is.

Physiology
The Great Izuchi is a flightless, medium-sized Bird Wyvern that lives alongside a pack of smaller Izuchi, to which he acts as the alpha male. His body is covered in a thick coat of silky orange fur that fades to white along the brows, shoulders, spine, and tail. He brandishes a large, crescent-shaped sickle lined with dark blue scutes at the tip of his tail. The wyvern features a narrow skull with a prominent pointed snout. Inside the mouth is a serpentine, forked tongue, small teeth, and two enlarged retractable fangs located on the jaw. Despite His appearance differing from that of the Izuchi, the Great Izuchi is an intraspecies variation exclusively observed in males.
The fur of the Great Izuchi is extremely valuable to the people of Kamura Village. Weapons and garments modelled after the Great Izuchi are said to have been favoured by a legendary bandit, and remain popular with the people of the village to this day. As the material does not deteriorate throughout the process, the fur is often used in both clothing and forging.
The most striking feature of the Great Izuchi is the sickle-like blade located on his tail. The wyvern wields this weapon with alarming precision; by swinging his tail, he can easily cut through the flesh of his prey. Furthermore, the sickle itself is sharp enough to cleanly cut through bamboo stalks. It is also used as a prehensile limb to hook onto tree branches. At birth, the claws and the sickle are black. Upon reaching adulthood, they turn blue, before bleaching into a dull white as an Izuchi reaches the later stages of its life. The tail and claws of an elderly Great Izuchi are valued at a high price, although the majority of white claws and sickles come from the smaller Izuchi.
Behavior
The Great Izuchi is omnivorous, as while known for his cooperative hunting strategies with the Izuchi, he also feeds on arboreal plants and fruits.
The Izuchi, and by extension its greater variation, is a gregarious species. The Great Izuchi is the alpha male of an Izuchi pack; these packs are arguably the most coordinated of all known pack-hunting species, with the Great Izuchi delivering commands to his subordinates through vocalizations and tail movements. Male Izuchi are the hunters of the pack, while the females are tasked with raising the young. The Great Izuchi is usually accompanied by two high-ranking males when patrolling his territory or searching for food, and when confronted by a potential threat, the Great Izuchi will command his brethren into specific battle formations. Males are specially trained to work in cooperation with their leader to ensure a high hunting success rate. The bond between a Great Izuchi and his pack is strong, and he can be seen grooming and playing with his smaller packmates.
When the Great Izuchi's subordinates fall in battle, he will call the next in rank. Males that are entrusted with the protection of the pack eventually rise in the ranks of the pack, and the Izuchi that is highest in rank will eventually grow to become the next Great Izuchi.
Development
The design team based Izuchi and Great Izuchi on kamaitachi (鎌鼬/かまいたち), weasel-like yōkai with sickle-like tails that attack during strong winds, slashing victims so cleanly and quickly that they barely realize they were cut. As the kamaitachi are typically depicted as attacking in trios, the Great Izuchi was designed to fight alongside two lesser Izuchi who would assist its attacks. Their design was adapted into a raptor-like body shape to better fit in with the Monster Hunter setting.

Physiology
The Great Jaggi is a medium-sized, raptor-like Bird Wyvern with a considerably larger body than its brethren. It acts as the alpha male of a pack consisting of Jaggi and Jaggia, and is able to deliver complex commands through varied vocalizations, such as barks and howls. Like other Dog Wyverns, the Great Jaggi boasts a muscular body and an enlarged stature that makes it stand out from its pack. Its scaly hide is a lavender color with an orange stripe that lines its matte-cream underbelly. The hide itself is quite durable and has a rugged texture, with the less battle-scarred hides being of higher quality for crafting. Long, white fur grows along the monster's spine, starting from the top of the head and ending at the mid-point of the tail. The tail itself is lined with sharp, stout spikes that protrude outwards, making the wyvern's tail whips more deadly.
Each hand has three fingers and a small, spiked, thumb-like appendage. The first and third finger are stout and tipped with tiny claws, while the second finger is especially thick and features an elongated, hooked claw. The structure of the feet is similar, as while the first and third toe are of typical length, the middle toe is adorned with a large sickle-claw. The thicker claws found on the monster’s hands and feet are incredibly sharp and are used to rend foes.
The Great Jaggi's snout is long and slender with a shallow subnarial gap and lined with small, sharp teeth. Stout, spiked ridges run along each side of the snout up to the brow. At the base of the neck sits a pair of large neck frills; the Great Jaggi's most important feature, as it is a signal of its status among its pack whilst also being indicative of the wyvern's strength; the larger and bolder the frill is, the tougher the Great Jaggi is. This neck frill has a variety of uses: intimidation, courtship, and body temperature regulation. Should the frill be damaged or torn, the Great Jaggi will lose leadership of its pack.
Behavior
When a young Jaggi reaches a certain size, it leaves its pack to live alone. Should it survive the challenges of a solitary life, it will eventually grow into a Great Jaggi, before returning to its pack of origin to fight for leadership over the pack. For unknown reasons, Jaggi packs never have more than one Great Jaggi at a time, with one theory proposing that a Jaggi's growth is suppressed naturally in packs that contain a Great Jaggi. Meanwhile, another theory suggests the pack's feeding order—where the Great Jaggi eats first, followed by the Jaggia, and finally, the Jaggi—arbitrarily stunts the growth of the young Jaggi so that the Great Jaggi does not have to worry about potential future challengers.
The Great Jaggi is fiercely territorial and does not back down from threats. With the help of its pack, it will stand up to larger monsters, such as the Rathalos, and can take down large prey like the Aptonoth. Using complex vocalizations, the Great Jaggi can deliver commands to its pack, allowing it to coordinate attacks with its smaller brethren. This can make large packs very dangerous, even to larger monsters that stumble into the pack's territory.
While the Great Jaggi acts as the pack leader, its packmates are given separate roles; the Jaggia are typically responsible for raising young and defending the pack's nesting grounds, while the Jaggi patrol the territory and gather food for the pack. Different areas of the Great Jaggi's territory are connected by a series of underground passageways, with it even being known to use the abandoned nests of Altaroth.
Super Biology Information
The Super Biology Book Series collects the thoughts and theories of real scientists that were asked to speak about monsters from the Monster Hunter series. Thus, they are inherently speculative and should be seen as such.
While examining the Velocidrome, Gendrome, Iodrome and Great Jaggi all at once, Fossil Expert Yoshitsugu Kobayashi ponders the implications of their shared physical traits. He compares their size and body builds to those of Deinonychus and observes how their slender, light bodies allow for quick movements, while the sharp claws on their limbs lend themselves to shredding prey while jumping towards it. Kobayashi also asserts that based on their muscle structure, these wyverns could have a top running speed of 50 km/h. He also notes that the four wyverns all share rows of narrow, conical teeth that display the same shape throughout the entire mouth and sit with notable gaps between them. This resembles the dentition seen in piscivorous creatures such as gharials or Spinosaurus, and might imply that these wyverns eat fish.
Kobayashi notes that the crests of Velocidrome, Gendrome and Iodrome all form through physical structures growing on the head and then extend past it. He compares them to crests found on Dilophosaurus, Monolophosaurus and Guanlong, and asserts that just as is presumed in those species, the crested wyverns likely use their crests as decorations that aid in identifying and communicating to rivals and mates. Kobayashi singles out the Great Jaggi however due to it possessing a frill, which he assumes additionally serves as temperature regulation. Despite the fact that all four species work in packs, Kobayashi asserts that social behavior does not necessarily indicate a high level of intelligence. Instead, these bird wyverns strike him as creatures that flock together out of protective instinct, since individually, they are all fairly weak. He does however propose that their ability to coordinate might imply a more sophisticated social structure than initially apparent.

Physiology
The Great Jagras is a medium-sized Fanged Wyvern that leads a pack of Jagras and is the mature male of the species, his body is covered by smooth oblong scales. The scales on his flanks, underside, and upper limbs are a dull green, while those on his head, back, and lower limbs are a bright-yellow. Two yellow stripes run length-wise below the border between the yellow and green; the green color broken up by the stripes makes for excellent camouflage in lush environments. The Great Jagras has stocky limbs that, unlike the smaller Jagras, project outwards from his body. His front legs are roughly the same length as his back legs, albeit slightly bulkier, and all four feet possess four long toes with curved orange claws. The Great Jagras is not as agile as his packmates, although he is much stronger and still capable of traversing environments thick with vines and trees.
In maturity, the Great Jagras' head has grown much larger and more rectangular, with the lower jaw developing a pronounced chin and jowls. Atop each jowl is a subtympanic shield; the larger the subtympanic shields, the more attractive they are to any potential female partners. Most of the teeth are curved fangs, with some pairs being much longer than others. The jaws of the Great Jagras can unhinge, allowing for the consumption of large animals whole; biting is his primary method of dispatching prey. His eyes are midway between the front and back of the skull, the pupils of which are slit while irises are gold, yet reflect orange light in dark spaces. The Great Jagras' nostrils appear as vertical slits at the tip of the nose, and spikes have grown along the midline of the skull and along the underside of the lower jaw.
There is a dewlap on his throat that is larger than that of the lesser Jagras'; it is mostly green with a yellow rim and five yellow spots, and there are six thin spikes along its edge. The Great Jagras' torso is short yet flexible, with the chest and shoulder region being larger than the hips, and his tail is as long as the torso. A row of spikes run down along the spine, and the neck and back are covered by scales that have grown so long they bend like hair. This "mane" grows throughout the Great Jagras' life, serving as a show of both age and fitness. It is primarily used to attract mates and intimidate rival Jagras.
The Great Jagras is a voracious creature whose appetite rivals monsters much larger than himself. His gut is extremely elastic and becomes softer when stretched; it is capable of distending greatly to hold prey as large as the Aptonoth within. When full, the Great Jagras' movements become slow and awkward, although with the added benefit that his belly can be used as a bludgeoning weapon against attackers, via slamming it down or rolling over them. His stomach produces large quantities of very powerful acid that quickly breaks down ingested prey, and he is capable of vomiting half-digested chunks of acid-covered meat as a defense against attackers. However, the drawback of such potent acid is that it will begin to break down the stomach itself if it is empty for too long. To keep the acid at bay, the Great Jagras makes sure to always keep himself full. The Great Jagras becomes fatigued after his food is fully digested, so it is more efficient for him to partially digest one prey item, vomit the remains, and then consume another.
Behavior
The Great Jagras inhabits the dense rainforests of the New World, namely the Ancient Forest and certain regions of the Guiding Lands, generally staying below the understory. The behavior of the Great Jagras is dominated by his extremely large appetite; if his stomach is not full, he is most likely hunting for food. He primarily preys upon Herbivores of similar size—such as the Aptonoth and Kestodon —however, he will attack much larger monsters when hungry, often with unfavorable results. A common predator of the Great Jagras is the Anjanath, which has been reported throttling the Great Jagras with its jaws. Additionally, the Great Jagras has been sighted cannibalizing the smaller Jagras. The wyvern's hunger has made observation difficult, as researchers are often forced to flee, or risk becoming prey themselves. The Great Jagras' food-motivated aggression earned the monster his title of The Great Glutton.
The Great Jagras uses his front limbs in tandem with its jaws to tackle prey. While his prey is knocked over, the Great Jagras will unhinge his jaws and swallow the prey whole. Once full and bloated, the wyvern will crawl back to his pack's lair, his belly leaving a trail of skidmarks along the ground. While less aggressive when full, the Great Jagras will still defend himself if attacked, using his increased bulk to bludgeon attackers as well as projectile vomit chunks of meat covered in his highly acidic stomach acid.
A pack of Jagras will seek shelter in underground cavities supported by tree roots and consists of one leading alpha male—the Great Jagras—an unknown number of smaller males, and 10-20 females. When a male Jagras reaches a certain age, he will leave his natal pack to lead a solitary life; should he survive, he will mature into a Great Jagras. During the mating season, he will return to the area he originated from and fight one of the local Great Jagras for dominance over their pack. The winner of the battle will attempt to court every female in the pack, who will go on to lay three to four eggs in a warm area of mulch. Neither the male nor female Jagras protect the eggs, leaving them at risk to predators such as Kulu-Ya-Ku.
The Great Jagras will not receive aid from his pack in hunting, as the threat of cannibalism makes it dangerous for them to approach. The Jagras leave the task of warding off intruders to the Great Jagras, yet when their leader becomes enraged or is severely injured, the Jagras will swarm the intruder to protect their leader. However, their chief benefit comes into play after their leader has eaten, as the Great Jagras will regurgitate pre-digested chunks of meat and call for the Jagras to eat. This meat provides much more nutrients to the Jagras than their usual prey, and the food offered by Great Jagras is the reason Jagras form packs around him.
Development
Great Jagras was made larger than the "mid-sized monsters" of previous games, as noted by Yuya Tokuda. It was done so that it will be easier to hit for new players. However, the development team made sure to make the monster a deeper experience. According to Kaname Fujioka, Great Jagras had a greater amount of effort put into its development than other mid-sized monsters like Great Girros. It received an amount of care closer to proper large monsters like Rathalos. It has a form change and several interactions with other monsters. Great Jagras was made to teach players of the mechanics and ecosystems of Monster Hunter World. It, along with Anjanath and Rathalos, were the first three monsters developed for the game; used to test how far they could take its mechanics.
Concept art shown of Great Jagras is quite similar to the final design. All of which are simple lizard-like designs with sprawled limbs. All except one have spikes on the back and a dewlap. The exception is "Fanged Wyvern 4" which lacks spikes but has horns that glow green like Scoutflies.

Physiology
The Great Maccao is a medium-sized Bird Wyvern that acts as the alpha male of a pack of Maccao. He bears a general resemblance to his subordinates; his body is covered with vibrant green plumage, although he also sports a patch of yellowish feathers on his rump and tail, while the skin on his head and underbelly is a contrasting red. His scaling thickens each time he is struck, with the bravest individuals sporting the toughest hides whose old wounds have only served to further reinforce it. While this dulls the coloration of the scales, over time this results in scarred hides becoming more resilient and highly-prized, with them being used to reward valor. Like his brethren, his arms, legs, and tail are protected by sturdy brown shells that are especially durable, even when compared to the rest of his hide. The shells on his forelimbs are curled into fists, allowing him to deliver swift, yet strong strikes.
The Great Maccao can still be easily distinguished from his pack mates due to his larger, more muscular build and his superior crown of feathers at the back of his head. One of the alpha's most striking features, while all males possess a decorative crest, the size and beauty of it is proportional to the strength of the individual, with the brilliant-gold, eccentric plumage possessed by the Great Maccao establishing his status as the alpha within the pack hierarchy. When he grows especially agitated, the crown feathers will spread apart and stand fully erect.
His paddle-shaped tail is powerful and muscular. Its wide and thick tip sports flexible structures along its underside akin to paw pads, allowing him to rest his weight entirely on his tail. The tip's sides are adorned with sturdy golden tail-spikes on either side that grip to surfaces, allowing the wyvern to maintain his balance. With these adaptations, the Great Maccao is capable of using his tail like a springboard, allowing him to launch himself forward to deliver powerful leaping kicks with his thick clawed feet. Before performing this strike, he will typically place one of his legs onto the ground, allowing him to better control his posture.
Behavior
Much like his subordinates, the Great Maccao primarily resides in the Jurassic Frontier. Despite being the alpha of a Maccao pack, his leadership skills are surprisingly poor, and his pack will only support and fight alongside him when he is healthy. Thus, when caught in a dangerous situation where their leader is weakened, the smaller Maccao will flee and leave the Great Maccao to fend for himself.
The Great Maccao primarily feeds on the eggs from nests of other large monsters. Alongside punching opponents, his hands are specially evolved for cracking open eggs. Once he has successfully snagged an egg in his jaws, he will bring it to a safe area where he will then crack the egg open with his fist, before feeding on the yolk inside.
Development
Great Maccao was developed to be different than other early-game Bird Wyverns like Great Jaggi. Its attack patterns were inspired by kickboxing, Muay Thai and kangaroos. It's appearance meanwhile was based on the Archaeopteryx, as well as incorporating Native American influences.
To match the Jurassic Frontier, the Great Maccao was designed to feel "primitive."

Physiology
While at first Great Thunderbugs resemble a swirling ball of light, in actuality they are composed of a swarm of several exceptionally large Thunderbug individuals. The cause of their increased size is a result of these Thunderbugs having been incubated inside the body of an Elder Dragon, namely the Yama Tsukami. Behavior
Despite no longer living inside the Yama Tsukami, Great Thunderbug swarms still prefer to remain inside the large ruins their host Elder Dragon frequents. Additionally, they have been known to frequent caves and above bodies of water at night, seemingly preferring to congregate in areas where they are out of reach of the sunlight.
Whilst the bright flashing flight of the Great Thunderbug swarm is said to be a fantastical sight, they are exceptionally dangerous, with this danger being frequently discussed amongst scholars. Highly aggressive, once an adversary is spotted, the once dull-blue light of the swarm shifts to an aggressive red as they begin to chase down their target, simultaneously discharging their electricity as they do so. If the swarm is threatened too severely, such as if a member is killed, the rest of the swarm will dissipate. Despite always being found in swarms, the reasoning behind why these controlled groups are formed in the first place is still unknown.

Physiology
A Subspecies of the Nargacuga with mottled green fur and a striking red tail tip, it shares many characteristics with the common Nargacuga: bladed wings, incredible agility, and a hardened upper jaw resembling a beak; even its skeleton is indistinguishable from that of its jet-black cousin. Its coloration likely emerged from living in lush areas, allowing it to camouflage amongst the dense greenery. Subtle irregular differences in the pelt's coloration, and the iridescent scales that shift in coloration in response to light, allow the wyvern to effectively disappear into the underbrush.
In addition to its coloration, the structure of the spikes on the Green Nargacuga's tail also differ from those found in its relative. Known as Tailspears, in addition to being extremely sharp and capable of being dislodged from the tail as projectiles, they can cause dizziness and stun victims upon impact. Usually concealed underneath the wyvern's fur, the Tailspears are revealed to be a bright red when bristled. The cartilage between the tail's vertebrae is speculated to be extremely flexible and will stretch when the monster makes a sudden movement—such as when slamming its tail downwards—extending the reach of its attacks. The tail additionally allows the Green Nargacuga to balance itself and adjust its trajectory when aiming at prey.
Behavior
The Green Nargacuga is found in lush forested environments, such as the Flooded Forest and Deserted Island. Much like the more widespread Nargacuga, it is an ambush predator that preys on Herbivores, with it favoring the Kelbi as a prey item in particular. When hunting, it remains as still as possible to not disturb the foliage around it, as any sudden movement could make noise. The unique properties of its Tailspears as well as its ability to perform successive leaps are thought to be adaptations to account for this. The Tailspears of the Green Nargacuga will bristle with excitement when prey is sighted, although it will also intentionally bristle its Tailspears when confronting a potential foe, acting as a warning sign. Curiously, the Green Nargacuga sleeps in areas in which it is exposed, such as in trees.

Physiology
The Guardian Arkveld closely resembles its basal form, with it having a slightly more pale coloration and possessing the signature glowing purple veins of other Guardians, along with pure-black eyes lacking visible pupils. The veins are distributed along its body, appearing most prominently on its head, dorsal plates, and chainblades. The Guardian Arkveld largely inherits the same abilities of the original species, such as its physicality, ability to dexterously manipulate its chainblades for combat, and the ability to absorb elemental energy and convert it into Dragon element. In addition, it can discharge Wylk energy from its chains, creating explosions that generate Wylkcrystals; these crystals react violently upon contact with its Dragon element discharges.
Similar to other Guardians, the Guardian Arkveld's digestive and reproductive organs have atrophied, and it has no need to eat food for sustenance. Instead, it subsists entirely on Wyvern Milk absorbed from surrounding Wylksprings, as well as uniquely leeching from unhatched Construct cocoons. Additionally, the absorption of Wylk allows it to swiftly recover from damage, whilst granting it an indefinite lifespan as long as it continues to absorb it. However, due to retaining parts of the unique physiology and energy absorption abilities of the Arkveld species, it is capable of additionally absorbing elemental energy to feed itself. This allowed it to regain parts of its original physiology and instincts, such as its predatory drive and reproductive capabilities, by absorbing energy from other monsters. The latter trait even allowed it to miraculously restore the Arkveld species back from extinction through parthenogenesis. However, it appears to still be unable to properly digest solid food.
Behavior
Originally created to serve Wyveria, the Guardian Arkveld managed to reawaken and break free after falling into dormancy, escaping the Ruins of Wyveria and starting to prey on other monsters. By aggressively targeting and draining the largest sources of energy it could find, namely singling out the apex predators of different locales, it was able to partially regain its nature as a Flying Wyvern, such as its drive to predate and ability to lay eggs. However, it was unable to control its intake of Wyvern Milk after learning feeding behavior, upon which the excess energy intake from feeding caused it to descend into a berserk frenzy where it slaughtered and attempted to devour every monster in its vicinity, despite seemingly being unable to properly ingest the food. The Avis Unit was forced to put it down to prevent it from decimating the ecosystem.
It is unknown how the Guardian Arkveld behaved prior to its reawakening.

Like Arkveld, both themes contain a motif of its debut game's main theme, in this case, Wild 's " The Beauty of Nature ".

Physiology
The Guardian Doshaguma largely shares the external physiology and body plan of the original Doshaguma species. However, the mane of fur covering its upper body has turned a pallid-white from exposure to Wylk energy, as has the rough hide on its forelimbs. Its claws have similarly turned white and rigid from energy exposure, allowing them to easily slice through armor. The Guardian Doshaguma's forelimbs and face additionally have the Guardians' signature glowing purple veins distributed throughout. Its eyes are pure black and lack visible pupils.
The Guardian Doshaguma inherits and enhances the advanced physical strength of the original Doshaguma, particularly in regards to its hide and fur, which has become as hard as metal thanks to the Wylk energy coursing through it. In addition, it is able to secrete a highly acidic saliva that corrodes bitten targets and can be spat out as a ranged attack; its fangs are durable enough to remain unharmed by the acid. By charging its forelimbs with Wylk energy, the Guardian Doshaguma's strikes are additionally capable of creating explosions that generate Wylkcrystals on impact.
Similar to other Guardians, the Guardian Doshaguma has atrophied digestive and reproductive organs, and has no need to eat food for sustenance. Instead, it subsists entirely on Wyvern Milk absorbed from its surroundings. Absorption of Wylk allows it to swiftly recover from damage, whilst giving it an indefinite lifespan as long as it continues to absorb it. However, the Guardian Doshaguma is still able to run out of Wylk if it overuses its abilities or receives heavy damage, which will force it to retreat and replenish it from the Wylksprings around its habitat.
Behavior
The Guardian Doshaguma shares the ornery and territorial natures of the original Doshaguma, readily attacking and killing anything that enters its domain despite no longer needing to eat or feed, including other members of its species. Additionally, the Guardian can occasionally be observed vomiting up a mixture of gastric juices and Wyvern Milk.
Like all Guardian monsters, it is exclusively found in the Ruins of Wyveria.

The Guardian Seikret has a general body structure similar to that of its normal counterpart, although there are key differences, the most striking of which being the coloration. In contrast to the vibrant blues, greens, and purples of the standard variety, it primarily displays a desaturated-gray hue adorned with white feathers, streaks, and spots across various areas of its body. The body additionally exhibits a subtle green tint in some areas, and there are purple veins that grow across the dorsal region and forelimbs. When charging up a Wylk-infused attack, these areas will also glow with a light-purple hue. Its eyes are pure black and lack visible pupils.
The majority of the Guardian Seikret's physiology is overall significantly sleeker and sharper than that of its natural counterpart. For example, the normally rounded feathers are instead thinner and much more jagged, and the scales found along the body similarly exhibit small spiked protrusions at their ends. The claws are daggerlike, with the innermost claw on the forelimbs having been modified into a prominent sickle claw used for slashing at enemies. Additionally, there are significantly more spines on the dorsal region of its body, most notably on the lower back and the back of the neck.
Similar to other Guardians, the Guardian Seikret has atrophied digestive and reproductive organs, and has no need to eat food for sustenance. Instead, it subsists entirely on Wyvern Milk absorbed from its surroundings. Absorption of Wylk allows it to swiftly recover from damage, whilst also granting it an indefinite lifespan as long as it continues to absorb it. However, the Guardian Seikret is still able to run out of Wylk if it overuses its abilities, which will force it to retreat and replenish it from the Wylksprings around its habitat.
Behavior
The Guardian Seikret is unique amongst its classification, as unlike other Constructs, it has been observed to form small packs of around two to four individuals. It is highly coordinated and cooperative within such a pack: alongside its packmates, it will surround a target and utilize both its claws and Wylk-infused attacks to subdue them. If a cocoon containing a Guardian Seikret is disturbed, whether it be due to a monster damaging it or a Hunter using their weapon on it, it will begin to emerge. After this occurs, the individual will call for the rest of its dormant packmates, causing them to exit their cocoons. Once hatched, any large monsters or hunters nearby will immediately be seen as a threat and violently attacked.

Physiology
The Gypceros is a strange medium-sized Bird Wyvern distinguished by the blue-gray hide that covers the majority of its body in the absence of any scales or shelling. Save for the ribbed plating on its chest, the underside of its body and neck is a contrasting shade of light-gray, while the band running down the length of its neck and the undersides of its feet are colored a rosy brown. Uniquely, its hide is rubbery and highly elastic in nature, insulating the Gypceros from both natural and man-made electric shocks, such as those of Shock Traps, and is known for both its surprising resilience to blunt strikes and its odd scent. The gray hide concludes abruptly at its tail, which is instead colored a pale pink. This tail is very thin, ends with a bulbous tip, and displays an exceptional elasticity even when compared to the rest of the Gypceros, being capable of stretching to over twice its original length when swung like a club. This pliancy makes it by far the most difficult part of the wyvern to damage.
Its front limbs consist of a pair of wings formed from three fingers that support a pale-pink wing membrane. Like the rest of its body, they are both highly elastic and resistant to both electricity and poisons. While the Gypceros is capable of flight, it appears to prefer to fight on the ground. By contrast, the hindlegs are stout and muscular, giving it excellent running capabilities, allowing it to even run up and along steep walls and cavern ceilings. The source of the near tireless energy that the Gypceros can output is a special bodily fluid, known as Dash Extract, that is secreted and pumped internally throughout its entire body.
The skull possesses a cream-colored beak that is distinctly buck-toothed, with a single upwards-curving, blunt-tipped horn atop its snout and several spiked growths on its chin, giving it an overall short, yet tall profile. Likely the Gypceros' most recognizable feature is the large ovoid crest planted atop its head, composed of quartz-like crystals or mineral fragments, such as Lightcrystals, which it has ingested—partially explaining its seeming attraction to shiny objects. The crest is attached to specialized muscles that allow it to be moved: by rapidly vibrating its head, the Gypceros causes its crest to repeatedly collide with its nasal horn. The resulting impact destroys the mineral organs contained within the crest to trigger a reaction that produces an enormous blinding flash of light. This flash can be used to disorient aggressors when the Gypceros is cornered, and can even be powerful enough to knock them fully unconscious.
To additionally protect itself from oncoming threats, the Gypceros can spew a toxin from its mouth, an ability that grants it the nickname of Poison Strange Bird. While this toxin is not considered particularly potent compared to other monsters, it is still more than that of an Ioprey, and due to the large quantities in which it is expelled, can easily prove fatal to humans. The globs of toxic sludge that the Gypceros spits are highly viscous and adhesive, causing them to both flow alongside and cling to terrain before dripping off, although they are harmlessly dissolved if exposed to water.
Behavior
The Gypceros primarily inhabits warm, humid regions, such as swamps and caverns. It has a timid nature, and as a result tends to not remain in one place for long, migrating frequently. It is also known to have an intense curiosity towards items carried by humans, which is often exhibited by an infamous tendency to steal them whilst it is attacking. Furthermore, it demonstrates a notable preference towards pilfering shiny objects, such as ores and precious metals.
While it has been speculated that due to the wyvern's high levels of intelligence the Gypceros might just enjoy collecting these shiny items, much like some humans do, it has also been observed that the male Gypceros uses these shiny items in courtship rituals. During the breeding season and after securing a nesting site, the male scatters his collection of shiny objects around his nest and, upon noticing a female flying overhead, begins to emit flashes from his headcrest, which are reflected off the various items he has used as decoration. Should the female approve of this display, she will descend and allow the male to mate with her. It has additionally been witnessed that the male Gypceros may personally gift some of his "treasures" to females in an attempt to court them, with larger and more reflective presents earning more appreciation from the recipients.
When the Gypceros is cornered and its arsenal of defensive tools have failed to deter its attacker, the wyvern will play dead. If the ruse is successful in causing the attacker to leave the apparently deceased Gypceros, it will seize this opportunity to flee. However if this fails, it will drop the act and thrash about in a violent surprise attack. This peculiar behavior has thus far not been observed in any other known monster.
The Gypceros is omnivorous and has been observed feeding on Vespoids, rotten carcasses, and Toadstools. Upon stealing something edible—such as meat, insects, or mushrooms—it will consume the item immediately. On occasion, it has even been observed drinking directly from naturally occurring pools of poison. On the inverse, the Gypceros serves as the primary food source for the Nerscylla, which alongside consuming the Bird Wyvern, also flays it and uses its skin as body armor. The left-over body gets suspended by string and left hanging inside of the Nerscylla's web.

Once the requirements are met, the quest will be available under the 8★ category in Port Tanzia.
Physiology
While this colossal Subspecies shares many physiological features with the standard Jhen Mohran, such as an identical skeletal structure, it is differentiated by its organs and the surface of its body. Superficially, the Hallowed Jhen Mohran has a darker skin tone and is covered in purple clusters of quartz, which has accumulated through the Elder Dragon's dives into the Great Desert, which sand off impurities and concentrate the mineral upon its body. The purer these crystals are, the more transparent they appear. As well, the Hallowed Jhen Mohran is believed to have larger lungs than its counterpart.
Behavior
Very little is known about the life of the Hallowed Jhen Mohran, although, based on the enlarged lungs and purified minerals of the Elder Dragon, it is believed the Hallowed Jhen Mohran dives deeper into the sand sea than the standard Jhen Mohran. The Hallowed Jhen Mohran is even rarer than the regular species, and only ever surfaces briefly from the sandy depths to take a breath exclusively at night. Curiously, it appears to stay on the surface for longer during the full moon. Research into the Great Desert has suggested that it was at one point an actual ocean, and that its deepest depths contain condensed layers of ancient coral reefs. These layers are saturated with bacteria specialized in breaking down dead corals, and it has been proposed that these deep desert bacteria form the main diet of the Hallowed Jhen Mohran.

The Harpios (ハルプス, Harupusu) is a small Wingdrake introduced in Monster Hunter Wilds.
Summary
Deep-blue piscivorous Wingdrakes with an elongated horn resembling a harpoon, which they use to spear fish as they circle and dive from above. This horn folds back when not hunting, concealing their vibrant, multicolored crest. They lounge around on land near active water spots, preening themselves whilst patiently waiting for when smaller fish are spooked towards the surface, inciting a feeding frenzy.

Physiology
The Harpios is a vibrant Wingdrake that, much like other Wingdrakes, resembles a miniature Flying Wyvern. It has a long neck and tail, a compact body, back limbs with claws, and a pair of front limbs modified into large wings. It stands in an upward stance using both its legs and wings. The ventral side of its body is sky-blue with darker spots and he dorsal side sports a darker hue; the two colors are separated by a yellow stripe.
An S-curved neck holds up the Harpios' small head, on the nose of which is a long, thin horn that extends far behind the head. This Snout Horn can rotate to point forward in order to pierce small fish when the Wingdrake dives into water. Additionally, the horn is also used by Hunters —who rip it off the Wingdrake with their Hook Slinger —to launch it as Piercing Pods through their Slinger. Behind the horn is a fin that is supported by flexible rays which extend down the neck, this fin is light blue on the bottom and bears a mottled pattern of dark-blue and yellow towards the top. Its needle-like teeth are small, and the mouth is lined by hardened skin that forms a cutting edge. The tiny eyes are black in color, and the tail has a blue fin that is similar to the one on the neck.
The wings are formed from modified hands with five digits each, three of which are small and yellow; they do not support the wing, although are used for walking. The main support for the wings comes from two digits that are blue and extremely long, while dozens of rays form secondary support structures. Skin stretched between the digits and rays display a mottled, wave pattern of varying blue shades. The Harpios is a capable flyer, able to dive into the water and precisely impale small targets before flying back out. The legs are yellow below the ankles and have webbed feet with four toes adorned with very small claws.
Behavior
The Harpios is endemic to the Forbidden Lands, having only been seen near the rivers of the Scarlet Forest and swamps of the Oilwell Basin. It is seen in groups of two or three in the forest and in much greater numbers in the Basin, where a colony has formed on the cliffs looking over its muddy waters. Several Harpios can be seen basking in the sunlight on the cliffs, while others descend to the swamps.
The Harpios spends a similar amount of time in the air as on land, typically near water. On the ground, it frequently preens its wings with its mouth or pecks at the water's surface. It is docile towards terrestrial creatures, although it will only tolerate hunters from a distance. Should a hunter stand too close for too long, the Harpios will take to the skies in much the same way as when a large monster approaches. The Harpios primarily feeds on fish, and generally hovers in one place or circles above water bodies, surveying for prey. When massive schools of fish form in the Scarlet Forest, the Harpios congregates alongside other piscivores to take advantage of the large gathering of prey in a feeding frenzy. The Harpios flies above the bait ball before diving into the water with its horn flipped forward. After which, it flies out of the water with its quarry skewered on its rostrum, which it eats in the air. These schools can be a trap for the Wingdrake, however, as the Lagiacrus may leap from the water and snatch a Harpios out of the air.

Physiology
The Hellblade Glavenus broadly resembles the common Glavenus, although is distinguished by several physiological differences that mark it as a Deviant. The base color of its armor shell has shifted to a darker red, while the previously blue spikes across its body have turned almost black in color, with glowing-red, lattice patterns and veins permeating them from the base upwards. Amongst the horns on its head, one has grown notably asymmetrically, being larger and more twisted than its twin.
The altered coloration indicates the more profound transformations that the Hellblade Glavenus' shell has undergone. The scales of this Deviant display an altered chemical composition that is similar to the blast powder found in monsters such as the Teostra. Due to an additional mutation to the wyvern's flame organ, the Hellblade Glavenus can spike its internal temperature far higher than common individuals. This increased heat carbonizes the outer layer of its scales, causing it to flake off the body and hover around the Hellblade Glavenus in the form of clouds comprised of light, highly explosive dust. It has further been discovered that the Hellblade Glavenus might emerge as a result of a regular Glavenus absorbing an unknown, unusual mineral into its body, triggering the mutations that turn the individual into a Deviant.
Behavior
The Hellblade Glavenus is known to be extremely aggressive and dangerous, as it expertly wields its new explosive abilities to decimate enemies. It is believed that this Deviant's greater aggression is actually a way for the monster to dissipate the unusually high heat within its body, with the wyvern's ferocious movements and explosions serving as a way to shed heat. Very little is known about its behavior beyond this, although it has been sighted alongside other regular and Deviant Glavenus individuals on occasion. Due to the threat the Hellblade Glavenus inherently poses, its appearance is an emergency that may only be dealt with by Wycademy Hunters who possess a Special Permit, as is the case with every other Deviant.

Physiology
The Hermitaur is a small Carapaceon species armored with a pale-red carapace patterned with several white stripes. It possesses four legs used for locomotion as well as an additional pair of limbs fashioned into a small pair of grasping pincers. Its face sports black eyes suspended on stalks, a pair of antennae, and a circular maw lined with teeth.
While most of its body is covered in a hard-layer of protective armor, the Hermitaur's back-side is exceptionally soft by contrast. Thus, it typically wears a hard piece of shelling over its backside to protect itself from danger. As the Carapaceon ages and its old shell grows too small, it will periodically replace it with a new one that is more comfortable. The Hermitaur is the juvenile form of the significantly larger Daimyo Hermitaur.
Behavior
The Hermitaur typically prefers to live in sandy areas and is most active during the warm and breeding seasons. While at rest, it will bury its entire body into the sand in order to keep itself safe, although careful observation can reveal where it is hiding as its breathing can cause the sand around itself to be stirred. If prey happens to pass above it whilst it is buried, it will quickly lash out with its claws to intercept them. The Hermitaur is omnivorous and feeds on a wide variety of foods, including sand-dwelling insects, fish carrion, and plants—such as mosses. It utilizes its sharp pincers to tear off edible chunks of its food before lifting it into its mouth.
If the Hermitaur encounters a new shell, it will first uses its claws to measure the space inside to see whether or not its body could fit. If it deems it a good fit, it will shed its old shell and move into the new one. While it most commonly will use the skulls of other monster species to fashion its shells, it is not picky about materials and will utilize anything that is both sufficiently hard enough to protect itself and spacious enough to fit its body. This can include pickling jars as well as the armor of hunters.

Physiology
The Hirabami is a medium-sized purple Leviathan with a long flat body and speckled teal spots on its grayish underbelly, with much of its body being wrapped in a pliable, cloth-like purple hide carrying insulating properties. Its stubby forelegs have small fins on the lower half and end in two talons each, with one being greatly elongated and hook-like, while its hind legs are spindly and have webbed digits. The Hirabami primarily slithers to move around on the ground, only using its small limbs for leverage or grip. Its body is extremely flexible and able to contort, fold, and roll up with no difficulty, allowing it to perform agile maneuvers while either grounded or airborne. The Hirabami is known to periodically shed its skin, leaving behind molts that are harvested by the region's people for their curative properties.
The Hirabami has a pointed bony head with beady yellow eyes, along with a bifurcated lower jaw that folds outwards when it opens its mouth; the inside of its mouth is teal and lined with many sets of small blunt teeth. Its mouth has a tube-like orifice at the base, from which the Hirabami can spit a freezing secretion that solidifies on contact to immobilize prey. Lining the underside of the neck are several pairs of gills.
The Hirabami has a two-layered elastic membrane on its neck that is able to flare out into a large hooded structure. When expanded, this lightweight membrane catches and modulates the strong wind currents in its habitat, allowing the Leviathan to hover in place and swim through the air. The Hirabami can maintain stable flight even in extreme weather, yet even in regions without strong winds—such as the Wounded Hollow —it still demonstrates the ability to hover relatively freely. Its small scales are sturdy, yet extremely light as well as easy to process.
The flat ribbon-like tail of the Hirabami accounts for much of its body length, the teal underside being lined with many rows of pincer-like claws that oscillate like swimmerets while folded. Several pairs of much larger barbed claws flank its rake-like tail tip and serve as the Hirabami's primary means of hunting, with the monster using them to immobilize and cut apart prey.
Unlike most other Leviathans, the Hirabami's blood is green in color.
Behavior
The Hirabami is a pack hunter that is most often found traveling in a group of three individuals, allowing them to surround prey from multiple directions. Should any member of the group be killed or seriously injured, the survivors may opt to retreat. The Hirabami will nest in groups and can be seen clinging to surfaces using its scales or foreclaws, often hanging from ceilings as it sleeps.
The Hirabami is known to prey on smaller monsters, like the Rafma, which it restrains by coiling around them with its tail before swallowing them whole. It has been seen in territorial disputes with other predators in the Iceshard Cliffs, such as the Blangonga.

Physiology
The Hornetaur is a small Neopteron whose body is clad in a blackish, turquoise carapace with a reddish abdomen. Its head bears a pair of proportionally long horns arranged vertically that curve inwards, their sides lined with spikes. It sports six pairs of orange legs lined with sharp thorns. Despite its exoskeleton being surprisingly tough, the rest of its body is exceptionally delicate and very easily destroyed by excessive force. As a result, poisons are typically used in order to kill the monster in a way that leaves its body intact.
While it possesses a pair of wings that it can use to fly, the Hornetaur instead prefers to remain on the ground and traverse by crawling; its wings are kept folded under the elytra on its back when not in use. These wings are particularly fragile, with even the slightest of excess force being enough to tear them in two, making harvesting the wings in perfect condition especially difficult.
Behavior
The Hornetaur is most commonly found in swamps, where it displays a strong preference for remaining in dark areas, such as caves, and becomes especially active at night. Despite this preference, it displays strong phototaxis towards light sources, such as open flames; particularly bright lights are known to send it reeling onto its back. It has a highly flexible diet, with it being known to feed on both the sap present in fruits and trees, as well as carrion if it is in an abundant enough supply.
Possessing a strong territorial instinct, the Hornetaur is highly aggressive towards anything that approaches it, instantly retaliating on sight by charging with its horns. It will often ambush its target by leaping at them from out of bushes. While its horns lack any additional toxin, they still serve as an especially dangerous weapon due to their sheer size.

Physiology
The Hypnocatrice is an elegant Bird Wyvern boasting rusty-orange feathers over its head, and a mixture of purple and orange fuzz on the underside of its neck and around at the front of its chest. However, the vast majority of its body is instead covered with dark-brown scaling. From the base of its tail sprout five especially large and beautiful feathers that refract rainbow colors depending on the direction that light hits them. For this reason, they are highly sought after for use as jewelry and hat decorations. Its front limbs have been modified into a pair of wings with downy membranes, while its tail ends with a heavily branched, root-like tip. It sports legs comparable in durability to iron, with strong claws able to inflict fatal injuries on its prey in a single blow. The wyvern's enormous thigh muscles support its incredible leg strength, even more so than other Bird Wyverns. Consequently, its successive flying kicks boast unimaginable speed and leaping power, and many Hunters end up confused from the contrast with its previous small and jerky movements. A notable characteristic of the Hypnocatrice lies in its ability to emit a sleep inducing breath to forcibly lull its natural enemies into a slumber. This breath is the primary reason behind hunting requests for it ending in failure, and is what granted it the nickname of Sleep Bird.
The Hypnocatrice sports a sharp and intricately hooked beak, adapted for pecking at small monsters and insects, as well as tearing apart the tough, fibrous food it prefers: evergreen shrubs, cycads, and ferns. However, due to this adaptation, its jaws are not suited for chewing. Thus, gastroliths are often found inside the Wyvern's stomach, intended to aid with digestion. Once swallowed, these gastroliths end up crystalizing, turning transparent and emitting a truly transcendent shine. The discovery of this has led some researchers to believe that other Bird Wyverns who share a similar diet to the Hypnocatrice might also utilize similar gastroliths, with them simply not having been discovered yet due to not being valuable as trading materials to hunters and thus never being able to reach the Royal Capital. However, the mere suggestion of this idea has been heavily criticized.
The lower mandible of the beak sports two outwards-facing protrusions that greatly resemble fangs. The fact they face outwards rather than inward suggests they could be used to hook large aquatic fish, such as Pin Tuna and Bomb Arowana. In fact, its beak closely resembles that of the extinct Poldor, a monster theorized to be the ancestor of the Yian Kut-Ku and Gypceros. However, in contrast to the Hypnocatrice's omnivorous diet, the Poldor was believed to be fully carnivorous. As a result of this, one hypothesis proposes the modern day Bird Wyvern may represent an evolutionary shift from a carnivorous diet to a more omnivorous one, providing living records of the Bird Leg suborder's evolutionary branching.
Behavior
The Hypnocatrice primarily roams dense forests and jungles. Despite its fearsome beak and talons, it is pacifistic and extremely timid, making liberal usage of its sleep breath in a defensive manor: should it be targeted by a potential threat, such as a pack of Velociprey, it will seek to escape the danger by instantly firing its sleep breath after a threatening display. This pacifism extends to its diet, with it rarely going out of its way to predate upon other monsters. Instead it prefers to act as a scavenger, feeding on whatever remains other monsters leave behind once they have finished.
As a result of the value and aesthetic of the Hypnocatrice's tail feathers, there have been several incidents in which youths from the city have attempted reckless hunting attempts in an effort to impress the ladies of the royal palace, only to be laughed at by experienced hunters.
Development
The behavior and ecological niche of the Hypnocatrice was inspired by vultures.

The Blue Bear Beast Invasive Arzuros (侵獣アオアシラ, Shinjū Aoashira) is a Fanged Beast introduced in Monster Hunter Stories 3: Twisted Reflection.
It is a Invasive form of the Arzuros.
Summary
A unique Arzuros Subspecies capable of dominating the territories of other monsters. Adorned in darker fur, they not only boast greater physical strength, but also intellect, allowing them to lead a pack of lesser Arzuros. Their hoards of honey not only feeds the pack, but is also used as a weapon, whether slung with great force or used to summon their kin.
Spin-Offs
Monster Hunter Stories 3: Twisted Reflection: An Invasive Arzuros is found in the Canalta Timberland, being responsible for the decline in the Canyne population that plagues Sheparden. After defeating it, Canynes can be restored to the ecosystem.
An Invasive Arzuros is found in the Canalta Timberland, being responsible for the decline in the Canyne population that plagues Sheparden. After defeating it, Canynes can be restored to the ecosystem.
Physiology
The Invasive Arzuros is a unique variation of Arzuros that largely resembles the nominate species, being differentiated by its much larger size and darker, more muted fur. It has a distinct patch of fur on its belly resembling a menacing face, while the fur, claws, and carapace on its forearms has become a rich gold in color, with stripes of this honey-colored fur also running along its back. When enraged, its eyes glow bright red.
In addition to greatly advanced physical strength that allow it to easily shatter rock with its forearms, the Invasive Arzuros is able to weaponize the honey it consumes as food and sling it with incredible force as a projectile attack. In addition, by using stored honey, it is able to command and rally other Arzuros in battle. As honey serves as the sole lifeline for the Invasive Arzuros's livelihood, it boasts an exceptional sense of smell that make it adept at finding and gathering large amounts of it.
Behavior
Like all Invasive Monsters, the Invasive Arzuros is characterized by a tendency to invade the territories of other monsters, particularly endangered ones, claiming the turf as its sole ruler. An Invasive Arzuros was once found to have dominated the territory of a local Canyne population and driven it to near-extinction.
The Invasive Arzuros is highly intelligent, hoarding honey to gather and command lesser Arzuros, and distributing it among them to strengthen their bonds and loyalty, allowing it to direct them in battle and lead them on coordinated hunts. Storing most of its stash underground for safekeeping, it will dig it up and use it as needed should its immediate supply run out. If it runs out of reserve honey during a battle, it may opt to retreat and gather more from its den to prevent its pack from falling into disarray.

The Horned Wyvern Invasive Diablos (侵獣ディアブロス, Shinjū Diaburosu) is a Flying Wyvern introduced in Monster Hunter Stories 3: Twisted Reflection.
It is a Invasive form of the Diablos.
Summary
A unique Diablos Subspecies capable of dominating the territories of other monsters. Characterized by an orange-and-black carapace and twisted, spike-studded horns, they boast enormously advanced strength and digging abilities, and prefer to spend prolonged periods underground before slaying prey in a single, decisive strike from below.
Spin-Offs
Monster Hunter Stories 3: Twisted Reflection: The Invasive Diablos can be found at the Colossal Dragon's Remains in Tarkuan. After making it retreat, a Tigrex egg can be recovered from its den.
The Invasive Diablos can be found at the Colossal Dragon's Remains in Tarkuan. After making it retreat, a Tigrex egg can be recovered from its den.
Physiology
The Invasive Diablos is a unique variation of Diablos that largely resembles the nominate species, but boasts a dark orange carapace studded with spikes, a black stripe pattern covering its entire body, and vibrant yellow eyes. Its horns are twisted and similarly studded with spikes, with their unusual shape being believed to have resulted from improper regrowth after they were damaged by pressure and rotation while burrowing. When enraged, its face will flush red and it will begin exhaling vapor.
The Invasive Diablos has much greater strength and lethality than a normal Diablos, in particular being able to burrow through the ground at exceptional speed, kicking up large dust clouds in its wake. By weaponizing the momentum it gains from its rapid digging, the Invasive Diablos is able to launch devastating ramming attacks when it breaches the surface. Its beastly roar is also louder and more powerful, able to majorly disorient foes.
Behavior
The original Diablos from which the Invasive Diablos descended once faced extinction due to poor thermoregulation, but the Invasive Diablos managed to survive by adapting to subterranean life instead. While still capable of remaining active above ground, it prefers habitats with moderate climates and protection from the elements. However, like all Invasive Monsters, the Invasive Diablos is characterized by a tendency to invade the territories of other monsters, particularly endangered ones, claiming the turf as its sole ruler. An Invasive Diablos was once found to have dominated the territory of a local Tigrex population.
The Invasive Diablos largely shares the same territorial temperament and highly physical fighting style compared to the usual one, maintaining a wide territory pockmarked with pits from its frequent burrowing and surfacing. In battle, it is known to build up momentum underground before suddenly ambushing prey from below, goring them with a single, decisive blow from its twisted horns. Because of the massive force with which it breaches the surface, it is vulnerable to being counterattacked should its foe predict where it'll surface, the shock of which can make it opt to retreat.

The Strange Wyvern Invasive Khezu (侵獣フルフル, Shinjū Furufuru) is a Flying Wyvern introduced in Monster Hunter Stories 3: Twisted Reflection.
It is a Invasive form of the Khezu.
Summary
A unique Khezu Subspecies capable of dominating the territories of other monsters. Wrapped in black-and-orange hides, unique vocal organs allow for the emission of explosively loud shrieks that strike fear into the hearts of enemies. Their vocal cords additionally fuel potent electricity generation, giving them immense electrical power to compliment their heightened intellect.
Spin-Offs
Monster Hunter Stories 3: Twisted Reflection: Invasive Khezu can be found in Serathis, in the North-Eastern corner of the Glacial Caps. Repelling it rewards a Barioth egg for habitat restoration.
Invasive Khezu can be found in Serathis, in the North-Eastern corner of the Glacial Caps. Repelling it rewards a Barioth egg for habitat restoration.
Physiology
The Invasive Khezu is a unique variation of Khezu that largely resembles the nominate species, being differentiated by its dorsal half being covered in dark grey hide, while its underbelly is instead a deep crimson. Its lips and mouth are pale blue, and its vocal tract has developed differently compared to the nominate species, with a specialized throat structure, a highly developed resonance organ, and abnormally thick vocal cords. By biting its prey, the Invasive Khezu is able to directly drain its vitality to fuel its own.
The Invasive Khezu's unique vocal physiology allows it to unleash a distinctive Death Shriek, the origin of the eponymous legend in the Glacial Caps' folklore: an explosively loud, shrill scream that elicits an instinctive fear response in listeners. The vibrations of its vocal cords during its shrieks also generate energy that stimulates its muscles and electrical organs, granting it vastly increased physical strength and electrical output compared to a normal Khezu, the latter of which also creates a magnetic field in the vicinity. By imbuing its Death Shriek with electricity, it can create an explosive burst of force and electricity to strike a wide area. However, this massive power generation also makes it consume much more energy.
Behavior
Like all Invasive Monsters, the Invasive Khezu is characterized by a tendency to invade the territories of other monsters, particularly endangered ones, claiming the turf as its sole ruler. An Invasive Khezu was once found to have dominated the territory of a local Barioth population.
The Invasive Khezu dwells in cold regions and exhibits unknown hunting behavior, though it has been known to leave desiccated corpses and shattered terrain in its wake. It is fairly intelligent, being able to learn from enemy attack patterns and develop appropriate countermeasures on the fly. As a result of its significant energy consumption, should it fail to eliminate its target even after charging and unleashing its power, it will often opt to retreat.

The Cruel Claw Wyvern Invasive Odogaron (侵獣オドガロン, Shinjū Odogaron) is a Fanged Wyvern introduced in Monster Hunter Stories 3: Twisted Reflection.
It is a Invasive form of the Odogaron.
Summary
A unique Odogaron Subspecies capable of dominating the territories of other monsters. Characterized by their black-and-green hide and tan shelling, their skin is slick with oil and fat derived from devoured carrion. Slashes from their specialized claws ignite these oils and set their claws ablaze, allowing them to simultaneously sear and gouge their prey.
Spin-Offs

The Invasive Odogaron can be found at Rococo Rocks in Tarkuan. After making it retreat, a Zinogre egg can be found in its nest.
Physiology
The Invasive Odogaron is a unique variation of Odogaron that largely resembles the nominate species, being differentiated by a black hide covered in beige-gold stripes, an enlarged series of beige dorsal spines, and rows of spines on its forearms. Instead of the bony claws of its normal counterpart, the Invasive Odogaron has metallic grey claws which boast a unique composition that renders them resistant to physical damage and heat. Its eyes are a blank, glowing orange.
The Invasive Odogaron has a unique metabolism that sequesters fat from consumed meat, then secretes it as a layer of flammable oil that covers its skin and claws, giving its hide an iridescent sheen. By striking the ground with its claws to create sparks, it is able to ignite this oil to burn enemies or set its claws ablaze, giving them even more striking power. These claws also grow back extremely quickly owing to the monster's unusually high metabolism, allowing them to recover from gradual wear or even completely regenerate in moments if broken. However, their ability to ignite can be hindered if the monster is on wet terrain such as mud.
Behavior
Like all Invasive Monsters, the Invasive Odogaron is characterized by a tendency to invade the territories of other monsters, particularly endangered ones, claiming the turf as its sole ruler. An Invasive Odogaron was once found to have dominated the territory of a local Zinogre population.
Stalking arid habitats, the Invasive Odogaron shares the same ornery disposition as the normal counterpart, with an all-consuming drive to butcher any living thing in sight. Like the nominate species, it is highly agile in battle, nimbly evading foes before tearing into them with its fangs and burning claws. As it relies heavily on its claws, however, it may retreat if the claws' ability to cut and burn are weakened.

A unique Seregios Subspecies capable of dominating the territories of other monsters. Their body is completely covered in a coat of metallic silver-blue Bladescales, which not only provide an ironclad defense, but can be shot at near-supersonic speed despite their weight, striking foes with deadly accuracy and incredible force.

The Invasive Seregios is a unique variation of Seregios that largely resembles the nominate species, being differentiated by its entire body barring its beige underbelly now being a light bluish-silver in coloration. As a slim Bird Wyvern with wingless forelegs and a large, crested head, the Iodrome closely resembles the Velocidrome. The similarities between the two are enough that the Iodrome was initially believed to be a Subspecies of the Veolcidrome, although it was later found to simply be a close relative of its. The Iodrome is the alpha individual of the Ioprey species and shares a deep-red red hide, which boasts only a sparse covering of scales. Additionally, it shares the characteristically bulbous head crest with its smaller kin, and it is believed the crest serves as a cooling organ that enables the Iodrome to thrive in its typically hot habitats. The Iodrome can be further differentiated from the Ioprey by its increased size and more elaborate head crest. Furthermore, it grows a unique secondary set of scales, called Violet Scales, that are considered quite precious. As the name suggests, these scales are violet in color, although turn black as the wyvern ages and their quality improves.
The most notable physiological feature of the Iodrome is its poison—produced in the wyvern's throat pouch, this toxic compound can be spat at prey to gradually kill it by worsening any existing wounds the target may have. While it is believed to have originally developed as a way for the Iodrome to incapacitate its insectoid prey, the toxins from this species are unusually potent and can even affect Flying Wyverns in large enough doses. The Iodrome most commonly administers this poison by spitting it at foes, however, its fangs as well contain it and allow the Iodrome to deliver the toxin through a bite. Due to its status as an alpha and its further physical development, the Iodrome produces a slightly more viscous poison than its smaller kin, thus allowing the leader's poison to persist on surfaces after it has been spat, creating highly toxic puddles that limit the movement of prey as a result. The Iodrome's poison pouch produces such high quantities of toxins that the entire body is permeated with the poison, down to each singular scale. Due to this high rate of production, the Iodrome has developed a strong resistance to all manner of toxins. Additionally, the Iodrome's constant exposure to its own poison grants it an above average pain tolerance as well as an excellent physical constitution, manifesting in its ability to shrug off physical injuries unflinchingly.
Behavior
Found primarily in subtropical zones, the Iodrome leads a pack of its smaller brethren as an alpha leader and holds a strong command over its flock, much like the Velocidrome. However, in turn, the lesser Ioprey are unsure of themselves and disperse quickly should their leader be injured. Amongst its immediate relatives, the Iodrome is considered exceptionally aggressive and angry. Moreover, while it is a carnivore and feeds upon various prey, the Iodrome prefers to hunt large insects, immobilizing them with its poison before eating them immediately after.
Super Biology Information
The Super Biology Book Series collects the thoughts and theories of real scientists that were asked to speak about monsters from the Monster Hunter series. Thus, they are inherently speculative and should be seen as such.
While examining the Velocidrome, Gendrome, Iodrome and Great Jaggi all at once, Fossil Expert Yoshitsugu Kobayashi ponders the implications of their shared physical traits. He compares their size and body builds to those of Deinonychus and observes how their slender, light bodies allow for quick movements, while the sharp claws on their limbs lend themselves to shredding prey while jumping towards it. Kobayashi also asserts that based on their muscle structure, these wyverns could have a top running speed of 50 km/h. He also notes that the four wyverns all share rows of narrow, conical teeth that display the same shape throughout the entire mouth and sit with notable gaps between them. This resembles the dentition seen in piscivorous creatures such as gharials or Spinosaurus, and might imply that these wyverns eat fish.
Kobayashi notes that the crests of Velocidrome, Gendrome and Iodrome all form through physical structures growing on the head and then extend past it. He compares them to crests found on Dilophosaurus, Monolophosaurus and Guanlong, and asserts that just as is presumed in those species, the crested wyverns likely use their crests as decorations that aid in identifying and communicating to rivals and mates. Kobayashi singles out the Great Jaggi however due to it possessing a frill, which he assumes additionally serves as temperature regulation. Despite the fact that all four species work in packs, Kobayashi asserts that social behavior does not necessarily indicate a high level of intelligence. Instead, these bird wyverns strike him as creatures that flock together out of protective instinct, since individually, they are all fairly weak. He does however propose that their ability to coordinate might imply a more sophisticated social structure than initially apparent.

Physiology
The Ioprey is a Bird Wyvern that is closely related to the Velociprey. It shares the general body plan of its relative, with a slim body, tan underbelly, and a long head, though it also shows several notable differences. For one its body is primarily covered in a glossy red hide interspersed by black markings, which is only scarcely covered in scales. Its head is much boxier and rectangular, with a characteristic bulbous head crest present at the tip. It is believed that this crest serves as a cooling organ that enables the wyvern to thrive in its typically hot habitats. It jaws contain much less teeth than those of its relatives.
While it still sports claws, they are smaller than those of its relatives. As a result, the most notable weapon of the Ioprey is its poison. Produced in the orange throat pouch located behind the wyvern's head, with the sac inflating when being used, this toxic compound can be spat at prey to gradually kill it by worsening any existing wounds the target may have. While spitting is the most common way for it to administer the poison, its fangs are additionally filled with it and thus allow it to deliver the toxin through a bite. Its poison even permeates throughout the entirety of its body to some extent, with its scales contain an especially potent concoction which irritates the skin of anyone who comes into contact with it. Additionally, its constant exposure to its own poison grants it an above average pain tolerance as well as an excellent physical constitution, with it displaying an especially strong resistance to all manner of toxins.
Behavior
Just like the Velociprey, the Ioprey also flocks together into packs led by an alpha Iodrome. Even more-so that its peers, it greatly relies on its boss' leadership, and a pack will disperse almost immediately should it witness the alpha being injured or killed. While it is a carnivore and feeds upon various prey, the Ioprey prefers to hunt large insects which its poison is particularly effective against. Upon exposure to the toxin, most insects will become immobilized almost immediately before they are devoured whole. However, this poison has proven to be unusually potent, allowing it to even affect Flying Wyverns in large enough doses, the natural enemies of the Ioprey.
Following the initial discovery that the Ioprey's poison was capable of harming powerful wyverns, such as the Rathian and Rathalos, many Hunters began requesting the creation of weapons that utilized this toxin. However, using materials from the Ioprey requires the complete removal of latent toxins by the craftsman, and there are only a few smiths who can do so reliably. In addition, if the venom in these weapons is handled incorrectly, then the hunter can easily find themselves the victim of this incredibly potent toxin.
