Physiology
The Ivory Lagiacrus is a Subspecies of the Lagiacrus that lives a primarily terrestrial lifestyle. Like the base species, the Ivory Lagiacrus is long and fairly stocky, sporting thick limbs and a paddle-shaped tail. Although its scales naturally sport a blue color, their hue lightens over time due to a quartz-like substance that adheres to their surface and results in the plating adopting a pristine white color. However, there are some areas of the body where the original blue coloration is still somewhat visible. The scales of the Ivory Lagiacrus are popular and valuable, yet only specially skilled craftsmen can work with the material.
By rapidly contracting and relaxing specialized muscles located on its back, the Ivory Lagiacrus can generate an electrical charge that is then stored in its blue dorsal spikes, referred to as Shockers. While the standard Lagiacrus utilizes the same method of generating electricity, the electrical discharges produced by the Ivory Lagiacrus are more powerful. In order to circumvent the incredibly poor conductivity of dry air, the Leviathan's body is lined with a subcutaneous tissue that retains moisture, aiding its ability to release electricity from its body. Furthermore, the quartz-like material adhered to its scales acts as an insulator and prevents the Ivory Lagiacrus from shocking itself with its powerful discharges. The monster's shell is incredibly hard as a result, making up for the lack of durability of its skin.
Despite the poor conductivity of air, the Ivory Lagiacrus is able to produce electrical discharges on land in the same way the base species can underwater. Although how exactly it achieves this is unknown, it is theorized to eject negatively-charged ions from its Shockers to charge the area around it, allowing the subsequent release of electrical energy to manifest in powerful Thunder element attacks. The horns of the Ivory Lagiacrus oddly possess numerous holes of varying sizes, believed to be for housing power storage cells similar to those found in its Shockers. Although it is incapable of discharging electricity from its horns, researchers believe the Ivory Lagiacrus may eventually evolve to be able to use its horns for the generation, storage, and discharge of electricity.
The Ivory Lagiacrus' teeth are suited for crushing the shells and thick skin of aquatic prey. Additionally, the throat is equipped with a bony flap that prevents water from entering the body when it opens its mouth underwater.
Behavior
Despite being more terrestrial than the standard Lagiacrus, the Ivory Lagiacrus is rather elusive. Very few recorded sightings exist, and most reports write of its appearance in the waters near Moga Village. As such, little is known about the Ivory Lagiacrus' behavior.
The Leviathan's diet consists of large terrestrial Herbivores, like the Aptonoth, as well as aquatic creatures. It is adept at hunting herds of prey, using its lightning breath to cut off the herd's retreat before using electrical shocks to kill the entire herd. Jaggi often loiter nearby after the Ivory Lagiacrus hunts a herd, seeking to steal any scraps.
Development
Other proposed names for the Subspecies were Ethereal and Splendent, which means shining or illustrious. Ivory was actually the first proposed name, and after the team listened to the localisation team a second time, they agreed to use "Ivory".

Physiology
While the Jade Barroth shares its general build with the common Barroth, it displays several physiological differences that differentiate it from its desert-dwelling relative. Most notable is the altered armor shell, which is now a vibrant-turquoise in color, while its underside has taken on a bright-yellow hue. Just as the shape of the Barroth's shell allows for mud to accumulate on top and between its segments, the shell of the Jade Barroth is shaped such that it can adhere clumps of snow and ice to itself for protection. The snow coating its body is then mixed with fluids it naturally produces, resulting in a suit of armor that never melts due to its sheer frigidity. Even in the absence of any visible snow armor, the Jade Barroth's shell is not entirely exposed. The carapace of this Subspecies is covered in a thin, nearly invisible layer of ice at all times, which adds to its strength and resilience.
Aside from its altered shell, the Jade Barroth can additionally be distinguished from the common Barroth by its crown, which is significantly taller in comparison. This enlarged crown is thick enough to easily shatter through solid ice. The claws of the Jade Barroth are frozen to their core and are so cold, a single scratch from one is enough to inflict others with an intensely painful frostbite. Due to having fermented inside, the meat inside of the Jade Barroth's frozen tail is considered to be a delicacy, although it must be thawed with care in order to properly prepare.
Behavior
The Jade Barroth lives exclusively in the Tundra, where it primarily feeds on the Bnahabra. When threatened, the brute Wyvern will cover itself in snow, both for protection as well as to fling large clumps of snow at enemies to freeze and slow them down. The Jade Barroth has been observed to be more agile whilst charging at enemies, as it is able to change directions mid-attack.

Physiology
The Jaggi is a small Bird Wyvern that is the male counterpart to the Jaggia and represents the younger stage of the alpha male of the species, both of which he is comparatively much more slenderly built. Save for his tan underbelly, his body's scales are primarily orange, although those along his back, hands, and face bear a purple hue. The Jaggi additionally possesses a pair of frills on each side of his head he uses for both intimidation and thermoregulation.
Behavior
While primarily carnivorous, the Jaggi prefers to feed predominantly on fish due to his small size, and he has also been known to feed upon Wyvern Eggs, with him often traveling long distances away from his pack's nest in order to secure himself food. However, after assembling a large enough pack, the Jaggi may end up bold enough to attack prey as large as the Aptonoth. The wyvern can understand and will diligently follow the commands given to him by his alpha, coming to his side when he is in trouble, or attacking on queue with his commanding howls. When it comes time to feed however, the young male Jaggi is typically the last to feed upon a meal. This is theorized to be done by the leading Great Jaggi in order to limit nutrient intake towards other males within his pack, preventing them from fully maturing into another Great Jaggi and developing into a potential rival.
While normally a territorial monster that attempts to fight off anything encroaching upon his turf, the Jaggi is deathly afraid of fire and will avoid approaching anyone who is carrying an open flame with them. In order to move about his territory more effectively, the Jaggi constructs a series of passages between his nest and the rest of his habitat, with the individuals living in the Sandy Plains even being known to convert old Altaroth anthills into their own passages.
Upon reaching a certain age, a young male Jaggi will leave his home pack to live alone. While most individuals who embark on their own are unable to fend for themselves, the few that do will fully mature into a Great Jaggi. While the exact mechanism behind this transformation is unclear, it has been speculated that the hormones that would normally transform the Jaggi into a Great Jaggi are suppressed whilst the young male inhabits a pack already possessing an alpha male, and are only expressed once the Jaggi leaves to fend for himself.

Physiology
The Jagras is a small, lithe Fanged Wyvern that may be either female or an immature male, with any mature male being the much larger Great Jagras. Its body is covered in scales, with those on its underside and upper limbs being a dark green, while those on its head, back, and lower limbs are a variable shade of yellow; two yellow stripes run below the border. This coloration makes for excellent camouflage in lush environments. The yellow scales become more vibrant as the Jagras ages, and along its spine grow several large spines tipped red in color.
The head is wedge-shaped with the exception of the upper jaw, which dips downward. The lower jaw curves up to fit the upper jaw, and most of the teeth are thin curved fangs. Biting is the Jagras' main method of attack. The nostrils are vertical slits at the tip of the nose. The eyes are midway between the front and back of the skull. The irises are gold and reflect orange light in dark spaces. The pupils are slit, and black stripes cross each eye vertically.
The throat dewlap is mostly green with a yellow rim and five yellow dots, with six thin spikes along its edge. The torso is thin and flexible, and chest and shoulder region is larger than the hips. The tail is as long as the torso and is very thin.
The Jagras has long limbs that project downwards from its body. The front legs are the same length as the back legs, with all four feet having four toes with long, orange claws; the second and third toes on each foot being longer than the first and fourth. It is an agile monster that can swiftly run, crawl, leap, and climb through the underbrush and understory of its forested habitat.
Behavior
The Jagras inhabits moist, well-vegetated habitats, such as the Ancient Forest, where it lives in a mix-gendered pack lead by an alpha male Great Jagras. Strangely, despite the Jagras being found in the Old World, no sightings of the Great Jagras have been reported outside of the New World thus far.
A Jagras pack seeks shelter in caves underneath the forest floor. Each pack consist of a single Great Jagras, 10-20 females, and an unknown number of smaller males. Like the Great Jagras, the Jagras possesses an insatiable appetite, although it lacks the boldness of its leader, with its cowardice even being striking when compared to other Fanged Wyverns. Although, if an intruding monster becomes incapacitated in some way, the Jagras will seize the opportunity to climb down from the treetops and attack it from all sides while it is down. When gathered in large numbers, it becomes more aggressive towards larger monsters. However, throwing a Scatternut can spook the Jagras away, and due to its instinctual drive to win through sheer numbers, killing one member of the pack will cause the remaining Jagras to retreat. Additionally, the Jagras can be distracted from its target by either starting a fire or by dropping Raw Meat nearby.
The Jagras mostly hunts smaller creatures when on its own, such as Shepherd Hares, however it vastly prefers to feed on the pre-digested meat regurgitated by the Great Jagras. After he has eaten, the Great Jagras will regurgitate pre-digested chunks of meat and then call for the Jagras in his pack to eat. This meat provides much more nutrients to the Jagras than its usual prey, with this food offering by Great Jagras being the main reason Jagras stay close to it. Despite this, the Jagras does not aid its leader in hunting. The large male is so gluttonous that it may eat one of its smaller pack mates, causing the smaller Jagras to flee into the treetops in order to escape from its hungry leader. The Jagras typically relies on the Great Jagras to defend its territory from intruders. It will only participate in a fight alongside its alpha if the Great Jagras becomes enraged or is severely injured.
When a male Jagras reaches a certain age he will leave his natal packs to lead a solitary life, should he survive, he will grow into a Great Jagras. During mating season, he will then return to the area he originated from and fight one of the local Great Jagras for dominance over his pack, with the winner of the battle then attempting to court with every female in the pack. A Female Jagras will lay 3-4 eggs in a warm area of mulch. Neither the male or female Jagras will protect or incubate the eggs, leaving them open to predators stealing them, such as the Kulu-Ya-Ku.
Development
Concept Art of Jagras shows several colorful Fanged Wyverns inspired by various small tropical predators. They include designs resembling felines, predatory birds, and even wasps. One of the designs has a body structure like a bird wyvern and rodent-like ears.

Its tail is thick and wide, and extending out from its small face are two enormous tusks. The rarely seen chin of the dragon is bulbous and covered in spiked bumps. On its back, the dragon has a blowhole from which it can breathe and expel sand it has ingested while swimming. The mouth and esophagus of the Jhen Mohran splits into two chambers through the use of a filter system; one side takes in food, the other the copious amounts of sand the Elder Dragon swallows, sending it to the blowhole to be expelled later.
While the Elder Dragon appears to be a dull-brown color to onlookers, the underlying scales of the Jhen Mohran are actually a bright blue. The brown coloration is created by sand and other debris sticking to the skin and solidifying.
A noteworthy feature of the Jhen Mohran is its back ridge, which is commonly covered in ore veins and mineral deposits. These deposits develop as the Elder Dragon swims through the sand sea, accumulating on its body through the force of its movement. The rarest of these materials is the Earth Dragongem, a mysterious jewel found only on the body of this behemoth.
Behavior
The Jhen Mohran only rarely surfaces, and it is assumed that it does so to breathe and expel sand through its blowhole. In doing so, it releases enormous quantities of sand into the air with tremendous force, which is believed to cause the sandstorms the Elder Dragon's emergence is generally associated with. Another omen of its appearance is the increased presence of the Delex, which follow around the surfacing Jhen Mohran to feed on organic matter that is swept to the surface by the movements of the massive Elder Dragon.
Due to the rare ores that accumulate on its back, the Jhen Mohran is regarded as a symbol of abundance, and the people who have lived in the Great Desert since ancient times call it a "Living Mine." When it appears in the sand sea, people follow its wandering path aboard Dragonships and attempt to climb onto its back to mine the precious ores. The obtained materials, seen as the bounty of nature, bring vitality and prosperity to the city of Loc Lac. They all fetch high prices, although the tusks in particular are highly prized. Sometimes, the Elder Dragon is used as a tool for city development by having it crash into bedrock.
Drawn long ago by members of the Scriveners is a sketch that was thought to be of the Jhen Mohran, although when compared to identified specimens, there are several clear distinctions. Hence, it is speculated the sketch may be of a separate individual that inhabits a specific region of the Great Desert, or perhaps instead it could be of a species with a similar evolutionary lineage to the Jhen Mohran and its Subspecies.
Super Biology Information
The Super Biology Book Series collects the thoughts and theories of real scientists that were asked to speak about monsters from the Monster Hunter series. Thus, they are inherently speculative and should be seen as such.
Marine Scientist Fumihito Muto attempts to understand the sheer magnitude of the Jhen Mohran by pondering its weight. A walrus, which has a body shape quite similar to the Jhen Mohran, reaches a maximum length of 3.5 meters and a weight of 1.5 tons. Since the weight of an organism increases in proportion to the cube of its body length, Muto estimates the weight of a Jhen Mohran by calculating what a walrus of the same size would weigh. With a body length of approximately 111 meters, a Jhen Mohran has an estimated weight of about 48,000 tons—roughly 32,000 times the weight of the largest known walrus. Considering the structural resilience of bone and muscle and their relationship to the geometric arrangement of the skeleton, Muto concludes that a walrus-like anatomy would be insufficient to support the Jhen Mohran’s massive weight. Consequently, the skeletal and muscular systems of a Jhen Mohran must be exceptionally robust. Muto additionally theorizes that the Great Desert contains extensive regions with lower gravity, which would be where the Jhen Mohran resides. It may be that a reduction in gravity, triggered by some unknown cause, led to the drying up of an ocean, resulting in the formation of this sea of ​​sand. This low-gravity environment would not only enable a creature of such immense size to swim or submerge itself within the sand, but would also facilitate the navigation of human-operated vessels and allow heavily equipped hunters to wield massive weaponry with relative ease.
Muto uses this theory as a springboard to explore a bold vision of the Monster Hunter world as a whole. He believes it is likely that gravity in this world is not constant. Muto argues that for some monsters, their very body structures would be impossible to support themselves under the same gravitational conditions as those of our own world. Furthermore, in low-gravity zones, certain behaviors, such as burrowing through sand, become possible. Low-gravity zones might be distributed like underground water veins or perhaps even like lakes. Muto also would find it conceivable that "low-gravity storms" exist. Some monsters may typically reside in low-gravity zones, occasionally venturing into areas with standard gravity. Others might inhabit low-gravity zones during their youth, only to emerge into standard-gravity regions upon reaching maturity. Muto even believes that some species may have undergone a secondary adaptation, transitioning from low-gravity land environments to the oceans of standard-gravity regions. While human life would primarily take place in standard-gravity zones, settlements located near the boundaries might be particularly vulnerable to attack. In low-gravity zones, human physical capabilities would likely be enhanced. Moreover, by training in high-gravity zones—which may exist somewhere in this world—it could be possible to achieve superhuman feats.
The next topic of Muto’s analysis is the Jhen Mohran’s feeding habits. He proposes that the Jhen Mohran likely hosts symbiotic bacteria capable of deriving energy from iron and other minerals. Beneath the shifting sands of the desert, there exists a layer of rocky substrate; mineral-rich springs periodically emerge from this layer. Sensing these, the Jhen Mohran appear and use their tusks to excavate and ingest the mixture of mineral-laden water and rocky debris. Within the creature’s body, a filtration system separates the rocky material, which is subsequently excreted in a form resembling conglomerate rock. The ingested, sediment-rich water contains organic matter from ancient oceans, various minerals, and dormant bacteria. Furthermore, Muto asserts that a constant population of bacteria may reside within the Jhen Mohran’s digestive tract. These bacteria proliferate rapidly in the favorable environment provided by the creature’s body, serving as a vital source of nutrition. In the process, specific compounds are extracted within the digestive tract and are eventually excreted as ore.
Muto then argues that the Jhen Mohran might be a migratory species. Creatures such as whales, tuna, and sea turtles undertake large migrations, returning to their original locations at regular intervals. The appearances of Jhen Mohran might be explained by such migratory behavior. Muto ponders that these could be foraging migrations timed with seasonal upwellings, or migrations for the purpose of reproduction. In tandem with the species’ movements, Muto concludes his analysis by considering the sustainability of hunters and their pursuit of the Jhen Mohran. The ore harvested from a Jhen Mohran can be considered a "self-renewing resource", as it replenishes itself if left to its own. It is preferable to extract it without harming the monster. While capturing a Jhen Mohran might be feasible, doing so would likely be detrimental; given that a single individual requires a vast expanse to survive, its loss would deal a severe blow to the local ecosystem. Should one nonetheless attempt a capture, a method akin to the net-based whaling practiced during Japan’s Edo period—where whales were driven into nets—would likely be the most efficient approach.

Physiology
The Jin Dahaad is a gargantuan cold-dwelling Leviathan covered in a gnarled gray hide and a carapace whose metallic properties make it highly resistant to freezing; this tough-as-steel armor does not impede its movement in the slightest. Metallic bony ridges resembling copper, called Iceplates, line the majority of its body, with a large crest of these Iceplates adorning its head, which is fairly flat in shape and has a tripartite jaw structure that folds outwards when the monster opens its mouth. Although mostly concealed by the ridges on its head, the Jin Dahaad has a pair of beady black eyes, each surrounded by three smaller eyes for a total of eight. Its teeth are pointed and relatively small, with the fangs on its outer jaw being larger than the rest.
It has a set of massive Iceplates protruding from its back, a row of smaller Iceplates running along its spine, and a protruding ribbed chest structure terminating in several bony spikes. Each of its arms has smaller Iceplates running along the forelimb, five large metallic claws that freeze anything they touch, and a spike in the palm position that digs into terrain while the Jin Dahaad is climbing, with its limbs also shedding clouds of vapor while idle. The Jin Dahaad's tail is long and slender, with more Iceplates at its base and tip, along with flat spines running along its length and a bifurcated rake-like structure at its end. The larger Iceplates on its head, back, abdomen, and tail can fold in and out, most often seen when the Jin Dahaad fans out the Iceplates after using its ice attacks, or oscillates them when agitated.
The metallic spikes on its claws, chest, and tail have extreme heat-absorbent properties, to the point where its extremities continue to chill the surroundings even once separated from the monster. Using these, the Jin Dahaad is able to absorb massive amounts of heat from the surrounding air and anything else in contact with it, which is then transferred to the Iceplates lining its body; the layered organs serve as heat sinks that store heat and rapidly dissipate it into the air above. This process allows the Jin Dahaad to drastically lower the temperature of its surroundings, with heightened activity even being able to cause locale-wide freezing. The amount of heat shunted to the Iceplates causes them to glow incandescently and emit vapor when the Jin Dahaad is using its abilities; in spite of this, the Iceplates are never seen melting or deforming, although the larger sets are noticeably tinted teal in a manner akin to oxidation or rusting.
By using its cooling abilities and internal Freezer Sac, the Jin Dahaad produces and expels massive amounts of supercooled vapor and frost from its mouth and various vents along its body—notably its chest, lower body, tail, and claws—allowing it to instantly freeze its surroundings. This additionally allows it to freeze its limbs to surfaces on contact, acting as a form of adhesion that helps it freely climb on uneven terrain and walls despite its enormous size and weight. Should the Iceplates be damaged, the Jin Dahaad's ability to vent heat and subsequently chill its surroundings will weaken accordingly, particularly if the largest one on its back is broken. The hide around the Jin Dahaad's largest set of ridges is extremely tough and renders it near invulnerable to attacks, but softens if all the other large Iceplates are broken.
Behavior
The Jin Dahaad is highly territorial and does not take kindly to intruders in its turf, pursuing them relentlessly the moment it detects them. Once angered, it is tenacious to the point that even severe injury is not enough to deter it from hunting down the offenders, with foes that damage its Iceplates in particular drawing its ire. When engaging a target in combat, the Jin Dahaad will oscillate and rattle the Iceplates on its head and back in a gesture akin to intimidation.
The Jin Dahaad inhabits mountainous cold locales, such as the Rimechain Peak overlooking the Iceshard Cliffs, where it reigns as the region's apex predator and descends to the Cliffs during the Frostwinds, the region's Inclemency period. However, it has never been observed feeding or predating, merely perching on steep cliffsides and attacking any who draw near with its ice breath, and retreating back to the Rimechain Peak should a foe manage to fight back against it for long enough.

"The Lord of Ice" is Jin Dahaad's theme and consists of three individual phase themes, with the suffixes "Scowl", "Resolute" and "Judgment" for each corresponding phase. Unlike the rest of Wilds ' apex monster themes, which all follow a 3/4 time signature, "The Lord of Ice" follows a rare 5/4 time signature. Interestingly, all 3 tracks lack pianos, an instrument that was used for the Iceshard Cliff's theme " Shadows Dancing on Ice ".

Physiology
The Jyuratodus is a lobe-finned Piscine Wyvern with a stocky build. Its true emerald-green color becomes washed out with exposure to its environment, with its scales instead adopting an element of brownish-gray, but this loss of color from saturation in the muck only serves to toughen their scales. The muddy layer caking these scales keeps them moist to facilitate cutaneous respiration, the process that allows the Jyuratodus to breathe underwater despite the absence of gills. Should the scales go uncared for and dry out, they will become brittle and weak. Additionally, the carapace—most prominently located on the head and neck—is toughened by prolonged exposure to mud and boasts great defense.
The aforementioned lobe-fins along the Jyuratodus' body are flexible, with the pectoral fins accompanied by large rigid barbs allowing for its trademark effortless traversal of the otherwise challenging mires it inhabits. They additionally assist the Jyuratodus' clumsy walking, as it turns and adjusts them while walking on land, aiding it as it moves over the uneven ground. Two rows of teeth compliment the Jyuratodus' strong, bone-cleaving bite; these teeth are used in holding prey down until they drown in mud. Once it claims a victim, the Jyuratodus has been found to prefer feeding on the internal organs of its prey, which it can occasionally be seen caching under the benthos.
The mud armor protecting the Jyruatodus' head ends in a horn-like protrusion acting much like a protective visor, allowing only its pale eyes and mouth to peak through. Furthermore, the mud armor sees use in marking territory; the Jyuratodus litters its range's water and rocks with sticky mud to signal its presence to competitors, who it directly confronts by kicking up mud. The traversal habits of the Barroth often leads to it destroying these territorial indicators, which often instigates battles between it and the Jyuratodus should the two cross paths. Due to their similar strength and natural abilities, the two are regarded as fierce rivals by many.
Being the most basal Piscine Wyvern currently known, the Jyuratodus' discovery has led to much discussion amongst researchers regarding its evolutionary history with its close relative, the Lavasioth. Most importantly, however, its discovery could help in uncovering the ancestor of all Piscine Wyverns.
Behavior
The Jyuratodus prefers to spend most of its life hidden away in its marsh, although demonstrate a high level of territoriality towards any intruders who would disturb its otherwise peaceful existence. To reduce the frequency of such intrusions, the Jyuratodus marks its territory with sticky mud. Although Hunters are no exceptions to its territorial demonstrations should they linger at close range, the Jyuratodus is comparatively slower to notice them wading through its waters. On the rare occasion the Jyuratodus ventures outside its territorial perimeter, it seeks out the Apceros as its prey of choice, biting through their tough shells before returning to the peace and quiet of its marsh. In the Flooded Forest, it has been sighted preying on the Slagtoth, drowning them beneath the muck and caching them for later consumption. The Jyuratodus is known to eat rather infrequently, having been observed only eating a maximum of once a day in the Wildspire Waste.
During the rainy season, the Jyuratodus will congregate in large numbers with others of its kind in marshlands; upon doing so, any female Jyuratodus will release unfertilized eggs, and the male Jyruatodus will respond by releasing their gametes in the vicinity to attempt fertilization. This reproductive ritual creates a novel scene by making the surface of the marsh appear as if it were undulating, however, it has not been recorded in recent years due to occurring only during particularly turbulent rainy seasons and is thus considered a rarity. Although many fertilized eggs successfully hatch, only a small quantity of hatchlings will survive to maturity due to predation as well as cannibalism from each other. The Jyruatodus is carnivorous in nature and displays such behavior at a young age, showcased by its unique feeding behavior. It seeks to enter the body of its target through its orifices or any open wounds and will proceed to eat its prey from the inside. The sharp spines lining the adult Jyuratodus' gills are believed to be a remnant from its juvenile form, the barbs preventing the young Piscene Wyvern to be expelled from the body.

Physiology
The Kecha Wacha is a medium-sized Fanged Beast covered in a coat of soft fur sporting an autumnal coloration, with an orange coating along its back towards its tail and on the lower parts of its limbs, the color darkening towards the top of its back and tip of its tail. This is mixed with a golden coat along its lower body and upper limb areas. Although soft, the Kecha Wacha's fur remains surprisingly durable, and its warm, vibrant colors result in fabrics woven from it to be quite popular, particularly amongst travelers. In contrast, its underbelly, hands, feet, and face are hairless, covered in a gray almost scaly skin.
Due to its habit of spending the majority of its life in the tree tops, the Kecha Wacha's toes have evolved to be long so as to make it easier to grip branches. Additionally, the Kecha Wacha possesses a trio of elongated and uniquely hooked claws at the end of each forelimb that are specially evolved to allow the Fanged Beast to easily climb and hang from the various vine and ivy canopies found throughout its environment, though these claws may also serve as formidable weapons when combating other threats. While they appear lean, the Kecha Wacha's forelimbs contain powerful muscles, allowing it to effortlessly swing between branches as well as hang from canopies for extended periods of time. Moreover, this enhanced musculature allows it to deliver swift and powerful strikes with its talons—even seasoned Hunters may not emerge unscathed when faced against these dangerous strikes. Its forelimbs' strength is even further reinforced through its bones, which in spite of being slender, boast considerable durability and density.
The tail of the Kecha Wacha is prehensile in nature, granting it the ability to hang upside down whilst keeping its forelimbs free to perform other actions, letting it move swiftly through the canopy. Much like the rest on its body, the tail's vibrant fur is wonderfully soft to the touch, and along its underside can be found several curved, claw-like protrusions, which further aid the Kecha Wacha in keeping its grip whilst hanging, permitting the tail to effectively serve as a third arm capable of supporting its weight. The Kecha Wacha also possesses a similarly prehensile trunk formed from the beast's nose, and when combined with the Aqua Sacs found inside its body, allows it to expel a viscous mucus at targets across vast distances, greatly restraining and hindering the movement of anything it comes into contact with.
Potentially the Kecha Wacha's most characteristic feature are its massive pair of ears. The inner ear is lined with 3 sets of spikes, while the outsides are orange and intricately patterned with orange-and-yellow ocellate markings closely resemble menacing eyes, with the spikes now resembling tusks. The exact patterning of these eye-spots is known to vary between individuals depending on both their age and the habitat in which thet live in. These ears filter out necessary background noise, bestowing the Kecha Wacha with an incredible sense of hearing, allowing it to easily detect whenever any potential prey or predator intrudes upon its territory. Unfortunately, this remarkable hearing notably grants the Kecha Wacha an exploitable weakness to loud noises, with abrupt sounds often startling it to the point it falls out of the canopy it was occupying. To counteract this, its ears are fairly mobile, allowing the Kecha Wacha to fold them over its own face as a means of protection. Typically done when angered, this motion serves to intimidate opponents through the face-like design, whilst simultaneously providing the Kecha Wacha protection against its aversion to sudden loud noises as well as to bright flashes of light.
Attached to its forelegs is a thin, stretchy membrane that enhances the Kecha Wacha's mobility by granting it the ability to glide through the air. The Kecha Wacha primarily makes use of this membrane by gliding to distant branches, as well as to maneuver around opponents and attack from creative angles. Furthermore, by repeatedly flapping its arms while the membrane is extended, the Kecha Wacha is able to briefly take off from the ground and gain height, allowing it to glide long distances. Whilst the Kecha Wacha displays exceptional traversal abilities in arboreal environments, its body is ill-suited for land-based movement.
Behavior
The Kecha Wacha primarily inhabits the canopies of dense woodlands in warm and humid regions, using all of its limbs—including its tail and gliding membrane—to skillfully maneuver throughout the tree-tops. Its diet mostly consists of Neopterons, with the Altaroth being an often sought after prey item in particular. Generally, the Kecha Wacha will fire the mucus stored within its trunk to immobilize its prey, which it will then capture with its claws and devour. Other times, however, the Kecha Wacha will hang from above with one of its claws while using the other to pry into the Altaroth's nest, plucking out and feasting on individuals one after another.
The Kecha Wacha is awfully curious by nature and recurringly comes into conflict with humans as a result, oftentimes by attacking and raiding the carts of traveling merchants. While the Kecha Wacha most commonly folds it ears over its face when angered as an act of intimidation or to defend itself from outside stimuli, this is not the sole usage for this behavior, as it is also a major part of its courtship ritual. During the breeding season when a male Kecha Wacha encounters and seeks to impress a female, he will repeatedly open and close his ears in rapid succession while facing her. As the female observes the display, she will pay close attention to the patterns of the male's ears, and will mate with the male who's patterns she favors, with her typically preferring males with larger patterning.
Super Biology Information
The Super Biology Book Series collects the thoughts and theories of real scientists that were asked to speak about monsters from the Monster Hunter series. Thus, they are inherently speculative and should be seen as such.
Zoological Author Yuumin Mori observes that the Kecha Wacha combines features and traits seen in many different animals. The ears, eyes and nose bear similarities to those seen in lemurs, while the Kecha Wacha’s highly flexible shoulders and ability to cross branches with its long arms resemble similar traits displayed by gibbons. Additionally, despite the Kecha Wacha possessing a tail, its high intelligence seems reminiscent of various ape species. The presence of long claws in an arboreal species also reminds Mori of sloths, while the flight membrane is a characteristic most associated with flying squirrels. Finally, the elongated upper lip resembles those seen in tapirs. Mori notes that on the evolutionary tree of the Monster Hunter series, Kecha Wacha is classified in its own independent suborder, Flying Membrane Beast. This likely indicates that this monster went through an extremely unique evolutionary path, which might explain its chimeric features. Mori observes that the large reflective eyes specifically resemble those of ring-tailed lemurs. Many lemurs are diurnal, but their eyes are thought to be remnants of nocturnal ancestors. Mori thus wonders if the Kecha Wacha may have at one point also been nocturnal.
Furthermore, Mori asserts that the Kecha Wacha is too large to be fully arboreal, as the kind of thick branches and trees that could support its weight would be extremely rare. Thus, Mori proposes that this species originally developed as a small, arboreal creature that gradually grew in size while developing advanced intelligence. Eventually, its weight forced the Kecha Wacha onto the ground, but its highly specialized long claws prevented it from fully adapting to terrestrial life. Thus, the species settled into a partially arboreal, partially terrestrial niche, wherein the Kecha Wacha sometimes traverses the ground by taking on a knuckle gait. This precarious in-between state was likely only successful due to the Kecha Wacha’s advanced feeding strategies, such as using its claws to access insect nests.
Mori concludes his analysis by giving advice on how to survive an encounter with a Kecha Wacha. Due to the beast’s size, most of its movements are likely to be deceptively simple - it swings across branches in a predictable rhythm and its flying membrane only allows for straightforward gliding without any special maneuvers. However, a single strike by the claws is almost definitely fatal, and the speed at which the Kecha Wacha can deliver such a blow is certainly quite dangerous. Mori proposes that when encountering a Kecha Wacha on the ground, the soundest strategy would be to try and circle around it, as its large body and awkward stance would make it difficult for the creature to turn its body quickly. But should one encounter a Kecha Wacha in the trees, one might have no recourse but to “pray to god”.

Physiology
The Kelbi is a small Herbivore that sports a highly gracile frame with thin hoofed legs, a spotted fur coat, and a pair of horns atop its head pointing skyward. While both the male and female Kelbi share a generally similar appearance, the two each display a strong degree of sexual dimorphism between one another. The male Kelbi sports yellowish fur on his underbelly, a moss-green coat on his back, a slender pair of ears which stick out horizontally from his head, and a large pair of sharply pointed, two-pronged horns. By contrast, the female Kelbi sports a white underbelly, a bluish coating on her back, a broad pair of ears which droop downwards, and smaller horns ending in blunt tips.
On rare occasion, often during the monster's breeding season, rare male Kelbi sporting an exceptionally large pair of horns have been documented.
Behavior
The Kelbi typically lives within dense forests, although it has also been sighted in a wide variety of other habitats, such as deserts and mountains. It primarily feeds upon grass, and it is not uncommon to see a mated pair grazing together. These pairs are known to display strong mating bonds, with their courtship displays typically consisting of them rubbing their necks together. Contrary to the behavior observed in other Herbivores, the Kelbi is almost always observed in monogamous couples, with polygamous family structures being exceedingly rare. Although as is the case with many Herbivores, it is very timid in nature will utilize its agility to nimbly leap away and escape upon spotting a predator. However, in certain circumstances, the male Kelbi might instead stay behind and use his larger horns to fight off threats in order to protect his mate.
Alongside being hunted by humans for its liver, which is especially popular due to its juicy texture, the Kelbi is highly sought after for the medicinal properties of its horns, which are used in wide variety of regions as a key ingredient in a so-called "Cure-all medicine." This can range from them being crushed up into an infused powder, which is then used as a cure for stomach aches, to them serving as the primary ingredient in Ancient Potions, arguably the strongest healing tool in a Hunter's arsenal. While the Kelbi can be killed in order to harvest items off of it, recent modern day research instead recommends hunter's to simply stun the monster, allowing for the horns to be easily severed while the Kelbi is still alive. Once the horns have been harvested, the Kelbi will typically regenerate a new pair in roughly a year's time.

Physiology
The Kestodon is a small Herbivore with an armored head that shares a similar body plan to the Banbaro due to its taxonomic relation to it and another herbivorous Brute Wyvern. The Kestodon is a sexually dimorphic species: the male Kestodon is larger and colored a rusty-red, while the female Kestodon is smaller and sports a sandy-brown hue, both have a pale blue underbelly.
The most distinctive feature of the Kestodon is its armored head, which is also dimorphic between male and female individuals. Both sexes have a thick, dark-gray, domed scalp, with the male additionally possessing three rock-like armor plates behind the dome, the largest being the one furthest back. The plates collide against each other when the wyvern shakes its head. The female Kestodon's dome and head plates are much smaller and curve down. The armor crowning the Herbivore's head is so tough that most weapons bounce off it, the crown's hardness allowing the wyvern to use its head as an effective bludgeoning weapon. The Kestodon's face is covered by pale, blue skin and sports a short beak from the front used to bite off vegetation; behind the beak are molars that grind up vegetation.
The arms are small, whereas the legs are larger and more muscular by contrast. The knees are protected by armor plates, while the remaining leg covered by larger gray scales. Along its back are three rows of brown osteoderms that end on the tail, which itself ends in a small club.
Behavior
Although the Kestodon predominantly lives in deserts, such as the Wildspire Waste and Sandy Plains, it has been known to settle in new habitats if the ecosystem becomes unbalanced. As was the case when the Kestodon began to appear in the neighboring Ancient Forest due to the influence of the Zorah Magdaros arriving in the New World. The Kestodon travels in groups of three, consisting of one male and two females, although two groups may stick close to each other for a total of six.
The male Kestodon is usually seen resting, while the female alternates between resting and keeping watch for threats. The female Kestodon is quick to spot potential predators and when she spots a similarly sized creature, like a Hunter, she will roar at it to attract the male's attention; the male will then charge at the intruder with his hard skull to protect the herd. If a much larger monster approaches, the whole herd will huddle together at a distance. The Kestodon will charge into the trunks of trees, causing fruits and nuts to fall to the ground for consumption. Despite the hardiness of its skull, the Kestodon may knock itself out from the impact of a headbutt in rare occurrences.
Development
The book Monster Hunter World: The Official Complete Works displays concept art of all of the new monsters in Monster Hunter: World, a few being early designs of the Kestodon. All of the designs have a simple body similar to the dinosaur genus Pachycephalosaurus (one example concept being identical to the real dinosaur) with a unique head crest. In some concepts, the crest is specialized to produce sound in some way, such as the armor-plate clacking seen in the final design or a hole that produces a flute-like sound when the monster waves its head. One piece of art shows two Kestodon antagonizing each other with the "klaks" of their head plates.

Physiology
The Khezu is a unique pale Flying Wyvern characterized by its translucent, mucus-covered hide in place of a traditional covering of its, which has lost all pigmentation due to its choice in habitat. This hide is both highly elastic and very sensitive to heat, and allows it to breath through it whilst still repelling moisture. Underneath its skin, pulsing blue and red veins are plastered from head to toe, with prominent arteries outlined in its chest; its blood vessels pulsate even faster when the wyvern is enraged, growing more red and visible. Its wings possess short nails and are used to climb walls and ceilings, as well as to fly short distances. The Khezu notably lacks talons, instead sporting webbed feet with suction pad-like toes, and its stubby, yet surprisingly hard tail ends in an extra orifice that—similarly to the mouth—is lined with smaller teeth. This rear orifice can open up and "bite" onto the floor, which it uses to hang from the ceilings of caves and to ground itself whilst using its electricity.
Eerily, the Khezu's eyes have completely degenerated due to its cavernous lifestyle, and it lacks any visible ears or nostrils, equipped only with a single large mouth marked with large light-red lips. When open, it reveals several unruly rows of triangular teeth that aid it in sucking out the flesh and blood from its prey. From its mouth, it can drool an acidic saliva that helps both with digestion and fending off opponents. The Khezu's neck is rubbery and elastic, able to reach and stretch twice its body length in distance. It is able to do this by virtue of most of its neck vertebrae being made of cartilage, as well as due to its powerful muscles, loose skin, malleable organs, and flexible blood vessels, all of which are fairly long. As it grows older however, its neck muscles weaken and its head begins to droop. Overtime this can leave its neck too weak to catch prey, leaving it unable to sustain itself and causing it to eventually die.
How exactly the Khezu perceives its surrounding is still something that is deeply contested. When researching the wyvern, Scriviners noted that despite having a fresh Kelbi corpse near it, the wyvern instead chose to target and eat a silent rodent nearby. This prompted curiosity on whether it relied on an additional sense to go after prey instead of merely sight or hearing. Some proposed theories include it utilizing a form of electroreception using the electricity its body generates, or by detecting its prey's body heat. Many Hunters have reported seeing it frequently sniffing its surroundings, which led to the prevailing theory that it possesses a highly-developed sense of smell which it uses to hunt. Despite this, observations from researchers have showcased it has the ability to detect silent and odorless objects. Currently, there has yet to be any captured specimen possessing any additional organs that would fully explain its ability to detect its surroundings.
Residing inside the body of the pale wyvern are multiple Thunder Sacs that grant it the ability to generate electricity, which it can discharge from its body or spit as electrical projectiles, which it can use to paralyze its prey for an easy meal. This ability is greatly benefited from its choice in habitat, with the water in the caves it inhabits expanding the range and power of these electrical attacks. Its flabby hide acts as an electrical insulation, protecting the wyvern's internals from its own electricity.
Life Cycle
Due to its hermaphroditic nature, the Khezu produces both male and female gametes, and can reproduce asexually as a result. To reproduce, the Khezu will find a suitable host—typically a large Herbivore, such as the Popo —and paralyze it using its electric spit, it will then inject its eggs into the still alive victim's body to gestate, before letting it escape. If the creature is larger in stature—such as a wyvern—a larger quantity of fertilized eggs will be inserted into the body. These eggs will eventually hatch into larvae known as Khezu Whelps and will proceed to feast on the internal organs of their host's body over a period of time. After having eaten all they possibly can from their host and upon reaching a sufficiently large enough size, these parasites will burst through the body and emerge as a juvenile Khezu, killing the host in the process. When young, the Khezu inhabits damp places and will prey on smaller creatures, like the Kelbi. Lacking wings or legs, the juvenile Khezu resembles a worm and will undergo a metamorphosis as it transforms into its more recognizable adult form.
Behavior
The Khezu prefers to inhabit dark, damp, and chilly environments, such as caves. During the warmer seasons, it spends most of its time in frigid environments due to their cool climate, however when the cold season approaches, most individuals will move into more swampy environments to escape the heavy snowfalls the previous areas experience. While it primarily spends its time moving from one cavern to the next, it is still able to be found outside of caves on rare occasions. The Khezu is an ambush predator, preferring to lie in wait on the ceiling of a cave near its entrance or an underground body of water for unsuspecting prey to enter its domain. Once prey is within sight, it will extend its neck down slowly before engulfing the target within its maw and devouring them entirely. This strategy has proved far more efficient then chasing down its prey in the dark, especially due to it possessing notably sluggish movements once it has descended to the ground—a byproduct of it rarely moving around normally. It prefers to feed upon living prey, avoiding eating already dead meat if it must.
As it is typically found in highly secluded areas, the Khezu appears to be unappealing prey for most predators. Even if were to be eaten, its meat primarily consists of lipids, leaving it a poor target for predation. Despites this, it may still end up becoming the prey of certain larger monsters, such as the Shrouded Nerscylla, which specializes in preying upon the Khezu and draping itself in its hide after eating the unfortunate wyvern.
In spite of wariness in how they'd taste, Khezu Whelps can be made into a full-baby ice cream and are further theorized to taste solidly delicious when deep-fried. Meanwhile, cuts of lean meat from the matured Khezu are considered gross, regardless of their extremely high quality. Similarly, its fatty meat is ill-advised to be eaten despite its tasty appearance. The Khezu’s fangs are popular amongst fans of the occult and are frequently sold through the black market as cursed items, they are even known to be used in certain rituals as a result.
Music
Khezu and its relatives are notable to be the only monsters that plays no theme during the fight, with not even the area theme accompanying it. In spite of this, both monsters ended up being "options" for the 20th Anniversary Hunter's Choice Best Monster Theme, and their sample audios included the monster's roar at the end. Selecting them as options would prompt you to pick another as they cannot be voted.
Monster Hunter
Khezu was created by Norio Hirose. Originally, the monster was designed to dwell in rivers and swamplands, hiding underwater, waiting for prey to approach. This prototype Khezu would ambush players while they were fishing, and would also attack by throwing lampreys, leeches and its own offspring at them.
Due to the monster's somewhat phallic appearance, Sound Designer Takeshi Kitamura originally gave all of the sound files associated with Khezu joke names pertaining to that quality. However, following the recruitment of female staff members after the release of Monster Hunter, Kitamura changed the names to be less vulgar out of respect for his new co-workers.

Physiology
The Kirin is a uniquely shaped, equine Elder Dragon, the smallest member of the class yet discovered. It is covered in sky-blue scales that are patterned with stripes in a darker shade across its flank and legs. Along the beast's neck and at the back of its angle grows a silver, almost ethereal mane, able to maintain its dignified beauty even after being cut from the dragon. Its tail is short and sports white fluffy fur, with the latent electricity stored within it causing it to give off a slight glimmer. The legs of the Kirin are adapted to allow it to easily leap off the ground with a surprising amount of force, with its hooves being the ideal shape for mountainous traversal. It is even able to easily clear obstacles several times its own height as if it were simply running across flat terrain. This is believed to only be possible due to the fine control the dragon exerts over the electricity impulses sent to stimulate its muscles.
After samples of the Kirin's luscious mane were brought back to researchers, it was discovered that it functioned as a store for electricity, with the material itself being highly conductive. It functions similar to the Thunder Sacs found within other monsters, albeit to a higher degree. Storing this amount of electricity within its fur causes its body to be shrouded in a cloak of electricity, constantly emitting a faint blue light. Even once the Kirin has died, its hide retains the electricity that has been imbued inside it, making successfully harvesting materials from the beast especially difficult.
Arguably the most prominent feature of the Kirin is the spiraling azure horn atop its head, said to give off a divine light and contain the charge of a thousand lightning bolts. While its sharpened tip already makes it an effective weapon, its true power lies in its believed role in the Kirin's most infamous ability: the power to directly manipulate the striking of lightning. Unlike most wyverns, which can merely generate and shoot electricity, this dragon is fully capable of controlling the trajectory of lightning strikes to target its victims. The horn is believed to be the source of these lightning bolts as, when it is preparing to cast down a particular strong bolt, excessive electricity will begin to gather around it. Before a summoned lightning bolt strikes the ground, it will begin to light up in a brilliant blue. This occurs as a result of the minerals in the earth reacting to the increased amount of static electricity present. Strength alone is not enough to save someone from these strikes, which are capable of traveling at blistering speeds.
In addition to striking opponents, it has also been sighted striking itself with its own lightning. While the exact reasoning for this behavior is still being debated, several hypothesis have been proposed that suggest it may be healing its own wounds, or promoting its own metabolism. Following the behavior, it has been observed that due to the increased energy flowing through its body, its muscles begin to significantly harden and render anything less than high-class weaponry incapable of harming it. Within specific regions, the Kirin has been observed performing a novel electrical technique that has it summon lightning parallel to the ground in a grid-like pattern, allowing it to cover a far greater amount of ground than usual. While it has been hypothesized that the weather conditions in places such as the New World is what makes this phenomenon possible, it is also plausible that the ability is a result of the Kirin adapting to a new environment. Furthermore, some reports assert the Elder Dragon to be capable of both appearing and vanishing with the flash of a thunder bolt.
Behavior
Whenever the Kirin appears, even if the weather was previously perfectly sunny, the sky begins to rumble and dark clouds begin to appear within mere moments, casting the area into a stormy gloom. While many are sceptical of the claims that it directly causes these changes in weather, with some believing it merely follows such storms, the fact that numerous legends speak of villages that had provoked the Kirin's wrath being destroyed in devastating thunderstorms leads many others to believe the Elder Dragon possesses a deep connection with the storms. To this day, the evolutionary lineage which the Kirin belongs to remains a complete mystery. While it superficially resembles the Kelbi at a glance, the structure of its limbs as well as its temperament—which is exceedingly aggressive towards humans —are a near complete opposite. While many people disagree with its classification as an Elder Dragon, it is for the above listed reasons that the Kirin is currently classified as one. with it being able to effect the environment around itself akin to a "natural disaster" at a degree comparable in danger to its larger peers.
In the Old World, the Kirin has been seen in a variety of environments, including temperate swamps and dry volcanoes, although it seems that its preference is towards polar or mountainous environments. Unlike most Elder Dragons of the New World, which mainly reside in close proximity to the energy rich caverns sprouting from the Everstream, the Kirin primarily resides within the Coral Highlands. However, the Research Commission has theorized the beast may reside in a secret location that has yet to be uncovered. Additionally, it has been sighted wandering especially close to Commission enclaves, which is believed to be in direct response to the Zorah Magdaros' crossing and the subsequent shifting of the flow of bioenergy. Actual sightings of it are exceedingly rare, with many going their entire lives without ever seeing one, granting it the nickname of Phantom Beast.
While its exact diet remains a mystery, the Kirin is believed to be herbivorous based on the shape of its teeth. Within higher plateaus, it has additionally been observed drinking water droplets from the surface of plants, shedding some of its mane in the process. It has yet to be witnessed drinking from any significant large bodies of water, thus it is tentatively assumed that it is capable of generating electricity by breaking down these small droplets of water.
Despite its regal demeanor, the Kirin is still an aggressive Elder Dragon that will enter an electrically-fueled rage when something is foolish enough to anger it. As a result of this, smaller denizens of the environments it inhabits are known to scatter as soon as they catch wind of a Kirin being present. However, in spite of this and its status as an Elder Dragon, the Kirin still finds itself prey to the Fanged Beast, Rajang. The Rajang primarily feeds on the Kirin's horn, which it will forcefully snap off the dragon's head before crunching it apart in its mouth. This behavior is considered a rite of passage for the Rajang to become an adult and for it to truly manifest its transformation into its Battle Spirit State. As a result, it is known to appear in various places in search of Kirin to hunt. Should the Elder Dragon survive such an encounter, it will be left in an abnormal unending state of rage.
Development
Kirin was conceptualized as a design that would create a strong sense of surprise and contrast within the world of the original Monster Hunter. Since the rest of the first game featured fairly grounded environments, visuals and creatures, an outright fantastical design like the Kirin would stand out much more than it would have in a more magical fantasy game.
For Monster Hunter World, the development team knew from the start that they wanted their Elder Dragons from the Elder's Recess to appear in regions outside it. With Teostra in the Wildspire Waste, Kushala Daora in the Ancient Forest, and Vaal Hazak in the Rotten Vale, that left the Coral Highlands, so Yuya Tokuda thought about what kind of Elder Dragon would live there. They decided on Kirin mainly because they wanted to add some balance and attribute changes, but also because Kirin armor and equipment has been really popular with players, so they wanted to see how it would look like with World 's high-end graphics.
The reason why Kirin is the only Elder Dragon the player can attempt from Low Rank in World is because Kaname Fujioka wanted players to go along with the theme of a research commission carrying out capture investigations. Kirin was their way of rewarding diligent players who took a break from the path of the main story to round up some monsters, so if Kirin is successfully slain with proper equipment, they would have a much easier time dealing with the Tempered Kirin quest, Thunderous Rumble in the Highlands, required to raise their Hunter Rank.
For Iceborne, Fujioka and the team wanted to try and properly depict its relationship with Rajang, which had been conceptualized from the beginning in Monster Hunter 2 and was vaguely hinted at in the Monster Hunter Festa '13 Official Pamphlet. The idea for this relationship originated from Tokuda asking Fujioka if he could feed Rajang Kirin horns in the pet system for Dos.

The Shield Bug Konchu (クンチュウ, Kunchū) is a small Neopteron introduced in Monster Hunter 4.
Summary
Small Neopterons covered in thick carapaces along their back whose color varies with the environment. Their shells provide a nearly impenetrable defense, however if knocked onto their backs, their soft underbelly is left exposed for striking. Konchu will roll into balls both for protection and to offensively roll forward, leading them to be quite the nuisance for Hunters. They have even been known to cling onto the hides of larger monsters, temporarily protecting their hosts from harm.

Physiology
Commonly known as the Shield Bug, the Konchu is a small Neopteron whose topside is covered completely by a tough, protective carapace that emits a glow impossible to describe. The exact coloration of this carapace is known to vary depending on the Konchu's inhabited region; the carapace tends to sport a greenish-yellow hue with a pale top in humid environments, whereas in arid regions it shifts to become a deeper and more vibrant gold. In cold regions, it transitions to a much paler coloration covered in a layer of white frost, meanwhile in volcanic regions the carapace takes on a darker color topped with a mix of fiery-crimson and ashy-black. Alongside the segmented shell, the Konchu possesses a pair of antennae, a pair of sharp, flattened arms primarily used to attack threats, as well as has four pairs of limbs lining its underside that it uses to scuttle about.
The Konchu is most famed for the hardness of its carapace, as the plating boasts an ideal shape and resilience to protect itself, bestowing upon it strength comparable to any mineral. As a result of this, its sturdy shell is quite simple to procure compared to the more fragile shells of fellow Neopterons, with it not fracturing upon death. By contrast, the pale underside of the Konchu lacks any protective shell and is much softer. In order to protect itself from threats, the Neopteron is capable of curling into a defensive ball, from which it can take evasive action by rolling if necessary. Due to this behavior, an odd game was conceived by certain upper-class members of society, known as Konchu Dodgeball.
Behavior
In thanks to its exceptional adaptability, credited to both its high vitality and rate of reproduction, the Konchu is able to be found in a remarkably wide range of habitats. It is frequently found traveling in groups formed with other Konchu for additional protection from predators, who they will attempt to ward off collectively. Upon sensing danger, this small Neopteron will curl into itself to protect its soft abdomen from attackers. However, although passive if left alone, the Konchu's high alertness results in it often perceiving an otherwise harmless passer-by as a threat, with it rolling itself into a ball before proceeding to charge its perceived enemies unprompted. This behavior from the Konchu has resulted in many hunters and villagers alike being rammed unexpectedly from behind. Additionally, an odd habit of the Konchu has it latch onto the bodies of larger monsters, inadvertently providing its host with an extra layer of protective armor.
The Konchu feeds primarily on decaying matter such as monster corpses or leaf mold and will travel far and wide in search of more, a trait that only further highlights its adaptability. Although, the Konchu itself is preyed upon by the Yian Kut-Ku and the Yian Garuga —two species of Bird Wyvern whose specialized, shovel-like beaks allow for swallowing the Konchu whole after unearthing it. Some Kut-Ku individuals have even been known to purposely dig up the Konchu to use in combat, throwing and rolling it at its foes. Within the Primal Forest, the corpses of the Konchu are known to become taken over by various fungi which feed on its remains.
Certain sketches from the Scriveners depict two Neopterons that resemble the Konchu closely. The first was thought to be the same species, but its simpler body shape leads some to wonder if it may instead be an ancestor of the Konchu. The second sketch on the other hand depicts a Neopteron whose form is much closer to that of the Konchu's, thus, it is thought it may represent a stage in the evolutionary process of becoming the Konchu.

The Kranodath (クラノダス, Kuranodasu) is a Bird Wyvern introduced in Monster Hunter Wilds.
Summary
Viscous, soot-colored Bird Wyverns that hunt in small packs, their unique external skull plating, comprised of copper pyrite, can expand and contract to uncover or shelter their head. When contracted, this impenetrable plating acts as a hammer used to brutally smash both foes and prey alike. On occasion, Kranodath packs have been sighted clashing with large monsters, clinging to their opponent before using their skulls to stun their adversaries with repeated bludgeonings.

Physiology
The Kranodath is a Bird Wyvern with an atypical anatomy compared to others of its kind. While its torso and limbs resemble those of Bird Wyverns such as the Talioth —with traits such as a long tail, strong hind legs, and clawed forelimbs—the Kranodath's head region sports several unique features. Reinforced muscles and shells around the sternum hold up a thick neck, at the end of which sits the relatively small head of the Kranodath, surrounded by four foldable plates that jut out from the back of the head in an "X" shape. The fleshy insides of these plates contrasts with their metallic, rock-like exterior, as the plating is enriched with minerals such as copper and pyrite. The Kranodath can freely move and adjust these plates, most notably allowing it to fold them together around the head to form a blunt structure reminiscent of a battering ram. This affords the wyvern great offense and defense, as the shell on the Kranodath's head is extremely resilient. Additionally, the Kranodath's true head sports a pair of small red lumps on the top, and a beak-like mouth with hard, external teeth. The sapphire-colored eyes of the Kranodath are extremely small, so much so that they are nearly nonexistent.
Behavior
Found only in the Oilwell Basin, the Kranodath is a social carnivore that prowls the region in small packs of around three individuals. As a group, the Kranodath pack feeds primarily on Gelidron, and can sometimes be seen transporting such prey in their mouth to a more suitable feeding location. The Kranodath will sometimes even engage in battle with large monsters, using its unique head shape as a powerful weapon: once folded, the armored head plates can deliver brutal concussive strikes that allow the Kranodath to stand up to monsters far larger than itself. When in a pack, the Kranodath may also leap onto a large monster and cling to its head before unleashing a powerful blunt impact from close range. The force delivered by these blows is strong enough to be able briefly to stun most targets.

Physiology
A flightless member of the Bird Wyvern classification, the Kulu-Ya-Ku is known for its habit of stealing eggs straight out of the nests of other monsters. Its hide is a creamy-white color with muted, orange stripes that transitions to a darker gradient towards the tip of its tail. The Kulu-Ya-Ku's hide is a popular material that is often used in clothing due to its coloration, sturdiness, and smooth texture. Small dorsal spikes and quills of varying lengths line the wyvern's spine from the head to the tail. Its arms and head feature a cluster of several large, orange feathers that are valued for their vibrant hues and patterns. However, only a male Kulu-Ya-Ku possesses these decorative feathers, and as they are used to attract females, the wyvern spends a significant amount of time grooming them. In addition, the colorful plumes act as territorial markers when they are discarded as the monster preens itself. Amongst researchers, some believe the Kulu-Ya-Ku's decorative feathers are the remnants of wings lost through evolution.
As an obligate ovivore whose diet consists solely of egg yolk, the Kulu-Ya-Ku will consume the yolk of three to four eggs each day. It primarily feeds on the eggs of Herbivores and Flying Wyverns, although it does not appear to have a preference between the two. Furthermore, many of the wyvern's unique adaptations have come about as a result of its exclusive diet. Its large, peculiarly-shaped beak is designed to extract the yolk from eggs, while the barb-like structures on its tongue keep the yolk from slipping out of its mouth. The beak additionally contains sensory organs that allow it to detect ordinarily imperceptible changes within its environment, helping it identify and unearth buried eggs and boulders. As a result, the beak is very sensitive, and striking it will cause the Kulu-Ya-Ku to immediately drop whatever it is holding. Yet, despite its sensitivity, the beak is strong enough to crack the protective shells of other monsters.
The forelimbs of the Kulu-Ya-Ku have three long fingers, with the middle digit being considerably longer than the outer digits. The shape of its hands and the lengths of its fingers are specifically evolved for carrying round objects, as each finger is adorned with a long, sharp claw and subcutaneous bumps on the palmar side. These bumps act as natural grips for any object the Kulu-Ya-Ku carries, whereas its claws are suited primarily for digging or clawing at foes. One account describes the Kulu-Ya-Ku lifting a boulder weighing 300kg, a feat that is possible due to its well-developed forelimbs as well as its unsuspectingly strong pectoral muscles. Perhaps to the shock of some, there exist researchers whose focus lies exclusively on studying this Bird Wyvern's pectoral musculature.
The Kulu-Ya-Ku boasts powerful hind legs, each of which comes equipped with a large, sickled claw. While they are specially adapted for bounding over the rocky ledges of its arid habitat, the Kulu-Ya-Ku may also utilize the strength of its hind limbs against foes, leaping at them with surprising force.
Behavior
The Kulu-Ya-Ku is not known for displaying aggressive behavior. It is a solitary creature that keeps to itself, not paying any mind to hunters or other monsters unless provoked or threatened. When confronted by a foe, the Kulu-Ya-Ku will dig up rocks and use them as both a weapon and a shield. It will protect its vulnerable beak by holding the rock in front of it, whilst also attempting to bash and crush enemies with it. When the Kulu-Ya-Ku is wielding a rock, it becomes emboldened and hostile, becoming brazen enough to attack monsters much larger and stronger than itself, such as the Diablos. Yet, as soon as the rock is broken or dropped, the Bird Wyvern quickly becomes timid and may attempt to flee.
The Kulu-Ya-Ku's primary method of feeding is stealing eggs from the nests of other monsters, which it will then only consume once it has safely returned to its den. When the nest's occupants are away, the wyvern will quickly slip in, grab an egg, and immediately retreat back to its own nest to avoid detection. To even further reduce the chances of being caught, the wyvern avoids repeatedly targeting a single nest. This process, while cautious and calculated, is extremely efficient and takes less than a minute from start to finish.
While its primary habitat in the New World is the Wildspire Waste, the Kulu-Ya-Ku has also been sighted in the Ancient Forest. The emergence of the Kulu-Ya-Ku in the Ancient Forest often coincides with the mating season of the Great Jagras. Considering that there is a substantial distance between the Wildspire Waste and the Ancient Forest, it is speculated that the Kulu-Ya-Ku travels to the Ancient Forest specifically to seek out Great Jagras eggs. More recent reports offer an alternative explanation, however, in that the increased bioenergy caused by the Zorah Magdaros' recent crossing has drawn the Bird Wyvern to the forest and led to it expanding its range of activity. Reports of the Kulu-Ya-Ku in the Old World suggest it has a much wider activity range comparatively, roaming between locales in search of nests to pilfer. There, it is typically found in forest and desert regions such as the Shrine Ruins and the Sandy Plains, as well, it has been sighted in the Lava Caverns. This nomadic lifestyle has risks, however, as predators such as the Anjanath prowl the same areas as the Kulu-Ya-Ku.
The Female Kulu-Ya-Ku lays two eggs per clutch, after which, she will separate from her mate—each taking one of the eggs to brood by themself. This is done to prevent predators and competing Kulu-Ya-Ku from targeting the eggs, as protecting a single egg requires less effort. Moreover, the eggs of the Kulu-Ya-Ku sport an exceptionally unique coloring compared to other eggs to prevent the wyvern from mistakenly feasting on its own egg. While brooding, some Kulu-Ya-Ku may fast until the egg has hatched, although a few fasting Kulu-Ya-Ku have been reported succumbing to their hunger and consuming their egg.

Kulve Taroth mantle themselves in thick coatings of solid gold and other valuable metals, and can emit enormous amounts of heat that can liquefy metal and rock, including their own protective mantle should they become angered enough.
