Physiology
The Kulve Taroth is a massive Elder Dragon identified by twirling horns and a mantle made of solid metal, it is capable of drawing out metals from the ground as it burrows and has a very high body temperature. The metal drawn from the ground adheres to the Kulve Taroth's body as it melts from the heat, forming a protective shell after having cooled down. This metal coat varies in size and composition between individuals, with the Kulve Taroth recorded by the Research Commission forming her shell from gold and the weapons of past humans; the following description is based on her.
When the Kulve Taroth is concealed in her mantle, made of molten gold which has solidified on her body, it is called her Gold-Plated State. A single large mantle covers the dorsal side of the Elder Dragon's body; it starts thick atop her shoulders and drapes over her lower body, hanging over her sides and back legs before reaching the ground. It continues over the tail and covers both its tip and sides, before ending in five long points. Separate from the main mantle, sleeves of gold cover her forearms, and a few sheets hang on the ventral side of her body. Two sheets hang from her rib cage and cover each side of her chest spikes, and another two start from behind her chest and cover her inner thighs. One more covering her pubic bones and ischia; these lower coverings protect vital organs from damage. Gold additionally coats the armor plates, horns, and small spikes lining her jaw, and her neck is armored by a solid, golden mane. The gold collected from the Kulve Taroth reflects light in a way described as exotic, captivating all who see it, as even those with the purest of hearts are tempted by greed when witnessing the gold's brilliance.
Although they are not visible, hunting weapons have been found melted into the Elder Dragon's armor—these weapons have been infused with gold, granting them special properties. The gold covering the Kulve Taroth's body is nearly impenetrable, allowing her to withstand most heavy impacts without noticing. However, the caveat to the gold's extraordinary defense is that the weight of the mantle greatly hinders the Kulve Taroth's movements. The weight forces the Kulve Taroth to change her posture and hold her hips closer to the ground. In the case of an Arch-Tempered Kulve Taroth, the metal coat is paler in appearance, although no less alluring. The white-gold pieces obtained from such an individual are called Emperor Nuggets, and are used to craft even higher-quality equipment.
A special organ in the Kulve Taroth's chest regulates her internal temperature, it is usually used to raise the body's temperature high enough so that metal adheres to the body. To lower her body temperature, the Kulve Taroth can fire powerful jets of superheated air—these blasts are capable of instantly melting walls of ore as large as the dragon herself. Although this ability is typically used to soften particularly hard rock, it may also act as a potent weapon against assailants. When the Kulve Taroth grows enraged, the organ will glow like a furnace and her internal temperature will increase to at least 1,400 degrees Celsius. This will partially melt and dramatically soften the Elder Dragon's metal coating, causing it to glow bright orange. This is called the Melding State, and it is during this state that the Kulve Taroth will attack intruders more aggressively.
Once a majority of the Kulve Taroth's armor is broken, she will become further enraged, shedding its mantle and revealing her Unconcealed State. The Kulve Taroth has a heavily built chest that is round in cross-section, with her torso being long and flexible; the waist and hips are small by comparison, and stalactite-like projections protrude downwards from the chest. The tail is long and thick, its latter half possessing gold spikes that point toward the tip, called Tailshells; a sweep from the tail can easily destroy boulders and swat away enemies. The Kulve Taroth's overlapping scales—most of which are an earthly, gray color—are rectangular in shape, and studded between them can be found small, emerald-like gemstones. Her back remains covered by a now thin layer of gold, particularly around the neck and upper back. Gold has seeped into the gaps between scales and has covered some scales in patterns resembling stripes throughout the body. The shine of these golden scales makes them extremely valuable, leading many to foolishly risk their lives to attain one.
The Kulve Taroth stands on four lean, albeit powerful limbs; the two front legs are longer than the hind legs and end in four-toed, golden-clawed feet. The legs are very strong, capable of carrying the weight of the giant Elder Dragon and her golden coating, however, her true physical ability is only showcased once her gold mantle has been destroyed. The Kulve Taroth is agile compared to other monsters of similar size, and is capable of quickly charging forward, clambering up rocky surfaces, leaping a considerable distance, and other sudden movements. Her claws, which can be used to deliver fatal strikes to foes, are used in tandem with her horns to burrow through solid rock, expanding the vast tunnel systems beneath the earth.
The small, narrow head of the Kulve Taroth is supported by a short and muscular neck; the upper jaw curves up and then back down in the middle, while the lower jaw curves up and then down to match. Two overlapping armor plates sit above the forehead and eyes—the irises of which are golden, and the pupils a dark, horizontal bar. The iridescent armor plates have four ridges that become backward-facing spikes that rest against the horns, which are the Kulve Taroth's most distinctive feature. When uncovered, the enormous Golden Spiralhorns glow an iridescent, blue-green light that does not wane over time. Their unique shape fully displays the shifts from blue to green, adding to their beauty. Their base points up from the head, then they curve down, forwards, outwards, backwards, and down again, the color fading to a pearlescent white when the horns curve outwards. More stalactite-like protrusions line the underside of the horns which, alongside the facial spikes and clawed limbs, are used to dig through solid rock. The Spiralhorns are believed to possess magnetic properties that are the key to attracting metal to the monster's body, collecting a sample from the horns is the highest priority of Kulve Taroth researchers.
Like many Elder Dragons, the Kulve Taroth may produce a powerful gemstone within its body over time. Depending on the quality, this gem may be called a Golden Glimstone, or a Golden Dragonsphire. It is said that the Golden Dragonsphire has the power to stain the world gold.
Behavior
Only a single Kulve Taroth has been recorded by the Hunter's Guild thus far, this being the individual surveyed by the Research Commission in the New World. The First Fleet initially found evidence of a subterranean Elder Dragon soon after they arrived, although it lacked the resources and manpower to commence a thorough investigation. It wasn't until forty years later, when a Fifth Fleet hunter slayed Xeno'jiiva, that the opportunity to do so arose. Following the newborn Elder Dragon's defeat, a surplus of bioenergy flooding the New World awakened Kulve Taroth, who proceeded to create a new passage that led the Commission to her domain: the Caverns of El Dorado. Although it has not been confirmed, this individual is believed to be female based on her appearance and behavior, and almost all data on the species comes from her.
The Kulve Taroth lives a subterranean lifestyle and has never been sighted aboveground, her tendency to stay underground is how she has remained hidden for so long. However, scattered gold chips were found throughout the New World shortly before the Kulve Taroth was rediscovered, suggesting she may venture to the surface. As she burrows, the Kulve Taroth attracts metals from the earth to her body, gradually forming a gold coating around herself. Although metal armor makes for an effective defense, the Kulve Taroth appears to forge the mantle primarily for vanity.
The irresistible gold from the Kulve Taroth has led to conflict with humanity, as humans of the past had entered the Caverns of El Dorado and approached the Elder Dragon for her priceless mantle and illustrious scales. It is not known what became of these past hunters, although their weapons can be found melded into the Elder Dragon's armor, altered by her gold. Humans aren't the only race that treasure and collect the gold, however, as a unique tribe of the Gajalaka —known as the Golden Tribe —live in the Caverns of El Dorado alongside the Elder Dragon. They harvest gold that has fallen off the Kulve Taroth's mantle, adorning their masks and other garments with it; these Gajalaka jealously protect the gold from any human trying to take a piece for themselves. Copper Calappa will also gather around fallen gold and carry away small shares of it.
The Kulve Taroth creates extensive tunnel systems as it burrows, with the individual encountered by the Research Commission carving out vast caverns along the Everstream. As she roams her cavern, chunks of her metal coat fall off, forming deposits of gold that decorate the tunnels over time, creating the Caverns of El Dorado. Each Cavern is a unique ecosystem with its own gold-loving Endemic Life, and is entirely dependent on the activity of its Kulve Taroth. Without the Elder Dragon to replenish the Caverns with precious metals, the Caverns will dry up and the ecosystem will collapse. Being the pillar that supports the ecosystem, the Elder Dragon has been called the Mother Goddess of Gold. The new tunnel discovered by the Fifth Fleet was found in a fissure in the Elder's Recess, a large distance away from the path in the Wildspire Waste found by the First Fleet. Due to the distance between the two entryways, it is possible that two different individuals dug them, and that multiple Kulve Taroth built multiple Caverns of El Dorado.
The Kulve Taroth is docile to all creatures, as she is far too large and well-defended to be threatened by most species. When she isn't burrowing, she roams around the Caverns of El Dorado and may demolish large rock piles in her way. Should an intruder harass the Kulve Taroth for a prolonged period, the Elder Dragon will become agitated and raise her body temperature, slamming foes with her metal-covered body and fire blasts of extreme heat. Should the intruder manage to damage the gold mantle, the Kulve Taroth will discard it, lure the intruder into its lair, and show off its true power. Her physical attacks will become stronger and faster, and her heat will cause molten gold to rain from the ceiling.
Music
Main article: Kulve Taroth (Music)
"The Brilliance that Rules the Everstream" is Kulve Taroth's theme and consists of three individual phase themes, with the suffixes "Confrontation", "Transformation" and "Tremor" for each corresponding phase. The Arch-Tempered Kulve Taroth siege adds a vocal layer to "Tremor". "Tremor" also includes a motif from its debut game's main theme, " Stars at Our Backs ".
When slain in World, "A Collection of Rewards" plays as the Quest Complete theme.
Development
The inspiration for the Kulve Taroth siege is a mix of several elements. The design is inspired by the image of a dragon covered by its hoarded riches. One that also added the weapons of fallen foes to its collection. Kaname Fujioka had wanted to tackle this trope for a long time. To match the idea of riches, the reward system was made to be randomised, like a lottery for weapons. Both Fujioka and Yuya Tokuda wanted to add a special event that encourages the cooperation of all sixteen hunters in a lobby. However, they saved the siege for postgame content because of how much it differs from normal gameplay.
Concept art of Kulve Taroth from the book Monster Hunter World: The Official Complete Works is treated as contradictory sightings of the monster or potentially other members of its species. The designs mostly resemble that seen in the game, but differ in the shape of the head, horns, and gold mantle. Some of the designs (Elder Dragon 13 and 14) better display the weapons melded into the mantle. Elder Dragon 15 is bird-like, with a beak, gold sleeves that resemble bird wings, and the gold over its tail fanning out like a peacock. Elder Dragon 13 has text that suggests the armor is partially composed of iron sand grains. An early design for Xeno'jiiva on the adjacent page, Elder Dragon 3, is also coated in iron sand and emits a golden light due to electricity surging through its skin.

Physiology
Known as the Tempest of the Wind for the violent storms it surrounds itself with, the Kushala Daora is a revered species of Elder Dragon recognized primarily for its ability to generate and manipulate wind. Like many other Elder Dragons, the Kushala Daora is a quadruped with two large wings attached to the shoulders. Its overall coloration is dull and, due to the nature of the steel-like plating that covers the entire body, it is granted a metallic appearance that has bestowed it the title of Wings of Steel. The individual scales of the Kushala Daora are incredibly sturdy and are said to be tougher than steel, as continued exposure to freezing winter temperatures over time has rendered the scales hardened and cold to the touch. Ancient wisdom of the Wyverian people describes the scales of the Kushala Daora as being imbued with the elemental essence of ice and frost, and any weapon's made from these materials appear to inherit these elemental properties. It has been found that the tissue of the Kushala Daora's body has the ability to retain cold for long periods of time after being exposed to low temperatures.
Similarly to an insect, the metallic shell is the Kushala Daora's exoskeleton that it repeatedly sheds as it matures—there is no way to differentiate the Elder Dragon's flesh from its bones. Depending on the progression of the molting process, the Kushala Daora’s plating will change its color; a newly shed shell will appear a pristine white, transition to take on a dark-gray hue, then shift to a brown, rusted color when the Kushala Daora is close to shedding due to oxidation. These variations in color were originally thought to belong to a Subspecies of the Elder Dragon that was reported to be particularly aggressive; this believed Subspecies—the Rusted Kushala Daora —was later reclassified as a Variant once researchers discovered the dragon's coloration was directly linked to the progression of its molt. When the Kushala Daora molts, it leaves behind an empty husk in the shape of the its body; the repeated molting of its shell has rendered it nigh impenetrable.
The Kushala Daora becomes notably belligerent and alert during the molting process, as the fresh, new plating is softer in comparison to the old plating, and the rusting of its shell hinders its movements. However, the shell is capable of expanding and contracting despite its stiff appearance, allowing the Elder Dragon to easily flap its wings. As the Kushala Daora repeats this process throughout its life, it will eventually be unable to form new scales, in turn causing its outer skin to being skeletonizing. This process will begin from its extremities where the layers of living tissue are the thinnest, and once the Kushala Daora's skin has completely skeletonized, it will die. By observing the progression of its exoskeleton, it is possible to determine the age of an individual in a similar manner to counting the growth rings of a tree. From this, the Kushala Daora's life cycle can be broadly separated into three stages: young, mature, and elderly.
In addition to its metallic exoskeleton, the Kushala Daora sports massive wings, each with four long phalanges and a clawed thumb. The wings themselves are sturdy, yet also lightweight and soft to the touch. Heavy enough to be unaffected by landslides and floods in the Ancient Forest, it is believed the Kushala Daora creates updrafts to generate enough lift in order to offset its body's tremendous weight and fly. The self-generated updrafts would help support its muscular wings in flight, while it uses its tail to control its center of gravity. Despite the Kushala Daora's hefty weight, it is surprisingly dexterous and light on its feet. Its limbs, particularly its hind legs, are lined with flexible and compact musculature that support the Elder Dragon's weight. Additionally, its hind feet have an increased surface area and curved claws that aid the Kushala Daora in gaining traction when running on the ground.
The Kushala Daora's most notable feature is its ability to control violent gusts of wind. By using a specialized organ, the Elder Dragon can generate winds able to be utilized in a variety of ways; it can envelop its body in a shield of fierce winds, create turbulent twisters, or expel compressed gales from its mouth. While the nature of the wind-producing organ is still unknown, it has been discovered the Kushala Daora's horns are a key component in its ability to manipulate wind, as breaking its horns will cause it to lose control of its gales. Based on the metallic properties of the horns, researchers believe the Elder Dragon utilizes electromagnetic waves to control its wind. Some scholars have proposed that the horns are an externalized extension of the dragon's nervous system, however this belief has not been backed up by any evidence thus far. Like its scales, the horns are incredibly cold to the touch, although they are much harder to handle properly.
To protect itself, the Kushala Daora will create a wind barrier around its body that gradually increases in intensity. Eventually, the wind pressure of this barrier becomes so great that alongside deflecting arrows and bowgun ammo, it makes even the act of approaching the Elder Dragon difficult. The barrier's strength may be subdued, however, with the use of Poison, or through weapons with Elderseal properties. On top of serving as an excellent defense, the wind armor additionally strengthens the Kushala Daora's wind breath. The dragon's mouth is lined with two rows of small fangs, the arrangement of which reduces drag and allows the Kushala Daora to expel compressed gales from its mouth as though it were the barrel of a cannon. The speed, potency, and distance of these wind blasts is dictated by the strength of the wind barrier. When the wind pressure of the barrier is at its strongest, it amplifies the power of the Kushala Daora's gale blasts, allowing them to travel longer distances at greater speeds.
Behavior
Of the known Old World Elder Dragon species, the Kushala Daora has the widest habitat range. Raging winds and violent storms accompany the appearance of the Kushala Daora, drastically altering the surrounding environment. Furthermore, incidents of the Kushala Daora attacking settlements are fairly well-documented, as the Kushala Daora acts the most aggressive when its shell begins to rust. Sightings and investigations of the Kushala Daora are common for an Elder Dragon, due to both how widespread the population is and the large number of reported Kushala Daora attacks against cities and villages.
The Kushala Daora population inhabiting the New World is noted to spend more time grounded compared to the population in the Old World, additionally, a distinct lack of molts has lead to the speculation that these individuals are more experienced in their wind manipulation. Moreover, since the most recent recorded crossing performed by the Kushala Daora took place around 20 years ago, it has been proposed that perhaps only some of the many individuals in the New World came to pass on. Consolidated by the existence of the Arch Tempered Kushala Daora, an intriguing hypothesis suggests the Kushala Daora that performed the Elder Crossing with the intent to pass on had their lifespans extended and were revitalized by the plentiful bioenergy present in the Elder's Recess. While originally only sighted in the Elder's Recess within the New World, the influence of both the Nergigante and Xeno'jiiva resulted in the Kushala Daora extending its range to the Ancient Forest. Furthermore, as the Elder Dragon travels to cold regions far from human civilization to shed its skin, the Hoarfrost Reach is the only region in the New World where the Elder Dragon's discarded husk has been recorded.
As there are few monsters capable of opposing the Kushala Daora, it typically pays no mind to smaller creatures, however, the Kushala Daora will not avoid conflict against other Elder Dragons. Although such clashes are few and far between, when it engages in combat against the Teostra, singed remnants of its skin can be found at the site of the battle. Like other Elder Dragons in the Elder's Recess, it is preyed upon by the Nergigante. On the verge of death, the Kushala Daora's wind manipulation is at its most powerful; by utilizing the atmospheric conditions of its high-altitude nest, the Elder Dragon will create powerful twisters with a flap of its wings in order to deter opponents.
Music
Main article: Kushala Daora (Music)
"The Shadow Upon the Tempest" is Kushala Daora's theme. Its World rendition contains a motif of its debut game's main theme, Dos' "Hunter, Go Forth".
Monster Hunter 2
Kushala Daora was created and designed by Kaname Fujioka. As the world of Monster Hunter expanded through the development of Monster Hunter G and the vision of a world filled with wyverns began to become more established, the development team decided that it was time to properly tackle an actual dragon in the field, rather than relegating them to special arenas and events as they had with Lao-Shan Lung. Fujioka believed that these so-called Elder Dragons should stand above the natural order and feel like extremely powerful entities. However, from a gameplay perspective, this proved difficult to realize at first: If Elder Dragons had simply much higher stats than regular monsters, it would make Flying Wyverns like Rathalos feel uninteresting and weak by comparison. But without a significant increase in challenge, Elder Dragons would not stand out compared to regular monsters. This led to the idea that Elder Dragons like Kushala Daora should have a unique quest system that would allow damage dealt to them to carry over from one quest to the next, turning dragon hunts into a longer and more exciting type of game experience.
Once the early concept was created, Fujioka added another key phrase to the Kushala Daora design: "A monster than cannot be defeated through previously known means". The idea was to make the dragon feel special by having it resist strategies that players may have developed for other monsters. In service of this, the team created an early prototype of Kushala Daora which was indeed literally impossible to beat: It stayed in the air and destroyed testers without letting any of them do anything. Its signature wind barrier ability - which pushed players away if they got too close - was especially oppressive and was deemed frustrating in this first iteration. Initially, the team tried to make the fight more bearable by making Kushala Daora weak to Flash Bombs, which could be used to drop the dragon out of the sky. Fujioka however felt that this undermined the monster's uniqueness, as this would just be the same strategy that players had already learned to use against Flying Wyverns. Instead, Fujioka proposed a unique interaction in which the dragon's wind barrier could be disabled by poisoning it. The second prototype was much better received due to this change. Shintaro Kojima however noted that because the wind barrier affected players near the dragon, the fight dramatically privileged ranged hunters. Annoyed at watching gunners take pot shots at the dragon during testing, Kojima suggested that the wind barrier should also repel projectiles.
When looking back on the first Monster Hunter game and on Rathalos, Fujioka felt that the game had missed an opportunity to build a rivalry between the player and the flagship monster. It was this insight that led to Kushala Daora receiving a different treatment: The player was to encounter the dragon multiple times and chase it across multiple maps, eventually leading to a showdown at the Snowy Mountains. It was decided early on that the Snowy Mountains map would serve as a buffer that would prolong the anticipation of finally slaying Kushala Daora. In service of that, Yuya Tokuda created Blangonga, which would serve as the "Gatekeeper" to the final battle against Kushala Daora.
As the concept of Kushala Daora's ecology came together, the team sought to make the dragon's oxidizing metal skin into a game mechanic. Initially, they attempted to have Kushala Daora rust in real-time during the quest, gaining new abilities as it went through its cycle. However, this proved too challenging given the technology and resources at the time. Thus, the ideas of an oxidized Kushala Daora were collected and turned into a separate monster, the Rusted Kushala Daora. This Variant would be the only type of Kushala Daora to attack Dundorma, which would communicate the heightened aggression the dragon feels as its skin rusts.
Monster Hunter 4
Following Kushala Daora's inclusion in Monster Hunter Freedom Unite, Tokuda believed that the Steel Dragon still had a lot of untapped potential. However, that potential seemed to be held back by various technical challenges, and with the development of Monster Hunter 3 moving towards an underwater gameplay system, the team made the decision to give Kushala Daora a long break until an opportunity to improve it would present itself. This opportunity ended up being Monster Hunter 4: Tokuda saw the stamina system that had been created for Monster Hunter 3 - which allowed players to exhaust monsters - and the introduction of mounting as the perfect new interactions for a revamped Kushala Daora. Thus, the dragon was added into the game with a new mechanic regarding its wind barrier. Players could now mount the Kushala Daora to exhaust an invisible stamina meter that controlled the intensity of the dragon's wind.
Monster Hunter: World
Like Teostra, the team simply couldn't leave Kushala Daora out of a place like the New World, with all of its Elder Dragons. It inhabits the region's highlands, which helped express how these monsters carve out their own territories. According to Yuya Tokuda, the leader of the graphics team did such a good job on both Teostra and Kushala Daora that he was dead set on coming up with gameplay that matched how great they looked. As a result, there would be players who like or dislike certain Elder Dragons for reasons that are unique and varied, and he thought it maintained a balance of challenging play with a variety of play styles, making for a highly polished product.
The team thought about how to improve the player's experience whilst increasing the size of the twisters, which were always a problem for players. They challenged themselves by devising different kinds of damage that could occur when tornadoes make contact with specific objects like crystals, or how the twisters could affect the surrounding area. Weapons like the lance work well against Kushala Daora until halfway through the hunt, and Fujioka joked that if Lance users had to go up to the nest, he wished them good luck.

The Sea Wyvern Lagiacrus (ラギアクルス, Ragiakurusu) is a Leviathan introduced in Monster Hunter 3.
Summary
Feared as the "Lords of the Seas", Lagiacrus are large Leviathans adorned with aquamarine scales. They dominate the aquatic food chain through impressive underwater strength and agility, as well as vast amounts of electricity stored and released through their dorsal Shockspikes to electrocute prey and explosively boil the surrounding water. Despite being native to the seas, they can sometimes be seen resting, traversing, or even fighting on land.

Physiology
The Lagiacrus is a large semiaquatic Leviathan displaying the elongated, slender body plan typical of its class, with a powerful oar-like tail and a long, flexible neck sporting a distinctive hood. Adapted exceptionally well for swimming, it spends most of its life underwater, coming onto land primarily to rest. Terrestrial locomotion is more cumbersome by comparison, with the limbs being held in a sprawled or semi-erect posture, bringing the body close to the ground while ambulating. The ends of each front limb are adorned with claws that are approximately 97 centimeters long and 18 centimeters wide that the Lagiacrus utilizes to kill prey up close. However, these claws are thought to be in the process of gradually developing into fins.
The dorsal portion of the body is covered in azure scales with gray to greenish-gray accents, while the ventral is white-brown, which acts as countershading while hunting out at sea. The scales of the Lagiacrus vary in size and color, with the largest among them beign the most prized. Situated on the skull, neck, hood, back, and tailfin are brownish-orange spikes of variable size and function.
Despite living primarily in water, the Lagiacrus still possesses lungs. Thus, it cannot remain submerged indefinitely and must surface for air at an estimated minimum of once every 12 hours. A palatal valve in the throat allows the Lagiacrus to seal off its esophagus and prevent seawater from entering its digestive tract.
The skull is long and slender, with a U-shaped snout and horn-like protrusions decorating the brows and region beneath the eye. The fangs are long and sharp, displaying both attributes of teeth found in terrestrial and aquatic predators, a structure believed to be specialized in penetrating both the hide and skin of terrestrial prey as well as the thick fat layers common in aquatic prey. In addition to these true teeth, the Lagiacrus possesses 16 pseudo-fangs that protrude directly out of the shell on the upper and lower jaw. These features aid the Leviathan's grip, allowing it to bite down and latch onto even the heaviest kinds of prey.
The most intriguing physical adaptation of the Lagiacrus, however, is the way it utilizes the Thunder element. On its back are specialized white muscles capable of producing electric charges by rapidly contracting and relaxing. The resulting charge is then stored inside of the dorsal spikes on the neck and back, called Shockspikes. These shockers are highly porous in order to house electrostatic cells that store and hold the charge produced in the underlying muscles. As the Lagiacrus produces higher electrical charges, the Shockspikes glow brighter and brighter. The Lagiacrus may then use the accumulated charge in combat or hunting; the maximum power output of this mechanism is known to vary between individuals. While the horns of the Leviathan resemble its Shockspikes and will glow with electrical charge, no Lagiacrus has so far been observed actually discharging electricity from them.
Like many powerful monsters, the Lagiacrus produces gemstones inside of its body, this rare gem boosts the resistances when used in crafting. The tail of the Lagiacrus is edible and consumed by the people of Moga.
Behavior
The Lagiacrus is an apex predator that rules over the vast aquatic food chain and makes a significant ecological impact in terrestrial ecosystems. Its prey includes Fish, Epioth, Aptonoth, Harpios, and Dalthydon, among many others. While it usually lives in the open ocean around the Deserted Island, it has also been sighted in the Flooded Forest and Misty Peaks, and was recently discovered migrating as far inland as the Scarlet Forest of the Eastlands to exploit the resource rich environment. Strangely, despite preferring two entirely different mediums to traverse and fight through, the Rathalos and Lagiacrus are fierce rivals who battle over securing prey. When underwater, the Lagiacrus can swim at speeds close to 70 km/h, although it is believed the Leviathan can reach up to 100 km/h in short bursts when necessary.
While it can hunt through brute force alone, the most iconic hunting strategy of the Lagiacrus involves the use of its Thunder abilities. When suitable aquatic prey is spotted, the Leviathan chases them up towards the water surface; once the prey is in position, the Lagiacrus begins swimming around them in a circle rapidly. By using the flaps of its neck hood to manipulate the water around it as it swims, the Leviathan creates an artificial whirlpool that traps its victims. The Lagiacrus then discharges a powerful electric current into this whirlpool, electrocuting the immobilized prey to death. This hunting strategy is where the Lagiacrus attained its name, which translates to "Shining Vortex" or "Glowing Whirlpool", a reference to the eerie maelstroms sailors saw in the waters where the Leviathan hunts.
Aside from this hunting strategy, the Lagiacrus can weaponize it's electric charge in numerous ways. It can rapidly arc lightning strikes from its spikes into the surrounding area, or shroud its body in the charge as it rampages. It may also discharge its entire reservoir all at once, resulting in a massive self-propagating electrical blast all around its body. The Lagiacrus can even imbue special mucus produced in its throat with its charge, spitting it out as globs of electricity. While less flashy, the Lagiacrus is also known to send a quick and weak electric shock through its salival mucus at the exact moment it bites down on prey, stunning them to prevent any escape attempts. However, as the use of its Thunder element relies on the continuous contraction of its muscles, using these abilities rapidly exhausts the Lagiacrus.
Based on research on other Leviathans, it is believed that the Lagiacrus probably lays its eggs on land, though no juveniles have been found thus far.
Super Biology Information
The Super Biology Book Series collects the thoughts and theories of real scientists that were asked to speak about monsters from the Monster Hunter series. Thus, they are inherently speculative and should be seen as such.
Marine Scientist Fumihito Muto begins his observations about the Lagiacrus by taking a look at its shockspikes. He proposes that these were originally free bony spines lining the back, which fused into larger plates over time. This in turn forced the underlying muscle groups to change in order to allow for stability and movement of these plates, which later led to the evolution of the electrical organs. Speaking of said electricity, Muto suggests that there might be more to it than mere electrical charges. He theorizes that in order for the charge to propagate successfully, the Lagiacrus would have to expel small quantities of conductive mucus from its spikes, which would spread out as near-invisible threads through water and allow the charge to travel. In fact, Muto wonders if it is the accumulation and production of this mucus that might lead to the glow of the spikes when charging. Furthermore, Muto muses that the shockspikes might not be purely an offensive adaptation. The light they produce could be used for communication among the species, as could the use of weak electrical discharges.
Next, Muto analyzes the Lagiacrus’ ability to stay submerged under water for extended periods of time. He asserts that this behavior can only be possible if one of two scenarios are true: Either the Lagiacrus is able to store enormous quantities of oxygen inside of its body, or it can limit its use of oxygen per unit of time. The former scenario seems unlikely to Muto - the nitrogen contained in the air dissolves into the blood after entering the lungs during a deep dive, which in turn causes it to bubble within the blood stream upon ascending. In such a case, the Lagiacrus would be giving itself divers sickness anytime it emerged from the water. Thus, Muto believes the second scenario to be true: He proposes that the Lagiacrus may have a mechanism similar to one found in crocodiles, where the circulatory system can switch between active and resting modes to carefully manage oxygen consumption. The size of the Lagiacrus would also be advantageous for this scenario, as oxygen consumption grows proportionally slowly per unit of body mass. An adjacent implication of this however would regard the Lagiacrus’ intelligence: As the brain consumes large quantities of oxygen, its development can be counterproductive in species that must dive regularly without a way to replenish it. Thus, it may be that the Lagiacrus has a poorly developed, unintelligent brain.
There are other mysteries about the Lagiacrus that Muto attempts to solve. In regards to the leviathan’s reproduction - of which nothing is known definitively - Muto says that perhaps the Lagiacrus is capable of performing parthenogenesis and reproducing asexually. Considering that some lizards and sharks can do it, Muto believes it to be a possibility. If the species was additionally viviparous, it would make Lagiacrus breeding essentially impossible to evidence, as they could just give live births without any traces and no need to mate. This would mean that all Lagiacrus ought to be considered females.
Lastly, Muto attempts to imagine what kind of natural enemies the Lagiacrus might have. He suggests that the greatest threats would come from the smallest adversaries: Parasites that feed on the electric charges on its spikes and corrode them in the process, for example. A long-term infestation could deprive the Lagiacrus of its electrical ability entirely, ensuring its death. Another possibility would be small, bioluminescent swarm predators that use lights to mimic the communications of the Lagiacrus species, leading a confused individual in circles until it dies of exhaustion.

Main article: Lagiacrus (Music)
"Tremors on Land and Sea", previously known as "Tremble of the Sea and Land" is Lagiacrus' theme. While the Deserted Island theme was only associated with Lagiacrus, it was not until Monster Hunter Wilds that "Tremors on Land and Sea" would be tied to Lagiacrus itself in-game, a similar situation with Rathalos. Monster Hunter 3
Being a major contributor in designing monsters for Tri, Yuya Tokuda helped design Lagiacrus. Other possible names that were considered for this monster at various points during development include Lariatooth, Radia and Lagiatus.
Due to Kaname Fujioka's personal dislike of elemental and projectile attacks, the group of developers tasked with designing Lagiacrus created two versions of the monster: One which only used physical attacks, and one that additionally had access to the thunder element. The purpose of this exercise was to demonstrate how the addition of elemental and projectile attacks enhanced the encounter with Lagiacrus. In the end, Fujioka was convinced of the benefits, and the latter version of Lagiacrus became the version that appeared in Monster Hunter 3.

Physiology
A medium-sized fanged beast, the Lagombi has a body frame similar to that of its relative, the Arzuros, albeit one more reminiscent of a giant hare. Its head sports a pair of long and highly sensitive ears, which are particularly vulnerable to to loud noises, as well as a beak-like structure over the mouth that facilitates the process of picking up food. It is covered from head to toe in white fur and a thick, subcutaneous layer of fat, making it highly adapted to frigid environments.
The belly of the Lagombi is not furred, and is rather covered with an elastic plastron. This plastron is lined with hardened ridges that serve to cut and shear the snow, allowing for fast, stable and surprisingly silent movement. By throwing itself to the ground on its belly with momentum, the Lagombi can slide across the ground at high speeds. The Lagombi's plastron becomes polished over many years of use, eventually turning into a tough and smooth armor shell.
The Lagombi's claws have a unique curvature to them, specialized for gripping and stabbing into the snow. While sliding, the Lagombi can dig these claws into the snow to perform emergency brakes and tight turns. Much like the Arzuros, it grows a shell bracer that enhances the claws' durability. Due to their constant exposure to the cold, the Lagombi's claws are often covered in a thin layer of permanent frost. This causes wounds created by these claws to freeze over instantly, giving the beast an additional offensive ability.
Given how well the claws can handle massive amounts of snow, the Lagombi can dig its hands into the ground and launch large snowballs at its enemies, slowing them down and freezing them. Meanwhile, the legs are highly muscular, allowing the Lagombi to leap into the air and come crashing down violently, or quickly pounce, allowing it to reposition with a slide at rapid pace.
Behavior
The Lagombi is primarily herbivorous in nature, feeding on the scarce nuts and plants it may find in its frigid homeland. However, it is known to eat meat and will actively hunt prey on rare occasions. Using its superior sense of hearing, the Lagombi tracks prey across the snowy tundra. By not relying on its sight, the beast is able to completely avoid the glaring sunlight reflected off snow, whilst also being less affected by blinding blizzards. Additionally, the Lagombi sliding on its plastron is surprisingly silent, increasing the beast's stealth significantly. Thus, the Lagombi hunts by identifying prey from afar through sound and then sneaking up rapidly on it by sliding.
Super Biology Information
The Super Biology Book Series collects the thoughts and theories of real scientists that were asked to speak about monsters from the Monster Hunter series. Thus, they are inherently speculative and should be seen as such.
Zoological Author Yuumin Mori begins his analysis of Lagombi by asserting that despite its speed, the beast likely has poor maneuverability. Its belly-slide attacks see it rushing forward with little agility or flexibility, after all. Mori proposes that the Lagombi’s large ears may have evolved due to this trait: By pinpointing the location of adversaries via its excellent hearing ahead of time, the Lagombi can set course and attack them quickly without needing to readjust its trajectory or react in the moment.
Mori further theorizes that the ears of a Lagombi aid in foraging. Specifically, he proposes that Lagombi can emit ultrasonic vocalizations that penetrate through the snow and bounce back to the ears, mapping out the ground beneath the snow and revealing the location of buried food sources. This might also be a reason for the Lagombi’s tendency to slide on its belly - perhaps it also senses ground vibrations through its abdomen when laying flat on the ground. Mori compares this to the ability of Elephants to sense low frequency communications from other individuals through the soles of their feet. Such an adaptation would allow the Lagombi to sense food and enemies from afar even in low-visibility conditions, and might even grant it the ability to predict natural catastrophes, just as Elephants were noted to visibly predict and escape the tsunamis caused by the 2004 Indian Ocean Earthquake.
The next topic of Mori’s analysis is the Lagombi’s large body. He invokes Bergmann’s rule, which proposes that species living in colder climates grow larger than relatives in warmer regions. This is based on the mathematical principle that as a body grows larger, it possesses a smaller surface-to-volume ratio and subsequently radiates less heat per unit of mass, allowing for more efficient heat conservation. The Lagombi appears to follow this rule, but also seems to violate Allen’s rule, which predicts that species living in cold regions would develop bodies that lacked wide or long shapes in their limbs and other features, as that would increase heat radiation. The large ears of the Lagombi do not conform to this prediction, as they create a wide surface that heat can escape through. As to how the Lagombi grew to this size and shape, Mori revisits his idea of this species’ echolocation ability and imagines the ancestor of the Lagombi as a small, bat-like creature. This progenitor would have been highly specialized in locating food via its echolocation and might have lived in milder climates. Once it migrated to cold environments though, the ancestor would have been pressured to grow larger to benefit from better heat management. As its echolocation was so crucial to survival though, it and any physical traits associated with it would likely not have been selected out during the evolutionary process. Thus, the Lagombi grew large without losing its massive ears.

Physiology
The Lala Barina is a species of Temnoceran with a black chitinous shell that is mottled with red patches. It has thin, spindle-like legs that end in spikes near the joints, as well as highly developed forelimbs that act as claws. These clawed hands can be seen in use to keep the Lala Barina stable as it lowers itself to drink from the river's edge. The edges of the Lala Barina's claws display a striking crimson edge that is noted to be sharp and keen. Its small head has a pair of red chelicerae that make up its jaws as well as six large red compound eyes, four of which are often obscured by hairs, with three smaller eyes embedded in its forehead.
A notable feature of the Lala Barina is the coat of fine and delicate hairs that dance in the wind and cover its body, leaving only its legs and face bare. Due to the pristine color and quality, the Lala Barina's covering could pass for a high-quality pelt, and while it appears a silvery-white, the hairs are actually transparent. At the Lala barina's rear lies the a large abdomen that contributes significantly to the Temnoceran's size. The abdomen hides a large segmented stinger resembling a spike that the Lala Barina can use to suddenly strike with, injecting prey and foe alike with a sticky fluid as red as blood. This thick mucus contains a potent agent that is used as a paralysing venom to incapacitate targets. The Lala Barina strikes with its razor-sharp stinger in rapid succession and penetrates even the thickest of defenses, its sharpness comparable that of to a sword.
Within its body, the Lala Barina produces a mucus partially comprised of a tranquilizing neuroplegic agent that produces the distinctive red petal-like bristles that decorate its abdomen when mixed with water. The Lala Barina is then able to unfurl its abdomen and reveal a stunning, rose-like structure formed entirely out of these Florets. By rubbing its hind legs against its opened abdomen, the Lala Barina can spread these Florets throughout the area, which then slowly and gracefully float towards the ground. Each Floret carries a deadly paralytic toxin that instantly affect whatever comes into contact with them. The Lala Barina may additionally form thin scarlet threads to hang from, and even use them to build its nest.
Behavior
The Lala Barina is a territorial inhabitant of the Scarlet Forest and will go after other monsters in its area irregardless of whether they are large or small, as such, it is often seen fending off Piragill swarms or a lone Doshaguma. When battling Hunters or other large monsters, the Lala Barina frequently incorporates pirouette-like movements, often leaping onto a monster's back and stabbing with its spear-like legs. While acting aggressively towards other species, the Lala Barina does not appear to be bothered by the presence of another of its own kind, although will keep to itself.
The Lala Barina will sporadically unfurl its abdomen briefly to spread its paralytic Florets into the air using its hindlegs; while a single Floret is not enough to subdue a hunter, contact with enough can render an individual incapacitated. This can be witnessed in the Lala Barina's hunting behavior against the Dalthydon, who it will paralyse before devouring. Other times, however, the Lala Barina will bring captured prey back to its nest, such was the case when Erik was unconsciously ensnared in its scarlet web. Further, the Lala Barina is liable to retaliate against those who steal its captured spoils, and when angered, it will keep its abdomen and rose-like bristles unfolded. During which, it will spread out its Florets more frequently and over a greater area.
Following a report that a Lala Barina was sighted in the Ruins of Wyveria mysteriously far from its ordinary home, an investigation by the Avis Unit at Olivia's request took place. This Lala Barina, assumed to possess abnormal traits that could result in harm to the surrounding region, was then confirmed and reported as the first Tempered Monster encountered in the Eastlands. Alongside other emerging Tempered Monsters, it was theorized to have begun appearing due to the Dragontorch pumping purer energy throughout the land, which in turn would affect the behavior of monsters and result in increased battling over territory.

Physiology
The Lao-Shan Lung is a massive Elder Dragon that few monsters rival in sheer size and power. Known by village elders as the "Old Mountain Dragon", this Elder Dragon is covered in incredibly thick, thorny shells, giving it the appearance of a rocky mountain. The shell of the Lao-Shan Lung is thought to be composed of minerals, volcanic ash, and other sediments that have melted into the carapace by its body heat. The Elder Dragon does not possess this shell at birth, suggesting the Lao-Shan Lung spends many years growing this shell, repeatedly heating and cooling the sediments that make up its hardened carapace. This process can take hundreds of years, meaning most individuals that are encountered may be thousands of years old. The color of the shell may be different depending on the minerals used to form the shell, ranging from reddish-brown to gray. Typically, the Lao-Shan Lung's carapace is a dark crimson with black spines protruding from its scales.
The Lao-Shan Lung has a massive skull decorated with a fan of cranial horns and a large rostral horn, the latter of which is considered a luxury item. Several large, black fangs that line the Elder Dragon's hefty jaw are always exposed. Although it moves slowly, the Lao-Shan Lung's legs are powerful, and the Elder Dragon devastates towns and villages simply by walking through them. Its claws are so big that even skilled artisans cannot work with the material. The Elder Dragon will use its incredible bulk to smash through obstacles, and by using its tail for balance, it can assume a bipedal stance to stand as tall as a fortress.
The Lao-Shan Lung is considered an oddity among Elder Dragons, as it possesses no wings or specialized organs to expel any kind of substance from its mouth. Despite the sheer mystery of the Lao-Shan Lung, observations and theories about how the giant can reproduce have been made. Several tales of discoveries of fossilised eggs the size of small mountains have been claimed, with speculation that the belong to the Lao-Shan Lung. However, there has been pushback against that idea, on the basis that the eggs would not be capable of supporting their weight if they were that large. Further, if the shell was strong and thick enough to not be crushed under itself, the embryo would be unable to breathe. Considering no eggs have been found—except for stories of fossil discoveries—an increasing amount of scholars have turned to the theory that the Lao-Shan Lung is viviparous, developing and nurturing its youth within itself as a pregnancy.
Behavior
The Lao-Shan Lung periodically migrates for unknown reasons, and its migration path often crosses through human settlements, requiring the construction of defensive barricades in order to defend against the Elder Dragon. Repelling or slaying the Lao-Shan Lung is no easy feat, as it requires the use of heavy artillery, Dragonators and teamwork. As such, fortresses have been built along the known migration paths of the Lao-Shan Lung in hopes of redirecting it away from towns and villages. It is said that, in one instance, the dragon's migration appeared to have been motivated by the desire to flee from a threat. The only monster believed to be able to make the great Elder Dragon run away in fear is the legendary black dragon, Fatalis.
It is hypothesized the Lao-Shan Lung spends most of its time in dormancy due to the extremely long process of forming its shell, only awakening under certain conditions. Despite the devastation it causes, the Lao-Shan Lung is docile and said to almost never attack other creatures. In a report of a Lao-Shan Lung that had appeared when a large mineshaft was built on the side of a mountain, rather than act hostile towards whatever disturbed it, it simply ventured further underground. Even during its crossing through human settlements, as ballista ammo and canons are fired into it, it only attacks the barricades that block its path.

The Lava Wyvern Lavasioth (ヴォルガノス, Voruganosu) is a Piscine Wyvern introduced in Monster Hunter Frontier Season 1.0 before debuting in the main series in Monster Hunter Freedom Unite.
Summary
Thermophilic Piscine Wyverns that can swim through lava pools as if they were water. By swimming through lava, the substance binds itself to their normally golden scales, forming protective layers of molten rock over themselves. As they swim, they suck in excess lava which they can later use to spew out against assailants. In addition, their powerful legs allow them to leap surprisingly high.

Physiology
The Lavasioth is a large lobe-finned Piscine Wyvern that dwells exclusively in volcanic environments and is a popular research subject due to its peculiar biology. Its body plan closely resembles that of its closest relative, the Jyuratodus: it has two enlarged pectoral lobe fins, a thick tail, stout legs, and webbed feet. Due to the ecological and morphological similarities between the two species, it is believed the Lavasioth speciated directly from the Jyuratodus. Many aspects of the Lavasioth's ecology remain unknown, including whether it is viviparous or ovoviviparous; it is thought to be the latter due to its habitat, similarly to the Plesioth.
The Lavasioth is specially adapted for living in lava-rich environments, having evolved to swim through lava as though it were water. As it swims through lava, the substance binds to its skin, then cools and hardens as an external layer. As cooled lava continuously accumulates around the Lavasioth over the years, it eventually forms a distinctive rock-like shell around the monster's body.
Underneath the blackened lava armor, however, its natural scales are golden in color and can sometimes be seen through cracks in the shell. Rare minerals and ores invaluable for crafting armor can also be found within the encrusted lava shell. Swimming through lava results in the Lavasioth's fins being sharpened to a pristine edge, and in compared to other Piscine Wyverns, the Lavasioth's legs are incredibly powerful to accommodate the weight of its volcanic rock armor, with it being able to leap and swim with surprising strength and agility in spite of its bulk.
To protect its internal organs the Lavasioth's nasal cavity functions like a valve, preventing lava from entering its respiratory system. Additionally, the lungs are capped to ensure that, should lava still manage to enter through the nose, it does not enter the lungs. Its eyes have completely degenerated as a result of its lava-dwelling lifestyle, and—as the Lavasioth does not react to Sonic Bombs —its auditory organs are thought to be underdeveloped.
Thus, it is believed it uses a specialized organ to detect the bioelectric currents of other creatures. The Lavasioth's jaws, lined with unusually large fangs for a Piscine Wyvern, have a wide range of vertical movement.
The Lavasioth routinely drinks lava to maintain its internal body temperature, which is then stored in a specialized organ. When the monster senses prey or a territorial threat, it will spew the stored lava from its mouth—this function is believed to have evolved to absolve the Lavasioth from expending additional energy in its already harsh environment. In the New World, the Lavasioth has been noted to spew greater quantities of lava at foes in comparison to the Old World population.
Behavior
The Lavasioth is incredibly territorial and marks its territory by repeatedly jumping in and out of lava pools, intentionally splashing lava around the area as it does so. It will fiercely attack anything that invades its territory by spewing lava at them, or leaping out of the lava and crushing them underneath its body weight. The Lavasioth will use the environment to its advantage, leaving behind trails of lava around the battlefield to give its enemies a massive disadvantage. Its intense territoriality makes it a threat to miners who venture into volcanoes in search of rare ore, and in the Elder's Recess, the Lavasioth shares a rivalry with the Uragaan.
Due to the scarcity of food in its habitat, the Lavasioth will come ashore to prey on Herbivores, to which it will crawl across the ground and leap at its prey, using its body weight to incapacitate them. The enhanced vertical mobility in its jaw allows the wyvern to sometimes swallow its prey whole.

Physiology
Legiana is an elegant Flying Wyvern that rules the skies of the Coral Highlands and sports the standard body plan of its classification—a small head connected to a flexible neck, a short torso, two legs, a long tail, and two large wings—although is more streamlined than other Flying Wyvern species. Unlike most wyverns, the Legiana lacks rugged scales or rigid shells, instead, most of its body is adorned by smooth skin. Its underside and back are cream colored, while the head, tail, and top surface of the wing membranes are blue; its body is highlighted by elegant black patterns.
Sharp dark-blue scales cover the head, which is small and triangular in shape, at the front of the snout lies a hooked beak with tomial teeth; the beak is used alongside the sharp teeth to tear into the flesh of other monsters. From the mouth, the Legiana can release a distinct high-pitched screech that travels far and wide in mountainous environments. Its large eyes have amber irises and round pupils, a long but thin flexible spine can be found over each eye, supporting a membrane connecting to its thin neck.
The chest serves as the anchor for the wings, which boast a unique anatomy. Instead of forming a single continuous surface, each wing has four separate surfaces: one stretches from the shoulder to the short first digit and around the longer second digit, two other membranes surround the third and fourth digit, and a final large membrane surrounds the fifth digit and connects it to the body. Black star-like patterns decorate each wing membrane and converge into a large black splotch atop its back. Two triangular membranes start at each side of the hip and end two-thirds down the tail, while a single membrane runs down the midline of the thin tail, resembling the caudal fin of a fish. The edge of each membrane is lined by a long and flexible tendon which gives them structure, muscles pull on the tendons to change the shape of each membrane. This fine control over the membranes, alongside the unique shape of the wings, allows the Legiana to take hold of the strong updrafts common to its high-altitude environments. This allows the Legiana to navigate winds that would prove difficult for other monsters. It is an exceptional flyer, capable of aerial maneuvers impossible for other airborne monsters, such as hovering without flapping or corkscrew-spinning. Its domination of the sky has been likened to that of the Rathalos, although the two monsters use different strategies to defend their throne.
Its long legs are colored below the knee by grey scales, and the feet have four long toes, with three positioned in front and one behind. Each toe sports remarkably long talons sharpened by constant clawing against rock, perfect for tightly grasping prey while airborne. The legs are thin, yet sturdy enough to handle the stress of struggling prey.
Bright-blue vents dot the underside of the Legiana's chest, tail, and wings; a Frost Sac within the body produces a fluid that instantly freezes water and is connected to glands inside the vents that secrete the fluid out of the body. By swinging its tail or flapping its wings, the Legiana can send a freezing wind in any chosen direction, creating mist and ice crystals on the ground. This ice is used to restrain the movements of its target, making escape even more difficult, and can also be transferred from its talons. During prolonged combat, ice will build up on the Flying Wyvern's body, transitioning the Legiana into its Ice-Covered State and greatly increasing the potency of its ice abilities. Outside of combat, the Legiana will prevent ice build-up by expelling excess fluid in a cold mist. This ability is the reason the Legiana is called the Freezing Gale Wyvern.
The Legiana is particularly vulnerable to poison, as toxins drain its physical strength and disrupts its sense of balance, making flight more difficult.
Behavior
The Legiana prefers cold high-altitude environments, nesting in the highest peaks of its habitat from which it can easily catch the wind. It was first discovered in the Coral Highlands, and later sighted migrating to the Hoarfrost Reach. It has not been reported outside the New World.
The Legiana is a fiercely territorial wyvern, scratching dozens of gashes throughout its territory each day as a warning. It endlessly glides over its domain in search of intruders; upon seeing one, the Legiana will let out an ear-splitting screech that warns enemies both near and far. Should the enemy refuse to retreat, the Flying Wyvern will immediately attack, using its superb aerial agility to dance around its target and attack from its blind spots. It attacks by impeding its victim with freezing gusts from its tail followed by slashing or grappling with its talons. The Legiana is the apex predator of the Coral Highlands and rarely faces threats to its rule, it is a proud ruler of its territory known as the Lord of the Coral Highlands. One notable individual attacked the Third Fleet's airship, stranding them in the Highlands beyond the reach of the Research Commission.
In the Coral Highlands, the Legiana targets aerial prey and hunts during the morning for a single meal, choosing to spend the remainder of the day on patrol; its prey consists of the Raphinos. It is also known to attack the Paolumu, although it is unknown if it is a predator and prey relationship. It attacks prey from above with outstretched talons, then uses its feet to squeeze or thrash its victim. The Legiana eats a relatively small portion of its quarry on the wing. It has to keep itself light so that it can fly unhindered.
The ecology of the Legiana located in the Hoarfrost Reach differs from those encountered in the Highlands. Although there is a population native to the Hinterlands, a large flock immigrated from the Coral Highlands following tectonic disturbances caused by the Old Everwyrm. Once they arrived, the Legiana formed a nesting colony in a narrow valley between mountains; like in their native habitat, they chose a location that is both too treacherous for other monsters to reach and constantly battered by strong winds. Whether this colony is standard to Legiana behavior, or a novel reaction to the circumstances remains unknown. They have been seen preying on Popo, putting them in conflict with other predators like Barioth.
A Legiana native to the Hinterlands may develop enhanced ice abilities and an otherworldly roar. Such an individual, recognised as a Shrieking Legiana, calls upon other Legiana to defend the colony against threats.
Development
Legiana's role in Monster Hunter: World was to establish the difficulty and faster pace of the Low Rank apex monsters and to utilize the updrafts in the Coral Highlands. To do this, the development team decided to create an agile ice monster that could corner the player. They took inspiration from jet fighters to create a monster with exceptional aerial maneuverability, shaping the wings in such a way to resemble wing flaps. The rest of the design was sleek compared to other monsters like Rathalos to communicate its reliance on speed.
Monster Hunter World: The Official Complete Works shows some of the earlier designs for Legiana. They are all similar to its final appearance but have a greater emphasis on bird or fish inspirations. One design, Flying Wyvern #6, has a face similar to a dromeosaur and wings resembling the webbed feet of a duck. The unique wings were made to better catch the wind. Flying Wyvern #7 had an extra pair of membranes on its calves. Flying Wyvern #8 has a piscine appearence; fish tail, fins down the back, and a face like a catfish.

The Leshen (レーシェン, Reeshen) is a Relict introduced in Monster Hunter: World for a collaboration with The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt.
Summary
Dangerous forest spirits that originate from the world of The Witcher. Their body is made of wood and bone, and they stand upright like a human, though they are much taller, and possess large antlers and long claws, with a single scratch from them causing their victims to bleed profusely. Leshen are particularly dangerous due to their ability to use magic to control nature, which is further enhanced in lush environments. Leshen are capable of teleportation, accelerating plant growth, mind-controlling Jagras, and summoning swarms of Revoltures. Despite these powers, their wooden bodies leave them vulnerable to fire.

Physiology
The Leshen is a thin bipedal creature with a build vaguely resembling a humanoid. It appears to be made of wood and its head resembles a cervine skull with attached antlers. The Leshen's arms possess elongated hands with massive claw-like fingers that can slash through enemies violently. Around its torso and lower body, the Leshen wears tattered pieces of cloth that look as if they may have been worn by a person once upon a time.
The Leshen found in the Ancient Forest is stronger than those found in its homeworld, likely due to the abundance of life and energy within the New World. While nesting in such a rich environment, the Leshen can draw nutrients from its surroundings to empower itself.
Behavior
Not being native to this world, the Leshen is a mysterious creature of which very little is known, although it is believed it hails from primeval forests where it stakes out its territory. Such a territory will be marked by the Leshen's totem, and harming or destroying this wooden construction will quickly summon the Leshen to its location. Within its domain, the Leshen will display the peculiar ability to manipulate and weaponize the flora and fauna around it. This can include sending roots forth from the ground to impale foes, compelling several Jagras to rend the flesh of its target, or assembling flocks of Revoltures to obscure and confuse targets.

Physiology
Larger than the common species, this Nargacuga Rare Species is characterized by the gleaming moon-white fur that blankets the topside of its body and head, as well as its pair of translucent Cutwings. Complimenting the pale fur, which is reminiscent of the moon floating in the sky, the rest of the Lucent Nargacuga's body is protected by dense blue fur that possesses remarkable resilience and flexibility. In addition to providing protection, this thick coat of fur may be used at times to pierce targets like needles. Where the Lucent Nargacuga lacks a fur covering, its body is protected by incredibly strong scales that are deceptively light despite their thickness. Often said to each be as hard as a diamond whilst weighing no more than a feather, the weightlessness of these overwhelmingly strong scales grant the Lucent Nargacuga its astounding agility. Accounts from the few Hunters to have been granted a permit to hunt the beast regale its captivating beauty, claiming it glows like the moon.
Every so often—whether due to their exceptional sharpness, or the speed at which they are swung—the translucent blades of the Lucent Nargacuga's forelimbs will appear almost transparent, much like when they are observed under moonlight. Called Cloudy Moonshards, certain exceptionally well-developed Cutwings resembling the moon are prized for their rarity, even amongst the wyvern's other highly sought after materials. The fangs of the Lucent Nargacuga are another material with high value and are amongst the most coveted materials by both craftsmen and researchers alike. Considered a miracle of nature renowned for their inability to chip or dull, these extremely thick fangs are as sharp as blades and gleam within the Rare Species' jaws.
Much like its more common cousin, the Lucent Nargacuga is able to bristle the sharp spines that grow from its tail to make them stand on end, allowing the wyvern to launch them with wide swings of its tail. Containing a potent venom that saps the life of targets, these spines gain both sharpness and speed as they fly far into the distance. With the tail raised, the Lucent Nargacuga is able to make use of these toxic spines in a variety of ways that mark it as a truly perilous beast, scattering them across a wide area in a manner that makes it difficult to approach. Moreover, the poisonous nature of the Lucent Nargacuga has been known to aid in furthering the understanding of various toxins within the medicinal field.
The Lucent Nargacuga is an extremely rare specimen that possesses the scarce and extraordinary ability to vanish from sight in an instant through the utilization of a special skill. By detecting the surrounding light with its exterior shelling and through controlling the refraction of light as it reflects it, the Lucent Nargacuga is able to conceal its body with great efficiency. However, as this ability requires specific conditions to function and will not work otherwise, it cannot vanish itself under the light of the sun; this Mist Concealment ability functions only when the Lucent Nargacuga is under moonlight or enshrouded by thick fog. Although the precise mechanism of its Mist Concealment ability remains undiscovered, it is theorized the Rare Species' radiant fur reflects moonlight off the mist in tandem with the translucent Cutwings to create a mirage-like phenomenon when conditions are ideal. Furthermore, the Lucent Nargacuga's blue fur is believed to play a crucial role in reflecting moonlight off the mist, and as such, it dislikes when this fur is disturbed—in particular, it appears to take care avoiding Ice elemental attacks. Should the Lucent Nargacuga grow enraged and the skin around its eyes grow bloodshot, its movements may be trailed as it hides in the mist.
Behavior
Until the Hunter's Guild began its research into the matter, the Lucent Nargacuga existed only in an old regional legend of unknown credibility which claimed it to appear on foggy nights in an isolated and hidden location. In recent years, an investigation of the Tower based off the legend would confirm the Rare Species' presence in the unseen areas of the region, and it would come to be known as the Moon Swift Wyvern by virtue of its moon-white coat of fur. The Lucent Nargacuga only inhabits specific environments that are shrouded in thick fog, for this reason, it only resides in certain regions of the Tower that possess the ideal conditions which allow it to vanish perfectly. Furthermore, the Lucent Nargacuga is primarily nocturnal and, during the day or whilst it sleeps, will hide itself in the shadows.
As the Lucent Nargacuga is an incredibly dangerous monster, only a select few hunters are given the hunting permit necessary to hunt it, and any who are challenged with the task require mastery over their senses. It possesses astonishing agility and physicality that greatly outclasses that of the standard variety, as a result, its movements are incredibly difficult to track with the naked eye. Considered a hunter of the night that fires venomous spines and disappears into the mist, the Lucent Nargacuga conceals itself during certain attacks and aims for its target's blind spots. As it does so, reacting after perceiving its movements is not enough, it is essential to not miss any warning signs and to be able to predict its upcoming attacks. Should one fail to do so, they may fall victim to a fatal tail slam. Although the danger posed by the Lucent Nargacuga is notorious, it is said an exceptionally powerful individual will appear when the moon shines in a strange way, and none who have set out to investigate its existence have returned.

Physiology
The Ludroth is a small Leviathan found in both saltwater and freshwater ecosystems, being the female counterpart of the significantly larger Royal Ludroth. Like most Leviathans, she has a proportionally long neck and tail, and is adapted primarily for swimming in water, although she is still capable of traversing well on land. The Ludroth is covered primarily in a green hide that is highly resistant to water. The Leviathan's front teeth, which are fused together into a single cutting blade, indicate that crustaceans make up the majority of her diet. While the forelegs sport full digits ending with claws, the back legs have instead adapted into flippers and allow for greater propulsion while swimming.
Much like the Royal Ludroth, the female Ludroth possesses a sponge-like tissue around her neck, however it is significantly smaller and not as fully developed as her male counterpart's. The mane is formed from modified scales and designed to help the female retain water whilst on land. In addition, by absorbing the stored water through special pores in her skin and by mixing it with internal bodily fluid, the Ludroth can produce a viscous liquid able to be expelled from her mouth to fend off threats.
Behavior
While the Ludroth is technically an omnivore, she has a strong preference towards carnivory and primarily feeds upon crustaceans and fish. Although she is ineffective at catching fast-moving fish, when multiple individuals band together in a large group, they become capable of taking down large Herbivores, such as the Epioth. While she will feed upon algae when she is especially hungry, she does not seem to enjoy doing so. The Ludroth is also a prolific scavenger and, whenever she detects signs of another monster hunting prey nearby, will immediately head after them in an attempt to steal scraps of food off their kill. She seems especially drawn to sounds made at the water's surface.
Unlike Dog Wyverns like the Jaggi, the Ludroth does not showcase any sophisticated form of social structure. Instead, she simply seems to swarm around the larger males whenever they appear to provide some security to herself. These "harems" typically consist of around 10-20 Ludroth and, due to the high frequency with which the Royal Ludroth gets into territorial disputes with other males, she typically does not remain with the same male for extensive periods of time. While the Ludroth does not get aggressive towards other members of her species, she is known to get aggressive towards any outsider who intrudes onto her territory.
The harems of the Royal Ludroth primarily form for the purposes of breeding rights. When the female Ludroth reaches her breeding season, she switches to spending time exclusively on land, whereupon the leading male will begin to store especially large quantities of water within his mane in order to "sprinkle" the water onto the terrestrial female to keep her moisturized during this extensive period out of the water. After mating, the Ludroth lays between 1-4 eggs that she then buries into the sand before they hatch. The Ludroth does not care for its offspring, with the juveniles needing to find their own group to belong to once they have grown up. Due to the fact the Ludroth is a poor swimmer as a juvenile, the young often gets swept away by strong currents. Physiology
The Lunagaron is a Fanged Wyvern that typically assumes a quadrupedal stance, possessing a full-body layer of blue shelling and scales which become darker in color moving towards its underbelly. Each armored shell is coated in countless layers of frost built up over many years to create an unmelting ice layer, while the scales are covered in numerous scars from the Lunagaron's many battles. The shelling on its tail is especially tough, aiding in cutting through anything the Lunagaron slashes with it.
The Lunagaron possess a very Canyne-like face, sporting a thin snout, several hard fangs, and a long pair of ears at the base of the skull. Its body is lithe, yet muscular, with several thick ridges adorning both its shoulders and hips, as well as a particularly large set of extendable spines running along its dorsal side. Its tail is thin at the base and thickens nearing the end, which terminates in three pointed tips. Each of its limbs ends with several vermilion colored claws used to both navigate terrain and fight enemies, with their color said to grow darker with each victim claimed. The Lunagaron's eyes are red and glow when it is enraged.
The Lunagaron possesses an organ known as a Bluecore that acts as the source for its power and elemental affinity, and also causes the gaps between the shelling on its underbelly to glow a pale blue. This is achieved through the organ chilling the air it has inhaled, which is then circulated throughout the Lunagaron's entire body using a body fluid that functions as a natural refrigerant, allowing it to thermoregulate its body's internal temperature regardless of most external factors. Furthermore, this organ allows the Lunagaron to expel a freezing mist from its mouth and the gaps between its scales; this mist is used to directly impair enemies and to cover its body in a layer of spiked ice armor for protection, with the ice coating its claws helping to extend their reach and lethality.
When in combat, the Lunagaron is capable of shutting down its Bluecore, stopping its regulation and spiking its internal body temperature. This results in a dramatic physical shift, with the ridges and muscles on its back greatly expanding in size; as it does this, its usual quadrupedal gait shifts into a predominantly bipedal, hunched one. This is typically performed alongside coating its body in ice, with the Lunagaron frequently shifting between the two gaits while in this state. This has its downsides, however, as shattering the ice armor appears to knock it off balance and create a large opening to counterattack, with the monster returning to an exclusively quadrupedal stance for some time.
Behavior
The Lunagaron is an aggressive predator that relentlessly pursues prey across an extremely wide territory, and is highly nomadic in nature thanks to its robust thermoregulation system allowing it to thrive in most habitats. It utilizes its agility to take down prey or intruders by leaping onto them and biting them, impeding their ability to escape by freezing the surrounding ground with cold exhaled air. The Lunagaron initially remains in its quadrupedal stance while fighting threats, utilizing ramming and biting attacks in conjunction with ice breath. Only when the threat persists and escalates will it shift to a bipedal stance, after which it will primarily fight with its ice-coated claws and empowered ice breath.
While idle on nights with a full moon, the Lunagaron can occasionally be seen standing on two legs and howling at the moon. It displays a degree of intelligence upon recognizing that it has failed to grasp a Hunter in its claws, drooping its ears down in surprise.
