Physiology
Perpetually cloaked in blue flames, the Lunastra is the female counterpart of a sexually dimorphic species of Elder Dragon. Much like the Teostra, her male counterpart, the Lunastra is capable of manipulating flames using a flammable powder that coats her entire body; the two share the vast majority of their ecology. Her general body plan closely resembles that of the Teostra's, albeit with a few notable differences. The Lunastra's beautiful, azure shell is treasured for its dazzling coloration, and her body is covered in a higher volume of fur that grows along the spine, from the mane to the tip of the tail. Her mane is comparably more voluminous than that of the Teostra—this adaptation is thought to give the Lunastra more control over the storage of her flammable powder. It is additionally believed the increased volume of the mane may aid in courtship as well as the protection of the Lunastra's vital regions. The hair from the Lunastra's mane is regarded as a high-class material for its silky texture and fire resistance.
The Lunastra's body temperature is remarkably high and the flames she produces burn hotter than her counterpart's; the presence of blue flames is a testament to how hot the Lunastra's flames burn. The Lunastra keeps herself enshrouded in flames at all times, and by releasing flammable powder from her wings and tail, she can create powerful waves of fire. The ignition of the powder leaves behind patches of blue fire that are hot enough to set volcanic rock ablaze. To ignite this powder, rather than gnashing her teeth like the Teostra does, the Lunastra smashes her wing spikes together to create sparks. The manipulation and dispersion of the powder is thought to be linked to the Lunastra's crown-like horns, which are hot to the touch even after being carved from the Elder Dragon's body. Furthermore, the Lunastra can expel a powerful flame breath from her mouth.
The Lunastra is capable of producing a unique explosive phenomenon, known as a Hell Flare. The flammable powder coating the Lunastra's body creates a pocket of air around her that retains heat and steadily raises her body temperature. Once it reaches above a certain threshold, the Lunastra will disperse a unique powder that will ignite and create a massive explosion of azure flames when lit. In addition to her mastery of fire, the Lunastra boasts incredible physical strength, as a swing of her tail is powerful enough to shatter even the hardest of stone. Moreover, she is an excellent flier, capable of crossing vast distances to aid a struggling mate.
Behavior
The Lunastra is rather elusive and seldom sighted; she is found in deserts and volcanic regions, and has been observed nesting at the top of an abandoned tower as well. Her appearance causes the ambient temperature of the environment to skyrocket. Surveying the Lunastra is a solo task in the Old World, as the sight of more than one Hunter causes the Elder Dragon to flee. However, the Lunastra has a wildly different temperament in the New World and is incredibly hostile to any creatures she perceives as trespassing upon her territory. This heightened aggression is a result of the breeding season, as the Lunastra travels to the New World to seek out potential mates.
The first recorded sighting of the Lunastra and Teostra as a pair occurred in the New World, where the former was observed defending her mate from the Nergigante. Prior to this, the partnership between the Lunastra and Teostra was only spoken of in legends. In Wyverian legend, the Teostra and Lunastra are crowned as the Flame King Dragon and Flame Queen Dragon respectively. Should you encounter one, it is unlikely that its mate is far behind. When research into the Teostra first began, the Dragonwatch began tracking down the Lunastra alongside it, and when the Lunastra had been found, a set of the Teostra's footprints were discovered nearby. Once bonded, the Elder Dragon couple will fight alongside each other and defend one another from threats. The Lunastra will spread her flammable powder around the battlefield, and the Teostra will ignite it with his flame breath. The pair will occasionally partake in an explosive courtship dance that combines the power of the Lunastra's Hell Flare and the Teostra's Supernova.

Their muscular legs allow for powerful kicks, while their equally strong spiked tail grants them the ability to stand vertically and attack, albeit only for a short while. Physiology
The Maccao is a small and lithe Bird Wyvern whose colorful body is covered by vivid green plumage on the top side, the male additionally sports a small crest of lime feathers at the back of his head, with their beauty being directly correlated to his strength. By contrast, its underside as well as its face is covered by a red scaly hide. Although these scales are soft, they still provide ample protection against the weather. More rigid and durable scales on the body serve as fine armor, with any that are especially tough offering great resistance against attacks. Underneath its layering of scales, its elastic hide enables it to move freely and easily, often leaping nimbly through the air. Each of the Maccao's limbs are covered by dull yellow scales, with its hands being permanently curled into fists. Its tail ends with a broad and flat paddle-like structure with several small bumps jutting out its side. This allows for the Maccao to lean back and prop itself upright on its tail, allowing it to aggressively attack prey with its strong hindlegs.
Behavior
Found primarily in the Jurassic Frontier, the Maccao lives in a large pack led by the larger Great Maccao. Unlike other social Bird Wyverns however, its loyality to its commander is heavily situational. The Maccao and its packmates will follow their leader if they are a healthy individual, even being known to mimic the actions the leader performs while hunting, whereas the moment the leader shows signs of being weakened or in danger, the pack will be quick to abandon them and flee. This timid and unique personality is also displayed in the Maccao's predatory behavior, with it being known to raid nests to steal their eggs. Nonetheless there have been instances where, alongside its packmates, it has been at fault for numerous attacks towards anyone who ventures into the region, leading to the wyvern's numbers having to be culled.

Physiology
The Magma Almudron is a Subspecies of the Almudron that is noticeably smaller in size, attributed to the scarcer resources in its volcanic habitat, resources that are allocated towards the production of its carapace and dissolving fluid rather than growth. Its body is covered in ashen-gray scales and black shells that glow red from residual heat, with the latter being durable enough to easily withstand the heat and pressure of being submerged in lava. The scales of the Magma Almudron have appeared in ancient texts, being described as equivalent in heat to boiling lava. The Magma Almudron's whiskers are gray and possess glands that secrete the monster's liquefying mucus; it lacks the "beard" of the original species, instead sporting a set of small barbs on its chin.
Instead of the usual mucus, the Magma Almudron's tail secretes a mucus that drastically heats up and melts surrounding rock into lava. By combining this lava with its secretions, debris, and any surrounding minerals trapped within its tail, it creates an Inferno Lava Mud with unprecedented toughness that is manipulated using the fins on its tail. In addition to being used for offense in the form of waves, explosive balls of lava mud, or structures of explosive mud, this lava mud soaks its scales, greatly enhancing both flexibility and durability. This is the primary way the Magma Almudron traverses, by melting the surrounding rock and swimming through the resulting lava in a manner resembling burrowing. This process has the additional benefit of sharpening its claws through the friction generated from their rubbing against surrounding gravel and debris. After being submerged in lava, its mouth, whiskers, dorsal carapace, and limbs will become superheated, taking on a bright-orange glow and temporarily softening in the process.
Behavior
The Magma Almudron nimbly swims through both earth and lava alike, often ambushing unsuspecting prey from the molten depths. It is notably more aggressive than its counterpart, violently attacking perceived enemies on sight. It battles similarly to the nominate species, using physical attacks in combination with its waves of lava and exploding rocks. The Magma Almudron has additionally been seen forming a ball of hardened lava mud on its tail that it utilizes for explosive physical attacks.

Physiology
The Magnamalo is a large, bulky Fanged Wyvern covered in a plated purple carapace resembling a suit of armor, said to be akin to tempered steel and impervious to any standard attacks. Rows of tan bony ridges line its large forelimbs and broad back, with its back being additionally adorned with a set of initially folded blade-like scutes whose edges have been damaged from countless battles. It sports a pair of ornate horns atop its head resembling those on a general's helmet, a pair of large retractable fangs, and enlarged claws mimicking notched blades protruding from its forearms which are capable of folding in and out at will. Tipped with three bony points resembling a spear head, its long and flexible tail can unfold into a cross shape whilst hunting prey. The Magnamalo's smaller scales, visible on its studded underbelly and between the plates of its carapace, are redder in color and more flexible, while still being resilient to fangs; some of these scales glow a piercing purple, said to invoke the beast's fighting spirit.
The Magnamalo has a unique metabolism that turns the bones of consumed prey into a gaseous, explosive, purple by-product known as Hellfire, which is first condensed and crystallized as a solid mass within its body. When in battle, it expels gaseous Hellfire from numerous pores lining its mouth, back, arms, and tail, engulfing its body in ghostly purple flames and producing a distinctive eerie howling sound. This Hellfire gas explodes violently when force is applied, allowing the Magnamalo to use it to fight by spreading and igniting explosive clouds, shooting blasts of Hellfire from its tail, and augmenting its forearm strikes and bites with explosions. It has even been seen propelling itself with explosions of condensed Hellfire, allowing it to leap across great distances or tackle flying prey to the ground.
When the Magnamalo becomes enraged, in addition to unfurling its arm blades, fangs, and tail blades to allow for more Hellfire to flow from its pores, the scutes atop its back will unfold and extend to allow Hellfire to flow freely from its back vents, granting its back a spiked appearance. As its Hellfire burns, it will also grow increasingly volatile, indicated by its coloration turning from purple to bright pink. This culminates in its Critical Hellfire State (鬼火臨界状態) at the peak of its rage, wherein all of its blades are simultaneously unfurled and its Hellfire burns at its brightest. However, while the Magnamalo's carapace will largely protect it from its own explosions, sufficient damage to vents expelling Hellfire can cause the gas to explode within the body and cause it severe harm, with its most volatile pink Hellfire being liable to explode from the slightest shock.
As a result of the high metabolism required to sustain its Hellfire, the Magnamalo is able to quickly regain its vitality and recover from injury given enough food nearby. However, its horns only grow once in its life and can never be regrown if they are broken. Within its body, it may grow a mysterious purple gem that seems to glow with the light of lost souls.
Behavior
Due to the high metabolic demand required to produce and sustain its Hellfire, the Magnamalo is a highly aggressive and voracious predator that will attempt to prey on anything regardless of its strength or size, even resorting to picking fights with Elder Dragons if given the chance. Due to this, it will often use its strong sense of smell to target locales where large groups of monsters gather, such as the Rampage that regularly threatens Kamura Village, where it will attack and gorge itself on the hordes of monsters, often being seen carrying prey in its jaws. The Magnamalo's appetite is so insatiable that it is well known for completely devouring prey down to every last bone, leaving no trace behind. It is further believed to sometimes even devour old and rotten carcasses with the specific purpose of producing more Hellfire gas within its body.
In combat, the Magnamalo favors reckless physical attacks with nearly every part of its body: slashing prey with its armblades and fangs, piercing them with its tail, or putting its entire body into Hellfire-propelled tackles and dives. When faced with a flying opponent, it will attempt to use its explosions as propulsion to leap onto it and tackle it to the ground, often aiming the descent towards any other enemy that happens to be in the vicinity. While idle, the Magnamalo can be seen grooming itself, often using its mouth to whet and clean its arm blades.
The male Magnamalo typically maintains a large territory, where he provides for multiple female mates and their young, and will constantly attempt to expand his territory and attract more mates by displaying his horns and Hellfire. The needs of his ever-expanding territory and family drive him to constantly hunt and patrol at all times of the day, and he ferociously defends his domain by dominating or driving off other large monsters inhabiting it—even apex predators such as the Bazelgeuse —and battling other male Magnamalo to maintain his dominance. The quality and size of the Magnamalo's horns and carapace are key factors for sexual selection, and a male whose horns are broken will be shunned by his kind and left unable to mate for the rest of his life. If this occurs, the male will forgo attracting mates in favor of recklessly hunting stronger prey to increase his strength and Hellfire production, with the most tenacious and extreme individuals potentially developing into the Scorned Magnamalo.
Relation with Kamura
A Magnamalo spearheaded the Rampage that devastated Kamura Village in the past and forced it to rebuild. During the events of the attack, Hamon battled it during the Rampage, and while managing to wound it and ultimately prevent it from destroying the village outright, he failed to slay it for good. Ever since the incident, the Magnamalo has been the sworn enemy of the village and spoken of with reverence and fear.
50 years after that Rampage, a different Magnamalo would reappear in the wake of the first hordes of monsters. It first encountered a newly-minted Fierce Flame, Iori, and Yomogi in the Red Stronghold, who chose to retreat from it. Fugen and Hamon would explain the Magnamalo to the fresh hunter, and the latter would elaborate on its regenerative abilities from consuming the horde, as well as hatch a plan to use a device made from a Bishaten stomach pouch to lure it away from the horde. The plan succeeded, and the Magnamalo was lured through a secret passage in the Red Stronghold to the Shrine Ruins, allowing the Fierce Flame to defeat it in a decisive hunt.
It is implied that the Magnamalo wounded by Hamon during the Rampage from 50 years ago would go on to become the first discovered Scorned Magnamalo, something which greatly troubled him.

Development
The design team based Magnamalo on the concepts of samurai armor and hitodama (人魂), spirits of the dead manifested as floating lights. The Hellfire gas emitted from its body was designed around the concept and imagery of onibi (鬼火), ghostly flames born from death and malice, emanating from a suit of haunted samurai armor; while not technically a yōkai, armored samurai ghosts or warrior spirits were a well-known image. Its design was also inspired by tigers inhabiting Asian countries.
In an interview with Rise game designer Uno and character designer Tanigawa, they explained that Yasunori Ichinose had proposed the initial motifs of "armored tiger" and "ghost of a warrior", with Magnamalo's tiger aesthetic also taking inspiration from historical illustrations of the animal. Its moves were designed around the concept of a "spearman" who wielded a weapon resembling that of a famous historic general, in particular using elements of bōjutsu, a school of martial arts known for graceful sweeping movements using staves or spears. The idea was for Magnamalo to gradually reveal more weapons hidden within its body as the fight progressed, while also expelling Hellfire from slit protrusions that gave it a striped appearance when enraged; while the concept of hidden weapons was kept, the design was changed due to it not looking striped and tiger-like enough while the slits weren't open. While tigers normally have fur, Magnamalo was given a carapace to reflect its adaptations and evolution to handle its own explosions. Some concept art had it with a brighter color scheme, but it was made darker on request to make it look more like a sinister yōkai and give it more of a Japanese flavor.
Magnamalo was designed with both recurring elements and unrealized ideas from previous monsters designed by Uno, and made to have impact befitting a flagship. It was was originally conceptualized as using the Fire or Blast elements to represent ghostly spirits, but the team ended up creating the new status Hellfire, wanting to create a new status that provided players with both risk and reward. The flexibility of Magnamalo's tail compared to most other monsters required wholly new animations for it to be made.

Physiology
The Malfestio is a medium-sized Bird Wyvern covered predominantly in a plumage of azure feathers, with those coating its breast shining a brilliant gold instead. The flamboyant, blade-like feathers on its three-pronged tail meanwhile fade gradually from azure to gold. It possesses striking red eyes that contrast the white mask of feathers on its face, and its long, blue ears—golden at the tips—droop downwards while at rest, causing them to resemble a jester's cap. However, when the Malfestio is sufficiently angered, its ears will stand on end, revealing their internal scarlet coloration. While its ears appear smooth, they are quite muscular due to the constant movements which they perform. One of the Malfestio's most defining traits lies in its ability to swivel its head a complete 180 degrees around its body, allowing it to more easily track its target as well as ambush foes looking to attack it from behind.
While one of the Malfestio's talons forms the membrane of its wings, two more are elongated into a pair of blades that are kept folded up against the wing. These blades, which are as sharp as swords, can be unfurled when facing opponents so as to be utilized as precise and devastating weapons. The webbing of the Malfestio's wings are elaborately patterned in a vivid-blue, dazzling anyone who glances upon them. The feathers coating its wings, dubbed Azurefeathers, are specially designed to allow the Malfestio to fly silently, allowing it to more easily ambush its prey in the dead of night. A famed treasure from the Malfestio, found in only a small variety of individuals, is a scalefeather from its plumage that shines with ethereal colors.
Perhaps the most renowned aspect of the Malfestio is the golden pollen found within the scales on its wings, it is often scattered in the form of a large, golden cloud when the wyvern slams down from the air. When inhaled, the pollen confuses the senses of the Malfestio's target, causing them to mix-up the directions in which they are moving and allowing the Malfestio to more easily strike its confused opponent. The sharp taste of a Bitterbug, however, is typically enough to snap a Hunter out of this daze.
The webbing that coats the Malfestio's wings are additionally capable of absorbing and emitting ultrasonic waves, causing its wings to glow and the patterns on them to pulse in the process. When applied to a specialized liquid stored within the wyvern's wings, these soundwaves cause the liquid to spray out similarly to a mist, putting anything that inhales it into a deep slumber.
Behavior
While the Malfestio may still be found active during the day, it prefers to hunt under the cover of night. It utilizes its silent flight to ambush unsuspecting targets from the sky, divebombing and capturing prey using its powerful talons and bladed wings. Further, the Malfestio has been shown capable of manipulating the position of its golden pollen-clouds through the flaps of its wings, letting them reach opponents who dodged its initial slam.
The Malfestio typically prefers to rest on top of tree branches, away from threats that may attack it from the ground.

Physiology
The Malzeno is a silver Elder Dragon with a gaunt, slender frame, appearing almost bony or emaciated. Its body is completely covered in heavy, metallic scales and shells that are lustrous and unsullied in appearance, with gold accents distributed across its scales. It boasts a pair of partially tattered, cape-like wings that each possess a large, golden talon protruding from the first digit; the wing membranes display a scarlet coloration on their undersides which will appear more vibrant if the Malzeno has recently fed on another creature. Its head is adorned with two webbed frills and a pair of large, curved, golden horns that glow softly in the dark, while its face is gaunt and almost skull-like. The Malzeno possesses vivid, red eyes and a bony jaw powerful enough to crush the shell and bone of its prey, pinning them before feasting on their life blood.
The long tail of the Malzeno has a pair of fins protruding from the base and grows wider moving closer to the tail tip, which sports a three-pronged claw dexterous enough to grab prey and able to light up with fiery red energy. Its tail is tough enough to shatter fortifications, and the claw on its end sharp enough to pierce iron. Each of the Malzeno's limbs additionally bear sharp golden claws, as well as several gold ridges running along their length.
The Malzeno has a special symbiotic relationship with the Qurio. Safely resting on the Elder Dragon's chest and arms, these winged parasites aid it in absorbing blood and energy from its prey, and the Qurio in turn feed on the Malzeno's own energy. Further, the Malzeno is able to command the Qurio in combat, ordering them to swarm foes or create clusters of Qurio energy it launches as projectiles. As consequence of its relationship with the Qurio, attacks from the Malzeno can afflict victims with the parasites' virus, manifested as Bloodblight. The Malzeno itself is highly resistant to the Qurio's affliction due to being able to produce antibodies against the virus, allowing it to serve as their host with little issue.
However, the Malzeno's symbiosis with the Qurio is not established from birth. The symbiosis comes to be when a Primordial Malzeno —the Elder Dragon's original uncorrupted state—is infested by the Qurio and transitions into an ideal host for them. As it adapts to the parasites and becomes increasingly dependent on them, it undergoes a morphological change over a lengthy period of time, in particular becoming more emaciated and losing most of its natural armor. This change appears to be permanent and lasts until the monster's death.
Outside of the Qurio, the Malzeno primarily uses its hooked wings and spiked tail to attack prey with agile physical blows or pins, as well as Dragon element breath attacks. It boasts a deceptive amount of physical strength for its lithe frame, being able to tear up rocky terrain, crush armor with its teeth, or fell trees with the wind pressure produced by its wings. It has been observed lifting and throwing a Lunagaron with only its tail, and biting a Rathalos before lifting it up with only its jaw and neck strength, with no visible difficulty in either occurrence.
After absorbing enough life energy, the Malzeno will enter a state known as the Bloodening: its scales become stained black, its wings, mouth, and Qurio glow a vibrant, bloody crimson, and its tail starts radiating energy. When in the Bloodening state, the Malzeno's attacks become more violent and its speed is dramatically increased, with it notably being able to use bursts of the Qurio's energy to catapult its body over short distances in a flash, as if seemingly disappearing and reappearing in another location. Sufficient harm to its Qurio-covered parts can dispel their accumulated energy, prematurely quelling the Elder Dragon's empowered rage.
Behavior
Under the influence of the Qurio, the Malzeno is an aggressive and voracious predator that constantly searches for lifeforce to drain, violently attacking any intruders in its domain. It is known to primarily hunt at night, stalking prey before suddenly ambushing them from behind to catch them off guard. While it appears and acts almost regal to begin with, it fights with notable brutality, particularly after feasting on prey.
Due to the metallic nature of its roar and scales, the Malzeno is believed to feed on—or to have once fed on—ores and hard-shelled prey. However, under the influence of the Qurio, it has only been seen attempting to drain the lifeblood of large monsters, through either its fangs or the Qurio themselves.
Music
Main article: Malzeno (Music)
"Scarlet Feast" is Malzeno's theme. Fitting with its medieval design, the theme notably consists of organs.
Development
Malzeno was designed and created by Monster Designer Aewha Shin (credited as Efa Shin in Monster Hunter Rise Sunbreak). While the main theme was "vampire", secondary themes of "noble baron" and "knight in shining armor" were given to spice up the design, as many of the prior designs "lacked punch" for a flagship monster. Some of these prior designs resembled bats or mosquitos, with many being dark and gloomy, while the current design took cues from snakes and raptors. As "Dracula" originally meant "son of a dragon", the team gave Malzeno elements of traditional dragons in addition to the vampire motifs, while its wings, fins, and Qurio clusters were designed to evoke noble attire typically worn by vampires. Malzeno was designed with a "noble and cunning" personality in mind, with the particular imagery of it sitting at the end of a candlelit table stirring a glass of wine being the inspiration for its overall behavior and the candlestick-like shape of its tail.
Shin detailed the deliberate contrast between Malzeno and the base game flagship, Magnamalo: a dark, eastern samurai tiger contrasted against a bright, western knight dragon. While Magnamalo was designed to represent strength with its rugged appearance and brutish demeanor, Malzeno represented intelligence with a cleaner appearance and elegant behavior. This contrast was also kept in mind when designing Malzeno's "teleportation" in contrast to Magnamalo's Hellfire propulsion, as while Magnamalo was described as “kicking the ground to dash forward”, Malzeno was described as “thrusting forward as if it’s being pushed”.
Yoshitake Suzuki shared in the May 2022 Digital Event that Malzeno was created with the keywords "aristocracy", "nobility", "grandeur", and "cunningness", which also served as the basis for composing its battle theme, Scarlet Feast.
According to Monster Modeler Aria Oishi, the coloration of Malzeno's darkened state was based on the color of silver that has oxidized or otherwise reacted with corrosive substances. Additionally, the monster was intentionally designed to be contradictory, with noble features such as the silhouette and stance contrasting with the sinewy limbs, dark eye sockets, and thin fangs. Sound Designer Yutaka Omuta noted that the sounds produced by Malzeno were all centered around metal, emphasizing the idea of clattering armor and steel. Additionally, Malzeno is designed to muffle all sounds around it when it prepares to "teleport", an effect the team added to further sell the surprising nature of that ability.

Physiology
The Mernos is a harmless Wingdrake native to the New World. It has a similar body plan to other Wingdrakes: a large head on a slim neck, forelimbs modified into wings, taloned feet, and a thin tail. Most of the Mernos' body is adorned by dark, teal scales, while the chest and underside of the wings are yellow. The head has a yellow beak with serrated edges, and a large yellow crest points backward from the top of the skull; two more crests protrude from the lower jaw, giving the whole head the appearance of an arrow. The beady green eyes are right behind the upper crest.
The wings are attached to a large bony chest and are themselves long and narrow, they are supported by three digits; the shorter fourth digit is free and possesses a claw. The Mernos is an exceptional flyer amongst other Wingdrakes, partially due to its crest acting as a rudder. The legs sport four-toed feet, each with a long curved talon. The tail possesses a rounded vane near its end.
Behavior
The Mernos is naturally found in the Ancient Forest of the New World and it usually lives in groups of 2-3, although multiple duos will converge into larger flocks when needed. The Mernos hovers in the same general area, feeding on nuts, berries, and fruit; Scatternuts are its favorite food. The Mernos often drops to the ground to preen itself. Naturally skittish, the Mernos will fly away if frightened, be it by a larger monster's presence or a shot from a Slinger. Due to its proficiency at flying, it tends to soar for longer distances than other Wingdrakes. The large crest on its head coordinates the flock by signaling the direction the Wingdrake is looking.
A hunter can use their Slinger to latch onto the foot of a disturbed Mernos. Unlike other Wingdrakes, the Mernos will carry the hunter for a considerable distance before the Slinger detaches. Other nearby Mernos will follow the first, and soon after they will fly back to their original position. Due to this unique behavior, the Mernos may be utilized by hunters as a form of aerial transportation, including when hunters wish to return to camp, or during special operations. A tamed Mernos is employed by members of the Research Commission and by the Forbidden Lands Expedition Team in the Eastlands.
Development
Concept art of Mernos depicts various colorful winged monsters, most with head crests and beaks. The idea being that the beak is pointing in a certain direction that coordinates the flock. The designs show various inspirations, including birds, pterosaurs, herbivorous dinosaurs, and even swordfish. Some of the designs have strange wings resembling those of Legiana.

Mizutsune is an Endangered Species. Its egg can be rescued in the Canalta Timberland from the Invasive Shogun Ceanataur.
Physiology
The Mizutsune is a large and slender Leviathan whose body has adapted for life in both aquatic and terrestrial habitats. The top half of its body is covered in an array of irregularly shaped scales that, while glossy, are surprisingly tough. Despite their white appearance, these scales are actually transparent in color, with their shape causing them to take on an iridescent quality. By contrast, the underside of its body is covered in a coating of deep-purple fur that goes all the way to its tail tip, which sports an especially large cluster of fur. Believed to have evolved from its scales, the hairs are normally quite stiff despite their appearance, although they become as soft as silk once exposed to the Mizutsune's bodily secretions. The female Mizutsune notably possesses less fur on her underside when compared to a male. The slender head of the Mizutsune is colored white and sports several whiskers growing both above and below it, with four large fins growing out the back and two smaller fins growing out below; both its fins and whiskers allow it to detect moisture in the air with a sensitive accuracy. This allows the Mizutsune to sense when any of the bubbles it has scattered around itself has popped, allowing for it to quickly detect for intruding predators.
Similar fins to the ones on its head are also present on its back in three distinct rows and at the end of its tail. The middle fins atop the back grow notably larger and with more elaborate patterns, and those surrounding the tip of the tail get progressively bigger nearer the tip. These fins, colored a vibrant pink and sporting yellow-and-red eye-like spots are thought to be evolved scales. As well, the prominent fins atop both the Mizutsune's head and back are capable of changing in color depending on its temperament. When it grows enraged, the increased blood flow causes its fins to turn a deep red, whereas while it is fatigued, the slowing of its heart rate causes its fins to contrastingly turn a deep blue as well as shrivel and sag. These especially large fins are only found on the male Mizutsune and are subsequently believed to be utilized to attract females. When combined with the fluids its body naturally produces, the fins gain an especially elegant pattern, one prettier than any dye.
The primary reason why the Mizutsune is capable of remaining active for extended periods of time is owed to its most recognizable feature, a soap-like natural fluid it secretes from its body known as Bubblefoam. This fluid serves several different functions, aiding in keeping the Mizutsune's body surface well moisturized and preventing it from drying out by remaining inside the crevices between scales. The Bubblefoam additionally acts as a very strong lubricant, and by secreting this fluid from its underside, the wyvern can reduce its own friction and move incredibly smoothly along the ground. To help it maneuver more easily while sliding around, the Mizutsune sports a pair of exceptionally long claws on each of its forelegs. These claws, in addition to being hook-like in shape, are covered with several smaller hooks that help to increase the wyvern's grip, preventing it from slipping around too much while sliding around on its Bubblefoam. The sides of the claws bear comb-like grooves that the Mizutsune appears to use to both groom and trim the purple fur on its underbelly. When combined with the Bubblefoam, its claws are capable of effortlessly slicing through its prey. The Mizutsune's Bubblefoam further acts as an excellent cleaning agent, able to easily remove impurities and transform even the murkiest of swamp water into a bubble bath with just a few drops.
Beyond these purposes, the Bubblefoam is capable of being applied offensively as well. Located at the back of its mouth below its eyes is a foam sac that secretes the Bubblefoam. By stimulating this secretion with its tongue and blowing air into it, the Mizutsune is capable of forming bubbles it can spray out of its mouth. These bubbles are also produced as a byproduct of the Mizutsune releasing its secretions from its underbelly, with them generating as it rubs the fluid against its fur or the ground. The bubbles share the same lubricating effects as its Bubblefoam, creating an environment in which the Mizutsune is best able to utilize its own mobility and causing anything that comes into contact with them to slip around uncontrollably. While most of its bubbles are transparent in color, some are known to take on different shapes and properties, such as green bubbles possessing a restorative quality, or red bubbles which boost offensive capabilities; it is believed the properties of these bubbles are influenced by the Mizutsune's diet. The Mizutsune individuals sighted in the Eastlands have also been seen producing an explosive Bubblefoam that burns with blue flames once enraged, causing their bubbles to explode violently when popped; it is currently unknown whether this also stems from a unique diet. In addition to spreading bubbles through the air, the Mizutsune is capable of spraying out a high-pressure beam of water, which is formed from the same components as its Bubblefoam.
Behavior
While the Mizutsune has evolved to be able to stay out of the water for extended periods of time, it still dislikes having its skin dry out and prefers to live in humid areas with access to bodies of water, such as mountainous streams and rainforests. This choice in habitat often overlaps with that of the Zinogre, which the Mizutsune is generally very wary of, and will typically take action to avoid conflict with upon sensing it intruding upon its turf. When normally faced with a formidable adversary, the Mizutsune's preferred tactic is simply to turn and run, using its bubbles to gradually drain its opponent's energy and allow it to easily escape, with its escape speed being especially high. Due to the ease with which it can escape from conflicts, the wyvern often appears relaxed when confronting potential threats, although its vigilance is often described as higher than even that of Herbivores.
The Mizutsune is carnivorous in nature and primarily feeds on fish, which it has been frequently observed catching and swallowing whole. By doing so, the Mizutsune also consumes the contents of the fish's stomach, with the balance of mosses, mushrooms, and seeds acquired from this method of feeding influencing both the color of its fur and the lubricity of its Bubblefoam. Its claws are also used extensively while hunting fish, with their sharp and pointed tips making them well suited for hooking into prey. While its bubbles are more effective when used defensively than offensively, the Mizutsune is still capable of utilizing them in a similar way to hunt prey on land.
While the female Mizutsune tends to live in a large social group, the male Mizutsune is entirely solitary. However, when the breeding season comes the male will join one of these female herds in order to mate, becoming notably more aggressive when the breeding season starts. The female is primarily responsible for hunting to feed the offspring, while the male stays behind to guard the nest. A male Mizutsune attempting to protect either his nest or his offspring will fight back viciously against intruders, even being known to repel an intruding Zinogre if necessary. Once the offspring have matured, the male once again will depart from the group, although he will occasionally return to check upon the herd he was once a part of.

The Generations version of "A Bewitching Dance" was voted among the Top 10 music themes in the Hunters' Choice: Top 10 Monster Themes - Monster Hunter 20th Anniversary.

The Great Roaring Wyvern Molten Tigrex (ティガレックス希少種, Tigarekkusu Kishō-shu) is a Flying Wyvern introduced in Monster Hunter 4.
It is a Rare Species of the Tigrex.
Summary
Living prehistoric fossils, this giant Tigrex Rare Species dwarfs their lesser brethren in power and ferocity. They are covered by a thick, heavy, and highly blast-resistant carapace, a necessity in order to withstand the explosive powder their claws ignite. Although appearing as sluggish, once angered, they will quickly build momentum and ramp up in aggression, relentlessly charging down Hunters. However, during this rageful rampaging, their hide will soften due to their increased metabolism.

Physiology
An abnormally large specimen, this Rare Species' predominantly scarlet body is covered by fine dark scales, save for its bright-blue wingtips and dimly-tinted claws. The thick scales lining the Molten Tigrex's body exude a burnt scent, likely the result of endless surrounding explosions, yet not one shows even a single mark of damage. Together, these scales form a supple heavy carapace worth its weight in gold, and one that requires the utmost care by craftsmen who wish to avoid setting off its explosive surface.
As a consequence of its larger size, the Molten Tigrex's metabolism is far more efficient and its body temperature is much higher, evidenced by its ability to consecutively generate and sustain intense shockwave producing roars. Its metabolic rate is accelerated by the vast quantity of air it inhales before thunderously roaring, something only possible due to its abundant lung capacity and powerful heart. However, the Molten Tigrex's epidermis is prone to keratinization as a by-product of its heightened metabolism, which causes its scales to flake and subsequently form the basis of its explosive dust. In addition, the Molten Tigrex's brawny red-splotched claws possess metallic elements in their composition, allowing it to use them as flints to generate sparks that combust concentrated clouds of the volatile dust. Each triggered explosion delivers astonishing power and causes impurities to adhere to its hide, further contributing to subsequent dust explosions.
The movements of the Molten Tigrex are sluggish due to the heft its gigantism bestows upon it, yet its larger frame has only elevated its strength to new heights; it not only eclipses the Tigrex in physicality, it far exceeds the raw power of even the Brute Tigrex. Some Hunter reports suggest it possesses devastatingly powerful jaws lined with heavy, rugged fangs that arouse primal fear in any onlookers. Similarly, reports originating from hunters experienced with tracking the Rare Species detail its staggering stamina and dynamism, claiming its forelimbs crush anything in their path and that the claws bring an agonizing end to one's life. Aside from its large frame and powerful lungs, the Molten Tigrex's heart is seen as a source for its untiring power, mysteriously, it continues to beat even once carved from the slain wyvern's body. Relatedly, among the materials harvested from the body of the Molten Tigrex, its imposing tail is particularly desired by artisans wishing to turn it into a formidable weapon, although very few possess the necessary talent for forging it.
The Molten Tigrex has an incredibly durable and resistant exterior capable of deflecting strikes from all but the sharpest of weapons, as is characteristic of Rare Species. Furthermore, similarly to its relatives, the Molten Tigrex is quick to enrage during combat, causing it to fight more vigorously. When it is attacked as it intensely battles, the Molten Tigrex will anger even further and enter an Explosive State, a transition apparent by the striking blood-red veins that suddenly appear all over its body. As it rampages in this state, now able to let loose roars that shatter the very air itself, its metabolism rapidly hastens in response to it inhaling even greater quantities of air. Due to the Molten Tigrex's now heightened metabolic rate and rising internal body temperature, it movements drastically ramp up in speed and its shell softens significantly.
Behavior
It is believed the Molten Tigrex did not evolve from its standard counterpart, and instead that it rather came about from mutation, with the primary factor behind its abnormal size lying in its habitat. The Molten Tigrex inhabits the Tower —an ancient, sky-piercing, monolithic structure located within a dense primordial forest whose surrounding environment is prehistoric in nature. The flora of this area retains traces of its primal state and the oxygen levels are notably high, as such, this unique habitat is thought to be linked to the Rare Species' enormous frame. It is often said that the Tigrex is a primitive species, with speculation suggesting that ancient individuals often inhabited such primordial regions and were even larger than those found today. One theory proposes that genetic information for this existed within the Molten Tigrex's body, and that a trigger of some sort induced a mutation that caused a reversal to certain ancestral traits. While it is merely conjecture, it represents the current understanding of the secret behind the Molten Tigrex's gigantism.
The Molten Tigrex is a ferocious monster whose roars echo in one's ears long after the hunt has ended, and it has earned the alias Great Roaring Wyvern. It is an extremely rare variation whose existence was a matter of debate for a long period of time, primarily due to a lack of confirmed first-hand sightings of it. Outside of rumors and ancient texts, one of which claimed the arrival of a hero to defeat it, the only evidence hinting towards the Molten Tigrex's existence were claw marks and footprints too large to belong to the ordinary Tigrex. Due to these reasons, and as it had only been seen a handful of times prior, its recent discovery caused great shock within the Guild
Monster Hunter 4
Following the creation of Lucent Nargacuga during the production of Monster Hunter 3 Ultimate, the team decided that the next Rare Species monster they would create should be a new version of Tigrex. Once it was decided that Tigrex would be included in Monster Hunter 4, the team thus immediately began prototyping a rare species version of it.
Since regular Tigrex was a very simple enemy that mostly attacked players by charging at them, it was hard to add new abilities to it without losing the monster's core identity. The team thus started out by making the prototype rare Tigrex much larger than a regular one. This caused its physical attacks to affect wider areas, increasing the fight's challenge in the process. However, the increased size also created more vulnerable spots on the monster, as this prototype had more surface area players could attack. To balance this out, the team wanted to give this rare species some kind of elemental ability that would punish players for trying to exploit the most obvious openings. Yuya Tokuda however advised the design team that Tigrex should not receive a breath attack, as that would detract from the wyvern's brute force identity. Instead, the team landed on the idea of having the rare species scatter explosive dust around itself, which would keep players on edge even when they stood in one of the monster's "blind spots". The size and explosive dust of this monster would also lend itself particularly well to multiplayer, as the ebb and flow of safe zones turning into danger zones and vice versa would make for engaging tactical team play. And so, the design was approved and refined into the Molten Tigrex found in the final game.

Physiology
The Monoblos is a large Flying Wyvern that resides in remote parts of deserts. Described as a subspecies of the Diablos, the two share the same general shape and body plan, although are distinguished by coloration. In contrast to the Diablos' beige shell, the Monoblos sports a darker and more saturated reddish-brown carapace. It is further distinguished by its unique head and tail shape.
The head of the Monoblos is its most iconic feature, giving the wyvern its common name of Monoblos as well as its alias of One-Horned Wyvern. Instead of the Diablos' jagged snout with pronounced tusks, the Monoblos sports a pointed beak whose tusks are much smaller and protrude outwards to a lesser degree. Just behind this beak is the Monoblos' namesake single horn: it is a long crimson horn with a spiral edge that twists along its length. This horn, which is the Monoblos' primary means of attack, is especially well-suited for piercing, and, can even pierce rock when backed up by a full-body charge. The horn has been found to contain a flammable substance that reacts violently to impacts, releasing a heated pulse with every horn strike and further adding to its lethality. The Monoblos' frill is another distinguishing feature, sporting long red spikes along its distal edge.
While the length of the Monoblos' tail is similar in structure to the Diablos, its tip ends in a rounded club with larger spikes that resembles that of the Rathalos'. Despite this difference, the tails of both the Monoblos and Diablos may prove interchangeable to some smiths. The Monoblos additionally sports a pronounced dorsal ridge that hardens through continuous exposure to desert sands. Particularly thick pieces are instead called Chines; ridges of all kinds, especially when cleanly and fully carved, are a popular material in forging hunting equipment.
Similar to the Diablos, the Monoblos' rugged appearance belies its agility. Its claws are built for burrowing through sand, a vantage point often used to strike from below. Its muscular legs afford it swift and powerful charges, which when paired with its horn, are capable of felling Hunters in a single blow. However, these charges can be turned against the Monoblos, as getting its horn stuck in especially hard rock can leave it momentarily vulnerable as it attempts to dislodge its horn.
The same Blos Medulla that may be obtained from the Diablos is found in the Monoblos. Additionally, the Monoblos can yield its own prized body part: its heart. Symbolically, the heart of the Monoblos represents pure and intense anger, although its true value lies in its utility for smiths, being able to restore dulled blades to their former glory.
Behavior
Very little is known about the Monoblos' behavior, perhaps owing to its preferred habitat of remote deserts; this reclusive nature makes it often avoid human contact. Should it nonetheless enter a more traveled area, such as by being forced out of its natural habitat, its power makes it a dangerous threat.
The Monoblos is known to feed on cacti.
Development
Monoblos was designed by Kento Kinoshita, the lead designer in charge of Monster Hunter's village mode. As the singleplayer mode was only a small fraction of the final game, Kinoshita's idea of making Monoblos entirely exclusive to it was not immediately accepted by the rest of the team. After "begging" fellow designer Shintaro Kojima for approval, the Monoblos was eventually implemented as the exclusive final boss of the game's village mode.

White and fluffy Herbivores found on remote islands, they are famed for their vast quantities of thick wool, which have been used by humans for generations to make clothing and various other tools. Physiology
The Moofah is a small Herbivore covered almost entirely in a thick layer of yellow tinted fur, with its brownish-gray skin only being visible on its snout and its long hoofed legs; the eyes of the Moofah are completely obscured by its fleece. The Moofah additionally sports a pair of horns atop its head which are known to vary in size between genders, with the male Moofah possessing a larger pair. While the female Moofah is entirely pacifistic, never making use of her horns in combat, the male will fight back if his herd is threatened, ramming his target down with his headgear.
Behavior
In the wild, the Moofah is exclusively found on the isolated Deserted Island. In addition to this however, the Moofah is kept as livestock by the people of Bherna village. A domesticated Moofah possesses much shorter horns than its wild counterpart, on account of them being frequently filed down by its caretakers. These horns are decorated with colorful ornamental cloth, with similar materials being wrapped around the herbivore's neck, typically with a bell also being attached. Its fur is also notably paler and more cream-colored comparatively than that of its wild counterpart. Alongside being incredibly fluffy, this fleece is typically used in the creation of thread that is both supple, yet strong.
Domesticated Moofah of all forms are highly receptive to affection—most commonly petting—however the juvenile Moofah in particular can become agitated if pet for too long, retaliating against its caretaker by headbutting them, followed by it charging around in a tantrum.

Physiology
A small and squat herbivorous monster whose body is supported by four short legs ending in hooves, most of the Mosswine's body is covered in a pale, musty, pink hide. However, the flat back of the monster is instead covered in a layer of moss and mushrooms. Its head is armored with a thick dome atop the forehead which is as thick as stone, that is surrounded with several spikes; it will utilize this dome to charge down anything that threatens it. The Mosswine additionally possesses a long snout ending in a bulbous nose that grants it an excellent sense of smell which it utilizes to effortlessly track down its food.
Behavior
While the Mosswine is primarily found roaming around grasslands, it can be found virtually wherever mushrooms are known to grow. It will either roam alone, or in a group consisting of up to two other individuals, although the Mosswine found within the New World does not form herds at all and leads an entirely solitary life, forming its territory from its own preference in mushrooms. In order to search for its food, it will utilize its heightened sense of smell: if a Mosswine stops and begins to snort, it is a sign that it has located some high-quality mushrooms, with Blue Mushrooms being a particular favorite of its due to the plentiful nutrients it contains. Despite it growing mushrooms atop its back, the Mosswine has never been observed feeding off of the fungus growing on another individuals back. By observing its movements, humans are able to utilize the Mosswine to locate mushrooms for themselves, which they will promptly steal. As well, spooking the Mosswine can cause the monster to flee towards its secret refuge, which often serves as a home to a mother-lode of mushrooms.
While normally peaceful in nature, not going out of its way to attack humans, if its own life is threatened the Mosswine will not hesitate to fight back with powerful headbutts. If it begins to kick its legs across the ground, it is usually a sign that it has turned aggressive and is about to charge. Within the New World, the back of the Mosswine often acts as a resting place and symbiotic host for the rare Bristly Crake.

The Constricting Snake Wyvern Najarala (ガララアジャラ, Gararājara) is a Snake Wyvern introduced in Monster Hunter 4.
Summary

Physiology
The Najarala, alongside its Subspecies, is the only large monster currently known to the Guild to be classified as a Snake Wyvern. The elongated body is adorned with a highly-segmented carapace of green shells with vivid-orange undersides; these shells overlap each-other to form a multi-layered carapace that provides it with immense protection. The shells, believed to have evolved from an original coating of simple scales, are capable of growing to a variety of different sizes, preventing them from potentially inhibiting the wyvern as it slithers around. Underneath its shell coating and covering its underbelly is a layer of hide which, when compared to its shell, is relatively flexible. As a result, despite its sheer length, the Najarala is able to remain quite fast and agile.
It has four relatively short limbs, with its forelimb being slightly longer than its hind legs and sporting more and longer orange shelling along their edges. Despite this, only its short hind-legs are used to support its weight while standing still. The Najarala's skull is stout with vibrant red marking around its eyes. Its top jaw possesses a curved beak with two fang-like protrusions, with two similarly large fangs also jutting from its bottom jaw. These fangs contain a powerful and highly-concentrated neurotoxin which it injects through its bites, inducing paralysis in its target. These toxins are also found within the Najarala's bone marrow and can similarly cause paralysis if handled improperly.
The shelling on its neck protrude outwards, fading from green to a pale yellow before being tipped in orange, forming a large sail-like shape; this organ is known as its Sounder. Meanwhile, the wyvern's tail tapers into a fan-like shape at the tip, sporting an array of similarly-colored Sounders around its edges. This tail-tip is also fairly hard, letting it act as a shield for the weaker parts of its body. As the Najarala rubs the protruding carapaces on both its neck and tail together, it creates resonating vibrations in the surrounding air, and by utilizing their Sounders unique acoustic properties, the strength of the sound-waves produces is able to be amplified, allowing for the production of powerful sonic blasts. The shelling covering the Najarala's tail can additionally be detached from its body and launched forward at enemies, where they will stick into the ground. These shells also function as resonating organs, much like its Sounders, and when they resonate with the sympathetic vibration caused by either its roar or the rattling of its shells, the shells will violently shatter, dazing anything that happens to be caught in the blast. While its body is usually fairly bright in coloration, if the monster becomes fatigued the orange of its shells will fade, instead turning a sickly lime. Similarly, its once hard-to-damage Sounders will soften significantly.
Rumored sightings exist of several different color variations of the Najarala. While the existence of these variations is still unconfirmed, if they did exist, it has been theorized these alternative hues may have evolved due to it living in certain habitats with differences in both climate and diet. For example: the rumored cyan individuals may lie around coastal areas with abundant seawater, due to them sharing similar body colors to several marine organisms. Meanwhile, the pale-white individuals could live within cavernous environment with literal to no natural light, while the crimson coloration could live inside volcanic climates. However, it is still unclear what environment that rumored purple variation could live within.
Behavior
Only found within either forested or similarly humid environments, although due to its massive body it prefers not to remain in the open areas of the forest, instead remaining within the densest parts. The Najarala appears to be quite intelligent, with it purposely targeting enemies stunned from its erupting scales. When preying upon small monsters, such as the Slagtoth, it acts as an ambush predator, attacking unsuspecting prey by burrowing underground and emerging them from beneath their feet. Alternatively, it can intercept prey by first scaring them using the loud sounds it produces, before revealing itself and launching its resonating shells before incapacitating them with the subsequent explosions; once its prey is stunned by either the blasts or its own roar, the Najarala wraps its serpentine body around them and constricts them to death, with it often using its paralyzing venom to prevent prey from escaping. Once it begins to coil, a decisive blow to the head is the only way its prey stands a chance of escaping.

The Skeleton Dragon Nakarkos (オストガロア, Osutogaroa) is an Elder Dragon introduced in Monster Hunter Generations.
Summary
Mysterious, blue Cephalopod-like Elder Dragons whose voracious appetites can depopulate entire ecosystems. While able to produce destructive beams of Dragon energy, Nakarkos primarily utilize a sticky mucus produced by their body, which not only ensnare foes, but also allows them to mantle themselves in a protective layer created from the bones of their prey. They are additionally able to use their tentacles along with the skulls of their victims to reproduce their abilities, giving them them the appearance of a frightening multi-headed beast while the main body is buried.

Physiology
The Nakarkos is a large, Cephalopod-like Elder Dragon whose unusual body is covered by a blue hide that, despite its highly elastic nature, is both incredibly strong and highly resistant to tearing, providing the Nakarkos with suitable protection and leading to the material being highly prized. The Nakarkos possesses bright, yellow eyes that seemingly lack any form of pupils, and around its face are four main arms; one pair is held to the side of the Nakarkos' face, while the remaining two—coated in suction cups along their entire length—rest above the head, seemingly to hold up the skull that rests atop it. These "oral arms" are covered in a keratinized brace and constantly ooze a strong adhesive, spawning a constant cloud of blue mucus around the Nakarkos' face. In between its arms, the Nakarkos possesses a sharp beak filled with countless fangs, which aid the Nakarkos in crunching through the bones of its prey. While most of its body is soft, the Nakarkos possesses a hardened component inside of its body, known as a Cuttlebone. Although it is colloquially referred to as a bone, this is a misnomer, with the structure actually being a part of the Nakarkos' shell that has become internalised, forming a pseudo-backbone.
Jutting out of the sides of the Nakarkos' mantle are a pair of proportionally long tentacles that sport suction cups at their tips. These tentacles are typically kept partially buried under the Nakarkos' bone-covered den and can fully retract underground with ease. Decorating the side of these tentacles are several bioluminescent spots; while they usually glow a soft blue, when the Nakarkos grows enraged, they instead take on a deep-red glow. It has been said the two tentacles of the Nakarkos move as if they have a mind of their own.
One of the most prominent features of the Nakarkos is the Radiant Mucus that it produces, responsible for the Elder Dragon's bioluminescence. This mucus can additionally be fired off in large globules from both the Nakarkos' tentacles and from the sides of its body, reminiscent of cannon fire from a ship. This mucus serves an additional purpose, however, as by covering the bones of its prey in the substance, it helps to prevent them from decomposing and can even help to harden them beyond their typical strength. After which, the Nakarkos will proceed to utilize the bones to armor the back of its mantle as well as its tentacles, helping to protect its body from harm. Its mucus is naturally sticky and easily adheres itself to bones, a fact the Nakarkos often weaponizes against its prey by coating them in the viscous mucus, causing them to ensnare themselves with the bones littering its den.
Typically, the Nakarkos will armor the top of its head with the skull of an unknown monster, whose mere presence is enough to frighten and even induce fainting in those who gaze upon it. The back of the Nakarkos is covered in a series of spiny bone fragments that serve to protect the Elder Dragon's rainbow-colored weak spot; the coloration of this weak point is a result of the Nakarkos' nacre. The tentacles of the Nakarkos are typically covered in the vertebrae of other monsters and topped with smaller monster skulls, with the echoing noises these bones produce inducing madness and terror. Nevertheless, these valuable bones are surprisingly easy for blacksmiths to work with. While the true head is hidden, the skulls armoring the tentacles' ends synchronize with the glowing spots along their length, resembling eyes and giving the impression the Nakarkos is a twin-headed, skeletal dragon.
Aside from its production of mucus, the Nakarkos can additionally produce the mysterious Dragon element, although the exact mechanisms behind how the element is generated is still a mystery. The Nakarkos is able to fire it off as small lasers from the ends of its tentacles as well as in the form of one, giant laser from its maw capable of colossal damage. However, this laser takes a long time for the Elder Dragon to prepare and, whilst charging it, the oral arms are unable to secrete as much mucus, leaving the Nakarkos' head more exposed. While charging energy, the underside of the Nakarkos' skull will begin to glow in a brilliant, rainbow visage, with it shifting to a deep-crimson hue when the laser is almost charged.
Behavior
The Nakarkos is naturally a marine creature that lives out in the open ocean. In order to move more efficiently when underwater, the Nakarkos can spray water out of its siphon to propel itself forward like a jet. In order to hunt while out in the ocean, the Nakarkos releases an odorous mucus from its tentacles that lures in small fish towards them. In turn, this leads larger Leviathans to follow, which the Nakarkos then preys upon; it is even known to prey upon the Ceadeus when the Elder Dragon is a juvenile. However, this strategy may result in the Nakarkos getting into fights with larger Leviathans it has also lured in. Despite this, the Nakarkos is still known to wander into more terrestrial environments, with one known individual creating its nest—entitled the Wyvern's End —underneath the Jurassic Frontier. This nest is still connected to the sea, allowing the Nakarkos to venture out into the open water to secure prey.
The Nakarkos exhibits ravenous predatory behavior, with its appetite consequently leading to entire ecosystems being disturbed or depopulated. This behavior even results in the consumption and disappearance of entire human settlements overnight. The Nakarkos has a broad variety of known prey: the Lagiacrus, Uragaan, Brachydios, Glavenus, and even the Rathalos. Due to its highly adhesive qualities, the Elder Dragon typically utilizes its mucus to secure its prey, furthermore, its ability to fire off the mucus like a cannon is believed to be how the Nakarkos is capable of taking down aerial prey, such as Flying Wyverns and even man-made airships. This hunting methodology has lead to the airspaces and areas above the Nakarkos' nest to be referred to as Cursed Skies as a result of the sheer number of both monster and airship disappearances in the region due to the Elder Dragon's voracious behavior. Once its prey has been secured, the Nakarkos will proceed to drag it back to its water-filled nest immediately in order to feast upon it. It typically does not feed on bone, using it instead to armor itself and leaving any left-over bone strewn across the floor of its den, often forming a solid surface able to be walked upon. This near constant consumption of prey is known to result in jewels forming within the Nakarkos' body.
At first, the Nakarkos will typically swim around with its real face hidden, leaving only its two tentacles poking out of the ground, this state is known as its Foraging Form. By utilizing the bones of its prey, the Nakarkos will decorate its tentacles to resemble the faces of other monsters as a form of mimicry. However, once the monster has spotted potential prey, or it needs to fend off potential threats to its territory, it will reveal its true face and enter its Predatory Form. While normally decorated with simple skulls, the Nakarkos can utilize the assorted bones of its prey in offensive ways, decorating its tentacles' tips with the bones of various prey items. It will then utilize the unique physical attributes of its prey, such as the massive chin of the Uragaan, to augment the physical blows from its tentacles. However, loud sounds can disrupt the Nakarkos and cause its tentacles to lose their additional bone weaponry. When the Nakarkos is angered, the plankton in the water of Wyvern's End will respond to that anger and begin to emit a pale blue glow that permeates across the entire nest.

During localization, other proposed names for Nakarkos were:

Rakendros, from the words kraken, hydra, and the Latin word for bone.
Sav’gaddha, from the Hindi words for cadaver and pit.

Lustrous Elder Dragons bearing a resemblance to oceanic life, most recognizable by their cape-like, bioluminescent wings. Physiology
Often referred to as the Abyssal Dragon, the Namielle is a large Elder Dragon endemic to the New World continent that is known for its entrancing and eccentric display of bioluminescence. Much like most Elder Dragons, it sports a pair of large wings and four muscular limbs. Its head is tough and triangular in shape, and it unusually possesses suction cups on the underside of its feet; the specific purpose of this feature is unknown. The Namielle's front limbs have small spines on the outer edges, which are used to discharge electricity.
The Elder Dragon's hide exhibits a variety of bright colors, ranging from the body's dazzling blue and purple hues, to the pink-orange accents that coat its neck fins, horns, and face. The underside of the Namielle's neck—along with its underbelly, arms, and shins—is a light, slate-gray; with the exception of the underbelly, these areas have splotchy, black stripes. The stripes are additionally found on the back of the Namielle's neck and its upper shoulders, and aside from its head, the Namielle's dorsal coloration is almost entirely black. Initial eyewitness reports of the Namielle were conflicting, with some stating the Elder Dragon's skin was discolored, while others described it as being extremely colorful. Due to this, some researchers believed the creature didn't even exist until it was discovered during the investigation of the Old Everwyrm.
Similarly to molluscs, the Elder Dragon’s skin is lined with flexible, fibrous muscle tissue that allows it to subtly alter the shape of the surface layer of its skin. By doing this, the Namielle's skin can dynamically change to absorb and retain large amounts of moisture from the environment. Once enough water is absorbed, the Namielle can turn it into a thick, watery mucus that protects its body from external blows—it is believed that the membranes of its vast, cape-like wings is where this function is at its strongest. The absorption and consumption of water influences the Namielle's ability to generate and store electricity, and the coloration of its hide reflects the its physical state. When dehydrated, the body loses its usual vibrant glow and becomes grayed and drab, whereas when it begins to absorb moisture, its luminescence and coloration becomes brighter. Finally, when the Namielle is charged with electricity, bright electric purples and blues adorn its hide, with a striped pattern appearing on its wings as a warning sign.
The water-like slime that coats its body is not only for defensive purposes, as the Namielle can also create pools of it, either by expelling condensed water jets from its mouth or by simply sliding around. This slime is highly conductive and takes a considerable amount of time to dry out, which the Elder Dragon uses to its advantage. By creating strong currents within these puddles, it is able to hinder the movements of its foes as well as gives itself time to prepare its most devastating weapon. Within the Namielle's body is an organ that generates and stores electricity; while it takes a long time to generate enough electricity, once it is charged up, the Namielle can release powerful electric currents from its wings and front limbs. As the Namielle pumps electricity into the pools of water it has created, the heat emitted from the discharge evaporates the water and causes a violent burst of steam. Although the nature of its power-generating organ is unknown, considering that the whiskers grant Thunder element properties when used in armor and weapon crafting, it is believed the whiskers may be somehow related.
Perhaps the most striking feature of the Namielle, outside of its ability to manipulate both water and lightning, is its bioluminescence. Its whiskers, wing membranes, the sides of its body, and its tail are all lined with flickering, luminescent markings. Contrasting this vibrancy is the jet-black coloration that covers the entirety of its back, this contrast suggests the Namielle uses a method of camouflage called counter-illumination; when seen from below, the Namielle's luminescence would allow it to blend in with the light from above. The source of this luminescence was once thought to be a result of the power-generating organ inside its body, although it was later discovered to be emitted by the dragon itself. The Namielle's bioluminescence may also be used to show dominance or for courtship, however, that is mere speculation. Interestingly, the Namielle is most closely related to the Chameleos, which shares similar bioluminescent properties.
Behavior
As an Elder Dragon, the appearance of the Namielle is paired with dark skies and violent storms, not unlike those attributed to the Kirin. It lives exclusively in the Coral Highlands and the Guiding Lands, and is typically spotted in the highest altitudes of the former, preferring to make its nest on the tallest coral plateaus. Generally, it is rather docile by the standards of Elder Dragons, and won't retaliate unless provoked or threatened.
The Elder Dragon's diet remains a mystery, as no one has ever observed its eating habits. However, the arrangement of its long and sharp, needle-like teeth suggest it to be either an obligate carnivore, or an omnivore that has a more carnivorous diet. The Namielle's counter-illumination would allow it to ambush prey from above, which supports the theory of it being primarily carnivorous. One researcher theorizes it may catch fish while drinking water, or that it absorbs the minerals from the water, although it is unlikely the Namielle would be able to maintain its physique on minerals alone.

Physiology
Cloaked in a veil of blackened fur, the Nargacuga is a Flying Wyvern that has evolved to inhabit forests with thick canopies and vegetation. Its body is covered in jet-black fur that grows atop scales uniquely suited for deflecting attacks, they are sturdy and tough whilst being surprisingly lightweight and smooth to the touch. The fur itself is made of keratin and is quite resilient; although it appears fluffy, the fur is actually quite stiff and hard. This curious adaptation serves multiple purposes: insulation, camouflage, and waterproofing, the latter of which evolved specifically to protect the Nargacuga from the heat and humidity of its jungle habitats. The Nargacuga's pitch-black glossy fur protects it from the fangs and claws of other monsters, and similarly to the armored shell of the Gore Magala, it absorbs all light.
Despite being rather hard, the Nargacuga’s pelt is described as having a beautiful and smooth texture, its dark-blue sheen making it a popular material for clothing and weaponry. As part of their culture, an indigenous tribe located in the Jungle made materials harvested from the Nargacuga part of their culture. They crafted armor from the scales and fur of the wyvern, in turn allowing them to utilize hunting techniques like that of the Nargacuga itself. After taking note of the outfits worn by the tribe, artisans from the Schrade region visited their villages in hopes of learning how to properly harvest materials from the Nargacuga.
While most of its body is densely covered in fur, thick scales protect its naked front limbs; each arm possesses three toes and two long phalanges that make up the wings. Curiously, the wings are not built for flight, having instead evolved into blade-like structures meant for striking down and slicing prey. The wings' taut membrane is attached to protrusions located on the elbow, as well as the blade-like phalanges. When the wings are in a folded position, the phalanges overlap each other, with the smaller blade remaining hidden underneath the wing membrane. The scales covering the Nargacuga's razor-sharp Cutwings are especially hard, as it uses them like swords to cut down prey with one swing. While the wings have evolved to allow the wyvern to cleave prey in half, it is also believed the Nargacuga's wings may have additionally evolved to allow the beast to push through dense foliage. As such, its highly developed forelimbs allow it to sprint at incredible speeds and leap long distances, using its tail as a rudder for steering.
The Nargacuga's huge muscular tail is its deadliest weapon; it is incredibly dexterous and extremely long, encompassing half of the monster's total length. The tip of the Nargacuga's tail is covered by a bouquet of thorny, spiky scales that can be dislodged from the tail with alarming accuracy in the form of projectile attacks. The tail spikes themselves are very sharp, yet unexpectedly heavy. Additionally, they are able to retract into a folded position alongside the tail to avoid getting caught on branches as the Nargacuga moves through its dense environment. Furthermore, the Nargacuga can whip its tail around to bash enemies and has a particularly deadly ability to slam its tail down with incredible power; the tail's flexibility deceptively extends the reach of the strike, typically resulting in instant death for its foes. Due to the sheer size and nature of the tail, it could be mistaken for a weapon when separated from the body. The strength and flexibility of the Nargacuga's tail makes it ideal for use as a crafting material.
The Nargacuga's head features a hardened upper jaw resembling a beak. Its teeth, which are mostly molars aside from the prominent canines at the front of the mouth, are small and incredibly sharp. They are built specifically for cutting and tearing rather than chewing, their jagged placement providing ancillary support in this regard. To offset its poor visual acuity, the Nargacuga's hearing is exceptionally well-developed, aiding it in its nocturnal hunting activity. However, this consequently makes it particularly vulnerable to sudden loud noises, such as those produced by Sonic Bombs.
The bone marrow of the Nargacuga is lightweight—lending to the monster’s agility—and difficult to properly harvest due to its delicate nature. The brain stem similarly is extremely difficult to harvest as well as craft with due to causing excruciating pain upon a mere touch.
Behavior
The Nargacuga is commonly cited as being a nocturnal creature. Owed to its acute hearing and jet-black fur that blends its form into the shadows, the Nargacuga is specially adapted to ambush prey in total darkness. It stalks unsuspecting prey before striking them with deadly precision, often cleaving smaller monsters with a single blow of its tail. Yet, despite being a specialized nocturnal hunter, the Nargacuga located in the New World has been reported to be active even during the day. Found in the Ancient Forest, the New World Nargacuga has been observed performing a regular routine. During the day, the Nargacuga would primarily wander around the western and northern portions of the locale, usually hunting Mernos or sunbathing. Whereas at night, it notably occupied the southern and eastern regions, prowling in search of Aptonoth. During daytime activities, the Nargacuga unsurprisingly prefers to stay under the shaded areas of the forest.
Occasionally, the Nargacuga has been documented vibrating its wings; while the reason for this particular behavior is unknown, it is theorized this is a form of echolocation. By using the sound reflected off nearby objects, the Nargacuga would be able to pinpoint the location of its prey even in total darkness, subsequently it is believed the Nargacuga's eyesight is poor. If the Nargacuga's prey is small, the wyvern devours it on the spot. If its victim is larger however, the Nargacuga transports the carcass into the treetops in portions, where the pieces are then feasted on.
Its nocturnal adaptations render it vulnerable to bright lights, which irritate the wyvern greatly. Hunters attempting to stun the Nargacuga with a Flash Bomb are often met with a flurry of aggressive attacks from the monster as it blindly strikes in a fit of rage. The usage of both Flash Bombs and Sonic Bombs can cause the Nargacuga to grow enraged, causing the thin skin around its eyes and ears to become bloodshot. In this state, caused by agitation or excitement, the Nargacuga's attacks become faster, more powerful, and the spikes located on its tail are constantly bristled.
