Main article: Nargacuga (Music)
"Red Glare in the Darkness", previously known as "Red Afterglow Trailing in the Darkness", is Nargacuga's theme.
Monster Hunter Freedom Unite
Nargacuga was originally pitched by the Monster Hunter Freedom Unite Planning Team and the design process was later handed off to Yuya Tokuda personally, who worked on it under the supervision of Yasunori Ichinose, Shintaro Kojima and Ryozo Tsujimoto. It was initially conceptualized as a thunder-element monster that would cause electric flashes whenever it lept. The glowing eyes and the light trails they produce were suggested by Tsujimoto. Due to Monster Hunter Freedom Unite having a very short production period, the initial design process for Nargacuga was quite fast and thus complex elemental abilities were ultimately discarded in favor of a simpler gameplay idea: Reusing the skeleton of the Tigrex, the team sought to create a related monster that would use its body in unexpected ways. This eventually led to the concept of a ninja-like monster that didn't charge directly at players, but rather circled them to confuse them before pouncing in for the kill.
Realizing this idea proved to be quite challenging for the team however. The first Nargacuga prototype was indeed fast and able to jump around players with impressive agility, but it was also an extremely frustrating enemy to fight. Tokuda identified the problem as one of visual communication: From the player's perspective, most of the prototype Nargacuga's attacks looked almost identical, as many of them involved a pounce followed by some kind of physical attack. Additionally, the idea of the monster confusing players by circling around them worked too well, as it would often leap out of the game's field of view and attack from an unseen angle. These aspects combined to make the prototype Nargacuga feel almost random in its behavior, as if it was simply throwing attacks out at the player with no rhythm or pattern. To fix this, Tokuda suggested giving the Nargacuga a set pattern of attacks centering around an ultimate attack. Specifically, he recommended that the monster's combat revolve around it starting with smaller, more focused attacks and then employing progressively larger moves, working its way up to its most powerful move - a massive tail slam with a deceptively long range. Through this change, players could gradually feel out the patterns of the Nargacuga and adapt, leading to a fight that would reward positioning and advanced strategizing.
The creation of the Nargacuga was the team's first experience with making a fast and agile monster, and both Kaname Fujioka and Tokuda consider it a turning point for the series, as it opened them up to the idea of making more action-oriented gameplay scenarios. It was also the first monster that forced Fujioka himself to employ the infamous "Monster Hunter Claw Grip" to beat it during testing. Due to the extremely short production period and fast design approval, only very few pieces of concept art were created for Nargacuga. The name was chosen as a reference to both Naga - a race of mythological snake-human hybrids - and cougars.
Monster Hunter 3 Ultimate
As the development worked on Monster Hunter 3 Ultimate and added Nargacuga into the game, Tokuda noticed that the monster had somehow become extremely easy to beat. After some testing, it became clear that the reason for this was the existence of the Target Camera feature, which allowed players to instantly turn towards their targeted monster at a press of a button. This mechanic inadvertently negated the main threat of the Nargacuga, rendering it much weaker than it had been in previous games. Thus, the team made some adjustments to compensate for this, giving Nargacuga more aggressive tracking, increased speed and trickier jump angles.

The Thunder God Dragon Narwa the Allmother (百竜ノ淵源ナルハタタヒメ, Hyaku Ryu no Engen Naruhatatahime) is an Elder Dragon introduced in Monster Hunter Rise.
It is a Variant of the Thunder Serpent Narwa.
Summary
The empowered form taken by the Thunder Serpent Narwa after consuming the lifeforce of its mate, the Wind Serpent Ibushi, as a last resort in their mating cycle. Now dyed in brilliant purple and pink, Narwa inherits Ibushi's power over wind and empowers their control over lightning, granting them immense strength that they use to eliminate all potential threats to their future progeny.

Monster Hunter Rise: Added in Version 3.0, Narwa the Allmother is fought as the final boss of the story in the 7★ Urgent Quest The Allmother, initially appearing as Thunder Serpent Narwa before devouring Wind Serpent Ibushi in the second half of the quest and transforming into the Allmother. The quest will be added to the list of Hub Quests once it is cleared for the first time. Following its first defeat, the Thunder Serpent Narwa responsible for the most recent Rampage managed to recover and meet Wind Serpent Ibushi at the Coral Palace, where the two made a nest and began courting in preparation for a new brood. Kamura tracks down the pair and mortally wounds Ibushi, causing Narwa to devour its lifeforce and turn into the Allmother in an attempt to eliminate the threat. Through the efforts of the Fierce Flame of Kamura and the intervention of a passing Magnamalo, Narwa is slain and the threat of the Rampage is dispelled.

Physiology
The Narwa the Allmother is a rare empowered Variant of the Thunder Serpent Narwa, referring to a form she only assumes after consuming her mate during the mating cycle and absorbing his "lifeforce" in a desperate attempt to protect her young from a threat. While she bears a strong resemblance to her normal self, her hide has become dark-purple, while her tentacles and Sparksacs are now considerably longer and a bright, bluish-purple in color. Many of the organs remain yellow at their base, while the crest of tentacles atop her head is a bright, pinkish-purple instead. The large sac on her belly now glows far brighter and turns partially see-through, with the Narwa's eggs now being visible within as eight translucent orbs. Unlike her original state, the Narwa the Allmother's eyes will turn bright red when she grows enraged.
As a result of consuming the Wind Serpent Ibushi's body fluids, the degenerated Windsacs and gills on the Narwa's body become reactivated, allowing her to inherit her mate's command over wind whilst drastically increasing her own electricity generation. She is able to use the Ibushi's wind to emulate the vast majority of his abilities with greater potency, primarily in the form of violent blasts and updrafts of wind, and can use the wind in conjunction with enhanced electric attacks wielded with far greater potency and range. Additionally, the Narwa the Allmother's control over electromagnetism is greatly enhanced, allowing her to simultaneously draw in foes while lifting and throwing massive objects—such as Dragonators —with no visible exertion. Further, the Ibushi's body fluids rapidly accelerate the growth of the Narwa's fertilized eggs, likened to an "explosive activation" of their vitality.
Deep within her body, the Variant Elder Dragon is said to grow a great treasure.
Behavior
The Narwa the Allmother is driven by maternal instinct at facing a direct threat to her offspring and the interruption of her imminent spawning. As a result, she devotes all her effort towards destroying anything that could be perceived as a threat to her next generation, displaying extreme aggression far beyond her original state.
The Narwa the Allmother is considered a peerless force within whichever ecosystem she chooses to inhabit, residing above the notions of territorial conflicts and rivals. However, historical records nonetheless suggest that the emergence of the Allmother has drastic effects on the surrounding environments, prompting other monsters and even Elder Dragons to move towards her place of appearance and attack her for unclear reasons.
Music
Main article: Narwa the Allmother (Music)
"The Allmother" is Narwa the Allmother's theme. This theme consists of both vocalists for Wind Serpent Ibushi's and Thunder Serpent Narwa's themes.
Development
The team had decided from the beginning to create both Thunder Serpent Narwa and Narwa the Allmother, so the two needed to have clear gameplay differences. Thunder Serpent Narwa was designed to focus more on gimmicks and use of gameplay mechanics, while Narwa the Allmother was chosen to instead represent a straightforward, back-and-forth battle.

Physiology
The Nergigante is a brutish, predominantly black Elder Dragon characterized by the vast amount of thorns sprouting from its muscular frame, from which extend six limbs: two forelegs, two hindlegs, and a pair of wings. Although the thick hide covering its top is primarily dark, the undersides of its wings and body are colored an assortment of vivid orange, pink, and purple shades patterned with dark speckles. The Nergigante's forelegs are thick and powerful, and the dragon is able to move with remarkable agility despite its size. On the underside of the Nergigante's feet and hands are paw pads, with the latter additionally sporting opposable thumbs. Its large fangs always jut out of its mouth, and atop its head it sports a twisting pair of pale, black-tipped horns, both of which are believed to symbolize its immense power. While the length of the Nergigante's tail is covered with noticeably fewer spikes than the rest of its form, it ends in a thick cluster and is tipped with a singular, large spike.
The Nergigante's tough and dark spikes grow from its scales, with one individual encountered by the Research Commission being found to have approximately 1,800 spikes adorning its entire body. The thickness of each spike is determined by how many scales contribute to its growth: a single scale or a small group developing into a spike will produce one that is thin, whereas a large cluster of scales fusing together to form a spike will result in a single large and thick spine. Spike growth is localized around certain points of the Nergigante's body, namely the neck, back, wing bends, forelegs, and tail tip. Alongside providing protection as a suit of armor, the areas these spikes grow in are the most likely to inflict severe damage to opponents during combat. In contrast to these dense clusters, areas like the underside of the neck lack any spikes despite possessing scales that can potentially develop into spikes, allowing for the Nergigante to remain agile and conserve energy. The distribution of spikes throughout the body follows this rationale, enabling it to be separated into three distinct areas: hyper regenerative areas that exhibit superior growth and possess many spikes, areas displaying standard growth that surround the hyper regenerative areas and possess some spikes, and other areas of its exterior that are adorned by very few spikes.
If the Nergigante has its spikes destroyed, or otherwise suffers a sufficient amount of damage, a regenerative mechanism within its body will be activate, upon which the cells will begin to divide at astonishing speed, and within seconds of the regeneration starting the Nergigante will have healed its wounds and replaced any broken spikes with a new set, with any newly formed spikes taking on a pale-white, milky tone. Pliable and highly susceptible to breaking, freshly regrown spikes are several dozen centimeters long, with them gradually growing stronger and darker as they harden through the special cells they are formed from. While the exact mechanism behind this process remains unclear, it is theorized that when elements on the spikes' surface undergo exposure to the surrounding air, they oxidise and cause the formation of an enamel-like oxide coating over each spike, turning their spikes black. This significantly increases the Nergigante's power and causes any strikes from Hunters to be deflected.
The Nergigante does not want its spikes to grow to their full length however, as a fully hardened set of black spikes can sometimes make it difficult for it to move, which in turn leads it to adjust the spikes by intentionally breaking them. As such, on account of the Nergigante's reckless, self-destructive strength and its regenerative powers, during battle it can unleash barrages of spikes, both damaging itself and shedding unwanted spikes, with any resulting wounds being small enough that it pays them no mind. This behavior results in a constant cycle of destruction and regrowth with the spikes constantly growing back even stronger than the previous set, continually improving its thorny armor.
However, upon sensing its life is finally at risk, the Nergigante may display the terrifying ability to instantly harden all of the spikes on its body once over half of them have already hardened. In this steeled state that can only be maintained temporarily, the Nergigante may perform a full-body tackle. Known as Heaven's Ruin and preceded by a guttural roar that instills fear into its prey, this divebomb has the Nergigante take to the air before violently throwing its entire being into ending the life of its prey, the impact alone shattering every single set of spikes and sending them hurling in all directions. The destructive power of this blitz is both incomparable to any other attack the Nergigante is capable of, and why the people of Astera bestowed it the title of Eater of Elders. Due to it breaking its spikes, this attack also serves as a method for the Nergigante to manage its occasionally restrictive spikes.
The energy expense of regrowing and hardening new sets of spikes is extraordinarily costly for the Nergigante, thus it constantly seeks high sources of energy to feed upon. Despite this exceptional price however, it has been observed that even after growing exhausted during a prolonged battle, the Nergigante will somehow grow even more ferocious and begin to fight with greater intensity and aggression, flailing its powerful forelimbs as if it were a demon bent on destruction. In this ruthless state, the Nergigante unlocks all the stored energy within its body, circulating the power of its Elder Dragon prey throughout its entire body in a single burst and elevating its already monstrous strength. By consequence of it showing absolutely zero concern for itself, people have come to call this energy-intensive tactic the Nergigante's Ruinous Impulse.
Behavior
Given the name of "Nergigante" by the Commander and the rest of the First Fleet when it had appeared long ago, and nicknamed the Extinction Dragon due to its relentless destructiveness without any regard for itself, the Nergigante is said to appear wherever an Elder Dragon is around, as if it were chasing it. By studying the Nergigante's tracks provided by the Research Commission's Star Hunter, following traces of its battle and feeding activity, as well as analyzing left behind carcasses, the Ecological Research Team was able to deduce that the Nergigante preys upon Elder Dragons. This, alongside the logic defying ecology of the Nergigante that had it relentlessly target the Zorah Magdaros, is what led it to be designated as an Elder Dragon. Although, with it showing no regard for itself as it eliminates everything that crosses it path of destruction, some wonder whether it is in actuality a demon.
Due to the vast quantity of energy needed to cover the exceptional cost of its regenerative ability, the Nergigante is constantly on the prowl for sources of highly pure bioenergy to feed upon. Found within the bodies of other monsters, the purity of this energy is directly proportional to the strength of a monster, resulting in more powerful monsters concealing purer and higher yields. While the Nergigante will readily prey on any living creature, its craving for energy with a higher potency has it primarily hunting powerful monsters, such as Elder Dragons. As the regenerative ability directly stems from the energy the Nergigante has fed upon, it is believed that purer energy enhances the capacity of this ability. The Nergigante has been known to travel across many regions in its search for energy, as well as to have crossed the ocean between the Old World and New World as it takes advantage of the Elder Crossing. Even among the few Elder Dragons who succeed in crossing to the New World, they remain under threat of being hunted by the Nergigante yet. Its arrival in the habitats of other Elder Dragons has been known to cause them to flee from the area in fear, consequently causing the Elder Dragons to invade regions they do not typically inhabit.
The Nergigante's belligerent nature is beyond comparison, even when measured against predators of the Old World vicious enough to wipe out entire species. It relentlessly chases after Elder Dragons, and even if faced against the deceptively heavy Kushala Daora, it will overpower and haphazardly fling its prey around without a second thought. Despite the Nergigante frequently being seen battling in the wide-open area's of the Elder's Recess, it is not native to the New World and the Elder's Recess is not its true lair, as such it is not known what it has been doing in the New World since it had first arrived. While it is theorized it may feed on younger Elder Dragons to sustain itself between each Elder Crossing, or perhaps that it simply hibernates until the next migration, no answer has been unveiled yet.
Reproduction
While the vast energy sought by the Nergigante is primarily used to regrow its spikes, there is a hypothesis that has emerged proposing the energy may additionally be instrumental in reproduction. When researchers exposed a spike to nutrients, it displayed strong signs of life for a brief moment and egg cells within it had began to divide. This experiment led the Ecological Research Center to propose that the Nergigante may be born directly from its spikes. Thus, the theory explains that the spikes may utilize a surplus of highly pure energy that has been absorbed into the body to change the special cells its spikes grown from into germ cells. Then, once shed, these spikes will grow into a genetic clone of its parent. However, since no one has actually witnessed this reproductive process, no definitive evidence has been obtained thus far and the specific mechanism remains unknown.
Despite the implausible nature of this method, researchers point to the Nergigante that was trailing an elderly Zorah Magdaros during the Research Commission's investigation into the Elder Crossing as evidence for the hypothesis, as if it were only seeking energy to promote spike regrowth, there were many other options of prey available to it. However, that particular Nergigante had instead showcased a strong attachment to the Zorah Magdaros and was repeatedly sighted alongside the mountainous Elder Dragon. If it was following the Zorah Magdaros due to needing extensive amounts of energy, then it is clear why it had chosen the giant Elder Dragon as its target, as the aged Zorah Magdaros had likely accumulated a vast amount of bioenergy over its life, the purity and strength of which was far greater than that of any other Elder Dragon's.
Elder Crossing
The Research Commission only recently had the opportunity to thoroughly research the Nergigante, as unlike many other Elder Dragons who have a long history of legends, sightings, or potential records, the oldest reports of it occurred only 30 years prior to the Fifth Fleet's arrival to the New World. During the Second Fleet's voyage to the New World, it had attacked a Teostra as it was attempting to perform the crossing, and when the Second Fleet had safely arrived, the Admiral and his Palico had sighted it for the first time. Together they fought the at the time unknown monster, although they were unable to harm it and were ultimately defeated. The Admiral later took a team out in the field in an attempt to track down and investigate the monster he had encountered, yet no trace could be found. Two more decades would pass until the next reports of the Nergigante would surface, where unfamiliar thorns were discovered and a strange black shadow was described. It would not be until the Fifth Fleet arrived in the New World that it began to show itself more frequently.
Around the same time the Research Commission had sent a convoy to the Wildspire Waste to investigate a giant slag left behind by the Zorah Magdaros they were tracking, strange black thorns were again found embedded in the ground as well as the corpse of a Barroth. Alongside these mysterious tracks, recognised by the Fourth Fleet to be similar to those from 10 years ago, rumors began to spread of a mysterious black, shadowy creature roaming in the field. Shortly after, during the Commission's bold attempt to capture the Zorah Magdaros, the Nergigante would appear suddenly to interrupt the operation and result in its failure, before once again vanishing. Up until this moment, there were only three members of the Commission who had seen the Elder Dragon prior: the Admiral, the Meowscular Chef, and the Huntsman. The same Nergigante then later showed itself once more alongside the Zorah Magdaros during a second large scale operation by the Research Commission, although its arrival was anticipated and the Elder Dragon was promptly repelled by the Fifth Fleet.
Having failed to feed on the Zorah Magdaros' energy, the Nergigante invaded the Elder's Recess in an attempt to prey upon the Elder Dragons there, however this too would end in failure. Through its frustration, it drove out the native Gajalaka from their home in the depths of the Recess and claimed the area as its lair. Forced to relocate after having been robbed of their home, the Gajalaka hold a grudge against the Elder Dragon and view it as their arch-enemy, with the tribe even facing off against it in combat. The Nergigante's presence in the Elder's Recess turned the Elder's Dragon's home into a hunting ground and synthetically sped up their activity, causing them to expand their territory to other regions of the continent. The effects of this could be seen in both the Kushala Daora and Teostra, who had fled to the Ancient Forest and Wildspire Waste respectively. Through its previous sightings coinciding with the Elder Crossing, as well as the Elder Dragons' sudden erratic behavior following its arrival in the Elder's Recess, the Research Commission was able to deduce the Nergigante had been taking advantage of the migratory event to feed on Elder Dragons containing high yields of pure energy in their bodies. It is even thought that, urged on by its desire for pure bioenergy, it headed towards the Elder's Recess to prey upon a particular cocooned entity.
Music
Main article: Nergigante (Music)
"Even Elder Dragons Tremble" is Nergigante's theme. Like many Flagship Monsters, it contains a motif of its debut game's main theme, in this case, World 's " Stars at Our Backs ". "World's End" is its Arch-Tempered theme, being a remix of the original theme with additional motifs from "Stars at Our Backs".
When slain in the main Assignment in World, "Quest Complete! (Main Theme version)" plays as the Quest Complete theme.
Development
The two main Monsters of Monster Hunter: World' s story - Zorah Magdaros and Xeno'jiiva - are both big setpiece battles that are also deeply tied to the stories' mystery, so the development team felt that they needed another main Monster that could be fought in regular environments. They also had the other Elder Dragons such as Kushala Daora already in the game, so for this monster, they wanted it to have no element and instead be a brutal brawler that pressured the player through sheer physicality. Thus, the idea of Nergigante was born.
The key phrase for its design was "destruction and rebirth", and the designers initially played around with various creepy ideas, including a monster with multiple faces. In its initial concept arts, there was even an iteration of Nergigante with heavily curved claws and spikes, paired with a splitting jaw, ideas similar to Vaal Hazak. This concept was then simplified into the Nergigante spikes - they grow and break, over and over, hence destruction and rebirth. This key phrase also inspired the idea of asexual reproduction.

Physiology
The Nerscylla is a large Temnoceran covered in a pale-white shell covered in brown protrusions, with parts of its shell—notably its chelicerae, claws and the perimeter of its body and abdomen—being colored a vibrant orange instead. Its lightweight shell aids its swift movements, while the aposematic coloration serves to warn potential predators of the Nerscylla's various toxins. Some thick parts of its shelling are even known to display iridescent qualities.
The Nerscylla possesses six limbs, four of which are used for walking, with the tips of these legs being a dark brown and covered by a thin layer of dull yellow hair. These limbs are adapted to allow the Nerscylla to cling to the underside of both canopies and its own webs, allowing it to ambush targets from above. Meanwhile the frontmost pair of limbs are instead fashioned into a pair of light, hook-shaped, scythe-like claws covered in several smaller spikes on their underside, specialized to deliver quick strikes,. with prey almost never surviving a direct blow from one. However, the claws of the Nerscylla are susceptible to being chipped, or even broken off entirely.
The Nerscylla possesses four pairs of eyes that typically shine a bright cyan, however, they shift to a red glow when the it grows angered, alongside the underside of its abdomen. Instead of jaws, the Nerscylla has a pair of chelicerae that are typically kept folded up against the head. When needed, it will extend them to several times their resting length before delivering a powerful bite, typically done to finish off whatever the Nerscylla was hunting. The chelicerae of the Nerscylla are lined with several small spikes on their interior and are highly venomous, delivering a potent toxin into anything caught between them. As a result. they require extreme care when being handled.
The large bulbous abdomen of the Nerscylla makes up over half of the monster's entire body; it is mottled with a mixture of off-white and brown, and ends with a stinger capable of injecting a sleep inducing toxin into its prey. However, in certain individuals, this stinger instead delivers the same venom that is administered by the chelicerae. The Nerscylla is additionally able to produce webbing inside of its body, with the thread being released from the tip of its abdomen as well. This string can be shot out as globules of sticky web projectiles to ensnare and immobilize its prey, or fired as a long strand the Temnoceran may use to pull itself forward or swing from a cavern's ceiling. Once its target is ensnared in webbing, the Nerscylla can use its spiked claws to reel in its target towards itself before retaliating with a lethal strike.
Behavior
Known as the Shadow Spider, the Nerscylla is most well known for its ability to spin webs, allowing it to weave elaborate nests across the territories in which it inhabits, often troubling the local ecosystem by doing so. In one such case, a single individual completely halted the production output and work ethic of the Troverians by blocking the entire lava flow of the Volcanic Hollow as a result of building its nest. In the Eastlands, young Nerscylla Hatchlings will typically stick around these constructed nests, attacking anything that intrudes upon them in large swarms.
What has been discovered through researching the Nerscylla's is that its main prey is the Gypceros; once its prey is spotted, the Temnoceran will wrap the Gypceros in its webbing, before leaping atop its target in an attempt to topple it to the ground. Once its target is bound within webbing the Nerscylla will typically attempt to put them to sleep using its stinger, with it being known to inspect its prey up close afterwards, seemingly to ascertain whether its target is truly asleep. If the capture attempt is successful, the Nerscylla will bring its prey back to its web. However, instead of merely eating its quarry, the Nerscylla will instead proceed to skin its target alive, hanging the remaining flayed carcass from the ceiling of its nest. When the monster does decide to eat its captured prey, it will inject specialized digestive fluids into the body of the Gypceros, which will pre-digest its meal and allow it to suck up whatever remains.
After harvesting the skin of the captured Gypceros, the Nerscylla will fashion the hide into a protective covering for its body, a habit it is infamous for. It is believed the Nerscylla does this to compensate for its body being naturally weak to the Thunder Element, with the Gypceros' Rubbery Hide providing a layer of natural insulation that completely nullifies the element; however, the draped hide is itself notably weak to fire. This cloak serves a secondary purpose of disguising the usually white Temnoceran into the dark caves it inhabits. Even after being flayed, the Gypceros hide retains some of the wyvern's poison inside it, causing the toxin to drip from the hide as the Nerscylla hangs upside-down. Eventually, this poison begins to crystallize as a set of large purple thorns adorning the Nerscylla's back. These crystals aid the Nerscylla whilst it is hanging from the roof of its nest by constantly dripping poison below on any intruders that pass by underneath. The dorsal spikes, which doubly act as Poison Sacs for the Nerscylla, demand the utmost care when being handled due to their high concentration of poison, and although sharp enough to serve as weapons while it swings, they are prized for their lethal toxins above all else. Even once the rubbery hide shrouding its back has been broken off, small remnants of the poison spikes can be found atop the Nerscylla's shelling.
While the Nerscylla found within the Sunken Hollow, Primal Forest, Marshlands, and the Eastlands primarily makes use of the hide of the Gypceros, it has been speculated that the Temnoceran may utilize the hide of other monsters in different habitats if the Gypceros is less common.

Physiology
The Nibelsnarf is a flat and wide Leviathan, with a wide disk-like upper shell sitting on top of a stubby body fronted by an enormous head with an equally massive maw. At the back end, the body tapers out into a thin and long tail that drives the Leviathan through the sand. Notably, the eyes sit on the top of the head and gaze perpetually upwards. Its eyes are not very well developed, however, and instead act as an accompaniment to the Nibelsnarf's excellent hearing.
The shell of the Nibelsnarf is extremely resistant due to the various horn-like growths that cover it, improving its defensive properties and making it difficult to forge, however, the resulting unique gear is worth the effort. Similarly, despite its versatility, the Nibelsnarf's heavy scalp is difficult to be worked with and must have its useful parts carefully cut out. The shell ridges on the face can be folded over the Nibelsnarf's eyes when diving and attacking to protect them from major sand irritation. Meanwhile, the underside is covered in bright and colorful elastic hide that has been honed by exposure to sand and boasts great strength; it is often used as armor lining. When the Nibelsnarf exposes its belly, the ventral coloration serves to intimidate potential foes.
A notable feature of the Leviathan is its massive head, the scalp of which is believed to hold various organs. This includes an advanced sand filtering system: the prominent uvula at the back of the throat can be used to seal off the esophagus, preventing sand from entering the digestive tract. Simultaneously, the inside of the mouth is line with layers of strainer-like tissue that filters sand and funnels it through special canals on the sides of the head. These funnels eventually lead to a pair of red gills at the back of the head, which then expel the sand in large bursts. As the gills sift through the sand before expelling it, they catch small nutrient particles as a bonus. When born, the Nibelsnarf dwells in water and respirates through its gills alone, and when it grows it develops lungs as well as the ability to traverse onto land. As part of its adaptations to sand dwelling, the Nibelsnarf's nose is shaped like cluster of sponge and is specialised to breathe in sand. When out of the sand, this nose struggles to maintain consistent breathing and the gills extend to compensate, and when enraged, the nose expands and starts puffing out large clouds of sand.
The body of the Nibelsnarf is known to produce a special fluid that aids in retaining water and remaining hydrated in the desert; when applied to equipment, it boosts both performance and style. Meanwhile, the Nibelsnarf's four blue limbs are stocky and strong, ending in five fingers with gray claws perfectly adapted to burrow through the sand. These claws make for an ideal material to craft superior equipment parts.
Behavior
The Nibelsnarf hunts by submerging itself in sand and camouflaging as a sand dune, waiting for prey to come near; its primary sources of food appear to be the Rhenoplos and Apceros. It senses its surroundings through its excellent hearing, although will sometimes poke out its eyes to roughly judge the distance between itself and its prey. The Nibelsnarf usually waits for its prey to be occupied by another action, such as a territorial clash, and once its prey is in range, it leaps out of the sand and attempts to swallow them whole, charging out with its maw agape and expelling sand en masse from the its back. However, when leaping out like this, the Nibelsnarf is completely oblivious as to what is in its path as it charges due to the position of its eyes. This factor has been exploited by Hunters fighting it who have learnt to plant explosives in the path of the Nibelsnarf that then get mindlessly swallowed up and explode within the Leviathan, leaving it reeling and vulnerable to getting fished up.
Development
Nibelsnarf cemented itself as the favorite child of Monster Hunter Portable 3rd monster designer Koki Kinoshita due to being the first design he got approved.
When asked what Kinoshita focused on when designing Nibelsnarf, he drew attention to the monster's uvula. He notes that the throat is a heart valve-like organ that protects it from swallowing sand, with it being reproduced on the model and in motion should one look closely. The gills positioned behind its ears were placed so sand flows over them and passes through the tube shaped carapace on its back, which is then expelled from these structures.
The stomach area's intense colors are said to have been designed as such to startle players when it's pulled out of the sand. This idea was suggested by the movement director and Kinoshita says the team was happy to incorporate it. He reports the design was completed in a way that made everyone excited.

In addition to the dander used to disorient their prey, which can be alternatively fired off as golden blades, they can utilize specialized scales on their body to reflect light around them, allowing them to turn almost completely invisible. Special permission is required by Hunters in order to hunt this Deviant.

Physiology
Being a Deviant of the Malfestio, the Nightcloak Malfestio generally displays the same physiology as its regular kin. Its most notable distinctive trait is the altered color of the wing feathers, which are a deep-red color rather than the blue seen in the regular variety. This Deviant additionally appears to grow more feathers on average compared to the common Malfestio, and both the wings and tail are slightly longer. Beyond superficial differences, however, the Nightcloak Malfestio sports a particular trait that sets it apart from others of its species. While the regular Malfestio possesses scattered scales in its feather coat that produce a disorienting dander, the Nightcloak Malfestio produces an extreme abundance of said scales, to the point where each individual feather is nearly completely coated with them. Due to the presence of these scales, it has been noted that the feathers of the Nightcloak Malfestio subsequently change color based on the angle they are observed from.
In addition, the Nightcloak Malfestio also produces a secondary type of scale, one that grows only on its head. These special scales are able to refract light in such a way that they can temporarily render anything they cover invisible. By scattering these refracting scales around its body, the Nightcloak Malfestio can briefly turn invisible and attack enemies unseen, earning the Deviant its moniker of Nightcloak. However, this invisibility may be disrupted by using the light of a Flash Bomb to reveal the wyvern's form. As well, it can be severely crippled by sufficiently damaging the Nightcloak Malfestio's head, thus impeding the production of its refracting scales.
It is believed the Nightcloak Malfestio is an evolved form of the Malfestio that has adapted to natural selection. Specifically, the Nightcloak Malfestio emerges when a Malfestio population finds itself in a particularly harsh environment in which their natural abilities do not suffice to ensure survival. While many individuals perish at the hands of predators, those Malfestio who are able to grow and adapt may develop their scale production to such a level that they manifest the ability to create light-refracting scales, thus becoming a Nightcloak Malfestio.
Behavior
Owing to its harsh habitat, the Nightcloak Malfestio is an aggressive and territorial monster, as well as a cunning and dexterous fighter. The Nightcloak Malfestio has been known to be able to steal items from Hunters with its large, hand-shaped tail and, rather than simply spreading its scale's powder, it has been observed launching feathers covered in disorienting scales. Due to the threat the Nightcloak Malfestio inherently poses, its appearance is an emergency that may only be dealt with by Wycademy Hunters who possess a Special Permit, as is the case with every other Deviant.

Physiology
Similarly to the Paolumu, the Nightshade Paolumu has a cute rodent-like appearance, yet still shows open hostility towards enemies and displays a frightening, almost malevolent expression. Its dark sunken shell distinguishes it from the pale-toned Paolumu, and it is less capable at moving on the ground than the standard species. The Nightshade Paolumu primarily floats in the air and is rarely seen descending to the ground, and while there may not be many differences in the appearance of its wings, it is possible its flying ability is superior to that of the regular Paolumu. Moreover, it stores air in its neck pouch and releases it to attack predators. In the case of the Nightshade Paolumu, however, the gas it releases has a soporific effect that causes any creature that inhales it to fall asleep within a short period of time.
When the Nightshade Paolumu's neck pouch is inflated, it reveals a striking red-and-green pattern on its neck resembling large eyes, displaying deimatic behavior. Like the normal Paolumu, this Subspecies is not a dominant player in its ecosystem, thus, it inflates its neck patterns to resemble a head and appear larger, increasing the chances of avoiding unnecessary conflict.
The sleep-inducing gas released by the Nightshade Paolumu is heavier than air, resulting in it accumulating near the ground and forming gas pools. In addition to drawing in air, the Nightshade Paolumu scatters the gas pools in all directions with the wind pressure of its tail, which it sways and slams against; it is rather adept at using these sleep-inducing abilities. However, if it exhales a certain amount of air, the neck pouch will deflate. In this state, the Nightshade Paolumu primarily inhales air and no longer scatters sleep-inducing gas, although it will move the surrounding gas pockets around to counter this loss of gas; the Nightshade Paolumu can additionally inhale to draw in the scattered sleep gas. When dispersing accumulated gas, its rubbery tail is flattened to create a current of air, and when attacking, the tail curls up.
Behavior
The Nightshade Paolumu has been spotted in the Ancient Forest and the Wildspire Waste. It primarily resides in the Wildspire Waste due to its diet consisting of Carrier Ants similarly to the Barroth, rather than land-coral eggs like the regular Paolumu. It takes a deep breath of air and blows it into the inside of the anthill, sucking up and eating the ants that were blown away from the gust. Such use of the unique abilities of a monster species makes this a rare feeding method.
Although the soporific gas the Nightshade Paolumu utilizes is considered dangerous, it itself does not appear to be an aggressive monster. Since the core of its diet is primarily insects, this ability is likely used to deter predators when attacked, and to escape from battle. Although, if an enemy falls unconscious from the soporific gas during combat, the Nightshade Paolumu will launch a powerful charge attack to finish them off. It expels a large amount of air in one go as propulsion, deflating and landing after the attack.
Development
Kaname Fujioka stated that Nightshade Paolumu was similar to Viper Tobi-Kadachi, being a monster that helps the player overcome abnormal conditions. Like the normal species, it floats by inhaling air, so its movements appear leisurely at first glance, but it controls the special sleep breath it sets by flapping its wings and suction, so if one is not careful, it will put players to sleep and cause some trouble. In that sense, it is a monster that has a very easy-to-understand strategy for those who have equipped themselves with skills such as sleep immunity. Nightshade Paolumu itself doesn't do much except put you to sleep, but if one is not careful enough, it can be quite a hassle.
In terms of design, Nightshade Palumu's patterns on its inflated neck pouch look like eyes and its face looks like a beak, so the whole thing looks like the face of a giant bird. This monster is timid by nature, so by making its body bigger it appears more threatening. In the cutscene where it first appears, the reason it did not attack the Hunter after they were put to sleep by it is because Nightshade Paolumu are timid monsters that will flee at any opportunity.

Physiology
The Noios is a noisy Wingdrake native to the Wildspire Waste. It has a similar body plan to other Wingdrakes: a large head on a slim neck, forelimbs modified into wings, taloned feet, and a thin tail. Most of the Noios' body is adorned by faded, brown scales, while its underside and face are white. The head has a dark pointed beak, and a beige wattle hangs from the lower jaw. The eyes are beady and orange.
The long and narrow wings are attached to a large, bony chest, and there are a cluster of spikes atop each shoulder. They are supported by three digits; the shorter fourth digit is free and possesses a claw. The legs sport four-toed feet, each with a long curved talon. The tail possesses a rounded vane near its end. The Noios utilizes an organ called a Screamer Sac, which allows it to release a powerful shriek capable of damaging the ears of humans. This Screamer Sac is used by Hunters to produce Screamer Pods.
Behavior
The Noios has only been seen in the arid regions of the New World, mainly the Wildspire Waste, where flocks gather among the Wildspires constructed by the Carrier Ants. Small areas around the Wildspires serve as the flock's territory. The Noios rarely lands on the ground or Wildspires to preen its wings. The Wingdrake circles and descends upon any carrion or other meat sources on the ground, quickly consuming its fill to take off again. It is generally a calm creature, yet when startled, it will flail about and fall to the ground. As it falls, and after it takes to the sky again, it will unleash a loud shriek. This will alert the rest of the flock, with a side effect of aggravating burrowing monsters, such as the Diablos. A hunter can use their Slinger to latch onto the foot of a disturbed Noios, however the Wingdrake will not fly far before the Slinger detaches as it refuses to stray from its territory.

The Hell Flame Octopus Nu Udra (ヌ・エグドラ, Nu Egudora) is a Cephalopod introduced in Monster Hunter Wilds.
Summary
Giant cavern-dwelling Cephalopods characterized by their six muscled, prehensile limbs and the coat of flammable oily secretions covering their body. As their eyesight has atrophied, they navigate the strata of the Oilwell Basin using blue-glowing sensory organs located at the tips of their arms, which can also fling off burning oil. As a result of their soft body, Nu Udra are able to traverse narrow gaps and tunnels. When enraged, they will ignite the oilsilt on their body, setting themselves ablaze.
Main Series
Monster Hunter Wilds: Nu Udra is first encountered in the 2★ Assignment The Black Flame Quietly Manifests, though its name is initially rendered as "The Black Flame". In High Rank, it is first encountered in the 6★ Assignment Scorching the Earth Once More. Arch-Tempered Nu Udra is first fought in the 9★ Event Quest Be Cursed, Ye Shadowy Flame, unlocked at HR 100. After having faded into myth as the "Black Flame", a Nu Udra emerges during the aberrant Firespring caused by Werner 's fixing of the blocked Wyrmway, defeating three Ajarakan threatening Azuz before vanishing. Out of fear that it will return, the Nu Udra is tracked down and slain, after which Azuz uncovers its true name and origins. In High Rank, the widespread intensified Inclemency in the Forbidden Lands causes another Nu Udra to become extremely aggressive, prompting the Avis Unit to hunt it before it causes more damage.

In High Rank, it is first encountered in the 6★ Assignment Scorching the Earth Once More. Arch-Tempered Nu Udra is first fought in the 9★ Event Quest Be Cursed, Ye Shadowy Flame, unlocked at HR 100.

Out of fear that it will return, the Nu Udra is tracked down and slain, after which Azuz uncovers its true name and origins. In High Rank, the widespread intensified Inclemency in the Forbidden Lands causes another Nu Udra to become extremely aggressive, prompting the Avis Unit to hunt it before it causes more damage.
Physiology
The Nu Udra is an enormous Cephalopod that coats itself in a tar-like Oilmucus excreted from the siphons beneath its large mantle, which is composed of a substance naturally produced within its body and crude oil from the surrounding environment. The body beneath the coat of Oilmucus is coloured a vibrant spectrum of greens and blues that give way to yellow at the ends of the tentacles and horns, and is broken up by patterns of deep-gray stripes. The hide is highly elastic and fire resistant, which—combined with its largely boneless body—allows the Nu Udra to travel between the narrow crevices and tunnels that perforate the Oilwell Basin without detection, as well as withstand the searing temperatures experienced in the depths.
Like the Xu Wu, the Nu Udra possesses a total of eight tentacles: six large tentacles used for locomotion and offense, and two smaller ones that conceal the beak like an upper lip. Lining each tentacle are rows of twisted spikes, the largest of which are found on the underside and serve to tear out chunks of flesh, while the ones on the topside serve as spots for its Oilmucus coating to build up and congeal. Despite their flexibility, the individual tentacles alone are powerful enough to restrain and lift other large monsters with no visible exertion.
Situated at the ends of the three largest pairs of tentacles are photosensitive oculi that are believed to act as sensory organs, each connected directly to the Nu Udra's nervous system through the heavy innervation in its tentacles, and normally tucked within small pockets on each tentacle tip. Life in the depths have significantly atrophied the Nu Udra's vision, with it almost entirely relying on its oculi to sense its surroundings. The eyes themselves sit at the base of a pair of twisted, spined horns atop its head, which are curved outwards to protect its eyes; each eye has a long and thin oblong marking inclined upward toward the horntip, giving it the appearance of having slit pupils while they are mostly constricted. When enraged, the Nu Udra will dilate its pupils to their full extent, causing them to overtake the entirety of the visible eyeball. The oculi, eyes, and horns protruding from the head will also emit a bright, sky-blue glow, concealing the pupil and color of the skin; should its tentacles be severed, the nerve bundles within can also be seen glowing. In an Arch-Tempered specimen, this glow is a deep purple instead.
The Nu Udra has the ability to spontaneously ignite the fluid it produces, allowing it to emit great deluges of fire towards enemies by pumping the flaming substance from its siphon, engulf itself in flames when enraged, or throw globs of explosive Oilmucus with its tentacles. The flames it ignites are exceptionally hot and burn for a prolonged period of time, scorching even other denizens of the igneous depths. The Nu Udra itself remains insulated even from this heat by its hide, which additionally secretes and maintains a layer of translucent, viscous fluid that acts as a barrier between its skin and the burning Oilmucus coat.
Behavior
The Nu Udra is highly aggressive towards intruders in its territory and seems to seldom venture out of it, as it had not been sighted in many decades before it was rediscovered by Azuz and the Guild. It is seemingly attracted to sources of heat and fire, and is noted to become more aggressive in its presence, as if consuming them for strength. The monster is highly dexterous, making full use of its many tentacles and soft body for offense and mobility.
The Nu Udra primarily hunts during the Firespring, the inclemency of the Oilwell Basin. It is known to prey on other large monsters, pinning them beneath its body and tearing pieces off of them with its beak to feed. Against territorial rivals, the Nu Udra has been seen restraining and gouging them with its tentacles, before burning them with flames from its siphon. Waste products are excreted from its siphon, leaving behind a small pool of Oilmucus and undigested bones.
The Nu Udra sleeps in tight cavernous pits, blocking off almost all access to its den. It pokes one tentacle out of the hole as a way to sense incoming intruders or danger. When idle, it will often adopt a stance with most or all of its tentacles raised to better sense its surroundings.
Life Cycle
The Nu Udra creates egg sacs within its nest during the Firespring. A young Nu Udra is called a Nu Yaya, and hatches from eggs en masse at night during the Plenty. As the Nu Yaya is prey for many larger creatures, it hides within crevices to avoid danger. Despite this, a fully mature Nu Udra is seldom seen.
Relation with Azuz
The Nu Udra was once responsible for an incident involving the Everforge during a past Firespring. Due to the dark coloration of the flames produced by the burning Oilmucus, the Nu Udra became known as the Black Flame to the people of Azuz, and stories of it have been passed down through generations. As nobody ever saw the beast again until much later, its true name and nature eventually faded out of memory outside of old tomes.
Music
Main article: Nu Udra (Music)
"Ebon Hellfire" is Nu Udra's theme. Ebon means "Black", referring to its alias, the "Black Flame".
Development
Since Nu Udra was meant to be an impactful monster, the original idea was to take an aquatic animal that is normally weak to fire, and as Kaname puts it: "turning that upside down." In addition, Nu Udra was given features such as horns and an unidentifiable face in order to make its silhouette appear more demonic. The battle theme was made to reflect Nu Udra's hellish aura as well, featuring phrases and instruments reminiscent of black magic.
When it came to movement, the developers wanted Nu Udra to "consciously use each of its tentacles" and interact with a hunter without needing to face them. Otherwise, it would constantly be spinning in an attempt to make eye contact.
As for combat, their desire was for Nu Udra to have a unique tempo as a large monster still capable of a flurry of attacks. However, that made it hard to figure out who it was targeting. The solution was for it to have a sensory organ at the end of each tentacle, which would emit light to tell the player who it is attacking.

Physiology
The Odogaron is a terrifying Fanged Wyvern covered in highly textured red skin, its body is slender and displays near zero amounts of fatty tissue, instead being highly muscular and defined. The Odogaron's head ends in a long snout, with multiple rows of pointed teeth being visible at all times; the top and bottom canines are notably enlarged. The jaw and neck muscles of the Odogaron are deceptively powerful and allow it to carry large Flying Wyverns, such as the Legiana, in its jaws.
The Odogaron's eyes are a dull-blue color and, due to the wyvern's lack of eyelids, are unable to close. Instead, the entire eyeball is covered in a thick cornea that is adapted to withstand the effects of the effluvium found in the environment the Odogaron inhabits. This makes the eyesight of the wyvern quite poor, enabling it only to differentiate between light and dark. However, this does not pose much of a problem for the Odogaron; in the dimly lit Rotten Vale, eyesight is not a particularly useful sense to begin with. Additionally, this reduced eyesight makes the Odogaron unaffected by the flashes of light produced by monsters such as the Tzitzi-Ya-Ku, which it may encounter whilst prowling the Coral Highlands. Nonetheless, the Odogaron has an extremely well developed sense of smell to compensate for its weak eyesight, which can be further enhanced by widening its large and flexible nostrils. Armed with its strong olfactory skill, the Odogaron can easily distinguish between the many different smells of corpses, identifying fresh ones and locking onto various tracks; It especially favors the smell of blood.
A very notable physiological feature of the Odogaron is its unique claw structure, as the Odogaron possesses two sets of claws on each foot. Four stiff claw-like spikes protrude from the knuckles and sit atop hard round pads that make contact with the ground and are almost always left extended. In addition to this set, the Odogaron has six serrated claws that usually remain folded upwards towards the ankle. Most of the time, these claws remain retracted, allowing the Odogaron to walk without making any sound. When prey is spotted, the Odogaron extends its large set of claws downwards and thrusts them into prey. The sharpened protrusions that comprise the Odogaron's claws are arranged into staggered columns and are serrated in a similar manner to a sawblade that ensures anything struck by them suffers deep and horrific lacerations, causing deep and profuse bleeding which is difficult to prevent.
As it does not tend to store fat, the Odogaron needs near constant caloric input to survive. Should the Odogaron eat after a long period of fasting it may enter a special state, called the Full-Body Flush. During this state, the body of the wyvern pulsates with a red glow and steam erupts from its mouth; the Odogaron grows significantly more aggressive during this state. The mechanisms behind the Full-Body Flush are not entirely understood yet, although it is believed to be a result of the Odogaron's body temperature suddenly spiking as digestion kicks in alongside its excitement at finally being able to eat again.
The tail of the Odogaron is distinguishable by the numerous hard white protrusions at the tip. These are hardened veils of skin that have grown and developed over the Odogaron's lifetime. Since this whitened tip forms as the Odogaron matures, the tail of a juvenile Odogaron mostly lacks them. In fact, these protrusions never stop growing, and can even allow the Odogaron to regrow some length of its tail after it has been severed.
Behavior
The Odogaron is entirely endemic to the New World and has thus far never been sighted anywhere else. It inhabits the Rotten Vale and the Guiding Lands, where it is known to be a brutal predator and scavenger, acting purely on a single-minded instinct to kill and feed, earning it the nickname of Cruel Claw. Perfectly adapted to the corpse heap of the New World, the Odogaron sniffs out the freshest corpses before any other scavenger can even think of claiming them. Alongside scavening, the Odogaron will actively hunt by overwhelming prey with its superior speed and agility. One brutal tactic it employs is to lacerate its target with its claws early on, condemning them to a slow death by blood loss. Even if they should get away, the nose of the Odogaron can track the scent of their blood all the way to their final breath. While it usually prowls the Rotten Vale, it has been observed venturing as far as the Coral Highlands to secure a meal.
Once it has secured a kill, the Odogaron will usually not immediately feast on it, instead preferring to carry it all the way back to its nest in the depths of the Vale. It does so by utilizing a network of tunnels that permeate the Vale, allowing the Odogaron to quickly travel across the region whilst protecting its bounty. Once it arrives at its nest, the Odogaron indulges in one of its more eccentric behaviors—it adds its kill to a massive stockpile of meat. While storage like this makes sense for a creature with such a demanding metabolism, it has been suggested the Odogaron intentionally dry ages meat this way, as it seems to prefer the taste of carrion after it has sat around in a dry pile for some time.
The Odogaron is known to often carry a slab of meat in its jaws while patrolling its habitat. This appears to be an insurance policy to have a quick bite if hunger sets in, allowing it to enter the Full-body Flush when needed for a quick power boost during challenging encounters.

Physiology
Amongst the variations of the Fatalis, the Old Fatalis is perhaps the most striking amongst them. In comparison to its relatives' darker colorations, this ancient Elder Dragon exudes an extraordinary beauty with its porcelain-white, sparkling scales. Its limbs transition to a muted brown coloration towards their end and its snout is sharper, bearing two backwards pointed spikes jutting out from each nostril. Said to be lightning personified, the structure of the Old Fatalis' shimmering white horns is unique; the more pronounced top set of horns sprout into antler-like formations, with their tips growing in darkness toward their ends. The Elder Dragon's claws and wing spikes share this black coloration, contrasting the luscious, white mane that adorns the backside of the dragon. The mane forms from the nape and lines the full length of its spine, all the way until its tail end. This brilliant mane is accompanied by a large beard which shapes the entire lower jaw. Unlike the usual yellow of its kin, the Old Fatalis' eyes are a fierce and unforgiving crimson red.
Behavior
The Old Fatalis resides in Castle Schrade and the Tower, targeting any intruders without hesitation. Once enraged, the Old Fatalis sports red accents along its horns and chest as it shrouds its body with crackling, scarlet lightning, deflecting virtually all incoming attacks.
Much like the other Fatalis, its natural habitat and origins are unknown, however, unlike its relatives, the Old Fatalis appears to be linked in some way to eclipses. In one instance, it mysteriously appeared through an eclipse, descending from the heavens clad in divine radiance. Moreover, it has displayed the ability to call forth lightning across great distances, flying off towards the eclipse before commanding crackling bolts of blood-red lightning with a resounding roar.
History & Mythology
The Old Fatalis is said to be the ancestor of all dragons.
Music
Main article: Old Fatalis (Music)
Ancient Dragon is Old Fatalis' theme.
In Monster Hunter Frontier Z, G Rank Old Fatalis receives another unique theme, named "The True Ancestor", though it does not share motifs with "Ancient Dragon".
Development
The idea of making a white colored version of Fatalis was partially inspired by the Iwakuni White Snakes, a real-life phenomenon in which Japanese rat snakes that are born near the city of Iwakuni have an abnormally high chance of being albino, leading to them being considered a symbol of divinity and good fortune. According to Yuya Tokuda, this case of an otherwise unpopular animal being seen as divine due to having a white body influenced the decision to make Old Fatalis white.

They are highly sensitive to sound, and loud noises such as those from Screamer Pods are able to draw their attention. Certain Omega Micros units have a blue glow to them and will create a temporary energy shield on their position upon being destroyed.

Summary
A quadrupedal, black-armored machine from another world with the directive to subjugate the planet. By analyzing foes, the Omega frame is capable of adapting to and copying their abilities, even creating digitized clones of existing life-forms. The Omega Planetes bristles with powerful weaponry that it uses to devastate targets, including numerous missiles, torrents of flame, mechanical minions, and a multitude of destructive energy beam attacks.
Main Series
Monster Hunter Wilds: Added in Title Update 4, Omega Planetes is first encountered in the 8★ Assignment Invader from the Stars. Afterwards, it may be refought in the 8★ Optional Quest Planetes Protocol. A special Tempered Omega Planetes with new behavior and mechanics can be hunted in the 9★ Event Quest Planetes Protocol (Savage). Omega Planetes crosses into the Forbidden Lands through a dimensional rift and deems the planet worthy of subjugation. After rescuing Alpha and Omega from the Omega Planetes's Nerscylla Clone, the Avis Unit learns of its objective and sets out to stop it, intercepting it as it overpowers and nearly kills a Jin Dahaad. The Avis Hunter manages to defeat the machine, but Omega warns that further spacetime anomalies may cause it to return.

Physiology
Hailing from a realm known as Eorzea, on another world, Omega Planetes is an otherworldly monster that defies known notions of monster classification, largely due to its completely mechanical nature. It is a member of a now-defunct society known as the Omicrons, specifically a digital entity controlling the Omega Frame, their finest and strongest weapon; this specific iteration was given the name "Omega Planetes" to distinguish it from the friendly Omega. It has the unique ability to manipulate spacetime rifts and travel between dimensions.
Omega Planetes has a body structure superficially similar to that of a Neopteron or Temnoceran, with an ovoid body encased in a black metal carapace decorated with ornate silver filigree, with particularly large shells on its dorsal half. The screws used to secure parts of Omega Planetes are made with such impossible precision and complexity that they cannot be replicated, while also containing highly detailed springs capable of bearing unusually heavy loads. Its body is supported by four comparatively spindly, double-jointed legs with numerous exposed mechanical parts, including unique pedals that are able to move many mechanical parts simultaneously. The upper joints of the forelegs are protected by metal pads, while each leg terminating in four claws arranged in a cross shape. Although usually found walking on its legs, it can fold its legs close to its body and freely hover or fly through the air.
Attached to the front of its body is a movable disc-shaped head bearing a symmetrical silver pattern divided by a narrow, glowing, yellow horizontal visor that it sees through; the lenses making up its visor are said to allow one to peer into another dimension when looking into it. A glowing-blue periscope-like power unit will occasionally pop out from a hatch on its back, able to rotate with immense force using a special axle incorporating interdimensional technology. When sufficiently angered, its visor will turn red as spiraling parts of its carapace fold open and begin glowing purple. Within its body is a puzzling core that continues to pulsate with heat as if still active, even after being removed from the main body.
As an alien weapon, the Omega frame is armed with a wide variety of dangerous armaments utilizing technology far beyond the scope of the Guild and its Hunters. Omega Planetes is capable of firing blasts of energy, a massive frontal beam from its visor, or unleashing arrays of high-powered energy beams in its cardinal directions. These energy beams can also be fired as a Wave Cannon, where several laser beams spontaneously appear from the space around Omega Planetes to decimate a wide area. Hatches on the dorsal half of its body can also open and fire a variety of projectiles with seemingly limitless ammunition, such as Rocket Fists, enormous rocket-propelled fists that independently seek and destroy enemies, MRV Missiles that are fired in large quantities to bombard foes from above, and Mustard Bombs that cover a wide blast radius in persistent flames. On its underbelly is an array of retractable nozzles that can expel large volumes of fire and be used as thrusters to allow for flight and sudden bursts of speed. Omega Planetes is additionally able to spontaneously manufacture Omega Micros, smaller copies of itself that will seek out targets and explode. Some of these miniatures will generate potent energy shields when destroyed; similar shields can be deployed by dealing heavy blows against the monster's head, which will cause abnormalities in its shield deployment coordinates and cause the shield to be deployed underneath itself.
The most powerful attack Omega Planetes can utilize is the Delta Attack, only authorized if the frame has sustained sufficient damage. After deploying a number of guard units to protect itself, it will begin a lengthy charging period that culminates in it firing a gargantuan laser beam that annihilates every living thing in the immediate area. The only thing able to stand up to it is a high-density shield of its own making, which can be deployed by slaying more powerful cloned entities created by the Omega Planetes itself.
Omega Planetes' signature ability is to thoroughly scan other lifeforms, internalize the data, and physically generate replicas of the scanned entities, effectively being able to copy and use their powers. By killing and scanning a Nerscylla and Jin Dahaad respectively, the Omega Planetes was able to create a digital clone of the former with enhanced abilities, and able to replicate the latter's ability to expel supercooled vapor. It uses this ability to continuously evolve and improve itself, adapting to all local threats and constantly growing more powerful.
Behavior
The Omega Planetes is driven solely by the directive instilled in it by its creators: assess planets as prospective targets for conquest, learn about their life-forms, and use that knowledge to evolve and subjugate the planet. It continues carrying out this will despite its creators being long gone. The Omega frame naturally seeks out the strongest foes in the immediate area—in the case of its sudden arrival in the Forbidden Lands, the Jin Dahaad—in an attempt to scan the opponent most likely to augment its power.
In battle, Omega Planetes will initially use a limited set of armaments as it gauges its opponent and attempts to learn from them, or simply eliminates those that it deems unworthy of note. As a threat persists, it will gradually start unlocking its restrictions and using more dangerous weaponry, even at the cost of other functions. Sufficient damage to its head can cause it to become more aggressive and single out an individual target.
Should it be pushed further in battle, Omega Planetes activates its Pantokrator Mode, redirecting internal power and resources normally allocated to other functions—such as navigation—towards combat instead. Indicated by its power unit extending and glowing red, this causes a drastic increase in the machine's aggression and power output as it focuses only on relentless attacks. However, should its legs be sufficiently damaged, it will halt the Pantokrator Mode.
Omega Planetes is highly intelligent and capable of human speech, with its general demeanor being cold and calculating. When first encountered by the Avis Hunter, it initially dismissed them as beneath its notice, although gradually started took them more seriously as the threat persisted against its calculations. Should its Delta Attack fail to eliminate its targets, it will be taken aback at the improbable outcome and start becoming more desperate as it nears defeat.
Music
"Heartless" and "eScape" are Omega Planete's 1st phase and 2nd phase themes respectively, tracks that were originally from the SHADOWBRINGERS: FINAL FANTASY XIV Original Soundtrack. The 2nd phase theme triggers when Omega Planetes unleashes its Delta Attack. In the Savage version of the hunt, "eScape" plays as its 1st phase theme instead and "From the Heavens" as its 2nd phase theme, also from the same soundtrack.
Similar to Behemoth, when slain in Wilds, "A Victory Fanfare Reborn (Full)" plays as the Quest Complete theme, originally from A REALM REBORN: FINAL FANTASY XIV Original Soundtrack.
Development
In an interview with the technology publication TechRadar Final Fantasy 14 's director, Naoki Yoshida explained that "the people who said that they really want Omega to make an appearance was the Monster Hunter team" and "they wanted to achieve a sort of world view which behind it there lies an unknown civilization and it's a little bit different to Monster Hunter, what you could see in Monster Hunter before, and for that reason they wanted Omega to make an appearance because it would expand on that world view which they have in the game and that battle experience".

An amethyst mane and a distinctive pink horn embellish this ebony-black Subspecies of Kirin shrouded in mystery and frost. The precious few records available tell of their presence freezing the very moisture of the air, causing a dramatic drop in temperature. Said to be able to conjure shards of ice at will, impaling and freezing solid any aggressor.

Physiology
The Oroshi Kirin is a Subspecies of the Kirin and shares its quadrupedal gait and hooved feet. Its body is coated in blackened scales and sports a brilliant, purple mane adorning its back, tail, and each ankle. Patterning its scales are several pale-blue stripes, present along its body and its legs. The tail of the Oroshi Kirin is coated in a permanent layer of ice that shines brilliantly under the light; a single swing from this tail is enough to summon a cloud of icy fog.
Atop the Oroshi Kirin's head is a single horn colored a bright pink, this horn is the source of the Oroshi Kirin's power and allows it to control and produce ice. A single swing of the horn is enough to significantly lower the surrounding air's temperature, creating areas of air cold enough to freeze anything that wanders into them. This power is even strong enough for it to summon shards of ice out of the ground from seemingly nowhere. The body of the Oroshi Kirin is shrouded by a permanent coating of cold air, this aura appears to intensify when the Oroshi Kirin becomes enraged, with the scales on its body hardening in the process—allowing only the sharpest of blades to pierce its hide.
Behavior
The Oroshi Kirin is seen as a divine being, with those who have chanced upon it remarking its mystical appearance and claiming it to be a sight everybone should one day witness. Due to its existence only recently being confirmed by the Hunter's Guild —with the Elder Dragon first being sighted within the Everwood —as well as the few reported sightings since, very little is known about the Oroshi Kirin's behavior, with even its diet remaining unknown to this day. Legends claim the Oroshi Kirin's control over ice to be so great, that it has frozen entire kingdoms in a single night.

Their extremely hard tail can also be used as a weapon, giving their attacks an extra punch, especially when their entire body comes crashing down.

Physiology
The Paolumu is a species of Flying Wyvern that roams the Coral Highlands and whose whole body is covered in a fluffy down. Parts of its skin contains a rubbery substance that helps the monster expertly wield its elastic neck pouch or tail. This same material is prized as an ingredient for specialized tool and arms crafting.
The most iconic feature of the Paolumu is its neck pouch, which is highly elastic. By sucking in air, the Paolumu can expand the pouch to a diameter greater than that of its own body. The constant winds of the Highlands allow the Paolumu to ride their currents when its neck pouch is full. Additionally, by expelling stored air, the Paolumu can change its course as it wishes, showing refined control over its aerial movement. It does not appear to inflate its neck pouch while it is on the ground, or while it is airborne, although when threatened, it displays deimatic behavior and inflates its neck pouch to appear larger and more threatening to its enemies. The elasticity and durability of the Paolumu's neck pouch makes it perfect for use in crafting a hot-air balloon that can handle the rough winds of the plateaus. The Paolumu may additionally use its air-filled neck pouch as a weapon against enemies, as well as expel air by firing compressed air like a bullet; these bursts are powerful enough to hinder the movement of enemies and territorial invaders. Should the air run out, the Paolumu simply needs to inhale more to replace its stock.
Riding the wind reduces how often the Paolumu must flap its wings to stay afloat, this energy-efficient method allows the monster to stay airborne for long periods. Floating in this fashion also provides the advantage of reducing noise, so that the Paolumu may silently swoop down on intruders. As such, the surface area of the Paolumu's wings are on the smaller end of the scale. on the inside of each wing are digit-like structures, signifying the wings were once arms that evolved alongside the development of the neck pouch.
While the Paolumu's ears are quite large, its sense of hearing is not particularly well developed. Screamer Pods do not affect the Paolumu, suggesting its ears are not adapted for ambient noise as much as they are for catching ultrasound. The Paolumu navigates the complicated and tangled Coral Highlands with ultrasonic waves emitted from its mouth. The monster's large ears detect the echoes of these waves, allowing it to avoid obstacles by accurately determining their distance and location.
The Paolumu's large flat tail is notably hard in comparison to the rest of its soft body. The easiest way for the airborne Paolumu to attack an enemy on the ground is with its tail, thus, the tail has evolved to be long and tough. The Paolumu can easily change the shape of its rubbery tail by balling it into a hard rounded shape, unleashing precise strikes on opponents and smacking them with the sharp protrusions on the dorsal side of the tail. When whirling around for a whiplike tail attack, the vigorous movement causes the tail to stretch, extending the attack's range. The tail is approximately half of the Paolumu's total body length and is heaviest at the tip, which helps the monster maintain balance while airborne.
Behavior
The Paolumu feasts on land-coral eggs, and is the only large monster species inhabiting the Coral Highlands that relies on them as its primary form of sustenance. As its prey differs from that of other large predatory monsters in the same region, the Paolumu does not normally battle over resources, instead exhibiting a comparatively placid personality. Its territory lies in the verdant central plateaus of the Coral Highlands, where many Raphinos gather. When the Paolumu discovers coral eggs floating in the air, it will suction the surrounding air into its mouth, bringing the floating eggs along for consumption. While feeding, it maintains low-altitude flight and releases the unnecessary abundance of air from its mouth, before repeating the same routine until its appetite is satiated. In order to properly maintain its large frame on a diet of such tiny eggs, the Paolumu usually spends a substantial amount of time feeding, usually doing so once or twice a day.
The Paolumu's rest area is different from where it goes to sleep. Generally, the Paolumu roosts in the lower region of the cliffs leading to the peak of the Highlands, although if it seeks to recover from battle wounds, it will sleep in the Coral Dome. This area is a series of large coral domes, whose ceilings are dotted with holes, holes big enough for the Paolumu to fit through. By flying in and out of them whilst concealing its flight path from its opponent, the Paolumu can launch silent strikes on a confused target. It is likely the monster is aware this area is advantageous to its abilities and willingly leads enemies here for the very purpose of putting them at a disadvantage in battle.
Development
Yuya Tokuda stated that since Paolumu floats instead of fly, players can attempt to control the monster's aerial height. The team started work by thinking about how they could add some variety to the encounters and came up with the idea of Paolumu attacking with its balled-up tail. In order for the tail to be tough when balled up and flexible when flat, they went with a rubber-based approach. As for how it attacks with its tail, the planning and design teams worked on that together. They tied that in with how it preys on land-coral eggs.
Kaname Fujioka wanted to add a new style of floating gameplay to the monster with the monster changing shape by blowing up like a balloon. On the planning side, the development team made it harder on themselves by covering it in fur and trying to make it as adorable as possible. Amusingly for Fujioka, however, contrary to how it appears in silhouette, its facial features made it look like a rodent and thought its eyes were slightly creepy.
