Physiology
The Pink Rathian is named for the color of her scales, a beautiful pink resembling blooming flowers. Due to this color, this Subspecies has been given the nickname Blossom Queen of the Land. Besides this, there is no apparent physiological difference between the Pink Rathian and her regular counterpart, which makes it difficult to determine whether tracks originate from the Subspecies or not. It is believed the Pink Rathian is a different color due to originating from nutrient-rich environments, strengthening her body as a result. She possesses the standard Flying Wyvern body plan, consisting of a large head on a flexible neck, two large wings connected to a short torso, two hind legs, and a long tail with a weaponised tip. The top side of her body is protected by shells that have grown harder, while her skin remains more elastic, making the Pink Rathian both tougher and more flexible than the standard Rathian. Additional shells adorn the large triangular head, where a small beak covering the nose and a long horn jutting out the chin lie.
Keratinous spikes jut out of the largest digit of the wings, whose membranes are pink with large spots. Depending on the individual, the outside of the spots are either black or cream colored, although the inside of the spots are always black. As a wyvern that primarily battles on the ground, all Rathian have powerful legs; however, the Pink Rathian boasts superior musculature to the base species, allowing her to attack with more force and use more advanced techniques. Although she shares the same terrestrial mobility, the Pink Rathian exceeds the standard Rathian in aerial capability. Patches of thin highly toxic barbs protect each shoulder and wrist, as well as the tip of the tail. The barbs on her tail are the primary method of defense for the Subspecies as they contain a more potent form of poison than the regular Rathian. This enhanced poison is painful enough to ward off powerful monsters, such as the Bazelgeuse. The Pink Rathian follows the same regional variation as the base species, with her shade of pink varying between regions. The Pink Rathian from the New World bears denser patches of barbs, and her wing structure differs in a way that allows a greater degree of spread. The altered wing structure further improves the flight abilities of the Pink Rathian.
Behavior
The Pink Rathian inhabits similar environments to the standard Rathian, however, she only inhabits productive regions that are rich in nutrients, hence her rarity. The Pink Rathian was not discovered in the New World until after the continent's ecosystem had been enriched by the energy of the Zorah Magdaros following its passing. The Pink Rathian was the first Subspecies to be reported in the New World, being sighted in the Wildspire Waste, the Guiding Lands, and the Coral Highlands. The behavior of the Pink Rathian is very similar to the regular Rathian, although she is known to be more aggressive. The Pink Rathian primarily roams her territory on foot, hunting smaller herbivorous monsters—such as the Gargwa, Apceros, and Raphinos —by attacking them with her venomous tail. The Pink Rathian exclusively mates with the Azure Rathalos, although the two are rarely seen together in the New World.
The Pink Rathian's presence in the New World is thought to have occurred by the wyvern developing in regions benefiting from the Everstream's energy, although this has raised questions due to the lack of any sightings of the Pink Rathian in the Elder's Recess. The ecology of the Subspecies and is standard counterpart does not differ greatly, an assumption strengthened by the Pink Rathian's pairing behavior with the Azure Rathalos. Thus, it is believed any Pink Rathian sighted in either the Coral Highlands or Wildspire Waste are individuals who have failed to become the Azure Rathalos' nesting mate. Alternatively, such individuals may have chosen to leave their mate to raise their young in less competitive environments.
Development
In Monster Hunter: World, Pink Rathian serves as the transition from Low Rank to High Rank. The regular Rathian was a monster that was entirely optional in Low Rank but also familiar to most players. The development team also wanted the first unique monster in High Rank to appear in the Coral Highlands. It was a great opportunity to introduce a stronger, brightly colored Rathian Subspecies with an advanced moveset. This would demonstrate to the player that monsters they had fought before have become stronger and that they need to prepare for the higher difficulty. They had the players gather data on the Subspecies before encountering to explain why it had not appeared until now despite being well-known in the Old World.

The Piragill exhibits a build similar to that of most other Leviathans: its body is long and flexible, allowing it to move effectively both on land and in the water. The iridescent scales across its body are primarily a mix of turquoise and cyan, although there is a long, purple and blue-black stripe running from the eye all the way to the tail, with a break around the shoulder and pelvic area. The limbs and tail of the Piragill generally display this purple-and-blue coloration, and it exhibits a splotch of orange against its otherwise predominantly countershaded white underside. It sports a quadrupedal gait, with the webbed four-toed feet of the wyvern possessing small blunt claws.
In extreme contrast to these claws, the majority of the Piragill's body brandishes large spined protrusions, mostly notably along the head and spinal region. These light-scarlet saw-like blades are the largest atop the Leviathan's head and decrease in size as they near the shoulder, with another sizable protrusion found on the Piragill's back starting this process again and reducing in size until it reaches the tip of the tail. This tail sports a notably hooked spike, and the membrane connecting these projections is littered with miniscule holes.
The head of the Leviathan is downturned at the front, with the upper jaw overtaking the bottom jaw, and the nostrils are located closer to the top of the head. The mouth sports small razor-sharp teeth, and each eye exhibits a blue sclera with a green iris as well as a vertically-slit pupil.
Behavior
The Piragill is a pack-hunting Leviathan that uses both numbers and precise strategy to overwhelm its opponent. When a suitable prey item is spotted, it will surround them alongside its packmates and wait for an opening to attack all at once, using its bladed protrusions to slice through targets like butter. While the Piragill is spotted during all seasons in the Scarlet Forest, it is most active and numerous during the Fallow and Inclemency. Occasionally, the Piragill can be spotted slashing at trees with its dorsal blades, causing a small amount of red sap to disperse into the water as a result. Interestingly, it also appears completely unaffected by the bramble that grows along the lower regions of the Scarlet Forest, often choosing to retreat within it when escaping from danger.

Physiology
The Plesioth is the largest amongst the Piscine Wyverns, and is rarely seen outside the water, as it is quite clumsy when on dry land due to its massive size. The size of the Plesioth can be attributed to its aquatic lifestyle on account of the buoyancy of the water supporting the wyvern's size and weight, allowing it to grow larger than most others. The Plesioth possesses a tall sleek build and is adorned with shiny, colorful scales that run dark-navy and salmon-pink across its back, and white along its underbelly. These scales are thick and—even when dry—have a lapis-like sheen to them, their thickness protects the Plesioth from the fangs and claws of other monsters. When used in the forging of armor, the scales help absorb the shock from sudden blows, however, they will become brittle once dehydrated.
The Plesioth's stout head has a pointed snout and is surprisingly hard, it is a highly valuable material for crafting armor and weapons due to its sturdiness, considered to be amongst the best in armor materials. Much like the Cephadrome, the Plesioth uses its acute hearing to compensate for its poor eyesight and navigate its surroundings. Consequently, sudden loud noises may startle the Piscine Wyvern, often enraging it and causing it to surface onto land. Its jaws are lined with two rows of sharp needle-like teeth powerful enough to crush the shells of large Carapaceons with little difficulty. Although its teeth are strong enough to crush the shells of the invertebrates it eats, intact lobster shells have been discovered inside the stomach of a beached Plesioth's carcass, suggesting the wyvern simply swallows its prey whole and relies on its powerful digestive capabilities. Shells that are too large to be fully digested and remain in the stomach may be used as the primary material for forming armor.
The Plesioth's fins are among its most notable features. The two largest wing-like pectoral fins allow it to swim through the water at great speeds, with it being noted to be able to swim faster than a sprinting horse. In addition, the Plesioth possesses three cranial fins, a tall dorsal fin, an adipose fin, a large caudal fin, and a smaller fin on the ventral side of its tail; each one is adorned with sharp orange spines. Within the barbs of these radiant fins lies a potent neurotoxin that acts as a powerful sedative, putting monsters and Hunters alike to sleep with the smallest scrape; although some individuals have instead been seen delivering this toxin through the fangs. Due to this property, as well as the fins' striking beauty, the Plesioth's fins are extremely valuable for forging armor, with the finest samples producing the best sets of armor. Owed to the moisture-retaining properties of the fins' webbing, they are a popular material to use as armor lining, even in spite of being difficult to work with.
Despite spending most of its life underwater, the Plesioth does not possess gills. Its respiratory system is instead like that of any other wyvern, leading researchers to believe the Plesioth's ancestors may have been terrestrial Flying Wyverns. It has no visible nostrils, however, breathing instead through its skin. This adaptation allows the Plesioth to absorb oxygen even while underwater, enabling it capable of staying submerged for long periods of time. Despite this, it prefers to stay near the surface where oxygen is more accessible. This trait makes staying on land for very long dangerous since the Plesioth cannot breathe as well if its skin dries out.
Behavior
The Plesioth is an ambush predator that lives in both saltwater and freshwater environments, attacking any prey that comes near the water's edge by spraying a jet of compressed water at it, although it may also grab large prey and drag it underwater. Alongside Carapaceons, the Plesioth will seek out a variety of fish, lobsters, and large Herbivores such as the Aptonoth and Epioth. Above all else, however, the Plesioth's favorite food are Frogs, which are often used by hunters as bait in hopes of luring the Piscine Wyvern onto land.
In order to successfully bait the Plesioth, it cannot be aware of the hunter's presence as the Piscine Wyvern is incredibly cautious and will not take the bait if it notices the hunter. Thus, if in a a small party of hunters, only one individual should attempt to fish the Plesioth out, while the rest should keep a distance until the Plesioth is dragged up. Should the Plesioth be hooked, hunters must be careful so as to not get dragged into the water whilst tugging the fishing line. Eventually, the Plesioth will grow agitated and leap out of the water to attack the hunter that has caught it. Although it generally avoids being on land as much as possible, the Plesioth will battle on land once angered if necessary, using its massive body to slam into opponents. Otherwise, the Plesioth is noted to be elusive and difficult to spot as a result of its aquatic lifestyle, and for some time, its appearance was only known through the testimonies of hunters.
The Plesioth is ovoviviparous, meaning the eggs are fertilized and hatched within their mother's womb. Upon hatching, the infant Plesioth will start devouring each other until only one individual is left in the womb. The unborn Plesioth will then feed upon the unfertilized eggs the Plesioth mother expels into the womb to provide it with nourishment; this child will be raised within the womb during a lengthy developmental phase. The male Plesioth stays with the gravid female during all this, routinely bringing food for her and her brood, even once the brood has been depleted to only one individual. Once the young Plesioth reaches a third of its parents' size, it will finally exit the womb and no longer receive any more parental support from its mother.
Monster Hunter
Plesioth was created by Norio Hirose. When reviewing the initial design document for the monster, Game Designer Tsuyoshi Nagayama thought he was being pranked, and that the monster would obviously not be included in the final game. Shintaro Kojima later contributed to the final design and insisted on the monster's affinity for frogs.
During the production of Monster Hunter, a peculiar bug caused the armor sets of Plesioth and Cephadrome to be switched around, with the former's materials being needed for the latter's armor recipe and vice versa. While this was a mistake, the development team thought that it was interesting and that this would likely surprise players. Thus, they left the two armors switched.
Monster Hunter 3 Ultimate
After it was decided that Plesioth would be added to Monster Hunter 3 Ultimate, Nagayama was tasked with giving it an underwater movement and combat style. This proved to be extremely difficult, and a critical bug forced Nagayama to spend an entire night at the office fixing Plesioth.
Monster Hunter Stories 3: Twisted Reflection
A scrapped Kinship Skill had Plesioth firing its water beam vertically, causing the ocean to split and crush the enemy in the middle with falling waves. The team rejected it as they figured the beam would have hit the enemy and was considered expensive. An additional idea involved Plesioth entering a "subspace" where time froze, allowing Plesioth to unleash multiple attacks on the enemy where it would be slain by the consecutive hits when time resumed. Despite liking it, Takahiro Kawano thought such a spectacle did not fit the monster.

Physiology
The Popo is a medium-sized Herbivore found within snowy climates. Its robust body is covered in a thick layer of fur that helps to protect it from the cold, while its back sports a visible hump. Its fur is notably oily, preventing its body from getting covered in snow when it ventures into it. Its fur is typically long enough that its eyes end up being completely obscured, and underneath this fur the Popo possesses a short trunk that extends down from its lower jaw, with its nostrils opening up on the underside. Perhaps the most striking feature of the Popo is the large pair of twin tusks growing from its upper jaw that curve upwards in front of its face, serving as its main form of defense against predators.
The Popo displays a slight degree of sexual dimorphism, with the males on average being larger than the females, although the tusks on both sexes are equally large. While the Popo possesses rudimentary tusks as a juvenile, they are notably smaller than an adult's.
Behavior
The Popo is typically found in a small family unit that consists of a mated male and female pair, as well as their offspring. A familial herd will move together in order to search for food: most commonly grass. While it is typically known for having a gentle temperament—preferring to flee when either it or another member of its herd is in danger—the Popo will become much more defensive and will lash out at threats with its tusks if its offspring is threatened, with the harshness of its surroundings seemingly making these strikes especially strong. The male of the group is typically the one to fight off threats, giving both his mate and his offspring a greater amount of time to escape. Even the Blango, which will readily attack humans who wander into its turf, seems to keep its distance away from herds of Popo. When a Popo herd does begin to flee, its members will typically flee towards other nearby Popo herds, who will join them in their escape to form an even larger pack for protection. In doing so, the Popo will often venture into areas it typically does not graze in, such as glaciers and hot-springs.
In spite of this, the Popo is still a common prey item for several tundra predators, most notably the Tigrex. The Popo is one of the Tigrex's most favored prey items, with the wyvern often traveling all the way into snowy mountains just to hunt and feed upon them. In order to more easily protect itself, the Popo's herd will often seek out and care for any young Gammoth calves. While Gammoth calves are also a frequent target of the Tigrex's predation, the Popo herd will still stand guard and protect it from harm. In return, the significantly larger adult Gammoth will aid in protecting the remainder of the herd from the Tigrex as reparation. The Popo is also commonly hunted by people for its highly nutritious meat, with its tongue specifically being considered a delicacy by many.

Physiology
The Porkeplume is a small flightless Bird Wyvern sporting a raptorial build. Its forelimbs are diminutive and pronated, with four fingers ending in short sharp claws that curl inwards towards the body. In contrast, the hindlimbs are highly developed, and the feet consist of three walking toes as well as a notable sickle claw, which is kept partially hidden within its feathery coat. The body coat of the wyvern is typically a cream color in smaller individuals, with larger ones sporting a white coat, while the underside, legs, and tip of the tail are a grayish brown coloration. The head sports large red eyes with circular pupils, a small blunt beak, and white-and-orange feathers that are arranged in an afro-like shape.
The most striking features of the Porkeplume however are the large barbed bristles that adorn the back of its head, which can be grabbed with the Hook Slinger by Hunters to gain Bleeding Pods. These orange-and-white striped spines are typically kept slicked backwards alongside the head, although when faced with a threating adversary, they are puffed outwards to their maximum extent. These protrusions are complimented by additional sets of smaller, orange spines located closer to the center of the skull.
Behavior
The Porkeplume typically lives in a small herd of around two to four individuals within the heart of the Ruins of Wyveria. Despite possessing apparent weaponry, it appears to be predominantly herbivorous in nature, displaying a particular affinity for the Hot Peppers that grow throughout the Iceshard Cliffs. When sufficiently threatened, the wyvern will stick up its barbed spines in an attempt to intimidate its opponent, screeching at them and rattling its spines all the while. If this proves to be ineffective and the threat continues to approach, a member of the herd will charge at the opponent and ram them with its head, often breaking off its bristles in the process. This display grants the rest of the herd enough time to make a hasty retreat.

Physiology
The original form of the Malzeno when not infected and altered by the Qurio, the Primordial Malzeno broadly resembles its infected version, distinguished by being more physically robust and well-built. It is covered in thicker, silver-and-gold scales resembling armor plating; these scales have remained unscathed even after protecting the Elder Dragon for eons. The patches of Qurio are completely absent from its body, with its chest and forelimbs instead boasting thick, plated shelling, while the frills on its head are now solid and metallic instead of webbed. Rather than gaunt and tattered, the Primordial Malzeno's wings are sturdy and armored with golden blades on their edges, reminiscent of an impenetrable fortress; its wings' membranes are a gradient of blue and purple shades instead of red. Its fangs are said to lure beholders into a sweet slumber.
The Primordial Malzeno's physical attributes are dramatically stronger than the corrupted Malzeno, as it has not yet been drained by the parasitic Qurio and is not reliant on their power. It primarily fights using its armored wings as a sword and shield to simultaneously slash and stab targets as well as block blows, using them in combination with its tail and claws for relentless attacks. In spite of its blows carrying enough force to easily tear apart terrain, the Primordial Malzeno is extraordinarily agile and fights with extreme precision and finesse, able to stab individual Qurio out of the air mid-flight.
The Primordial Malzeno is not the natural host of the Qurio, however, if the Qurio manage to catch it off guard and forcibly bond with it, they can force it into a Bloodening state similar to that of the original species. In this state, the Qurio attach to its chest and arms, its scales become duller, and its tail begins radiating red energy; the Primordial Malzeno will subsequently begin to discard its finesse for brute strength, and starts using the Qurio themselves for attacks. If the infection persists, it will progress to a Bloodrage state, where the Elder Dragon's scales turn dark-gray, the Qurio patches on its body start glowing, and its wing membranes become tinged with magenta and red. In this further enhanced state, the Primordial Malzeno becomes even more aggressive and reliant on the Qurio over its physical strength, using their energy to rapidly zoom towards several positions and for more violent attacks. Should the Primordial Malzeno expend a vast amount of power in this state, it will revert back to the Bloodening state. Moreover, sufficient damage to the Qurio-covered patches on its body can also dispel them, returning the Elder Dragon to its original untainted form until the Qurio return.
When the Primordial Malzeno's body is about to give out, the Qurio will expend all their stored energy and push the Elder Dragon's body to its absolute limit as it assumes a final Bloodlust state, in which its scales turn black while its wing membranes, frills, and the gaps between its scales glow a bright, molten-orange. In this state, the Primordial Malzeno is at its most aggressive and relentless; having been corrupted by the overflowing energy coursing through its body, it unleashes a seemingly unending barrage of attacks against foes. However, it continues to resist the forced symbiosis, causing it to undergo periods of fatigue and struggle. Once the Primordial Malzeno is forced into the Bloodlust state, it will usually remain that way until death; however, some individuals have been shown to be able to overcome it and return to normal.
Behavior
Unlike its corrupted counterpart, the Primordial Malzeno is known to be more peaceful and solitary in nature, to the point where humans of old were able to coexist in its territory without issue. However, it is still intensely territorial and will use extreme force to remove an interloper if it or its turf are directly challenged. Unlike the Malzeno, which uses underhanded tactics and stealth to ambush prey, the Primordial Malzeno is known to battle enemies head-on and overcome them with a combination of strength and finesse, with its refined and graceful fighting style being likened to that of a elegant knight.
When the Primordial Malzeno becomes infected by the Qurio, it becomes dramatically more aggressive and begins regressing to the underhanded brutality of its parasitized kin. It additionally begins favoring indiscriminately destructive attacks that leave it fatigued afterwards. However, it continues to struggle against the symbiosis and resist the Qurio's influence, even whilst critically infected. Before infection, it is highly aggressive towards the Qurio, attempting to kill any who approach it in order to prevent them from bonding to its body.
In spite of its initial pacifism, the Primordial Malzeno is considered a major threat by the Hunter's Guild, and not just on the merits of its power. As it has been confirmed that this Elder Dragon can succumb to the Qurio and irreversibly turn into a devastatingly powerful creature that actively seeks to drain ecosystems of life, the risk of the Primordial Malzeno being overtaken looms over any instance of it emerging, urging Hunters to take action before the worst comes to pass.
The Primordial Malzeno demonstrates an unusually high level of intelligence even for the standards of an Elder Dragon, between its skillful use of its limbs as weapons and being able to seemingly show gratitude towards those who aid it. It is also said to hold a level of enmity towards the Qurio themselves beyond self-preservation and territoriality, believed to be hatred of how they attempt to corrupt it and its brethren into bloodthirsty monsters. However, it is not confirmed if this behavior indicates a higher level of sentience.
History & Mythology
Due to its solitary tendencies, humans living in the territories of the Kingdom seldom encountered the Primordial Malzeno, and neither party encroached on each other's turf. It was able to coexist with humans whilst still repelling other monsters from its territory, leading to the people beginning to revere Primordial Malzeno as a mythical guardian and savior, with its shed scales being passed down as charms said to bring eternal peace. Out of respect for it, after the first advent of the Gaismagorm that inspired the prophecy of the Archdemon of the Abyss, an addendum to the prophecy would describe the Primordial Malzeno as the Demonlord that would be summoned in the Archdemon's wake and use its silver spear to deliver judgement, purifying the land until only ashes remained of the invaders.
Unbeknownst to many, the Primordial Malzeno was indeed the one that drove off the Gaismagorm's first invasion, although it had subsequently been infected by the Qurio after the battle. Over time, this caused it to mutate into what would become known as the Malzeno's normal form. By consequence of its massively increased aggression over the following decades and the Qurio plague it brought, the Elder Dragon's original form was mostly forgotten, and the Malzeno became feared instead of revered.
After the deaths of both the corrupted Malzeno and the Gaismagorm, a Primordial Malzeno was discovered wreaking havoc across the Kingdom, and was given its current name owing to how it seemed to have arrived unchanged from a primordial era. At the same time, the addendum to the prophecy was rediscovered and interpreted as the Primordial Malzeno seeking to destroy the Kingdom, leading to Elgado Outpost dispatching Dame Fiorayne and the Fierce Flame to eliminate it before it could re-establish symbiosis. However, after observing its behavior in battle and determining that the "purification" in question was directed towards the Qurio in its territory, the pair decided to instead help it kill all the Qurio seeking to parasitize it, after which it left them in peace.
Development
Primordial Malzeno was designed to play a pivotal role in concluding the ages-long conflict between Malzeno and the Kingdom and capping off the Kingdom's storyline, being depicted as a knight who rejected symbiosis with the Qurio and regained its bearing as a noble Elder Dragon, returning to reclaim its rightful home from invaders. The team wished for the player to experience Primordial Malzeno's story through its battle, emphasizing the duality between the noble, resolute bearing of its pure state and the violent rampaging of its infected states, as well as its gradual corruption beyond the point of no return.
Primordial Malzeno's base form was designed with the image of a solemn, imposing holy knight, to contrast the original Malzeno being an unbridled vampire. Its wings were designed to resemble swords, while the thickened carapace on its chest conveyed the feeling of plate mail, creating a straightforward and classical design. Special attention was given to how Primordial Malzeno would physically change as the infection progressed, such as its body gradually getting overwhelmed and breaking down from rampant Qurio energy, while still conveying the overwhelming power that its failing body still wielded. Because Primordial Malzeno is larger and bulkier than a normal Malzeno, emphasis was given to the sound design of its physical movements, particularly those involving its much larger wings. The sounds Primordial Malzeno makes during sudden bursts of movement were intended to convey "light", as opposed to the base Malzeno's sounds invoking "darkness".

Physiology
The Pukei-Pukei is a medium-sized Bird Wyvern covered in scales and feathers that boast a wide variety of bright colors. Its dorsal scales are primarily green, while the ventral scales and the undersides of its wings are a pale, cream color. Its arms, back and tail possess small, lump-like spines that go to the tip of the tail. The Pukei-Pukei's green hide aids it in camouflage, as it typically lives in areas that are rich in vegetation. The scales of the Pukei-Pukei are lightweight and sturdy, making them valuable as crafting materials. Their shade of green varies depending on which part of the body the scales were harvested from. The Bird Wyvern's forearms are covered in green feathers up to the wrist, from which a small, clawed thumb protrudes. The rest of the wyvern's fingers are long and end in a rounded oval shape, and each fingertip has an orange dot marking. The Pukei-Pukei's wing membranes are extremely elastic whilst maintaining exceptional rigidity, their poison resistance grants them a wide variety of uses.
The feathers of the Pukei-Pukei are iridescent, and by altering the angle of its plumage, the light refracting off the microscopic crystalline particles in its plumage creates the illusion that the coloration of the feathers has changed. When provoked, the Pukei-Pukei's plumage will fan out to make itself look bigger while the feathers will take on a red-orange hue. When frightened, it will tuck its feathers in, causing them to appear duller and itself smaller. The feathers from Pukei-Pukei are used for decorative purposes.
The Pukei-Pukei has incredibly large and spherical, yellow eyes with a vertical, oblong pupil. Compared to those of other monsters, these eyes have extremely well-developed photoreceptors and can detect a much wider variety of colors. The thin pupils allow the Pukei-Pukei to control the amount of light absorbed by its eyes, which grants it the ability to accurately perceive colors even in low light environments. Using its superior ability to differentiate colors, it can spot threatening monsters from far away in an instance and quickly flee the area. Despite dwelling close to the ground, the Pukei-Pukei's four-toed feet appear to closely resemble those of creatures who live in the treetops and have adapted for holding on to branches. Some researchers speculate this trait may be a holdover from a time long ago when the species once roosted in the treetops of the Ancient Forest, this theory simultaneously bolsters another regarding the migration of the Rathalos to the New World.
The Pukei-Pukei's most notable trait is its ability to store and spew poisonous gas. As it feeds on plants and nuts, such as the Poisoncup and Scatternut, it stores the food in its tail and expandable chin. The chin houses a toxic digestive liquid that, when mixed with the nuts consumed by the monster, creates a potent toxin with unique properties dependant on which plants it eats. When the mixture of digestive fluids and plants is given time to ferment, it turns into vapor that is combined with the fluids within the Pukei-Pukei's Poison Sac, creating a much deadlier poison gas. The gas is stored in the wyvern's expansive tail, and is only released as a last resort. Due to the highly-toxic nature of the dewlap, it must be handled carefully when harvested.
An incredibly unique trait the Pukei-Pukei possesses is its large and stretchy tongue. By pushing a specialized bone near the center of the tongue forward, called the hyoid, the Pukei-Pukei is able to stretch the surrounding muscles and the tongue. Able to extend beyond 4 meters in length, the tongue is incredibly strong and unable to be stretched by human force. Only the Pukei-Pukei can manipulate its tongue, which it uses to grab nuts and fruits growing in the canopy.
Behavior
Despite being exclusively herbivorous, the Pukei-Pukei is incredibly territorial. It spends most of its time patrolling its territory on foot and is known to bully smaller monsters, such as the Great Jagras, out of its territory. However, if confronted with a monster that is larger and stronger than it, the Bird Wyvern is quick to flee.
The Pukei-Pukei's plant-based diet gives it a symbiotic relationship with the flora of the Ancient Forest. As the seedlings of much of the locale's flora is covered in a thick shell and often fail to germinate, the Bird Wyvern cracks the shell open when it eats these plants and allows tiny seeds to fall to the ground where they can germinate. Seedlings are also spread by the Pukei-Pukei when it deposits dung or when seedlings fall from its mouth during travel. It is for this reason the flora surrounding the Pukei-Pukei's nest is often the most diverse of its home locale.
In terms of reproductive habits, the Pukei-Pukei relies on brood parasitism. During breeding season, the Pukei-Pukei will seek out active Mernos nests that have been left unattended and will lay an egg amongst the Mernos' clutch which will hatch before the Mernos' own. The Pukei-Pukei chick will then proceed to push the other eggs out of the nest, ensuring it receives undivided attention from the Mernos parents. Eventually, the young Pukei-Pukei will leave the Mernos nest to seek out its own territory.

Physiology
A Subspecies of the Gypceros that distinguishes itself by little other than its coloration and heightened toxin production. The Purple Gypceros makes use of the same defensive armaments: the ability to spew poison, a tail able to stretch twice its length as a potent whip, a head crest containing hard minerals that can flash overwhelmingly bright light, and a curved, bucktoothed beak with surprising dexterity. Despite its more vivid coloration, this Subspecies shares the yellow eyes and cream-colored streak along its neck. While most of the body of the Purple Gypceros' body is colored as its name would suggest, the wing membranes are tinted a reddish-orange, and running down the sides of its neck is a bright line of emerald-green. The end of its elastic tail shares this color, as does the area around the monster's eye when enraged, and the head crest shares a comparable shade of reddish-orange to the wings.
Rarely seen, the Purple Gypceros' highly valuable wings are considered an excellent forging material, much like the elastic hide from its belly, due to their high resistance to poison. The purple hide of this Subspecies is considered a fashionable material that makes for excellent bags, while multiple parts are considered useful for providing quality padding and covers in furniture, especially for dirigible balloons.
The poison produced by this Subspecies' Poison Sac is much more potent than that of its more common cousin; colored a reddish magenta and black, it causes noxious poisoning in those afflicted. The copious Dash Extract in the Purple Gypceros additionally allows it to sustain its threatening acts for as long as, or even longer, than the regular Gypceros, enabling it to easily run along walls and ceilings alike with the fantastic grip provided by its feet, whilst also spewing copious amounts of deadly venom without risk of tiring easily.
Behavior
The Purple Gypceros is comparatively more belligerent and violent once agitated, rarely letting up compared to its timid, gray cousin. Even guards employed to guard traveling merchants have been known to lose all their confidence when faced with the aggression of the Purple Gypceros, which occasionally disrupts trade routes. The Purple Gypceros is notably more adept at using its crest flashes, with it being able to hold the flash after clicking its crest to unpredictably blind targets when they believe they are safe to press an attack.
When engaging in battle, the Purple Gypceros displays a similarly gluttonous intelligence and curiosity as its relative, using its massive beak to snatch away shiny objects and other consumable items from any humans it comes across. However, when agitated, the Purple Gypceros' poisonous maw drools venom and laces each of its pickpocketing attempts with poison, weakening opponents as it takes their advantaged items to viciously capitalize on. The Subspecies will even play dead as the regular Gypceros does, and is tolerant enough to allow Hunters to carve from its skin, before it suddenly thrashes them into submission, or flashes them while their guard is lowered.
Sharing the same omnivorous nature as the normal Gypceros, the Purple Gypceros feeds on Vespoids, mushrooms and carcasses, and mineral deposits.

Physiology
The Pyre Rakna-Kadaki is a Subspecies of the Rakna-Kadaki, differentiated by its ashen-white exoskeleton branded with orange markings, as well as deep-maroon silk boasting blast-resistant properties. Its carapace is highly resistant to heat and explosions, and its many layers make it notably challenging to pierce. The hooked spikes adorning its legs are now darker in color, their molten tips a sight to see due to their resemblance to open flames. Similarly, the Temnoceran's mandibles, horns, and eyes glow a fiery orange.
The Glowguts on the abdomen of the Pyre Rakna Kadaki are now a duller orange and said to burn with the monster's rage to a point where they are too hot to touch. Instead of the flammable gas characteristic of the nominate species, the Dull Glowguts produce a more volatile gas that is ignited by the use of the forelimbs as strikers, creating powerful explosions that ravel along its silk. Furthermore, the Pyre Rakna-Kadaki is able to expel this gas from its maw in the form of short-lived jets of flame.
The Pyre Rakna-Kadaki is the mother of a brood of Pyrantula, which it is able to command using a special sound-producing organ. In addition to swarming prey and expelling explosive gas of their own, the young Pyrantula can have flammable silk threads attached to them by their mother, which the Temnoceran ignites to send flames towards them. When touching the flame, the Pyrantula will release another burst of gas to create an explosion, akin to a bomb being ignited by a fuse. Similarly to the standard species, the Pyre Rakna-Kadaki will spin a silken egg sac on its abdomen to quickly spawn additional Pyrantula should its brood be depleted. The egg sac of the Pyre Rakna-Kadaki additionally glows with molten light, giving it an appearance similar to cooling lava.
Behavior
The Pyre Rakna-Kadaki shares the nominate species' preference for warm and dry climates, as well as its reclusive nature that makes researching its behavior difficult. On occasion, it has been known to battle the normal Rakna-Kadaki in violent territorial struggles.

Despite their size, the flames produced by the brushing of the Quematrice's tail make for a dangerously impressive display that, when compounded with their stocky build and sweeping motions, make them surprisingly capable combatants.

Physiology
The Quematrice is relatively small for a Brute Wyvern, with an unusually bird-like appearance. Its scales are gray in color with blue mottling, and have a sharp, fine edge capable of polishing armor or cutting into stone; its scales and hide are highly heat-resistant. It has a short, robust skull with strong jaws, with the lower jaw showing protruding incisors and canines when closed. Its eyes are golden in color and possess slit pupils. There is a bright red comb atop its head, with two more crests surrounding each eye and projecting backwards, resembling a reddish-orange mask. All three crests naturally have holes in them, and their bright color serves as a decoy for predators to target. The Quematrice will shake the bright comb on its head to display its aggression toward opponents.
The sides of the neck have two large dewlaps which are gray with red spots, and dark-blue at the fringes. Its torso is stout with short and pudgy arms, each of which has a small hand with three short fingers. The legs are similarly short, yet muscular. The tail of the Quematrice is very long and muscular, and is lined with long tasseled frills, called Pleats, which make the Quematrice appear larger. Where they attach to the tail, the pleats are gray; moving outwards, they are dark-blue, and then red near the fringe.
The Quematrice's tail secretes a flammable, oily fluid known as its Igniter, which is occasionally left behind on the ground as a stain of splattered oil, and vaporizes quickly after being secreted. When it swings its tail, the Quematrice can release this fluid as a gray gas that settles on the ground, then gets ignited by the sparks created from rubbing the pleats of its tail together or across the ground, with more viscous fluid creating hotter flames. The gas creates impressive flames, although they only burn for a very short time before dissipating, leading researchers to believe that they function more as a threat display rather than an actual weapon. Severing or otherwise damaging the Quematrice's tail makes it more difficult for it to create sparks. Additionally, if the Quematrice releases its Igniter fluid in water, it will be unable to ignite it.
Behavior
The Quematrice primarily inhabits the savanna areas of the Windward Plains, where large groups of the local Herbivores gather. It primarily rests inside cut-out areas of the cliffside. The Quematrice is chiefly a scavenger that feeds off carrion, particularly that of animals slain by other carnivores, often being found carrying carcasses in its jaws and carrying them to its lair. Highly opportunistic, the Quematrice will often fight to scare off and seize food from smaller predators, be it Talioth or Felynes delivering meat. Due to its preference to scavenge, the Quematrice is docile towards living herbivores. In contrast, it is highly intolerant towards competition from its own kind; when two Quematrice see each other, they immediately engage in combat and fight until one retreats.

Physiology
The Qurupeco is a medium-sized Bird Wyvern with a relatively small and compact body. Uniquely, it habitually holds its head high, giving it a distinctive silhouette amongst other Bird Wyverns. It is among the few extensively feathered Bird Wyverns, with lime down covering the majority of its neck and body, fading to a paler cream around its belly and cheeks, which are themselves covered in naked white-and-red skin. Lilac feathers grow along its neck and arms, with a display of particularly long feathers vividly decorating its back. This distinctive coloration is what granted it the nickname of Colorful Bird. Underneath this feathering is a concealed coating of scales. While its plumage typically makes them difficult to see, the dark-orange scales are plainly visible on the wyvern's feet and legs, with larger black scales growing out the back of its thighs. The scales of the Qurupeco are known to become sturdier with age.
The Qurupeco's neck is long and slender, while its head is narrow and heavily elongated, covered almost entirely by a black beak. A short black horn grows out from the back of the beak and its nostrils are modified to form an orange rubbery membrane that covers the upper jaw. While normally kept flush with its beak, it can be soften and stretched out to form a trumpet-shaped orifice when it is performing a call. Before broadcasting a call, the Qurupeco will inhale large quantities of air into the red teardrop-shaped gular skin on its chest, causing the organ to inflate in the process. This air is then passed into and through the membrane on its beak, causing it vibrate and produce sound. The wyvern possesses fine motor control over both organs, allowing it to create a wide variety of tones and even mimic the sounds produced by other monsters.
In addition to mimicry, it can combine these sounds with its dancing to temporarily increase its own metabolism, boosting its own power or defense. It has even been noted that these vocalizations have similar effects on any monster near the Qurupeco, with some songs causing monsters to instantly become angered. While these dances are typically viewed as courtship displays, they can also serve as a threat display when the wyvern is angered. Certain individuals are even known to produce songs capable of lulling listeners into a deep slumber. However, when performing its own vocalizations, the wyvern is vulnerable to disruptions from particularly loud sounds. Despite these abilities, it is believed that its vocal organs instead evolved primarily to allow for communication with other members of its species through the use of a wide variety of complex noises.
Its forelimbs are fashioned into a pair of wings, formed from a bright-green membrane supported by its arms and a single elongated finger. The remaining claws on its wings are fashioned into large Flintstones that, when struck together, are capable of producing sparks used both as a deterrent towards threats and as a weapon. The Qurupeco additionally produces a highly flammable mucus within its body that can either be spat out at enemies to make anything hit more flammable, or combined with its sparks to create small blasts of fire. The tail possesses an oar-like structure comprised of a pair of thick-rimmed membranes that run from the base to the tip; they are habitually contracted, fanning out whilst attacking or during certain displays. While these membranes are typically a pale-cream color, when angered they are flushed a more vibrant red.
Behavior
The Qurupeco primarily resides within both forested and arid regions, where it feeds primarily on fish and nuts. When threatened, the timid wyvern employs its unique ability to mimic the calls of other monsters to attract them, allowing it the opportunity to escape in the ensuing commotion. The movements the Qurupeco performs during its call will vary depending on the size of the monster summoned, as when summoning smaller monsters—such as the Jaggi —it will hold its wings to the ground and its head high in the air. Whereas for larger monsters, such as the Rathian, it will stand on one leg and swing its head in an arc.
The male and female Qurupeco typically live within separate territories, however during the breeding season, both sexes will migrate to areas with a more stable climate. Once the season has commenced, the male will attempt to use the same dancing and singing skills he displays during combat to attempt to court a female. To accomplish this, the male will attempt to make himself appear as large and flashy as possible by spreading out both his chest and tail, and using a wide-range of varied vocalizations, often resulting in the cries of the Qurupeco being heard far-and-wide during the breeding season. As he dances, he will click the flints on his wings together, a method that the wyvern utilizes in order to stay in rhythm to its own music. If the male successfully courts and mates with a female, the pair will construct their nest atop a high place in which the female will lay her eggs. A mated pair will incubate their eggs together, and both the male and the female will participate in raising their offspring, taking turns between watching the nest and gathering food. Unlike the adults, the chicks primarily subsume on earthworms and small insects.
A juvenile Qurupeco is born with its vocal apparatus already fully developed, and will begin practicing its songs very early. However, this can lead to it accidentally calling a dangerous predator to the nest, which the parents then counteract by imitating the calls of an even greater predator to scare the threat off. Specific calls and dances, typically those used to mimic and call for monsters, are believed to be passed down from the parents to their children, with the predominant cause of death for a Qurupeco chick being it falling from the nest whilst practicing its dances. Should a parent be present during such an incident, they may catch the falling chick with their wide fan-tail, which has been theorized to have evolved for this very purpose.

The Rachnoid is a small Temnoceran that blankets its purple spider-like body in a silky white thread. The Bone Hammer Wyvern Radobaan (ラドバルキン, Radobarukin) is a Brute Wyvern introduced in Monster Hunter: World.
Summary
Naturally ivory-colored Brute Wyverns enveloped by a layer of black tarred oil used to secure large bones to their body as armor, which also serve as the monster's primary food source. Although docile by nature, provoked Radobaan will attack by rolling around in a curled ball and bashing adversaries with their often bone-clad lower jaw. Radobaan can also emit a sleep inducing gas from their underside to subdue opponents.

Physiology
The Radobaan is a large, spiny Brute Wyvern sporting an ivory colored carapace layered in tarry oil. Incredibly picky about the bones it adorns its body with, among the more recognizable bones are a ribcage encasing its large lower jaw and horns reminiscent of those seen in the Diablos. These horns double as rudders, allowing the Radobaan to make sharp turns while rolling with additional precision. The ambiguous collection of bones accompanying its natural back spines are similar in this regard, affording the monster more traction when rolling at high speeds. Should these back spines be damaged, the Radobaan becomes more prone to losing traction and falling mid-roll. Beyond serving as the basis for its iconic traversal method, the Radobaan's bones serve the more obvious role of protection, acting as an armor that offers some reprieve from attempts at predation.
Immediately apparent in the Radobaan is the physical similarities it shares with the Uragaan. The two bear a strong resemblance to one another and their ecological parallels, as they both rely on rolling as their primary mode of transport and feed on hard substances: bones and Machalite respectively. Members of the Research Commission currently believe, based on the Radobaan being exclusive to the New World, that the species is an evolutionary response to the abundance of bones in the Rotten Vale, with it and the Uragaan potentially sharing a common ancestor whose bones still litter the region's boneyards. The Radobaan is quite different from most denizens of the Vale in its aversion to effluvium. Some researchers speculate the narrow paths in the region's upper layers to have been carved out by the gentle giant.
The Radobaan's dental structure is similar to that of its volcanic relative, featuring two rows of thick molars with a pair of small tusks jutting from its lower jaw, perfectly suited for grinding the bones it so carefully selects. Within the bones it ingests, it seeks to sustain itself on soft bone tissue and the Rotten Vale's bacterial microbiome.
Behavior
Despite the competitive nature of its environment, the Radobaan is a notably passive monster. Its size affords it a great deal of protection from most of the Rotten Vale's gallery of opportunists, with the bone armor it dons further dissuading potential predators. It achieves its tarry overcoat by burrowing beneath bone piles, layering itself in a sticky substance before meticulously picking out bones it deems worthy to affix to its armor. Upon detecting choice bones, the Radobaan strategically augments its defense by rolling around in the selected boneyard before emerging with its new selection. Should it find itself to be the target of an assailant capable of standing up to its sheer size, the Radobaan can resort to expelling a sleep-inducing gas built up from its digestion of bacteria and bones from the pores on its underbelly as a secret weapon.
Although the Radobaan is normally skittish in the presence of other large monsters, it has been seen holding its ground against the Odogaron.
Feeding on the bones of carcasses that have fallen from the Coral Highlands, the Radobaan takes advantage of its rolling speed's capability to outpace its bipedal movement to traverse the upper layers of the Rotten Vale with exceptional proficiency. The traction gained from its spike-like armor allowing it to maintain fine control of its movement, even making hairpin turns by driving the exceptionally large horns on its legs into the ground.
The male Radobaan will adorn itself in bones to attract a female, with more orderly arrangements of bones denoting a higher presentability to the opposite sex. Further, although the Radobaan lays eggs, it does not care for its young. A Female will bury her eggs underground, beneath corpses and bones where they're kept warm by thermal decomposition. By laying eggs underground, the newborns will be exposed to the tar layer at a very young age, allowing them to quickly adhere a layer of bones to themselves for protection.
Development
Tokuda notes that the Rotten Vale is covered in three main layers, the topmost strata being covered in bones. As such, the team wanted a monster that could make use of these bones by affixing them to its body.
He additionally recalled the "hellish" imagery the Rotten Vale had going for it, so he wanted Radobaan to take cues from Wanyūdō, a yokai with a human head attached to a flaming wheel that also gets around by rolling. With Uragaan already having been a well-established monster in the series, Tokuda states it felt realistic for Radobaan to be a closely related but evolutionarily different monster in the New World.
Though Uragaan wasn't initially planned to be a part of Monster Hunter: World, the development of Radobaan would ultimately lead to its inclusion. According to Fujioka, the team wanted to make a looped pathway in the Rotten Vale, going onto believe a monster that could speed through that region would be a good fit. They considered that the bones Radobaan would use wouldn't be as tough as the Machalite Ore used in Uragaan's shell and felt it would make the Radobaan look weaker, as such, they started "heaping mounds of bones on it." Fujioka humorously remarks that what came out of that process was the Radobaan we know today, a monster that "looks way fiercer than Uragaan ever did."

The Rafma (ラフマー, Rafumā) is a Herbivore introduced in Monster Hunter Wilds.
Summary
Small Herbivores adapted to live and move alongside steep, frozen cliffsides. Rafma live in small herds led by a singular large alpha individual, distinguished by their more developed horns. These horns store static electricity inside, which can be discharged to fend off anything that threatens the herd, shocking even large monsters in place.

Physiology
The Rafma is a quadrupedal Herbivore displaying a similar build to that of an Anteka, although with an overall posture more akin to a horse. The legs are muscular, with the feet sporting black two-toed hooves and two dewclaws on the posterior side. The lumbar section of the Rafma's spinal region is hairless and covered in a platinum-colored carapace that is also found on the sides of its large and muscular neck, the top of the head, and the upper lip. The mouth lacks teeth on the upper jaw, with the lower jaw sporting a row of incisors. The eyes are amber colored and possess horizontally slit pupils.
The body coat exhibits a notable brindle pattern, with lesser individuals possessing a golden-tan color, and an alpha Rafma boasting a burnt-orange coloration as well as a larger mane on its neck. Another striking trait that varies between the two varieties of Rafma are the large notched horns that adorn their foreheads. These horns are much larger in an alpha individual, and the base of them—along with the protrusions on its neck—appear to glow a faint yellow in dark environments. The horns additionally accumulate static electricity, and can be broken off using a Hook Slinger to grant Hunters Para Pods.
Behavior
The Rafma is generally docile, being typically sighted moving in a herd of around three to six individuals, most often accompanied by an alpha in tow. This alpha individual is the herd's primary defense against adversaries and will defend them vigilantly. When faced with a threat, the alpha Rafma will selflessly charge at its opponent, electricity brimming from its horns. When these horns connect with their target, the monster is immediately paralyzed, allowing for the rest of the herd to quickly escape. This electric charge is strong enough to even affect naturally Thunder-resistant monsters, such as the Gypceros. Additionally, the Rafma can periodically be observed scaling exceptionally steep cliffsides, using its superior agility to leap between ledges.

Physiology
The Raging Brachydios is easily distinguished from the comparatively much smaller Brachydios by its far greater size, discolored shell, and constantly primed Slime Mold. Regarded as the sturdiest known material, the surface of the Raging Brachydios' staggeringly blast resistant Ebonshell bears an incomparable quantity of slime to the regular Brachydios, which has caused the body to take on a greenish coloration that gives off an emerald glow. Investigation into the Variant's coloration difference yielded the discovery and presence of mineral components on the shell's surface that are formed only under high-temperature and high-pressure environments. This is believed to be the factor that resulted in the Raging Brachydios' discoloration, furthermore, having been pushed to a critical state, the Slime Mold's astounding explosive force has likely altered the shell. Moreover, the head and forelimbs—areas that are typically discolored—as well as the back, torso, and tail have been variegated by the activated Slime Mold, signified by a constant yellow hue. Warped by rage, the Raging Brachydios' skull is considered the pinnacle of materials, and its tail resembles that of its ancestors.
Able to proliferate only under specific conditions native to select regions of the world, the specialized strain of Slime Mold used by the Raging Brachydios differs greatly to that of the standard variety's. Ordinarily, the Slime Mold scatters spores upon detonating that begin to germinate immediately after, however, these spores will fail to germinate under rare circumstances and will enter a dormant state buried under strata. In extremely rare occurrences, when such Slime Mold reawakens due to tectonic shifts or magma eruption, it exhibits a dangerously activated state capable of producing tremendously powerful explosions. Having stored energy underground for several years in this state of dormancy, the Slime Mold generates staggering explosive force when it suddenly reactivates and is in a significantly more intense activation state than ordinary Slime Molds. The sheer magnitude of the explosive force released by the reactivated Slime Mold is astonishing, earning it the name of Flashpoint Slime.
In its normal state, the critical mass of slime that envelops the Raging Brachydios drips onto the ground before exploding. Although it generates the same explosive force upon detonation, it is considerably more dangerous in comparison to the standard Slime Mold, as the time until detonation is much shorter and it carries the risk of inflicting burns. Nevertheless, it may be calmed down or washed off the Raging Brachydios' body with the use of Watermoss, or with weaponry infused with the Water element. However, the Raging Brachydios' Slime Mold Active State exhibits the activation of its Flashpoint Slime, which itself displays proliferation and increased activity. Characterized by a red hue that signifies its approaching criticality, it appears to be actively and rapidly stimulated by the Variant's excited state. The Raging Brachydios' slime is far more volatile than that which can be found on the regular Brachydios, with the Flashpoint Slime accumulated heavily on its head and forelimbs gradually turning red. Extreme caution is necessitated, as merely touching the primed slime will cause it to explode.
The Raging Brachydios' enlarged body is influenced by environmental factors, alongside a reversal to ancestral traits triggered by mutation. For the Brachydios, the strength of its symbiotic Slime Mold directly correlates to its own, and it is expected of any male of the species to seek out and show off greater power. Naturally, if the Brachydios is unable to withstand the explosive force of the activated Slime Mold, it will either perish on the spot, or flee and seek out an ordinary colony instead. The reason the Raging Brachydios developed a body much larger than usual likely lies in this extraordinary power, as from its perspective, it is an irresistible Slime Mold whose hardships are worth overcoming. Its symbiosis with the Slime Mold at the critical threshold of immense explosive force places significant strain on its entire body, thus, only a Brachydios possessing such a robust and hefty frame is able to secure its survival as a Variant upon bonding with the special Slime Mold. Believed perhaps to be due to the weight it has gained proportional to its size, or to dampen the impact of the attached Slime Mold, the Raging Brachydios' movements are overall heavier. However, this heaviness allows it to concentrate great amounts of force into each individual strike, granting it exceptionally high attack power.
Having bonded with a rare and specialized Slime Mold, the Raging Brachydios is a specimen that bears a high concentration of a Slime Mold which displays an exaggerated activation rate. Due to this, should the entire Slime Mold colony on the Raging Brachydios activate to the point of reaching critical mass, it is able to trigger a state whose extreme danger is self evident and which does not appear favorable, even for it. Marked by a brownish hue permeating the body and a steam-like vapor escaping from its head and forelimbs, it is the species' truest form. Poised to strike down any foe using its full might, it is regarded as the Raging Brachydios' Slime Mutation Activation State. By utilizing its Immortal Reactor, a rare and hard to obtain organ, the Raging Brachydios is able to render its slime more volatile when in peril. The Flashpoint Slime, when primed and at its most volatile, is capable of generating blasts well beyond the capability of any bomb, living up to the name of Raging Explosion. Despite its normally impervious blast resistance, the blasts are able to inflict serious harm to the Raging Brachydios when it is in this state. Thus, perhaps to prevent itself from inflicting injuries to itself, the Raging Brachydios will scatter the slime over a vast area with a sudden roar once its activation has progressed sufficiently. Any puddles of it showing signs of activating should be promptly eliminated or pacified, as the Slime Mold that has permeated the area will promptly be engulfed in a massive explosion.
Behavior
Prior to the Raging Brachydios' emergence, the existence of a rare variation of the Brachydios was merely speculated upon. It wasn't until the prophecy contained within the 7th Aged Text was deciphered that the Raging Brachydios' existence was confirmed by the Hunter's Guild. This ancient text—entitled Aged: Crusher —prophesized the emergence of the Variant and warned of its deadly slime; based on the ancient documents, the Guild came to call the Variant the Fierce Exploding Brachydios, and has collaborated with both researchers and Scriveners to expedite investigative expeditions surrounding the Raging Brachydios.
In the Old World, the specialized Slime Mold has only been confirmed in the Ingle Isle, a harsh environment that nurtures unique Slime Molds and where magma and rock solidify. The Brachydios is able to instinctively recognize differences between Slime Molds due to its drive to heighten its power and sex appeal, which encourages it to travel to the Ingle Isle in search of the specialized Slime Molds native to the region. However, the Brachydios will not search far and wide for it, rather, it will be drawn to the Ingle Isle by chance. Consequently, the Raging Brachydios' presence in the Guiding Lands of the New World came as a great shock to the Research Commission, although even there, its activity appears to be limited to an extremely narrow range centered around the volcanic region. The anomalous activity of the specialized Slime Mold has always been attributed to the unique environment of the Ingle Isle, however, following close examination of the Slime Mold present in the Raging Brachydios of the Old World, it was concluded the activation states were identical across both continents. In the opinion of researchers familiar with the Ingle Isle's climate, the volcanic region of the Guiding Lands shares a striking resemblance to the environment of the Ingle Isle; further investigation is needed to determine which of the two is the source.
Reports indicate the Raging Brachydios' behavior patterns are extremely dangerous, as it makes use of its inherent fighting instinct in tandem with its immense explosive power. During combat, the Raging Brachydios will swing its forelimbs and head, as well as scrape them along the ground to propel the Slime Mold's explosive discharge and drive prey into a corner. Similarly, attacking the Variant from the rear is ill-advised, as it is notably vigilant and will lash foes with its tail. Additionally, in the Guiding Lands, the Raging Brachydios exhibits a certain behavior during battle that has not yet been observed in the Old World. When a formidable opponent threatens the Raging Brachydios to the degree it senses its imminent peril, it will lure the battle to a more strategic area; in the case of the Guiding Lands, it will migrate deep into the core of the volcanic region.
This is not the Variant retreating to the safety of its nest, nor it fleeing its opponent, instead, the Raging Brachydios aims to lure its foe into a location that is advantageous to itself to secure victory. Should its pursuer follow it, the Raging Brachydios will unleash a wrathful barrage upon the ground, activating Slime Mold that permeates the entire area and triggering an instant, enormous explosion that uplifts terrain to block any exit and engulfs the entire area in a sea of scorching heat. Through this sheer heat intermixing with slime, the battle ground known as the Land of Death nullifies the effects of the Farcaster and prevents Hunters from being able to place traps. Conversely, the fiery inferno the Raging Brachydios has produced consumes its own stamina and causes it to fight with far more ferociousness in a desperate attempt to eliminate the threat as swiftly as possible, even if it must withstand the harm of its own explosions to do so.

The Gold Lion Rajang (ラージャン, Raajan) is a Fanged Beast introduced in Monster Hunter 2.
Summary
Extraordinarily ill-tempered Fanged Beasts covered in black fur and boasting a pair of curved horns, Rajang are so reclusive and aggressive that few are seen and even fewer are survived. In addition to their phenomenal strength, Rajang can fire electricity from their mouth, and can grow so angry that their fur turns bright gold and stands on end, even being capable of toughening their arms to further increase their destructive power. However, reports state that damaging their tail can quench their anger.
