Physiology
The Rajang is a powerful Fanged Beast characterized by the pitch-black fur coat across the majority of its body, with its skin being hairless around its chest, face, hands, and hind legs. This fur consists of thick, tough hairs that form together to create an insulator layer between the surface of the pelt and the surface of the underlying skin. This protective layer prevents outside air from reaching the Rajang's skin, completely sealing it off from outside temperatures. It is believed that this adaptation allows the beast to survive a wide range of extreme environments that range from scorching volcanoes, to frozen wastelands, and any other variety of harsh climates. The Rajang possesses two large twisted horns that jut outwards from the sides of its head, decorated with ridges from the base to the tip. These golden horns are believed to somehow be related to its emotional regulation, as impact to the the horns appears to greatly affect the monster's temperament. They are hard enough to pierce the scales of even Elder Dragons and additionally serve as an indicator of an individual's strength amongst male specimens. The Rajang additionally sports a short and slim tail with a tuft of black fur at its tip.
While its hind legs adopt a digitigrade stance, its forelimbs exhibit knuckle-walking—the combined stance is what enables the swift movements the beast displays. While this physique is common across several Fanged Beasts, what sets the Rajang apart is how developed its upper body truly is, granting it truly immense physical strength. This strength is especially concentrated into its large and muscular arms, allowing it to dislodge large pieces of the earth to hurl at enemies, or simply batter adversaries to death—a sight described as profoundly intimidating. Furthermore, the particularly well-developed structure of its arms is noted as being quite similar to those of a human, especially in its hands, which sport an opposable thumb each. This grants it excellent dexterity and gripping ability, allowing it to grab prey or other objects, as well as brace itself if it were about to fall.
Nonetheless, the most peculiar feature of the Rajang is its ability to weaponize the Thunder element. Despite lacking any kind of elemental sac organ, it is able to generate and expel both lightning—in the form of spherical blasts—as well as highly destructive lasers of golden light. Furthermore, it is able to undergo a startling transformation in which parts of its black fur turn a glistening-golden and begin to stand on end, granting it the nickname of Golden Lion. This form, called the " Battle Spirit State " (闘気), is considered so powerful that it strikes fear into even the hearts of Elder Dragons. This change in coloration occurs due to the unique properties of the Rajang's hairs: their hollow structure and high conductivity. When electricity generated inside its body travels through these cavities, the resulting charge causes its hairs to be dyed a brilliant gold. Even once the fur is removed from the body, it continues to retain its electrical charge and will still glow gold.
In this form, as its entire body overflows with power, each of the Rajang's Thunder abilities are enhanced and its muscles' power output is multiplied significantly. Beyond increasing the potency of its attacks, this heightened performance bestows the Rajang with improved mobility that enables it to execute more agile movements. Although, should the beast need additional power it will flood its forearm muscles with a stimulating current, causing them to swell so violently that they turn red and begin to emit steam. During this vehement form, known as the its Rampage Mode, the Rajang's arms grow as hard as steel and will deflect most attacks, as well as allow it to retaliate with enough monstrous force to tear through bedrock. While the Rampage Mode is extremely powerful, the Rajang will be instantly forced out of it should its tail be injured sufficiently, with it being believed to play a similar role to its horns in regulating its emotions.
Curiously, the Rajang is not capable of accessing the Battle Spirit State from birth. While it appears to have an inherent affinity for the Thunder element, its full power must be unlocked through a very special maturity ritual: upon reaching a certain size and age, the Rajang must set out and hunt a Kirin. Following a successful hunt, the beast will tear off the Elder Dragon's horn and devour it. As a result, special electrolytes within the horn will then react with its body and activate its latent potential, unleashing the Battle Spirit State for the first time in its life. Once this has occurred, the Rajang gains complete control over its Thunder abilities and becomes a fully mature adult.
While the Rajang is now classified as a Fanged Beast, there used to be a significant amount of scholarly discussion over its classification. Its unusual and overwhelming power set it apart from other Fanged Beasts, and for a time it was even suggested that it should be considered an Elder Dragon. Key to this confusion was the presence of multiple conflicting reports regarding its appearance, as while some witnesses described it as "black as night," others spoke of its "golden wings shining brightly." These discrepancies were eventually understood to be the result of the Rajang's ability to transform, with the reports of "wings" originating from an onlooker seeing the large tufts of golden fur that stand up from the beast's back during its Battle Spirit State and mistaking them for wings. For a time, it was also believed there might be multiple Subspecies of the Rajang, although that too was eventually concluded to have been a misunderstanding due to the changing fur color. It has since been theorized that the Rajang evolved from a population of the Blangonga which had to rapidly adapt to extreme climate conditions, although there is not enough evidence to verify this theory currently.
Behavior
The Rajang can be found roaming all sorts of environments due to its tendency to migrate often, establishing new and vast territories each time. This migrating behavior stems from its reputation of fighting just about anything it encounters, which has the adverse effect of causing lesser creatures to flee in fear as soon as it appears in a region, resulting in a lack of food if it does not move. In battle, the Rajang is extremely brutal and capable of annihilating most opponents through sheer power, and it is even rumored that following the sound of its roars will lead one to the carcass of an Elder Dragon. Moreover, it appears to possess a non-trivial degree of intelligence, such as purposely evading Pitfall Traps, or intercepting those attempting to clutch onto its body. Detailed reports on the Rajang remain scarce as most people that encounter it do not return alive, and those who do are often so shaken that they refuse to ever speak of the matter. It is thus no wonder the Rajang is considered one of the most dangerous monsters outside of the Elder Dragon class, feared all around the world for its power.
Despite being an omnivore, the Rajang prefers a carnivorous diet, with it curiously seeming to prefer the taste of meat from monsters that also utilize the Thunder element in some capacity. Even though it technically only has to hunt a Kirin once in its life to unlock its internal electrical production, it has been noted that some individuals may continue hunting the Elder Dragon afterwards as well, presumably for its meat. Beyond its aggression however, the Rajang appears to be quite confident in its abilities, as indicated by its habit of sleeping with its belly exposed and without any concern for its safety. As a result of being a completely solitary creature, nothing is known about its social or mating behavior. Conjointly, as none have ever been sighted or found, it is unknown what a juvenile Rajang may look like.
Super Biology Information
The Super Biology Book Series collects the thoughts and theories of real scientists that were asked to speak about monsters from the Monster Hunter series. Thus, they are inherently speculative and should be seen as such.
Zoological Author Yuumin Mori takes a look at Rajang and notes the peculiar absence of any data regarding reproduction and child rearing. Based on this monster’s rarity, Mori assumes that Rajang are likely fully solitary, usually considering any and all members of their own species rivals, much like they would other creatures. The Rajang’s mating behavior might thus be similar to that of cats: Males and females only approach each other sexually during very limited times, and even then, the interaction can turn sour at any moment. If mating is successful, males leave the female immediately, with the mother Rajang caring for her young until they themselves reach sexual maturity. Mori however points out that Rajang have never been observed pairing up, which leads him to three possible explanations: a) Rajang only mate in a specific, extremely remote breeding ground that has not been discovered yet; b) Rajang have extremely long fertility cycles and only become interested in reproduction very rarely; c) Rajang might reach sexual maturity extremely early in their lives and mate when they are still quite young, before they begin roaming around.
Rajang are known for their elusive and solitary nature, which Mori takes as evidence to suggest that their overall population size is quite low. He proposes that this might be related to the amount of food a single Rajang requires - those muscles must burn an enormous amount of energy, perhaps so much that nature can only support a small number of Rajang at once. The lonesome Rajang might thus also attempt to avoid meetings with others of its kin, as such an encounter could turn violent. Mori proposes that Rajang probably use territorial markings and secretions not to claim a particular zone, but rather to communicate with other distant Rajang to stay away and delay their arrival if they are headed that way too. With this “travel-lag” strategy, even the solitary Rajang end up cooperating to stay away from each other. Mori also asserts that the horns of the Rajang may be used for communication across shorter distances, with their shape and size warning potential rivals in advance. He also wonders if the horns may only be as large and visible on males, comparing them to those seen in the Order Artiodactyla. Sexual dimorphism may also be expressed through body size, and Mori wonders if the Gold Crown large and small individuals might be male and female Rajang respectively.
Discussing the Rajang’s habitat, Mori proposes that the beast’s ability to generate and discharge electricity probably also aids in heat regulation. Additionally, while Rajang have been sighted in both volcanic and arctic habitats, those might not actually be the same kind of monster: Mori ponders that perhaps the Rajang species can be split into two populations, one adapted to the heat of the volcano and one evolved to survive in the bitter cold, and that those two populations do not actually venture far out from their respective habitats. Furthermore, Mori notes that regardless of hot or cold, Rajang is consistently found in extreme environments. He thus suggests that the Rajang may have a genetically weak immune system, and that its habitat is a result of the species fleeing towards extreme temperatures where many types of bacteria cannot survive.
The Rajang’s ability to turn its black fur coat golden is quite infamous, and Mori proposes an explanation for how it might work. Generally, the color of hair is determined by the presence of certain amounts of melanin. It might be possible that Rajang can alter the amount and density of melanin in its fur - but this would necessarily imply that a Rajang’s fur is alive, unlike the dead matter that makes up all other known types of hair. Mori suggests an alternative; perhaps the hairs of the Rajang are hollow, which would allow microorganisms to nest within it. If the Rajang’s natural hair color were then white or light, the color of the accumulated organisms would alter the appearance of the beast, as is seen with captive Polar Bears turning green due to algae growing within their fur. Mori proposes that perhaps such organisms could in fact be the source of the Rajang’s electric power, as well as the reason for its remote habitat: The Rajang lives in symbiosis with microorganic colonies that nest within its fur. These organisms are able to produce electricity, but are sensitive to temperature. The fur of the Rajang thus shields them from extreme cold and heat, and in return, the beast augments its power with the electricity produced within the microorganic colonies.

Development
Rajang was created by Yuya Tokuda. It was added into Monster Hunter 2 at the very last minute, and due to most other members of the development team being too busy with end-of-production responsibilities, Tokuda had to test Rajang by himself. His feedback was then used to balance the stats and AI of Rajang around the idea that it would be fought by "four Tokudas". Since Yuya Tokuda is noted to be quite skilled at Monster Hunter, this led to Rajang being extremely difficult even for skilled players, establishing its reputation for years to come.
According to Kaname Fujioka, the inspiration behind Rajang was the Monster Hunter team's desire to create their own version of the character Akuma from the Street Fighter series. Its ability to harden its arms and throw giant boulders from Monster Hunter 4 onwards was inspired by the Incredible Hulk comics.
Originally, Rajang was intended to be called "Gorilaion" (ゴリライオン). The name was later changed to "Rajang", borrowing the Sanskrit word for "King" (rājan).

Physiology
The Rakna-Kadaki is a large Temnoceran, having a heftier body compared to other members of its class. It has the ability to extend its neck outward, allowing it to lunge out at prey, or have better reach with its fiery breath attacks; it can additionally expel fire from its abdomen. Its body is adorned with spikes all throughout which grow large and curved. Its body sports shades of light and dark grays, as well as hints of burgundy along its two front claws and mouth. Its claws are extremely hard, allowing the Rakna-Kadaki to shatter a dragon's hide with a single punch. However, most of its body is covered with silken webs, made surprisingly durable to cushion it and its young from attacks on top of its already defensive shells. These silken threads give the Rakna-Kadaki an appearance of elegance and beauty, and any items woven from the threads evoke eternal glory. On the abdomen, it bears luminous organs known as Glowguts that function to repel those that would attack its babies. When angered, it fixes all its silken threads and covers its abdomen to make a large cocoon for its young, while also using it as a form of attack and defense against foes.
The Rakna-Kadaki faced by Hunters are all noted to be female, as the males are roughly the same size as the Rachnoids that cling onto their mother's abdomen.
Behavior
The Rakna-Kadaki is a highly aggressive monster that will attack many other foes who are within its area, considered to possess a "fiery temper." Against both prey and foe alike, this Temnoceran uses webs to trap them in place, before unleashing surges of flaming breath attacks to burn them alive. While not as physically agile as other Temnocerans, the Rakna-Kadaki will make use of the terrain if possible to make up for this. It may attach itself onto cave ceilings to hang in the air, allowing for its heated gas exhaustions and breath attacks to cover more ground. It may also use its young during combat, able to throw them around using silk threads to either trap or burn targets, or for the Rakna-Kadaki to pull itself across an area. Having its young attached to it at all times, the Rakna-Kadaki is constantly roaming around to both stay out of danger or to find a meal for both itself and its babies.

The Raphinos (ラフィノス, Rafinosu) is a small Wingdrake introduced in Monster Hunter: World.
Summary

They primarily feed on the countless coral eggs released into their environment, though they themselves often fall prey to the larger monsters in the region. Physiology
The Raphinos is a docile Wingdrake native to the Coral Highlands. It has a similar body plan to other Wingdrakes: a large head with a beak, forelimbs modified into wings, taloned feet, and a tail. The underside of its body is covered by cream skin, while the upper side is peach-colored. The skull is boxy compared to other Wingdrakes, with its dark beak being tall, broad, and sporting nostrils which are set high up on the beak. Behind the beak are the beady black eyes, and on top of the head and neck is a row of fleshy filaments.
The muscular chest serves as the anchor for the wings, each of which have two long digits that the membrane stretches between and a shorter free digit with a claw; the longer digits end in filaments trailing behind the wing. The wing membranes are also supported by a flexible rod extending from the elbow. The thick legs have feet adorned with gray scales, and each foot has four toes with sharp talons. The tail is stout compared to other Wingdrakes and sports two membranes on either side that taper into more filaments. The Raphinos' whole body is streamlined to take full advantage of the wind as it flies.
Behavior
The Raphinos is commonly seen in small groups in the Coral Highlands and Coral Region of the Guiding Lands. Its diet includes the eggs of land coral, found in a species of pink tree-like coral that releases eggs en masse. When these tree-corals begin to produce eggs, multiple groups of the Wingdrake congregate beneath them, with the sight of a flock of Raphinos frolicking under the coral being considered to be incredibly beautiful. It rarely lands, only to groom itself.
The flesh of the Raphinos is full of flavor, making it a common prey item for the carnivores that share its habitat. When danger approaches, the Wingdrake will fly sporadically and make noise to alert others of its kind. Like when feeding, smaller flocks will join with others, forming large swarms of panicked Wingdrakes. The Raphinos is the primary food source of the Legiana, which specifically targets large groups of them, swooping through the flock with incredible grace. The Raphinos that have been scattered when fleeing predators will rejoin the main flock when the danger is gone.
The Raphinos will stagger in the air if it is damaged; this allows a Hunter to hook onto its feet with the Slinger. The Wingdrake, along with its entire flock, will then fly to a nearby area. After the hunter's Slinger falls off, the flock flies back to where it came from.
The Raphinos can also be found in the Rotten Vale. Many of these are dead individuals that fell from the Coral Highlands, although the others are individuals that have been infected by Effluvium and have become aggressive. An infected Raphinos will attack hunters on sight by either ramming them, or kicking with its talons. An infected Raphinos is also attracted to the Vaal Hazak, seemingly under the Elder Dragon's control.
Development
Monster Hunter World: The Official Complete Works presents concept art of small monsters in the context of being unreviewed sketches made by members of the Research Commission. Concept art of Raphinos follows an "aquatic theme." The designs generally have bright, pastel colors and wings that resemble fins. Some foreshadow the hard beak of the final product, while others possess a wide mouth and throat pleats like a whale.

Physiology
The Rathalos is an archetypal Flying Wyvern, displaying the common body type of the class: two hind limbs, two large wings consisting of a membrane stretched over bone phalanges, and a long tail; his ends with a bulbous spiked tip. The Rathalos belongs to the same species as the Rathian and is the male counterpart, he can be distinguished by his red and black shell, blue eyes, and lack of the female's characteristic toxic barbs, which is believed to be an adaptation that reduces air resistance on his body during flight. The Rathalos additionally sports a shorter chin spike, which is solid and thicker than in the Rathian; during the breeding season, this spike grows notably.
The signature red shell of the Rathalos is unique in many ways, as instead of being a fused armor shell with a handful of gaps to account for joints, the Rathalos' shell consists of large armor plates that sit on top of flexible hide, which itself is covered in small scales. The shells are not fused together and thus do not impede the wyvern's range of movement. While this reduces the defensive capabilities of the shell somewhat, the structure grants the Rathalos unparalleled flexibility and articulation among Flying Wyverns, especially around the upper torso and shoulders. This adaptation is believed to be key to the monster's mastery of flight. Very rarely, a Rathalos may grow a reverse scale that points against the grain of the rest of its coat. Such a deformed scale is called a Rathalos Plate and emerges from deep within the wyvern's skin, causing its owner significant pain when touched and making it difficult to carve and study. Some believe that the appearance of such reverse scales is a sign of further evolution within the Rathalos species, although the idea remains unverified at the moment.
The Rathalos possesses excellent eyesight that allows him to spot prey from the air and swoop down on it with speed and precision. In one instance, a scholar had camped atop the peak of a tall mountain for an entire month solely to witness the Rathalos capture its prey in a sky-bound hunt, a privilege few are granted. However, while his impressive sight is oftentimes a boon, many Hunters know the Rathalos' eyes can be easily weaponized against him, as flashes of light or other assaults to the sensitive eyes will send him crashing to the ground, flailing in a panic. The Rathalos sports elongated toes that allow him to securely grip his bounty. However, to avoid the length of these toes interfering with walking on land, the Rathalos instinctively curls them when grounded, shortening them and thus maintaining a respectable degree of terrestrial mobility. Moreover, the Rathalos is able to secrete venom from its talons that robs the strength of afflicted prey. The inner edges of the Rathalos' talons are serrated, an adaptation that ensures that gripped prey cannot easily escape the wyvern's grasp.
Just like the Rathian, the Rathalos is capable of spitting out fire balls through a specialized Flame Sac in the body that produces and stores a flammable powder, which can be used to create a flaming breath. The Rathalos is capable of unleashing these flames even from the air.
The Rathalos found in the New World differs in some key ways from the population of the Old World. The New World Rathalos has an additional bone phalanx in its wings, granting them greater stability and structure. As well, its thighs are notably thicker and stronger, leading to more effective take-offs. It is believed these adaptations allowed the Rathalos to steal control of the Ancient Forest's treetop ecosystem from the Pukei-Pukei when it migrated to the New World long ago.
Behavior
The Rathalos is a powerful predator that dominates the ecosystems he resides in. In the Old World, the wyvern is known far and wide as the King of the Skies due to his extraordinary airborne agility and wild intensity during a hunt. Meanwhile, the First Wyverians of the New World call the Rathalos the Lord of the Forest in reference to and reverence in of its iron grip over the Ancient Forest's food chain. The Rathalos is an extremely territorial and aggressive monster, to a degree that it used to be common practice within the Guild's territories to ring alarm bells at the slightest hint of this wyvern's presence.
Using his powerful wings, the Rathalos can stay airborne for several days without rest. Once he spots suitable prey from above, it assaults it relentlessly, attempting to slash it with his toxic talons. Once envenomated, the victim loses the strength to fight back and the Rathalos grabs it tightly, flying back to his nest to feast while the venom finishes the job. If the Rathalos chooses to spend some time on the ground, his sheer power makes fending off other creatures easy. Further, the wyvern is not opposed to scavenging and will bully smaller monsters, like the Velociprey, off their kills. However, the Rathalos has no issue with carrying corpses or live individuals during flight to devour at his nest if necessary. Aside from hunting, the Rathalos may spend his time marking his territory by leaving characteristic claw marks across the land he claims.
During the breeding season, the Rathalos will seek out the Rathian. Here, the behavior between the Rathalos of the Old World and the Rathalos of the New World differs greatly. In the Old World, the Rathian and Rathalos will form a monogamous mated pair that equally shares parenting duties. Meanwhile, the New World Rathalos will mate with an entire harem of Rathian, and only the most dominant female will be allowed to raise her offspring with the Rathalos. All the other Rathian are pushed out of the male's territory and take residence in the Wildspire Waste, where they must raise their young on their own. By contrast, the chosen Rathian will enjoy the loyal and ferocious protection of her mated Rathalos. As far as parenting goes, the Rathalos will use his enlarged chin spike to help build the nest by digging up the necessary materials, and once the eggs are laid, he will take on the role of surveying the territory from above and vanquishing potential threats to the young indiscriminately.
After the young grow to a certain size, the Rathian will hand over parental duties to the Rathalos, who will begin bringing small live prey to the nest to develop the juveniles' hunting instinct. The most important development comes when the young develop their wings to a point at which they can just about fly clumsily. When the Rathalos notices its young reach that stage he will pick up his young and transport them away from the nest, leaving them on cliffsides and other areas with strong, yet stable wind currents. If the juveniles wish to return to the safety of the nest, they must learn to fly by themselves and consistently. This behavior is believed to be a test by the parent, and only juveniles that are able to take off and return home grow into adults.
Due to their ecological dominance and fascinating social behavior, both the Rathalos and Rathian have long since inspired awe among the people. There are even areas—such as the hunting town of Dundorma —in which the pair are worshiped as part of a religious belief. Within the Hunter's Guild, facing a Rathalos in battle is considered a rite of passage for those that wish to become true hunters. Subsequently, wearing armor made from the Rathalos' materials is said to be a sign of authority and strength, proving that one stands above even the King of the Skies.
Super Biology Information
The Super Biology Book Series collects the thoughts and theories of real scientists that were asked to speak about monsters from the Monster Hunter series. Thus, they are inherently speculative and should be seen as such.
Fossil Expert Yoshitsugu Kobayashi notes in his report that the Rathian and Rathalos are likely poorly suited for movement on land: The tibia and femur bones in their legs are the same length, which suggests limited mobility when walking. By comparison, the wings of the two wyverns possess a number of internal bones - similar to bats - which suggests that they are exceptionally good at turning and maneuvering mid-air. Kobayashi also theorizes however that the trade-off here might be that these wings excel at short-distance bursts of agility to hunt prey, but are less suited for long-distance migratory flights. Either way, since the Rathian and Rathalos rely so heavily on their wings, Kobayashi believes that they are unlikely to degenerate over the course of evolution.
Kobayashi notes that both the Rathian and the Rathalos are covered in short, backwards pointing spikes, which he suggests likely evolved as a way to defend against attacks from above and behind. The angle and arrangement of the spikes prioritizes defending the back of the neck, and Kobayashi likens it to structures that were possibly found on Pachycephalosaurus. The spikes could have also served as decoration.
Rathian and Rathalos’ parenting strategy - wherein the female secures food while the male defends the young - reminds Kobayashi of descriptions of Troodontidae. Such a division of labor is known to increase survival rates through specialization of the parents. Kobayashi also notes that this sometimes leads to females of a species being more physically powerful than the males, as it has been proposed to be the case with Tyrannosaurus rex.
The Rathian and Rathalos’ ability to create and expel fire is considered a miracle beyond all known limits of nature, as no real creature has ever been observed having such an ability. Kobayashi asserts that because in traditional biology, internal tissue is known to break down at temperatures nearing or exceeding 45 °C, the Raths must possess special organs made from special cells that are exceptionally heat resistant. The flame production mechanism must require fuel, ignition and expulsion processes, and Kobayashi believes that these three elements are handled by this species’ Flame Sac, which likely sits near the lungs. A specialized one-way valve connects the Sac to the lungs: Fire and fuel is prevented from entering the lungs, but air from the lungs can be pushed into the Sac to catalyze the flame creation and funnel the created fire breath into the throat to be expelled by the mouth.
Music
Main article: Rathalos (Music)
"Roar" is Rathalos' theme. It is an iconic track that has been used many times for cross-promotional material involving Rathalos. While the Verdant Hills theme "Roar - Rathalos" was only associated with Rathalos, it was not until Monster Hunter Wilds that "Roar" would be tied to Rathalos itself in-game. Before Wilds, it was the only flagship in mainline games outside of Azure Rathalos and Lagiacrus that did not have a theme tied to it in-game. In the Wilds version, "Roar" contains motifs from "Awakening", the theme for Kokoto village.
"Roar" is also directly used for Fatalis’ theme, " The Legend Descends ", a track that simply adds vocals on top of the main melody.
Monster Hunter
After Rathian had been created fairly early into the development of the first Monster Hunter game and following the addition of Kaname Fujioka to the team, Rathalos was created with the express purpose of being the game's mascot monster. In order to be more memorable and have a more "main character" feel, the team modified the existing Rathian design by removing the barbs, changing the shell shape and altering the color from green to red. In terms of gameplay, Fujioka initially recommended that Rathalos should not use the poison ailment like Rathian, as the mascot of the game fighting with such tricky tactics felt off to him. From this, the team developed the Rathalos to be an airborne menace with a powerful flame breath that would signal destructive power and violence to the player. Ultimately, Fujioka returned to the matter of the poison ailment and chose to add it back into the Rathalos' arsenal to create a stronger connection between it and Rathian. However, unlike Rathian, Rathalos would use the posion through its talons.
By far the most difficult aspect of the Rathalos to develop was the so-called "World Tour" attack, in which the monster would fly high above the player and circle them before descending towards them. This behavior proved extremely challenging to create due to the monster needing to keep track of its angle and position relative to the player. Rathalos was later one of the monsters included in the public demo of Monster Hunter that was shown at Tokyo Game Show 2003.
Rathalos was indirectly responsible for the creation of elemental damage and weapons. While reviewing the design documents for Rathalos to help with creating its equipment sketches, Tomonori Kambe read a description about the wyvern's flammable bone marrow and was struck by an idea: Weapons created from Rathalos materials could be covered in that marrow and be themselves able to inflict fire damage onto monsters. This eventually evolved into the elemental damage system seen in the final game.
Rathalos' Japanese name "Rioreusu" was created by combining two Greek words. "Rio" is taken from Λιοντάρι ("Liontári"), which means Lion. Fujioka chose this part due to the Lion being the "king of animals". Meanwhile, "reusu" is taken from the Ancient Greek work βασιλεύς ("Basileus") which means King, adding to the Rathalos' royal nature. Thus, the two fragments combined into "Lioleus" which in Japanese turns into リオレウス ("Rioreusu").
Monster Hunter 3
At the beginning of the production of Monster Hunter 3, it was decided that the game would put greater emphasis on ecology and imaginative realism in its monster designs. Yuya Tokuda, who was already known for his passion regarding real-life ecology and biology, was subsequently given the task to oversee the re-design, the first of two design overhauls, of Rathalos and Rathian. This included reworking various physiological aspects such as the wyvern's stance, the length of its tail, the structure of its skeleton and the shape of its legs and feet. The wing spikes became shorter and its wings were made larger, with its membranes becoming more fan-shaped and its patterns made larger. The position of the ears were moved down to its lower jaw cheek.
In terms of gameplay, Rathalos had its behavior adjusted to be able to hover near the ground for long periods of time, with the fight revolving around grounding it. Making sure that the monster would able to track the player correctly and respond to Flash Bombs in a fair and satisfying way was especially difficult.
Monster Hunter: World
During the development of Monster Hunter: World, Rathalos was one of the first three monsters that were worked on, alongside Great Jagras and Anjanath. This also made Rathalos the first returning monster to be included in the game. In order to not let the King of the Skies be out shined by newer monsters, the team decided to give Rathalos a second design overhaul, starting with his skeletal structure. The head of the original Rathalos model for the PlayStation 2 had 1390 polygons, and World increased it to 11274, almost ten times the amount. The upper jaw cheeks were made white, and its wing membranes became less fan-shaped, returning to its shape in the 1st and 2nd Generation, with the underside's red coloration removed. They were so pleased with the result that Rathalos' inclusion in Monster Hunter: World is now the baseline of quality all redesigns for returning monsters must live up to.
Rathalos was intended to work as a kind of environmental hazard that high-level players could use. The idea was that players that understood this monster’s pattern could intentionally lure it towards the quest target and let the Rathalos do some of the work for them, rewarding game knowledge. Yuya Tokuda was convinced that this approach was the right one when during testing, a night-time battle between his hunter and an Anjanath was interrupted by a Rathalos blocking out the moonlight.
Monster Hunter Wilds
Besides the model and texture quality, the general design for Rathalos was largely unchanged, but the red coloration of the underside of its wings returned from older generations.

Physiology
The Rathian is an archetypal Flying Wyvern, belonging to the same species as the Rathalos and acting as his female counterpart. She can most easily be distinguished from her mate by her coloration, sporting a coat of emerald green scales along her back, with the size and the thickness of these scales increasing as with age. These scales overlap and layer on top of each other to form a highly resistant carapace, with the pointed tips of these shells being colored a dark brown. Very rarely, the Rathian may grow an inverted scale on her tail that points in the wrong direction, such a scale is searing hot and extremely valuable.
She sports a long pointed spike at the end of her lower jaw, which is significantly longer than the chin spike the Rathalos sports; while useful as a weapon, this is not the only function it can perform. The chin spike is not a solid structure like that of her mate's, and is instead a hollow feeding tube that functions similarly to a mammary gland, allowing the Rathian to push pre-chewed food stored within her mouth through it to provide a nutritious liquid to feed her young with. As the breeding season approaches, this chin spike grows even longer and is employed as a shovel that she will use in digging holes to create her nest.
In addition to the spikes on her chin, the Rathian grows characteristic rigid, needle-like spikes across her body, with notable patches arranged on her shoulders, wingarms, and the tip of her tail. These barbs, which are actually modified strands of hair, house an extremely potent toxin within them that is administered upon contact. The barbs present on her tail are primarily used offensively, allowing for her signature venomous tail swipes, while the patches on her back serve a defensive purpose, protecting the typically grounded wyvern from airborne assaults. While they are largely uniform in length and shape, a handful of barbs on her body grow thicker and sturdier, with their sharpness being comparable to that of a blade's.
The forelimbs of the Rathian are fashioned into an impressive pair of wings formed from four of her fingers as well as membranes decorated with several eye-like markings, and which themselves possess a high resistance to heat. Her outer most wing-fingers are adorned with sharp talons, able to easily cut down trees and rend boulders to rubble. While her wings do allow her to fly solidly well, she lacks the aerial adaptiveness that her mate possesses, preferring to instead remain on the ground during combat and for general movement purposes. In contrast to her wings, her muscular thighs are exceptionally well-developed, with them being much sturdier than those of the Rathalos. This increased lower body and leg strength allows her to comfortably charge across the ground with surprising speed and stability. The reason for the clear sexual dimorphism in terms of aerial and terrestrial prowess is believed to be an evolutionary adaptation to the role each Rath takes during brooding behavior: the Rathian is tasked with providing food for the young, and as hunting on land is more reliable than hunting in the air, the Rathian establishes her territory on the ground. Thus her legs ended up more developed than her wings to aid her in terrestrial predation.
Like the Rathalos, the Rathian is capable of shooting fireballs. This ability is fueled by a specialized Flame Sac within her body that produces and stores a flammable powder. By stimulating this sac and exposing this powder to air, it will immediately ignite, allowing her to breathe blasts of fire from her mouth. Within certain regions, she has additionally been known to utilize even deadlier fireballs with an explosive quality once sufficiently angered. Curiously, the bone marrow of both the Rathian and the Rathalos is highly flammable, igniting instantly upon coming into contact with air.
The Rathian displays a degree of regional variation, specifically between the Old World and the New World. In the New World, the Rathian sports denser barb patches and more flexible wings, as well as a wider wing span on average. Furthermore, it has been observed that the New World population is more proficient at flying compared to that of the Old World, likely stemming from the fact that those who originally flew to the New World were already better adapted to flying.
Behavior
The Rathian is a powerful terrestrial predator and is known far and wide as the "Queen of the Land" due to her preference for remaining on the ground. Much like her mate she can be encountered in forests and jungles, although she is also known to further range into both marshland and desert environments. She marks her territory multiple times a day, using her thick talons to leave impressive scratch marks into rocks, however she does not display strong territorial aggression towards small animals that invade upon her territory, humans included. When she is not paired with a male and nurturing young, the female wyvern lives in habitats completely lacking any Rathalos; one such colony was observed to the east of Dundorma.
During the breeding season, the Rathian will leave the areas she typically inhabits in order to seek out the Rathalos. Here, the behavior between the Rathian of the Old World and the Rathian of the New World differs greatly. In the Old World, she will usually form a monogamous mated pair that equally shares parenting duties, although in some instances the Rathian will instead leave her partner in order to return to her original habitat, proceeding to lay and raise her eggs by herself. While the exact reasoning for this behavior remains unknown, several proposed theories exist, such as regulating population size, or attempting to avoid competition with her mate for prey. Whereas in the New World, the Rathalos will mate with an entire harem of Rathian, and only the most dominant female will be allowed to raise her offspring with the her mate. All the other Rathian are pushed out of the male's territory and take residence in the Wildspire Waste, where they must raise their young on their own. This typically results in any rejected Rathian being far more vigilant about guarding their nest as a result, with them even being known to become confrontational with other members of their own species as they fight over territory. By contrast, the chosen Rathian will enjoy the loyal and ferocious protection of her mated Rathalos: if she ever finds herself in potential danger, he will immediately come rushing over to her side to protect her.
In both cases, the Rathian will end up laying a clutch of 10 eggs into a nest she dug out with her chin spike, typically located inside of caves or on mountainsides and especially tall trees. The nest itself is typically constructed out of decaying plant-matter, with the resulting run-off of nutrients from these materials accumulating as pools of flammable oil around her nest, which she will often intentionally ignite to ward off potential nest thieves. Once a mother, the Rathian's demeanor changes significantly. While the wyvern still largely ignores smaller monsters, if anything disturbs her eggs she will attack with relentless fury. As well, if she detects an unfamiliar presence within her nest she will aggressively pursue the prospective egg thief. The Rathian is considered highly intelligent, particularly due to certain behaviors she displays whilst rearing her young. In one such case, it was observed that the mother may not kill small prey, such as the Velociprey, on the spot. Instead, she chooses to merely weaken them before dragging it back to the nest. Once there, the injured prey is presented to the young, who can then practice hunting in a safe environment.
During this period of increased aggression, she will even attempt to ward off especially dangerous threats, such as the Kirin. However, instead of engaging these adversaries up-close in her usual manner, she seems to prefer to remain afar and repeatedly roar and spew flames in an attempt to intimidate them away. Despite this extreme protectiveness towards her nest, she will allow certain species of small carnivores to live in peace nearby. The species that are spared from the wyvern's wrath are chosen based on their ability to ward off ovivores—such as rats—who would snatch up the Rathian's nutritious eggs. By allowing these carnivorous wyverns to exist, the Rathian ultimately protects her young by proxy. Once the eggs hatch, a mated paired will continue to cooperate with each other, with the Rathalos patrolling their shared territory from the skies to protect against intruders; the Rathian meanwhile will primarily occupy herself with securing food. This dual parenting prevents the pair from leaving their hatchlings unoccupied for prolonged periods, as their defenseless selves are prime targets for all sorts of predators.
Due to her ecological dominance and fascinating social behavior, alongside the Rathalos, the Rathian has long since inspired awe among the people. There are even areas—such as the hunting town of Dundorma —in which the pair are worshiped as part of a religious belief. Nonetheless, the Rathian is occasionally hunted for food, with chops made from her meat being beloved by many.
Super Biology Information
The Super Biology Book Series collects the thoughts and theories of real scientists that were asked to speak about monsters from the Monster Hunter series. Thus, they are inherently speculative and should be seen as such.
Fossil Expert Yoshitsugu Kobayashi notes in his report that the Rathian and Rathalos are likely poorly suited for movement on land: The tibia and femur bones in their legs are the same length, which suggests limited mobility when walking. By comparison, the wings of the two wyverns possess a number of internal bones - similar to bats - which suggests that they are exceptionally good at turning and maneuvering mid-air. Kobayashi also theorizes however that the trade-off here might be that these wings excel at short-distance bursts of agility to hunt prey, but are less suited for long-distance migratory flights. Either way, since the Rathian and Rathalos rely so heavily on their wings, Kobayashi believes that they are unlikely to degenerate over the course of evolution.
Kobayashi notes that both the Rathian and the Rathalos are covered in short, backwards pointing spikes, which he suggests likely evolved as a way to defend against attacks from above and behind. The angle and arrangement of the spikes prioritizes defending the back of the neck, and Kobayashi likens it to structures that were possibly found on Pachycephalosaurus. The spikes could have also served as decoration.
Rathian and Rathalos’ parenting strategy - wherein the female secures food while the male defends the young - reminds Kobayashi of descriptions of Troodontidae. Such a division of labor is known to increase survival rates through specialization of the parents. Kobayashi also notes that this sometimes leads to females of a species being more physically powerful than the males, as it has been proposed to be the case with Tyrannosaurus rex.
The Rathian and Rathalos’ ability to create and expel fire is considered a miracle beyond all known limits of nature, as no real creature has ever been observed having such an ability. Kobayashi asserts that because in traditional biology, internal tissue is known to break down at temperatures nearing or exceeding 45 °C, the Raths must possess special organs made from special cells that are exceptionally heat resistant. The flame production mechanism must require fuel, ignition and expulsion processes, and Kobayashi believes that these three elements are handled by this species’ Flame Sac, which likely sits near the lungs. A specialized one-way valve connects the Sac to the lungs: Fire and fuel is prevented from entering the lungs, but air from the lungs can be pushed into the Sac to catalyze the flame creation and funnel the created fire breath into the throat to be expelled by the mouth.
Monster Hunter
Rathian was originally created and designed by Tomonori Kambe. It was the first monster designed by the development team, which is why she is the monster displayed on the Monster Hunter logo instead of Rathalos. The original concepts were a 'poisonous green dragon'.
Monster Hunter 3
Much like Rathalos, Rathian would be re-designed and overhauled by Yuya Tokuda during the game's production.
Monster Hunter: World
During development, the team had already decided to include Rathalos, so it was obvious that Rathian would appear as well. She is first encountered during the quest The Best Kind of Quest, which according to Yuya Tokuda was done so that players could choose to face her at their own pace. When Rathian quests first become available to the player, the next story-related monsters are Tobi-Kadachi and Jyuratodus, two monsters that require specific approaches to defeat. By comparison, Rathian's attacks are clear and easy to avoid but with heavy consequences for failure. The idea was that players would use Rathian as encouragement to craft some new equipment and prepare for the battles ahead.

The Redhelm Arzuros closely resembles the regular Arzuros, although displays a few notorious differences that greatly distinguish it. Like many other Deviants, the Redhelm Arzuros is notably larger than its regular counterpart, being over twice as long as a common Arzuros in its case. Physiology
The Remobra is a species of small monster currently classified as a Snake Wyvern. While it was originally considered a Flying Wyvern, the Hunter's Guild revised the Remobra's classification upon the discovery of the Najarala and classed it instead as a Snake Wyvern. The Remobra is countershaded with dull, tan scales on its underside and a lustrous coating of black on top, whose luster has been likened to that of a black pearl. Its head is snake-like in appearance and sports a pair of enlarged fangs. The most notable feature of the Remobra is its wings and their patterning of a series of red striped markings. It is almost always seen airborne, with it typically only ever landing when it feeds.
The primary weapon of the Remobra is the sharp claws present on its limbs. Alongside being able to support its weight while it hangs off small ledges, they can also easily pierce through the hide of its prey as the wyvern kicks at it from the sky. The Remobra additionally possesses the ability to produce a mild toxin it can spit out at its prey, and the tip of its tail possesses a rattle-like structure designed to produce noise. By violently shaking its tail, it can produce a sound that both intimidates its prey and serves to call other Remobra to its location. Subsequently, it has a sharp sense of hearing, however this means that sudden loud noises may startle it and cause it to collapse out of the air.
Behavior
The Remobra typically travels within small flocks. When selecting its prey, it typically attacks something that has already been weakened, which has been suggested by researchers to be a sign of the monster's high intellect. Once prey has been selected, it will swarm around the target with its flock, repeatedly lashing it with strikes from both its legs and tail. In addition to actively hunting prey, the Remobra is a prolific scavenger. It is infamous for its habit of appearing in areas that are frequented by Elder Dragons, with flocks of the wyvern typically appearing in the sky before one appears. This has given the Snake Wyvern a reputation amongst people as a harbinger of disaster. The Remobra follows around Elder Dragons so it may feed upon the corpses of any other monster the dragon has crossed paths with and subsequently killed. It is not a picky eater, and will eat from any dead corpse it can find, including members of its own species.

Physiology
The Rey Dau is the largest Flying Wyvern wherein flight capabilities are not reduced—distinguishing it from other giant species such as the Gravios or Diablos —and is exceeded in wingspan only by the Bazelgeuse. Spiked yellow shells cover the length of the head, body, forearm, talons, and thighs; the length of the shells' spines and overall shape of the shells varies considerably between arrangements. The scales beneath its shells are dark-gray and metallic.
The Rey Dau's short skull is stout and characterised by two pairs of horns that are covered in an armor of conductive carapace and supported by powerful muscles at their base which allow them to be moved freely. The primary pair grows from the sides of the cranium and points outward at rest, while the smaller secondary pair is attached to the jaws and points forward. Within its mouth are several concentric rows of barbed, jagged teeth that allow it to easily tear the flesh of its prey.
The forelimbs of the Rey Dau are two fingered, of which the primary forms an exceptionally large elongated talon, and the secondary supports the wing membrane. This membrane is decorated by a distinct pattern of dark-blue stripes, with the yellow deepening to orange at its length, and unlike in many other Flying Wyverns, is not supported further by any additional fingers, rods of cartilage, or bone. Should the Rey Dau grow to become Arch-Tempered, the stripe pattern is more prominent and sports a more striking blue color. The talon is almost as long as the wing finger itself and sheathed in sharp protruding scales that form a blade on its edge. The tail is long and coated in particularly large spiked scales, with the largest pair forming a fork at the tail-end.
Distributed throughout the body are glowing blue organs capable of generating an intensely powerful electric charge the Rey Dau uses to hunt. These are the most densely packed within its wing talons, tail, horns, and mandibles, which have small gaps in their shelling that expose these organs, maximizing their electrical output while producing a characteristic pale glow. Within its neck are two sets of translucent blue organs resembling scales or fins that function as capacitors to store excess electricity.
When an electrified body part is charged with electricity and dragged through sand, the intense heat causes a reaction that fuses Fulgurite glass to the scales, forming a blue-indigo mantle of jagged armor that enlarges the coated appendages and acts as an insulator. This covering minimizes the loss of electricity through its body parts and allows the Rey Day to store the electricity that would have otherwise been naturally dissipated. While mantled in this armor, their movements produce a distinctive threatening sound when the Fulgurite spines scrape against each other during motion, reminiscent of wind chimes. While the mantle is intact, its increased charging capacity will result in more violent and wide-reaching discharges of lightning; should it be shattered, the sudden leakage of electrical charge will cause the Rey Dau to become fatigued.
By folding the primary horns over its snout, the Rey Dau is able to utilize them as a thrusting weapon to stab enemies, or a means to discharge large amounts of stored electricity, producing powerful lightning blasts that can melt and fuse struck terrain. The powerful electric blasts from the Rey Dau's horns are used as a means of attack and as a method of rapidly discharging excess electricity when its charging capacity reaches its maximum. When using its most powerful electric blast, the Rey Dau will dig its wingtalons into the ground and tense its neck to counteract the recoil while the charge travels from the tip of its tail towards the horns, forcing the capacitor organs located within its neck to be pushed outward and extrude through slits running along its length. The process of firing lightning from its horns generates large amounts of heat, with the horns afterwards emitting vapor as the Rey Dau fans them out to cool down.
The Rey Dau's entire body is highly conductive to electricity, a trait in part owed to the complex patterns and shapes found in its scales and carapace. This both aids in channeling its natural electricity and allows it to attract and absorb electricity from its environment to expedite its charging, best seen from the violent thunderstorms that characterize the Sandtide. As a result of this, the Rey Dau experiences no adverse effects from being exposed to external sources of electricity, such as lightning strikes, Shock Traps, or swarms of Thunderbugs.
Behavior
Reigning as the supreme apex predator of the Windward Plains, the Rey Dau is extremely territorial and instantly aggressive towards any intruders in its turf, attacking them on sight. When in combat, the Rey Dau primarily relies on a combination of sweeping and slashing attacks with its blade-like wingtalons, as well as firing powerful charged blasts of electricity from between its horns, or stabbing enemies with them and subsequently electrocuting them. Against larger monsters, it will often attempt to physically pin down the target with its wings before sinking its electrified mandibles into them, or attacking with a point-blank blast of electricity.
In the Windward Plains, the Rey Dau appears to hunt primarily during the Sandtide and can be seen feeding on Herbivores like the Ceratonoth, snatching them away to its nest in the Wind's Gasp. Much like certain other Flying Wyvern species, such as the Rathian and Rathalos, the Rey Dau feeds by tearing chunks of flesh from its prey using its beaked jaws whilst restraining it with its hindfeet. When resting, it will occasionally beat its wings to dislodge shards of Fulgurite that became wedged between the scales on its talons.
Due to its power and aggression, every monster in the region is put on edge upon hearing the noise produced by the Rey Dau's coat of Fulgurite armor. Due to this, the people of Kunafa Village revere and fear the Rey Dau as Destruction's Knell, and stay away from its territory in the Wind's Gasp. The Gemchimes decorating the village, shards of Fulgurite glass fashioned into ornaments resembling wind chimes, are designed to emulate the sound of the Rey Dau's movements when armored by Fulgurite, scaring off potential monsters and protecting the village.
Music
Main article: Rey Dau (Music)
"Earth-Piercing Bolt" is Rey Dau's theme. Unlike many themes from Thunder monsters like Zinogre or Astalos, "Earth-Piercing Bolt" notably lacks any electric guitars, instead opting for electronic synths following the music direction of Wilds.
Monster Hunter Wilds
At a panel at Monster Hunter Festa 2025, several aspects of Rey Dau's ecology and etymology were explained. Its electrical organs and mandible/jaw structure were respectively inspired by the electric organs of electric eels and the mandibles of centipedes. Yuya Tokuda also revealed that the skin of the Sulawesi black sailfin lizard was used as a reference for the texture of Rey Dau's scales.
The keywords used to describe Rey Dau in development were "voltage", "vertex", "light beam", "charge", and "king", which led to the eventual creation and etymology of its current name.
Monster Hunter Stories 3: Twisted Reflection
For its Kinship Skill as a Monstie, the team wanted to make a dynamic shot out of Rey Dau's Railgun move, which can only be used whilst its stationary. They decided to implement it into a sequence: steep dive → wing drift → firing.

Physiology
The Rhenoplos is a small Herbivore covered primarily in tan scales. Its back is coated with large osteoderms, while its tail is covered in several smaller ones and eventually ends in a broadened tip. Despite its relatively small size, the Herbivore's shell is surprisingly sturdy, with it gaining additional strength as the monster ages. Its head possesses an especially sturdy and large frill that protects the monster from blows aimed at its front. While its eyesight is relatively poor, it makes up for it with an acute sense of hearing.

The Rhenoplos is a highly territorial monster, and should it hear any intruder within its territory, it will proceed to charge them down using its hardened frill. However, it is very difficult for it to stop once it has started running, often resulting in it charging head-first into obstacles and leaving it in a dazed state. Even just attempting to block the charge with a shield would typically result in a Hunter flinching backwards.

Risen Chameleos is the first of five Risen Elder Dragons discovered in the wake of the Qurio outbreak following Gaismagorm's death. Because of the danger it poses to the environment and its value for Qurio research, Elgado Outpost requests its slaying.
Physiology
An unusual, dull-colored Chameleos that has grown in strength and fury after having overcome the Qurio's poison. As proof of the Elder Dragon's survival, its entire body is mottled by ghastly, pink and pale scars, including even its tongue. Ordinarily, the Qurio Virus is a death sentence for monsters, however, this Chameleos was able to overcome the worst of its effects by supressing the Qurio Virus, being likened to having risen from the grave. Due to its formidable physique, the corruption caused by the Qurio's poison was resisted, resulting in the substance mutating upon entering the Elder Dragon's body, empowering the Chameleos tremendously and transforming it into a Risen Elder Dragon. Most Qurio were expelled from its body during the process, whereas others promptly perished upon exposure, or were digested internally. The changes throughout its body are manifestations that arose from mutations within its bloodstream that came about after the Risen Chameleos absorbed the life energy held by the Qurio. Its life energy is amplified through this process, resulting in its physicality and general traits being enhanced; its poison notably is since significantly more noxious and deadly.
Due to having overcome the Affliction, the properties of the Risen Chameleos' blood have changed, so much so that it is now incomparable to regular Elder Dragon Blood. As well, its very bones have consequently grown even more distorted, and a brilliantly pure mass has formed deep within its body as a result of the Elder Dragon storing energy. As a Risen Elder Dragon that has grown exponentially in strength, its very biology is a threat to the ecosystem.
Should the Risen Chameleos sustain sufficient damage during combat, its fury and rage will reach its zenith, and it will transform into what is known as the Risen State; the sinister scars littering its body now glowing, as if set ablaze. This phenomenon causes drastic behavioral changes and amplifies the Elder Dragon's unique abilities to an unprecedented degree of danger. The Risen Chameleos' agility is beyond that of its ordinary counterpart and it excels in utilizing its poison, spewing it in incomparably larger quantities and blanketing the entire area in a sickly violet haze. Should one lose sight of it in the fog, its venom will plunge them into an inescapable nightmare.
Behavior
Upon entering the Risen State, the Risen Chameleos will fight with unparalleled fury, imbuing its noxious poison into the very fog it spawns and flooding entire areas with its toxins. The Kingdom Survey Team designates any special individual that wields this state as a Risen Elder Dragon. Furthermore, certain individuals have been reported to be more hazardous and fight far more aggressively, wielding even greater power.

An unusual, pale Shagaru Magala that has grown in strength and fury after having overcome the Qurio's poison. Summary
Bizarre indigo-and-blue mottled Brute Wyverns that boast pick-like forearms, and an elongated proboscis with a prehensile tongue. Their most distinguishing features are the numerous inflatable sacs on their body that swell to several times their resting size with pressurized, toxic gases, which they can not only spray at enemies with their tongue, but inject into the oilsilt with their stinger, causing the gas to bubble to the surface as violent explosions.

Physiology
The Rompopolo is a bizarre-looking Brute Wyvern with insectoid traits, such as lidless red compound eyes, a curved proboscis-like beak, and an elongated tail with a large stinger at the end. Its forelimbs have been adapted into purple, pick-like raptorial structures used to pierce the vitals of prey, while its hind limbs end in three digits resembling purple suction cups. The monster's entire body is covered in a saggy, mottled, indigo hide with spots of teal and purple throughout. The Rompopolo is highly territorial and aggressively attacks intruders, with it regularly picking fights with its own kind. Physiology
The Royal Ludroth is a medium-sized Leviathan found in both saltwater and freshwater ecosystems, being the adult male counterpart to the significantly smaller Ludroth. Like most Leviathans, he possesses a proportionately long neck and tail with a body primarily adapted for swimming through water, although he is still capable of traversing well on land. The wyvern’s body is primarily covered in green scales that display slight iridescent qualities. The front teeth have fused together into a single curved cutting blade, while at the back of his head he possesses a series of several flexible spines which give the impression of a crown; while these crests typically lie against the wyvern’s neck, they will become rigid when agitated and stand erect. The more spines that a Royal Ludroth possesses, the higher his perceived status.
Easily the most recognizable feature of the Royal Ludroth is his yellow spongy mane located around his neck and stretching all the way to his back, significantly larger than the mane possessed by the females. Being highly elastic in nature, the mane evolved from the wyvern’s scales and, alongside hair-like keratinous fibers that combine together to form a mesh-like structure, is composed of dead cells. The purpose of this is to retain water while the wyvern is maneuvering on land. Inside the mane are a series of spines that—like the crests on his head—can be relaxed or erected, allowing for the entire mane to inflate in size when water levels are especially high to allow for greater storage. This stored water additionally serves a role in combat, as by absorbing the stored water through specialized pores within his skin and mixing it with his own internal body fluids, he is capable of expelling a viscous liquid capable of slowing the recovery of his opponents, trapping them in the process. The Royal Ludroth has a strong dislike of drying out however, with him experiencing a strong bout of fatigue if his mane is to ever lose its moisture. When this occurs, he is forced to either return to the water, or bathe under the flow of a waterfall in order to replenish his fluids and regain his stamina. In addition to its role in storing water, the mane also serves as a display structure to indicate the wyvern’s authority, as well as to protect his neck from potentially fatal damage.
While his back legs have adapted into flippers that aid him in paddling underwater, his forelegs are more reminiscent of those of a Fanged Wyvern and still retain both digits and claws. These claws are primarily adapted to aid the wyvern in locomotion over attacking, digging into the ground with every step. While these forelimbs still aid him in paddling underwater, it is currently unclear if they evolved specifically for this purpose, or if they are simply remnants of a primarily terrestrial lifestyle. His long tail supports a large fin that runs down roughly half its length; the tail’s strength showcases how it has been honed in harsh conditions. When the wyvern enters an especially excited state, his body produces a special fluid within that serves to suppress muscle fatigue throughout the entire body, known as Dash Extract.
Behavior
While the Royal Ludroth is technically an omnivore, he has a strong tendency towards carnivory, preferring to feed upon fish and crustaceans; the latter makes up a large proportion of his diet, as suggested by the shape of its teeth. By contrast, he is relatively poor at catching fast-moving fish. While he will feed upon algae if he is especially hungry, he does not seem to particularly enjoy doing so. When he has gathered together with his harem of Ludroth, he is additionally capable of preying upon large Herbivores, such as the Epioth, and due to his highly development mane, is even capable of venturing onto land to capture terrestrial prey, like the Aptonoth. Despite this, he remains significantly more agile within the water than on land, with the shape of his scales enabling for especially graceful maneuvers while underwater. The Royal Ludroth is also a highly prolific scavenger, and as soon as he sees signs of another monster hunting for prey, he will immediately head towards the hunting grounds in an attempt to steal any scraps of food he can find. He is even capable of occasionally stealing a kill from another monster and seems especially drawn to sounds made at the water's surface.
The Royal Ludroth acts as the leader of his pack and typically lives in a harem of female Ludroth, consisting of him as the only male and around 10-20 smaller females. Unlike Dog Wyverns such as the Jaggi, he does not display any high level of command over the members of his pack, with his presence instead providing a sense of security to the smaller females, allowing them to emerge from hiding. As the leader of the harem, the Royal Ludroth constantly patrols his own territory to keep a watch out for any rival males who may attempt to encroach upon it. If one is spotted, a territorial dispute is initiated, consisting of the males flexing the crests atop their head to try and intimidate his opponent into backing down. Additionally, he will showcase the amount of water stored within his mane in order to display his dominance, demonstrating the amount he has by shaking his body and scattering it around himself. These disputes can turn violent, with the males' spongy mane acting to cushion blows from any potential rival. By winning these disputes, the victorious male is capable of forming an even larger harem. These disputes occur frequently and, due to this, the amount of time that any one Royal Ludroth rules over his harem is typically very brief. By contrast, the Royal Ludroth rarely—if ever—has territorial disputes with other large monsters living within his ecosystem due to each having a specialised ecological niche and habitat, with the him in particular preferring to remain around flowing water.
When the breeding season arrives, the female Ludroth will switch her habitat to being exclusively terrestrial as she lays her eggs. It is then the responsibility of the Royal Ludroth to store a large quantity of water within his mane and sprinkle it onto the females within his harem, providing them with the necessary amount of moisture while they remain on land. Afterwards, the female Ludroth will lay between 1-4 eggs into holes she has dug in the sand. Neither parent sticks around to raise their offspring after the eggs have been laid, with the juveniles remaining mostly solitary until they reach maturity and find their own harem to belong to. Due to the fact the Ludroth is a poor swimmer as a juvenile, it often gets swept away by strong currents. Instead, the juveniles prefer to mature in relatively calm and shallow waters, where it will choose to feed upon polychaete worms and crustaceans.
Super Biology Information
The Super Biology Book Series collects the thoughts and theories of real scientists that were asked to speak about monsters from the Monster Hunter series. Thus, they are inherently speculative and should be seen as such.
Marine Scientist Fumihito Muto begins his analysis of the Royal Ludroth by taking a look at its massive mane, which characterizes this male individual as the alpha of its pack. While no known vertebrate on present-day Earth possesses such a sponge-like structure, Muto could believe that this is the result of a symbiotic relationship with another organism. A similar phenomenon can be observed in the sponge hermit crab, which does not inhabit a mollusk shell, but instead covers itself with a living sponge. These symbiotic organisms attach to a special skeletal protrusion on the crab that possesses additional musculature. Based on research into the muscular anatomy of the frilled-neck lizard conducted by De Vis, Muto states that it is plausible that a Royal Ludroth might be able to consciously move its sponge mane through even just a moderate amount of specially developed muscles around its neck. The mane borne by a male that maintains a harem is quite heavy, imposing a significant physical burden on the Royal Ludroth. Muto notes that paradoxically, a male with an impressive mane is perceived by females as actually possessing superior fitness, which makes it easier for him to secure females for his harem.
Muto then dedicates some time to unravelling the Royal Ludroth’s mating habits and proposes the following hypothetical reproductive cycle, based on what is known about the monster and shared traits with other harem-forming species such as seals: Both Royal Ludroth and Ludroth congregate on remote island chains to breed. The environment surrounding these breeding grounds experiences dry and rainy seasons, with the breeding period occurring toward the end of the dry season. There are no predators in these breeding areas that pose a threat to the Ludroth. Males arrive at the islands first, competing with one another until the most dominant individuals establish territories. These territories must be sufficiently spaced apart, and certain smaller islands may by themselves constitute a single territory. Subsequently, females arrive at the breeding grounds in waves. They come ashore within the territories of their chosen males, forming harems consisting of one male and multiple females. The males provide moisture to the females in their territory using their sponge-like manes. The females remain on land for several days, mating with the male and laying 1 to 4 eggs, which they bury in the sand at some distance from the shoreline. After laying their eggs, the females depart from the breeding grounds. Throughout the breeding period, females continuously arrive, mate, lay eggs, and depart. During this time, a territorial male may be defeated in a confrontation and replaced by another. Meanwhile, weaker males—those unable to secure a territory—lurk ​​in the vicinity, waiting for any opportunity to participate in reproduction. Neither males nor females feed at all while at the breeding grounds. After the breeding season, Royal Ludroth and Ludroth migrate to fertile marine regions—typically at mid-to-high latitudes where warm and cold currents converge—to feed voraciously on slow-moving bottom-dwelling organisms, such as fish, crustaceans, and shellfish. This allows them to accumulate subcutaneous fat, which sustains them during the fasting period following the breeding season. During this phase, Ludroth tend to form groups, while Royal Ludroth typically lead solitary lives. As the breeding season concludes and the rainy season begins, young Ludroth are born. At birth, they already exceed one meter in length and possess internal yolk reserves that allow them to endure periods without food. Leaving the breeding grounds, the young Ludroth are carried by swift currents toward higher-latitude waters. These regions, which become covered in sea ice during the winter, provide an abundant food source for the young, who feed heavily on shellfish, shrimp, and crabs. Toward the end of the rainy season, before these high-latitude waters freeze over, the young Ludroth migrate to warmer, lower-latitude regions to overwinter. As the winter season draws to a close, they move once again within these food-rich, lower-latitude zones; through these repeated migrations, they continue to grow until they eventually encounter a group of adults and begin to live alongside them. Muto asserts that the specific strategy of forming harems on islands might be key to understanding the Ludroth’s evolutionary history: Their ancestors were likely land-dwellers, and breeding still requires the relative safety of isolated land habitats. Congregating into harems may thus be a defensive strategy that maximizes reproductive success.
