It finally becomes available to be hunted once the hunter reaches MR99 in To the Very Ends with You.
Ruiner Nergigante is encountered at the end of the story in To the Guided, A Paean, and suddenly makes an appearance in Origin Isle. After it is "slain", Shara Ishvalda quickly drags its body beneath the ground. Once it reawakened, so did Ruiner Nergigante, and it breaks through the floor and swoops in to finally finish the Elder Dragon off. Once the hunter discovers the Guiding Lands, a Bazelgeuse ambush is quickly interrupted by the Ruiner Nergigante. It finally becomes available to be hunted once the hunter reaches MR99 in To the Very Ends with You.
Physiology
The Ruiner Nergigante is a Nergigante that has survived through many fights with other monsters in its endless hunger for bioenergy. It retains many of the same features as its standard counterpart, although there are a few notable differences, such as the Ruiner Nergigante's darker coloration due to its new metallic spikes that grow in between its regular and now darker bone spikes. The two bull-like horns on the Ruiner Nergigante's head are a metallic-gray instead of their typical pale color, as they have hardened and turned black over years of conflict.
Some of the metallic spikes are reflective and shiny, resembling white crystals, they are called Diamond Thorns. These unique spikes form after countless battles where the Elder Dragon's thorns repeatedly break and regenerate, as a mutation occurs at a certain point that births these silvery spikes. This mutation additionally makes the spikes stronger each time they break. Unlike the normal spikes, the Diamond Thorns cannot regenerate if destroyed, however, they are more lethal and can cause lacerations upon contact. These vagrant spikes grow in areas of the Ruiner Nergigante's body that have encountered repeated physical trauma. Every time the Elder Dragon senses danger, it gradually grows the Diamond Thorns on its forearms, wings, and head.
In addition to its regenerative abilities, the Ruiner Nergigante grows sharper and stronger thorns as its stamina decreases. Destroyed spikes instantly regenerate and undergo a rapid "super-regeneration" process, in which the soft, white spikes immediately transform into the hardened, oxidised black spikes. Like the standard Nergigante, it sheds and scatters its hardened black spikes.
Behavior
The Ruiner Nergigante appears to act as a nature-balancing agent in the ecosystems it is part of, preying on dangerous Elder Dragons that threaten the balance of nature. In one case, the Ruiner Nergigante was observed preying upon the Shara Ishvalda, an Elder Dragon possessing the potential to cause large-scale impacts upon the environment and bring about major turmoil in the ecosystem of the New World. However, this balancing effect is not intentional on the Ruiner Nergigante's part, and is instead a by product of its desire to hunt increasingly powerful prey and devour their bioenergy. As spikes instantly regenerate as the Ruiner Nergigante battles, it becomes stronger and sharper as combat continues. Thus, the more threatening the target, the greater the threat the Ruiner Nergigante will become should it survives the encounter. These traits make the Ruiner Nergigante the battle-hardened Elder Dragon that reigns atop its ecosystem.
Development
Kaname Fujioka planned for Nergigante to show up more in Iceborne 's story, but did not want it to overshadow the Flagship Monster, Velkhana, and Shara Ishvalda, the story's 2 key actors. Due to this, the team chose to make Ruiner Nergigante be the bridge between the story and the Guiding Lands, the endgame of Iceborne. According to Fujioka, the Ruiner Nergigante is a different individual than the one seen in the story of the base game, and has lived for much longer.

Physiology
The Safi'jiiva is a giant Elder Dragon with a muscular frame, a strikingly draconic appearance, and the typical six limbs of its classification: two front limbs, two hind legs, and a pair of powerful wings. Although acknowledged as a separate species, its true identity is that of an adult Xeno'jiiva that has shed its skin countless times. Its once translucent exterior has darkened with maturity into a reddish-brown carapace, and its underside is now protected by cream-colored shelling. This change was predicted by researchers who believed the Xeno'jiiva's translucent appearance was something that would disappear in a theoretically mature individual, with the theory being proven with the discovery of a fully grown individual's existence. While present in its juvenile state and beginning from the head and neck, the spines jutting from its back and littering its tail are significantly larger and more numerous, with those sprouting from the sides of the tail growing randomly across its surface. The Safi'jiiva sports a massive wingspan, with each wing being comprised of a muscular limb and a pair of ragged beige membranes. Their structure is closely reminiscent of that of certain Flying Wyvern species, such as the Rathalos, and their larger interdigital membrane connects the second to fifth bone fingers to the back. In comparison to the Xeno'jiiva, the greater development of the second finger is particularly noticeable.
While the wings share a similar structure to other monster species, the same cannot be said for the head, which defies conventional biological boundaries and exudes an otherworldly presence. It sports a slender snout at its front, the jaws feature a bifurcated tongue, and pairs of prominent dark horns, grotesquely twisted by excessive growth, extend from the skull. Unable to keep up with the larger curved horns' rapid growth, the second newer set of horns that have sprouted from the primary pair have splintered and split as they are pulled by the original horns; the spines in the area below the horns have also begun to split. Additionally, while once a crucial feature of the head that resembled the eyes of its juvenile form, six unique sensory organs that served as substitutes for sight in the darkness of the underground have since grown unnecessary. Yet, despite these bioenergy-detecting organs having gradually degenerated during the molting process until they completely disappeared, faint remnants of their existence in the form of sockets along the brow and horns can still be seen when the Safi'jiiva's head has been greatly damaged.
After molting repeatedly, and having lost its ethereal veil and other features, its outer shell—through which its internal organs were once visible—has grown darker and sturdier. Maturation has caused the Safi'jiiva's outer shell to form complex layers and for patterns to emerge on its thick scales, both of which hold immeasurable value as precious materials. Combined with each individual scale and plate being extremely hard, its astonishingly developed muscular strength grants it flesh as tough as armor. The abnormal strength of its scales demands that Hunters soften its hide through the use of their Clutch Claw, although a certain degree of fragility has been noted in the points where the outer shells appear to join. This fact is corroborated by research findings confirming the Clutch Claw to be particularly effective, with it reportedly being easier to wound than other monsters in this way, and with the injured area persisting for a relatively prolonged time. However, further showcasing its immense physical development, the base of the wingarms and the area around the smaller anterior membrane possess particularly strong muscular power. Through this, the Safi'jiiva is able to soar across the earth despite its massive frame, producing powerful gusts as it spreads or beats its wings. Its enhanced muscularity additionally allows it to smash through large quantities of rock, as well as punch its limbs and even tail deep into the ground as it attacks; it is even said that a single swipe of its tail can cause cyclones.
Although the Clutch Claw has proven especially successful at wounding its hide, such fragility is a mere inconvenience for a creature such as the Safi'jiiva, which can heal its wounds by using its internal energy to accelerate its metabolism to an astounding degree. The process involves it activating wounded body parts with bioenergy it has absorbed directly from Everstream currents in the land and stored within itself, using it to forcefully increase its metabolism and rapidly regenerate injuries. As it heals a body part, outer layers of the shell peel off and are discarded as they are replaced by freshly generated tissue, and that part glows with bright, blue energy. However, since this process is exhausting for the Safi'jiiva and requires an enormous amount of Everstream energy, it must replenish its internal supply by absorbing energy directly from the land. During the act of siphoning the land's energy, a glowing constellation-like pattern appears across its wings, and numerous veins of luminescent energy flow from the surrounding area into its limbs. This behavior is performed solely for the sake of replenishing its supply of energy to accelerate its metabolism, and it is not done to secure energy for breath attacks.
Beyond utilizing it to rejuvenate its internal energy supply, the Safi'jiiva is able to control the energy it absorbs to reshape surrounding regions and their ecology to meet its own needs, resulting in neighboring regions growing unfathomably different from one another. It does this to create an environment that is even more favorable for itself, such as the Secluded Valley, terraforming the area into a place where it can absorb bioenergy with exceptional efficiency. In regard to the Secluded Valley and the residing Safi'jiiva, it was able to absorb the bioenergy of the nearby Guiding Lands and the myriad of uniquely energized monsters found there. Furthermore, it is able to attract foreign monster species from different habitats and locations by influencing the Everstream's energy currents, luring in monsters that possess strong bioenergy into the region. The sudden appearance of the Stygian Zinogre in the Guiding Lands' tundra zone was one such example of this, as analysis confirmed it to not be native to the region. The effects of this alluring force extend even to other dragons, and the manipulation of the Everstream's currents can be felt as energy stirring within the land. While the remarkable abundance of the Guiding Lands was initially thought to be due to the foundational corpse of a Zorah Magdaros, it is now thought that the Safi'jiiva's influence might have also played a key role.
To design a nest optimized for siphoning the Everstream's energy, it may terraform the land in such a way that it becomes a barren region devoid of life. Being situated deep in a ravine considered outside the realm of habitation for living creatures, the Secluded Valley is an example of a region being reshaped for such a purpose. While it is thought to have originally contained a fair number of plants and animals, a Safi'jiiva altered the environment and gradually purged these organisms to create its home. As such, the valley houses no life beyond colonies of slime mold that erode its terrain. Although its ability to absorb energy from everything around it and alter ecosystems to such a degree has been abundantly researched, much remains a mystery. It is unknown how it was able to evolve the way it did, or how that in turn affected its surrounding environment. Even how it is able to siphon the energy of everything around it, or change the environment to be aligned with its desires, has no answer. While the Xeno'jiiva possessed organs in its claws that allowed it to directly absorb the Everstream's energy, these organs were deemed unnecessary during maturation and were subsequently lost.
Much like the Xeno'jiiva, the Safi'jiiva circulates the Everstream's energy inside its body through its venous system, at the center of which lies a luminescent organ positioned in the chest. Unlike its immature counterpart however, which lacks a developed central organ, it is capable of establishing a perpetual loop of energy generation within its body, marking it as the only known self-sufficient lifeform. This development occurs as the Xeno'jiiva undergoes metamorphoses and matures into adulthood, at which point it no longer requires external energy intake and instead relies entirely on its internal supply for any necessary functions and activities within its body, becoming the Perfect Being. The feat of sustaining itself with the energy stored in its centrally located organ was previously speculated by researchers to be something possible in a mature individual, although it was only with the discovery of the Safi'jiiva's existence that the theory was proven to be true. Located in the chest's organ lies what is known as a Zionium Crystal, which holds within its core the immense energy of both the Elder Dragon and the Everstream. Another resource that may be harvested from its body, similarly hold senergy, and which possesses unusual potentia is Dracolite, stored within which is anywhere between a small and a vast amount of energy.
Having stored the energy it generates inside its body, the Safi'jiiva is able to spend it against any attackers by compressing that energy and releasing it as a bluish-white beam from its mouth. These breath attacks require extreme caution and come in several diverse forms, which it achieves by controlling the ratio and compression of its internal energy as it gets released; one form of variance that has been observed has it grab an enemy with its jaws and then build up a concentration of energy, before unleashing a condensed breath attack. Among the variety of breath attacks the Safi'jiiva is capable of, there is one that possesses unparalleled destructiveness and power. Beating its enormous wings, it hovers above the ground and spews a torrent of glowing, pale, azure flames upon the land, before releasing a tiny sapphire droplet of condensed bioenergy as if it were being squeezed out of its body. This star-like droplet harbors extraordinary explosive power that is released the instant it drops to the ground, obliterating all life in the vicinity with a blinding light. Formed by concentrating and compressing internal energy to the absolute limit, it generates immense power upon detonation and is the Safi'jiiva's ultimate attack, christened by those who witnessed its spectacle as the Sapphire of the Emperor.
In its adult form, the Xeno'jiiva—which was once called "The one who wants to be the Emperor of Elder Dragons" —has undeniably become the Emperor of Elder Dragons. The power of this condensed energy is exceptionally high; it is so extreme that, unless protected by hiding behind a sturdy barrier, anything caught in its blast is instantly erased. Possessing power beyond what human knowledge could ever hope to reproduce, the Safi'jiiva appears to only perform the Sapphire of the Emperor under select circumstances, perhaps due to the action placing a strain on even itself. Furthermore, although not as innately dangerous as its various breath attacks, it uses its massive body to fend off those who pose a threat, employing body slams, charges, tail swipes, and bites. It is additionally able to trigger eruptions of Everstream energy with its physical strikes by slamming its limbs or tail against the ground. If the strike is performed with a body part that has been wounded, the erupting energy will simultaneously promote healing in that area. However, despite the wide variety of attacks it is capable of, it is only in the deepest part of its nest that the Safi'jiiva will unleash its astonishing power.
By concentrating the energy circulating through its venous system into its central organ, a surge of energy spreads across the ground as it takes on a form that empowers its body, known as the Supercritical State. An intense glow will flare from its chest, its eyes will become illuminated, and as if it were absorbing energy, its wings will adopt glowing patterning in a constellation-like arrangement. The power flowing through its body causes a brilliant light to seep through its carapace, and the ferocity of its attacks is incomparable to that of its juvenile form. In this enhanced state, a greater variety of attacks are accompanied by eruptions of Everstream energy, and when it swings its breath attacks upwards, it triggers cascading rockfalls. However, although the Safi'jiiva exhibits tremendous power when in the Supercritical State, its hide softens dramatically and its chest becomes particularly vulnerable.
Life Cycle & Reproduction
Due to its heat-generating organ being underdeveloped at birth—and thus being unable to generate an endless supply of energy itself—upon emerging from its cocoon, the Xeno'jiiva will search for a place to settle in that suits it. It will then remain in this chosen area and shed its skin countless times, growing while absorbing energy from the Everstream. As it repeatedly molts and undergoes metamorphoses, its old skin, membranes, and even exoskeleton are left strewn throughout the area. By the end of this process, it will lose its ethereal appearance, the bioenergy sensing organs on its head, and its claws' energy-absorbing organs. Over the course of a long period of time and many repeated molts, the residing Xeno'jiiva emerges from a large cocoon and finalizes its metamorphosis into a Safi'jiiva, entering adulthood. No longer reliant on external energy intake and having gained the power to reshape the ecosystem, it has become biologically optimized and instinctually driven to seek self-preservation and proliferation. Thus, it will transform the area into an environment better suited for its needs, or it may search for another suitable habitat and reshape the entire surrounding ecological system should it find one. In the process of altering an environment to create its nest, any plant life or animal originally inhabiting the land are gradually purged, and even if there are any bodies of water, no life can be found.
As it absorbs energy over a long period of time from the Everstream as well as from creatures of all sizes that it has attracted, it accumulates a stockpile of energy during its lengthy maturation in preparation to produce offspring. One researcher from the Third Fleet has proposed the idea that the concentrated bioenergy harbored within the Sapphire of the Emperor may be the key to unraveling the Safi'jiiva's reproductive strategy and behavior. Believing it to reproduce asexually, the reasoning behind their theory lies in the vast explosive power released by the droplet of energy—if the compressed bioenergy is potent enough to give birth to the Xeno'jiiva, then its immense power makes far more sense. Although the precise nature of the components related to affecting organic matter remains unknown, perhaps the blast repurposes energy originally intended for reproduction. Regarding the Safi'jiiva encountered by the Research Commission deep in the Guiding Lands, it has been confirmed to have been a separate individual from the Xeno'jiiva discovered in the Confluence of Fates by the Fifth Fleet.
This key distinction has led to the inference that the New World acts as a breeding ground for the Elder Dragon, with the evidence lying in the Secluded Valley. Driven almost exclusively by the instinct to reproduce, this Safi'jiiva created a convergence point of bioenergy that allowed it to spawn numerous cocoons housing developing Xeno'jiiva in the valley's deepest layer. Furthermore, in order to avoid newborn individuals competing over the Everstream's energy, it turned its attention beyond the valley and eventually arrived at a different bioenergy convergence point: the Confluence of Fates. Once there, it released a single Sapphire of the Emperor whose energy spawned the Xeno'jiiva that was later confronted by the Fifth Fleet. Since the Confluence of Fates is a place where energy gathers far more intensely than in the Secluded Valley, it is possible that the aforementioned Xeno'jiiva grew significantly faster than would be considered typical, or that it was born as an abnormal individual. While details from the most recent investigation have yet to arrive, this theory appears to be coherent.
Behavior
The Guild regularly receives reports from the New World sent by the Research Commission, yet despite having completed their investigation into the Elder Crossing and Old Everwyrm, these reports never diminished in quantity and only appeared to grow more shocking. The survey report that caused the greatest astonishment within the Guild was that of a mature Xeno'jiiva's existence, discovered during an expedition into the Guiding Lands by a squadron of Commission members intending to investigate various anomalies that had begun to appear in the region. The first to notice these anomalies, which included changes in the terrain, was the Seeker, who when investigating their cause alongside the Admiral, uncovered the Secluded Valley deep within the earth and beheld a giant red dragon. While it was later recognized by the Guild as being the Xeno'jiiva's fully grown form and given the official name of "Safi'jiiva," meaning Perfect Being, it would continue to bear the title of Red Dragon. Following the initial encounter, the Handler attempted to cross-reference it to already documented monsters, although there were too many discrepancies and a match was unable to be found. Nonetheless, there exist several records of unknown origin that contain illustrations of large creatures in a manner suggesting a possible lineage to the Xeno'jiiva.
These records are why researchers had always speculated about the existence of the Elder Dragon's adult form, and with the discovery of the Safi'jiiva, a new understanding of these records has led to them being considered as valuable evidence believed to depict various closely related species. There are four primary depictions, with the first being of an enormous dark dragon that exudes a demonic aura and is defined by a mane-like carapace that covers its head and is believed to have evolved to protect its energy vent; its appearance is similar to that of a "demon king wearing a red crown." In contrast, the second illustration is of a creature that is far more slender and with elongated horns, its purple skin and black exterior shell highlighting its eerie appearance. The third is of a dull-green dragon bearing a head adorned with thick, twisted, horn-like whiskers, and the large protrusions lining its neck and back seem to have formed from spines that are encased by its outer carapace. Finally, the fourth illustration depicts an individual that has undergone repeated molting, which has resulted in its dark skin and fins hardening. As such, it retains heat very well and is said to release more energy with each molt, gaining bioluminescent patterning across its body.
In order to thoroughly investigate and survey the Safi'jiiva, a special recon assignment was launched with the intent to study it before the launch of a full-scale investigation with a larger group. It was during this recon that it was discovered to be able to absorb energy from the surrounding area and heal its wounds, and that once it has temporarily drained an area of the Everstream's Energy, it descends to a deeper layer of its nest in search of more energy. Additionally, as it grew and gained more power, it learned to carefully discern which targets deserve its focus. Unlike the Xeno'jiiva, which instinctively attacks without gauging the threat of whatever danger it faces, the Safi'jiiva shows a tendency to target those it deems the most threatening with an almost excessive level of persistence. Those who draw the Safi'jiiva's Ire are relentlessly hunted down, yet should its attention be lost, it will go berserk. Although it had fled the valley during the recon and disappeared, the Research Commission recruited its most tenacious hunters to eliminate it when it next returned. Once scouts reported its return, this team—comprised of 16 hunters from the Fifth Fleet—was able to gradually corner it deeper within the valley, where a fierce confrontation ensued as the Safi'jiiva unleashed its true power. Faced against its brilliant blast of condensed energy, many hunters fell during the battle, yet through their bond with one another, the expedition team emerged victorious.
This swift action was in response to the immense threat the Safi'jiiva posed, as if allowed to leave its nest, it may have unleashed unimaginable catastrophe upon the entire New World. Its most dangerous ability, to absorb so much Everstream energy that it depletes an entire region's reserves and reshapes the environment, is considered too threatening to allow it to escape the New World under any circumstances, thus the goal of the Research Commission was to slay it before it could escape to the outside world. Furthermore, had the many cocoons housed in the Secluded Valley's deepest level hatched into numerous Xeno'jiiva, the entire planet would have faced calamity. However, as the Safi'jiiva is a monster whose presence risks disrupting the world, it is innately engaged in a territorial dispute on a global scale against other monsters that possess similar influence. These Forbidden Class Monsters (禁忌クラスのモンスター) are beings whose very existence causes them to clash with one another, they are immense forces of nature that influence each other in a chain reaction whenever something major happens. The numerous cocoons spawned by the Safi'jiiva lording over the Secluded Valley were one such major event, and their potential threat led to the arrival of an Alatreon in the New World.
According to a report by the Research Commission's observation team, the Alatreon appeared to clearly be heading towards the Secluded Valley, and shortly after its arrival, it scorched the surrounding area as if attempting to remove any and all traces of the Safi'jiiva. After taking time to reflect on the homeostasis of ecosystems and how the state of balance of individual organisms contributes to that of nature as a whole, a certain ecological researcher posited whether the Alatreon might have been a countermeasure against the unprecedented change represented by the Red Dragon. They proposed that a being capable of utter destruction was perhaps necessary to reshape the environment and ecology that had been purposefully reengineered by the Safi'jiiva; even if the conclusion lacks supporting evidence, the reasoning behind it holds up. While the two catastrophic Elder Dragons never directly encountered one another, the balance of the situation was delicate enough that a clash between the two could have erupted at any moment. Another instance of monsters of this caliber reacting to one another is thought to have occurred with the recent awakening of the Fatalis, as throughout history, a certain line present in the legend of the Black Dragon from fairy tales has been interpreted in a myriad of ways. It is thought that the line "With the death of the Giant Dragon, the legend shall be reborn" could be in reference to the Safi'jiiva. Thus, perhaps the Fatalis' most recent appearance might have been triggered by its existence.
Music
Main article: Safi'jiiva (Music)
"The Emperor Emerges From Under the Veil" and "For the Emperor's Amusement" are Safi'jiiva's 1st and 2nd phase themes respectively. Both themes contain motifs from Xeno'jiiva's themes, and "For the Emperor's Amusement" contains a motif from " Proof of a Hero ". During the siege fight for Iceborne, gaining Safi'jiiva's enmity will add a "heartbeat" percussion layer as well as disturbing synths to both themes. For unknown reasons, the drop of the Sapphire of the Emperor ultimate attack is included as "music" in-game and in the files.
When slain in Iceborne, World 's "Quest Complete! (Main Theme version)" plays as the Quest Complete theme, instead of the Iceborne version.

Monster Hunter World: Iceborne
Early ideas for Safi'jiiva were to make it look more similar to its juvenile form. However, Kaname Fujioka wanted to create Safi'jiiva as a counterpart to Fatalis, so the design changed into a classic "Western" appearance. The team made it red in colour to make it stand out from the other powerful monsters, which tended to gravitate towards dark colorations. The now Western red dragon design was also to surprise people with the idea that "this is what Xeno'jiiva looks like when it reaches adulthood".
The team wanted to make a siege event similar to Kulve Taroth in World, but also incorporate new elements for the 16 player sessions, so they removed the preparation stage of collecting monster tracks and implemented a system where every player could contribute to the siege, regardless of skill level; players can simply inflict damage, deplete energy and reach the deeper layers of the Secluded Valley instead of directly slaying Safi'jiiva. They also introduced weapon awakening to encourage for longer play times, instead of simply collecting materials.

Physiology
A desert-dwelling Subspecies of the Barioth, the Sand Barioth sports many of the same characteristics as the type species: a sturdy dorsal carapace, a long two-pronged tail, and large tusks that protrude downwards from its upper maw. Although the tusks first appear a dull-gray, they turn a lustrous, ultramarine-blue when polished. As opposed to the pristine white of its close relative, the Sand Barioth's hide is colored copper and tinted with red and yellow accents throughout its body. The monster's pelt is highly shock resistant and well-suited for use in armor crafting, although some dislike the fur's copper coloration. The Sand Barioth's red cortex, which is surprisingly lightweight, helps protect it from harsh sandstorms. The reddish coloration of the shell comes from the Sand Barioth's prey, as due to the sheer power it uses when hunting, it ends up covering itself in its prey's blood. This is not an accident, however, as coating itself in blood protects it from the harsh desert sun.
To provide traction on the sandy terrain of its habitat, the Sand Barioth possesses three long sharp claws on its forelimbs, which it also uses to attack its foes. Conical spines line the outermost digit that supports the wing membrane. Like the base species, the Sand Barioth has well-developed forelegs, making it a proficient flier, especially compared to other closely related wyverns, such as the Tigrex and Nargacuga. In place of the type species' Frost Sac is a thin, yet tough organ known as a Rugged Pleura. As cold air is expelled from this organ, it collides with the hot desert air, and the temperature difference results in the formation of a violent vortex. The Sand Barioth uses these tornadoes to travel across the desert at high speeds and gain vantage over its foes, typically by using the momentum of the vortex to launch itself directly at them.
Behavior
Indicated by its name, the Sand Barioth inhabits arid regions, such as the Sandy Plains. Alongside providing protection from the harsh desert sun, the blood coating its body serves as an indicator of strength, and the more red an individual, the stronger it appears. This intentionally painted coloration additionally helps the Sand Barioth attract potential mates.

Physiology
Being a Variant of the Deviljho, the Savage Deviljho broadly resembles the regular individual; it is a massive and muscular Brute Wyvern that is covered in a dark-green scaled hide, possesses a long tail, and a powerful set of jaws. In comparison, however, the Savage Deviljho's bulging muscles are constantly in a swollen state, making the Variant appear larger than its regular counterpart. While it is otherwise completely anatomically identical to the regular Deviljho, the primary way in which the Savage Deviljho differs from the regular species lies in its extreme strength and aggression, which comes about from the interplay between a combination of different factors. It is believed that the Deviljho has a fairly short lifespan due to both its constant conflicts with other monster species as well as its abnormally enormous necessity for food to survive. Further, when the Deviljho grows older than it should, parts of its body begin to fail. The apparatus that controls its hunger and satiation is one such part, and its failure leads to a constant, agonizing feeling of hunger that can never be quelled. This is a natural phenomenon that, in most cases, would simply kill the individual and serve as the natural limiter on the species' lifespan.
Crucially, however, the same internal organ that controls the beast's hunger performs a secondary function that is equally as vital. Although the Deviljho is aggressive towards other members of its species—and does occasionally prey on its own kin—its hunger organ regularly produces a hormone that suppresses the Brute Wyvern's desire to fight and feed on its own brethren, especially if the creature has recently eaten a full meal. Yet, when the hunger organ fails—or is otherwise destroyed—the body can no longer produce this suppressive hormone. The lack of this hormone in tandem with the pain of undying hunger may lead an aging Deviljho to viciously prey upon and cannibalize other members of its species far in excess of what could be considered normal. As it does so, the Deviljho ingests an abnormally high amount of the Dragon energy that is present in the bodies of its brethren. This violent energy then begins to react with the aged Deviljho's own Dragon element as it accumulates internally. Together with the hulking wyvern's worsening emotional state, this aberrant presence of Dragon element in the body coalesces it into a violent madness, completing the monster's transformation into a Savage Deviljho. Surprisingly, this process can occur shockingly fast—the original research team that discovered the existence of this ravenous Variant reported that they watched a Deviljho "turn savage" over the course of only 9 days.
Once the Savage Deviljho emerges, it is locked in a self-perpetuating cycle of suffering. The overflow of Dragon energy causes its already enormous muscles to expand to their maximum size, where they require even more energy to maintain themselves, in turn only furthering the painful hunger of the Variant. Feeding is nearly futile, however, as the rampaging Dragon energy within the Savage Deviljho's body snatches away any calories it consumes by instantly converting them into more Dragon energy, starving the beast even more. The ceaseless flow of Dragon energy within the body is so violent and volatile, that any movement at all can trigger it to start multiplying aggressively—for the Savage Deviljho, there is no escape from its own draconic power.
The influence of its Dragon energy reaches its zenith when the Savage Deviljho is consumed by rage. When this happens, the Dragon energy begins leaking out of the Brute Wyvern's body in the form of a dark vapor containing red arcs of energy. It emanates from the gaps between the Variant's exposed muscles and sinews, enveloping much of the torso and, especially, the face. This form is called the Dragon Fortification State (龍強化状態), and reinforces all physical and elemental abilities of the Savage Deviljho, making it even more dangerous than it already was before. In conjunction, the shroud of violent energy that masks the face is unmistakeably so dense, that merely being near it can cause other creatures harm. In fact, there is no lack of reports of Hunters who have Clutch Clawed onto the Savage Deviljho's head as it is concealed, only to find themselves being counterattacked by the Dragon energy itself. Yet, this appears to affect the Savage Deviljho itself, as the painful flow of Dragon energy around its face only appears to enrage it further and further, allowing it no rest and no calm. For as of yet unclear reasons, the draconic vapor that surrounds the head does not nullify elemental attacks, in fact, it instead makes the area especially vulnerable to exposure to the Thunder element.
Even if it may not be apparent at first glance, the draconic turmoil within the Savage Deviljho has altered its body irrevocably, evidenced by the sickly color of the wyvern's black blood and its darkened scales. The ebony hide of the Savage Deviljho is no different, as it is varnished with a dark, tar-like slime, believed by some to be crusted blood from its victims; ceaseless hunts by the voracious beast has left the blood unable to dry.
Behavior
Due to the continuous flow of Dragon energy and its agonizingly constant hunger, the Savage Deviljho is an unimaginably aggressive and violent monster, using a mix of desperate physical attacks and devastating Dragon breaths to overpower and devour foes. There is next to nothing the Savage Deviljho will not resort to attacking, and as a result, the Savage Deviljho is constantly engaged in violent Turf Wars with other large monsters. It does not yield and it does not tire, partially because its extreme hunger overpowers any feelings of exhaustion that would otherwise temper its rage. Interestingly, it has been noted that the Savage Deviljho is at its most violent and hungry while traversing cold climates.

The Malice Tiger Wyvern Scorned Magnamalo (怨嗟響めくマガイマガド, Ensadoyo meku Magaimagado) is a Fanged Wyvern introduced in Monster Hunter Rise: Sunbreak.
It is a Variant of the Magnamalo.
Summary
A battle-hardened Variant of Magnamalo characterized by increasingly volatile Hellfire, longer arm blades and back shells, and a damaged horn leaving them unable to find a mate. Vastly more aggressive and powerful, they utilize their longer arm blades and stronger Hellfire with far more mastery, often concentrating pressurized Hellfire into their blades. Pushing them to their limits even enables them to utilize the dangerous and mysterious Dragon element, tinging their Hellfire scarlet.
Main Series
Monster Hunter Rise: Sunbreak: After reaching MR 100, Scorned Magnamalo can be hunted in the M6★ Urgent Quest Back with a Vengeance. The quest becomes added to Hub Quests after it is cleared for the first time. Following Gaismagorm's death and the subsequent Qurio outbreak, a Scorned Magnamalo is discovered in the Citadel, believed to be the same Magnamalo fought and wounded by Hamon in the Rampage that destroyed Kamura Village 50 years ago. After receiving a formal request from Kamura Village, the Guild gives the newly-discovered Variant its current designation and issues a quest to hunt it.
Physiology
The Scorned Magnamalo broadly resembles the regular Magnamalo, with the most notable differences being its larger size, much larger serrated arm blades, and enlarged jagged back shells that can fold in and out to modulate the flow of Hellfire from its back. It is missing both an eye and horn, does not possess extendable scutes, and has noticeably larger fangs. Its entire body is darker in coloration and covered in faintly glowing red scars resembling those of Apex monsters, and its form is shrouded in pink Hellfire at all times—even when not in combat—causing it to constantly emit a moaning wail. Further, the Scorned Magnamalo is covered entirely by countless scars, down to even its individual scales. The one remaining eye of the Scorned Magnamalo has an eerie glow that is said to never fade, even after being removed from the wyvern's socket.
The Scorned Magnamalo is much stronger than the normal Magnamalo, having much greater physicality and a finer control over its Hellfire. The Hellfire produced by the Scorned Magnamalo is comparatively more condensed and thus more explosive and violent, capable of reshaping surrounding terrain. In addition, while the standard Magnamalo is able to selectively emit Hellfire from specific parts of its body, the Scorned Magnamalo is able to actively concentrate the distribution of its Hellfire on specific body parts, greatly empowering them at the cost of extinguishing other parts. While Hellfire is normally evenly distributed across its whole body, it may unfold its arm blades and focus all of its Hellfire into them upon growing enraged, causing them to glow bright pink and extinguishing its back and tail. While Hellfire is focused into its blades, it has been seen building up pressure in its arms before unleashing a far-reaching blast of pressurized Hellfire, likened to swinging a blade of flame and said to be capable of faltering even an Elder Dragon.
When sufficiently harmed or angered, the Scorned Magnamalo can enter a further state of fury known as the Raging Hellfire State, where it reignites its tail and fully flares out its back shells. In addition to a further increased level of ferocity, some of its Hellfire will take on a crimson hue and become infused with Dragon elemental energy, further increasing its destructive power. While this state is said to be extraordinarily deadly, it puts the Scorned Magnamalo's body under extreme stress and makes it highly vulnerable should its opponent mount a counterattack.
Behavior
The Scorned Magnamalo is said to come to be when a male Magnamalo has its horns broken, rendering it undesirable for females and unable to mate for the rest of its life. As a result, the Magnamalo forgoes mating and focuses entirely on hunting prey, recklessly facing and devouring increasingly dangerous foes to accumulate power and bolster its Hellfire. If the Magnamalo survives for long enough, it can undergo gradual morphological changes that transform it into a Scorned Magnamalo.
Being scorned by its kind and enduring a lifetime of battle scars has caused the Scorned Magnamalo to become even more aggressive than usual. Onlookers describe it as a malevolent demon filled with the hatred of the many monsters it has slain, with the people of Kamura Village calling it the Devourer of the Rampage. As it now solely focuses on seeking out sources of energy to increase its strength, it ruthlessly attacks anything that it comes across and appears to actively seek out powerful foes to battle and devour, having even being reported trying to hunt Elder Dragons.
Development
As the final and most difficult monster introduced in Monster Hunter Rise: Sunbreak on release, the team aimed to create a powerful, challenging encounter that could create a no-holds-barred, do-or-die final battle. When designing its introductory cutscene, its presence was designed to invoke the feeling of an indomitable foe that no strategy nor force could stand up to, as well as a malicious entity that devoured the souls of its victims. Adjustments to the body shape of the base Magnamalo were carefully considered to differentiate it from the original, particularly the shape and glow of its arm blades. To emphasize the power of its pressurized Hellfire attacks, the sound designers made it so that its sound effects would become muted in the instant between the attack charging up and being fired, explaining that this was a way to express strength or power through means other than sound itself.
Monster designer Uno deliberately left the origin of Scorned Magnamalo's Dragon element abilities ambiguous, wishing to encourage players to speculate on its diet and habits given existing knowledge of its Hellfire and its presence in the fight with Narwa the Allmother.

Physiology
The Seething Bazelgeuse is a Bazelgeuse Variant best identified by the silvery-blue scutes adorning its upper body, the perpetual fiery glow between them, and its scales' constant incandescent state—akin to a permanent version of the nominate species' enraged state. Its scales have grown incredibly volatile, making the whole monster appear as if it is about to go critical at any moment. Its scales are much hotter and more destructive than those of its cousin, with the Distilled Blast Fluid that forms them being so dangerous, only expert craftsmen are permitted to handle it. The Seething Bazelgeuse's intense body heat is responsible for tempering its shell and giving it its signature silver sheen, permeating every part of its body and making it difficult to approach.
It is believed that extreme bioenergy-rich conditions—such as those of the Elder's Recess —are what gave rise to the Seething Bazelguese, by granting it the power to maintain its heated state indefinitely. When sufficiently angered, the Seething Bazelgeuse may enter an even greater state of rage that causes its body temperature to soar even higher. This makes its scutes glow with molten light and its scales with a superheated, pale, lavender light, dramatically increasing their destructive power and blast radius. However, sufficient damage to its clusters of superheated scales can detonate them prematurely, damaging the Seething Bazelguese in the process and dissipating the accumulated heat.
Behavior
While retaining the infamously violent and territorial nature of its standard counterpart, the Seething Bazelgeuse is said to have finer control over its explosive scale attacks; demonstrated by its ability to accurately sling scales at enemies from afar instead of dropping them indiscriminately. It is additionally able to intentionally withhold its scales to allow them to condense further in open air, giving them even more destructive power when they are detonated, often all at once in an incredibly destructive dive bomb.

Physiology
Known as the Piercing Beetle, the Seltas is among the larger Neopterons and part of a sexually dimorphic species, with the Seltas being the male counterpart to the significantly larger and flightless Seltas Queen; his body is almost entirely covered by a thick deep-green carapace composed of several shock-resistant layers. This shelling is incredibly light-weight and boasts a smooth surface to reduce air resistance, aiding the Seltas when he is flying at high speeds. The orange head of the Seltas possesses a pair of mandibles as well as two illuminated, orange, compound eyes. Atop the head rests a massive three-pronged horn lined with several smaller spikes; white stripes pattern its underside and the tip is tinted orange. This horn acts as the Seltas' primary weapon and is often used to skewer prey whilst flying towards them at high speeds. However, the Seltas may be prone to getting his horn lodged into walls if he charges at them too quickly. The Seltas is known to perform upkeep on his horn, utilizing boulders as whetstones to keep it as sharp as possible.
The Seltas possesses six limbs: four are used for general locomotion whilst grounded, whereas the front-most pair are instead fashioned into an enlarged pair of orange sickle-shaped claws. When under the influence of the Seltas Queen's pheromones, the Seltas is capable of greatly increasing his striking range by extending his claws to roughly twice their original length, although some individuals seem capable of this feat even in the absence of the Queen. Additionally, the Seltas possesses a pair of fluid-filled wings on his back whose rapid beats allow him to stay airborne. As they are a vital organ for his survival, they are typically kept folded underneath the elytra on the Seltas' back when not in use. The Seltas will spend the majority of his time on the wing, only ever landing when he is tired.
Stored within the Seltas' abdomen is a highly acidic substance it can spray directly from his abdomen onto prey in order to decay and corrode them, allowing for easier consumption. While resting on the back of the Seltas Queen, the chemicals shot from his abdomen change in composition and will instead sap away the stamina of whatever they come into contact with.
Behavior
The Seltas is often seen alongside the Seltas Queen, who herself is almost always seen with at least one Seltas accompanying her wherever she may go; on occasion, two male Seltas have even been observed battling over their Queen. The Seltas Queen is able to release pheromones that allow her to command the actions of her mate, who is highly responsive to the pheromones and will immediately rush to assist. Upon arriving by her side, the male Seltas will be instantly grabbed by her pincer-like tail and forced onto her back to aid in combat. The male Seltas is able to lift three times its own size, allowing him to carry his Queen around and considerably aid in her mobility despite the significant difference in size between the two. While doing so, the Seltas is able to allow the usually flightless Queen to become airborne and even pull her out of a Pitfall Trap. However, in the end, the Seltas Queen is still the dominant one in the relationship, and she will not hesitate to cannibalise the smaller male if she ever gets too hungry.
When resting, the Seltas will typically do so whilst clinging to the side of a cliff-face.
Development
Other proposed names for Seltas were:
Scorius, a combination of Scorpion and Sagittarius, as the female has a stinger-like tail that she uses when attacking, while the male fires projectiles like an archer when attacking.
Scarath, making ties to a scorpion, and also a scarab. The "–ath" suffix was added for consistency with the Monster Hunter world.

Physiology
Standing as one of the largest species of Neopteron known to the Hunter's Guild, the Seltas Queen is covered in compact emerald-green shelling that is decorated by several white stripes and is much thicker and stronger than that of her male counterpart. Alongside earning the Seltas Queen her title of Heavy Beetle, the carapace fades to a more chestnut tone near the back of the body as well as the top of each of the Seltas Queen's four legs. This iridescent exoskeleton boasts tremendous defensive properties that transforms the Queen into a living fortress. This hard shelling also serves to protect her golden and more vulnerable abdomen from potential blows. The back of the Seltas Queen is broad and flattened, with the shelling making up her chest being surprisingly light due to its hollow structure, helping to reduce the otherwise massive weight of the monster's exoskeleton. While the Seltas Queen formally possessed wings, they have degenerated over evolutionary time, leaving her in the modern day completely flightless without the assistance of her mate.
The Seltas Queen possesses four limbs used for locomotion; these limbs consist of four overlapping plates patterned with white down both their middle and sides, whereas the shelling on the underside of these limbs is instead colored yellow. Once the outer layer of armor has been stripped away, the remaining shelling sports a beige yellow-like coloration. The head of the Seltas Queen is a dull red and ingrained with two orange compound eyes. Normally held in front of the head are a pair of reddish claws—also covered in white stripes—whose sturdiness helps to protect the Seltas Queen's head from damage. These dull claws are covered in a non-slip coating and aid the Queen primarily in pulling herself up steep terrain and tunneling beneath the ground. however they appear to be ill-suited for use as weaponry. These claws additionally appear to assist her as she eats, aiding in shoveling food into her maw. These mandibles open laterally and are capable of chewing through even exoskeleton with relative ease.
Extended from the rear of the Seltas Queen is an incredibly long and wide tail, taking up around half of the monster's entire length. It consists of several overlapping plates whose green coloration gradually fades to a rusty-orange closer to the tip, at the end of which is a sharp point. On either side lies a crescent-shaped shear lined with additional spikes, forming a mobile and deadly pincer. This pincer is a lethal weapon for the Queen which is typically used defensively when she is approached, holding the tail over her head and lashing out at targets with quick strikes. It is said that this impressive pair of pincers both strike fear into humans and inspire the male Seltas to serve and obey their Queen.
The Seltas Queen possesses several Aqua Sacs within her body that aid her in her production of the Water element, which takes the form of a fluid circulated throughout the body that is secreted through the mandibles. Once the fluid comes into contact with the outside air, it quickly transforms into a highly corrosive acid, causing it to bubble and fizz around the Seltas Queen's jaws. Once enough acid has concentrated around her face, the Seltas Queen is able to fire off three powerful blasts of water, severely debilitating anything struck by the blast. However, the Seltas Queen will momentarily expose an opening in her defense as she gathers the acidic mist by removing her claws from shielding her face. If she is disturbed while gathering enough fluid, she will lose her acidic build-up and be prevented from firing off her blast.
Underlying the plating present on the Seltas Queen's chest are several holes utilized for releasing gases, giving the chest plating a unique aroma. The Seltas Queen utilizes these openings in order to release the pheromones her body produces, which by doing so, allows the Queen to forcibly attract the significantly smaller males towards herself, enslaving them to unquestionably follow her commands.
Behavior
The Seltas Queen is almost always accompanied by at least one male Seltas who will follow her wherever she may go; if her partner Seltas ends up dying, a new Seltas will typically arrive as a replacement to accompany her shortly thereafter. While the Seltas Queen and her mate typically begin battles fighting individually, when faced against a tougher opponent, she will resort to using her pheromones to attract her mate towards her. As the male approaches, he will be forcibly grabbed and directly injected with pheromones by the tail, placing him completely under his Queen's control. From here, the Seltas will be placed atop her carapace, whose flatness and non-slip properties provides a surface that is easy for him to mount. Now together, the pair will combine their strengths and fight in unison, with the Queen using the male's horn to violently charge down opponents. Despite the significant size and weight difference between the two, the male Seltas is plenty capable of lifting and carrying his Queen through the air, negating her otherwise flightless nature and vastly improving her mobility. The Seltas is even strong enough to pull the Queen out of Pitfall Traps to safety if she is ever caught in one.
However, the relationship between the Seltas Queen and her servant is not entirely beneficial. If the Queen is in a dire situation and is low on energy, she will not hesitate to grab her mate off her back with her clawed tail and repeatedly slam him on the ground, killing him in the process. From here, the she will proceed to cannibalize her own mate in order to sustain herself.

Other proposed names for the Seltas title were Regent, Rhea, and Duchess, as the localisation team had an image of a fierce queen going into battle with her loyal subjects.

Physiology
The Seregios is a species of Flying Wyvern recognizable by the unique blade-like golden scales that cover its entire body. Dark-red stripes accent the sides of its neck, shoulders, wrists, legs, and its singular horn, otherwise the wyvern's coloration is almost entirely a shimmering gold, with a lighter tan underbelly. The beauty of these scales is not their only notable trait; when the Seregios is angered, the scales on its head, back, legs, wings, and tail will stand on end, revealing them to be razor sharp. Due to their sharpness, these scales are commonly referred to as Bladescales. This display is rightfully threatening, as the scales on their own are sharp enough to gouge foes by merely grazing them. The scales of the Seregios are constantly growing and are made of heat-resistant minerals. As these scales grow, they discard their upper layers in favor of newer uncorroded strata. This allows the Seregios' scale coat to essentially sharpen itself over time, a quality that is inherited by any weapons made from the wyvern's materials.
Additionally, the Bladescales can be launched by the Seregios and will ride the wind until they embed into targets, making them exceptionally dangerous. The Seregios is alarmingly accurate with this maneuver, able to hit small Remobra out of the sky with individual Bladescales. When the scales make contact with an object or a creature, they will burst into smaller scale fragments that cause heavy bleeding. The Seregios does not appear to have a limit as to how many scales it can dislodge from its body, and as such, it uses them rather freely in combat.
Alongside the knife-like Bladescales, the Seregios' extremely powerful hind legs are remarkably dangerous, partially a result of its zygodactyl feet that are perfect for gripping and slashing. It uses its sharp talons to latch onto its prey, tearing through skin and armor alike. The talons are often used to make weapons, and they are said to be sharp enough to rend the air itself with their lightning-fast strikes, causing prey to bleed profusely.
The Seregios' skull features a singular large horn resembling an axe protruding from its snout, this horn is hefty and sharp, yet conveniently agile, making it a popular material for crafting blades. The horn typically remains partially folded against the monster’s face, standing upright once it grows enraged. The skull additionally features a beak-like maw, a small lone spike protruding from the lower jaw, and dark-orange markings surrounding its blue eyes. The skeletal structure of its unexpectedly tough two-pronged tail is not unlike that of the Rathalos and Rathian's; the thick Bladescales that cover it completely can be flung by the Seregios with violent swings of its tail. The spear-like tail tip may also be used by the Seregios, often to cleanly pierce through the hide of its prey.
Few can match the Seregios' mobility and superiority in the air, it is incredibly fast in flight and capable of making sudden sharp turns and performing various acrobatic stunts to attack and reposition, sometimes both in a single motion. Its wings are each equipped with a sharp wingtalon that helps shift the monster's weight during flight, in turn enabling the Seregios to perform tight turns. However, due to the composition of its muscles, the Seregios is not suited for continuous long-distance flight and must often take breaks on the ground when traveling far. Like the talons on its hindlegs, the Seregios' wingtalons are prized as a crafting material. Excluding the talons, the wings feature four fingers that attach to the wing membrane, each of them tipped with a sharp claw; when angered, only the scales on the outermost digit will stand on end. Strangely, the Seregios rests its wingtalons on the ground and uses them when walking, suggesting it may be more closely related to the Tigrex due to its posture. Furthermore, due to its unrivalled flying capabilities and hunting strategy, the Seregios was initially thought to be a Bird Wyvern when it was discovered.
Behavior
Until recently, the Seregios was only known to exist in an extremely remote area and was considered to be incredibly elusive. Due to its inhabited area having limited space, the Seregios would commonly fight over turf with others of its kind, which in turn resulted in a relatively small population as weaker individuals were killed off in these battles. The position of the Seregios' nest is representative of its standing within its territorial hierarchy: the Seregios who nests in higher altitudes is considered a stronger individual, while the weaker Seregios will nest in lower areas. A Seregios that nests high in the region it occupies creates the strongest Bladescale bursts and possesses superior flying capabilities comparatively. Due to this behavior, the Seregios tends to flock in areas with vertically-stretched terrain, such as mines. The size of the marks left behind by a male Seregios' Bladescale bursts, as well as the level of muscular control over them while flaring them up, is believed to be a sign of sexual fitness that the females of the species pay attention to.
During an outbreak of the Frenzy Virus, one individual was reported to have overcome the virus and become an Apex Seregios. This single Seregios drove the entire rest of the Seregios population out of their native habitat, resulting in the species spreading out into other locales and more frequent sightings. The population has become so widespread that the species has been seen in regions as far as the Forbidden Lands.
The Seregios is fiercely territorial, often attacking other large monsters and frequently competing with the apex predators of the ecosystems it invades in intense combat. When hunting prey or attacking other monsters, the Seregios will make use of its powerful hind legs while launching Bladescales from its body. Once the Seregios' prey has succumbed to its aggressor's brutal assault, the wyvern will use its Bladescales to form a golden grave marker, embedding them into the ground in a circle around its fallen foe's corpse. The Seregios is known to come into conflicts with the Rathian, which are known to sometimes end fatally. It is believed that this particular rivalry is the result of the Seregios' relatively recent habitat expansion: in its ancestral roosting grounds, the Seregios stood as the singular unopposed Flying Wyvern species at the top of the food chain. Thus, encountering other Flying Wyverns may trigger a spontaneous aggression response to the unacceptable reality of a related species daring to cross paths with it.
When a female Seregios goes into estrus, she seeks out the most dominant male in her region and enters his territory to mate. Following that, the female returns to her own territory and lays several eggs, which she then protects and hatches with no further interaction from the father. A juvenile Seregios will spend its first years under the protection of its mother, who will even fight and kill any male Seregios that come too close to her young. During this time, the juvenile will learn how to fly and hunt. Eventually, a young Seregios will shed its first coat of scales, leaving behind scattered shards that signal to the mother that her young have matured. When this happens, the mother will chase her offspring out of her territory, forcing the newly matured Seregios to find and establish a territory of its own.

Monster Hunter 4 Ultimate
Seregios was created by Yuya Tokuda. When Monster Hunter 4 Ultimate entered production, the series had gone many years without a Flying Wyvern Flagship Monster. Additionally, the most recent representatives of the class - Tigrex and Nargacuga - both emphasized a flightless combat style and were in a sense atypical Flying Wyverns. Thus, Tokuda suggested that the Flagship Monster of Monster Hunter 4 Ultimate should be a proper Flying Wyvern that attacks players from the sky. However, merely flying around and attacking from above would not make for a unique enough monster, and so Tokuda created the concept of a Flying Wyvern that attacked using its powerful legs to kick players.
Based on this concept, the design team created prototype designs for the monster based on Secretary Birds. Kaname Fujioka advised them to pay close attention to how they shape the wings of the monster: In order to counteract the image of the Tigrex' muscular forearms, he suggested that the Seregios should have light and delicate wings, with the main muscle mass being reserved for the legs. This would give the Seregios a more distinct look compared to previous Flying Wyvern designs. Fujioka also asked the designers to consider the stance of the monster, and requested that it actually use its wing-arms for light support when grounded, as a reference to its creative ties to Tigrex. Tokuda took this insight to further differentiate the combat style of the Seregios. In order to make it feel appropriately different from Rathalos, he designed the flying style of the Seregios to revolve around it pushing itself off the ground with its powerful legs and then rapidly gliding from place to place using its light wings. This gave the monster a fast and ferocious look during combat, and also made it feel like it could rival the King of the Skies.
Visually, the Seregios was designed to look immediately distinct from the Rathalos and Rathian. Initial concepts for it gave it a blue coloration to contrast against the Rathalos' red shell, but that idea was scrapped due to concerns of it looking too similar to Azure Rathalos. Eventually, the team decided on giving Seregios a golden body, as that would be new and unique. During this stage, a creature designer presented Tokuda and Fujioka with a draft that featured strange, pinecone-like scales. The two felt that this idea was just what the monster needed, and Tokuda pushed to implement it into the gameplay of the monster as well. This resulted in the creation of the Seregios' bladescale ability, as well as its rage state allowing it to change shape.
Other proposed names for Seregios were:
Aurelos: a combination of aer (Latin for air), Regius (Latin for King) and a traditional Monster Hunter suffix "-los", going for “the king of the skies to rival Rathalos”.
Ceralos: a combination of celertias (Latin for high speed) and Regius.
Aegios: a combination of aer and Legion, which the Japanese name also utilizes.
Aurthelos: a combination of Aur (Latin for gold), and a traditional Monster Hunter suffix "-thalos", going for “the golden rival of Rathalos”.

The Heavenly Revolving Dragon Shagaru Magala (シャガルマガラ Shagarumagara) is an Elder Dragon introduced in Monster Hunter 4.
Summary
The mature form of the Gore Magala, now a full Elder Dragon covered in glittering golden scales and possessing a pair of permanent horns. Their vast wings grant them the distinct silhouette of a six-pointed star. Shagaru Magala spread the Frenzy Virus through their scales, which are spread in such vast quantities that they darken the sky and plunge entire regions into calamity. They also employ their heightened command over the Frenzy for combat, in the form of various breath attacks and explosive Frenzy blasts.
Main Series

As a result, the residence of Cathar had to be evacuated. Per the request of the Hunter's Guild and after consulting with the Grand Guru of Cathar, the Hunter is granted permission to slay the Shagaru Magala once and for all.
