Physiology
Blessed with divine beauty by its shining, pure-white shelling, the Shagaru Magala is the adult form of the juvenile Gore Magala. Having finally molted its dark shell, its body is covered exclusively in thick golden scales that shine a blinding white and whose lack of any impurities is remarkably rare. These dignified scales boast outstanding resistance and strength upon maturing, which is only further heightened when they layer over each other to form a glittering stalwart shell. Likened as the Elder Dragon's impervious "Celestial Armor," from which scratches vanish before one's very eyes, this carapace is considered impenetrable. It is said that humankind is incapable of breaching its defense, with it being believed a miracle to be vital for the hands of a human to pierce the armor and make the Shagaru Magala yield.
Unlike the Gore Magala, which uses special sensory organs to survey its surroundings, the Shagaru Magala possesses a pair of orange eyes. These eyes are thought to develop as the Gore Magala undergoes the process of molting, during which the feelers that made up for a lack of eyes regress and harden, losing their functionality as they transition into horns. Although the now hardened sensory organs have lost any and all functionality, they still house the Frenzy Virus (狂竜ウイルス, "Mad Wyvern Virus") and its inherent madness within their form. In stark contrast to the rest of the Shagaru Magala's body, the color of which is reminiscent of light from the heavens, the slightly arched pair of segmented horns preserve the jet-black coloration of the Elder Dragon's immature form as a vestige. Mysterious in nature and able to withstand the test of time without decaying, these horns are believed to exist outside the flow of time.
Able to wrap its entire body with their giant form, the Shagaru Magala's divine wings are split with three prongs in a manner similar to the leaves of a Trident Maple. The wings' thin membrane, featuring a repeating pattern of tiles radiating outward, reflect iridescent light when in the sun—thinner wing membranes hold greater value. Their airy membrane hides rock-like strength, and each wingarm is well-defended by a spiked carapace. At the ends of the Shagaru Magala's wingarms lie prehensile hands, each possessing four massive hooked claws that harden with age and emit a mystic shimmer—this shimmer is used in much the same way as the growth rings of a tree. While these beautiful purple claws are ordinarily tender, they will harden to an extraordinary degree when the Shagaru Magala is threatened; at their hardest, the almost translucent claws are proof of the Elder Dragon's cyclic death and rebirth. In comparison to the Gore Magala, the Shagaru Magala bears noticeably greater muscle mass—seen best in its humped back and thickened tail—allowing it to effortlessly grab and overpower other monsters. The sheer muscularity of the tail is hidden by a coat of bristly inverted scales whose pure color grades their quality. The scales shine with a God-like brilliance and a pure-white glow, making it difficult to fathom how such a creature could have emerged from the shed skin of the dark Gore Magala.
Much like the Gore Magala, the Shagaru Magala utilizes the Frenzy Virus, although its production and output greatly outclasses that of its younger form. When spread, the black scales remain around longer than the juvenile Gore Magala's; these scales contain the Frenzy, and the threat of contracting the Frenzy and decaying is ever present. In addition to the airborne particles that carry the bulk of the Frenzy, a special bodily fluid found in its breath and other similar attacks enables the Shagaru Magala to achieve the same effects as the dispersed scales when the liquid evaporates. Through this fluid, it is able to expel and perform explosive attacks that react with the scales in the air and cause a chain reaction. Moreover, upon growing enraged and entering its Frenzy State, the sheer volume of airborne scales the Shagaru Magala releases blots out the sun and causes a blackout in the surrounding area. When in this state, it emanates a far greater quantity of Frenzy Virus particles—which take on a lighter shade—and a cloud of Frenzy will sit in its jaws. Additionally, the Shagaru Magala can summon a constant barrage of viral pillars all throughout the area with its roar, or summon additional ones as it attacks with its wingarms.
Within the Shagaru Magala's body, a pristine jewel of light can be found. Known as the Elder Dragon's Phosgem, it is said to "ignite the skies and eradicate all darkness." However, despite the Shagaru Magala's pure and divine appearance, a lone black scale may be found and claimed by those who stand beneath its wings and survive. Another rarity of the Elder Dragon's body is a white scale: believed lost, equipment crafted from it is bestowed with superhuman power.
Life Cycle
The Shagaru Magala is the final life stage of the Gore Magala and a fully matured Elder Dragon, attained only after a Gore Magala that has traveled through various places and grown to maturity is reborn through a molting process. During the metamorphosis, the Gore Magala will undergo drastic morphological changes: its outer layer of skin will peel and fall off, eyes will develop in its head, and its sensory organs will devolve and harden into horns. However, the process may be inhibited and result in an incomplete, malformed Variant of the Gore Magala, known as the Chaotic Gore Magala. The cause for this abnormal form lies in the Shagaru Magala itself, as—aside from infecting other creatures with the Frenzy—its scales uniquely contain certain components that both supresses the growth and obstructs the molting of other Gore Magala. Consequently, it has been determined that not all Gore Magala are capable of developing past their juvenile state. As a result, the Shagaru Magala is ensured an eternal, unilateral rule within the Sanctuary where it reigns supreme over the species as a solitary ruler, permitting other Gore Magala to exist only as its vassals.
In regards as to why it infects other creatures with the Frenzy, the Shagaru Magala does it for a different reason than its younger state. While the Gore Magala does so to heighten its perception, the Shagaru Magala spreads its fine scales for the purpose of reproduction. In addition to containing a substance to prevent the appearance of another Shagaru Magala, its scattered scales carry germ cells that implant themselves and parasitically live within a Frenzied Monster, treating them as a nursery as they mature within their body. Should the infected monster be a compatible host, the germ cells will transform their host into a Gore Magala upon reaching a certain growth stage before further continuing their development. Due to this method of reproduction, alongside its singular existence, both the Shagaru Magala and Gore Magala lack any breeding behavior and have no determinable sex.
It is theorized the Sanctuary is the Shagaru Magala's home, and that it partakes in a cycle that spans an extraordinarily vast stretch of time. As a Gore Magala, it is believed to be born and raised in the mountain, before leaving the region and eventually shedding its skin upon reaching maturity, returning to the mountain once more after having been reborn as the Shagaru Magala. Once the reigning Shagaru Magala has lived out its life cycle, one amongst a myriad Gore Magala will be given the chance to successfully molt and take the place of its predecessor, repeating the cycle in perpetuity.
Behavior
A mysterious Elder Dragon whose body is blessed with God-like beauty, the Shagaru Magala calls a sacred ground at the base of Heaven's Mount its home. Known as the Sanctuary, its gate has been sealed off completely and entry into the site is strictly forbidden following the events of a tragedy. As it rarely leaves its sealed off home voluntarily, sightings of the Shagaru Magala are few and far between, with its presence only being recorded in Cathar's Sanctuary and the mysterious Everwood. However, an appearance within the ruins of the Citadel's frozen icescapes recently occurred shortly after the defeat of the Malzeno and the subsequent ecological collapse. Drawn to the Citadel by the arrival of a Gore Magala that had entered the region seeking to replace the fallen Elder Dragon, the Shagaru Magala would leave its home to deal with the juvenile. As a result, due to the risk of it inevitably polluting the area with the Frenzy, the Elder Dragon's presence in turn threatened to devastate the Citadel and leave the Kingdom with an additional crisis to face.
Known to have ravaged and brought to ruin many kingdoms, the Shagaru Magala is an incredibly dangerous Elder Dragon whose appearance demands the evacuation of the immediate area, as well as any surrounding villages and their inhabitants. Seeking to defeat its foes through a myriad of versatile attacks, caution is advised to those fighting it up close as it favors using its tough wingarms and tail for close combat. In addition to physical blows, it scatters scales across the ground through breath attacks and unleashes dust explosions that follow targets, as well as much more. Even so, the largest threat posed by the Shagaru Magala lies in the spread and pollution of the Frenzy Virus throughout entire regions. The Elder Dragon's infectious scales spread across the land and afflict living creatures with the Frenzy, the virus causing them all to lose their minds and go berserk, soon leaving the land piled with decaying corpses and devoid of any life. The volume of fine scales released by the Shagaru Magala has even been known to cloud entire mountains and cause a localized extinction event. Should such a disaster occur, the Hunter's Guild would have no choice but to evacuate any surrounding villages and permanently quarantine the entire area.
There have been several creatures depicted in ancient texts and illustrated in sketches that bear some degree of resemblance to the Shagaru Magala, although certain key features differentiate them. One of the illustrations details a monster that could be interpreted as a Fanged Wyvern or Fanged Beast, although no known species of either classification resembles it, leading to the thought it may be portraying an entirely new species. Meanwhile, another shows a creature that shares a great amount of similarities with the Shagaru Magala and its juvenile state, with the striking resemblance having led to scholars suspecting it may be a Subspecies. The third illustration depicts a seemingly spherical creature, however it appears to simply be spreading its wings to create the rounded appearance, speculated to be done in the habit of mimicking the moon. While closer inspection has revealed it resembles the Shagaru Magala with its wings spread, the existence of the creature is currently uncertain due to the illustration having been found in an ancient text. Lastly, a recently discovered ancient record found during the investigation into the Gore Magala illustrates a pair of monsters with unusual forms and whose coloration is notably distinct and contrasting to one another. It may be possible for them to be a species that resembles, or is perhaps a close relative of the two Magala.
History & Mythology
Although it was only recently discovered and classified as an Elder Dragon, the Shagaru Magala is deeply rooted in a myriad of legends from long ago, with it itself being regarded as a legend amongst monsters and revered as a God. Due to its habit of only appearing at the peak of Heaven's Mount in times of calamity, the Guild chose to name the Shagaru Magala after a mountain God. Alongside this name, it is also known as the Great Wheel, the Wheel of Heaven, and the Heaven's Wheel Dragon in awe of its transcendence over life. Similarly to its etymology, the three prongs of the Shagaru Magala's divine wings represent Heaven and earth, with the Shagaru Magala ruling over them. As well, they themselves are believed to guide the living towards both prosperity and ruin, with the radiance of the Shagaru Magala's golden scales staying with one's eye for a thousand nights. Yet, despite their radiance, scales from the Shagaru Magala are believed to be bad omens due to their origin point being the site which entry to is forbidden. In the culture of Cathar, there exists a poem regarding the Elder Dragon and its juvenile form that has been passed down since ancient times through many generations. The poem is said to embody the birth and death of all living things since time immemorial, as well as the endless cycle of souls and life. Furthermore, in some folk lore the Shagaru Magala is described as having traveled across time, with one village even having a song dedicated to it having traversed through time as a traveler.
Of the abundant mythology surrounding the Shagaru Magala, one particularly infamous legend recounts the events of a tragedy that befell Heaven's Mount long ago. Preserved through Cathar's oral and written history, the legend takes many forms and speaks of an incident that is colloquially known as the Calamity. Long ago in the distant past, long before time was time, a terrible disaster took place upon the mountain that caused all the monsters to go berserk and tear apart the land, before eventually perishing themselves. What was left following the Calamity was the annihilation and indiscriminate extinction of every living creature in the region.
In an effort to prevent further spread, the people of Cathar sealed the infection's believed place of origin with a gate and marked it with a symbol, one which evokes a sense of the divine. This event has been recorded in various surviving literature, as well as history books and retellings, that often describe the Calamity as a baleful wind that consumed and withered the mountain in its entirety; some accounts additionally describe a God descending from Heaven as a scourge upon the mountain's inhabitants. It is said the Sanctuary was the origin point of the Calamity, although since all first-hand witnesses to the event are long dead, it has been impossible to confirm. Moreover, despite Cathar's deep history, there remains some who believe it to be merely a fairy tale.
It would only be in recent times that the events of the Calamity would be fully understood, in particular, after the believed demise of a Gore Magala which had been designated the Guild's top priority. When Guild scholars arrived at the scene to conduct their study on its body, they would find the beast to have shed its skin and vanished, and around the same time, worrying reports of monsters mysteriously going berserk on Heaven's Mount would surface. Once the Gore Magala had shed its skin and developed into a fully fledged Elder Dragon, it headed straight for the Sanctuary and polluted the entire area with the Frenzy. With the mountain clouded by a black haze and monsters going berserk following the newly confirmed Elder Dragon's return to its home, the Shagaru Magala was verified as the culprit behind the Calamity. This conclusion would be further corroborated by the realization that the sigil on the Sanctuary's gate depicts an image of the Shagaru Magala airborne, as the symbol was long suspected to be in the image of the Calamity's cause.
To prevent the legend from repeating itself, a famed Caravan Hunter would be directly requested by the Guild to slay the Elder Dragon. However, slaying the Shagaru Magala does not guarantee the Frenzy to stop its expansion, as it may have already spread too far across the land whilst the Elder Dragon was heading for Heaven's Mount. In such a case, monsters who have overcome the Frenzy and possess the ability to maintain the virus' spread themselves—known as Apex Monsters —may begin appearing. Although the mystery behind the Calamity has been resolved, legends of destruction following the Shagaru Magala's emergence persist.

The Serpent Emperor Dragon Shah Dalamadur (ダラ・アマデュラ亜種, Dara Amadyura Ashu) is an Elder Dragon introduced in Monster Hunter 4 Ultimate.
It is a Subspecies of the Dalamadur.
Summary
A Subspecies of the Dalamadur with heightened aggression and an unstable metabolism resulting from having recently shed their skin. Their erratic metabolism consequently causes frequent shifts in body temperature, to such a degree that a mere touch can turn the ground to molten slag. Correspondingly, the strength of their hide fluctuates significantly due to their body's instability, causing them to either soften up and become highly susceptible to attacks, or harden and deflect any and all.

Physiology
Mountainous in size, the unmistakable coloration of this Dalamadur Subspecies—which is covered all over by twisted crimson Glaives —originates from it having recently shed its skin. Although it is known to bear a characteristic tan coloration decorated with scarlet spines, several descriptions found in ancient documents claim the existence of differing hues. Members of the Scriveners thus made sketches of the unconfirmed colorations, drawing green, purple, and red serpents as claimed, further investigation is necessary nonetheless. The Elder Dragon's hide has been bestowed an unbreachable, yet flexible armor through a layered defense of overlapping compacted scales. In particular, the thick plating that shields the chest and protects the Shah Dalamadur's heart is doubtlessly impervious, not even an atom of its can be harmed by weaponry forged by man. Its tail is defended by a steeled shell and adorned with a dense forest of glaives, and its eyes' piercing gaze is too much for most humans to be acknowledged by.
Shedding its outgrown skin has had the side effect of causing the Shah Dalamadur's metabolism to grow unstable, resulting in certain parts of the Elder Dragon's body to sporadically experience an abnormally high metabolic rate. These areas of its body consequently undergo irregular temperature shifts that cause them to soften and change properties, resulting in a constant state of fluctuation. As such, the Shah Dalamadur's otherwise invulnerable hide may temporarily soften dramatically and grow more susceptible to attacks due to the extreme temperature shift, indicated by an intense, blazing glow that pulses throughout its Glaives and claws. Alongside sharing all the physical and mysterious abilities of its more stable counterpart, the Shah Dalamadur's irregular metabolic balance allows it to melt the ground into molten slag instantaneously upon scraping its body's heated areas across the terrain. Merely holding out its arm can cause it to combust, and as the Elder Dragon drags it or its jaws across the ground, only a path of molten lava remains.
Behavior
The Shah Dalamadur exhibits a calm disposition before shedding its old skin, however it will immediately begin displaying heightened activity following the process.
History & Mythology
Much like the standard Dalamadur, the Shah Dalamadur was long thought to be exclusively found in fairy tales and legends from across the lands, however, multiple sightings in recent years have disproven this and lead some to fear the great serpent as a herald and grave omen of ruinous events. Alongside reported sightings, the Shah Dalamadur's existence was confirmed through the deciphering of an Aged Text that referred to one individual in particular as the Indestructible Emperor and Serpent Emperor Dragon, prophesizing its emergence by way of legend: "When the colossal mountain is reborn, heaven and earth will stain crimson." The same text heralding its appearance further describes the Elder Dragon as having been worshipped as a god in ages long passed, and feared in fairy tales as a symbol of both life and death, as well as as an avatar of rebirth. There are even some who appeal to the Elder Dragon, requesting its guidance and protection, and referring to it as a grand monument of varying form: a peerless star in the sky, a steep mountain above the earth, and a great pillar, among others.
Amidst the mythology surrounding the Shah Dalamadur, there is a tale that recounts how it shaped the world itself over the course of 14 days, with the Elder Dragon adding a new aspect to the world each day: it began by drawing the horizon and creating both the fields and the land, then came the wind, time, and joyous songs. It carved mountains from the darkness, created pillars that the earth would shake, and it created Heaven. On the 10 th day it invented fantasy, then on the next the crucible of life, followed by the stars in the sky, and the caverns below. With the coming of the 14 th sunrise, it is said the Shah Dalamadur created the light that sparked everything.

Physiology
The Shakalaka is a small, thin, humanoid Lynian. Its skin is a pale-tan and covered with little to no fur, with the only article of clothing commonly worn being a small leaf tied around the waist like a belt, which is itself connected to an acorn carried around on the Lynian's back. The head of the Shakalaka is almost always obscured due to its habit of wearing a mask to cover its face, however, those who have witnessed its face describe it as being surprisingly cute. Most commonly, this consists of a brown gourd-shaped mask covered with four forward-facing diagonal spikes colored white at the tips with a red band below it. The halves of the mask are capable of detaching from one another to create the illusion of a mouth. Additionally, both false eyes and several false teeth are decorated onto the mask in white. Below these teeth markings are two small holes located where the Shakalaka's real eyes would be, which allow it to see out of its mask. The exact reasoning behind why the Shakalaka wears a mask is still unknown, however it has been theorized to be to help compensate for its weak eyesight as the mask would help block out especially bright light, which its eyes are highly sensitive to.
Behavior
The Shakalaka inhabits a wide variety of habitats, although it tends to prefer darker places, such as caves and jungles. The Shakalaka spends a majority of its time hidden underground, placing both stones and mushrooms onto its head in order to better disguise itself into the surrounding terrain. Only the most observant of individuals are capable of spotting the Shakalaka once it has camouflaged itself. This camouflage additionally allows the Shakalaka to easily ambush its prey. As the Shakalaka's eyesight is poor, it instead relies on its other senses, such as hearing and smell to track its prey, leaping out at any small creatures which pass it by. Instead of attacking with its body or with a substance produced from its body, like most monsters, the Shakalaka prefers to attack by wielding weapons. Most commonly, the Shakalaka wields a short and broad iron blade easily capable of dealing fatal injuries to a Hunter with a single blow. However, the Shakalaka has been known to wield other tools while hunting, such as thrown Barrel Bombs or cases that release a sleep-inducing mist.
The mask of the Shakalaka is known to vary between individuals, with the subtle differences between the masks believed to represent the societal ranking an individual holds, which would help to demonstrate both the high intelligence and sophisticated culture the species holds. However, the lack of uniformity amongst these masks has lead some researchers to question the validity of this hypothesis, positing instead that the Shakalaka simply wears whatever mask it feels like wearing. The leader of a tribe of Shakalaka, the one bearing the most impressive physique, is known as the King Shakalaka, with his rank being showcased by a bizarre crown consisting of a meat grill. The masks also play a role in a coming-of-age ritual performed by Shakalaka tribes. A Young Shakalaka who has yet to acquire a mask of their own is tasked with venturing outside of their tribe to bring back a mask for themself, before having it be brought in front of the chief to be recognized. It has also been shown in certain individual Shakalaka that they are capable of imbuing specific abilities into the masks they wear, granting the wearer a significant change to their abilities upon being worn. However, this behavior has so-far only been observed in young Shakalaka, leaving the potential power of this ability in the hands of an adult up to speculation.
Unlike fellow Lynians, such as the Felyne, the Shakalaka is not friendly towards humans, attacking them on sight and refusing to participate in human civilizations. Thus far, there have only been two notable exceptions to this rule. However, both individuals were young when they began to interact with humanity on a deep level, leading some researchers to believe the natural ferocity towards humans that other Shakalaka experience would have simply never had any time to develop. Some have additionally added that the intense curiosity exhibited by one of these individuals could have played a role in this greater degree of sociability.

The Shamos (シャムモス, Shamumosu) is a small Fanged Wyvern introduced in Monster Hunter: World.

Fanged Wyverns with a pink face and large eyes. They form packs that patrol the lower levels of their environment, as their well-developed vision gives them a strong aversion to bright lights. Shamos hunt by overwhelming prey with numbers, surrounding their target and attacking sporadically, continuing the fight even if members of their pack are killed.

Physiology
The Shamos is a small and social Fanged Wyvern with a lithe, yet flexible frame covered primarily in light-gray scales splotched with darker spots; this dark coloration allows it to slink through and blend into its environment during the night. From between the shoulders juts out an orange ridge, the hue of which is shared with the tip of its very thin and long tail. The Shamos' two pairs of darkened limbs end in sideways curling talons.
Among Fanged Wyverns, the Shamos boasts a unique head with several features reminiscent of a Felyne's. Two crests project from the back of the skull in a form mimicking ears, and its face—colored a bright, vibrant pink—unnervingly stands out even in low-light conditions. The jaws of the Shamos display a noticeable underbite, however, its most striking feature of the face is its pair of large orange eyes adapted to see clearly in the dark. Its large pupils are especially reactive to light, able to shift shape from circular to slits depending on the brightness of the surrounding environment, allowing the Shamos to pick up on even the faintest traces of light. Consequently however, such sensitive vision may be used against the Fanged Wyvern, as it is particularly vulnerable to bright lights. As such, Torch Pods and Flash Pods are proven successful deterrents against the Shamos, with Brightmoss resulting in even greater effectiveness.
Behavior
The Shamos is known to primarily inhabit the Coral Highlands and is a nocturnally active social scavenger that feeds primarily off carrion. It spends much of its day resting under shade in small groups, periodically awakening to survey its surroundings. Once the light of day has vanished, the Shamos will patrol the nearby area with its packmates, although it may choose to go alone as well. The nocturnal nature of the Shamos is revealed through examination of its eyes, which allow the Fanged Wyvern to prowl the Highlands' Coral Forests in the dark of night.
When a much larger monster draws near, the Shamos will keep its distance and screech at the threat. Even if accompanied with packmates, it will not attack unless the monster is left assailable by another force. If a Shamos becomes isolated, it will call for others to aid it in combat. In response, up to seven other Shamos may respond to its call. Among the smaller Fanged Wyverns the Shamos is notably more fierce and will not retreat even after multiple members of its pack are slain. The Shamos is famed for possessing a particularly antagonistic relationship with the Tzitzi-Ya-Ku, primarily due to it being severely vulnerable to flashes of light and the Bird Wyvern's habit of suddenly dazzling its adversaries with bright light produced by its antennae.
Development
Concept art of early Shamos designs shows lithe Fanged Wyverns with large eyes. They all have features that imply an aquatic lifestyle, such as blue coloration, fins, and fish-like faces.

The Earth Singing Dragon Shara Ishvalda (アン・イシュワルダ, An Ishuwaruda) is an Elder Dragon introduced in Monster Hunter World: Iceborne.
Summary
Known in scant myths as the "Old Everwyrm", the Shara Ishvalda is a colossal subterranean Elder Dragon resembling a bulky golem of stones and sand, with gigantic hand-like structures in place of wings. This is in truth an outer shell that protects a grotesque, body with gnarled, spindly wingarms resembling roots, and maddened red eyes. Powerful vibrations emitted from their wingtips turn rock and dirt into sand, allowing them to easily burrow and causing seismic activity that can alter the geography and ecology across entire landmasses.
Main Series
Monster Hunter World: Iceborne: Shara Ishvalda is first hunted in the M6★ Urgent Quest Paean of Guidance as the final boss of Iceborne's main story, though with its name initially displayed as "Unknown" and its part descriptions obfuscated. After clearing the quest, it can be refought in the rotating M6★ Optional Quest Faraway Lorelei. Shara Ishvalda is responsible for the mysterious "song" causing anomalous monster behavior across the New World. It is eventually tracked down to the Origin Isle, but a Ruiner Nergigante attacks the party, only for Shara Ishvalda to ambush them after Nergigante is seemingly slain. The Shara Ishvalda is seemingly hunted, but reveals itself to be still alive afterwards, only for the still-living Ruiner Nergigante to ambush it and finish it off before leaving.

The Shara Ishvalda is seemingly hunted, but reveals itself to be still alive afterwards, only for the still-living Ruiner Nergigante to ambush it and finish it off before leaving.
Physiology
The Shara Ishvalda is a large subterranean Elder Dragon that initially covers itself in a thick armor of rock and sand, which is stuck to its body by an adhesive secretion and accumulates as it digs through the earth. Called the Elder Dragon's Rock-wrapped State (岩纏い状態), this form appears as an enormous, bulky, golem-like dragon made of numerous beige, blue, and yellow rocky chunks, many of which can be seen shifting and shuddering as it moves. Its body is stout, with four somewhat stubby legs, a short tail, and two enormous four-fingered structures resembling hands or claws in place of wings. The Shara Ishvalda's head is blocky in shape, with an armored jaw that is capable of movement despite its solid appearance, and two beady, faintly glowing, yellow eyes visible deep within the rock plating. The Elder Dragon having very few potential predators suggests the rock shell is not a defensive adaptation.
Hidden beneath the rock layer, the Shara Ishvalda's true body is that of a gangly dragon with a gnarled glossy hide resembling a cross between wood and stone. It is primarily beige in coloration, although the ends of its limbs and chest are more blue and stony, while the tips of its wingarms are pink hued. Its chest bears a unique structure resembling a lattice of shallow indentations, the sides of its body have rows of rib-like structures running along their length, and its dorsal side is covered in small pinkish bumps. Its wingarms, claws, and tail are spindly and resemble plant roots, with the individual digits of its wingarms being flexible enough to move independently; they are believed to have once been conventional wings that degenerated as a result of its subterranean lifestyle.
The Shara Ishvalda's head bears a crown-like crest and a pair of initially closed eyes, which have degenerated due to its underground lifestyle, with the Elder Dragon instead using a unique sensory organ in its forehead crest to perceive its surroundings with. When in sufficient peril, its large eyes open and are revealed to be greenish-yellow with shrunken red pupils. Despite being normally hidden, the eyes selectively opening only during crucial moments suggest they are still able to sense their surroundings, possibly through methods other than conventional sight.
The wingtips of the Shara Ishvalda contain organs that generate extremely powerful vibrations capable of dissolving earth into sand and reshaping surrounding terrain, allowing it to effortlessly dig through solid earth and rock. The Shara Ishvalda is additionally able to induce seismic activity over an enormous area by emitting these vibrations into the ground; as the waves echo and resonate within the earth, they cause earthquakes and tectonic disruptions powerful enough to destroy, reshape, and recreate local geography on a scale likened to that of a natural disaster, and with it their climates and ecosystems. Further, the resonance of these vibrations produces a "song" reminiscent of howling wind that can be heard across vast distances and greatly irritates other monsters, causing them to exhibit anomalous behavior; it is believed the frequencies of this song disrupt the natural navigational instincts of migratory monsters, such as the Legiana.
When threatened, the Shara Ishvalda is able to utilize these vibrations for self-defense. In addition to being able to trigger seismic explosions and turn surrounding terrain into quicksand by sending vibrations into the ground, its exposed wingarms are able to amplify and focus the vibrational waves they produce into a narrow area, emitting destructive sonic "beams" from its wingtips resembling jets of pressurized air. Individual beams are able to pulverize terrain and targets alike, but by putting its wingtips together, the Shara Ishvalda is also able to converge the beams into larger, more concentrated beams or blasts. The most deadly demonstration of its abilities is a colossal sphere of condensed vibrational energy formed between the Shara Ishvalda's wingarms and thrown at its target, creating an explosion that annihilates all living things and terrain in a wide area; this attack has been dubbed the Imperial Lotus Kalpa Cannon (入減蓮華劫珠砲) and is only used if the Shara Ishvalda is particularly enraged or threatened. A peculiar trait of its vibration attacks is the emission of bright flashes of light from its wingtips whenever firing the beams; the reason for this is unknown.
Behavior
Very little is known about the Shara Ishvalda's behavior outside of ancient texts describing the Old Everwyrm and the mysterious song it produces. While the one known living specimen was abruptly discovered for the first time in the Origin Isle, then promptly slain, it is believed the Elder Dragon lives a strictly subterranean lifestyle and seldom surfaces, spending time burrowing along the bioenergy-rich Everstream. While burrowing, the Shara Ishvalda sends powerful vibrations into the earth, creating its disruptive "song" as it digs and moves. The Shara Ishvalda's diet is unknown, with researchers theorizing it feeds directly from the Everstream's bioenergy and only moves in order to find more plentiful feeding spots.
The Shara Ishvalda's activity and geological reshaping is hypothesized to have played a role in the formation of the New World and its ecology, in particular being tied to the rapid cooling of the Hoarfrost Reach after neutering the activity of its volcano, which resulted in the Velkhana migrating to the New World continent as it could no longer replenish its scales using the volcano's magma. Another hypothesis proposes that it formerly resided in what would become the Rotten Vale, reshaping the locale into its current state before migrating along the Everstream. Additionally, the Shara Ishvalda notably appears to be unaffected by the Xeno'jiiva's ability to lure Elder Dragons to its location.
While in combat, the Shara Ishvalda is initially weighed down by the bulk of its rocky layer, making it cumbersome on land, although it remains capable of leaping deceptively high or far while encumbered. While still able to burrow or reshape its surroundings with vibrations, it favors using its sheer weight to crush intruders with slow physical attacks carrying immense force. Should this armor be stripped off and its true form revealed, the Shara Ishvalda becomes considerably faster and more aggressive, and will leverage the full power of its sonic arsenal to eliminate the threat, now favoring ranged attacks with its sonic beams and seismic explosions. As the Elder Dragon's ire grows, it will cause increasingly drastic destruction and reformation of the surrounding terrain in an attempt to gain an advantage, eventually opening its eyes and fighting with awe-inspiring ferocity.
Music
Main article: Shara Ishvalda (Music)
"From the Rumblings Come a Song" and "A Single Bloom in an Eternity" are Shara Ishvalda's 1st phase and 2nd phase themes respectively. As a final story boss monster inspired by Buddhist mythology, both themes contain instruments from South Asia and motifs from " Succession of Light ", the debut game's main theme.
When slain in Iceborne, "Songs of Triumph in the Winter Sky" plays as the Quest Complete theme.
Development
According to Kaname Fujioka, Shara Ishvalda was created with the idea of creating an "earth dragon", similar to how Velkhana's design started with the basic concept of an "ice dragon". This led to the design of a golem-like earthen monster, and after considering its placement in the game, the team decided to add a two-phase progression with gradual changes over the fight, with the reveal of a plant-like, Buddha-inspired monster from beneath the rocky shell. This dramatic phase change was intended to make Shara Ishvalda more memorable as a final boss, with a dynamic transition that opened up the available space in the arena.
At some point, the production team had suggested adding a song-like phenomenon as a major story element. While conventional singing was deemed unfitting for the series, they chose to interpret the "song" as a natural phenomenon, akin to a sound portending disaster. As vibrations formed the basis of sound, this resulted in Shara Ishvalda gaining the ability to dissolve the ground through its vibrations.

Physiology
Considered the largest known Carapaceon, the Shen Gaoren is a towering monster covered extensively in a dull-gray carapace. As the Carapaceon ages, its shell will gradually toughen, leading to it eventually growing tougher than most metals. As a result, it is difficult to make even a dent against its exterior through the use of conventional weaponry. The shells along its spine are especially sturdy, with the defense they provide being comparable to that of a fortress. This stronghold-like presence has granted the monster the nickname of Fortress Crab. Additionally, the Shen Gaoren is known to occasionally molt its old shelling, leaving behind a massive cast of the monster.
The Shen Gaoren possesses black eyes suspended on stalks, a circular maw lined with teeth, and a pair of incredibly long antennae that reach almost all of the way to the ground. Further, it also possesses four exceptionally long legs that it utilizes for walking, preferring to either suspend its body high in the air, or keep it held close to the ground. Should these limbs sustain sufficient damage, they are known to become flushed bright-red. Additionally, a long pair of supplementary limbs which end in a pair of pincers jut out from the front. While they are proportionally small compared to the rest of the monster, they are exceptionally powerful, able to easily tear through metal and reduce solid walls to mere dust.
Like most other Carapaceons, the Shen Gaoren has a soft and unarmored underside that it protects by wearing the skulls of other giant monsters; oftentimes, the skull of the Lao-Shan Lung. Alongside serving as protection, the Shen Gaoren can utilize the mouth of the skull to fire off a projectile liquid, much like the Shogun Ceanataur, with it being capable of shooting it up to a distance of 300 meters. The sheer power behind the Shen Gaoren's projectile is staggering, and the liquid that is shot out contains a highly corrosive acid strong enough to melt through almost anything it comes into contact with. Records tell of a group of soldiers defending a fortress who were struck by such a projectile, resulting in them being killed instantly.
However, despite the gradual learning of information gathered from the records of battles against it, much else about the Shen Gaoren's ecology—including both its life span and means of reproduction—still remains unknown.
Behavior
Due to its massive size, the Shen Gaoren is known to claim a massive territory, which it will roam at regular intervals. These movements can lead to the monster unintentionally destroying entire human settlements as it walks. Much like the Lao-Shan Lung, the Shen Gaoren appears to show little regard to Hunters who attack it whilst it travels, as it rarely, if ever, decides to actively fight back against them. However, the Shen Gaoren will turn significantly more aggressive if it encounters a fortress along its path. Fortresses are typically constructed by humans along the path that the monster is known to wander in order to protect their settlements from being completely destroyed. These fortresses built to stop the Shen Gaoren typically end up the subject of the monster's ire, with it prioritizing attacking the structure until it is completely destroyed. This is believed to be the case due to the monster being highly territorial and possessing a strong instinct to eliminate any who encroach upon its territory, with it mistaking the fortress for an intruder.

The name references to the surprise that Hunters may get when seeing the skull of a Lao-Shan Lung, only to face a giant Carapaceon instead. Physiology
The Shogun Ceanataur is a large species of Carapaceon covered in a bright-blue shell, whose sheen causes it to be of great value in ornamentation. Unlike the squatted body possessed by the Daimyo Hermitaur, the Shogun Ceanataur's is much more slender, with the bottom half jutting downwards into a blunted tip, while the dorsal side extends into a serrated, saw-like top. It possesses black eyes atop blue stalks, a long pair of antennae, and a mouth surrounded by two pairs of mandibles. The Shogun Ceanataur possesses six limbs, four of which have been fashioned into appendages used for walking. These legs are incredibly strong and are easily able to support the weight of the Carapaceon, as well as of the shell it wears. They are additionally adapted to allow the Shogun Ceanataur to easily scuttle along the ceilings of the caverns it inhabits. In order to accomplish this, it will stab its legs into the cavern's ceiling, alternating between stabbing and withdrawing its legs as it moves to prevent it from accidentally falling from the surface. The Shogun Ceanataur only appears to perform this behavior when an enemy is present, presumably as a way to avoid the attacks of its foe.
The most notable trait of the Shogun Ceantaur is its pair of sickle-shaped claws, which serve as its primary weapons. While they are normally kept folded inwards against its arms, once the monster grows agitated enough, they will unfurl to their full length and transform into truly devastating weapons with exceptional reach. Additionally, the unfurling of these claws can be used to intimidate threats into backing down. The unfurled edge of the Shogun Ceanataur's claws are covered in rows of sharp spikes, allowing them to cause deep lacerations into anything it strikes with them. The sharpening of the Shogun Ceanataur's claws cause them to emit a sharp, metallic sound—implying they are structurally similar to that of a sharpened blade. In addition to serving a combative role, the Shogun Ceanataur is able to use its claws to burrow into bedrock, primarily as a method of transportation.
Much like the Daimyo Hermitaur, the Shogun Ceanataur has a completely unarmored abdomen, which causes it to seek external shells to protect itself with. While the Daimyo Hermitaur almost exclusively wears the skulls of the Monoblos, the Shogun Ceanataur is known to wear a much greater variety of potential armor: skulls belonging to unidentified monsters, large snail shells, and the skull of the Gravios. Should it lose its shell, the Shogun Ceanataur will almost immediately retreat in order to acquire a new one to protect itself with, which is hypothesized to be the result of the Carapceon's highly defensive instincts. It has been theorized that Carapaceons belonging to the same species have different preferences when it comes to picking out shells, with them preferring to wear shells of similar shape to one another. The skull of the Gravios allows the Shogun Ceanataur to pull off an additional trick. By utilizing the skull's mouth, adapted for firing off the Gravios' signature heat ray, the Shogun Ceanataur can fire off a jet of highly pressurized liquid out from behind itself, composed primarily of the Carapaceon's own urine. It appears that this attack is not intended to cause harm, rather, it is used merely to scare away potential threats. However, it may still be considered a powerful attack due to the pressure with which it is fired with. While most individuals only show this ability whilst clinging to ceilings, certain Shogun Ceanataur may perform the attack even whilst on the ground.
Exquisitely polished pearls are capable of forming within the Shogun Ceanataur's body over the course of many years, presumably formed from a diet of oysters. These pearls are occasionally released from the body through the jets of water it can expel.
While the younger and significantly smaller Ceanataur are capable of producing poisonous bubbles to defend themselves, this ability is atrophied as the Carapaceon ages. As the Ceanataur ages, it typically replaces the smaller shells it wears with larger ones more able to accommodate its size.
Behavior
The Shogun Ceanataur prefers to live within volcanic and marshy environments, specifically preferring to reside in dark caves. While it possesses a high resistance to heat, its body is highly susceptible to the cold, causing it and its young to remain in already warm environments such as volcanoes, or areas where ground temperature is kept constant, such as marshlands. This difference in temperature resistance is believed to be the reason why the Hermitaur and Ceanataur inhabit the differing environments that they do. Within its territory the Shogun Ceanataur maintains numerous underground burrows filled with shells and monster skulls, these stockpiles serve as emergency armories the Carapaceon can access if its shell were to be broken in combat. It has been noted that the Gravios skulls worn by the Shogun Ceanataur are much larger than the heads of commonly seen living Gravios. This has led to the belief that the Shogun Ceanataur maintains a collection of exceptionally large Gravios skeletons deep underground.
Despite its large size, the Shogun Ceanataur is capable of moving at surprisingly fast speeds, enough to mask what the monster actually looks like. When hunting prey, the Shogun Ceanataur has been known to leave its shell in place to act as a decoy whilst it burrows itself underground, allowing it to perform surprise attacks upon its enemies. The Shogun Ceanataur has a varied diet that includes hunting small creatures, scavenging large cadavers, plucking insects from the ground, and even chewing on rocks and minerals to stock up on calcium.
The thick flesh within the Shogun Ceanataur's legs are highly valued in cooking.
Development
The visual design of the Shogun Ceanataur was based on the alien bugs seen in the 1997 science fiction film Starship Troopers.

Physiology
The Shrieking Legiana is a Variant of the Legiana that has adapted to harsh, cold environments. First discovered in the Hoarfrost Reach of the New World, it is physiologically similar to its standard counterpart, albeit with a more developed body. Visually, its smooth outer skin takes on a darker coloration, while its underside appears paler due to the frost that clings to its secretory glands. Having developed a slightly larger frame from the standard Legiana, it possesses greater reach with its claws and tail in the air, although its efficiency in grounded combat suffers slightly as a result of the increased bulk. The Shrieking Legiana's Frost Sac and secretory glands are especially developed, able to release the Legiana’s signature freezing fluid in greater amounts and with more potency, aided in part by the colder climates the Variant tends to prefer to call home.
One key distinction from the standard species is the spiky layers of frost that can nearly always be seen lining its chest and radiating from the tail. Both the Legiana and this Variant can cover their body in frost to enhance their abilities whilst angered during combat, however, while the standard Legiana is known to expel excess liquid from its Frost Sac outside of combat, this behavior appears to be absent in the Shrieking Legiana and subsequently causes frost to constantly accumulate on its secretory glands with time, resulting in what researchers have dubbed the Frostclad State. In this state, the freezing liquid it expels is even more potent, able to briefly remain on the ground and trigger additional reactions with moisture in the atmosphere, causing spikes of frost resembling those clinging to its body to erupt from the ground.
Behavior
Amongst the Legiana population, very few manage to become a Shrieking Legiana, with the majority of the population remaining as they are even in cold environments, such as the Hoarfrost Reach. Some have theorized the Legiana originally came from the Hoarfrost Reach, although this has yet to be proven to be the case. The Shrieking Legiana often cohabits with the standard variety, and in spite of any variance, the two love to nest far out of reach in steep mountain valleys, upon crags, and other similar locations, reportedly becoming attached to certain perching spots from which they can swoop down in unison to patrol their surroundings for potential threats as well as their next meal. When either one is threatened, both the Legiana and Shrieking Legiana can call upon each other for aid. However, while the standard Legiana is more prone to doing so—freely calling upon Shrieking Legiana when enraged or desperate—the Shrieking Legiana will only call upon other Legiana for help when returning to its nest on the brink of death.
During a hunt, the Shrieking Legiana takes on a more distinct role and calls for other standard Legiana through its namesake shriek to corner prey. Physiology
The Shrouded Nerscylla closely resembles the common Nerscylla, being a large six-eyed Temnoceran with six legs, four of which are used for walking while the anterior two limbs are modified into hooked claws. Much like the common species, the Shrouded Nerscylla possesses massive extendable chelicerae doused in venom. A distinguishing feature of this Subspecies is its coloration—its shell is black with purple nodes around the joints and blue accents on the underside. Just as with the regular species, the true shell of the Shrouded Nerscylla is often hidden by the skin of other monsters, which the Temnoceran wears as a cloak. While the common Nerscylla generally makes use of the Gypceros' hide to benefit from its thunder resistant properties, the Shrouded Nerscylla is generally seen wearing the skin of the Khezu. The purpose of this is believed to be related to moisture retention, as the wet hide of the Khezu can protect the Shrouded Nerscylla from drying out in the desert and reflect sunlight due to its color. It has been suggested the Shrouded Nerscylla may wear other monster skins as well depending on regional variations.
Despite the Shrouded Nerscylla displaying the same venomous bite of the common species, the large crystal spikes on its back are quite different, being a sickly yellow instead of purple. While these spikes are similarly made up of crystalized venom, they contain a special paralytic compound unique to this Subspecies. These spikes can easily paralyze foes, as the venom they consist of is highly concentrated.
Behavior
The Shrouded Nerscylla mostly inhabits the Dunes and is generally considered a desert-dweller. Its hunting strategy differs quite drastically from the common species: the Shrouded Nerscylla does not build webs—although it does possess the ability to produce webbing—and instead digs into the sand where it lies in wait until suitable prey walks by. When such an opportunity presents itself, it emerges with its chelicerae extended, snapping together violently in an attempt to kill the target in one bite. The Shrouded Nerscylla additionally uses its hooked claws to gut and skin prey.
The Shrouded Nerscylla is born in desert regions, although cannot reach maturity there as the monsters it needs to skin—namely the Khezu—do not live in those climates. In order to grow into a state in which it can survive the desert sun and is able to find secure sources of food, the juvenile Shrouded Nerscylla will build a small sail with its webbing in order to catch the winds that whip across the arid wastes, allowing itself to be carried away into new lands. Its goal is to land in cavernous areas, such as the Sunken Hollow, where it can feast on the rotten carcasses left behind by large cave predators. Should the Shrouded Nerscylla survive long enough to successfully skin a Khezu, it can then return to the desert it was born in, reigning over it and eventually laying eggs there itself to start the cycle anew.
Development
The idea behind creating a subspecies for Nerscylla was to play around with the skin it wears. While this initially meant just changing the properties of the Gypceros skin, the design team later moved on to experimenting with having the design use the skins of different monsters. Early ideas included the Shrouded Nerscylla wearing the skins of Gendrome, Kecha Wacha and Khezu. The latter was ultimately chosen.

Physiology
Being a Rare Species of the Rathalos, the Silver Rathalos closely resembles his crimson cousin. His sole distinctive visual feature is his armor shell, which sports a shining silver coloration and scales said to glow like the moon. It is believed this Rare Species is the result of a mutation that reverted a Rathalos population back to some of their ancestral traits that the regular species had lost over eons of evolution. What brought on this mutation is unknown, although it has been suggested to have been caused by the Silver Rathalos' remote and extreme habitats. Some researchers believe the mutation was catalyzed by the ingestion of enriched materials found only in the remote habitat this rare species dwells in. It has specifically been proposed that the mutation that gave rise to the Silver Rathalos resulted from the bio-accumulation of energetically enriched minerals and ores, either by direct ingestion, or through their accumulation in species the affected Rathalos preyed upon.
Beyond its coloration, the shell of the Silver Rathalos displays numerous additional alterations. Believed to perhaps be due to the electrical conductivity of the precious metals present in his shell, the Silver Rathalos is vulnerable to the Thunder element. Conversely, the shell appears to be unaffected by the Dragon element. The Silver Rathalos' body sports more profound changes than just the shell, however, as his musculature is vastly superior compared to the common Rathalos and he is especially well-adapted to aerial combat. In fact, the Silver Rathalos displays the most sophisticated aerial mobility and agility out of all known Rathalos variations. While all of the Silver Rathalos' movements are extremely fast, particularly when enraged, it is not merely about an increase in speed. The Silver Rathalos is more dexterous, able to take off into the air immediately after attacking whilst still grounded. Crucial to this is the Rare Species' powerful wings, which also appear to have mutated, as they are said to exude a faint warmth when spread for unknown reasons.
Perhaps the most significant trait of the Silver Rathalos, however, is his vastly empowered flame breath. Due to the ways in which the remote habitat of this Rare Species has altered the body, the Flame Sac of the Silver Rathalos has been found to be mutated to allow for two new functions. Firstly, the sac has been modified to be able to continuously take in air from the wyvern's respiration and funnel it into the flame production. Secondly, the flame sac now produces another substance in addition to the flame powder found in all Rathalos: a flammable fluid that enhances the flames significantly. Called Rath Gleam, this special fluid is known to glow and boil seemingly on its own. Additionally, Rath Gleam protects the internal tissue of the wyvern from extreme heat. Curiously, Rath Gleam seems to be produced and concentrated in the wyvern's head, which had led to the belief that the mysterious substance might be some kind of modified cerebrospinal fluid. Through the combination of the additional air circulation and the Rath Gleam, the Silver Rathalos' flame sac can activate and maintain a critical state in which heat permeates the body and allows for extremely powerful flames to be born. This ability is known as the Incandescent State.
It is believed that—aside from environmental factors—it was the ability to enter this Incandescent State that pushed the Silver Rathalos towards becoming as powerful as he is, with the leading theory suggesting his body grew more powerful and resilient in order to withstand the wyvern's newfound power. A purple-blue glow envelops the body as the shell of the Silver Rathalos brims with incandescent heat, which causes even the armor plates on the wyvern's head to soften. Fire production increases dramatically, to the point where small wisps of flame continuously leak from the Silver Rathalos' mouth. The Silver Rathalos is capable of producing a unique kind of fire, called the Incandescent Flame, which distinguishes itself through its pale-blue color. Due to the constant critical heat within the Silver Rathalos' body, the wyvern can produce these magnificent flames near instantly, allowing for violent and rapid fire breaths. Aside from simply burning hotter than most fire produced by wyverns, the Incandescent Flame contains small embers that are prone to reacting with each other, resulting in powerful flame explosions and heat waves. This flame breath is so powerful that some believe it bestows the Silver Rathalos with power that surpasses Elder Dragons.
Behavior
Due to his rarity and remote habitat, very little is known about the Silver Rathalos. He is most commonly sighted in unusual and distant environments, such as the Guiding Lands or the Tower. However, the wyvern has been noted to pair up with the Gold Rathian, and the two were on one occasion observed attempting to build a nest in the Elder's Recess. A Silver Rathalos successfully pairing up with a Gold Rathian would be considered a disaster, as the pair's claimed territory would have to be declared a no-man's-land due to the immense threat these wyverns pose.
Both the Silver Rathalos and Gold Rathian have held some degree of cultural significance over the years. The two were the defining members of the Rare Species classification, which was created to describe the limited remote habitat and small estimated population of these mysterious creatures. Beyond their relevance to the Hunter's Guild, the two rare wyverns have also been worshiped by various cultures across time, with the Silver Rathalos being revered under the title, Silver Sol.

Physiology
The Slagtoth is a medium-sized Herbivore that is adapted equally well to live in both humid and volcanic environments. The Slagtoth's head is boxy with a small bony frill positioned at the back, with it also possessing a large black nose, although its most characteristic feature is the incredibly loose hide that sags over the side of its body, most notably around the neck. The coloration of this hide is known to vary depending on the kind of environment in which the Slagtoth lives: the hide is colored green in individuals who live in more humid environments, and a dull-orange in those who live in volcanic ones. Each side of the Slagtoth's body is lined with several brown spots outlined by a cream hue in humid individuals, and a vivid orange in volcanic individuals.
The sagging hide serves several different purposes. While it predominantly aids the Herbivore in evading strikes that might otherwise prove fatal, it additionally serves the purpose of storing excess nutrients for the monster as well as providing it with resistances to both water and heat, allowing it to effectively survive in both wet and dry environments. Moreover, the oils secreted by the Slagtoth are frequently used in both Potions and salves.
Behavior
The Slagtoth is both a territorial and stubborn monster, behaviors that are exemplified by the male Slagtoth's refusal to leave even when another monster significantly larger than itself invades upon its turf. However, it typically will not go out of its way to attack intruders, only going after those who directly approach it.

Physiology
The Somnacanth is a Leviathan with a body covered in faded yellow scales that glisten and shimmer due to their watery coating, as well as sharp yellow shells that slice through water and injure enemies on contact. Its forelimbs have small yellow fins attached at the forearm, and three long hooked talons—which can be repurposed as farming tools due to their shape—that tear through prey, its hindlimbs lack both the fins and elongated talons. The Somnacanth's head bears two sets of drooping purple fins on either side, a pair of small purple horns, a wide mouth, and blank, lidless, white eyes lined with luminescent blue tissue. The underbelly of the Somnacanth is exceptionally hardened, allowing it to crack open its preferred food of oysters on it.
The Somnacanth's head, back, and tail boast large, draping, purple fins, with the smaller fins along its tail being used for underwater mobility. The largest fin on its head, the density of which fluctuates depending on its mood, is lined with fast growing dart-like barbs that can be flung at high velocity when the Somnacanth swings its head. When enraged, the Somnacanth flushes blood into its fins, giving them a brighter blotted appearance; in legends, its beautiful fins were often mistaken for the souls of those who had drowned at sea. The Somnacanth's tail is long and extremely strong, able to support its entire body weight as it swings its upper body around.
The Somnacanth's body produces a glimmering blue powder with soporific properties that is expelled from the glowing blue gills along its neck and tail, as well as from its mouth. This powder is potent enough to induce near-instantaneous sleep to any creature that inhales, or so much as touches the expelled substance.
Behavior
The Somnacanth is a ferocious monster that shows no mercy to intruders in its territory, utilizing every means at its disposal to get rid of them. In addition to its barbs and sleep powder, the Somnacanth battles using powerful swings from its head fins and tail, and favors initially neutralizing the target with sleeping powder to prevent them fighting back, before descending upon them whilst they are out cold. The Somnacanth will often stand on its tail instead of its legs, and mostly swims on its back when near the surface.
The Somnacanth hunts and feeds on aquatic life, with a particular preference for large oysters, which it digs up underwater and cracks open on its hardened belly. Its diet of oysters is said to provide it with the substances used for the production of its signature sleeping powder. In addition, the Somnacanth is known to gather special oysters with unique properties, such as oysters that release explosions, flashes of light, or healing powder, and strategically break them open in combat.
An odd behavior of the Somnacanth is its tendency to vocalize in a manner akin to song, even when nothing else is around. This behavior has led to the monster gaining a reputation as a siren that lures in unsuspecting victims.
Development
The design team based Somnacanth off of mermaids in both western and eastern folklore, along with elements from otters to model its swimming patterns. While Somnacanth was intended to have mermaid-like behaviors such as "leading players astray", the team found it difficult to implement into gameplay, with it instead being represented as Somnacanth's ability to put players to sleep.

Physiology
The Soulseer Mizutsune closely resembles the regular Mizutsune, although is mostly differentiated and easily identified by its crooked and over-developed front claws, whitened fur, and injured eye. This Deviant emerges when a Mizutsune is blinded—through either combat or natural processes, such as age—following which, the Leviathan may overcome the loss of its vision by becoming even more attuned to its other senses, specifically its auditory perception. While the regular Mizutsune uses its ability to sense and hear its bubble's pop and bounce around the environment merely as an auxiliary sense, the Soulseer Mizutsune relies entirely on its bubble sense to understand its surroundings.
Like the regular individual, this Deviant is able to produce bubbles for combat purposes. In addition to the regular variety, however, the Soulseer Mizutsune can produce flaming azure bubbles that explode violently as they pop. These flaming bubbles are a result of the Soulseer Mizutsune feeding primarily upon the Burst Arowana, a species of fish known to contain volatile compounds. These compounds are repurposed by the Deviant into its Synovial Fluid, allowing it to create these explosive bubbles. However, trace amounts of these compounds are secreted from the body and accumulate around the eye sockets of the Leviathan. Thus, as the Soulseer Mizutsune enrages and its body temperature rises rapidly, these deposits near its eyes evaporate into a blue flame-like cloud of vapor.
Behavior
Unlike the fairly active regular individual, the Soulseer Mizutsune can often be seen curled up and resting, surrounded by a large cluster of bubbles. If even one of these bubbles is disturbed, the Deviant will wake up immediately and investigate. Should its bubbles be popped further, it will ignite into a fiery rage and attack with new found vigor. Physiology
Being a Subspecies, the Stygian Zinogre closely resembles the physique of the standard Zinogre: it is a front-heavy Fanged Wyvern with an extremely muscular torso, a long armored tail, well-developed front limbs, porous horns, a dorsal mane, and a two-colored carapace. The primary difference that distinguishes this Subspecies from its much more common counterpart lies in its coloration, as while the Zinogre is adorned in blue and yellow shells, the dual-colored carapace of the Stygian Zinogre is instead characterized by drab black and white shells. Its fur is a shining, silvery-white, and similarly lacks any eye-catching hues, as opposed to the yellowed fur often associated with the regular Zinogre.
The differing coloration belies a deeper change in the Stygian Zinogre's physiology; the Shockshells used by the common species to generate electricity are mutated in the Stygian Zinogre and have gained two additional modified functions. For one, they are now able to produce small quantities of the Dragon element, which is then immediately converted in an amalgam of electricity and Dragon energy, called Dragonlight (龍光). The Stygian Zinogre weaponizes this entirely unique element in a manner much like the standard Zinogre does with the Thunder element, channeling it to enhance all of its physical attacks. The flow of Dragon energy alongside the Dragonlight has the additional benefit of producing heat, granting the Stygian Zinogre an abnormally delicate control over its body temperature and thus enabling it to venture into any manner of extreme climates.
Alongside the subsequent output of Dragonlight, the Stygian Zinogre's production of the Dragon element is by itself not strong enough to withstand the kind of battles the wyvern engages in, which is why this Subspecies further makes use of symbiosis. Instead of bonding with Thunderbugs, however, the Stygian Zinogre symbiotically lives alongside Dracophage Bugs, a rare variety of insect that is known to feed on Dragonfell Berries. These bugs produce Dragon energy as a natural by-product of their metabolism, which they then donate to their Stygian Zinogre host to further empower it. They charge the Stygian Zinogre with Dragon energy that is then stored in its shells; the more power that is stored, the greater equipment can be forged from the shell. Curiously, Dracophage Bugs have never been seen in the wild and have thus far been exclusively found on and in the body of the Stygian Zinogre, where they breed in the gaps between the wyvern's scales.
Using the influence of its bugs, as well as its own natural production of Dragonlight, the Stygian Zinogre can charge itself up until intense red lightning envelops its entire body. This state bestows it with the same boosts seen in the regular Zinogre's super-charged state: increased physical strength, elemental attributes that enhance its strikes, and a greater range of attack. Although, unique to it, the Stygian Zinogre's super-charged state also hardens its body significantly, deflecting physical assaults. Yet this benefit comes at a precarious cost, as when the Stygian Zinogre is clad in Dragonlight, it becomes extremely vulnerable to elemental counterattacks.
The Stygian Zinogre is known to occasionally produce odd and valuable rocks inside of its stomach, called Umbrages. The origin and function of these stones remains unknown.
Behavior
Unlike the common species, the Stygian Zinogre is mostly found wandering harsh environments with extreme climates. It has been found inhabiting both broiling volcanic mountains as well as desolate frozen wastelands, which it thrives in thanks to its excellent internal temperature control. The Stygian Zinogre is extremely aggressive and will attack perceived intruders in its territory mercilessly. It has been theorized it may sometimes wander in search of other powerful monsters, as the Stygian Zinogre's appearance in the Guiding Lands is thought to have been influenced by the emergence of the Red Dragon.
In combat, the Stygian Zinogre expertly utilizes its bonded Dracophage Bugs to expand its repertoire of attacks. The bugs are capable of carrying Dragonlight charges at a distance, redirect lightning arcs that originate from their host's body, or even serve as lightning rods that catch and subsequently expel Dragonlight, extending the range of the wyvern's assaults.

Physiology
The Teostra is the male counterpart of a sexually dimorphic species of Elder Dragon and is the mate of the Lunastra, the Teostra's female counterpart. Heralded as the “Emperor of Flame”, its presence creates a temperature imbalance wherever it appears. The Teostra boasts a muscular appearance and a body plan similar to that of most Elder Dragons, being a quadruped with two large wings attached at the shoulder. Despite its size, the Teostra is surprisingly agile due to its well-developed limbs and feet; its paws are protected by thick padding on the undersides and long claws, which are used for rending foes and for traction when it dashes about, ensuring it doesn't slip on volcanic rock. These claws are difficult to work with even for expert smiths, and retain their heat even when removed from the Teostra's body. Its head resembles that of a Fanged Beast; it is adorned with two massive horns that twist backwards, sports fur on its cheeks and head, and large fangs that protrude outwards.
The body of the Teostra runs incredibly hot, so much so it impacts the area it inhabits. In order to sustain itself and maintain its high body temperature, the Teostra’s diet consists primarily of minerals rich in thermal energy, with coal in particular being said to be the Elder Dragon's favorite food item. However, whether the minerals it eats actually provide the Teostra with any nutrition remains a mystery. A testament to how hot the Teostra's entire body runs can be found in a gem that forms within its body over its lifetime and is constantly shrouded in flame. Its body is covered in thick and heavy, eye-catching scutes resembling red-hot steel; these shells are difficult to harvest and handle due to their high temperature, and are notoriously heat-resistant. Covered in thick, red shelling with a large tuft of fur at its tip, the Elder Dragon's stone-hard tail is incredibly difficult to sever.
Its high body temperature is crucial to its survival, as the Teostra’s primary weapon is its mastery of flame. Able to enshroud its entire body in a cloak of flames, the Elder Dragon can transform a refined gas in its body into a searing, flame-like breath, theorized to form due to the coal the Teostra consumes. In a short burst, the Teostra can emit an intense wave of fire that creates a strong enough wind pressure to block Slinger ammo, bowgun shots, and arrows. When covered in this flaming armor, the entire body burns with flickering flames and its paws scorch the ground where it walks. To achieve this, the Teostra's body is covered in a flammable powder composed of its dead skin cells, this powder is typically stored in the small hairs that grow along the underside of its wings. By jostling its limbs or wings, the powder particles disperse and can then be ignited by sparks created when the Teostra gnashes its teeth. When the Elder Dragon is covered in the volatile powder, the tips of its horns glow red, leading some researchers to believe the distribution and dispersal of the particles is controlled through its horns. While the spreading and ignition of its dander can cause damage to surrounding organisms and the environment, it is believed the primary function of these explosions is to dispose of biological debris from the body; the powder is additionally said to magnify the abilities of other materials. Analyzing samples of the Teostra's scale powder is incredibly difficult, however, as in addition to the substance undergoing a complex chemical reaction that makes analysis troublesome, it is highly volatile and may explode at the slightest touch.
The Elder Dragon’s mane grants it its regal appearance and serves several crucial ecological functions. The mane allows the Teostra to maintain its body temperature, aids in the storage of its explosive powder, and protects its neck from attacks; when in its Dispersion State, the Teostra's mane glows a bright orange. In the New World, the Teostra is noted to have a thicker mane in comparison to the Old World population, with its mane extending to the base of its neck. It is speculated the Teostra’s mane aids in courtship, although there is no current evidence to support this theory. The Teostra’s wings lack phalanges, instead consisting of only a single, elongated finger that is attached to the wing membrane. This wing membrane is covered in tiny hairs and is incredibly heat-resistant. The surface of the Teostra’s coat extends to its wingtips so as to maximize the storage of its flammable powder. As well, unlike the Teostra of the Old World, the Teostra residing in the New World is noted to be a skilled flier and demonstrates aerial maneuverability once thought impossible by Old World researchers.
Behavior
The Teostra primarily resides in volcanic regions and creates its nest by carving through rocky crags with its explosive powder until the nest is spacious enough for its liking. Guild researchers believe the Teostra's nest is crucial for attracting the Lunastra as a mate; a nest that is wider and has easy access to food is favored when the Lunastra picks her mate. Should an intruder infiltrate the nest of the Teostra, the increase in the dragon's body temperature as it prepares for battle results in lava erupting from the ground. Despite its preference towards volcanic environments, the Teostra has additionally been known to claim deserts as its territory. In the New World, the Teostra has been sighted in the Wildspire Waste following the emergence of the Xeno'jiiva, although research suggests the region is only visited by the Fire Dragon occasionally, and not inhabited. Instead, it claims the volcanic caverns in the Elder's Recess as its home territory.
The Teostra can sometimes be seen accompanied by the Lunastra, and when pair-bonded, the two Elder Dragons show exemplary cooperation in combat. While the Lunastra spreads flammable powder throughout the battlefield, the Teostra ignites it using his flame breath. Pairs of the Teostra and Lunastra have been observed performing an explosive courtship dance, in which a chain of explosions surround the couple as they fly around each other, their flammable powder swirling in the air around them. This dance, referred to as The Emperor of Flame's Bond, is a combination of the Teostra's "Supernova" and the Lunastra's "Hell Flare," making it dangerous to witness up close.
There are reports of the Teostra having been sighted alone in the Lava Caverns with no Lunastra in sight, it is theorized that the appearance of Teostra in this locale is tied to the Rampage. Moreover, there are reports of it clashing with the Kushala Daora in violent territorial disputes, as well as those of it repelling the Magnamalo. The Lava Caverns aren't the only place where Teostra has conflicts with other monsters, just the same, the Elder's Recess houses many other powerful monsters the Teostra must defend its territory against, including the Nergigante.
Although its sheer presence is enough to disrupt entire ecosystems, the Teostra has been described as having a "lackadaisical attitude" when it comes to harmless creatures in its vicinity. Contrastingly, however, the Teostra has been noted to be short-tempered and aggressive in the Old World, having been cited as displaying a particularly violent temperament by researchers.
Music
Main article: Teostra (Music)
"Ruler of the Flame" is Teostra's theme. The theme used to be shared with Lunastra until her appearance in World, where she gained a new theme.
Monster Hunter: World
Yuya Tokuda said that from the start of development, the team had Teostra and Kushala Daora already in mind to use for the game. From an elemental standpoint, Kushala Daora's ice abilities complement Teostra's fire and thus made a good pair, so they felt that refining both of these monsters would be satisfying for veterans and newcomers of the franchise. Teostra was the starting point of developing the Elder's Recess' lava region, and it also fit into the story of World as the basis for the Everstream. Both gameplay and setting combined to help make Teostra a standout monster.
The team tried to express how the Elder Dragons were strong enough to directly affect their surrounding environment, which is why Teostra causes lava to erupt whenever it enrages. Since World was developed for high-end platforms, they were able to use fire in new ways, and Kaname Fujioka thought that helped make Teostra stand out even further.
