Physiology
The Tetranadon is a stocky, robustly built Amphibian with a broad flattened beak, a sturdy armored carapace on its back, and thick forelimbs. Its belly is a cream color, whereas the rest of its hide and carapace are a swampy-green. A thick layer of moss and algae grow on the Tetranadon's head, shell, tail, and limbs, which soaks up water and allows the monster to keep its skin moisturized, whilst additionally serving as a layer of cushioning that lends the stout carapace on its back even greater resilience and prevent attacks from behind.
Bolstered by a lifetime of combat and able to stretch considerably, the hide on its belly is notably sturdy and rupture-resistant, allowing the belly to swell to several times its original size once the Tetranadon has gorged itself with grit and water rended from the earth with its powerful beak. During this swelled up state, the Tetranadon will dig up and throw large boulders, and leverage its greater mass as a weapon. The limbs are proportionally long and muscular, enabling the amphibian to leap great distances even when its belly is bloated with swallowed grit. Due to its amphibious nature, the hind feet are webbed, while the forefeet are broad, with thick padding on the finger tips and palms. Due to its unique shape, the Tetranadon's toothless beak is able store and expel highly pressurized water.
The Tetranadon's moisturizing organ is protected by a disc-shaped bone atop its head that fetches a high price if retrieved in flawless condition. This cranial disc hardens as the monster ages and eventually becomes a brilliant blue color; underneath, the monster's head is incredibly tender. The Tetranadon's eyes are red and highly adapted to vision in murky water, allowing it to easily detect underwater prey.
Behavior
The Tetranadon hunts by lurking motionless in deep, quiet waters and swallowing anything that approaches it, including any surrounding rocks and soil that can then be used to help the Tetranadon digest its food. It particularly favors Goocumbers, nonetheless, its voracity leads it to ambush and eat any aquatic life it may find, or leap out of the water to attack terrestrial prey. It has even been known to do this to humans in certain occasions, which usually ends with the Tetranadon spitting them back out as it cannot digest an entire human properly, especially if they are wearing clothes or armor.
In addition to aiding digestion, the Tetranadon will intentionally bulk itself up with debris and water during combat, greatly increasing its weight and physical might. However, it must eventually expel this weight, often done violently in the form of a high-pressure jet of debris and water.
The female Tetranadon will lay her eggs on clumps of seaweed and hide them in spots where she is able to lay low and watch them as they hatch, often preferring the bottoms of waterfalls. The male Tetranadon, on the other hand, is instinctually drawn to such spots and will engage in competitions of strength against other males nearby, pushing and throwing one another in hopes of impressing a watching female hidden nearby, and eventually earning the right to mate with her.
Development
The Tetranadon was based on the kappa (河童/かっぱ), a humanoid, turtle-like yōkai that dwells near riverbeds and often causes trouble for humans. Several elements of the kappa were reflected in its design, such as its turtle-like body shape, distinct bill, and the dish-like formation on its head. As kappa were alleged to enjoy sumo wrestling, this was used to design Tetranadon's sumo-inspired moveset. Additional aquatic animals like crocodiles and platypuses were used for inspiration.

They primarily utilize unearthed boulders during combat, either laying them as hazards or carrying them in their mouth to be crushed later. However, if they exert themselves too much while manipulating terrain, their tail softens and weakens.

Physiology
The Tetsucabra is a large toxic Amphibian which few have successfully hunted, it is characterized by an array of blood-orange scales covering its rounded body that are interspersed by several rows of black scutes along its back, with the scutes nearer the center being larger. The color of these scales aids the Tetsucabra in blending in with its cavernous environment, while their toughness often causes people to mistake them for minerals. The shelling covering itself is highly flexible and rubbery, yet still displays a strong degree of durability. By contrast, the hide on its underside is a light tan coloration, while its head is adorned with two pairs of small tan horns, bestowing it an appearance akin to an oni and granting it the nickname of Oni Frog.
The Tetsucabra possesses highly-muscular limbs—covered in deep-blue scales—that allow it to effortlessly leap great distances or high into the air, aiding it in traversing steep terrain. However, while its limbs aid in propelling itself with linear movements, the Tetsucabra is not very maneuverable and struggles to move in more elaborate ways. To compensate for its lackluster agility, the amphibian will frequently spit a slimy mucus from its mouth to immobilize prey, as the fluid will sap the stamina out of those it entraps. The short yet stout claws located on the ends of these limbs are tough enough to easily shatter through large boulders with ease. Its short tail is rounded and covered in several smaller spikes with its color slowly fading to a dark grey; it is used by the Tetsucabra to assist with maintaining balance during movement.
The most notable feature of the Tetsucabra are the enlarged pair of "tusks" on its lower jaw, although despite the common name they are actually just projections of the jaw itself, formed when its dense jaw bone hardens and enlarges. These tusks are used in unison with its shovel-like jaw as not just effective weaponry for hunting but as tools for excavation and movement. The Tetsucabra is able to use them to burrow into the ground to move between locations as well as to unearth and carry boulders with little effort in its maw. Although, should it strain itself whilst exerting significant strength in its upper body to lift these boulders, the soft white skin of the Tetsucabra's tail end will inflate and expose itself, causing it to become notably more vulnerable to damage. Recent discoveries have revealed that should the Amphibian's tusks sustain damage or is lost in its entirety, it will be replaced by a harder and stronger iteration that grows in its place every time. The growth of these new tusks mimics that of a tree, with the insides displaying similar growth rings. The bones that make up the Tetsucabra's robust skull are significantly tougher and more resilient and than what is typical, and the evolution of this warped and sturdy skull warrants further study by researchers. Furthermore, while the mouth of the Tetsucabra may appear to be small at a glance, it is capable of opening extremely wide, allowing it to easily swallow small monsters whole with a single bite.
Like the Zamtrios, the Tetsucabra possesses the mysterious Paddock Oil, the properties of which make it an ideal material for smithies. It is commonly used as a lubricant or additive, with purer oil resulting in higher temperatures for forging. When in the form of a thick cream, the oil enhances the strength of equipment by a significant amount.
As a juvenile, the Tetsucabra greatly resembles a fully matured individual, although key differences in appearance may be found in the juvenile's paddle-like tail and lack of darkened scutes along the back; the tusks and jaws are also notably less developed than the adults.
Behavior
The Tetsucabra is an Amphibious monster that dwells in a variety of environments, ranging from forests and caverns, to islands, and even harsh, frigid and fiery regions. Oftentimes, the Tetsucabra is associated with the Sunken Hollow and the trouble it frequently causes for the Troverians, with the presence of one in the region typically completely halting their attempted mining efforts. A common way it causes interruptions in the local ecosystem is by using its tusks, which are effective tools of terrain manipulation both in and out of combat. They can be utilized for throwing rocks as projectiles, or for carrying boulders in its mouth, with its jaw muscles being powerful enough to crush these rock into dust. Moreover, they are used to unearth massive slabs of rock that act as walls to obstruct the vision of predators, allowing the Tetsucabra to make a hasty escape by burrowing away.
The Tetsucabra will fight another of its own kind if need be, even to the death, however, it should not be confused for battling over mating rights. In order to attract a female to mate with, the male Tetsucabra will utilize its ability to uproot and crush rocks in an attempt to showcase its physical power—females will only mate with the males that showcase the most impressive displays. After mating, the female will construct a "nest" by digging up rocks from the ground, before laying her eggs directly onto the soil underneath that has soften from the rocks removal. Afterwards, the male will scoop the eggs up with his shovel-like jaw and keep the eggs in his mouth to incubate them. Until the clutch of eggs hatch, the male Tetsucabra will neither eat or drink.
While the Tetsucabra displays aggression in its maturity, the Amphibian appears to have a much calmer demeanor as a juvenile. In the village of Kamura, there resides an old Wyverian who has befriended and sits atop a young Tetsucabra. Affectionately called Tetsy, the two amicably play together until she tires.
Development
Many of Tetsucabra’s attacks are based on sumo techniques, such as the sidestomp, which mimics a traditional shikogeri.

Physiology
The Thunder Serpent Narwa is the female of a sexually dimorphic species of Elder Dragon, with the Wind Serpent Ibushi being the male. She has a massive serpentine body covered in a tan rubbery hide that is so well insulated, lightning strikes could be mistaken for bug bites; her hide is additionally armored with a flexible and light carapace able to ward off attacks without infringing on the Elder Dragon's mobility. She has four fin-shaped limbs, with a pair of larger clawed forelimbs and smaller paddle-like hindlimbs that cradle a large, pulsating, yellow sac on her belly that is used to store her eggs and generate electricity. Vibrant orange tentacles line the dorsal side of her body and arms, and she also possesses larger purple Sparksacs on her head, chest, back, arms, and tail. Her head has a pair of straight horns, beady yellow eyes, and a unique pharyngeal jaw structure, with a folding outer jaw enveloping a set of four toothed inner mandibles. When enraged, the Narwa's eyes glow orange.
By rubbing her numerous tentacles together and utilizing her Sparksacs, the Thunder Serpent Narwa generates a vast electrical charge that accumulates within her Sparksacs and generates a powerful magnetic field, granting her the ability to freely float by repelling herself off of terrain, with the Narwa often adopting an unusual upside-down flying orientation. Due to the magnetic field, the Narwa is additionally able to freely lift and throw metal-containing objects or terrain, or even rip them out of the earth. When threatened, the Narwa discharges this electricity through a variety of yellow and purple lightning attacks fired from her mouth, belly sac, and tentacles; mostly consisting of rings, beams, pillars, and bolts of electricity fired in dense patterns. As she accumulates an electrical charge, her tentacles and Sparksacs will become wreathed in electricity and begin glowing bright purple, and the strength of her discharges will intensify. Once charged up, the scale of her electrical output can cause severe burns just by being in her vicinity, while passively causing nearby terrain to begin sporadically floating around her and violent thunderstorms to engulf the surrounding area. While the Narwa's body is so well insulated that it suffers no ill-effects from the vast electrical currents flowing through her, sufficient damage to her Sparksacs—particularly the largest sac on her abdomen—can explosively discharge their stored electricity and disrupt her magnetic field.
When angered, the Narwa will exert a large influence on her environment through her resonant roar and the thunderstorms she stirs up, with her presence in an ecosystem agitating nearby monsters and causing them to exhibit unusual movement patterns. The behavior of the monsters agitated by the Narwa is said to be analogous to those in the Rampage created by her mate's storms.
Deep within her body, the Thunder Serpent grows a mysterious shimmering gem said to grant whoever wields it dominion of thunderstorms.
Behavior
The Narwa's behavior beyond the mating cycle is unknown, as she has never been seen outside of it. During this cycle, she is less nomadic than her mate, preferring to establish a territory and wait for the Ibushi to find her. Should her nest be threatened, she will attempt to eliminate any and all intruders with extreme prejudice.
As she shares a similar jaw structure with her mate, the Narwa is also presumed to be predatory, albeit with an unknown diet.
Mating
Little is known about the Narwa's developmental process and usual habits beyond her mating cycle, which is noted to coincide with the Rampage. When it comes time to find a mate, the Narwa will emerge and stake out an area for a nest as she waits for the Ibushi to unite with her. While the two serpents use a currently unknown method to locate each other, certain Wyverians —such as Hinoa and Minoto—are able to "Resonate" with this method and translate the Serpents' thoughts into spoken language.
After the nesting stage is complete, the two Elder Dragons perform an airborne mating dance that culminates in the fertilization of her eggs and a terrifying storm engulfing the area. Following this, the Narwa descends into the depths of the nest and awaits to lay its clutch, while her mate hovers in the skies above, ready to protect his mate with his life. However, it has been observed that this process can also occur differently. If the nest is breached and a threat to the next generation presents itself during the courtship phase, the Narwa will devour the Ibushi's "lifeforce", a process that is fatal to the Wind Serpent. This empowers the Narwa and transforms her into Narwa the Allmother, granting her the Ibushi's command over wind as well as accelerating the growth of her eggs.
Music
Main article: Thunder Serpent Narwa (Music)
"Lady of Lightning" is Thunder Serpent Narwa's theme. Paired with Wind Serpent Ibushi, "Lady of Lightning" shares melodies with "Breath of Ire", and additionally like this theme contains a motif of the Rampage. The theme is sung by solo vocalist Minoto, performed by Kanae Miyazaki), who resonates with the monster. "Lady of Lightning" is also one of the very few Monster Hunter themes with official lyrics.
Both Ibushi and Narwa share a theme for their appearance in Monster Hunter Stories 3: Twisted Reflection, acting as a mix of both "Lady of Lightning" and "Breath of Ire" but without vocals.
Development
Narwa was designed to invoke a feeling of fear with its mysterious, bizarre appearance and ability to freely float in any direction, while its design was also made with the intention of ensuring its distinctive features were visible from any angle. Similar to Ibushi, in order to represent Narwa's relationship with Minoto, Narwa's introduction poem is narrated by Minoto, also being written to emphasize how Narwa "waits" while Ibushi "searches". The team had decided from the beginning to create both Thunder Serpent Narwa and Narwa the Allmother, so the two needed to have clear gameplay differences: Thunder Serpent Narwa was designed to focus more on gimmicks and use of gameplay mechanics, while Narwa the Allmother was chosen to instead represent a straightforward, back-and-forth battle. The design team described difficulties making Narwa's fight, as they had to balance the floating rocks and unique Wirebug mechanics with Narwa's own actions.
While Ibushi's hide textures were inspired by whales and sea turtles, Narwa was more inspired by fish and sea anemones; the tentacles in particular were difficult to create, as the modelers wanted them to appear translucent and jelly-like without actually rendering them as transparent. Narwa's visual effects were considered the ones that required the most trial and error out of any monster in the game, as its unique gimmick of manifesting lightning as tangible shapes and objects was a highly unique scenario that ended up creating a one-of-a-kind, mysterious atmosphere. In contrast with Ibushi's sound design being crafted to invoke fear and unease, Narwa's roars and audio telegraphs were designed to invoke a feeling of awe and divinity, while being audible even from the base camp.

The Thunderlord Zinogre is a Mutation. It is unlocked by raising Zinogre's Ecosystem Rank to S with an area with at least one Mizutsune or Soulseer Mizutsune.
Physiology
While the Thunderlord Zinogre broadly resembles a regular individual as far as its basic body plan, there are several drastic differences to be found beyond that. The skin has a more intense green hue compared to the regular Zinogre and most of the fur and spikes of the Deviant display a regal, golden color; the front limbs meanwhile have a reddish hue to them, the result from having slain a vast amount of prey. The horns of the Thunderlord Zinogre are asymmetrical, with the right horn being much larger and more distorted than the left.
The body of the Thunderlord Zinogre is said to be constantly overflowing with Thunder energy, a phenomenon that may be observed in the fur, which glows a golden color and is known to continue expelling electricity even after it has been removed from the body. The Thunderlord Zinogre can reach a level of power unseen in regular individuals, wherein its body becomes robed in golden lightning. Entitled the Deviant's Ultracharged State, the Thunderlord Zinogre is able to discharge more powerful thunderbolts when empowered. It is currently unknown how the Thunderlord Zinogre comes to be.
Behavior
Very little is known about the Thunderlord Zinogre's behavior, although it is considered extremely aggressive and its temper is subject to folkloric tales of its anger tearing the skies apart. Furthermore, while it is mostly solitary, the Thunderlord Zinogre has been noted to sometimes appear in groups and pairs; on at least one occasion, it has even been sighted in a hoard of up to six individuals. Due to the threat the Thunderlord Zinogre inherently poses, its appearance is an emergency that may only be dealt with by Wycademy Hunters who possess a Special Permit, as is the case with every other Deviant.
Development
Thunderlord Zinogre was the first Deviant to be designed.
The design team wanted to focus on highlighting bold differences between the normal version and the Deviant, so they chose to slightly change the shape of the body and horns, which were designed to somewhat resemble a crescent moon. They also wanted to play with colors - the idea of a solid gold Zinogre led to much of the color design, while the reddish hues around its forelimbs evoke the image of them being splashed with blood.
From the beginning, Thunderlord Zinogre was intended to have a level of charge above the regular species. However, the design team worried that if they simply increased all of its attributes in this new state, the monster would become too fast. Thus, the Ultracharged State was designed to focus on energy output and strength instead.

The Water Snake Wyvern Tidal Najarala (ガララアジャラ亜種, Gararājara Ashu) is a Snake Wyvern introduced in Monster Hunter 4 Ultimate. It is a Subspecies of the Najarala.

A light-blue-and-yellow Subspecies of Najarala with characteristic purple plates. Their distinct colors not only aid in camouflage, but also act as a warning to any attackers. While they retain their paralyzing bite and tendency to coil around prey, the dislodged scales cannot shatter by sound. Physiology
A tundra-dwelling Subspecies of the Najarala, the Tidal Najarala's body is adorned with a thick vibrantly colored carapace consisting of several yellow, purple, and light-blue stripes. These bright colors act as a warning to other monsters, although they will fade when the Tidal Najarala grows fatigued. Underneath this carapace lies a thick, yet flexible hide that is a popular material for its use in luxurious leather products. The shells on the Tidal Najarala's body are composed of a transparent crystal-like material that absorbs sunlight, which helps keep the Subspecies warm in its otherwise frigid habitat.
The Tidal Najarala's back and tail are armed with shells unique to this Subspecies; called Splashers, they are colored in a vibrant mixture of blues, greens, and purples. Possessing innate hydrophobic properties, which the monster appears to be aware of, the Tidal Najarala is able to dislodge these Splashers from its body by lashing with its tail to use them as projectiles. Contained within its body are several Aqua Sacs that allow it to spit out a water-like bile from its beak. When the Tidal Najarala shoots this bile at one of its dislodged scales, the liquid is deflected and changes directions, allowing it to reach distant targets. Further, the dislodged scales are capable of altering their shape, allowing them to better channel and reflect water.
The Tidal Najarala's beak is strong enough to bore through thick ice and bedrock. Its fangs retain the same paralytic neurotoxin as the type species, which it typically utilizes whilst attempting to coil around its prey.
Behavior
The Tidal Najarala is found in the Frozen Seaway. While its cousin is entirely terrestrial, the Tidal Najarala is capable of swimming through freezing waters.
Its awareness of the properties of its scales suggests the Tidal Najarala is a rather cunning predator, as research into the monster's hunting mechanisms concluded that it purposely aims its water breath at its scattered Splashers to hit an enemy's blind spot. In addition, the Tidal Najarala still utilizes the same method of constriction seen within the common Najarala.

Physiology
As a Subspecies, the Tigerstripe Zamtrios closely resembles the nominate, blue-scaled Zamtrios, however, it instead possesses a dull-orange scaling and is covered in darker-shaded stripes. These scales are smooth to the touch, due either to them being weathered by the sand, or as an adaptation so as to better move through the sand. The outer layer of its body additionally possesses a mucus covering, helping to keep the monster hydrated by protecting it from the arid desert winds. This mucus can affix sand to the Tigerstripe Zamtrios' body, aiding it in camouflaging better into the desert. The underside of the Tigerstripe Zamtrios is covered in a highly elastic pale-blue piel that assists the Amphibian in retaining water, aiding in its survival in arid deserts. This hide is mottled with several orange spots that become more prominent when the Tigerstripe Zamtrios inflates. This Subspecies retains the fins on its back and forelimbs, as well as webbed toes, aiding it when swimming. The mere sight of its dorsal fin in the sand is enough to make traveling merchants and caravans uneasy.
Instead of possessing Frost Sacs within its body, the Tigerstripe Zamtrios contains Paralysis Sacs that allow it to spit out a paralytic venom. Furthermore, it is able to intake and store large quantities of water from the oases it lives around, which—after mixing it with its internal body fluid—can be fired off in the form of powerful jets. Unlike the Zamtrios, the Tigerstripe Zamtrios is incapable of forming a protective layer of armor atop its body through its internal fluid. Instead, when the Tigerstripe Zamtrios becomes excited, the water stored inside of its body will evaporate and cause its body to swell up significantly larger than its regular size. The Tigerstripe Zamtrios is comparatively much more skilled at utilizing this inflated state, as it is able to instantly evaporate the water it has ingested, allowing it to enter its inflated state much quicker. To exit the state, the Tigerstripe Zamtrios will fire off the water stored inside its body in the form of a concentrated beam.
Behavior

The Roaring Wyvern Tigrex (ティガレックス, Tigarekkusu) is a Flying Wyvern introduced in Monster Hunter Freedom 2.
Summary
Ferocious Flying Wyverns distinguished by their quadrupedal gait, orange scales, and blue stripes. Tigrex will doggedly charge down prey with the help of their massive forelimbs, tearing into them with their sharp claws and extremely powerful maw upon getting close enough. Their most distinctive ability is a deafening, concussive roar powerful enough to cause small shockwaves. Nomadic in nature, Tigrex will travel through extreme climates in search of prey.

Physiology
The Tigrex is a primitive Flying Wyvern species, easily identifiable by its distinctive quadrupedal gait and highly-developed winged forelimbs. It is thought to be a direct descendant of the believed common ancestor of all Flying Wyverns, the Wyvern-Rex, and its adaptations have served it well since its speciation. Since which, it has remained largely unchanged, lending to its prehistoric appearance and characteristics. Its scaly orange hide sports blue stripes along the top side, whereas its cream-colored underbelly remains clear. The scales themselves are quite large and sturdy, and become stronger than steel when fastened together. The striped pattern of the scales helps the Tigrex camouflage, as its prey recognizes shapes rather than colors. Additionally, the thickness of the scales helps it withstand extreme temperatures. When enraged, the Tigrex's head and forelimbs adopt a red glow due to a rise in body temperature and blood flow, greatly enhancing its muscular strength.
The winged forelimbs of the Tigrex, which extend laterally from the scapula, are abnormally long. As the Tigrex cannot perform self-sustained flight, able only to glide on air currents after leaping from a great height, the forelimbs are functionally useless as wings. Instead, its muscular forelimbs are built for terrestrial traversal and charging at foes with incredible speed, enabling the Tigrex to run faster than 50kph. To aid in flexibility, its shoulders and hips are lined with extra skin. Each of its three toes are adorned with a large claw bearing a striped pattern on the tip, which are the largest of any mid-sized Flying Wyvern and are unique to the Tigrex.
The Tigrex's mouth is lined with a row of small fangs and its bite force is notoriously strong, capable of crushing bone, logs, ice pillars, and even small rocks. Rather than tear flesh with its teeth, the Tigrex smashes prey with its powerful bite. Due to this, the work of the Tigrex is easily recognizable to even those who are not part of the Hunter’s Guild, as prey ravaged by the monster is left in a gruesome state. The title of the Roaring Wyvern comes from the Tigrex's deafening roar, which can be heard across great distances. The monster possesses an enlarged Screamer Sac that allows it to create such loud roars. These roars create shockwaves that shake the earth around it, and no amount of hearing protection can lessen the roar’s impact.
Above the Tigrex's eyes are two horn-like protrusions, of which the purpose of are unknown. As they protrude directly from the skull, some scholars have been led to believe they may function as ears—the presence of structures resembling an auricle or external auditory canal supports this theory. However, others believe they instead serve as a distinguishing feature between the two sexes, suggesting the male Tigrex may develop them for display, or that they help individuals identify each other. The positioning of the protrusions may also suggest they help protect the monster's eyes. These are simply theories, however, and the true purpose of these protrusions is still unknown.
Behavior
The Tigrex is widely revered by Hunters and monsters alike due to its aggressive nature and overwhelming strength. It does not have a fixed domain and lacks a strong sense of territory, as such, it has an incredibly wide habitat range. Its hunting strategy relies on athleticism and brute strength: charging and leaping at its prey, applying its full body weight using its forelimbs and hind legs to hold down its prey. The Tigrex will relentlessly pursue its prey or any potential foe, undeterred by ledges or potential obstacles, until it is killed. On occasion, it may choose to ambush its prey, stalking it before charging it down, where it then pins its prey and delivers the killing blow. Other large monsters typically avoid confronting the Tigrex whenever possible, as its ground maneuverability, physical strength, and violent disposition is enough to deter most competitors. As a result, the Tigrex typically sits at the top of the food chain of any region it travels to. However, the wyvern does not stay in one area for long, and once it has eaten, it will move on to a new hunting ground. Despite its aggression towards other monsters, the Tigrex has been observed coexisting peacefully and, in one instance, working together to ambush a hunting party.
The wyvern typically prefers warm climates, such as Deserts, however, it is also sighted in frigid, mountainous habitats where it is not uncommon for it to be seen near Pokke Village. The Tigrex will only venture into the snowy mountains to hunt large Herbivores, with the Popo being its most favored prey item, although it has also been known to hunt juvenile Gammoth. It prefers to hunt larger prey due to the fact it struggles making sharp turns when charging. Unlike many Flying Wyverns, the Tigrex does not possess any sort of breath attack, and instead hurls excavated earth at distant targets—rocks thrown by the Tigrex can travel up to 30 meters or more. Its utilization of the terrain, in combination with its habit of specifically targeting the rear of fleeing prey, suggests the wyvern possesses an instinctive intelligence.
In the New World, the Tigrex has been sighted in every locale barring the Coral Highlands, although it was originally thought it would be found exclusively in the Hoarfrost Reach due to the abundance of Popo in the area. The Tigrex from the New World often partakes in territorial disputes with other large monsters, such as the Odogaron and Glavenus. The Tigrex will eat and drink twice a day before resting, and typically preys on Gastodon and Raphinos, in addition to the Popo in the Hoarfrost Reach. Curiously, the Ancient Forest is the only place where the Tigrex has been observed sunbathing.
Super Biology Information
The Super Biology Book Series collects the thoughts and theories of real scientists that were asked to speak about monsters from the Monster Hunter series. Thus, they are inherently speculative and should be seen as such.
Fossil Expert Yoshitsugu Kobayashi proposes that the Tigrex might have retained its prehistoric body build due to already being perfectly adapted to a stable niche. Specifically, harsh regions such as Deserts and Tundras produce ecosystems in which most species have to be highly specialized just to survive. Often, this has the added effect of leaving many prey species without a natural predator, since few animals can evolve to specialize in both extreme survival and hunting. The Tigrex then might have evolved specifically to prey on dwellers of such ecosystems, which would be used to life without predators and have thus no advanced defenses against it. Kobayashi proposes that the Tigrex may have evolved to be supremely resistant to dry heat and cold temperatures, as well as developing a type of movement that allows it to traverse varied kinds of terrain.
Noting the visual similarities between the Tigrex and the Tyrannosaurus rex, Kobayashi asserts that those two creatures would be highly unlikely to be actually related. The Tigrex’s ability to walk on all fours and presence of wing membranes fully rules out any relation between the two. Rather, Kobayashi suggests that any similarities between Tigrex and T.rex are the result of convergent evolution.

Main article: Tigrex (Music)
"The Beast Bares Its Fangs", previously known as "The Roaring Wyvern Bares Its Fangs", is Tigrex's theme. As of 2026, it is the theme with the most remasters, with a total of 4 versions appearing across 4 games.
Monster Hunter Freedom 2
Tigrex was designed by Yuya Tokuda with supervision from Yasunori Ichinose and Shintaro Kojima, based on the team's earlier sketches of a wyvern ancestor called the Wyvern-Rex. The design process started with Ryozo Tsujimoto telling the team that flagship monsters for the portable games should have a simple, easy to understand appeal, which Ichinose echoed. Tokuda thus suggested making a monster that would charge at the player with its maw agape, ready to brutally swallow them. Kaname Fujioka additionally suggested that the visual design should take cues from the image of a T-Rex, as that would be very easily recognizable and iconic. After some initial attempts, the team created the Tigrex design by adding bulky muscles to its limbs, distinguishing it from the earliest Wyvern-Rex sketches. The name "Tigrex" was chosen as a combination of Tiger and T-Rex. Since Rathalos had been partially based on a lion, the team felt it was appropriate if the Tigrex incorporated the image of a tiger. This manifested both in its name and its stripes.
Once the initial design was completed, Tokuda handed off the combat design and balancing to Kojima, who oversaw the rest of the Tigrex' development. The first prototype Tigrex was completely relentless and much too challenging. As a result, Kojima requested that its attack speed be lowered and that the monster should take breaks from charging at the player. A continuous problem in creating the Tigrex' motion was the lack of useful real-life reference material, as its gait was intended to be quite unlike any real creature.
Monster Hunter Portable 3rd
With the introduction of the monster stamina system in Monster Hunter 3 - which allowed players to exhaust monsters - the team looked towards Tigrex as a possible monster that could benefit from that mechanic. For the monster's addition into Monster Hunter Portable 3rd, the development team thus experimented with ways in which exhaustion could affect the Tigrex. Getting the balance right was quite difficult however - if the monster fell over and tired too easily, players would be disappointed that a previous flagship monster would be so weak and uncool. There was at one point the idea to make Tigrex entirely immune to being exhausted, but Tokuda insisted that allowing players to tire it out would make for a fun interaction.
Monster Hunter 4
For Monster Hunter 4, Tigrex received overhauled combat behavior largely overseen by Tokuda. The most important goal of this redesign was to give Tigrex new attacks that were smaller and could be used to chain together its bigger moves. Additionally, the monster was given greater control over its motions to allow it to smoothly adjust its distance to the player.

Physiology
The Tobi-Kadachi is a Fanged Wyvern with serpentine features that is covered in blue scales and white fur, it can easily be identified by its massive, broad, furry tail. Oftentimes, this tail matches the main body in length and, depending on the individual, even exceeds it. Much like most other Fanged Wyverns, the Tobi-Kadachi walks on four muscular legs, however, its body is adapted to life in the canopies of dense forests. As such, it is an agile and flexible wyvern able to clear wide gaps with a single jump and weave around complex networks of branches and unreliable terrain with astounding ease. Key to this mobility is the Tobi-Kadachi's curved claws, which allow for a secure grip on even the most uneven surfaces; pads on the palms of the feet allow for even further stability. However, the claws need to remain extremely sharp at all times to allow for the best grip possible, and the Tobi-Kadachi will meticulously sharpen them regularly.
The Tobi-Kadachi's agility is further enhanced by its gliding membrane, which the wyvern grows on each side of its body between the front and hind limbs. This membrane typically remains folded alongside the body, with its soft texture dampening the sounds of the wyvern's movements and concealing its presence. By spreading its legs and bending its front wrists inwards, the Tobi-Kadachi can unfold thin cartilage spines that immediately extend the entire membrane, allowing for gliding flight after a jump.
As it moves around the forest, the Tobi-Kadachi generates static electricity by rubbing its fur against the trees it passes; the largest surface for this to occur on is the wide topside of the tail, which plays a key role in generating this charge. Consequently, the strength of the charge that can be produced this way depends on the size of the tail, with individuals possessing larger tails being able to generate stronger electric charges. While the charge is produced in the fur, it is stored in specialized spikes hidden beneath the fur, called Electrodes. These sharp, modified scales are spread throughout the Tobi-Kadachi's fur and are heavily localized around the tail—some of the smaller ones are able to be detached and launched at enemies by swinging the tail. On top of holding the electric charge, Electrodes grow in their capacity over time, eventually becoming powerful Cathodes. The entire process of electric generation and storage happens on the surface of the body, with the scales and skin of the Tobi-Kadachi serving as insulators that prevent any electricity from penetrating into the wyvern's insides.
Once a sufficient level of static electricity has been stored, the Tobi-Kadachi can ruffle its fur to activate a Charged State, in which the electric charge envelops its fur. During this state, all physical attacks of the wyvern are enhanced with electric properties, and it is believed the circulation of electricity additionally stimulates the muscles into higher tiers of performance. Should a further level of charge be reached, the Tobi-Kadachi can activate its Discharge State, in which the electrodes that were previously hidden amongst the fur grow erect and protrude visibly from the body. Lightning arcs between the spikes, and the Tobi-Kadachi can prick enemies with its erect electrodes to cause shocks and stun them. It has been noted that exposure to water dampens the output of the electrodes and disrupts their function.
In addition to its normal fangs, the Tobi-Kadachi possesses two modified fang-like scales on its lower jaw that aid with holding onto prey with the mouth. The jaw itself can also be unhinged to allow for the swallowing of large prey.
Behavior
The Tobi-Kadachi generally lives in dense forests, where it marks its territory with claw marks and fur left behind on tree bark. The Tobi-Kadachi will spend its entire life in the branches and canopies of its environment, avoiding the ground entirely if possible. This behavior allows it to live in regions with many powerful monsters, as its avoidance of the ground level keeps the Tobi-Kadachi out of most Turf Wars.
When hunting, the Tobi-Kadachi relies on stealth to pounce upon its prey, pursuing it persistently should it manage to survive the initial attack. The Tobi-Kadachi's speed and agility is unmatched in its territory, and the wyvern will outmaneuver enemies swiftly to then attack from behind. When fighting, the Tobi-Kadachi will use both its teeth and tail to inflict damage, although not its claws, as they are far too valuable for climbing and the wyvern cannot risk them getting damaged.
The Tobi-Kadachi is entirely solitary and has never been sighted grouping up, even for mating purposes. Be that as it may, it is believed the size of a male Tobi-Kadachi's tail may be an indicator of sexual fitness.

Physiology
A featherless species of Bird Wyvern endemic to the New World, the Tzitzi-Ya-Ku is known for its colorful scales and flashy displays. Its body features a supple hide covered in iridescent, purple scales with a blue-gray underbelly. The wyvern’s vibrant coloration allows it to blend in with its natural habitat of the Coral Highlands, which is rich in lustrous hues. As a result of the vivid hues present in its habitat, the iridescence of the Tzitzi-Ya-Ku's scales do not affect the strength of its camouflage.
Each of the Tzitzi-Ya-Ku’s forelimbs are adorned with small, blue feathers along their underside, while its forearms, knuckles, and the back of its fingers feature black scutes. Each hand has three long fingers tipped with long, hooked, black claws. The wyvern’s claws—which are the longest of the Bird Wyverns in the New World—are well suited for slashing its foes and additionally allow it to easily traverse the terrain of the Coral Highlands. It uses its claws like climbing picks, digging into cliff faces to climb up vertical terrain. Used similarly, the hind legs of the Tzitzi-Ya-Ku are incredibly powerful, much like those of its closest relative, the Kulu-Ya-Ku. Equipped with a large, sickled claw on both feet, the Bird Wyvern is able to leap impressive distances and kick foes with surprising strength. By using the curved claws on its feet, the Tzitzi-Ya-Ku gains grip on the ground beneath it, before pushing itself off the ground with its full body weight. This powerful leaping ability also aids the Tzitzi-Ya-Ku in travelling across the lower regions of the Coral Highlands, as it can jump over smaller ledges with ease.
The Tzitzi-Ya-Ku’s most unique feature comes in the form of the strange structures that sit atop its head and which resemble antennae when folded. These structures can fan out to reveal large flaps that are controlled by two bones which act simultaneously. Furthermore, contained within its forehead is a pulsing organ that stimulates the photophores contained within the wyvern’s luminescent flaps, producing a blinding flash that can stun predators and prey. The nature of the substance within the wyvern’s pulsing organ is unknown, although there are several theories as to the origin of this substance.
Behavior
The Tzitzi-Ya-Ku primarily resides in the lower strata of the Coral Highlands. While it isn't aggressive at first, should a Hunter linger in its sight, the Tzitzi-Ya-Ku may become hostile. Flashing lights are similarly liable to trigger an aggressive response from the Tzitzi-Ya-Ku, as it may mistake it as a territorial threat. The territory the Tzitzi-Ya-Ku occupies is shared with the pack-hunting Shamos, who despise the flashes that the wyvern produces. Thus, it is not uncommon to see the two quarreling with one another.
To catch its favoured prey, the Raphinos, the Tzitzi-Ya-Ku will use a blinding flash to stun them. The luminescent flaps are not only useful for bringing down prey, however, as they also help defend the Bird Wyvern from large predators. The flashes produced by the Tzitzi-Ya-Ku are strong enough to stun even large monsters, such as the Legiana and Pink Rathian, after which, the Tzitzi-Ya-Ku is quick to flee.
The Tzitzi-Ya-Ku routinely collects lustrous seashells to decorate its nest with. Should an enemy enter its nest, the luster of the seashells diffuses the Tzitzi-Ya-Ku's flash, enhancing the effect and leaving its foes dazed. While the seashell decor serves a defensive purpose, it may also serve as competition between males; females may see a decorated nest as a sign of a male's strength.

Physiology
The Ukanlos is an enormous flightless Flying Wyvern characterized by the several ridges of ice-white armor covering its entire body, whose astounding durability is owed to the various ambient minerals that have infused themselves into its structure. The Ukanlos' back is aligned with multiple streamlined fins coated in saw-like serrations—similar to Sharq teeth—aiding it in cutting through and burrowing beneath frozen rock and densely packed ice alike. Coating the Ukanlos' underbelly, as well as the underside of both its jaw and tail, are thick scales with spiked edges that further aid it in cutting through the snow and ice, increasing its mobility. These features allow the Ukanlos to effortlessly slice through the ice as if it was swimming through water, with the fins lining its back doubling as weapons to slice anything in its pace, homing in towards its target the entire time.
The Ukanlos possesses stout forelimbs covered with raised protective ridges of shelling over their joints, with notably smaller hindlimbs. All of its limbs are mottled with patches of light-blue scales and each one ends in three curved black claws covered in a thin layer of frost, their shape formed throughout the years by the wyvern's repeated voyages across the ice. These massive claws are coated with ridges that allow the Ukanlos to find the grip needed to pull itself across icy surfaces. While normally taking a quadrupedal stance close to the ground, the Ukanlos is able to take a temporary bipedal stance atop its hindlimbs, often done when roaring or expelling ice. The Ukanlos' hindlimbs are deceptively powerful, allowing it to leap several times its body length with a single jump, and its icy tail is incredibly thick, with a single swing being enough to crack glaciers.
Perhaps the Ukanlos' most distinctive feature is its lower jaw, which is formed into a wide spade-shaped structure. Nicknamed a Shoveljaw, it acts as a potent front facing weapon capable of easily slicing through the ice and shoveling large quantities of snow, with it being frequently used by the Ukanlos to fling large snowballs at targets. It is a powerful tool, creating a spectacle whenever it is used to smash apart hunks of ice; a single scoop is capable of summoning an avalanche. Several large honed exoskeleton teeth protrude from the Ukanlos' mouth and bestow it a vigorous bite that crushes both rock and ice without issue, guarding a mouth housing sharp teeth that confirmed the wyvern's predatory status. The Ukanlos can unleash loud roars that damage any who get too close, powerful enough to cause massive chunks of ice to crumble from the ceilings of the frosty caves it frequents. While it cannot weaponize sound to the degree the Akantor can, the Ukanlos is able to expel powerful blasts of ice from its maw. By intaking massive amounts of crushed ice and snow, and compressing it into a freezing slush inside its body, the Ukanlos can fire it out as a potent sub-zero breath attack. This concentrated beam is powerful enough to rip apart the very ground beneath it, with certain Ukanlos individuals even being capable of creating large, freezing tornadoes when utilizing their beam.
As is the case for many monsters, rare gemstones may form within the Ukanlos' body. One such gem is rumored to have been once owned by a tyrant ruler who nearly destroyed the world.
Behavior
The Ukanlos rules a variety of remote and cold regions—from polar caves to the peaks of snowy mountains —and is infamous for its destructive nature, often resulting in it attacking and destroying human settlements. This has necessitated involvement from high ranking Guild officials, with His Immenseness himself commissioning Urgent Quests whenever one is reported by the Dragonwatch. The Ukanlos often roams the hoarfrost blanketed wastes of its home, its large visage commonly mistaken as a moving snow covered mountain. Its routine of digging and smashing through ice can easily cause devastating avalanches and glacial collapses. Furthermore, the Ukanlos appears strongly related with powerful blizzards, which are known to often help mask its presence. Additionally, the Ukanlos is one of the few monsters not belonging to the Elder Dragon classification able to avoid being captured by the Guild's Shock and Pitfall Traps.
History & Mythology
The Ukanlos has a storied cultural background amongst the people of Pokke; the name, Ukanlos, is inherited from a local deity of legend, as Snow White God in the ancient language of Pokke. Legends passed through those inhabiting the lands north of the Furahiya Mountains claim the Ukanlos capable of a variety of feats, asserting that the God's voice "cuts the seas", its roar "smacks the sun", its fingers can " crush the moon ", that " the sky and stars are pierced " with a glance from its eyes, and that its limbs shall "trample all life." For so long, this wyvern was assumed to be a representation of the harsh cold of the north rather than a flesh and blood monster. Other titles that have been bestowed upon the Ukanlos are White God, Collapse Dragon, and Master of the Absolute Zero. Additionally, it is considered as one half of a duo of Twin Walls, the other being the Akantor.
One legend in particular tells the tale of both sides of the Twin Walls, placing the Ukanlos as the originator of Pokke itself. It informs that long ago, the ancestor of the Pokke Village Chief and Treshi headed into the Furahiya Mountains to confront a giant white wyvern known as the White God, having already driven off the Black God. Wielding a massive sword crafted from the flesh and materials of a legendary Elder Dragon, this ancestor would valiantly fight the Ukanlos. Unfortunately, the victory would go to the White God, who would kill the legendary hunter and leave him unable to be honored with a burial; the legendary hunter's blade left embedded in the earth within a cavern of ice. Many years following the tale, the two mentioned descendants of the hunter would arrive to the site of the battle in search of both the sword and body belonging to their ancestor. Unable to do so, however, the two would create a settlement close to the site of battle to keep searching, centralizing it around a large boulder of Machalite Ore. Thus, the thriving village of Pokke came to be founded.
Meanwhile, the Ukanlos was driven deeper into the mountains towards the north of the continent, to the Snowy Mountains, leaving the area safe for a time and proving the ancestor's efforts were not in vain. Yet, the area was also impenetrable to the Hunter's Guild, despite that, attempts were repeatedly made to set up camp in the Snowy Mountains Peaks area. The Ukanlos would be hidden from human eyes for centuries, leaving it to fade into legend until its reappearance. The Ukanlos would not remain forgotten in the past, as north of the Furahiya Mountains, a massive avalanche would occur deep in the peaks. From the frigid wastes, the Ukanlos would emerge and wreak devastation once more, however, whether this was the same individual as the one from legend is unknown. Many villages deeper in or on the Snowy Mountains were crushed beneath its might, and many human lives were lost to its rampage. Faced by the sudden presence of such a divinity, the Hunter's Guild would call for an evacuation of Pokke, the set up of a camp on the Snowy Mountains Peaks to no changing avail, and for all G-Rank hunters in the vicinity of Pokke to slay the Ukanlos. The Pokke Village Chief would call upon the aid of a village hunter in desperation, requesting they battle the beast and save her people from death. This unknown hunter would succeed and slay the Ukanlos at the top of the mountain, restoring peace to the village and avenging the fallen hunter of lore.

Physiology
The Uragaan is a large Brute Wyvern that can be easily identified by its golden armor shell, massive lower jaw, and tar-covered underside. It tends to walk with its spine in a horizontal position, using its muscular hind legs. The front limbs are held under the body as arms. There are usually no visual differences between a male and female Uragaan.
The Uragaan feeds exclusively on ore and rocks. While it is believed to have a preference for Machalite, it will attempt to feed on most kinds of ore, seeking out energy-rich minerals especially. As a juvenile, the Uragaan is believed to be a plant eater, with the dietary transition to rocks occurring during adolescence. The process of extracting nutritional value from rocks is extremely slow and energy inefficient, and is only made possible by various bacterial colonies that live in the Uragaan's gut. The resulting chemical reactions create a dense flammable gas that builds up in the Brute Wyvern's body over time. This gas is initially stored inside of a special, sac-like organ before it can be expelled through vent-like openings on the Uragaan's underside.
The minerals the Uragaan devours influence the properties of its shell, with many scales emitting a faint glow due to their unique composition. Over time, these scales grow by having increasing amount of material layered on top of them, with the hardest scales forming once the layers fuse together into one dense mass. Large numbers of scales form the Uragaan's shell, which is said to be especially resistant in areas where it covers sensitive organs. Besides protecting the Brute Wyvern from physical impacts, the shell of the Uragaan serves as thermal insulation, protecting the body from the heat of its habitat. In rare cases, the shell of the Uragaan can layer on top of and fuse with itself, not unlike the scales—this is called the Pallium and is considered highly valuable.
The most prominent feature of the Uragaan is its massive lower jaw. This is an adaptation to its diet, as it uses the jaw to smash rocks apart like a hammer into smaller, easier to eat pieces. The jaw grows as the Brute Wyvern ages, and the Uragaan enhances its size by covering it in molten rock, creating additional layers as it hardens. The molten rock fuses directly into the bone during this process. The Uragaan finely tunes the shape and size of the jaw in order to maximize stability and weight distribution.
The Uragaan is capable of moving around by rolling its body into a wheel. The Brute Wyvern grows vertical spines on its back that help it maintain grip while rolling. Like the jaw, these spines grow continuously and can eventually become so large that they interfere with rolling. In order to prevent this, the Uragaan regularly sands them down on sharp rocks, which leads to their edges looking smooth and shiny. The Uragaan is born without these spines.
Behavior
The Uragaan exclusively inhabits volcanic regions, and is found both in the Old World and New World. It has been noted that in the New World, the Uragaan is more proficient at rolling in comparison to Old World populations.
The Uragaan employs a peculiar strategy to maximize the energy it obtains from digested rocks. The Uragaan nests on natural deposits of mineral tar, an oily substance that naturally occurs in volcanic zones. By sleeping on this tar, the Uragaan covers its underside in a layer of adhesive sludge. While feeding, the Uragaan will then sometimes stick rocks to the tar on its underside instead of eating them. These rocks are often stuck such that they are near the vents the Uragaan uses to expel its digestive gases. Over time, exposure to those gases begins chemically activating the rocks, breaking them down and preparing them for digestion. When the Uragaan chooses to finally feast on the rocks it has stuck to itself, they can be digested much faster and more efficiently than raw rocks. Thus, the Uragaan uses its underside to recycle its digestive gases into an external pre-digestive system.
The Uragaan is generally considered highly aggressive and territorial, and it is not uncommon to observe the Uragaan engaging in Turf Wars with other large monsters, such as the Lavasioth. The Uragaan has many ways to pressure an adversary, such as rolling over or crashing into its target with its heavy body in an attempt to crush them, however, this Brute Wyvern is cunning. The digestive gases of the Uragaan have strong sleep-inducing properties, and the beast seems to be instinctively aware of this. Thus, by timing its gas expulsion correctly, the Uragaan can spray an enemy with it and knock them out, leaving them open for a finishing blow. If the Uragaan is enraged, its body temperature rises, which in turn ignites the gas as it leaves the body, causing it to instead cause a flaming explosion when expelled.
In dire situations, the Uragaan can choose to sacrifice some of its stored food rocks to cause damage. The chemical reactions that break the rocks down into a more digestible form also give them explosive properties, and by swinging its long body around, the Uragaan can detach these rocks and fling them at enemies like bombs. This maneuver is also the key to the Uragaan's most devastating attack, as by strategically detaching its explosive rocks, the Brute Wyvern can cover a large ground surface with unexploded but primed rocks. Once the target is sufficiently surrounded, the Uragaan then smashes its heavy jaw into the ground. Even if this attack misses the opponent initially, the shockwave from the impact is enough to trigger the primed rocks, causing them to detonate rapidly and engulf the entire area in flames. However, the Uragaan must be especially careful when fighting the Brachydios, whose explosions can cause fatal injuries.
The Uragaan is usually solitary, although there appears to be some social hierarchy between them. It is believed that the size and shape of the jaw determines an Uragaan's position amongst its peers, and that larger jaws lead to higher success in mate selection. The mating season is the only period in which a male and female can be identified visually. A male Uragaan seeking a mate will attempt to become as sparkly as possible by eating clear and beautiful ores, whose properties are then reflected in its scales and shells. The male will also adhere gemstones and other shiny materials to its body in an attempt to impress a female.
Development
When developing the Elder's Recess in Monster Hunter: World, the dev team wanted to add a monster that would link the various strata of the area together. Kushala Daora inhabits the highest perch of the region, while Teostra reigns over the magmatic depths, and there needed to be a monster that would travel between both levels to get players acquainted with the map. An idea began to stir about a monster that would normally live in the upper stratum that would however venture down below to feed on ores. Yuya Tokuda also wanted this monster to inflict the Sleep Ailment. Uragaan ticked all of those boxes and was added as a result. Tokuda believes that Uragaan fills the same mechanical role in the Elder's Recess as the Kulu-Ya-Ku does in the Wildspire Waste. Additionally, Uragaan's mobility in a region inhabited by numerous Elder Dragons ensures that players will eventually run into such a dragon while hunting the Uragaan. Kaname Fujioka imagined that players seeing a large, powerful monster like the Uragaan get pushed off by an Elder Dragon would instantly show off their ecological dominance.

Physiology
The Uroktor is a small Leviathan and the juvenile form of the Agnaktor. Alongside its significantly smaller size, it can be distinguished from its adult form by its paler coat of scales as well as the under-developed nature of both its beak and fins. The latter is significantly smaller than the adult Agnaktor, with it only traveling down the monster's neck as opposed to its whole body. While the scales of the Uroktor are still highly resistant to fire, they remain underdeveloped and only allow it to remain submerged in lava for brief periods of time. Its hardened beak is capable of piercing through rock and enables it to dig through the ground to ambush its targets from below. It is additionally specialized to allow the Uroktor to feed on incredibly small pieces of meat from carcasses, giving the Leviathan the nickname, Volcano Cleaner. While it is incapable of shooting heat rays to the extent which the Agnaktor does, it instead spits out small globules of fire to hit its prey from a distance.
Behavior
Much like its adult counterpart, the Uroktor is specialized for living within volcanic environments. Due to its underdeveloped hide, it is predominantly terrestrial. The bite of the Uroktor is unremarkable, leading to it primarily scavenging the kills made by larger monsters, swarming around these corpses in large numbers. In rare circumstances however, the Uroktor has been known to hunt its own prey. It typically does not go after large Herbivores like the Agnaktor does, preferring instead to feed on Neopterons, such as the Bnahabra. To do so, it may either spit out flames to shoot the flying insects out from the sky, or use its beak to burrow into the ground and ambush its prey from below, thrusting upwards with its beak in the process.
The Uroktor hatches from its egg internally before its parent inevitably gives birth to it. At the time of birth, the Uroktor typically only measures around 50cm in length, with a single Agnaktor typically giving birth to anywhere between 20-30 Uroktor at a time. Due to the fact it can take a long time for a newborn Uroktor to mature and develop into an Agnaktor, only a very small number of an Uroktor brood will ever survive to reach adulthood.

The Wave Dress Wyvern Uth Duna (ウズ・トゥナ, Uzu Tuna) is a Leviathan introduced in Monster Hunter Wilds.
Summary
Large, heavyset Leviathans covered in striped patterns of red-and-black scales. They mix the ample moisture present in their habitat with bodily secretions to create a gelatinous fluid that adheres to the fine strands on their tendrils, forming a protective veil. The great mass of their body combined with their water veils allows Uth Duna to use powerful slams to create large surface waves. Despite their robust builds, they are agile predators and capable swimmers.
Main Series
Monster Hunter Wilds: Uth Duna is first encountered and repelled in the 2★ Assignment A Feast in the Deep. In High Rank, it is first hunted in the 6★ Assignment Tide Overtaking Timber. Arch-Tempered Uth Duna is first fought in the 8★ Event Quest These Roots Run Deep, unlocked at HR 50. During an investigation into the Scarlet Forest, an Uth Duna ambushes the party, forcing Olivia and the Avis Hunter to repel it. However, the wounded Uth Duna is subsequently killed by the White Wraith. In High Rank, the widespread intensified Inclemency in the Forbidden Lands causes another Uth Duna to become extremely aggressive, prompting the Avis Unit to hunt it before it causes more damage.

However, the wounded Uth Duna is subsequently killed by the White Wraith. Physiology
Unlike the typically slender and elongated build common in Leviathans, the Uth Duna sports a robust and stoutly built frame. The torso is broad and long, while the horizontally triangular tail is proportionally short and thick, with almost a third of the monster's impressive length being owed to the long cilia growing from it. These cilia also grow off tentacles on its shoulders, which extend long over the tail when not supporting its water veil.
The flat skull is V-shaped and, uniquely among Leviathans, the lipless jaw is able to protrude from the mouth in a similar manner to fish species such as the Great Trevally. The upper portion of the jaw is broad and rounded at the snout, and shorter in length than the lower portion, which ends in an elongated pointed chin. Like the Nibelsnarf and Hirabami, the Uth Duna possesses gill-like structures at the sides of its head which are covered by a developed gill-flap. The eyes are lidless and covered in a milky white membrane, and like in most monsters, shine in the dark.
Most of the body is colored a vibrant red, with a striped pattern of light blue and turquoise cycloid scales that is separated from the light gray-brown belly by a thick band of black scales. The hindlimbs and skull are black in coloration as well, with yellow stripes decorating the gill-flaps and area around the Uth Duna's eyes. To enhance water retention and strength, thin grooves run across the surface of these scales.
Pairs of long fleshy tentacles lined with long strands of wiry light-blue cilia protrude from the Uth Duna's skull, shoulders, and forehand, that support a veil of gelatinous fluid composed of water and a substance produced in its body. Those situated at the shoulder are almost longer than the body itself and support a pair of veils that run across the sides of the back to the hip. The second longest pair are the ones growing from the skull, where the veils run across the length of the neck to above the shoulders. The tentacles on the forehands are the shortest and support veils that run along the length of the arm, across the sides of the belly, and to the hindlegs.
The forehands possess claws on the fingers that are tough and curved, allowing the Uth Duna to anchor itself amidst strong water currents and climb up waterfalls.
The cilia grow from the body in different lengths and arrangements. The longest are found on the tentacles and tail, ordered into thin rows, and support the length and width of the water veil, ending at the depressions between the teardrop shapes on its rim. Shorter curly cilia grow in thick bands on the tail tip, forearms, sides of the belly, and portions of the tentacles, forming a woven mesh to which the water veil anchors.
The gelatinous fluid forming the veil is tough and heavy, protecting the monster and increasing its mass and surface area, which causes it to stir up large waves whilst moving in deeper water. When the veil is destroyed, the tentacles growing from the skull and shoulders are tucked into deep grooves that line the length of the body, and the cilia are bound into a long false tail. The tentacles on the forehands are not retracted, and the attaching cilia form a tangled mesh vaguely resembling wing membranes. Due to their length, the shoulder tentacles extend a short distance over the tail when folded.
Behavior
Reigning over the Scarlet Forest as its supreme apex predator, the Uth Duna viciously attacks most intruders in its territory on sight, using its great size and weight to physically overpower other large monsters. Its muscular forearms and robust belly serve as its primary weapons against perceived threats.
The Uth Duna appears to hunt primarily during the Downpour, the Inclemency period of the Scarlet Forest, emerging from the deep waters of the loch to patrol the forest growing beneath. It feeds on large predatory fish, such as the Gajau or Great Trevally, by ambushing them from below and eats underwater. Due to the high speeds achieved in the attack, the Leviathan will breach from the water, launching its victim into the air before catching it in its protruding jaws.

Physiology
The Vaal Hazak is a ghastly Elder Dragon endemic to the New World continent, easily identifiable by its cadaverous appearance. In comparison to most Elder Dragons, the Vaal Hazak is quite scrawny, boasting a rather slim frame that makes it appear skeletal. It is hexapedal, with four thin legs tipped with hooked claws, and two large wings with reduced membranes. Its skull is slender and narrow, with a small pair of red eyes located near the tip as well as two pairs of glowing yellow organs nearer the back of the head. It has two sets of jaws; an outer jaw lined with long, needle-like fangs and a pharyngeal jaw that protrudes outwards when the Vaal Hazak opens its mouth. The structure of its jaw is uniquely shaped for grasping prey, rather than tearing through flesh.
While many Elder Dragons can be found in a variety of habitats, the Vaal Hazak is restricted to living in the Rotten Vale. This is a consequence of the Vaal Hazak's inability to survive without effluvium, a unique type of colonial bacteria that is abundant in the Vale due to the endless supply of monster corpses. In addition to feeding on the effluvium, the Vaal Hazak utilizes it as a defense mechanism, able to disperse and expel effluvium from its body at its foes.
The Vaal Hazak has been bestowed with the title of "Putrid Elder" due to the rotting flesh draping from its body. This flesh is not its own; the Vaal Hazak deliberately coats itself in rotten flesh to attract effluvium colonies, which feast on and propagate in decaying organic matter. To aid in this, the Elder Dragon's body is lined with hooked spikes that easily catch on flesh. Underneath its cloak of meat, the Vaal Hazak's scales possess a silver-blue sheen and resemble those of fish.
The Elder Dragon uses the effluvium for sustenance and absorbs energy from the bacteria by inhaling it. As its body acts as a feeding and breeding ground for effluvium colonies, the Vaal Hazak is constantly shrouded in an effluvial mist, and can store large amounts of the miasma in its body. Using gill-like organs located around its body, the Vaal Hazak can disperse clouds of effluvium, which it can then suction back into itself. This is the Vaal Hazak's primary weapon; the effluvium slowly eats away at its foes, and by drawing it back, the Vaal Hazak can feed on its opponent's stolen energy.
In spite of its grotesque appearance, the Vaal Hazak's existence is vital for the balance of the Rotten Vale's ecosystem. When a sudden influx of corpses drops into the Vale, it results in increased effluvium concentration and, consequently, decreased oxygen levels from excessive decomposition. This then causes the effluvium colonies to consume each other, resulting in a decrease in the overall abundance of miasma. The Vaal Hazak prevents this from happening by absorbing excess effluvium. Similarly, in the event of low effluvium concentration, the Vaal Hazak's body helps the bacteria reproduce and flourish, thus maintaining the ecosystem's balance.
Behavior
The Vaal Hazak was first sighted twenty years ago by the Third Fleet. Due to the Vaal Hazak's reliance on effluvium for sustenance, so long as it has a steady supply of organic material, it does not need to leave its lair; some believe the Vaal Hazak went unseen for many years due to this.
The Vaal Hazak is considered docile by Elder Dragon standards, and is unbothered by the presence of small monsters in its territory, although this is mostly due to the fact it will eventually prey upon them. It is not uncommon to sight Raphinos and Girros that have become victims of effluvium poisoning; their bodies shrouded in an eerie miasma that robs them of their energy, eventually killing them and turning their corpses into breeding grounds for the bacteria. Interestingly, small monsters afflicted with the miasma gather around the Vaal Hazak and seem to bend to its will. One researcher theorizes the Vaal Hazak may be manipulating the monsters through the use of effluvium, although there is no concrete evidence to support such a claim.
When hunting, the Vaal Hazak utilizes its jaws to clamp down on prey. Its outer jaw is extremely flexible due to the unique structure of its joints, which allows it to grasp larger prey. It then uses its secondary jaw to draw its prey to the back of its throat, where it then releases a cloud of effluvium from its bowels.
Although it does not directly compete for food with other creatures residing in the Rotten Vale, the Odogaron will sometimes foolishly challenge the Vaal Hazak in territorial disputes. During these disputes, the Vaal Hazak does not directly fight back, instead allowing the effluvium to absorb the wyvern's energy. The encounter typically leaves the Odogaron weakened as the miasma consumes its vitality.
Music
Main article: Vaal Hazak (Music)
"Keeper of Hades" is Vaal Hazak's theme. The name references Hades, the ancient Greek God of the dead and ruler of the Underworld, which marks it the first time the name of a Monster Hunter theme directly references a real-life legend.
Development
Yuya Tokuda believed the Rotten Vale, a key locale in the New World ecosystem, deserved an Elder Dragon that could utilize the environment to its fullest extent. That aspect was more important than simply adding a Flying Wyvern for no reason. Since it uses effluvium, Vaal Hazak has a number of advantages over the player compared to other Elder Dragons, which limited how the player could approach it. The team made it so that it required the player to strategize by thinking about how to best utilize their skill set, their equipment, and prepare nulberries.
Vaal Hazak thrives on caloric intake obtained from effluvium, so under normal circumstances it would not swallow anything with the intention of digesting it, meaning that it probably could not sustain itself outside in locales that lacked effluvium. It has these gill-like organs all over its body that it uses to draw in or expel effluvium, but when Vaal Hazak coats its body in effluvium, instead of being some kind of courtship behavior or camouflage, the coat is part of its basic needs for survival. Kaname Fujioka explained that is one of the reasons why Vaal Hazak acts as a living extension of the Rotten Vale itself.

Summary
Extremely rare, silver-scaled Elder Dragons that reside high in the atmosphere, Valstrax are most known for their vaguely avian features and their bizarre wings, which have evolved into flexible claw-like shapes capable of expelling Dragon energy from their tips like jet engines. This Dragon energy serves as their main means of propulsion and defense, allowing them to fly through the sky at supersonic speed, although this requires an extreme amount of air intake, accomplished via the openings on their chest.
