Physiology
The Valstrax is a slender, aerodynamic Elder Dragon covered almost exclusively by reflective, silver scales that are jagged in appearance. The scales' reflective shine evolved to help protect the Valstrax from ultraviolet light while it flies at high altitudes. Its head is avian in nature, with it possessing a gray beak as well as blue eyes with red sclera. Along its back protrude several large spines that serve to protect it from potential threats, with their sharpness being reminiscent of blades. The Valstrax possesses a long and slender tail which ends with four sharp points; the tail is known for its eerie glow making it resemble the trailing tail of a comet. This bioluminescence is caused by the Shimmering Dragonfluid coursing through the Valstrax's body, which produces a warm red glow.
Underneath its scales, the Valstrax's skin is colored a dark gray. While the skin is normally not visible, parts of the Valstrax's shell will begin to peel off as it flies around at its top speed. In particular, those located along its wings are more likely to be shed during flight due to the high amount of metabolic activity undergone within them. Pieces of the Valstrax's shell that have fallen off rain down upon the land as a shower of miniature comets, leaving the Elder Dragon with patches of exposed skin. Upon crashing into the ground, these Burned Husks leave behind a small crater. While their crashing is unpredictable and often dangerous, these objects still remain of great interest to the Wycademy's researchers, being one of the only clues towards the dragon's true identity.
The wings of the Valstrax are a highly unusual structure that are unlike almost any other monster known. Connected to its body by highly flexible limbs, each wing consists of 3 heavily elongated fingers that collectively resemble a three-pronged trident structure, with each prong being extremely sharp and possessing a vent at its tip. The 3 wing tips are connected by a membrane, with the underlying muscles able to contract to greatly extend the length of the wing into a sharp lance-like structure. The wings themselves are extremely flexible in their movement, allowing the Valstrax to both face the vents backwards to allow it to fly, or forwards to discharge Dragon energy from its wing-tips in the form of explosive bursts or projectiles. The inside of its wings are lined with several slits, which are closed when the Valstrax folds its wings to jet forward, helping to increase the forward thrust.
The nostrils of the Valstrax are located at the back of the head and, combined with the developed exoskeleton surrounding both them and the Elder Dragon's mouth, allow it to easily breathe even when flying at top speed. Additionally, the Valstrax possesses several gill-like slits along its chest that can also take in air, allowing for air to be delivered directly to the lungs when flying at top speed. Embedded within the Valstrax's bones are a series of air sacs connected to the lungs and which penetrate into the wings. As air is taken in through the mouth, nostrils, and the gills on the chest, the air sacs inflate to draw the air towards them, before finally expelling the air through the holes in the wings. This results in a completely uni-directional method of breathing, preventing inhaled and exhaled air from mixing and allowing for more efficient oxygen absorption, which in turn allows for more efficient flight and cooling within the wings. Due to the lungs not being sac-shaped, and the fact they extend all the way into the wings, they are much more easily able to adapt to changes in air pressure.
This breathing mechanism is additionally what allows the Valstrax to fly, as by firing the air out from the vents at the tips of its wings, the Valstrax is capable of propelling itself forward. Additionally, the Valstrax is capable of converting the large quantities of air inside of its body into Dragon energy, which can also be fired out from its wing tips to aid in propelling it through the sky. Further, when agitated, additional Dragon energy is expelled from a snorkel-like organ at the back of the head that is connected to the nostrils and mouth. Using this propulsion, the Valstrax is able to fly at supersonic speeds, with its scales having specifically adapted to withstand traveling at such speeds. The Valstrax's body is even able to withstand collisions whilst at its top speed, with it frequently weaponizing this fact by ambushing its targets from far-away distances by jetting towards them. This process consumes a lot of energy, as a result the Valstrax prefers to live in areas where Dragonveins are active to help keep its metabolism high. If the Valstrax cannot sustain itself on enough Dragonveins, it will lose the ability to fly.
When enraged, the Valstrax experiences a sharp increase in Dragon energy flow within its body, causing both its head and wings to blacken as a result and making it appear as though it has grown red horns and wings. As the areas that experience air-resistance remain white, it is believed this black coloration is caused by "soot" from the Dragon energy. While the Valstrax is typically highly vulnerable to any element with the exception of the Dragon element, this influx renders these parts of its body completely immune to any element. After remaining in an agitated state for too long, the Valstrax will typically need to re-fuel by taking in more air through its chest. However, if disturbed while this is occurring, the energy being taken in can combust, severely damaging the Elder Dragon in the process.
Behavior
The Valstrax is a legendary and highly elusive Elder Dragon that is rarely sighted due to inhabiting extremely high altitude regions. The Valstrax will fly to a wide variety of different locales, with the environmental temperature seemingly not playing a factor in where it lands. While well known about from ancient tablets, it had never been sighted previously and was commonly believed to have gone extinct. It soars at high altitudes far from human dwelling and is carnivorous in nature, preferring to hunt its prey on the wing by blind-siding and dive bombing them at high speeds, before grabbing them with its talons and flying off to roost and eat its quarry. While it is advised that airships working in areas where the Valstrax may be flying should exercise caution, due to the perceived danger of a potential collision sending the airship crashing to the ground, the sheer speed the Valstrax can reach makes such incidents impossible to predict, rendering the warning meaningless. However, the altitude it typically flies at means running into one is exceptionally rare.
The Valstrax is known to go through cycles of dormancy and activity linked to the activity of the Dragonveins it uses for sustenance. As well, it is known to fly all across the world in migratory patterns in order to follow where the Dragonveins are active. Due to how critical the veins are for its sustenance, the Valstrax is highly territorial and shows no mercy to anything that encroaches upon it. The length of these cycles is what granted the Valstrax the nickname of Heavenly Comet Dragon. As the Elder Dragon flies between locales it can commonly be seen in the distance resembling a red star, which when paired with its flight patterns leading people to believe it was a comet prior to being studied, resulted in the Valstrax being bestowed the moniker of Argent Comet.
Old tomes describe the Valstrax as a comet of doom that "shall deliver all unto ruin," and it is present in ancient literature under many ominous names. As well, several parts of the Valstrax's body are believed to sow disaster: its claws and tail are claimed to have disrupted numerous peacetimes, and merely gazing upon the claws' disaster bringing form chills one's blood. Within the Elder Dragon's body grows a ruby which is seen as the source of evil heavenly omens, and it is said that whoever owns it is bestowed the power to bring about disaster.
Worship
The ancient people who once lived within the Ruined Pinnacle are believed to have worshiped comets, which in turn lead to them worshiping the Valstrax as well. This worship likely originated from the native people witnessing the Valstrax roosting atop the Ruined Pinnacle's peak and feeling a sense of awe and fear from its presence. The crimson trail that it creates as it flies was utilized by these people to predict either good or bad futures. It is believed that the phrase "a red star that flies in from the heavens," which has been passed down through communities of fringe mountain worshippers, might in actuality be referring to the Valstrax.
In order to worship the Valstrax, these people created several structures to honor the monster. Large temples were erected to serve as altars towards the dragon, however most of them are now left in a state of disarray. Other patterns showcasing comets, thought to be representations of the Valstrax, have also been discovered. It is believed that offerings and sacrifices were made at these engravings in an attempt to ward off the Elder Dragon's anger. No engravings have been found further up the mountain close to where the Valstrax nests, as beyond that point was believed to be a sacred place where only a select few priests could venture. Legends from such sites of worship also offer theories on how a Valstrax might come to exist: Some passages describe the dragon as being birthed by the Dragonveins themselves, while other tales describe it as a visitor from a place beyond the heavens.

Physiology
The Velkhana is an Elder Dragon with a similar body plan to many other members of the classification, such as the Kushala Daora. It has a slender frame covered in feather-like, silvery-blue scales resembling ice crystals in both appearance and temperature. Its head sports a beak-like snout and is adorned with a set of crown-like horns that constantly exude bitter cold, with similar spines running along the back of its neck and a set of enlarged ridges atop the shoulders.
The Velkhana's limbs are thin and bear jagged spines, with each forelimb additionally bearing an extra claw-like protrusion on the outer edge, sharp enough to slice through ice as if it were butter. Its prehensile tail is pointed and able to easily crush large, frozen rocks with a single sweep despite its thin appearance; the tail is a favored means of attacking other creatures in prolonged fights, being used for agile stabbing and swiping attacks. The Velkhana's wings are large, thick, and as majestic as the Elder Dragon they come from, with each flap wings being capable of producing freezing gusts that chill and scatter beholders.
The larger, iridescent, blue scales adorning the Velkhana's body are comprised of special igneous minerals that only form under highly specific conditions, and act as as a medium through which the Elder Dragon exerts cooling effects on its surroundings, causing dramatic temperature drops in its vicinity. The sheer cold emanating from its body is likened to blades of ice piercing its surroundings, and it is capable of freezing living beings solid, solidifying ambient moisture, and inducing snowy weather in its vicinity. The Velkhana's strength can be gauged by the blue hue of its shelling, with it being more formidable in correspondence with deeper shades of blue. This ability is most famously seen in the Velkhana's jagged icy-blue armor, which it will cover its body with by secreting Supercooled Water (過冷却水): a fluid created within its body that is constantly kept below the freezing point due to its cooling abilities. This fluid freezes on contact with its carapace and primarily accentuates its horns, shoulder ridges, wings, forelimbs, and tail—the locations that the fluid is directly secreted from. The Velkhana is even able to temporarily counteract a severed tail by creating a replacement tail out of ice.
The Velkhana is additionally able to use its Supercooled Water in the form of breath attacks, primarily as highly pressurized jets and clouds that flash-freeze on contact with solid surfaces. Using this, the Velkhana is able to instantly freeze terrain and creatures, and spontaneously create massive walls, spires, or explosions of ice. When agitated, the Velkhana's heightened body temperature causes Supercooled Water to leak from the gaps in its shelling and disperse as lingering clouds of mist that, when struck by the Velkhana's cold breath attacks, crystallize into large ice crystals that litter the ground and rain from the air. As it becomes more enraged, it secretes more Supercooled Water that freezes to its body faster than it can disperse, making its armor grow more robust. The increase in fluid and cold generation additionally makes its attacks more dangerous, causes the surrounding temperature to drop even further, and tinges the area a pale blue. Should the Velkhana's reservoir of Supercooled Water reach its maximum capacity, it will launch a risky, yet devastating attempt to eliminate its foe: dubbed Absolute Zero, it is an all-out barrage of freezing breath and exploding ice pillars that completely expends the Velkhana's reservoir of Supercooled Water, leaving it unarmored and weakened for some time afterwards. However, the parts of its body that directly secrete its fluids are sensitive to attack, with enough damage to them being able to temporarily disrupt the armor and weaken the Velkhana's abilities.
Behavior
The Velkhana is an extremely rare Elder Dragon whose existence is largely only known through scant texts and oral traditions passed down in the New World, being known as the Ice Dragon that Freezes All and the Iceborne Wyvern. When sighted, the Velkhana displays a highly confident demeanor due to the lack of any danger to it in any given ecosystem and will often ignore anything it does not deem a threat. However it is still territorial and, when provoked or disturbed, it will immediately mantle itself in its ice armor and attack viciously. Should it encounter an unfamiliar or legitimate threat, it may also attempt to track down the offender and eliminate them even after the initial encounter. The Velkhana is also known for attacking smaller monsters and leaving their frozen corpses around its territory as a display of intimidation towards any would-be intruders, and has been seen singling out and freezing intruders if they interrupt its ongoing battle against another foe. As a result of the Elder Dragon's ruthless, yet majestic temperament, those who witnessed rare sightings of the Velkhana eventually gave it the moniker of Splendiferous Silver Sovereign.
The Velkhana primarily nests in extremely cold locales far from human civilization, particularly ones plentiful with the minerals used to create and replace its blue scales, which gradually deteriorate from combat and age. Should its supply run out, the Velkhana has been occasionally seen traveling to volcanic regions, where it will molt its old mineral scales and rapidly cool magma, adhering it to the gaps in its carapace to create a new covering. A particular locale it has been sighted in is the Hoarfrost Reach, home to a formerly volcanic area that was flash-frozen mid eruption by a Velkhana, turning it into its new lair. While mostly seen in the New World, it has more recently been sighted in the Old World following the mass energy pooling caused by the Qurio outbreak in the regions around Kamura and Elgado. In the Old World, the Velkhana has been sighted in a wider variety of climates.
Music
Main article: Velkhana (Music)
"Splendiferous Silver Sovereign" is Velkhana's main theme. Like many mainline Flagship Monsters, it contains a motif of its debut game's main theme, in this case, Iceborne 's "Succession of Light". "Iceborne's End" is its Arch-Tempered theme, being a remix of the original theme with additional motifs from "Succession of Light". The theme is notable for heavily utilizing the piano to signify Iceborne, as well as incorporating a military-esque march between the melodies. Its first and second encounters in the main story of Iceborne play two themes, "Behold, the Ruler of the Frost" and "The Defense of Seliana".
When slain in the main Assignment in Iceborne and its Hub Quest in Sunbreak, "Songs of Triumph in the Winter Sky" plays as the Quest Complete theme.
"Splendiferous Silver Sovereign" was voted among the Top 10 music themes in the Hunters' Choice: Top 10 Monster Themes - Monster Hunter 20th Anniversary.
Development
For Iceborne, the team naturally wanted to make an ice dragon, so Velkhana was created to be "mage-like" in contrast to Nergigante's more brutish design. However, having a flagship monster use "spells" would be unrealistic for Monster Hunter's style and they thought that would make an unsatisfying fight. Thus, they utilised its tail for more physical moves, like stabbing.
Kaname Fujioka wanted Velkhana to resemble a "witch"; beautiful at a glance but deadly on the flipside. An idea spread around of Velkhana being able to produce ice out of thin air, reiterating the "mage" concept. However, Fujioka favoured the idea, so to make the concept more "MH-like", they came up with "Supercooled Water"; a liquid that Velkhana can use that rapidly freezes and crystalises. Thus, by scattering the supercooled water around Velkhana's surroundings, ice is created, and finally the original idea of a mage-like ice dragon could come to fruition.
Wakana Kuroiwa revealed how she made the sound effects for Velkhana, stating that she focused on certain key words like "crystal" with more violent aspects, wet nuances to the sounds and elements of a typical orthododox dragon. Since Iceborne already had Legiana, another ice monster with bird-like sound effects, the sound design team went for a more reptilian approach. Several foley methods were used; such as ice and dry ice smashed together with a hammer, wind chimes dragged along ice and a bucket and pebbles being thrown at ice.

Physiology
The Velocidrome is a sexually mature male Velociprey and acts as the alpha male of his pack. He shares a similar coloration to his brethren: sporting a blue scaled hide decorated with black stripes along its length, a cream underbelly, and a beak-like yellow upper jaw lined with needle-like teeth. He can be distinguished due to his notably larger size, more developed head crest, and the enlarged, scythe-like, orange claws on both his middle fingers and inner-most toes, able to slice through prey with little-to-no trouble. His hide is tough and heavily scarred from the many conflicts he faces as a pack leader, signifying the amount of punishment he is able to withstand. The Velocidrome additionally possesses a Screamer Sac, allowing him to summon members of his pack for aid during combat through his vocalizations.
Behavior
Much like his smaller counterparts, the Velocidrome primarily resides within lush jungles. Unlike the Velociprey however, which prefers to remain in one spot within its turf, he will continuously patrol his territory to scout for both prey and potential threats. Once it spots prey, it will leap at them with his strong legs and pin them to the ground, upon which he will then call for his pack and they will all strike together. The Velocidrome typically hunts in tandem with his pack and displays remarkable intellect when working alongside his brethren. Once a situation becomes especially dire, he is quick to retreat to a safe den using a series of tunnels around his territory, allowing him to recover in peace.
Typically, the Velocidrome's pack consists of: several juvenile Velociprey of both genders, sexually immature males, and roughly 10-100 adult females. Only the pack's alpha is allowed to breed with the pack's females, and once another male in the pack becomes sexually mature, the leading Velocidrome evicts them. In order to gain breeding rights, they must challenge the active leader of a different pack and kill him, taking over the group's leadership in the process. While most packs typically have just one leading Velocidrome, on occasion a pack may be lead by up to three, with these individuals usually being brothers. After mating with the alpha, the females are then tasked with raising the young and will work together to create nests composed of decaying materials. The decomposition of the nest's materials helps keep the eggs at a stable temperature of 35°C. As Velociprey are carnivorous from the moment they hatch, the adults of the pack regurgitate meat to feed the young.
Super Biology Information
The Super Biology Book Series collects the thoughts and theories of real scientists that were asked to speak about monsters from the Monster Hunter series. Thus, they are inherently speculative and should be seen as such.
While examining the Velocidrome, Gendrome, Iodrome and Great Jaggi all at once, Fossil Expert Yoshitsugu Kobayashi ponders the implications of their shared physical traits. He compares their size and body builds to those of Deinonychus and observes how their slender, light bodies allow for quick movements, while the sharp claws on their limbs lend themselves to shredding prey while jumping towards it. Kobayashi also asserts that based on their muscle structure, these wyverns could have a top running speed of 50 km/h. He also notes that the four wyverns all share rows of narrow, conical teeth that display the same shape throughout the entire mouth and sit with notable gaps between them. This resembles the dentition seen in piscivorous creatures such as gharials or Spinosaurus, and might imply that these wyverns eat fish.
Kobayashi notes that the crests of Velocidrome, Gendrome and Iodrome all form through physical structures growing on the head and then extend past it. He compares them to crests found on Dilophosaurus, Monolophosaurus and Guanlong, and asserts that just as is presumed in those species, the crested wyverns likely use their crests as decorations that aid in identifying and communicating to rivals and mates. Kobayashi singles out the Great Jaggi however due to it possessing a frill, which he assumes additionally serves as temperature regulation. Despite the fact that all four species work in packs, Kobayashi asserts that social behavior does not necessarily indicate a high level of intelligence. Instead, these bird wyverns strike him as creatures that flock together out of protective instinct, since individually, they are all fairly weak. He does however propose that their ability to coordinate might imply a more sophisticated social structure than initially apparent.

Physiology
The Velociprey is a social Bird Wyvern adorned in a blue-scaled hide and decorated by dark stripes over its spine and along the entire length of its body; in contrast, the underside of its body and the lower half of its legs sport tan scales. Its beak-like upper jaw is a bright-yellow and is accompanied by a small reddish-brown crest that sits at the back of the head. Its bright-orange eyes provide it a keen sense of sight, useful for spotting its prey. Surprisingly, its blue hide is able to easily blend into the dense foliage of its preferred forested habitats, granting it exceptional camouflage. The Velociprey possesses three natural weapons: long and black claws on its fingers, jaws filled with needle-like teeth, and feet sporting dark talons, with each foot also bearing a prominent sickle-shaped talon. The power of its well-developed legs allow the wyvern to run fast as well as perform great leaps.
At times, variations of the Velociprey known as White Velociprey that boast pale hides may be found within a Velociprey pack. Although closely resembling the Giaprey, these individuals were found in warmer seasons, and were found to be incapable of spitting an icy liquid.
Behavior
Despite its diminutive appearance, the Velociprey is highly adaptable in comparison to its fellow wyverns and can be found inhabiting a wide array of different environments. It is a pack hunter, with the leader of the pack being the significantly larger and stronger alpha male Velocidrome; while capable of hunting alone, they become much deadlier when in groups. A Velociprey pack displays a strong degree of coordination while hunting and is highly vocal; once prey has been sported, the wyvern will use its shrill cries to alert its companions, allowing the pack to easily ambush and surround a target. After the prey is successfully surrounded, members of the pack will take turns leaping over and around it, repeatedly biting at it with their jaws and slashing with their sickled claws until the target succumbs to the confusing onslaught; even master Hunters are wary to avoid getting surrounded by a pack of Velociprey. Once the kill has been made, the pack-members directly responsible will proceed to feast on the carcass, as rather than attempt to bully their brethren away, the remaining Velociprey and even the pack's leader will act as watchful guardians whilst their kin feeds. However, the Velociprey is also predated upon by larger monsters, such as the Rathian, who often feeds the wyvern to her young, or uses it as an injured victim for the clutch's hunting training.
A Velociprey pack is made up of plenty of juveniles, sexually immature males, and 10-100 females, with each pack being led by 1-3 Velocidrome; in instances where a pack has multiple leaders, they are typically all brothers. Only these Velocidrome are allowed to breed with the females, with male Velociprey being driven out of the pack upon reaching sexual maturity—the only way these males may breed is by killing the current leading male and taking over his pack. After mating, the female Velociprey will build underground nests lined with hay, whose decay will help incubate the eggs at a consistent 35°C, the ideal temperature for development. Females are primarily in charge of caring for the hatched young, who are born carnivorous with their teeth already fully developed. In order to feed their young, adult Velociprey will regurgitate easily digestible chunks of eaten prey for them to consume, allow them to develop safely.
As a result of the Velociprey's behavior and large packs, the wyvern often comes into conflict with humans, be it by approaching worryingly close to villages, or more commonly through terrorizing farmers and inflicting serious damage upon their livestock by feeding on them. As a result of this, it is often the first monster a Hunter will have to overcome. Despite the issues it can cause, the Velociprey has a surprisingly deep relationship with humanity, due to the fact almost all parts of its body can be considered as a useful material: its scales make for incredibly sturdy armor that still manages to be light, its supple hide is in high demand for usage in clothing as well as a connecting material in the construction of metal armor, and its fangs can be processed to be used in both bullet casings and in decorational ornaments. Due to this, its presence is still considered to be indispensable to humanity.

Physiology
The Vespoid is a small Neopteron, although it still grows to an enormous size compared to most common insects, presumably a result of an evolutionary mutation. It possesses an incredibly slender frame armored with a dark, purplish carapace striped with pale-yellow, as well as six elongated legs and two pairs of wings on its back; a single graze from one of these wings is more than enough to cut through skin. Its body is exceptionally delicate and very easily destroyed, as a result, it is typically best for Hunters to utilize poisons to kill the Neopteron if its parts are desired to be harvested. At the end of its abdomen is a long stinger which is used to deliver a potent paralyzing venom stored inside.
Behavior
Being highly adaptable in nature, it has been discovered living in almost every kind of biome in the known world. The Vespoid is predatory in nature and will search for prey from the air, whereupon finding a suitable target—normally an insect or other small animal—it will snatch them in its legs and drag them back to its nest. If faced with a larger target, it will repeatedly stab them using its stinger, injecting its venom into its victim's body and immobilizing them for long enough to allow it to tear into their flesh with its sharp mandibles, eating them alive. It demonstrates a strong affinity towards bright lights, with it being drawn towards sources of it, including even open fires. However, if exposed to a sudden bright flash of flight, it is known to be knocked out of the sky and onto its back.
The Vespoid establishes its territory as a swarm, with these groupings being known to be highly aggressive towards intruders. Upon spotting a large monster in its territory, the swarm will gather in wait before assaulting its target in a violent flurry with the intention of driving them away. It has been demonstrated that the Vespoid fears the presence of large monsters in its turf to a noticeable degree more than it does the presence of humans. This Neopteron frequently experiences massive explosions in population within lush jungles and other such areas, with these outbreaks typically being credited to a Vespoid Queen at the center laying a large collection of eggs. While the species was previously believed to simply form swarms, the official discovery of the Queen led researchers to understand that it is a highly social animal, with individual Vespoid taking on specialized roles such as foragers or soldiers, the the Vespoid Queen sitting at the top of the social hierarchy. The Queen is typically rarely seen, though it is not uncommon during the warm seasons to spot a larger Vespoid carrying around its Queen's egg sacs on her behalf. While this is normally a task the Queen would carry out herself, this behavior is believed to have evolved to ensure her safety in areas dominated by large numbers of external threats, such as wyverns or hunters.

Physiology
The Vespoid Queen appears similar to an enlarged Vespoid upon initial inspection, however her abdomen is notably engorged in comparison to standard individuals. The body's greatly increased size stems from her constant consumption of nutritious food, with the swollen abdomen being a result of her primary function lying in the laying of eggs, with numerous eggs being found inside of it on rare occasions. The Vespoid Queen's wings are brilliantly iridescent in appearance, while her thorax sports a crown-like, warped outer shell consisting of five upturned golden spikes and a bright-red center. The thorax possesses a large specialized ovipositor that secondarily functions as a stinger to deliver her paralyzing venom. In addition to this, the Vespoid Queen is able to weaken her prey by spewing a corrosive gas at them, an ability not seen in the standard Vespoid that indicates her high hunting prowess and heightened aggressiveness.
On certain occasions, the Vespoid Queen undergoes a metamorphosis and takes another form, losing her cerci and thorax spikes, with the rest of her thorax turning black. Other transformations include the size of her wings decreasing dramatically—as if she had just emerged from her cocoon—her head growing a pair of antennae, and her abdomen appearing as a white sac-like pouch. As this form has never been encountered by Hunters, she is not believed to be aggressive when in this state. While the exact nature of this transformation remains unclear, it is believed to occur during her breeding season, if one exists. The shortened wings are thought to be a result of her losing them during the metamorphosis before growing a new pair shortly afterwards.
Behavior
Unlike the wide-ranging standard Vespoid, the Vespoid Queen has only ever been sighted inside of lush jungles. While previously believed to only form simple swarms, recent discoveries have unearthed that the Vespoid is a eusocial creature; the smaller Vespoids each fill out specialized roles, such as gathering food or acting as Soldiers, while the Queen reigns at the top. She builds her nest inside the trunk of a giant and normally remains secluded inside of it, laying eggs throughout the year and forming a gigantic colony that may consist of hundreds—or even thousands—of individual Vespoids. Furthermore, recent sightings of multiple Vespoid Queens suggests that, when a colony gets too large it will begin to swarm, dividing its nest in the process. Soldiers travel long distance to gather food, with them building small temporary colonies of around 10-30 individuals in tree hollows or caves as they do so; these nests typically only last for around 1-3 months. Once they have collected the requested quota of food, they will bring it back to the large colony to provide for their Queen.
The Vespoid Queen will ordinarily never leave this colony, although if a large number of her Soldiers are killed, she may go on solo hunts accompanied by only a few personal guards. She displays remarkable intelligence and is capable of having her Vespoid attack in a co-ordinated fashion. To achieve this, she emits her corrosive gas and changes both the sound of her wing beats as well as the pattern of her flight, in turn alerting and commanding multiple Vespoids to attack all at once. By doing this, she ensures her hive is attacking already weakened prey.
When it comes time to create a new nest, the Vespoid Queen will typically create an egg sac and venture outwards alongside some of her trusted guards. However, during the breeding season, large individual Vespoids can occasionally be seen carrying out this task instead. It is believed that this occurs to ensure the Queen's safety in areas that are teeming with potential threats, such as large wyverns or hunters.

Physiology
The Violet Mizutsune is a rare, recently discovered variation of the Mizutsune characterized by its whitish, purple-tinged scales. Along with its fins, the fur on the dorsal half of its body is a vibrant lilac color, whereas the fur on its underbelly is a pale purple, and the fur on its tail is a dark indigo. Similarly to the nominate species, the Violet Mizutsune maneuvers by covering its body with slippery Synovial Fluid and sliding across terrain, while its sharp claws provide grip and maneuverability. However, instead of the soap-like Synovial Fluid secreted by the nominate species, the Violet Mizutsune secretes an oily fluid that ignites with the slightest friction. The White Synovial Fluid of the Violet Mizutsune is several hundred times more concentrated than that of the normal Mizutsune, rendering it useful for medicinal purposes, yet also potentially toxic if used improperly.
When ignited, the fluid creates a brilliant whitish-blue flame that can often be seen burning on the Violet Mizutune's hide and fins, augmenting its physical strikes with flames. It is additionally able to spread the substance around to engulf its surroundings in fire, spray it from its mouth, and create flaming blue bubbles that independently seek out targets before exploding. The Violet Mizutsune is largely unharmed by its flames due to its heat-resistant scales, which possess fine grooves for the Synovial Fluid to run through whilst sliding, further enhancing its mobility. However, the Violet Mizutsune has nonetheless been observed suffering harm if caught in its larger explosions.
Behavior
Similarly to the regular Mizutsune, this Rare Species is quite placid and spends a large amount of time sleeping or relaxing. However, when hunting prey or repelling enemies, it fights with violent ferocity by sliding around to spread its Synovial Fluid over a wide area whilst utilizing barrages of explosive bubbles. When further enraged, it will ignite the fluid in its fur, before fighting more aggressively and engulfing its surroundings in an unrelenting sea of white flame. Despite being a Leviathan, the Violet Mizutsune is entirely terrestrial, being only classified as such due to its relation to the base Mizutsune.

Physiology
The Viper Tobi-Kadachi is a Subspecies of the Tobi-Kadachi that has discarded its electrical capabilities in favor of two types of deadly venom due to drastic changes in its habitat and living conditions. The scales along its back and limbs sport a spotted brown and orange pattern, giving greater contrast to the dark green iridescence given off by the underbelly and allowing the Viper Tobi-Kadachi to camouflage into the dark caves in which it resides. Considering the cold environments it lives in, it is worth noting it carries very little fur compared to many of its cohabitants. Any fur it retains from the standard species is largely vestigial, as it no longer lives amongst foliage with which to rub its fur against to generate static electricity. The Viper Tobi-Kadachi's body additionally holds on to very little subcutaneous fat, thus making it quite susceptible to cold temperatures, and it retains the webbed membrane between its limbs from the standard species. However, without treetops from which to glide down, it has developed better gliding control with its membranes as well as stronger legs so as to gain adequate gliding elevation purely from leaping into the air.
The spines along its forehead and tail mirror the spotted pattern of its scales, although they also carry a striking red and purple glow at their ends, as if to present a warning of the deadly venom that is sure to follow should one come into contact with them. These spines secrete one of the Viper Tobi-Kadachi’s two venom types from its Deadly Poison Sac, a potent hemotoxin that whittles away at its victim’s vitality. This is frequently followed up by its sharp fangs, which are tipped with its second venom from its Ultraplegia Sac, a paralytic neurotoxin that stops foes in their tracks. The difficulty that comes with facing off against two venoms at once means that Hunters frequently prepare specialty equipment to face off against the Viper Tobi-Kadachi. A creature possessing multiple venom types, like the Viper Tobi-Kadachi, is noted by researchers to be a very rare occurrence in nature. There is ongoing research regarding the relationship between the Viper Tobi-Kadachi’s hemotoxin and the poisonlanterns native to its habitat, although any understanding towards the origins of either of its venoms remains in conjecture for the time being.
Behavior
Despite living in frigid climates, the Viper Tobi-Kadachi has not developed adaptations to improve its cold resistance; it has instead adjusted its habitat to reside primarily in caves warmed by geothermal vents. It has been known to enjoy sunbathing, although this is limited to light that leaks into the caves, which often puts it in contention with the Fulgur Anjanath which frequents the same areas. However, when it comes to hunting, venturing out is a necessity. The Viper Tobi-Kadachi likes to minimize this time by tearing out the flesh of incapacitated prey from the snowfields and dragging them back into its nest in the caves where it will have its meal.
While in combat, the Viper Tobi-Kadachi retains much of the standard species’ mobility, despite losing the vantage points with which to jump off of in its new habitat. Its more developed legs grant it improved jump height, such that it is able to gain enough elevation to glide with its membrane in virtually any environment without needing to rely on the surrounding terrain. Its ability to weaken and paralyze its targets with its venoms further makes its mobility significantly deadlier. However, this mobility does come with drawbacks, as the Viper Tobi-Kadachi is lacking in stamina. Focused assaults on its weak points will quickly tire it out, and blows on points from where it delivers venom has the added benefit of weakening said venom as well.
The Viper Tobi-Kadachi’s two venoms are actually seldom used in tandem, as they typically serve different functions. From its Deadly Poison Sac, hemotoxins are secreted onto spines that line the head and tail; spikes on the tail can be dislodged and fired as a projectile with a quick swipe. This venom’s primary use is against opponents in a fight, as it can affect the taste of the meat if used on prey. Mostly benign, a single prick is enough to hinder a target’s vitality, however repeated exposures can be fatal if not quickly treated. Meanwhile, its Ultraplegia Sac secretes neurotoxins onto its fangs, which it prefers to use to paralyze prey—such as the Popo —for easier hunting. Only during heated exchanges with a powerful opponent does the Viper Tobi-Kadachi employ both venoms, making it an unassuming deadly threat for the inexperienced and unprepared.

Physiology
The Volvidon is a medium-sized monster with the same body plan as its close relatives, the Arzuros and Lagombi, however, it displays significant physiological differences beyond that. Its face is flat and long, and the hands only have four fingers—as opposed to five on both of its relatives—with the second finger and claw being abnormally large, often compared to a trowel. The Volvidon is covered in a segmented red shell that is thick and sturdy in spite of its elastic properties, granting the beast high defense with virtually no downsides to its mobility. The shell is also supremely heat-resistant, able to withstand magma for a short while. The resilience of this material is noted by blacksmiths to be extremely difficult to work with. By curling its body, the segments on the Volvidon's shell overlap such that they turn the moster's body into an armored ball. The elasticity of the shell is capable of redistributing force, and by strategically contracting and expanding the muscles under it, the Volvidon can bounce while rolled up, gathering momentum and moving at high speeds.
Another trait that makes the Volvidon stand out from its close relatives is its tongue, which is prehensile and can extend to a total length of nearly 20 meters. While this adaptation seems to have emerged for feeding purposes, it can also serve as a weapon: during combat, the Volvidon may use its long tongue as a whip, striking foes from afar with wide-ranging attacks.
Many of the insects the Volvidon devours, such as the Bnahabra, contain various paralytic poisons. When feeding, these poisons are stored in its Paralysis Sac that is connected to its saliva glands. By mixing these compounds in its mouth, the Volvidon can spit globules of concentrated paralytic venom that gets absorbed through the skin of whatever gets splashed by it. Furthermore, when digesting the shells of insects, the monster's gut produces various foul gases that get stored in a layer under its skin. When necessary, the Volvidon can expel these gases from the gaps between its shell segments, dowsing any unlucky enemy in a pungent cloud of odor.
Behavior
The Volvidon is omnivorous, although has a strong preference for insects. It can infiltrate the nests of Altaroth and pull them out of their tunnels, or it can swipe Bnahabra straight out of the air using its long tongue.
Super Biology Information
The Super Biology Book Series collects the thoughts and theories of real scientists that were asked to speak about monsters from the Monster Hunter series. Thus, they are inherently speculative and should be seen as such.
Zoological Author Yuumin Mori notes the Volvidon’s similarities to various animals, such as pangolins, armadillos and anteaters. The latter serves as a significant reference point for the diet of the Volvidon, which is said to be an insectivore. Insects are high in calories, but small and difficult to devour in large quantities. As such, they are usually the staple food of small animals. The giant anteater can only maintain its size by eating 30 000 ants a day, which it achieves by roaming across vast territories. In order for the much larger Volvidon to sustain itself on insects, it would need to have additional strategies to maximize its caloric intake. Mori proposes that the Volvidon might specifically target collector insects such as Altaroth, which themselves gather highly nutritious substances like nectar and bring it to their nests. By raiding their nests shortly after a gathering troupe has returned, a Volvidon could feasibly take in enough calories to survive, both from the insects themselves and from their accumulated storage of nutritious fluids.
Mori next ponders the Volvidon’s ability to spit paralyzing mucus. He explains that with venom, which has to be injected into the bloodstream to take effect, it is fairly intuitive that the venom user would not suffer the effects of the toxin themselves, as it would be delivered by an organ that is sealed off from the blood. But the Volvidon’s paralytic toxin takes effect merely by making contact with the target - this implies that the beast must have some specialized immunity or safeguard against its own toxin, as it would otherwise paralyze it as well. Mori theorizes that the Volvidon’s mucus likely only takes effect under specific pH conditions: When in contact with a surface of neutral acidity (such as the skin of an enemy), the toxin penetrates and paralyzes. But the Volvidon’s mouth might be covered in an acidic mucus membrane that prevents the toxin from taking effect on its master.
When discussing the Volvidon’s shell, Mori stresses that in order to protect the creature from the heat of its volcanic habitats, it must be made of material that does not distort or change at high temperatures and boast high structural integrity. Mori struggles to imagine this being the case for living tissue, and instead proposes that the shell forms through the Volvidon secreting special fluids from its skin, which harden and crystallize into the armor shell. Subsequently, Mori imagines that the Volvidon’s shell would chemically be comparable to ore and crystals. Additionally, Mori suggests that perhaps the Volvidon grows this shell by supplementing its diet with ores and minerals from volcanoes, which are turned into the secreted liquid and allowed to re-crystallize on the skin. From that, Mori wonders if the noxious gases expelled by the Volvidon may be a byproduct of the chemical process that results in the shell.

Physiology
The Wind Serpent Ibushi is the male of a sexually dimorphic species of Elder Dragon, with the Thunder Serpent Narwa being the female. He has a massive serpentine body covered in azure hide that is as flexible as rubber while being rigid enough to repel blades, and is able to defend the Elder Dragon from any and all attacks; his carapace boasts similar qualities, although it is oddly lightweight. He has four fin-shaped limbs, with a pair of larger clawed forelimbs and smaller paddle-like hindlimbs, as well as a long tail tipped with a bell-like structure; the fins and tail are believed to help him control his positioning during flight. The Wind Serpent Ibushi's gray claws and underside are adorned by numerous slits resembling gills, rows of dorsal spines, and a large crest of bony spines protruding from his head. These beautiful rock-hard spines serve as a natural deterrent for airborne foes, discouraging their approach. His face is adorned with blank, yellow eyes and has a unique pharangyeal jaw structure, with a large folding outer jaw enveloping a set of four toothed inner mandibles. The crest converges into a large, lustrous, azure horn, so perfectly honed in the winds that simply polishing it can turn it into an excellent blade. When enraged, the Ibushi's eyes turn orange and the gills on his body begin glowing red.
Several glowing, bluish-indigo Windsacs can be found on the Elder Dragon's arms, back, chest, and tail; these sacs create and store a special, lighter-than-air gas that the Elder Dragon expels from his gills to freely float and manipulate the wind around him, with the Ibushi often being seen adopting an unusual upside-down flying orientation. Expulsion and modulation of this gas allows the Ibushi to both surround himself in gales to propel himself, as well as use various wind-based attacks infused with Dragon elemental energy, such as violent air currents, cannon-like blasts of compressed air, or updrafts capable of lifting heavy debris. The Wind Serpent Ibushi's nature of flight and wind manipulation additionally causes violent wind turbulence and draconic storms around him that can reshape the landscape and, combined with his deafening roar, terrify nearby monsters into fleeing their habitats. Even his physicality is notable, as alongside being able to swiftly destroy the reinforced gate of the Red Stronghold with a single swing of his tail, strikes from his pointed claws leave the land disfigured, with these claws being claimed to rend the heavens and be powerful enough to destroy a country. However, the Windsacs are also delicate, with sufficient damage being able to forcibly disperse the gas and cause the Ibushi to falter.
Many myths tell of the legendary dorsal horns of the Ibushi, which are said to contain the power to wield the sky itself. Simultaneously, other tales tell of a jewel that grows within the Elder Dragon's body and which grants the power to bend storms to one's will.
Behavior
The Wind Serpent Ibushi's behavior beyond the mating cycle is unknown, although during said cycle, he is single-minded in his solitary search for a Thunder Serpent Narwa to mate with, stopping only to remove obstacles or enemies that get in his way. Alongside the accompanying storms he creates, it is this pursuit that is believed to be the source of the phenomenon known as the Rampage, where hundreds of monsters stampede in a frenzy, now interpreted as them fleeing the wrath of the Ibushi. Powerful monsters who manage to survive the storms may be scarred and transformed, becoming empowered Apexes who carve a path of destruction out of the rage and terror instilled in them by the Ibushi's storms.
While the Wind Serpent Ibushi is presumed to be predatory, owing to his jaw structure appearing adapted to trap and immobilize prey, it is unknown what his diet consists of.
Mating
Little is known about the Ibushi's developmental process and usual habits beyond his mating cycle, which coincides with the Rampage. When it comes time to find a mate, the Wind Serpent Ibushi will begin patrolling a vast area in search of the Thunder Serpent Narwa. While the two serpents use a currently unknown method to locate each other, certain Wyverians —such as Hinoa and Minoto —are able to "Resonate" with this method and translate the Serpents' thoughts into spoken language.
When the two Elder Dragons meet, they perform an airborne courtship dance that culminates in the fertilization of the eggs and a terrific storm engulfing the area. Following this, Narwa descends into the depths of their nest and awaits to lay her clutch, while the Ibushi hovers in the skies above, ready to protect his mate with his life. However, it has been observed that this process can also occur differently. If the nest is breached and a threat to the next generation presents itself during the courtship phase, the Narwa will devour the Ibushi's "lifeforce", a process that is fatal to the Wind Serpent. This empowers the Narwa and transforms her into Narwa the Allmother, granting her the Ibushi's command over wind as well as accelerating the growth of her eggs.
Music
Main article: Wind Serpent Ibushi (Music)
Breath of Ire is Wind Serpent Ibushi's theme. Paired with Thunder Serpent Narwa, Breath of Ire shares melodies with Lady of Lightning, and additionally like her theme contains a motif of the Rampage. The theme is sung by solo vocalist Hinoa, performed by Izumi Kato, who resonates with the monster. Breath of Ire is also one of the very few Monster Hunter themes with official lyrics.
Both Ibushi and Narwa share a theme for their appearance in Monster Hunter Stories 3, acting as a mix of both Lady of Lightning and Breath of Ire without vocals, not too similar to The Allmother.
Development
Ibushi was designed around idea of a flying seahorse whose unrestricted aerial movement would change what body parts the player interacted with depending on Ibushi's current orientation. In line with the Japanese mythology theming of Monster Hunter Rise, Ibushi was designed as one half of a pair of final bosses based on Fūjin and Raijin, the Shinto gods of wind and thunder. While the team had trouble implementing Ibushi's unique movement in a way that felt natural like most normal monsters, they considered the end result a balance between embodying its otherworldly aura while still allowing for dynamic action sequences. To match with its role in the story and relationship with Hinoa, Ibushi's introduction poem was written to be specifically narrated by Hinoa herself.
The 14 undulating, individually deflatable Windsacs on Ibushi's body were noted as the key features of its model, while the texture of its hide - while often overshadowed by the monster's glowing parts and Windsacs - was inspired by marine life such as whales and sea turtles. The team cited difficulty in visually depicting Ibushi's combination of wind and Dragon energy, though its usage of thrown rocks was specifically meant to represent the cataclysmic power of an Elder Dragon to overturn the surrounding environment. Ibushi's roar was created by combining sounds from whales, cows, and bell chimes, then putting them through synthesizers, with the intention being to create a sound that felt eerie and not quite alive.

Physiology
The Wulg is a small and gracile Fanged Wyvern covered entirely in a thick coating of fur. The front half of its body is colored black, transitioning to a bright white along its rear half, legs, and tail. This fur is especially good at retaining heat within the frigid environments it inhabits. While the Wulg's paws do possess several small claws, each of its front paws additionally sport a large cyan "hidden claw" that is typically kept retracted next to its ankles. However, when hunting prey, these blue toned claws are unsheathed, allowing the Wulg to effortlessly cut into its prey, even if they are covered in thick layers of fur.
Behavior
The Wulg primarily inhabits frigid climates and lives alongside its kind in packs typically consisting of around 3-5 individuals. These packs are known to display some form of hierarchy amongst members, with individuals taking on different roles within the pack dynamic, suggesting a high degree of sociability within the species. During the daytime, the Wulg spends most of its time hiding and resting inside of caverns, only ever emerging under the cover of night. Scout groups are frequently sent out of these caves to both maintain the pack's territory from rival predators as well as to search for potential prey.
Once prey is spotted, the Wulg displays a highly sophisticated strategy for bringing it down. One member of the pack hangs back, maintaining a distance from the target as it slowly stalks it and guides the prey towards a suitable hunting location to begin the ambush. The remaining members of the pack hide within the deep snow at the designated ambush spot, waiting for the tracker and the prey to arrive. Once prey has been successfully guided, the remaining Wulg will leap out of the snow to attack. Once an attack has been initiated, one Wulg will typically leap onto the prey and wrapping its body around them, immobilizing them in the process and allowing the remaining members of the pack to more easily pounce. It has been shown that the Wulg preferentially targets monsters who appear exhausted or are otherwise impaired, although its cunning and opportunistic hunting style still allows it to attack and prey upon superior opponents when the opportunity presents itself. Despite this impressive coordination, research has demonstrated that the tracker can be distracted away from its target prey if Raw Meat is placed in its vicinity.

The Dark Beacon Dragon Xeno'jiiva (ゼノ・ジーヴァ, Zeno Jīva) is an Elder Dragon introduced in Monster Hunter: World.
Summary
Enigmatic Elder Dragons previously unknown to the Guild, identifiable by their otherworldly translucent blue body and six orange eye-like sensory organs. Xeno'jiiva lure in dying monsters as they incubate in crystalline cocoons, feeding on their bioenergy and, after hatching, using it to unleash devastating energy attacks. However, being a newborn, they seem unable to properly control this power. The adult form of this species is known as the Safi'jiiva.

The Tracker discovers the Confluence of Fates, and together with The Admiral, the Hunter finds Xeno'jiiva in its coccoon, afterwards waking up to eliminate the hunter's team. At first, the monster and its items are classified as unknown, but are revealed to be from Xeno'jiiva after the main story ends. The Useful Information section in the Hunter's Notes for Xeno'jiiva are still unknown, however.

Physiology
With the accumulated bioenergy of countless Elder Dragons, the Xeno'jiiva's body glimmers an azure-blue in contrast with the fiery, bioluminescent organ in its chest, leading to people granting it the title of Emperor of Elders. It shares the same conventional body plan as most other Elder Dragons, sporting a pair of large wings and four limbs, although it holds itself in a more hunched position similarly to the Nergigante. Atop its head sprouts two backwards-facing horns that are jet-black in color, along with six bright-orange sensory organs that are lined above the eye towards the horns; the cheeks are accompanied by large, flowing membranes. After emerging from its cocoon, the Xeno'jiiva's body is delicate, with its internals being visible through its translucent body. Its wings are slightly bent and curled up due to the prolonged time spent in its pupa state, and they take time to fully spread and smooth out. After a short while, energy begins transferring to the wings, granting the Elder Dragon the ability to fly. The Xeno'jiiva has five-fingered hands and four-toed hind legs that are paired with a clawed protrusion from the wrists and heels. The sturdy musculature of Xeno'jiiva's hind legs fully supports its large frame when rearing up.
Contrary to its luminescent appearance, the Xeno'jiiva's skin is actually white, with the glowing bioenergy painting the Elder Dragon's body a pale, blue hue. As it matures, the Xeno'jiiva loses the translucency of its skin. The tips of the Xeno'jiiva's plating remain wrinkled and diaphanous until energy is flowed into them, after which they fully expand and flutter like blue flames. Energy tends to accumulate in its head, forelimbs, and tail, resulting in brighter colors in comparison to its other gray-ish body parts, such as the base of the wings, tail, and hindlegs.
The crimson organ located within the Xeno'jiiva's chest is the central point of its venous system and manages the flow of energy throughout its body. A mature Xeno'jiiva does not "feed" on prey for nourishment in the traditional sense, and instead gains energy directly from the stock generated in this centrally located organ. Just as it can distribute energy, this organ can stop the flow of energy and store it. Once a certain threshold of energy has been reached, its entire body seems to explode with light as if literally overflowing with energy, entering what is called its Critical State. Upon entering the Critical State, a flaring light bursts from the Xeno'jiiva's body, illuminating the entirety of its trunk from its chest organ—while in this state, the Xeno'jiiva's physical capabilities increase dramatically. Further, its attacks can create small craters in the ground due to its physicality operating at peak performance; should the Xeno'jiva's bioenergy fuse with the Everstream energy leaking from the ground, the craters may erupt with devastating explosions. In the Confluence of Fates, the Everstream itself responds to the Xeno'jiiva's Critical State and causes large-scale eruptions of energy.
The Xeno'jiiva can gather energy in different regions of its body with varying effects, including its head. As it pools energy in its head, the Xeno'jiiva is able to spew concentrated energy in the form of a searing laser, although the purpose of this beam is not solely to destroy. The Xeno'jiiva can only contain a limited amount of energy before it loses control, as such, it periodically releases energy via these beams to maintain its internal energy levels. However, this exhausts the Elder Dragon and leaves it vulnerable for a while. As it is a newborn, the Xeno'jiiva ends its Critical State prematurely by firing this beam. With this relatively immature mind, the Xeno'jiiva is rather clumsy and may fire beams that melt the ground beneath itself, causing the ground below to cave under its weight and the Elder Dragon to sink.
Behavior
The Xeno'jiiva is instinctively destructive towards other beings, firing the energy stored within itself as a weapon and displaying violent behavior as it courses throughout its body. It weaponizes this energy by allocating it to specific regions of its body, where it is then compressed and subsequently discharged all at once. The Xeno'jiiva may even be able to establish a loop of perpetual energy generation for itself if enough time passes, however, as the Xeno'jiiva is a newborn, it is not yet able to fully control the vast stores of energy at its disposal.
Elder Crossing
In the Rotten Vale, the bodies of Elder Dragons decompose and release their bioenergy to the Everstream where it then eventually crystallizes, creating the Confluence of Fates as a result. Inside, the Xeno'jiiva entered its pupal stage and began absorbing life energy, causing a shift so great that the environmental ecology of the New World continent was altered. Upon the Zorah Magdaros' death, there was an unprecedented release of energy that awoke the Xeno'jiiva from its cocoon. Feeding on the energy of deceased Elder Dragons for decades, the accumulated energy finally reached its threshold and initiated the Xeno'jiiva's emergence from its crystal cocoon, which afterwards attempted to eliminate all living beings around it.
The Xeno'jiiva is hypothesized to primarily feed on the energy of other monsters, which it accomplishes by drawing powerful monsters to its vicinity with pheromones. By making its home in the New World, a place that naturally draws Elder Dragons at the end of their life cycle, the Xeno'jiiva's presence may have augmented the Elder Crossing, which may explain the exponential increase of the phenomenon's activity.
Music
Main article: Xeno'jiiva (Music)
"Guiding Lamp to the Otherworld" and "How Life Springs Anew" are Xeno'jiiva's 1st phase and 2nd phase themes respectively. As the final story boss for World, both themes contain a motif from " Stars at Our Backs ", the debut game's main theme. "Guiding Lamp to the Otherworld" is one of the only monster themes from World that include vocals.
Xeno'jiiva's motifs are referenced in both of Safi'jiiva's themes, as Safi'jiiva is the mature version of the monster.
When slain in World, "Quest Complete! (Main Theme version)" plays as the Quest Complete theme.
Development
Yuya Tokuda stated that the only reason Xeno'jiiva could be slain was because it was only a newborn. The concept of Xeno'jiiva as the "Emperor of the Elder Dragons" is something the team wanted to carry over into gameplay by making it fearsome in how it gathers energy to unleash its laser beam-like breath. Tokuda had always wanted to make a laser attack where "a bead is drawn on the ground and everything stops for a second before the beam pierces the location", and this type of attack was made possible thanks to Xeno'jiiva.
Kaname Fujioka wanted there to be an element of gameplay involving a monster that could control energy flowing throughout its body. The glowing organ in Xeno'jiiva's chest can control energy flow by either dedicating it to strengthening the monster, or stock the energy up for an explosion, and this strengthening and stocking is a cycle that it repeats. It can use energy recklessly like this because of internal biological heating constructs, and with this infinite source of energy, it never needs to feed. If Xeno'jiiva matures and escaped to the New World, it would be a "real troublemaker". While it seems like its skin is glowing, the inside out is actually radiating light, similar to an X-ray scan of a body.

Physiology
The Xu Wu is a medium sized Cephalopod that shares the general body shape of its class, with six thin and muscular tentacles used for locomotion, and two smaller ones on the front of its body. The larger tentacles are flexible enough to stretch to several times their original length. Its head is large, rocky, and mushroom-shaped, with several teeth on the top, and a small, saggy mantle hanging off the back. Beneath its mantle is a "false face" resembling a set of teeth with gray fibers mimicking a beard, the former of which will glow blue and start emitting vapor when the Xu Wu grows enraged. Its body and tentacles are fibrous in texture, with numerous undulating tendrils adorning its backside, while its mucus-covered hide is highly flexible, yet tough enough to repel attacks from Guardians. Its body underneath the tentacles is bright-blue and lined with many rows of sharp, golden teeth—it is able to unfold to reveal a large mouth directly beneath the head, capable of crushing nearly any prey. The Xu Wu does not have eyes, although its other senses are highly developed to compensate.
The Xu Wu's body secretes a unique golden mucus that hardens on contact with air, forming a tough glistening Corneum over parts of its body, giving its tentacle tips a shiny appearance, and dotting its head with golden protrusions; purer secretions will produce an appropriately harder Corneum. The Xu Wu's tentacle tips secrete large amounts of this mucus, allowing it to create a variety of crystalline structures it uses as weapons to hunt its prey. It is able to create sharp spear heads, wide blades for slashing attacks, and brush-like crystal clusters it both swings for crushing attacks as well as breaks off to launch as knife-like shrapnel. In addition, it is capable of forming curved hooks that can be used to immobilize prey, or to reposition by dragging itself across terrain. Despite their apparent hardness, the Xu Wu appears to capable of dissolving its crystalline weapons at will.
The Xu Wu's cerebrospinal fluid contains great amounts of energy, causing it to glow.
Behavior
Known by some as the Piercing Assassin for its ability to create bladed weaponry with its mucus, the Xu Wu is a predatory Cephalopod that primarily hunts through ambush tactics, leveraging its agility and ability to squeeze through small crevices to to catch prey off guard and kill them without a sound. It is adapted to prey on the Guardians of the Ruins of Wyveria, and is attracted to Guardians, their cocoons, or anything which resembles them, although it will also attempt to prey on anything else that enters its turf, including humans. Despite its preference for stealth, it can also be observed in direct conflict with Guardians, outmaneuvering them in melee and bringing them down with its tentacles before attempting to crush them within its maw.
When idle, the Xu Wu will often form blades on its arms and aimlessly point them around as if surveying its surroundings. It has also been seen using its tentacles to clean and groom its teeth while resting.
Life Cycle
The Xu Wu lays clutches of egg sacs on the ceiling of its lair, which hatch en masse into its young, known as Xu Yo. After hatching, the Xu Yo will move in disorganized groups with siblings that hatched at the same time as it, and is sustained for the first part of its life by the nutrients from its egg.

Physiology
The Yama Tsukami is an incredibly bizarre Elder Dragon with an appearance highly atypical from what most people expect a dragon to resemble, appearing instead as a floating mountain. It has an exceptionally long lifespan, existing far outside the bounds of time that most humans can measure, with many claiming it to be the oldest of any Elder Dragon. Its body is round and bulbous, with its underside covered in a pale, gray hide. It possesses four large tentacles around its sides, each tipped with two finger-like protrusions, as well as two thinner tentacles present at its front. The meat inside these tentacles is described as being both slimy and light. Atop the Elder Dragon's back grows large quantities of parasitic plant life—such as mosses and even entire trees—which when combined with the shape of its body, grants the Yama Tsukami the appearance of a living, forest-covered mountain. Having grown atop the Elder Dragon's body, this vegetation has been imbued with mysterious power; in the case of the moss that coats the Yama Tsukami's body, its power is able to heighten the quality of crafted goods, whereas the beauty of the wood harvested from the mysterious trees is able to be transferred directly to equipment.
Despite not possessing any form of wings, the Yama Tsukami is capable of flight. This is accomplished through an internal gas stored internally that is formed from the large quantities of both dirt and rotten flesh decomposing inside the body. By taking in air through its mouth, the Yama Tsukami is capable of inflating its body further, allowing it to control the height at which it flies. The underside of the Yama Tsukami's body contains several gills that can be used to release the gas from inside its body, granting it even further control whilst flying. This gas expulsion can additionally be weaponized offensively by releasing it near potential threats, as this internally stored gas is also highly flammable.
Whilst normally kept hidden, the Yama Tsukami possesses a massive mouth filled with teeth that uncannily resemble those of a human's. Using this mouth, it is capable of sucking in large quantities of air, allowing the Yama Tsukami to suck up entire forests and lakes in a single gulp as it flies overhead. The Yama Tsukami will additionally suck Thunderbugs into its body as it sucks up food, however, instead of being swallowed with the rest of the Elder Dragon's food, these insects remain inside of their new host and will slowly mutate over time, gaining a new explosive quality. The Yama Tsukami can then expel these new Great Thunderbugs from its mouth to attack those it deems a threat.
Behavior
Known as the Floating Dragon, the Yama Tsukami was initially sighted by researchers in polar regions, with it specifically appearing the most frequently around a small side tower near the Forlorn Arena, next to the main central tower. However, it has also been sighted passing overhead the Jungle. Due to it being sighted across vast stretches of sea, it can be assumed that it is capable of migrating very long distances. While research on the Elder Dragon has been slow due to the scant few records that exist—with some people even going so far as to believe it does not even exist—thanks to the efforts of the Dragonwatch, the speed of research in recent years has increased dramatically.
Witness accounts of the appearance of the Yama Tsukami vary drastically between different eye witnesses. While it is conceivable these people witnessed a different Subspecies of the same Elder Dragon, due to both the Yama Tsukami's massive size and the long lifespan it possesses, the likelihood of these differences belonging to a Subspecies seems improbable. Moreover, while it is possible these accounts could present the Yama Tsukami at different stages of its life, it is currently believed that these differences are simply the result of disparate witnesses attempting to describe the same monster under different conditions.
