Physiology
Being closely related to the Yian Kut-Ku, the Yian Garuga shares several physical traits in common with its fellow Bird Wyvern, although there are also several significant differences. Notably, the Yian Garuga grows to a much larger size than its close relative does, and unlike the reddish-pink scales of the Kut-Ku, the Garuga sports a coating of ominous blackish-purple scales. While superficially looking very similar, they are much tougher in composition, being hard enough to deflect the strikes of most blades and with its mere presence said to give off an intimidating and ominous aura. As it ages, the strength and durability of its shelling will naturally increase, with the strongest among the scales sparkling as if they were purple quartz. The back of the Yian Garuga is coated in several sharp spines that jut out in all directions as well as small tufts of silver fur—this fur is much more prominent around the back of the head, forming an unusually intimidating mane for its size.
The Yian Garuga shares a similar shovel-shaped beak to that of the Yian Kut-Ku, with its instead being colored a pale purple. Differentiating the two however, the Garuga's beak is proportionally larger and its lower mandible sports notably sharper protrusions, granting the beak an overall much fiercer appearance. As well, similarly to the Kut-Ku, it sports foldable, fan-like ears patterned in vivid shades of purple. It typically keeps them folded against the side of its head, although when it is engaging its targets, it will fan them out to their full size, only folding them back up again once it has become gravely injured. Compared to its relative, its ears are proportionally much smaller, with the Garuga seemingly lacking the same strong sensitivity to loud noises. The overall shape of its ears showcases the different evolutionary paths the two species have undergone in comparison to one another. While it is also capable of breathing fire, unlike the fiery liquid spat out by the Yian Kut-Ku, the Yian Garuga is capable of shooting archetypical fireballs.
The front limbs of the Yian Garuga are fashioned into a pair of wings consisting of three of its fingers, with the interconnecting membrane colored a lime-green. Contrasting its somewhat delicate frame, the Yian Garuga possesses an explosively powerful set of muscles within its legs, with it displaying unparalleled bursts of agility when running across the ground. These muscles allow it to easily perform impressive leaps while attacking, co-ordinate several of its attacks together, and enable it to easily leap out of danger at the very last moment. However, this out of control frenzy leaves the Yian Garuga with incredibly poor stamina reserves, causing it to tire easily. Unlike the consistently thin tail of the Kut-Ku, the Garuga's tail end is bulbous and adorned with several thorns along its side, with three especially prominent thorns being present at the tip—two pointing to the sides and one pointing straight back. Inside of its tail is stored a deadly toxin, and when the tail is whipped into its victim, the shock of the impact causes the thorns on the tip to release the venom into the target's body, typically killing them within seconds.
While the Yian Garuga was once thought to simply be a Subspecies of the Yian Kut-Ku, the sheer physiological difference between the two has led to that hypothesis being dropped. Instead, it is believed to have evolved from Yian Kut-Ku individuals who preferred to stray away from their flock, which resulted in them evolving a more aggressive temperament to survive this lone wolf lifestyle, undergoing speciation in the process. The reasoning behind the blackish coloring of its body still remains unknown, however there are some prevailing hypotheses, namely that it was influenced by predation, or through crossbreeding with another species. The Yian Garuga is infamous for the high-pitch shrieks it can emit, much louder than any roar the Yian Kut-Ku could produce, which can be of sufficient volume to stun even the Deviljho. While the Kut-Ku uses such calls for communication within its species, due to the Garuga's more solitary nature, these calls are instead used only to assert its territory against other members of its species.
Behavior
The Yian Garuga first appeared around the village of Kokoto, with particularly frequent sightings subsequently being seen around the village of Jumbo. When it was originally discovered, its superficial similarities to the Yian Kut-Ku lead many Hunters to assume it be a simple challenge to take down, causing many to equip themselves very lightly when tasked to hunt it down. However, the wyvern would end up putting up a significantly tougher fight than its relative ever could, leaving many hunters to retire after having their spirits crushed by the encounter. While it has a preference towards living in forested habitats, it does not form a permanent territory, with the suggested reasoning being that it is constantly on the move looking for new battles due to its love of fighting. It has also been discovered living in the New World, and it is believed the species originally settled there upon following the migration patterns of the Yian Kut-Ku, which typically travels towards warmer habitats during colder seasons. However, due to the fierce competition present within the Guiding Lands, it is believed that while the Yian Kut-Ku was unable to achieve a stable population, the Yian Garuga meanwhile was able to thrive. Unlike the Kut-Ku, which typically lives within large gregarious flocks, the Garuga has never been seen cooperating with itself. As a result, it is believed to live an entirely solitary life.
The demeanor of the Yian Garuga is incredibly "warlike," having been repeatedly documented actively seeking out other species to battle and challenge with no clear advantage towards its own survival, seemingly for no other reason than it enjoys battling. This attitude frequently results in individuals bearing notable scars, most commonly a torn ear and a scar over its eye on the lefthand side of its face; its ferocity even allows it to fight a monster as strong as the Deviljho on roughly equal footing. Furthermore, the individuals living within the Guiding Lands of the New World is shown to express particular animosity towards the Zinogre, frequently engaging in territorial disputes with it due to its status as a rival species within its forested habitat. In particular however, the Yian Garuga shows a very strong animosity towards the closely related Yian Kut-Ku. Upon seeing one, it will immediately fly into a frenzy and seek to battle its fellow Bird Wyvern. It is believed that, due to their similar appearance and shared ecological niche, the Yian Garuga simply finds its relative to be instinctively repulsive. On occasion, the Garuga has even been known to interrupt the mating rituals of the Kut-Ku, with no clear motivation apart from a desire and love to fight.
Despite its brash personality, the Yian Garuga still displays a keen intellect when it comes to surveying its surroundings, demonstrated through its habit of purposely avoiding Pitfall Traps. It has even been known to step into the trap to set it off before leaping backwards at the last moment, with it seemingly being aware of the hunter's intention of capturing it. Further, several attacks performed by the wyvern are known to resemble those of other large monsters it shares its habitat with. This has lead researchers to suggest the Yian Garuga will purposely imitate the movements of other monsters it has engaged in combat with, whereupon it will incorporate those maneuvers into its own fighting style.
The Yian Garuga shares both its primary diet and method of feeding with its closest relative, where it uses its shovel-like beak to dig holes into the ground and skillfully scoop up hidden larvae to feed upon; it shows a notable preference towards both the Konchu and earthworms. In the New World, the Yian Garuga has additionally been seen scavenging on the remains left behind by other predators, although it currently remains unknown whether this indicates a shift in the diet of New World individuals, or if it is simply attracted to the swarms of insects that surround carcasses.
In the Old World, it is heavily theorized that instead of raising its chicks itself, the Yian Garuga acts as a brood parasite towards the Yian Kut-Ku, laying its eggs in its relative's nest and tricking the parents into raising its young in its stead. Within the New World, it has been additionally speculated that it has evolved to parasitize the nests of Flying Wyverns, such as the Rathian. This is believed to be the case since the it has not been observed engaging in territorial disputes with these monsters despite its aggressive demeanor, leading researchers to believe it displays some degree of symbiosis towards species it intends to make into foster parents. Some have even suggested that the Yian Garuga could hybridize with these species, although this is purely speculation.
Music
Main article: Yian Garuga (Music)
"The Howling Lone Wolf" is Yian Garuga's theme. It was the first unique non-Elder monster theme introduced for the Monster Hunter series that was solely attributed to the monster itself.
Monster Hunter Freedom
The design team wanted to make an "evil" version of Yian Kut-Ku within the constraints, so Yian Garuga was created as a monster that combined the best features of various creatures, with a Bird Wyvern skeleton with Flying Wyvern movements.
Monster Hunter: World
Kaname Fujioka stated that Yian Garuga's inclusion in the Guiding Lands was thought of in the beginning of development. The team initially thought it might be difficult for those unfamiliar with action games, but the locale is a place where various monsters appear the more you play, so they wanted to introduce an aggressive monster that would easily spice up the variety. To emphasise Yian Garuga's fast-paced combat, they made its breath attacks fire in rapid succession like a machine gun, which Fujioka thought gave it a good, "impatient" feel. With Yian Garuga being the combination of different monsters and its weird behaviors like avoiding traps, it did not feel out of place when the team introduced it in the Guiding Lands. The returning monster also served as a reward for those who have played through the game thoroughly.
Since Yian Garuga was one of the earliest monsters in the series, the design team did not change its image too drastically and simply refined it. They increased the amount of spikes and made those spikes thinner, the size of its lower jaw, and perhaps most significant, redesigned the wings of the monster. The digits are no longer sporadic and disjointed, and are instead all long and large, connected to the wing claw of the Yian Garuga; staying consistent with the rest of the winged monsters. This wing design change was carried over to Yian Kut-Ku when it returned in Monster Hunter Wilds.

Physiology
The Yian Kut-Ku is a medium-sized Bird Wyvern with an impressively large beak and pair of ears. It sports vibrant, pink dorsal shells that protrude outwards like spines, while its ventral scales are primarily cream colored. It has long legs and three-toed feet, and is known to be agile on foot. The lateral scales separating the dorsal shells from its underbelly are bright yellow, and the wings of the Yian Kut-Ku have blue webbing that is incredibly resistant, making the membrane highly valued as fusing material. As well, the Yian Kut-Ku's carapace is fire-resistant. The Yian Kut-Ku is thought to share a common ancestor with the Gypceros, known as the Borudoru.
One of the Yian Kut-Ku's most impressive features is its large ear frills which can fold and expand at will. These frills can be used to intimidate predators by making the monster look bigger, as well as by amplifying the sound of the Yian Kut-Ku's screeches. When expanded, the ears resemble fans in appearance and allow the monster's highly developed audio receptors to pinpoint the locations of both predator and prey. The Yian Kut-Ku's exceptional hearing allows it to even detect changes in its chicks' health by picking up on subtle differences in the calls of its young. Consequently, the Yian Kut-Ku's sensitive ears render the monster particularly vulnerable to loud noises, such as those produced by Sonic Bombs, which can damage its ear canals and momentarily paralyze it. A fully-grown pair of the yian Kut-Ku's ears are considered to be good luck charms and are often used to craft Bowguns due to their fire-resistant nature.
The Yian Kut-Ku utilizes its large beak to dig holes in the ground in the search of prey—the Konchu is its favourite food, and the Bird Wyvern bypasses its tough exoskeleton by swallowing the Neopteron whole. Its beak is uniquely shaped to act as a shovel, aiding it in unearthing insects and larvae hiding underground. As such, holes can be seen scattered around the monster's territory as a result of it foraging. While primarily insectivorous, during the breeding season, the Yian Kut-Ku has been observed eating the Honey from beehives. While feeding on such hives, the Yian Kut-Ku is often so forceful that it sheds many of its scales in the process, leaving them behind underneath the beehives. Since its scales are easily regrown, the wyvern isn't hindered by this loss.
Behavior
The Yian Kut-Ku is typically quite skittish, although it will act aggressively towards perceived threats. It is agile and enough of a threat to be considered dangerous to humans, especially since it possesses a Flame Sac and is capable of spitting fireballs at enemies. As well, the Yian Kut-Ku at times has been known to weaponize the Konchu it digs up by rolling them along the ground at hunters.
The Yian Kut-Ku will occasionally reproduce en masse when weather conditions are favourable for earthworms to multiply in large numbers, one of the monster's favourite prey items. However, due to the increase in the Yian Kut-Ku population, the Bird Wyvern will seek new territory to forage and avoid food scarcity, which eventually ends with it attacking human settlements. In response, large-scale Yian Kut-Ku hunts are ordered to reduce the population before it spirals out of control. This ends up with a notable decline in the Yian Kut-Ku population's numbers, which returns to normal the year following the reproduction bloom. During the season of Plenty in the Eastlands, the Yian Kut-Ku migrates to the Scarlet Forest in huge flocks. The lack of any eggs or young individuals suggests this is done to both find a mate as well as food.

Physiology
The Zamite is a small to medium-sized Amphibian and the juvenile form of the significantly larger Zamtrios. Its underbelly is covered in a highly elastic beige hide, the thickness of which results in it being highly resistant to tearing. Its scales can feel both smooth or rough depending on which direction they are rubbed across, and its fin-like tail is vertically flattened and colored a golden-orange at the tip, with the rear half of the monster being mottled by green spots. Its limbs are colored a greenish-brown on their lower half and a deep blue on their upper half, with its toes additionally being webbed to allow for better swimming capabilities.
Atop its head extends a large horn consisting of three serrated edges jutting out from both the top and to either of the horn's sides. This horn aids the Zamite in both leaping towards and stabbing into its targets; it will lose this horn upon maturing into a Zamtrios. It eyes are pure white and appear to lack a pupil, while its teeth are sharp and pointed; if the Zamite were to lose some of its teeth, it is capable of quickly growing them back.
Upon initially hatching, the Zamite is very small and lacks any hindlegs, forcing it to move by sliding around on its belly. However, even just a single meal is enough for it to balloon to several times its size prior to feeding; this also causes its once purposeless hindlegs to fully develop. Once the Zamite has consumed enough food, the Ice Sacs present in the adult stage will begin to develop, allowing the Zamite to fire off small balls of snow.
Behavior
Despite its small size, the juvenile Zamite will feed on monsters significantly larger than itself, such as the Popo. Once it has spotted potential prey, it will launch itself at them and bite down with its sharp teeth; the Zamite's grip onto its prey is especially strong, making it difficult to pull one away, although even if the target is able to knock the Zamite away from itself, several of its teeth will remain embedded in its victims skin. Once it has properly secured itself onto its target, it will utilize its arrow-shaped horn to drill into the surface of its prey's skin, allowing it to enter the prey's body and begin to eat it alive from the inside out. Once it has finished eating, it will use its horn to drill and leap back outside the carcass.

Physiology
The Zamtrios is a large, Sharq-like Amphibian covered in a cyan hide across its back which is counter-shaded by an off-white coloration present around the underside. The hide covering its back consists of several small, yet thick scales whose course texture functions akin to sandpaper, their razor-sharp edges shredding whatever makes contact with them. The Zamtrios' hide covering its belly is constantly growing new harder layers underneath itself, with the older surface layer eventually tearing to make way for the next layer. This process of tearing also functions as a defense mechanism against attackers, giving the hide a surprising amount of durability. Furthermore, its hide boasts remarkable resistance against the cold.
The jaws are one of the Zamtrios' most defining feature, capable of opening to a much wider size than one would initially suspect and allowing it to swallow even large prey in a single bite. While feeding on a target, the hide on its stomach demonstrates its exceptional elasticity, causing it to expand to several times its original size. Within its jaws lie several rows of triangular teeth that, rather than slice through flesh like a razor, instead crush due to their blunt edge. Known as its Sawtooth due to the serrated ridges present around the teeth's edges, each one will slowly and excruciatingly tear apart whatever they embed into, and if the Amphibian were to ever loose its teeth a new set will grow in its place.
A notable feature of the Zamtrios is the large dorsal fin atop its back, with it bearing smaller fins extending out from each foreleg. It utilizes its dorsal fin, which shares the coarse texture of the hide, to smoothly cut through ice as it swims beneath the frozen surface. The Zamtrios has webbed toes that make it better adapted for swimming underwater, and its razor-sharp crescent tail is additionally able to serve as an effective weapon. Mimicking an axe, it is capable of knocking out prey with a single hefty lash.
The Zamtrios contains several Frost Sacs within its body that produce a specialized liquid. This liquid may be spewed from the monster's mouth in the form of a high volume spout, or as concentrated spheres that drain targets of their body heat and freeze them in place. Furthermore, the Zamtrios is able to secrete this special fluid through its skin, at which point it will instantly freeze upon contact with the air and form a layer of protective ice armor over its back. However, the Zamtrios will reveal one more trick once sufficiently threatened—by gasifying the liquid in its body by heating it to an ample temperature, the Amphibian is able to expand its extremely elastic abdomen to several times its original size. Whilst in this bloated state, the Zamtrios is capable of crushing anything in its path by throwing its heft around through rolling or leaping, much to the astoundment of hunters. However, the stretched-out skin is exceptionally soft and vulnerable during this ballooned form, and if the Zamtrios receives too much damage to its expanded belly, it will release the freezing gas from its abdomen in an attempt to fend off anything still attacking it, returning to its original form in the process as the internal liquid re-condenses. It is worth noting that the various states the Zamtrios enters do not seem to be done intentionally, with the fluid instead being automatically secreted when it grows especially agitated, with the internal fluid vaporizing once its levels of anger has reached its absolute peak; the diverse array of forms this monster can adapt is what granted it the nickname of Monster Sharq from common folk.
Behavior
The Zamtrios inhabits frigid regions, with it spending a lot of time near or around water. It hunts by burrowing beneath the ice and swimming towards its target, before lunging from below the ice once close, with it even being known to attack ships. The Zamtrios relies extensively on both its sense of smell hearing to track its prey, with its hearing being especially useful to it while swimming. As such, sudden loud noises can often startle it when it is attempting to strike, causing it to leap back to the surface as a result. Whilst the Zamtrios feeds on a variety of smaller animals, it has been noted to be especially fond of the taste of Frogs, considered to be its favorite meal.
Life Cycle
As a juvenile, the Zamtrios is known as a Zamite and is significantly smaller than an adult; it is famed for piercing through the hide of prey and entering them internally, devouring them from the inside. Moreover, it is notable for its extraordinarily rapid growth that allows it to often grow several times its original size from merely a single feeding. As it ages, the serrated horn at the tip of its snout atrophies as it no longer needs it to burrow into its prey, morphing instead into the adult's flattened snout. However, the adult Zamtrios can still form a similar horn when materializing its ice armor.

Physiology
The Zinogre is a large, primarily cyan toned Fanged Wyvern with a thick torso, a small head, and a long broad tail; it typically orientates itself by holding its bulky torso semi-upright and its head high. While most of its scaling is green-blue, the ends of each limb—as well as the several rows of spikes lining its back—are colored an off-yellow; this scaling acts as an insulator to the monster's charge. Running along its back are two rows of white fur that take the form of a large flowing mane, with additional smaller patches being present on its limbs. The skull is proportionally small and bears a narrow snout and robust lower jaw, with several scales on each lip having formed into "pseudo-teeth." The lower jaw features a distinct pair of spikes situated on the chin, forming a distinct two-pronged fork. A pair of forward-facing, magnificent horns grow out from the top of the skull behind the eyes, which can be used to bestow equipment with tremendous power. Their surface contains several porous holes and they are permitted a limited range of motion by a muscle underneath. The horns are made from thin, overlapping bones and are placed such that they protect the brain from impacts.
The Zinogre possesses extremely muscular forearms, with each bearing five sharp and incredibly powerful claws—two of these claws possess great flexibility, although they are normally kept folded up against the forelimb. The Zinogre's high voltage claws are capable of dicing up prey with little effort, and any electrical attacks they unleash are especially brutal. The Fanged Wyvern's body is adapted to living in rough and mountainous terrain, and as such, the forearms are extremely muscular in order to allow the Zinogre to pull itself up steep ledges, with the sharp claws also being shaped for this purpose. The tail of the Zinogre is broad and flat, as well as covered in several rows of spike-like plates and fur, it acts as a devastating weapon when swung. The monster's back and tail are heavily armored, with the latter being especially so along its topside. The underside is comparatively unarmored and is believed to indicate that its defenses developed primarily to protect it against Flying Wyverns. While the armored tail can be utilized as a weapon when swung, its main purpose appears to be to counterbalance the wyvern's muscular torso.
As a juvenile, the Zinogre is much fluffier and possesses more fur, which protects the yet underdeveloped shockshell; as it matures, its fur falls out. While it is a powerful hunter from the offset, its electrical ability is not present at birth and must be developed over time. It remains unknown if the Zinogre lays eggs.
Thunder Ability
The Zinogre's unique physiology is shaped by its signature ability to generate, amplify, and release electric charges, an ability based on a complex multi-stage process that begins in its armor shell, namely with the yellow segments of the carapace, called Shockers. While these Shockers may appear as superficial structures, they are actually the external tips of a massive network of generator organs that permeates the entire body. Within these Shocker organs, the Zinogre produces special lipids that can be used to generate electrical charges. The resulting electric current is then funneled into and stored in the cream-colored fur of the wyvern, where it then gets magnified. Retaining its charge even after having been carved and removed from the body, the electrical charge causes the Zinogre's fur to shine a dazzling white. The charge is further guided by the tail, which maintains a low position to the ground at all times to aid in the flow of electricity across the back and maximize the wyvern's generatory capabilities.
Through this set of unique adaptations, the Zinogre is able to reliably produce electric charges within its body and store them in its fur, granting the wyvern various benefits. Stimulation of its muscles through the charge enhances its physical strength, and exposure to the continuous flow of electricity makes the Zinogre almost fully immune to both paralytic poisons and Shock Traps. However this ability comes with distinct limitations as well: the shocker organs sit directly atop its musculature and cannot be stimulated whilst it is exerting itself—in other words, the Zinogre has to stand still in order to charge up, leaving it wide open for attacks by opponents; the maximum voltage the wyvern may reach is also limited. In order to overcome these weaknesses, it maintains a symbiotic bond with Thunderbugs, a species of insect known to be able to produce and amplify electric charges as part of their natural metabolism.
These bugs are usually preyed upon by the Gargwa, which itself happens to be a primary food source for the Zinogre. For this reason, Thunderbugs nest within the Zinogre's fur for protection against the Gargwa, and in exchange they serve as a secondary external generator system by storing and amplifying the charge produced by the wyvern's shockers. In effect, this allows the Zinogre to surpass the usual limits of its body and hold a much greater charge than would be possible otherwise. This has numerous benefits for the monster, such as allowing it to charge up faster as well as granting it the use of ranged attacks by launching charged clusters of Thunderbugs forward.
As this symbiosis is central to the lives of both species, they each sport adaptations to facilitate it. In addition to the yellow shocker shells, the Zinogre also grows blue insulatory shells that aid in containing the amplified electric charges produced in tandem with the Thunderbugs. The shape of the shocker shells is formed such that it provides numerous grooves and nooks for the Thunderbugs to nest in. In turn, the Thunderbugs become increasingly more powerful as they spend their time stimulated by the electric current of the Zinogre, with some of them turning into a special kind of Thunderbug, called a Fulgurbug. These empowered insects sport much greater electric potential then regular Thunderbugs. Curiously, the type of Thunderbug bonded to the Zinogre is always the Old World variation, regardless of if the Zinogre itself inhabits the New World.
When sufficiently charged with electricity, the Zinogre will enter its Supercharged State, in which the Thunder element will begin to course freely throughout its body. When in this state, numerous physiological differences can be observed: the horns fold downwards as the shockers extend, and the outer claws on the wyvern's feet unfold into their full length. Additionally, its back alights with an electric blue glow, which can even be seen inside the monster's throat. While charged with electrical power eclipsing lighting, many of its physical blows release explosions of electricity from the claws and spines, and it becomes capable of releasing lightning strikes, or sending out charged Fulgurbug clusters as ranged attacks. Additionally, the surge of electricity within the Zinogre's body further enhances the activity of its muscles, making it much stronger than normal.
Behavior
The Zinogre can be most commonly found in forests near mountain ranges and is known to live in the regions near Yukumo. It primarily feeds on the Aptonoth and Gargwa, and hunts by dispatching them with its sharp claws—holding a preference for the latter in particular. It is known to be an extremely successful predator, to the point that many have given it the nickname, Peerless Hunter. When facing off against a rival or a Hunter, the wyvern has been observed dispersing a swarm of Thunderbugs as a threat display. One curious behavior of the Zinogre lies in its relation to the night and to the sky, for in rare circumstances, it can be seen sitting peacefully at night, staring at the moon and howling sporadically; the cause and purpose of this behavior is not known. Additionally, it has been noted the Zinogre appears to be more active on cloudless days.
Despite being commonly sighted traveling alone, the Zinogre is not actually a solitary species. Instead, it congregates into large packs, in which several adult Zinogre coexist mostly peacefully. A Zinogre pack is structured around a hierarchy derived from each member's maximum electric voltage, where the stronger the produced charge, the higher an individual's status within the pack. There is also a division of labor between the sexes: the female always remains with the pack, taking care of the young and maintaining the pack's territories. The Zinogre's territory is often aligned with the population density of Thunderbugs, and it is the role of any female to ensure that the pack's symbiotic partners thrive in the realms the pack claims. Meanwhile, the male Zinogre's role is to routinely venture alone out into the wilds to procure food for the pack, returning with his bounty regularly. It is these lonesome male hunters that the Hunter's Guild most commonly encounters.
Super Biology Information
The Super Biology Book Series collects the thoughts and theories of real scientists that were asked to speak about monsters from the Monster Hunter series. Thus, they are inherently speculative and should be seen as such.
Fossil Expert Yoshitsugu Kobayashi notes how well-developed the forelimbs of the Zinogre are. Due to their length compared to the wyvern’s hind legs, he compares the Zinogre’s body build to that of the Brachiosaurus, a sauropod dinosaur. But despite this similarity, the Zinogre exhibits great agility and speed, which is not generally attributed to sauropods. Zoological Author Yuumin Mori adds that the shape of the forelimbs, as well as the monster’s forested habitats, implies that the Zinogre is a solitary ambush predator, with its hunting behavior likely resembling that of Tigers.
While examining the head of the Zinogre, Kobayashi compares the two large horns of the monster to some structures found on the heads of certain theropod dinosaurs. Such horns are likely ornamental and serve as displays, either to intimidate rivals or attract mates. Kobayashi theorizes that they probably evolved out of the many spiny shells on the rest of the Zinogre’s body, which would originally likely have been a defensive adaptation. The snout of the Zinogre meanwhile appears to imply a fish-based diet; Kobayashi compares it to that maw of a Spinosaurus and asserts that a slender shape with long sharp teeth is usually associated with animals that catch fish from the water, as the slim snout reduces water resistance. Thus, the Zinogre is likely at least a partial piscivore.
The muscles of the Zinogre are highly developed, and Kobayashi notes all the many shells and spikes the monster must carry and swing around during combat. This particular trait seems to be similar to the weapons seen in Ankylosaurus, and Kobayashi muses that the Zinogre likely possess similar muscular strength. Mori meanwhile focuses on the energy expenditure: Due to the size and shells of the Zinogre, the monster is likely well-adapted to retaining heat within its body. Despite this, the high level of activity of this species would require it to consume frequent, high-calorie meals to remain at peak performance. Mori especially singles out the ability to jump as problematic here; small animals, such as Fleas, are known to be able to jump long distances easily, in this case nearly 100 times the Flea’s own body length. But jumping becomes exponentially more difficult the larger the animal gets, and if one were to grow a Flea to a size of one meter, it would not suddenly be able to jump 100 meters. Thus, the Zinogre’s leaps likely consume a monstrous amount of energy.
Mori then attempts to explain the electric generation ability seen in Thunderbugs. He proposes that the bugs exploit ionic imbalances between their cells' exteriors and interiors to build up electric charges within their entire bodies all at once. This would also explain why they appear to glow from within. Mori then theorizes that since Thunderbugs group together for defensive purposes, they might use this glow to identify potential allies to swarm towards. This may have been the impetus that led to their symbiosis with the Zinogre, as the wyvern’s own electricity might have produced an enticing glow that activated the Thunderbugs’ cooperative instincts.
When discussing the Thunderbugs, Mori investigates how exactly the symbiosis between them and the Zinogre actually functions. While the basic interaction of Thunderbugs receiving protection and the Zinogre using their charges to empower its own seems straightforward, there might be more to it: Mori proposes that the Thunderbugs relatively weak electric ability may have developed not as a defense, but as a way to attract tiny microorganisms to itself. In swarms, they can create stronger charges and thus attract more of these organisms, which in turn would mean that the electrically charged back of a Zinogre would be a veritable buffet of such critters. This would not just feed the Thunderbugs already on its back, but also attract Thunderbugs from the nearby environment - which in turn might lure Gargwa towards the Zinogre.
Music
Main article: Zinogre (Music)
"Spark of Blue", previously known as "Violent Flash of Blue Light", is Zinogre's theme. It is known for using electric guitars paired with Monster Hunter' s standard orchestral elements. "Spark of Blue" was remastered in Monster Hunter World: Iceborne and Monster Hunter Rise, and was voted among the Top 10 music themes in the Hunters' Choice: Top 10 Monster Themes - Monster Hunter 20th Anniversary.
Monster Hunter Portable 3rd
The development of Monster Hunter Portable 3rd coincided with a large influx of new design staff being added to the Monster Hunter production team. Many of them were thus assigned to the task of creating a new flagship monster as a way to initiate them into the process. The only mandate they received from Director Yasunori Ichinose was that Monster Hunter Portable 3rd was going to have a "Japanese-style world", and that the monster they created should fit into that idea. This was enough inspiration for the newcomer team, which immediately went to work creating a plethora of concept designs for this new flagship monster. There were so many ideas in fact that the team struggled to unify them all into a solid pitch, as many of them featured fantastical, Yokai-like designs. Kaname Fujioka advised them to consider the skeletal structure of their concept designs - how would this creature move, and how could that motion be depicted? The team ultimately landed on the idea of a wolf-like demon that called forth thunder. The monster was named ジンオウガ (Jinōga), deriving its name from the English word "ogre" and the first Kanji of the the Japanese expression for "thunderclap", 迅雷 (jinrai). One near-final prototype of the monster could even spew electrified streams of saliva at players. This ability was ultimately scrapped, as it did not fit the Zinogre well.
Once the visual design and abilities of the Zinogre had been completed, the design team realized that this monster had become extremely complex. It was a new monster type, with never before seen attack movements, that could also charge up electricity and transform. Communicating all of this to players would be a challenge, which is why Yuya Tokuda was assigned to the task of designing the combat flow for Zinogre. His solution was to create a behavior cycle in which the Zinogre gradually works its way up to its most powerful form, with each attack serving as a way to move towards that goal. For example, some attacks allow it to charge, while others allow it to reset its position. Due to the Zinogre's skeleton, players would naturally be drawn towards attacking either the head or the tail, both of which were softened to accommodate for that. During testing however, players crowded the tail, since that way they could avoid the front of the monster entirely, which is where most of its attacks were targeted. Due to this, the tail was hardened again to make for a more interesting fight.
Monster Hunter World: Iceborne
Zinogre is a popular monster who's appeared in every game since its introduction in Portable 3rd, so Kaname Fujioka, fearing fatigue, initially shelved it for Iceborne. The development team never allocated any production costs for it and didn't plan for its last minute addition. However, as popular returning monsters were announced for Iceborne, players became so enthusiastic for Zinogre and believed it would feature in the game that the tean just could not leave it out. Thus, the team consulted with Ryozo Tsujimoto and director Daisuke Ichihara, adjusting the costs they had been saving for title updates to add Zinogre. This was why Zinogre did not appear in the main story, only being introduced in the Guiding Lands; the post-game locale.
Zinogre also received a complete design overhaul, and its body figure was significantly changed. The monster was made to be significantly bulkier, its head with more dragon-like proportions and its chin mandibles smaller. Its howl when charged up was changed to be more wolf-like, and shares its death roar with Nergigante's.
Adding Zinogre was pointless unless it was put in a place where it could shine. They decided to make it an individual that was led to the Guiding Lands, and made it appear as a surprise in the first cutscene of the Guiding Lands. Humorously, Fujioka was glad that Thunderbugs appeared in World.
Monster Hunter Rise
Zinogre's design was once again changed significantly in Rise, and its proportions matched more with the original Portable 3rd model. Its legs, horns and arms were made larger while its back became smaller. The claws got more stout, with its folded up claws becoming longer. Zinogre's roars were back to the originals, albeit remastered in audio quality. Rise was the subsequent game after Iceborne, so the reason for this quick design change remains to be seen.

The White Seraph Dragon Zoh Shia (ゾ・シア, Zo Shia) is a Construct introduced in Monster Hunter Wilds.
Summary
An enormous Construct with a pair of gigantic wingarms and a body clad in a sleek, flowery armor comprised of crystallized Wylk, which both protects it and stores energy. The most powerful of the Guardians created by Wyveria, intended to be a saviour against an unknown threat, Zoh Shia instead brought about the extinction of the once prosperous civilization before falling into a deep slumber, silently absorbing the energy of the Dragontorch. Hidden beneath this shell rests its true form, a deformed, black monstrosity littered with malformed horns, capable of using destructive fire and lightning.
Main Series
Monster Hunter Wilds: Zoh Shia is hunted as the final boss of Low Rank in the 3★ Assignment Guardian Zoh Shia, and cannot be refought in Low Rank. In High Rank, it is refought in the 8★ Assignment Germination. Afterwards, Zoh Shia may appear as a quest target in the Ruins of Wyveria, allowing players to create an Investigation for it and battle it in the Dragontorch Shrine. After the slaying of Guardian Arkveld and subsequent investigation of the Dragontorch, Zoh Shia is found to have taken over the Dragontorch, despite being believed to have fallen dormant in the event that destroyed Wyveria. Faced with the choice of destroying the Dragontorch to kill Zoh Shia at the cost of upending all life in the Forbidden Lands, the Avis Hunter takes the initiative and directly awakens Zoh Shia, then slays it. However, its fragments continue to regrow after its death, forcing the Forbidden Lands Expedition Team to continue monitoring it and slaying it when it reappears until a more permanent solution is found.

Physiology
Zoh Shia is an enormous monster with traits similar to those of Elder Dragons. It sports a slender, quadrupedal frame, with two massive wingarms growing from its back. Its entire body is covered in a coiled, layered shell of crystallized Wyvern Milk, with numerous crystal protrusions resembling flower petals or feathers sprouting from all over, although most prominently on its wingarms. Its head is ovoid in shape and somewhat beak-like, lacks eyes, and boasts a frill of wedge-like spikes lining it, with two more prominent spikes at the top in the place of horns. Its claws are elongated by uniform Wylk growths and resemble stakes, while its tail is long and thin, resembling a whip. The flesh beneath its armor is an unnatural purple, visible when it opens its almost toothless mouth. Should its face plate be broken, a single black eye—or eye-hole—can be seen beneath the surface.
Its crystal Wylk shell continuously regenerates from damage, as well as stores large amounts of energy that Zoh Shia discharges from its wingarms to defend itself, infusing the ground with energy and creating large explosions that crystallize the surroundings into more Wylkrystals. The crystals on the shell have even been observed growing after they have been removed from the monster. In spite of this, the shell is noted to constrict Zoh Shia as much as it protects it. Hidden within Zoh Shia's body is an elaborate inorganic gem that seems to have something wriggling within.
As Zoh Shia is damaged, it will slowly shed parts of its shell and reveal its true body, a hideously deformed, dragon-like monster seemingly made of an amorphous, wax-like, black substance. This Blackember Mass can reform and transform freely, allowing Zoh Shia to fit into its original shell and regrow it if needed, and constantly pulses in an alien manner. Its head becomes an asymmetrical tangle of large twisted horns that cover its small and yellow, reptilian eyes, with its mouth becoming more toothy and exposing an elongated, serpentine tongue. Its wingarms expand in size and begin growing horn-like protrusions all over them as well, while the glowing purple parts on their undersides begin to glow bright red when the monster is further angered. All of the feathery spikes along its body are revealed to be more traditional and draconic in appearance, similarly to its claws. As the Guardian continues to shed its shell and enrage, the horn-like growths all over its body will continue to grow larger and more malformed. While Zoh Shia retains its Wylk explosions in its true form, dubbed the Fallen State, it gains the ability to breathe fire from its mouth and emit it from the palms of its wingarms. When the monster is angered enough, it will begin emitting red lightning in addition to flames, both from its body and summoned from its surroundings.
As a Guardian, Zoh Shia does not need to eat or reproduce, able to subsist solely on Wyvern Milk. However, due to an unknown mechanism, it is able to reproduce through fragmentation, where not only can Zoh Shia continue to regenerate and come back to life provided enough energy and time, each fragment separated from Zoh Shia has the potential to grow into an entirely new Zoh Shia. These fragments take on a black liquid form contained in flowery cocoons as they grow, although the first Zoh Shia to emerge appears to break and absorb all remaining cocoons. Furthermore, it appears that upon successfully reforming, Zoh Shia grows in strength.
Unlike other Guardians, Zoh Shia does not have a specific original species it was based on, with its creation being said to involve extremely unique monster cells.
Behavior
Little is known about Zoh Shia's original behavior due to the length of time that passed between its awakening and recent rediscovery. It can be presumed to be a destructive monster that wiped out a civilization, although the exact circumstances of the event are unknown. Following that, it took up residence in the Dragontorch Shrine and absorbed energy for an unknown reason—speculated to be some kind of metamorphosis—reacting violently when suddenly reawakened. As it sheds its shell in battle, it becomes increasingly aggressive and destructive as it reveals its true power from the days of yore.
There are claims that Zoh Shia is in a perpetual state of conflict as its Guardian nature suppresses its destructive impulses. However, the truth of these claims remain unknown.
Relationship with Wyveria
Zoh Shia was the final and most powerful Guardian of Wyveria, known as the Savior, created as their last line of defense and ultimate weapon for a war of ambiguous nature. Although the exact details are unknown, Zoh Shia brought about the end of the once prosperous civilization by laying waste to the capital, before entering a deep slumber.
Music
Main article: Zoh Shia (Music)
"Arrant Calamity" and "Justice Breaks Forth" are Zoh Shia's 1st phase and 2nd phase themes respectively, first playing in its debut game. Curiously, they do not contain any motifs of " The Beauty of Nature ", Wilds ' main theme, despite it being a Final Boss monster.
When slain in the main Assignment in Wilds, "Dreams Hereafter" plays as the Quest Complete theme.
Development
In order to portray Zoh Shia's innocence and purity, the design team implemented elements of eggs, ceremonial staves like gohei, and chrysanthemum flowers.

The Molten Mountain Dragon Zorah Magdaros (ゾラ・マグダラオス, Zora Magudaraosu) is an Elder Dragon introduced in Monster Hunter: World.
Summary
Massive, quadrupedal Elder Dragons, known for their great stature and volcanic bodies. A rocky molten shell covers most of their body, with the exception of their strange beard and horn-like weak spots called Magmacores. Vestigial wings also exist beneath their massive shell. Most of Zorah Magdaros' shell is immune to weapon attacks, save for their Magmacores. Siege weapons like ballistae, cannons, and Dragonators are effective tools in damaging these ever-moving gargantuans.
Main Series
Monster Hunter: World: First seen in the beginning cutscene where it emerges from the water and capsizes the Fifth Fleet ships. Throughout the Low Rank campaign, the player looks for traces of the Elder Dragon across the New World. The player confronts Zorah Magdaros for the first time in the ★4 Assignment One for the History Books, which ends in failure but opens a path to the Coral Highlands and Rotten Vale. Zorah Magdaros is confronted a second time in the ★6 Assignment A Colossal Task. Completing this quest allows the player to enter the Elder's Recess and marks the beginning of High Rank. The Fifth Fleet of the Research Commission followed Zorah Magdaros across the sea to the New World. The Commission continued to track the Elder Dragon to discover the cause of the Elder Crossing. While attempting to travel to the Everstream, Zorah Magdaros was repelled by the Research Commission. See History for more details.

Physiology
Noted to be similar in appearance to its close relative, the Lao-Shan Lung, the Zorah Magdaros is a gargantuan Elder Dragon that sports a shell comprised of volcanic rock upon its back and which is regarded as the largest known living species. The Zorah Magdaros consumes explosive minerals, with its digestion process extracting pure energy from the minerals and melting indigestible matter into magma. The energy is sent to an inner core, while molten waste is sent to various Magmacores —porous organs that dot the Elder Dragon's spine that resemble orange crags—where it is subsequently expelled onto the back, solidifing into rock and gradually building a sturdy shell. Expelling magma additionally maintains the Zorah Magdaros' body temperature, and damaging the fragile Magmacores hinders the Elder Dragon's ability to stay cool, exhausting it. The efficiency of the energy extraction process increases as the Zorah Magdaros ages, with old individuals—such as the one pursued by the Fifth Fleet—containing an unbelievable amount of energy in their body.
The shell is made of black volcanic rock dotted by large holes leaking magma, streams of magma flow throughout it whose paths will change depending on the Elder Dragon's movements. The shape of the shell is dominated by a single large platform draped over the Zorah Magdaros back that extends over its neck, tail, and far past its sides. On top are dozens of plateau-like features that culminate in two large structures; on the back is a tall, volcano-like structure, and behind it is a rocky ramp that starts at the hip and leads tailward. The tailward cliff beneath the ramp houses a large cavity, and when the Zorah Magdaros stands on its hind legs, the volcano rests horizontally on the ramp and blocks the cavity's entrance. There are three Magmacores exposed throughout the shell: one inside the cavity over the tail, one at the hip between the ramp and volcano, and the largest Magmacore over the mid-back inside the volcano. The largest Magmacore expels the greatest amount of magma, which is why the shell around it is the thickest. Being formed from cooling magma, the shell holds ore deposits that can be mined, along with chunks that can be broken by hunting weapons. Since the shell grows over time, the age of the Zorah Magdaros can be approximated by counting the layers of magma that have accumulated. The shell of the individual that guided the Fifth Fleet has grown to be as large as the Elder Dragon itself, although it is far heavier due to its density, thus demonstrating the strength of the Zorah Magdaros.
The shell makes the Elder Dragon appear bulkier than it is, as the lanky body of the Zorah Magdaros is covered in keeled, glossy scales—most of the scales on its body are dark-brown with a red sheen. The front of the head comes to a beak-like point, and on the nose is another, smaller Magmacore; behind the beak are two pairs of large teeth. Midway between the back and the front of the skull are small eyes, and two gray horns point straight back from the head. The Zorah Magdaros has black tendrils hanging from its head that form a beard and mutton chops, they continue down the sides of the neck, torso, and tail, and are long enough to cover the upper arms and thighs. Five thick plates run from the head halfway down the neck, at which point they give way to the Magmacores, which run down to the tail.
Much like many other Elder Dragons, the Zorah Magdaros has six limbs, with the third pair being flightless wingarms. The arms and thighs are warm-gray in color and transition to the brown seen on the rest of the body. The lower pair of arms end with broad hands sporting five clawed fingers for digging, whereas the wingarms are more peculiar. Resembling the trunk of a tree more than any wing, each wingarm is three-fingered and is the primary method of support for the shell at its thickest point: the volcano-like spire that has grown over the arms. The hindlimbs are larger and more muscular than the forelimbs and end with broad, five-toed feet to distribute the Zorah Magdaros' weight. The Zorah Magdaros' limbs have adapted to traverse any terrain, with the Elder Dragon generally traveling by crawling on all fours with the head retracted under the shell, or by burrowing beneath the earth with its claws. When walking, the knuckles on the feet are bent so that the claws can dig into the ground. Additionally, the Elder Dragon's webbed feet allow it to traverse across the sea floor. When confronted with an obstacle, the Zorah Magdaros can stand on its two powerful hind legs to leave its arms free to attack.
The Zorah Magdaros can expel large globs of lava from its mouth that explode on impact and can charge a fireball inside its throat to build the flame's destructive capacity until it glows blue. As well, the Zorah Magdaros produces a gemstone within its body over time, believed to hold incredible potential.
Behavior
The Zorah Magdaros spends long periods buried underground or deep underwater, during which, it forages for minerals that it breaks down to extract pure energy from. This produces a significant amount of heat, enough to warm the surrounding seawater to a similar temperature to the body of a human. Although records of sightings are scant, the Zorah Magdaros is known to live in the Old World; the lack of sightings may be due to the Elder Dragon's shell being mistaken for features of the land—such as volcanoes—making younger individuals appear rarer. It is a docile creature, attacking other creatures only if it is continually harassed. Although a Nergigante has been observed trailing it and attempting to feed off its energy, the Zorah Magdaros is far too large and is capable of repelling its attacker by pelting it with magma.
Due to its immense size and the boundless energy it contains, the Zorah Magdaros can have a strong effect on the ecosystems it visits, as it is able to alter the landscape merely by moving, bulldozing through forest and rock alike. The individual pursued by the Research Commission created a fissure in the Great Ravine that bestowed many creatures with access to previously inaccessible regions. As it travels, the Elder Dragon will shed parts of its shell that fall off, leaving smoldering slags of volcanic rock across the land. The ambient heat of the Zorah Magdaros makes its shell a perfect nesting ground for the aggressive Barnos, which are frequently sighted alongside the colossus.
Life Cycle
Sightings of the Zorah Magdaros as a juvenile are just as rare as those of a mature individual. Inferred through the growth of mature specimens, the Zorah Magdaros is believed to be born with a less efficient internal core and without a shell. The Elder Dragon stays in its birthplace and gradually grows as it consumes available minerals and builds its strength when young, and once its core has developed enough, the Zorah Magdaros will leave in search of new feeding grounds. In spite of the available information, the reproductive habits of the Zorah Magdaros are unknown, and researchers are still in the process of determining the existence of separate male and female forms.
Like many Elder Dragons of the Old World, the Zorah Magdaros will engage in the Elder Crossing and travel across the sea to the New World. There, it will search for a final resting place in the Rotten Vale. After which, the energy within its body will be distributed throughout the Everstream to nourish the ecosystem of the New World. When the Zorah Magdaros passes, it releases all of its energy in a single burst at the moment of its death, the result of which can both destroy and create entire ecosystems. This is true for the Guiding Lands, where a skull of the species can be found in the Rotted Region. The large individual trailed by the Fifth Fleet had unexpectedly veered off towards the Everstream instead of the Rotten Vale, where it was theorized the release of its energy directly into the Everstream threatened to ignite the veins of the earth and engulf the New World in flames, causing untold destruction. However, the Research Commission repelled the Elder Dragon away from the Everstream and into the open ocean to prevent this outcome, where tens of thousands of years in the future, a new landmass full of life may form from the individual's body.
History
Records of "volcano-like Elder Dragons" crossing the sea date back several hundred years, and the Research Commission was founded in order to study this phenomenon, dubbed the Elder Crossing. The Research Commission sent fleets of ships containing Hunters and other specialists across the sea in ten year intervals. The most recent fleet—the Fifth Fleet—set sail to follow the Zorah Magdaros; this individual was the largest and oldest living specimen recorded yet. The fleet consisted of six ships transporting 500 members, including the hunter who would soon earn the moniker, the Sapphire Star. When they had nearly arrived at the New World, the Zorah Magdaros arose from beneath the fleet and sank the fleet. Incredibly, the entirety of the Fifth Fleet survived and made it to Astera. After this incident, the Research Commission's main objective was to pursue the old Zorah Magdaros to solve the mystery of the Elder Crossing.
As the Zorah Magdaros moved through the New World, it disturbed the ecosystems it crossed. As it wandered through the Ancient Forest, many of the local monsters became agitated, and other monsters—such as the Kestodon —moved to new habitats. Tracks from the Zorah Magdaros led to the Wildspire Waste, where a large chunk of the Elder Dragon's shell had fallen off and landed next to the Wildspire. From the data gathered, the Zorah Magdaros was predicted to be headed to the Great Ravine, and the Commander ordered everyone in the Research Commission to capture the Elder Dragon there. All of the Research Commission came together to ensure the operation succeeded, constructing two wooden barriers in the Great Ravine, both laden with ballistae and cannons. At dawn, the Zorah Magdaros emerged from the ground and the operation began; the Commission bombarded the giant Elder Dragon, to no avail, as it smashed through the first barrier and forced hunters to begin the mounting phase and descend onto the Zorah Magdaros' shell. They traversed its rocky surface and destroyed several Magmacores. The Commission fired a volley of binders at it and the Elder Dragon was finally restrained, when a new monster suddenly appeared. The Nergigante landed atop the Zorah Magdaros' back and attacked the hunters, dislodging several Binders as it fought. Consequently, the Zorah Magdaros broke free and destroyed the second barrier, burrowed into the ravine and escaping.
Following the operation's failure, the Research Commission would explore the newly accessible Coral Highlands and Rotten Vale in search of the Elder' Dragon's tracks through an opening in the Ravine caused by the Zorah Magdaros. After another discarded molten slag was discovered in the depths of the Vale, the Fifth Fleet turned to the First Wyverians for a clue, where they learnt the Elder Dragon had been lured away from its resting place and threatened to reduce the New World to ash with its pent-up energy. Intending to push the Zorah Magdaros into open waters, the Research Commission made a final stand at the Everstream, this time with the aid of a Dragonator. In spite of the predicted appearance of the Nergigante, the Zorah Magdaros was repelled successfully and the New World saved from annihilation. Following the operation, the Research Commission sought to discover what had lured the Zorah Magdaros astray, culminating in the discovery of an entirely new Elder Dragon species.
The Zorah Magdaros has a penchant for greatly affecting the ecosystem around it as it perishes, with the bioenergy from the individual repelled into the open ocean possessing the potential to create another New World in tens of thousands of years. At some point in the distant past, a massive Zorah Magdaros was among the dragons attempting to cross to the New World, however, this individual perished at sea before it could reach the Rotten Vale. The bioenergy contained within this giant roiled through its corpse and over time, formed a bizarre region atop its remains, a land in which contradictory climates coexist and monster species of all kinds thrive. The resulting land mass would come to be known as the Guiding Lands.
Elsewhere, after many months at sea, a ship of veteran warriors had finally delivered with a harpoon the final blow to a gargantuan dragon. In a pyrrhic victory, both the monster and the ship crashed onto the northern shore of the Frost Islands, marooning the warriors. The Elder Dragon's corpse attracted monsters into a feeding frenzy, and what became of the warriors is unknown. Littering the area are the remains of the giant Elder Dragon's—its skull pierced by a Dragonator along with its spine—and the splintered ship.
Music
Main article: Zorah Magdaros (Music)
"Beast with Fire Upon its Back" is Zorah Magdaros' theme. As a penultimate story boss for World, the theme contains a motif from " Stars at Our Backs ", the debut game's main theme. When the Dragonator is used to attack the monster, "Proof of a Hero - Monster Hunter: World version" will play.
Development
According to Yuya Tokuda, the purpose of Zorah Magdaros in Monster Hunter: World was to make both the gameplay and story equally exciting. The gameplay features the spectacle of a battle on top of a moving volcano. Meanwhile, the story features the struggle between Zorah Magdaros, Nergigante, and Xeno'jiiva, with the Research Commission keeping all three at bay. From Kaname Fujioka, Zorah Magdaros underwent heavy experimentation. The shape of the shell needed to be designed to allow for various features. These included its two halves fitting together when Zorah changes stances, the Hunter accessing the Magmacores in both stances, and the appearance of other monsters.
The book Monster Hunter World: The Official Complete Works displays concept art of several earlier Zorah Magdaros designs. Many of the designs have legs spread out like a lizard. The shells tend to have only one large Magmacore in a volcano-like structure. Few of them appear to have topography that a hunter could traverse. Two of the designs bear a striking resemblance to Dire Miralis. The Monster Hunter: World Hunter’s Thanksgiving 2018 Official Pamphlet provides more early designs. One depicts a giant serpent with a line of volcanoes on its back. One takes inspiration from snails and carries a caldera lake on its shell. The last two designs show portions of the shell flipping forward, acting as a weapons platform that launches magma balls from various crater-like organs.
There were ideas to put more emphasis on species that live in symbiosis with Zorah Magdaros. Concepts show crab-like arthropods that produce hydrogen sulfide, protecting the Magmacores from the hunter. A swarm of insectivorous Wingrakes (who would become Barnos) would have flocked around the Elder Dragon that the hunter would use to traverse the shell instead of tamed Mernos.
